frame.name: Causation
frame.definition:
A Cause causes an Effect. Alternatively, an Actor, a participant of a (implicit) Cause, may stand in for the Cause.
Those frames that inherit the Causation frame have as their background the idea that some event is responsible for the occurrence of another event (or state). In the inheriting frame, typically an FE like Agent or Causer is proposed in the place of the Actor, but in the daughter frames, as in this frame, the Actor is semantically dependent on the idea of a Cause (an event or state-of-affairs) that the Actor is a participant in.
Ex: ["act" He] MADE ["Effect" me] ["Effect" angry].
Ex: If ["Cause" such a small earthquake] CAUSES ["Effect" problems], just imagine a big one!
Ex: ["Cause" The strange mutations of the rumor mill] ["Time" in the end] LED ["Effect" to it being said that he was actually a woman].
Ex: ["Actor" You] 've MADE ["Effect" it] ["Effect" impossible to continue]!
Ex: ["Cause" The ending] LEFT ["Effect" me] ["Effect" feeling kinda empty].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
A force, process, or event that produces an effect.
Ex: ["Cause" The wind] MADE the door rattle. Ex: ["Cause" The accident] CAUSED them to be more careful the next time.

fe.name: Affected
fe.definition: Agents in a joint or reciprocal action (e.g. exchange)

fe.name: Effect
fe.definition: A positive or negative evaluation of the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Actor
fe.definition:
An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not.
Ex: ["Actor" That one stone], apparently, CAUSED the avalanche that engulfed square miles of forest. Ex: ["Actor" Stephen Hawking] CAUSED an uproar when the results were published.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (_the same way_) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor's influence on the character of the event (_eagerly, quietly_).

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The natural reason for which the Causation occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action through which the Actor or Cause accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the action denoted by the target occurs.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

lexunit.name: cause.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be the cause of; make happen.

lexunit.name: cause.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing that gives rise to an action, phenomenon, or condition.

lexunit.name: make.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to exist or come about; bring about or perform

lexunit.name: lead_(to).v
lexunit.definition: FN: "One thing leads to another"; a rather vaguely defined sort of causation, although often used in quite definite cases: "Smoking leads to higher rates of lung cancer".

lexunit.name: reason.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cause, explanation, or justification.

lexunit.name: send.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to be in a specified state:

lexunit.name: bring_about.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause something to happen.

lexunit.name: precipitate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause (an undesirable event) to happen unexpectedly or prematurely.

lexunit.name: causative.a
lexunit.definition: COD: acting as a cause

lexunit.name: render.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to be or become.

lexunit.name: bring.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to be in a particular state or condition.

lexunit.name: bring on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lead to

lexunit.name: induce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring about or give rise to.

lexunit.name: wreak.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause (usually damage or harm)

lexunit.name: put.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring into a particular state or condition.

lexunit.name: since.c
lexunit.definition: COD: for the reason that; because.

lexunit.name: because.c
lexunit.definition: COD: for the reason that; since

lexunit.name: because of.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: by reason of.

lexunit.name: raise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to be heard, felt, or considered

lexunit.name: result_(in).v
lexunit.definition: COD: have (a specified end or outcome).

lexunit.name: mean.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have as a consequence or result.

lexunit.name: result.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the outcome of an occurance

lexunit.name: leave.v
lexunit.definition: FN: render

lexunit.name: for.c
lexunit.definition: : because, for the reason that

lexunit.name: see.v
lexunit.definition: FN: for the existence of one thing or event to lead, even subtly, to the occurance of another thing or event.

lexunit.name: force.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to do something by hostile means

lexunit.name: give rise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make happen or produce

lexunit.name: so.c
lexunit.definition: FN: in order to, causing

frame.name: Communication
frame.definition:
A Communicator conveys a Message to an Addressee; the Topic and Medium of the communication also may be expressed. This frame includes no specification of the method of communication (speech, writing, gesture, etc.). The frames that inherit the general Communication frame can add elaboration to the Medium in a variety of ways (_in French, on the radio program, in a letter_) or to the Manner of communication (_babble, rant, shout, whisper_). There are also frames that either do not inherit all of the FEs of this frame or do not inherit them in a straightforward manner (such as Conversation, in which Communicator and Addressee alternate roles, and are often expressed by a single, plural NP).
Ex: Let's hope ["Communicator" it] did n't have time to COMMUNICATE ["Message" any of its findings] ["Addressee" to its overlords] .
NB: For many words in this domain (those which do not inherently ascribe cognitive/social processes to a Communicator, position a statement within a conversation, or specify Medium in detail), there is a metaphorical usage which maps Communication onto an alternate POV of Becoming_aware, with corresponding maps for frames related to Communication. This metaphor is most felicitous with Means or Medium subjects, which are mapped onto the Evidence FE of Becoming_aware. In many cases this metaphor maps Communication onto the Evidence frame, but not always. Some words from the Communication domain are listed in the Evidence frame since they are deemed to be lexicalized.
Ex: ["Means" A flick of his gaze toward the doorway] TOLD ["Addressee" me] ["Message" what he really wanted] . MET Ex: ["Medium" This painting] really SPEAKS ["Addressee" to me] . ["Message" INI] MET Ex: ["Means" Putting his arm around her protectively] achieved nothing but ANNOUNCING ["Addressee" to their captors] ["Message" their vulnerability] . MET Ex: _It_ SAYS ["Message" alot] ["Means" that he did n't come back] . ["Addressee" INI] MET

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The sentient entity that uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person. Ex: ["Communicator" He] finds it hard to COMMUNICATE with people, not least his separated parents .

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator. Ex: The company must be able to COMMUNICATE ["Addressee" to potential customers] the way in which its product would satisfy their needs, and provide competitive value.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: Message A proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted. Ex: How do you COMMUNICATE to them ["Message" that you really like them] ?

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is the entity that the proposition or propositions conveyed relate to, that they are about. Ex: Had someone COMMUNICATED to the capital ["Topic" about the flagrant disregard of the religious law] ?

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed. Ex: Opinions are usually COMMUNICATED ["Medium" over the telephone] and are often given within 24 hours.

fe.name: Amount_of_information
fe.definition: The amount of information exchanged when communication occurs. Ex: He never really ["Amount_of_information" fully] COMMUNICATED his intentions.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Communicator communicates.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the communication takes place.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration is the length of time during which the communication takes place.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE describes the number of times per unit of time that the Communicator conveys a Message.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the act of communication occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which a Communicator communicates.

lexunit.name: communicate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: convey a message to someone verbally or non-verbally, e.g. He communicated his feelings mainly through his paintings.

lexunit.name: speech.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the faculty of speech

lexunit.name: indicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: point out; show.

lexunit.name: signal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: instruct or indicate by means of a signal.

lexunit.name: communication_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of communicating.

lexunit.name: communication_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: a letter or message containing information or news.

lexunit.name: contact.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a communication or relationship.

lexunit.name: codeword.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A word or phrase to protect secrecy.

lexunit.name: password.n
lexunit.definition: COD: secret word or phrase used to gain admission to something.

lexunit.name: convey.v
lexunit.definition: COD: communicate (an idea, impression, or feeling).

lexunit.name: say.v
lexunit.definition: FN: communicate a message nonverbally

frame.name: Motion
frame.definition:
Some entity (Theme) starts out in one place (Source) and ends up in some other place (Goal), having covered some space between the two (Path). Alternatively, the Area or Directionin which the Theme moves or the Distance of the movement may be mentioned.
Ex: ["Theme" That kite you see just to the right of his head] was MOVING ["Area" around] ["Speed" pretty fast] but the camera seemed to catch it ok.
Ex: There are several accounts of ["Theme" the stench] DRIFTING ["Goal" to shore] ["Source" from the ships in the middle of the river]
Ex: ["Theme" Dust particles] FLOATING ["Area" about] made him sneeze uncontrollably.
Ex: ["Theme" The grill], unsecured, ROLLED ["Distance" a few feet] ["Path" across the yard].
Ex: ["Theme" The swarm] WENT ["Direction" away] ["Goal" to the end of the hall].
The frames that inherit the general Motion frame add some elaboration to this simple idea. Inheriting frames can add Goal-profiling (_arrive, reach_), Source-profiling (_leave, depart_), or Path-profiling (_traverse, cross_), or aspects of the manner of motion (_run, jog_) or assumptions about the shape-properties, etc., of any of the places involved (_insert, extract_). A particularly complex area in the vocabulary of Motion is the depiction of the relation of Vehicles to the Theme. In some cases, no separate Theme is expressed:
Ex: The plane FLEW over the city.
In this case, the sentence is annotated in Self_motion. When the Vehicle is profiled as being operated by a Driver, the sentence is annotated in the Operate_vehicles frame:
Ex: Don't try to FLY an F-16 without training!
This is very similar to the Bringing frame which covers cases where the Vehicle is necessarily involved, but the movement of the Theme (something carried by the Vehicle) is profiled:
Ex: It's scary FLYING hundreds of people over thousands of miles of ocean every day.
Some of the same vocabulary is also used to describe the situation where Passengers Ride_vehicle or Operate_vehicle (each of these a perspective on Use_vehicles):
Ex: I FLEW to Chicago on the red-eye. Ex: I FLEW my plane across the Canadian border
Finally, there are cases where, despite the use of similar vocabulary, there is no self-propelled Vehicle involved at all:
Ex: The ball FLEW over the fence.
This last type is annotated in the simple Motion frame.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the entity that changes location. Note that it is not necessarily a self-mover. Ex: The explosion made ["Thm" me] MOVE in a hurry.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the location the Theme occupies initially before its change of location.
Ex: The policeman MOVED ["Src" away from the door].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Theme travels or to a landmark by which the Theme travels.
Ex: Jo MOVED ["Path" past Dad] into the hall.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is the location the Theme ends up in.
Ex: The car MOVED ["Goal" into the slow lane].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
Area identifies the setting in which the Theme's movement takes place without a specified Path.
Ex: Emily MOVED restlessly ["Area" around the room].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of the Motion. Ex: The twig FLOATED atop the water ["Dist" for about 100 yards].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
This FE is used for the Speed at which the Theme moves.
Ex: The ash cloud DRIFTED ["Spd" at twenty-five kilometres per hour].

fe.name: Carrier
fe.definition:
The Carrier is the means of conveyance of the Theme.
Ex: The nest BLEW from its tree ["Car" in a gale].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Motion takes place.
Ex: The balloon FLOATED ["Dur" for hours].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Motion occurs.
Ex: A radioactive cloud DRIFTED across Britain ["Time" after the fire at the Windscale nuclear factory].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Motion takes place. Ex: A naval airship DRIFTED ["Manr" wildy] in the stormy sea.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result identifies the ultimate effect of the Motion. Ex: The feathers FLOATED ["Result" together] on the water's surface.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Theme while the motion is occuring.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the general area in which a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal) occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Theme cross a boundary as it moves away from a Source region or into a Goal region.
Ex: Pluto has MOVED ["Degree" fully]into Sagittarius

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the Goal of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body. Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Protagonist, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
In cases wherein the Theme is construed as a sentient entity, this FE denotes the state of affairs that the entity wishes to bring about by moving.
Ex: Johnny WENT to Langley ["pur" to turn himself in].

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition:
The shape of the overall Path travelled by the Theme.
Ex: They DRIFTED ["sha" in circles] for weeks before rescue .

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: An event that the described motion forms an integral part of.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

lexunit.name: move.v
lexunit.definition: FN: go in a specified direction or manner

lexunit.name: go.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move from one place to another; travel.

lexunit.name: drift.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be carried slowly by a current of air or water.

lexunit.name: glide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move with a smooth, quiet, continuous motion.

lexunit.name: blow.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be carried or driven by the wind.

lexunit.name: float.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move slowly or hover in a liquid or the air

lexunit.name: coast.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move easily without using power.

lexunit.name: roll.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move by turning over and over on an axis.

lexunit.name: soar.v
lexunit.definition: COD: glide high in the air.

lexunit.name: fly.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move or be hurled quickly through the air.

lexunit.name: slide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move along a smooth surface, especially downwards, while maintaining continuous contact with it.

lexunit.name: swerve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: abruptly diverge or from a straight course

lexunit.name: snake.v
lexunit.definition: COD: extend with the twisting motion of a snake

lexunit.name: meander.v
lexunit.definition: COD: follow a winding course, or wander aimlessly.

lexunit.name: undulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move with a smooth wave-like motion

lexunit.name: weave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move from side to side to progress around obstructions.

lexunit.name: wind.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move in or take a twisting or spiral course.

lexunit.name: zigzag.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take a zigzag course.

lexunit.name: circle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move in a circle

lexunit.name: spiral.v
lexunit.definition: FN: go in a spiral course.

lexunit.name: swing.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move quickly changing direction

lexunit.name: travel.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move.

frame.name: Perception
frame.definition: A Perceiver perceives a Phenomenon. The general Perception frame is an inherited background to all frames that have to do with some sentient being responding to changes in the environment, independently of the sensory modalities. The inheriting frames may specify the modalities (_see, hear, taste, smell_), or may emphasize the experiences or acts of the perceiver (_peek, eavesdrop_), or the properties of the perceived phenomena (_clank, rattle, thump_).

fe.name: Perceiver
fe.definition: The FE Perceiver refers to someone whose cognitive state or experience (e.g. knowledge, beliefs, ideas judgments or classifications) is being described.

fe.name: Sought_entity
fe.definition:
The Perceiver is the entity or event which causes the perceptual experience of the Perceiver.
Ex: So do our domestic dogs PERCEIVE ["Sou" smells] with the same range of subtle `hues' as we perceive colour?

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver.
Ex: Kim PERCEIVED ["Phenomenon" a flaw].

frame.name: Reciprocality
frame.definition: This frame characterizes states-of-affairs with Protagonists in relations with each other that may be viewed symmetrically. When the Protagonists are equally prominent, each equally serving to identify the others, they are expressed together as Protagonists. When one of the Protagonists serves to define the other (more or less as a Ground), it is called Protagonist_2, and the other is called Protagonist_1 (i.e. the Figure). Ex: This frame exists as a background for a number of lexical frames, including Chatting, Similarity, Exchange, and Being_attached. The most basic frames inheriting from this one are symmetrical states. (For example, Being_attached is symmetrical, since if A is attached to B, B is attached to A.) Ex: Other frames exhibiting reciprocality either have a causative/inchoative relation to such a stative frame (e.g. ), or are stative-like summarizations of multiple events of the same kind. This second type, in which events are performed reciprocally, with two equal participants acting on each other, can be exemplified by the Chatting frame in which two people are effectively both speakers and addressees in a joint act of communication. Ex: The basic characteristic of this frame, inherited in the daughters, is the equivalence of Protagonist_1 + Protagonist_2 to Protagonists, and the further equivalence (modulo figure/ground profiling) of the following: Ex: Protagonist_1 _Relation_ with Protagonist_2. Ex: Protagonist_2 _Relation_ with Protagonist_1. Ex: Protagonists _Relation_.

fe.name: Protagonist_1
fe.definition: The particpant in a reciprocal event that is encoded as the subject of an active-form sentence or as a by-PP in a passive. `Ex: ["Protagonist_1" You] can't ARGUE politics with foreigners,' sighed the policeman.

fe.name: Protagonist_2
fe.definition: The participant in a reciprocal event that is coded in a with-PP. Ex: We have been ARGUING the point ["Protagonist_2" with the inspector at claims branch] for many many months and we just seem to go round in circles.

fe.name: Protagonists
fe.definition: The jointly expressed participants in a reciprocal activity. Ex: ["Protagonists" They] were GOSSIPING about the weather and American football.

frame.name: Transitive_action
frame.definition: This frame characterizes, at a very abstract level, an Agent or Cause affecting a Patient. This frame is inherited by many lower-level frames.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: Agent is the entity that acts on another entity.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: Patient is the entity that is being acted on and that may but need not undergo a change.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: Event is an event in which an agent acts on an entity.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action. Ex: The ["Depictive" sloppy] person DID the room.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of a transitive action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by anAgent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the event takes place

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the event takes place.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event which causes the Patient to be affected in some way.

frame.name: Duplication
frame.definition:
This frame involves a Creator making a duplicate, the Copy, of some Original entity. A Source, the location of the Original, and Goal, the location of the Copy, may be expressed.
Ex: ["Creator" The teacher] COPIED ["Original" the problem] ["Goal" onto the blackboard].
Ex: ["Copy" His handouts] were ["Manner" poorly] PHOTOCOPIED ["Creator" by his assistant]["Original" from my originals ].

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: The Creator produces the Copy based on the Original. It is normally expressed as an External Argument. Ex: ["Creat" Pat] PHOTOCOPIED the article.

fe.name: Original
fe.definition: The Original is the entity which is copied. With verbs it is frequently expressed as an NP Object:Ex: Pat PHOTOCOPIED ["Orig" the article].

fe.name: Copy
fe.definition: The Copy produced by the Creator is frequently not expressed. However, when Copy does occur, it is usually expressed as the External Argument of verbs: Ex: ["Copy" The results] REPLICATE those of an earlier study.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the location from which material is copied, i.e. the location of the Original. Unlike the FE Source in other domains and frames, there is no actual movement of either Copy or Original from this location. Source is usually expressed by a PP Complement.
Ex: I COPIED the design ["Src" from a magazine].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is the location to which material is copied. Unlike the FE Goal in other frames, there is no actual movement of any entity to this location. Goal is usually expressed as a PP Complement: Ex: COPY the file ["Goal" onto the hard drive].

fe.name: Characterization
fe.definition: This FE designates the character of the medium in which a Copy is made. Usually, it is expressed as PP-in or AP. Ex: They sold a million COPIES ["Char" in hardback]. Ex: Opposite is Pilinsky's ["Char" wood-engraved] COPY. Ex: The margins are covered in COPIES of the works of Shelley ["Char" in Joan's handwriting].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Creator that lets them bring about the duplication.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE identifies anyDepictive phrase that describes a primary participant, either the Creator or the Copy/Original.
Ex: Such leaflets have to be DUPLICATED ["Depict" en masse]. Ex: She did the COPYING ["Depict" unaware of the fact that John had already finished it].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes Place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Fidelity
fe.definition: The way in which the Copy matches or does not match the Original. Ex: I made a ["Fid" half-size] COPY.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The Iteration is the number of times the Original is copied. Ex: ["Creator" Jim] COPIED ["Original" the book] ["Iteration" 300 times].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency is the frequency with which the Original is copied. Ex: ["Creator" The scribes] COPIED ["Original" the scripture] ["Frequency" every 80 years].

lexunit.name: clone.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing regarded as identical with another; a copy or double.

lexunit.name: copy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a thing made to be similar or identical to another.

lexunit.name: copy.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make a copy of.

lexunit.name: duplicate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: one of two or more identical things.

lexunit.name: duplicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or be an exact copy of.

lexunit.name: photocopy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a photographic copy of something produced by a process involving the action of light on a specially prepared surface.

lexunit.name: photocopy.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make a photocopy of.

lexunit.name: reduplicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: repeat or copy so as to form another of the same kind.

lexunit.name: replicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make an exact copy of; reproduce.

lexunit.name: reproduce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce a copy or representation of.

lexunit.name: replica.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an exact copy or model of something, especially one on a smaller scale.

lexunit.name: duplication.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the fact of making an exact copy

lexunit.name: run off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce a copy on a machine.

frame.name: Feigning
frame.definition:
An Agent acts in such a way as to give the incorrect impression to observers that a particular State_of_affairs holds.
Ex: ["Agent" Jordan] FEIGNED ["Original" a love of jazz music] ["Purpose" to get her phone number] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that a State_of_affairs holds.
Ex: A year after ["agt" Audrey Seiler] FAKED her own kidnapping while at college in Wisconsin, her lawyer says she's getting help and paying restitution.

fe.name: Original
fe.definition: This is the entity which is copied. With verbs it is frequently expressed as an NP Object: Pat FALSIFIED ["Original" the papers].

fe.name: Copy
fe.definition: The Copy produced by the Creator most commonly occurs as the External Argument of a predicative use of an adjective or noun target: ["Copy" The painting] is a FAKE.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation. Ex: I FEIGNED death ["Mns" by breaking a bag of pig's blood and falling to the floor].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
The State_of_affairs is a an event, a state, or a property that the Agent wants others to believe have occurred or hold.
Ex: A college student who STAGED ["State_of_affairs" her own disappearance] last month will try to reach a plea agreement and avoid trial on charges she obstructed officers.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action or state that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the feigning of some State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the feigning event logically follows.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Agent engages in the Feigning event.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Agent feigns something.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that the Agent feigns something.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs as being in some state during the feigning action.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place in which the Agent feigns something.

frame.name: Cause_to_amalgamate
frame.definition:
These words refer to an Agent joining Parts to form a Whole. (The Parts may also be encoded as Part_1 and Part_2.) There is a symmetrical relationship between the components that undergo the process, and afterwards the Parts are consumed and are no longer distinct entities that are easily discernable or separable in the Whole.
Ex: ["Agent" Chuck] MERGED ["Parts" the corpora].Ex: ["Agent" Chuck] MERGED ["Parts" the corpora] ["Whole" into a database]. Ex: ["Agent" Chuck] MERGED ["Part_1" the BNC] ["Part_2" with the AP Corpus] ["Whole" into a database]. Ex: ["Parts" The two forces] MERGED ["Whole" into a single, undifferentiated mass of murderous mayhem].(Sense 2) Ex: Melt the butter, then BLEND ["Part_1" it] ["Part_2" with the room temperature milk]. ["Agent" CNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: In causative uses of these verbs there is an Agent responsible for amalgamating the Parts. The Agent is generally the External Argument (or the object of a PP-by in passives).Ex: ["Agent" The chef] COMBINED the ingredients.Ex: The ingredients were COMBINED ["Agent" by the chef].

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: This FE identifies Whole as the entity resulting from combination of Parts. When overtly expressed, it is usually a PP Complement (often headed by into).Ex: Chuck MERGED the corpora ["Whole" into a database]. Ex: The directors MERGED the two companies ["Whole" into a conglomorate].

fe.name: Parts
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Parts entities being combined, and is often expressed in a single plural NP, usually the direct object of a verb. Ex: Chuck MERGED ["Parts" the corpora] into a database.Ex: The directors MERGED ["Parts" the two companies] into a conglomerate.

fe.name: Part_1
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the first of two Parts mentioned. It is most often the NP-Object of a verb.
Ex: The workmen JOINED ["Part_1" the annex] to the main building.

fe.name: Part_2
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the second of two Parts mentioned. It is usually a PP Complement.
Ex: The workkmen JOINED the annex ["Part_2" to the main building].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the amalgamating occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the thoroughness of the mixing job, i.e. to what degree the resulting Whole is undifferentiated.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the amalgamating occurs.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE is used for indicating the Result of amalgamating. Ex: Chuck MERGED the corpora ["Result" together].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Parts during the amalgamation. Often it refers to the proportion of the Parts to one another.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Agent seeks to bring about by the Amalgamation.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location that the event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the amalgamation occurs.

frame.name: Separating
frame.definition:
These words refer to separating a Whole into Parts, or separating one part from another. The separation is made by an Agent or Cause and may be made on the basis of some Criterion.
Ex: ["Agent" I] DIVIDED ["Whole" the class] ["Parts" into groups] ["Criterion" in alphabetial order] .

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The Whole is a single entity or an aggregate of entities which is separated into Parts. It is usually the NP Object of a target verb. Ex: The directors SPLIT ["Whole" the company] in two. Ex: The teacher DIVIDED ["Whole" the children] into groups.

fe.name: Parts
fe.definition: This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from separation of a Whole: Ex: The directors SPLIT the company ["Parts" in two]. Ex: The teacher DIVIDED the children ["Parts" into groups]. Ex: The teacher SEPARATED the children ["Parts" from each other].

fe.name: Part_1
fe.definition: Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned. This is most often the Object of a verb. Ex: First, SEPARATE ["Part_1" the yolks] from the whites.

fe.name: Part_2
fe.definition: Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement. First, Ex: SEPARATE the yolks ["Part_2" from the whites].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: With causative uses of these verbs, an Agent separates or divides something. The Agent is usually expressed as the External Argument: Ex: ["Agent" The researcher] DIVIDED subjects into groups.

fe.name: Criterion
fe.definition: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which is used as the basis for separation. Criterion is typically expressed as a PP headed by _by_, or as a complex PP of the form _on the basis of_.... Ex: The researcher DIVIDED subjects into groups ["Criterion" on the basis of eye color]. As with the frame General.Joining (above), words in this frame can be used statively, as in _The rooms are separated by a partition_, inchoatively, as in _The group separated_ or causatively, as in _I separated the laundry_.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent who separates or the undergoers of the separation. Ex: ["Depictive" Naked], ["Agent" Selma Bouvier] SEPARATED ["Part_1" the yolks] ["Part_2" from the whites].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Agent that accomplishes the separation. Ex: You can BISECT an angle ["Mns" by drawing three circles].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-agent that brings about the separation.

fe.name: Recipients
fe.definition: The Recipients are the groups who come into possession of the Parts of the Whole. Ex: ["Agent" Mrs. Simpson] DIVIDED ["Whole" the candy] ["Recipients" between her children].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the separation occurs. Ex: I DIVIDED the prize money among the winners ["Time" that night]..

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the separation occurs. Ex: You should SEPARATE the yolks from the whites ["Place" over the sink].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument used to cause the separation. Ex: I SECTIONED the block ["Inst" with a knife].

frame.name: Body_movement
frame.definition:
This frame contains words for motions or actions an Agent performs using some part of his/her body.
A number of words in this frame occur as blends with Communication, in which the action has an Addressee. For example,
Ex: Pat NODDED ["Addressee" at Kim].
These examples differ from Communication.Gesture in that no specific message need be expressed, as in Ex: She NODDED to him to sit down.
Since this frame involves a particular type of motion, it contains the frame elements Source, Path, Goal and Area, which originate in the motion frame. All of these frame elements are generally expressed in PP Complements. Ex: The boy SWUNG his legs ["Source" from under the table].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent uses some part of his/her body to perform the action. Agent occurs as the External Argument. Ex: ["Agent" The boy] SWUNG his legs.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: With some verbs in this frame, the Body_part involved in the action is specified by the meaning of the verb and cannot be expressed separately. For example, Ex: Pat YAWNED (*his mouth). With others, the Body_part is specified by the verb but can optionally be expressed separately, although its presence is generally redundant, as in Ex: Pat NODDED ["BodP" (his head)]. A few verbs have a default Body_part which need not be expressed, but can be overridden by the expression of some other Body_part. Ex: Pat WAVED ["BodP" (his arms)]. (The objectless version of the sentence, _Pat waved_, is a blend with communication.) The remainder of the verbs require a Body_part to be expressed in a separate constituent: Ex: Pat ROLLED ["BodP" his eyes]. Body_part generally occurs as the direct object.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: Body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement. Ex: Kim BENT her head ["ICause" in concentration]. Ex: Kim THREW her hands up ["ICause" in despair].

fe.name: External_cause
fe.definition: Cause is something in the external environment that causes the Agent to move part of his/her body. Cause is usually expressed in a PP Complement:. Ex: Pat JERKED her head ["Cause" at the sudden noise]. Ex: Kim's nose WRINKLED ["Cause" at the smell]. Ex: Cause does not include any physical force moving the Agent's Body_part. This type of situation is described by the frame Motion.Cause-to-move.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: Addressee only occurs in the Body-movement frame in sentences which are blends with Communication. Where it occurs, it is typically a PP Complement: Ex: Pat FLUTTERED his eyelashes ["Add" at me].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source is the place from which the Body_part is moved. Ex: The boy SWUNG his legs ["Source" from under the table].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path identifies the trajectory of motion of the Body_part without specifying a start or end point. Ex: Pat FLUNG his arms ["Path" up].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal is any expression that identifies the endpoint of movement.
Ex: Pat DROPPED her hands ["Goal" to her lap].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
Area identifies any expression describing a region in which the motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. (This FE should be contrasted with Place.)
Ex: Pat WAVED her arms ["Area" about her head].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the body movement occurs.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Message that the body movement conveys.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the body movement occurs.

fe.name: Sub-region
fe.definition: This FE specifies the subregion of the body that is involved with movement. Ex: ["Agent" He] BENT ["Body_part" his legs] ["Sub-region" at his knees]

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose of the body movement. Ex: He winked his eye ["Purpose" to give her a hint]

fe.name: Cognate_event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event noun of the verb. Ex: He CLAPPED ["Cognate_event" his loudest clap]

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time during which the movement of a Body_part occurs.
Ex: It seemed like we were clapping our hands ["dur" for hours].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location within which the movement of a Body_part takes place.
Ex: There was singing for joy in the streets, and ["pla" everywhere] people lifting their arms into the air.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition:
An alternative description of the Body_movement.
Ex: ["ree" In a bid to reenter the conversation] , he kept WAVING his hand towards the rest of them.

fe.name: Coordinated_event
fe.definition:
An event that the Agent perceives and responds to by moving in coordination with it.
Ex: They BOBBED their heads ["coo" to the beat].

frame.name: Manipulation
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe the manipulation of an Entity by anAgent. Ex: ["Agent" Ian] SQUEEZED ["Entity" Mara's hand]. Ex: A number of lexemes listed in this frame also occur in the frame Cause-to-move (for example, _push, yank_). Only the non-motion uses of these words belong in this frame, e.g., combinations such as _push at, push on, yank at_.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent manipulates an object. Agent typically refers to animate beings, but is also extended to mechanical and other inanimate objects. Agent is most frequently expressed as the external argument of verbs: ["Agent" A robot arm] GRASPS the box on the conveyor belt and seals it.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity being manipulated often occurs as the direct object of verbs: SQUEEZE ["Entity" the ball] as many times as you can. Pat SQUEEZED ["Entity" Jo's hand].

fe.name: Locus
fe.definition: The Agent's manipulation of an Entity may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Entity, a Locus. The Locus is usually expressed as a PP Complement. Ex: Pat SQUEEZED Jo ["Locus" by the hand].

fe.name: Bodypart_of_agent
fe.definition: The part of the Agent's body being used to manipulate the Entity may also be expressed. While the default is for an Agent to use his/her hands, other body parts may be specified. This frame element usually occurs as a PP-complement. Ex: Kim GRASPED the needle ["Bodypart_of_agent" between finger and thumb].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of the manipulation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of manipulation.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Manipulation takes place Ex: I SEIZED the letter ["Time" before he did].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Agent's purpose in performing the manipulation. Ex: The President GRABBED HOLD of the handle of the helicopter ["Purp" to avoid being blown away].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with the Entity to accomplish the action indicated by the target.
Ex: Smithers NUDGED the insect["Instrument" with a paper towel].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action by the Agent to accomplish the desired manipulation.
Ex: Martin CLUTCHED it ["Means" by pulling a rope attached to a pully which tightened the belt to the PVC]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The spatial setting in which the manipulation takes place.
Ex: ["Place" In the hallway] he managed to GRABthe monarch by the ankles

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the Agent or Bodypart_of_agent that holds throughout the action.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs leading to the manipulation

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

frame.name: Posture
frame.definition:
An Agent supports their body in a particular Location. The LUs of the frame convey which body part is the Point_of_contact where the Agent is supported, what orientation the body is in, and some overall arrangement of the limbs (especially the legs) and the torso.
Ex: ["Agent" He] KNELT down Location , ["Depictive" hand on heart] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the individual whose body is in a particular posture. The Agent FE is generally expressed as the external argument of verbs: Ex: ["Agent" Kim] was KNEELING by the window.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: A description of the position of the Agent. The Location of the Agent is frequently expressed and generally occurs as a PP Complement: Ex: Kim was KNEELING ["Location" by the window].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Agent's state throughout the time they are in a particular posture.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition: A state of the Agent which crucially depends on their posture. Ex: She SAT ["Dependent_state" upright]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Agent held a certain posture.
Ex: ["Time" Yesterday evening] he was SITTING in his armchair as usual

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which the Agent holds the posture.
Ex: Joel SAT on the porch ["Purpose" to watch the traffic go by]

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time for which the Agent holds the posture.
Ex: I could have STOOD there ["Duration" all afternoon]

fe.name: Point_of_contact
fe.definition:
The part of the body that provides support to the Agent's body in the posture.
Ex: I STOOD ["poc" on my heels] and looked out the window

frame.name: Awareness
frame.definition:
A Cognizer has a piece of Content in their model of the world. The Content is not necessarily present due to immediate perception, but usually, rather, due to deduction from perceivables. In some cases, the deduction of the Content is implicitly based on confidence in sources of information (_believe_), in some cases based on logic (_think_), and in other cases the source of the deduction is deprofiled (_know_).
Note that this frame is undergoing some degree of reconsideration. Many of the targets will be moved to the Opinion frame. That frame indicates that the Cognizer considers something as true, but the Opinion (compare to Content) is not presupposed to be true; rather it is something that is considered a potential point of difference. In the uses that will remain in the Awareness frame, however, the Content is presupposed.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Your boss] is AWARE ["Content" of your commitment].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer is the person whose awareness of phenomena is at question. With a target verb or adjective the Cognizer is generally expressed as an External Argument with the Content expressed as an Object or Complement. Ex: ["Cognizer" Your boss] is AWARE of your commitment. Ex: ["Cognizer" The students] do not KNOW the answer. Ex: ["Cognizer" Pat] BELIEVES that things will change for the better.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The Content is the object of the Cognizer's awareness. Content can be expressed as a direct object or in a PP Complement.
Ex: Your boss is AWARE ["Content" of your commitment]. Ex: The students do not KNOW ["Content" of your commitment]. Ex: Pat BELIEVES ["Content" that things will change for the better].

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: The source of awareness or knowledge which can be expressed in a PP Complement: Ex: The sailors KNEW ["Evid" from the look of the sky] that a storm was coming. Ex: I KNEW ["Evid" from experience] that Jo would be late.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Some verbs in this frame allow a Topic to be expressed in about-PPs. Ex: Kim KNOWS ["Topic" about first aid]. However, a number of nouns and adjectives in this frame which cannot take about-phrases allow Topic to be expressed as an adjectival or adverbial modifier. Ex: Kim is ["Topic" politically] AWARE. Ex: ["Topic" Environmental] CONSCIOUSNESS is increasing.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer knows or thinks something.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: Expressor is the body part that reveals the Cognizer's state to the observer. Ex: Bob's ["Expr" eyes] were overly AWARE

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Role is the category within which an element of the Content is considered. Ex: He UNDERSTOOD her remark ["Role" as an insult].

fe.name: Paradigm
fe.definition: This frame element identifies the Paradigm which serves as the basis for the Cognizer's awareness. Ex: ["Content" The formation of black holes] should be UNDERSTOOD ["Paradigm" in astrophysic terms].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the Cognizer is aware of the Content.
Ex: Yet there is no evidence that Mr. Parrish was COGNIZANT ["tim" at the time of the signing of the notes] that the clauses in issue were present.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why or how it came to be that the Cognizer has awareness of the Topic or Content.

frame.name: Becoming_aware
frame.definition:
Words in this frame have to do with a Cognizer adding some Phenomenon to their model of the world. They are similar to Coming-to-believe words, except the latter generally involve reasoning from Evidence. Ex: The words in this frame take direct objects that denote entities in the world, and indicate awareness of those entities, without necessarily giving any information about the content of the Cognizer's belief or knowledge. These words also resemble perception words, since creatures often become aware of things by perceiving them.
Ex: ["T" Later that night], ["Cog" they] FOUND ["Phen" the barely-alive victim] ["Ground" inside the Red Hall estate flat].
Ex: ["T" Almost immediately], ["Cog" the police] DISCOVERED ["Phen" the wrought-iron crypt gate] ["State" swinging open].
Ex: ["Ground" In the bag on the table]["Cog" I] could ["Deg" vaguely]DISCERN ["Phen" two bottles of wine and several cartons of cakes and other goodies].
Ex: ["Cog" People passing through] RECOGNIZE ["Phen" it] ["Ground" from afar], ["Evid" by the clouds of coal dust darkening the air].
General Grammatical Observations: Passive forms of the verbs in this frame can occur with extraposed clauses expressing Phenomenon: Ex: That year it was DISCOVERED ["Phen" that consumers preferred the older model]. Ex: It is not always RECOGNIZED ["Phen" how much work goes into a dinner party].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the person who becomes aware of a Phenomenon. It is normally expressed as an External Argument.
Ex: ["Cog" Pat] DISCOVERED a great little restaurant in Soho.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
Thm Phenomenon is the entity or situation in the world of which a Cognizer becomes aware. It is normally expressed as an Object:
Ex: Pat DISCOVERED ["Phenomenon" a great little restaurant] in Soho.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The Ground is the background or context against which a Cognizer becomes aware of a Phenomenon. It is normally expressed by a locative PP:
Ex: Pat DISCOVERED a great little restaurant ["Ground" in Soho]. Ex: I NOTICED a hint of sarcasm ["Ground" in her voice].

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
The State indicates the state or situation of the Phenomenon at the time when the Cognizer becomes aware of it. It is normally expressed by a Predicate expression (e.g. a PP or a participial VP):
Ex: We DISCOVERED the children ["State" playing in the pantry].

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
The Evidence is some fact that allows the Cognizer to become aware of something. It is normally expressed with PP-_from_:
Ex: We DISCOVERED ["Evidence" from their job performance] that they were well-trained.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which becoming aware is occurring.
Ex: Sue could ["Deg" faintly] DISCERN the shape of a skull under Cheeks ' plump face.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the Manner in which becoming aware occurs.
Ex: Pupils ["Manr" quickly] DISCERN what is acceptable to the teacher and merely aim to fulfil those expectations.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the Means by which the Cognizer becomes aware of the Phenomenon.
Ex: ["Mns" By opening the book to page 10], you will FIND the Van Eerdens' number.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
Topic indicates the general field within which the Phenomenon is found.
Ex: Scientists attempt to make DISCOVERIES ["Top" about the laws of nature].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer becomes aware of the Phenomenon.
Ex: Robbie had wondered if they would be able to FIND the path ["T" at night].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The goal that the Cognizer has in mind, which they believe to be accomplishable by finding the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
The Cognizer uses an Instrument to (enable themselves to) become aware of the Phenomenon. In some cases, the Instrument may appear in subject position.
Ex: Olson says the deputy came out to the farm and DETECTED a radioactive substance ["ins" with his Geiger counter].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: his frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative.

frame.name: Categorization
frame.definition:
A Cognizer construes an Item as belonging to a certain Category. In this process, the Cognizer may either passively perceive the Item and note that it fits the Criteria for a Category, or, alternatively, actively examine the Item for certain Criteria that define a Category (or set of Categorys).
Most members of the frame can also describe a resulting cognitive state of the Cognizer with respect to the Item and Category which no longer requires the current perception or consideration of the Item. A few LUs (e.g. _peg.v, pigeonhole.v_) do not readily allow stative interpretation, and a few LUs (e.g. _deem.v, regard.v_) only allow stative interpretation.
Ex: ["Cognizer" You] 've already STEREOTYPED ["Item" me] ["Category" as a bimbo], have n't you?

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Kim] CATEGORIZED the books under fiction. ["Cognizer" Kim] CATEGORIZED them on the basis of genre.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
This is the entity which is construed or treated by the Cognizer as being an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as an Object.
Ex: Kim CATEGORIZED ["Item" the books] under fiction.

fe.name: Category
fe.definition:
This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by _as_ or _under_.
Ex: Kim CATEGORIZED the book ["Category" as/under fiction].

fe.name: Criteria
fe.definition:
This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified _by color_ or _by finish (matte or gloss)_; if they are classified by color, one can be classified _as orange_ and another _as red_. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by _by_, or as a complex PP of the form _on the basis of..._:
Ex: The students were CATEGORIZED ["Crit" on the basis of their test scores]. Ex: The librarian CLASSIFIED the books ["Crit" by subject].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Cognizer categorizes.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.
Ex: ["Time" 20 years ago] people would CONSIDER this as nothing unusual

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds. Ex: ["Item" Material posessions] are DEFINED ["Category" as valuable] ["Circumstances" in a particular society].

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Cognizer categorizes the Item in the given way.

frame.name: Cogitation
frame.definition:
A person, the Cognizer, thinks about a Topic over a period of time. What is thought about may be a course of action that the person might take, or something more general.
Ex: ["Cognizer" The men] were ["Manner" silently] MULLING OVER ["Topic" the proposition of committing an assassination]

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
With a target verb, the Cognizer is usually expressed as an External Argument, with the Topic appearing as an Object NP, a gerundive verbal Complement, or a PP. Ex: ["Cognizer" Pat] CONSIDERED a career change. Ex: ["Cognizer" The employees] CONTEMPLATED going on strike. Ex: ["Cognizer" Everyone] THOUGHT about the game.
With a target noun, the Cognizer is typically expressed as the External Argument of a _support verb_, as a possessor, or in a PP. Ex: ["Cognizer" The teacher] GAVE some THOUGHT to a career change. Ex: ["Cognizer" Your] THOUGHTS about art are not relevant. Ex: Your application was submitted for CONSIDERATION ["Cognizer" by the committee].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
With a target verb, the Topic is usually expressed as an Object NP, a gerundive verbal complement, or a PP. Ex: Pat CONSIDERED ["Topic" a career change]. Ex: The employees CONTEMPLATED ["Topic" going on strike]. Ex: Everyone THOUGHT ["Topic" about the game].
With a target noun, the Topic is typically expressed in a PP. Ex: Your CONTEMPLATION ["Topic" of a career change] is understandable. Ex: Your THOUGHTS ["Topic" about art] are not relevant.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The FE Degree indicates the degree to which the cognizing occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The FE Manner indicates the way in which the cognizing is being done.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer that makes them able to cogitate.

fe.name: Result

fe.name: Medium

The physical or abstract setting in which the Cognizer considers the Topic.
Ex: ["Medium" Over the telephone], Frank PONDERED telling Maria about the fire.

fe.name: Purpose

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Cognizer considers the Topic.

frame.name: Coming_to_believe
frame.definition:
A person (the Cognizer) comes to believe something (the Content), sometimes after a process of reasoning. This change in belief is usually initiated by a person or piece of Evidence. Occasionally words in this domain are accompanied by phrases expressing Topic, i.e. that which the mental Content is about.
Ex: ["Evidence" Based on the most recent census] ["Cognizer" I] have CONCLUDED ["Content" that most Americans sleep too much].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: Cognizer is the person who comes to believe something. ["Cognizer" Sue] REALIZED that Bob was lost.

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: Words in this frame may occur with a PP headed by _from_ which expresses the Evidence on which knowledge or belief is based: I have LEARNED ["Evidence" from experience] that poison oak can be painful.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: With a target verb, the Content is usually expressed as a finite clausal Complement or an Object NP, and may sometimes be expressed by a PP: The President LEARNED ["Content" that the reporters were hungry]. The children DETERMINED ["Content" the answer].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Some verbs in this frame may occur with postverbal Topic expressions: They FOUND OUT ["Topic" about us]! More generally verbs in this frame may occur with quantificational nouns followed by Topic expressions: The jury LEARNED something terrible ["Topic" about the suspect].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive phrase describing the Cognizer.
Ex: We REALIZED it ["Dep" eating dinner]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Cognizer which enables them to figure something out. Ex: ["Means" A post-mortem examination] was unable to ASCERTAIN the cause of death.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Cognizer discovers the Content.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the text created by the Cognizer to communicate that they came to believe a specified Content.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the Cognizer realizes the Content.
Ex: ["pla" Back at the tailor's shop], I DEDUCED that our murderer was not the owner of the kerchief.

lexunit.name: infer.v

lexunit.name: inference.n

lexunit.name: learn.v

lexunit.name: realization.n

frame.name: Differentiation
frame.definition:
Words in this frame have to do with a Cognizer being aware (or not being aware) of the difference between two Phenomena, which may be expressed jointly or disjointly.
Ex: It is very difficult for ["Cognizer" people] to ["Means" visually] DISTINGUISH ["Phenomena" between living and non-living things] ["Circumstances" from such a great distance] .

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The cognizer is the person (or other sentient being) who potentially determines that two Phenomena are distinct from each other. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: Ex: ["Cognizer" The teacher] couldn't DISTINGUISH one child from the other.

fe.name: Phenomenon_1
fe.definition: The phenomena that are potentially judged to be different from one another can be expressed as separate constituents. When they are, one is typically expressed as an NP Object, and the other as a PP Complement headed by _from_: Ex: The teacher couldn't DISTINGUISH Pat from Kim. In this case, the phenomenon expressed more prominently as an NP Object is called Phenomenon_1: Ex: The teacher couldn't DISTINGUISH ["Phenomenon_1" Pat] from Kim.

fe.name: Phenomenon_2
fe.definition: See Phenomenon_1, above. The phenomenon expressed less prominently as a PP complement is called Phenomenon_2: Ex: The teacher couldn't DISTINGUISH Pat ["Phenomenon_2" from Kim].

fe.name: Phenomena
fe.definition: Both phenomena that are potentially judged to be different from one another can be expressed jointly by the same constituent: Ex: The teacher couldn't DISTINGUISH ["Phenomena" the twins]. Such constituents are assigned the FE Phenomena. They are always plural, as in the above example, or involve conjunction: Ex: The teacher couldn't DISTINGUISH ["Phenomena" Pat and Kim].

fe.name: Quality
fe.definition: This is a property that is potentially used by the Cognizer to distinguish one phenomenon from another. It is normally expressed as a PP headed by a preposition such as _from_, _by_, or _on the basis of_: Ex: The coach could DISTINGUISH the twins ["Quality" by their hair]. General Grammatical Observations: Verbs in this domain often occur with the modal auxiliary _can_.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: State of a participant while the action is ongoing. Ex: We DIFFERENTIATED between the squid, ["Dep" certain that their characteristics put them in different species].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer that allows them to differentiate the Phenomena.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances describe the situation in which the Cognizer evaluates the Phenomena. Ex: It is difficult to DISTINGUISH ["Phenomena" contrasing figures] ["Circumstances" from a distance].

lexunit.name: distinguish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: see or point out the difference of

lexunit.name: separate.v

lexunit.name: know.v

frame.name: Evidence
frame.definition:
The Support, a phenomenon or fact, lends support to a claim or proposed course of action, the Proposition, where the Domain_of_Relevance may also be expressed. Some of the words in this frame (e.g. argue) are communication words used in a non-communicative, epistemic sense.
Ex: ["Support" The latest poll results] SHOW ["Proposition" that support of the president is at an all-time low.]

fe.name: Support
fe.definition: Support is a fact that lends epistemic support to a claim, or that provides a reason for a course of action. Typically it is expressed as an External Argument. Ex: ["Support" The fact that you lied to me] SHOWS that I shouldn't trust you. Ex: ["Support" The look on your face] REVEALS that you are lying.

fe.name: Proposition
fe.definition: This is a belief, claim, or proposed course of action to which the Support lends validity. Normally it is expressed as a Finite Clause Complement: Ex: The fact that you lied to me SHOWS ["Proposition" that I shouldn't trust you]. Some words in this frame require the proposition to be expressed as an NP Object: Ex: The fact that you lied SUBSTANTIATES ["Proposition" the claim that you can't be trusted].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the degree to which a Proposition is supported.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the manner in which a proposition is supported. Ex: The results of the experiments PROVED the hypothesis ["Manner" brilliantly].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intermediate logical step that justifies the relationship of the Support to the Proposition. Ex: Tiny patterns in fossil rocks can DEMONSTRATE that dinosaurs and pterosaurs were (at least potentially) warm blooded ["Mns" by showing that they had feathers or hair, today found only among endotherms].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A description of the status of the Support within its relationship to the Proposition. This PROVES my conclusions ["Depictive" all by itself].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Domain_of_Relevance
fe.definition: This FE identifies the domain (usually, time or space) for which a given Proposition is true.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The person for whom the Proposition is supported by the Support.
Ex: The behavior of the children INDICATED ["Cognizer" to the teacher] that further action was required on his part.

lexunit.name: argument.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a set of reasons given in support of something.

lexunit.name: attest.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide or serve as clear evidence of.

lexunit.name: confirm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: establish the truth or correctness of.

lexunit.name: corroborate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confirm or give support to (a statment or theory)

lexunit.name: demonstrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: clearly show the existence or truth of.

lexunit.name: evidence.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be or show evidence of.

lexunit.name: evince.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reveal the presence of; indicate (a quality or feeling).

lexunit.name: prove.v
lexunit.definition: COD: demonstrate by evidence or argument the truth or existence of.

lexunit.name: reveal.v
lexunit.definition: FN: disclose or make known.

lexunit.name: show.v
lexunit.definition: FN: act as evidence or serve as proof of something

lexunit.name: substantiate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide evidence to support or prove the truth of.

lexunit.name: testify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: serve as evidence or proof of something.

lexunit.name: verify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make sure or demonstrate that (something) is true, accurate, or justified.

lexunit.name: disprove.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prove to be false

lexunit.name: contradict.v
lexunit.definition: FN: the truth of (a statement) by asserting the opposite

lexunit.name: argue.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be evidence for a conclusion

lexunit.name: mean.v
lexunit.definition: FN: indicate a fact

lexunit.name: evidence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true or valid.

lexunit.name: from.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: indicating source of evidence

lexunit.name: suggest.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause one to think that (something) exists or is the case; evoke.

lexunit.name: indicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be a sign or symptom of; strongly imply.

lexunit.name: imply.v

lexunit.name: proof.n
lexunit.definition: COD: evidence establishing a fact or the truth of a statement.

lexunit.name: tell.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be evidence for a conclusion

frame.name: Expectation
frame.definition:
Words in this frame have to do with a Cognizer believing that some Phenomenon will take place in the future. Some words in the frame (e.g. _foresee.v_) indicate that the Phenomenon is asserted also to be true, while others do not.
Ex: ["Cog" Michael] EXPECTED ["Phen" Abby] ["Phen" to demand examples]. Ex: ["Evidence" From the look on her face] ["Cog" Michael] EXPECTED ["Phen" that she would say she got the job].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: This is the person who believes some Phenomenon will take place in the future. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: ["Cognizer" Pat] EXPECTS that the Yankees will win the World Series.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: This is what the Cognizer believes will happen in the future. It can be expressed as a Finite Clause Complement, an NP Object, or a VP Complement with or without an NP Object (see General Grammatical Observations): Ex: Pat EXPECTS ["Phenomenon" that the Yankees will win the World Series]. Ex: Pat EXPECTS ["Phenomenon" a big win]. Ex: Pat EXPECTS ["Phenomenon" the Yankees] ["Phenomenon" to win the World Series]. General Grammatical Observations: Many of the verbs in this frame allow Raising: Pat EXPECTS it to rain. In the example above, the word _it_ is grammatically the Object of the target verb _expect_, but it does not express an FE. Rather, it is merely construed as the External Argument of the verb _rain_, which heads the VP Complement of the target. In this situation, both the raised consituent _it_ and the VP Complement are marked with the ["Phen" Phenomenon] FE, but are marked as separate constituents. That is because the Object can be passivized and therefore not appear adjacent to the VP Complement: It is EXPECTED to rain.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action Ex: We AWAITED the lunar eclipse ["Depictive" sitting atop a hill].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: Words in this frame may occur with a PP headed by _from_ which expresses the Evidence on which knowledge or belief is based: I have LEARNED ["Evidence" from experience] that poison oak can be painful.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Cognizer foresees the Phenomenon.
Ex: ["pla" Even at the far side of the house] I could PREDICT what was going on the kitchen.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Cognizer makes the prediction.
Ex: She PREDICTED the outcry ["tim" several months ago].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
An entity that serves as the focus of a predicted Phenomenon.
Ex: PREDICTIONS ["Topic" about stock prices] are notoriously undependable.

lexunit.name: anticipate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: regard as probable

lexunit.name: await.v
lexunit.definition: COD: wait for

lexunit.name: expect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: regard as likely to happen, do, or be the case.

lexunit.name: foresee.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be aware of beforehand; predict.

lexunit.name: predict.v
lexunit.definition: COD: state that (a specified event) will happen in the future.

lexunit.name: wait.v
lexunit.status: Problem: this is out of fram
lexunit.definition: COD: stay where one is or delay action until a particular time or occurrence.

lexunit.name: predictable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be predicted

lexunit.name: unpredictable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not able to be predicted; changeable

lexunit.name: unforeseeable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: which cannot be foreseen

lexunit.name: foreseeable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: able to be anticipated

lexunit.name: expectation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: belief that something will happen or be the case.

lexunit.name: prediction.n

lexunit.name: premonition.n

lexunit.name: unexpected.a

frame.name: Coming_up_with
frame.definition:
Words in this frame have to do with a Cognizer creating a new intellectual entity, the Idea. These words are similar to words of physical creation such as _build_ and _make_, and in some cases may be understood as metaphorically based on such words. However, the Ideas in this frame are predominantly conceptual in nature.
Compare this frame with Achieving_first. In that frame, the fact that the idea is new to society is emphasized, whereas Coming_up_with refers to an agentive Cognizer using mental effort to figure something out, without any implication of the impact of the idea.
Ex: ["Cog" I] 've been trying to COME UP ["Idea" with a plan] .

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
Cognizer is is the person who comes up with or conceptualizes the Invention. It is normally expressed as an External Argument:
["Cognizer" Kim] DEVISED a new recipe.

fe.name: Idea
fe.definition:
Invention is the intellectual creation of the Cognizer. It is normally expressed as an NP Object, but sometimes as a PP Complement:
Ex: Kim DEVISED ["Idea" a new recipe].
Ex: Kim CAME UP ["Idea" with a new recipe].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
Some of the words in this frame frequently occur with a constituent expressing the Purpose for which the Idea is intended. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by _for_ or a _to_-marked VP Complement:
Ex: This car has been DESIGNED ["Purpose" for quicker performance]. Ex: Kim CREATED this plan ["Purp" to prevent a hostile takeover].

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Words in this frame sometimes occur with a constituent that expresses the intellectual material from which the Idea is created. This frame element is characteristic of physical creation verbs like _make_; its presence gives sentences in this frame an especially strong metaphorical quality. The Material FE is normally expressed by a PP Complement headed by _from_ or _out of_:
Ex: The composer CREATED the symphony ["Material" out of snippets of popular melodies].

fe.name: Amount_of_progress
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Cognizer succeeds in coming up with the idea.
Ex: Before he could even ["Degr" half-way] IMPROVISE a response, she moved on.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of a focal participant during the time the invention takes place. Ex: The Arvanids CONCOCTED a desperate plan to break the siege, ["Dep" unaware that the Ahurmids themselves were starving].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A state of the Cognizer that directly and palpably influences the overall action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Cognizer that contributes to the creation of the Idea.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Location_of_appearance
fe.definition: (This FE belongs in Achieving_first, not here.)

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Cognizer comes up with the Idea.
Ex: She had COOKED UP the story ["Place" in Pisa], before she even left Italy.
The following belongs in Achieving_first:
Ex: Sandboarding was INVENTED ["Place" in Florianopolis, Brasil].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Idea is created.
Ex: You had better HATCH some plans ["Time" before you get there].
The following belongs in Achieving_first:
Ex: Toilet paper was INVENTED ["Time" in 1857]
