frame.name: Judgment
frame.definition: A Cognizer makes a judgment about an Evaluee. The judgment may be positive (e.g. _respect_) or negative (e.g. _condemn_), and this information is recorded in the semantic types Positive and Negative on the Lexical Units of this frame. There may be a specific Reason for the Cognizer's judgment, or there may be a capacity or Role in which the Evaluee is judged. Ex: This frame is distinct from the Judgment_communication frame in that this frame does not involve the Cognizer communicating his or her judgment to an Addressee. Ex: JUDGMENT: She ADMIRED Einstein for his character. Ex: JUDGMENT_COMMUNICATION: She ACCUSED Einstein of collusion. Ex: Currently, however, some lexical units and annotation for both remain in this frame.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer makes the judgment. This role is typically expressed as the External Argument (or in a _by_-PP in passives). Ex: ["Cognizer" The boss] APPRECIATES you for your diligence. Ex: ["Cognizer" The boss] is very APPRECIATIVE of my work.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object: Ex: The boss APPRECIATES ["Eval" you] for your diligence.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the REASON for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a _for_-PP, e.g. Ex: I ADMIRE you ["Reason" for your intellect].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Role is used for the capacity in which theEvaluee is judged, and is expressed in _as_-PPs. Ex: I ADMIRE you ["Role" as a composer].

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the judgment made by the Cognizer. Ex: She viewed him with an APPRECIATIVE ["Expressor" gaze].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the judging occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies any expression describing the state of a participant in the event. Ex: We ADMIRE him , ["Depict" certain that he is a great leader].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner of judging.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Cognizer judges the Evaluee.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic identifies the entity to which the proposition or propositions conveyed relate. Ex: Jon was DISAPPROVING ["Topic" about Madie's managerial style].

fe.name: Extent_of_acclaim
fe.definition: The Extent_of_acclaim is a description of the number or locales of the Cognizers. Ex: ["Evaluee" The proposal] _gained_["Extent_of_acclaim" widespread] APPROBATION.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the judgement event.

frame.name: Mental_property
frame.definition: The adjectives and nouns in this frame are all based on the idea that mental properties may be attributed to a person (Protagonist) by a (usually implicit) Judge on the basis of that person's Behavior, as broadly understood. Though on a conceptual level these words always attribute mental properties to people, they may be applied to Protagonist's Behaviors as well, with the understanding that the Behavior is revealing a (usually temporary) property of the Protagonist responsible for it. For example, while we may speak of a _stupid person_, we may also speak of a _stupid thing to say/do/think_. In addition, we may mention both the Protagonist and the Behavior, as in Ex: It was STUPID of me to do that. Some of the words in this frame also have slightly different uses, in which there is a constituent expressing the Practice with respect to which the mental property holds of the Protagonist, as in: Ex: She is ASTUTE ["Practice" at math]. While Practice expressions do not co-occur with Behavior expressions, they seem sufficiently different semantically to warrant a distinct frame element (FE) name. Also, while the FE Behavior usually occurs in sentences expressing judgments that are based on specific events, Practice occurs in sentences that are about general capabilities. In addition to the frame elements which are expressed, there is an understood judge (usually the speaker) in the background who forms the opinion of the Protagonist's mental properties, judging the Protagonist or the Protagonist's Behavior to be _stupid_, _brilliant_, etc.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: This is the person (or people) to whom a mental property is attributed. The FE may be expressed as External Argument of a predicative use of the adjective, as a PP Complement, or as the head noun modified by an attributive use of the adjective: Ex: ["Protagonist" You] were SMART to save all your receipts. Ex: It was SMART ["Protagonist" of you] to save all your receipts. Ex: You are a SMART ["Protagonist" person] to save your receipts.

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior refers to any action, utterance, belief, or artifact thereof on the basis of which a mental property is attributed to the Protagonist. The meaning of the English word _behavior_ should not be taken to constrain the identity of this frame element too much---conceptually, this frame element includes things that would not normally be described using the word _behavior_. Note the following examples: Ex: That was a STUPID ["Behavior" mistake]. Ex: The manager made a few STUPID ["Behavior" remarks] and then sat down. Ex: What a STUPID ["Behavior" book]! Ex: It's STUPID ["Behavior" to think that everything will improve].

fe.name: Practice
fe.definition: Some of the words in this frame have a slightly different use in that they evaluate someone only with respect to their mental performance in some particular domain or capacity. We call this domain or capacity PRACTICE. E.g., She is ASTUTE ["Practice" at math]. Note that this does not mean she is considered to be astute in general for doing math. Rather, she is astute with respect to math, but may be dumb with respect to other things. These uses probably belong in a different frame with words such as _skilled_, but for the time being they are marked with the FE Practice. General Grammatical Observations: The adjectives in this frame may exhibit Extraposition of a _to_-marked infinitive VP, with an optional Protagonist expressed in an _of_-PP: It was BRILLIANT (of you) ["Prac" to invite the clowns to the party].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree marks the extent to which the Behavior or Practice is exhibited or attributed.
Ex: Jenkins is ["Manr" far too] ASTUTE to fall for that Ex: She was ["Degr" a bit] CARELESS at adding drops.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner refers to the method or way in which the Mental_property is attributed to the Protagonist.
Ex: It was not licence he wanted -- his goal was the ["Manr" forcible] ENLIGHTENMENT of mankind.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The domain in which the Behavior or Protagonist has a given mental property. Ex: It was ["Domain" politically] ASTUTE to decline the offer.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition:
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.
Ex: ["jud" To my mind], his dialogues with his Vietnamese counterpart were the most trenchant, ASTUTE and screamingly funny things Trudeau has ever done

frame.name: Scrutiny
frame.definition: This frame concerns a Cognizer (a person or other intelligent being) paying close attention to something, the Ground, in order to discover and note its salient characteristics. The Cognizer may be interested in a particular characteristic or entity, the Phenomenon, that belongs to the Ground or is contained in the Ground (or to ensure that such a property of entity is not present). Some words in this frame allow alternate expressions of the Groundand the Phenomenon: Ex: We SEARCHED ["Ground" the yard] ["Phen" for my contact lens].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it. The FE is normally expressed as an External Argument: Ex: ["Cognizer" Leslie] EXAMINED the glass for cracks.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon. This FE can be expressed as an NP Object or as a PP Complement. Ex: Leslie EXAMINED ["Ground" the glass] for cracks. Ex: Kim SEARCHED ["Ground" the woods] for mushrooms.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: Phenomenon identifies the property that belongs to an entity or that the entity contains. Typically, it is expressed as a _for_-PP. Ex: Leslie EXAMINED the glass ["Phenomenon" for cracks]. Ex: Kim SEARCHED the woods ["Phenomenon" for mushrooms].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE is used for the Means by which the Cognizer to scrutinize the Ground. Ex: We ANALYSED the sediment ["Mns" by putting it through the mass spec].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: Direction is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver, that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception. Ex: The detective LOOKED ["Direction" across the street] at the suspect.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
Some of the words in this frame occur with a constituent that expresses the desired outcome of the Scrutiny. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by _for_ or a _to_-marked VP Complement.
Ex: You should INSPECT your mail ["Purp" to determine the outcome of the module transfer].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The Medium is the piece of text or work in which the Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it. The FE is normally expressed as an External Argument: Ex: ["Medium" Chapter four] EXAMINED the case for free speech.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Cognizer that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.
Ex: The temperature controller MONITORED the temperature ["ins" with a calibrated silicon diode].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Cognizer is scrutinizing the Ground.

frame.name: Candidness
frame.definition:
This frame contains adjectives and nouns that describe the truth or sincerity of communication. These words, analogously to behaver-evaluating words, can apply either to Speakers or to the Messages they produce. They can occur with _about_-PPs expressing Topic.
Ex: ["Speaker" Evelyn] was CANDID ["Addressee" with me] ["Topic" about the party].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker produces the Message, the truth or sincerity of which is at issue. It is normally expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of the TARGET word, or as the Nominal Head of prenominal uses. Ex: ["Spkr" Evelyn] was CANDID about the party. Ex: Evelyn is a CANDID ["Spkr" person].

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. This FE often remains unexpressed. When expressed, it normally takes the form of a PP Complement headed by _with_. Ex: Evelyn was CANDID ["Add" with me] about the party.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: Message is the communicative content whose truth or sincerity is at issue. This FE does not normally co-occur with the other FEs in this frame. When it does occur, it is normally the External Argument of a predicative use of the TARGET word, or the modified Nominal Head in a prenominal use. Ex: Evelyn made some CANDID ["Msg" remarks]. Ex: ["Msg" Evelyn's remarks] were CANDID.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It often occurs without the Message FE in predicative uses of the TARGET word. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about". Ex: Evelyn was CANDID ["Top" about the party].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed. Ex: Evelyn made some CANDID remarks ["Medium" in French].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which a communication is candid--some are more candid than others.
Ex: Evelyn's remarks were ["Degree" very] CANDID.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE indicates the manner of candidness. Ex: "He was a fool," John pointed out with ["Mnr" ruthless] CANDOUR.

frame.name: Commitment
frame.definition: A Speaker makes a commitment to an Addressee to carry out some future action. This may be an action desirable (as with _promise_) or not desirable (as with _threaten_) to the Addressee. Some of the words in this frame allow an Addressee to be expressed. Ex: ["Speaker" You] PROMISED ["Addressee" me] ["Message" you'd come to my graduation]. Other words cannot normally occur with an Addressee. Ex: ["Speaker" Kim] UNDERTOOK ["Message" to finish the project by June].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the person who commits him/herself to do something. Speaker is usually the External Argument of predicative uses of the target or the Genitive modifier of a noun: ["Speaker" Jo] made a PROMISE to me. ["Speaker" Jo] PROMISED me she would cook dinner. ["Speaker" Jo's] PROMISE to cook dinner came to nothing.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Speaker's commitment can be made to an Addressee. With those words which allow this frame element to be expressed, Addressee usually occurs as a PP Complement headed by _to_ or the (Indirect) Object of verbs: Kim made a PROMISE ["Addressee" to me]. Kim PROMISED ["Addressee" me] that everything would be okay.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: An expression of the commitment made by the Speaker expresses the frame element Message. Message is expressed as a finite or non-finite clausal Complement or an NP Object: I SWORE ["Message" that I would never make the same mistake again]. The owner finally CONSENTED ["Message" to sell the business]. They THREATENED ["Message" revenge].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic expressions are not very frequent in this frame. They can occur with noun targets. Jo made endless PROMISES ["Topic" about working harder at school].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the MEDIUM of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the Message. Bob THREATENED the workers ["Medium" in Spanish].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the commitment is made.
Ex: "I'll help you any way I can", he promised ["Manner" softly]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Speaker makes the commitment.
Ex: The chancellor ["Time" yesterday] PROMISED to increase defence spending in real terms next year.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Speaker makes the commitment.
Ex: The july framework has reaffirmed what was PROMISED ["Place" at Doha].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by taking on the commitment.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE is used to indicate length of time from when Commitment event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

lexunit.name: consent.v

lexunit.name: covenant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a solemn agreement

lexunit.name: covenant.v

lexunit.name: oath.n

lexunit.name: pledge.n

lexunit.name: pledge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: solemnly undertake to do or give something

lexunit.name: promise.n

lexunit.name: promise.v

lexunit.name: swear.v

lexunit.name: volunteer.v

lexunit.definition: COD: a solemn promise.

lexunit.name: commit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to obligate or pledge oneself

lexunit.name: commitment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a pledge or undertaking.

lexunit.name: vow.v

frame.name: Discussion
frame.definition:
Two (or more) people (the Interlocutors, also encodable as Interlocutor_1 and Interlocutor_2) talk to one another. No person is construed as only a speaker or only an addressee. Rather, it is understood that both (or all) participants do some speaking and some listening--the process is understood to be symmetrical or reciprocal. This frame differs from the Chatting frame in that the Interlocutors have a particular question that they are attempting to decide or understand.
Ex: ["Interlocutor_1" I] would rather DISCUSS ["Topic" politics] ["Interlocutor_2" with anyone but him].
Ex: ["Interlocutors" World leaders] met to DISCUSS ["Topic" global warming] ["Time" on the coldest day of the year.]

fe.name: Interlocutor_1
fe.definition: In cases where the Interlocutors involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, this FE identifies the conversational participant with greater semantic and syntactic prominence, as compared with Interlocutor_2. That is, Interlocutor_1 is generally encoded as Subject, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Interlocutor_1. Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Interlocutor_1, not necessarily that of Interlocutor_2 or the group of Interlocutors as a whole. Ex: ["Interlocutor_1" The President] CONFERRED with his top advisor. Ex: ["Interlocutor_1" I] DISCUSSED evolution with Gould to prove he was wrong about it.

fe.name: Interlocutor_2
fe.definition: In cases where the Interlocutors involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, Interlocutor_2 refers to the semantically and grammatically less prominent group. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by _with_). Note that it is possible for a single role to correspond to multiple referents. For example, if the prepositional object in the example below were plural, we would still assign it the single role Interlocutor_2. Ex: The President DEBATED ["Interlocutor_2" with his top advisor].

fe.name: Interlocutors
fe.definition:
In some sentences both participants are expressed by the Subject, and there is no 'with'-phrase (cf example 1). In sentences like this, the Subject is assigned the FE role Interlocutors. In such sentences, the Subject always denotes more than one person, and it is understood that the reciprocal communication takes place between these two (or more) people. The Subject may denote two or more people either through conjunction, as in example 1, or through plurality, as in example 2, or by denoting a group, as in example 3. In each of these cases the FE Interlocutors is assigned. Notice that for nouns in the Discussion frame, it is possible for the Interlocutors role to be expressed by a prepositional phrase as in example 4.
Ex: (1) ["Interlocutors" The President and his advisor] DISCUSSED the Venezuelan situation briefly before the summit. Ex: (2)["Interlocutors" The lawyers] CONFERRED before the trial. Ex: (3)["Interlocutors" The committee] DEBATED the bill for only a few minutes. Ex: (4) There was a brief EXCHANGE ["Interlocutors" between the lawyers].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
Topic expresses the subject that the Interlocutors are trying to come to some agreement about. It may refer, for example, to an undesirable issue that the Interlocutors want to have the proper response to, or it may refer more directly to an unresolved question.
Ex: The President and his top advisors DISCUSSED ["Topic" the scandal]. Ex: They had a DISCUSSION ["Topic" about the scandal]. Ex: The participants DEBATED ["Topic" whether the US should soften its response].

fe.name: Language
fe.definition:
The linguistic system(s) used by the Interlocutors to discuss something.
Ex: In our house everybody debated politics ["Language" in three different languages at once].

fe.name: Amount_of_discussion
fe.definition:
Amount_of_discussion applies to phrases expressing how thoroughly a Topic has been discussed.
Ex: This issue had been ["Amount_of_discussion" exhaustively] DISCUSSED

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing Interlocutor_1 or the pair of Interlocutors.
Ex: Jack and Jill DISCUSSED the issue ["Depictive" unaware of its full import].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This frame element marks phrases that expresss the Manner in which one or both of the Interlocutors communicate.
Ex: They DEBATED ["Manner" amicably] over who should pay the restaurant bill.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This Frame Elememt marks constituents expressing the means the parties to the conversation use to talk to each other.
Ex: Email allows people to COMMUNICATE ["Means" electronically] Ex: They briefly CONFERRED with each other ["Means" via a quick series of eyebrow twitches and a quirk of the mouth].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The Duration of the conversation.
Ex: They had a ["Duration" short] CONFERENCE off by the stable.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The goal that Interlocutor_1 or the Interlocutors jointly have, i.e. the state of affairs that they wish to bring about by the conversation.
Ex: You engage in such idle DEBATE ["Purpose" just to see how long I'll let it go].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the discussion takes place.
Ex: ["Time" Last year] the participants DISCUSSED taking down the last trade barriers without consensus.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which a discussion takes place.
Ex: We just CONFERRED for a couple of hours ["Place" up in her room].

fe.name: Means_of_communication
fe.definition:
The device or system that facilitates a discussion.
Ex: If we held a DEBATE ["Means_of_communication" on the radio], noone would be listening -- you could say whatever you wanted!

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
This FE denotes an event that occurs or a state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the discussion takes place and of which it is taken to be part.
Ex: Did you catch that ["con_eve" "Your Local News Now"] DISCUSSION about rising crime in suburban areas?

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times the discussion happens in a given period of time.
Ex: I came to enjoy our ["fre" frequent] DISCUSSIONS.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The general field or area in which the discussion takes place, or which shapes the discussion or its topic.
Ex: This prompted a rather ["dom" philosophical] DEBATE about the importance of having a purpose in life.

lexunit.name: communicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: share or exchange information or ideas.

lexunit.name: communication.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of communicating

lexunit.name: confer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have discussions.

lexunit.name: debate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal discussion in a public meeting or legislative assembly

lexunit.name: debate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: discuss or argue about.

lexunit.name: dialogue.n
lexunit.definition: COD: discussion directed towards exploration of a subject or resolution of a problem.

lexunit.name: discuss.v
lexunit.definition: FN: talk or write about (a topic) in detail

lexunit.name: discussion.n
lexunit.definition: FN: consideration of a question or issue in open debate

lexunit.name: exchange.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a short conversation or argument

lexunit.name: meeting.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an assembly of people for a particular purpose, especially for formal discussion.

lexunit.name: conference.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal meeting of people with a shared interest, typically taking place over several days.

lexunit.name: parley.v
lexunit.definition: FN: hold a conference between opposing sides in a dispute, especially regarding an armistice

lexunit.name: parley.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a conference between opposing sides in a dispute, especially regarding an armistice

lexunit.name: interlocutor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who takes part in a dialogue

lexunit.name: discussant.n
lexunit.definition: FN: somebody who participates in a formal discussion

lexunit.name: negotiation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: discussion with others to try to reach an agreement or compromise

lexunit.name: negotiate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: try to reach an agreement or compromise by discussion with others

lexunit.name: talk.n
lexunit.definition: COD: formal discussions or negotiations over a period.

lexunit.name: consultation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a discussion between two parties in which advice or information is being shared.

lexunit.name: talk_(to).v
lexunit.definition: FN: discuss or confer with another about something

frame.name: Encoding
frame.definition: A person (Speaker) expresses a Message or mental content, broadly understood, in a particular Manner. The content may be emotional, as in Ex: ["Speaker" Humans] EXPRESS ["Message" feelings] ["Medium" through words] intellectual, as in Ex: FORMULATE ["Message" the idea] ["Manner" carefully] or linguistic, as in Ex: PHRASE ["Message" your question] ["Medium" as a comment].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: Speaker, the person who encodes the Message, occurs as the External Argument of all the verbs: Ex: ["Spkr" The teacher] PHRASED the question carefully.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message is almost invariably expressed in an NP Object. (The only exceptions occur with the verb EXPRESS, which is occasionally used with that-clause complements.) Ex: The Prime Minister EXPRESSED ["Msg" her sympathy for the victims]. BUT:Ex: The Prime Minister EXPRESSED ["Msg" that she was worried about the victims].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: For most of the words in this frame, some expression of Manner or Medium is obligatory. As in other frames, Manner expressions characterize the action (in this case, the speech act performed by the Speaker). However, a wide range of Manner expressions occurs in this frame, including the following types: Ex: True Manner: You should PHRASE it ["Manr" carefully]. Ex: Illocutionary Force: You should PHRASE it ["Manr" as a question]. Ex: Purpose: You should PHRASE it ["Manr" so that everyone understands].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium expresses the Medium of communication, such as the language used or the specific type of text in which the Message occurs:Ex: Kim FORMULATED her objections ["Medium" in French]. Ex: Kim FORMULATED her objections ["Medium" in a letter].

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee is the person to whom the communication is directed.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act done by the Speaker whereby they achieve the phrasing of the Message. Ex: He WORDED his response with precision ["Mns" by consulting the relevant case law].

lexunit.name: couch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express in language of a specified style.

lexunit.name: expression.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of expressing something

lexunit.name: formulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express (an idea) in a concise or systematic way.

lexunit.name: formulation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of formulating.

lexunit.name: frame.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formulate.

lexunit.name: phrase.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put into a particular form of words.

lexunit.name: put.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express in a particular way

lexunit.name: word.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express in particular words.

lexunit.name: wording.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the words used to express something; the way in which something is expressed.

lexunit.name: phrasing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the way a text is formulated

lexunit.name: misword.v
lexunit.definition: FN: express incorrectly

lexunit.name: express.v
lexunit.definition: COD: convey (a thought or feeling) in words or by gestures and conduct

lexunit.name: cast.v
lexunit.definition: COD: arrange and present in a specified form or style.

frame.name: Gesture
frame.definition:
The words in this frame have to do with non-verbal communication. Topic is not normally expressed with these words. This seems to be related to the absence of a verbal code in cases of gestural communication. Topic can be viewed as a partial characterization of a Message, but such partial characterization is either difficult or irrelevant in the absence of a verbal code.
Ex: ["Communicator" I] GESTURED ["Body_part" with my hand] ["Message" for him to come over].

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: This is the sentient entity that communicates a Message non-verbally. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: ["Communicator" The teacher] GESTURED us into the room.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: This is the person to whom a non-verbal Message is communicated. It may be expressed as an NP Object or as a PP Complement: The teacher GESTURED ["Addressee" us] into the room. The teacher GESTURED ["Addressee" to us] to enter the room.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: This is the content of non-verbal communication. It may be expressed as a _that_-clause Complement, a _to_-marked infinitive VP Complement, or a directional PP Complement: The teacher GESTURED ["Message" that it was time to leave]. The teacher GESTURED to us ["Message" to enter the room]. The teacher GESTURED us ["Message" into the room].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Communicator that results in the successful transfer of a Message. Ex: He SIGNALLED John to fold ["Mns" by touching his ear and leaning back].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: The Body_part is the specific body part of the Communicator which gestures.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the gesturing occus.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the gesturing occurs.

fe.name: Indicated_entity
fe.definition: The Indicated_entity is the entity which the Communicator is pointing out to the Addressee as meaningful.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An Instrument that the Communicator uses to gesture to the Addressee together.

lexunit.name: beckon.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make a gesture to encourage or instruct someone to approach or follow

lexunit.name: gesticulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: gesture dramatically in place of or to emphasize speech

lexunit.name: gesture.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make a gesture.

lexunit.name: motion.v
lexunit.definition: COD: direct (someone) with a gesture.

lexunit.name: nod.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lower and raise one's head slightly and briefly to convey a message

lexunit.name: signal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: instruct or indicate by means of a signal.

lexunit.name: wave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move one's hand to and fro in greeting or as a signal

lexunit.name: signal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a gesture conveying information or an instruction

frame.name: Hear
frame.definition:
The Hearer receives a Message or communication on a particular Topic. Words in this frame denote events of verbal communication, but express the Hearer rather than the Speaker as an External Argument.
Ex: ["Hearer" Teenage fans] first HEARD ["Topic" about the tragedy] ["Medium" on a popular radio show]. Ex: ["Hearer" Teenage fans] first HEARD ["Message" the tragic news] ["Medium" on a popular radio show]

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
This is the person who produces a Message. Typically, it is expressed in this frame as a PP-complement headed by _from_:
Ex: The students HEARD ["Speaker" from Pat] that class was canceled.

fe.name: Hearer
fe.definition: This FE is the person who receives a Message. It is expressed as an Exteranal Argument in this frame: Ex: ["Hearer" The students] HEARD from Pat that class was canceled.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message is the content that is communicated from one person to another. It is normally expressed as an NP Object or a finite clause Complement: Ex: The students HEARD ["Message" the news].Ex: The students HEARD from Pat ["Message" that class was canceled].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is the subject matter about which the Message is communicated. It is normally expressed as a PP-complement headed by _about_, with or without a quantificational noun: Ex: The students HEARD ["Topic" about class].Ex: The students HEARD something ["Topic" about today's class]. The quantificational noun, if present, is treated as the Message.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the Message. It is normally expressed as a PP-complement headed by _on_ or _in_: Ex: The students HEARD the news ["Medium" on the radio].Ex: The students READ the news ["Medium" in the paper].

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

lexunit.name: hear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be informed of; listen

lexunit.name: read.v
lexunit.definition: COD: understand or interpret the nature or significance of

frame.name: Communication_manner
frame.definition:
The words in this frame describe Manners of verbal communication. All of them can occur with quoted expressions.
Ex: ["Speaker" He] SLURRED ["Message" his confession].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: Speaker is the sentient entity that produces a Message or communicates about a Topic. It is expressed as the External Argument of verbs: Ex: ["Speaker" The boy] MUMBLED an apology.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker is communicating. When expressed, the Addressee occurs as a PP Complement: Ex: The taxi driver CHATTERED away ["Addressee" to me] about gardening.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: Message is the content which is communicated by the Speaker. The Message may be a direct quote, a finite complement clause or an NP Object: Ex: ["Message" "I- It was an accident,"] Jo STAMMERED. Ex: Jo STAMMERED ["Message" that it was an accident]. Ex: Jo STAMMERED ["Message" an apology].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is the subject matter of the communicated Message. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by _about_ and, in this frame, is frequently preceded by a quantificational noun which is treated as referring to the Message: Ex: The actor CHATTERED ["Topic" about the difficulties of being famous]. Ex: The person next to me MUTTERED something ["Topic" about pride coming before a fall].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This frame element expresses the medium of communication, such as the language used or the specific type of text in which the Message occurs. It is normally expressed as a PP-complement headed by _on_ or _in_: Ex: The Beatles SANG ["Medium" on the Ed Sullivan show]. Ex: The drunk man MUMBLED ["Medium" in French].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive is used for any phrase describing a participant in an action. Ex: Jo BABBLED ["Depictive" in a tuxedo].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

fe.name: Reversive
fe.definition: This FE indicates that the communication act denoted by the target is in response to an earlier communication act in which the roles of Speaker and Addressee were reversed. This is conceptually akin to the Communication_response frame in which the targets themselves denote the responsive nature of the act.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that the communicative event lasts.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the communication event takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the communication event takes place.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action that the Speaker performs in order to communicate in the particular way described by the target.
Ex: She could only SING along ["mea" by watching others singing].

lexunit.name: babble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish, excited, or incomprehensible way

lexunit.name: bluster.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk in a loud, aggressive, or indignant way with little effect

lexunit.name: chant.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say or shout repeatedly in a sing-song tone

lexunit.name: chatter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk rapidly or incessantly about trivial matters

lexunit.name: drawl.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak in a slow, lazy way with prolonged vowel sounds

lexunit.name: gabble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk rapidly and unintelligibly.

lexunit.name: gibber.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak rapidly and unintelligibly, typically through fear or shock.

lexunit.name: jabber.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk rapidly and excitedly but with little sense.

lexunit.name: lisp.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to speak in a manner in which 's' is pronounced like 'th' in 'thick' and 'z' is pronounced like 'th' in 'this'

lexunit.name: mouth.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say (something) in an insincere or pompous way

lexunit.name: mumble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say something indistinctly and quietly.

lexunit.name: mutter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say in a barely audible voice.

lexunit.name: natter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: chat casually.

lexunit.name: prattle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk at length in a foolish or inconsequential way.

lexunit.name: rant.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak or shout at length in a wild, impassioned way.

lexunit.name: rave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk wildly or incoherently.

lexunit.name: shout.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak or call out very loudly.

lexunit.name: simper.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to speak with a silly, self-conscious, coy smile.

lexunit.name: sing.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make musical sounds with the voice, especially words with a set tune.

lexunit.name: slur.v
lexunit.definition: FN: speak or articulate speech indistinctly.

lexunit.name: stammer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak with sudden involuntary pauses and a tendency to repeat the initial letters of words.

lexunit.name: stutter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk with continued involuntary repetition of sounds, especially initial consonants.

lexunit.name: whisper.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak very softly using one's breath rather than one's throat.

frame.name: Communication_noise
frame.definition: This frame contains words for types of noise which can be used to characterize verbal communication. It inherits from Communication (possibly more specifically Communication_manner) and the Sound_emission frame (which simply characterizes basic sounds of whatever source, including those made by animals and inanimate objects). As such, it involves a Speaker who produces noise and thus communicates a Message to an Addressee.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
Speaker is the sentient entity that delivers the Message.
Ex: ["Speaker" Kim] WHINED that it wasn't fair.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee refers to the one toward whom the Communication_noise is directed. Addressee generally occurs in _to_ or _at_ PPs.
Ex: Kim WHINED ["Addressee" to Jess] that it wasn't fair. Ex: Jess SCREAMED ["Addressee" at Kim] to be quiet.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: Message has a number of different realizations in this frame, including _that_-clauses, direct quotes, infinitival complements, _for-to_ phrases, and NP Objects. Ex: Kim WHINED ["Message" that it wasn't fair]. Ex: ["Message" "Get moving!"] Jess GROWLED. Ex: Jess GROWLED at me ["Message" to get moving]. Ex: Jess GROWLED ["Message" for me to get moving]. Ex: Jess GROWLED ["Message" an order]. Quoted Messages may either precede or follow the External Argument and verb, or may be discontinuous. Ex: ["Msg" "Get moving!"]Jess GROWLED. Ex: Jess GROWLED angrily ["Msg" "Get moving!"] Ex: "For goodness sake," Jess GROWLED, ["Msg" "get moving!"]

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
Topic occurs in PP Complements, usually headed by _about_.
Ex: Kim HOWLED ["Topic" about the unfairness of it all].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is used for a physical entity or channel that transmits the Message. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by _on_ or _in_.
Ex: Pat SCREAMED something ["Medium" in Spanish].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the state of the Speaker during the communication.
Ex: "Get outta here!" he BARKED ["Dep" unflinching].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner describes the manner or style in which the Communication_noise is delivered.
Ex: "Huh!" he GRUNTED ["Manner" disbelievingly]. Ex: `"Long , dark hair" he MURMURED ["Manner" thoughtfully].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The Communication_noise may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement.
Ex: Kim GROWLED at Tim ["Internal_cause" in frustration].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Speaker communicates.

fe.name: Voice
fe.definition: The Voice describes the ["" Speaker']s utterance or other message-encoded production. Ex: ["Voice" John's voice] BELLOWED for her to be quiet.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where an event occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE idenitifes the Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Reversive
fe.definition: This FE indicates that the communication act denoted by the target is in response to an earlier communication act in which the roles of Speaker and Addressee were reversed. This is conceptually akin to the Communication_response frame in which the targets themselves denote the responsive nature of the act.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time where the Communication noise event occurs.

lexunit.name: babble.n
lexunit.definition: COD: foolish, excited, or confused talk.

lexunit.name: bark.v
lexunit.definition: COD: utter (a command or question) abruptly or aggressively

lexunit.name: bawl.v
lexunit.definition: COD: shout out noisily or angrily

lexunit.name: bellow.v
lexunit.definition: COD: emit a loud, deep roar, typically in pain or anger.

lexunit.name: bleat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak or complain in a weak or foolish way.

lexunit.name: bray.v
lexunit.definition: FN: issue a loud, harsh cry.

lexunit.name: burble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak unintelligibly and at unnecessary length.

lexunit.name: cackle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk inconsequentially and at length.

lexunit.name: chirp.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say something in a lively and cheerful way.

lexunit.name: chirrup.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make repeated short high-pitched sounds.

lexunit.name: chuckle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: laugh quietly or inwardly.

lexunit.name: cluck.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express fussy concern about.

lexunit.name: coo.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a person) speak in a soft gentle voice.

lexunit.name: croak.v
lexunit.definition: COD: utter a croak.

lexunit.name: croon.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hum, sing, or speak in a soft, low voice.

frame.name: Questioning
frame.definition: The words in this frame have to do with a Speaker asking an Addressee a question which calls for a reply (as opposed to making a request which calls for an action on the part of the Addressee).

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The person asking a question generally occurs as the External Argument of verb and noun targets: Ex: ["Speaker" Pat] QUIZZED me about where I had been. Ex: ["Speaker" Pat's] QUESTION surprised me.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee is most frequently the NP Object of a target verb. However, with the verb _inquire_, Addressee can only occur as an _of_-PP and with a noun target, Addressee occurs in a PP Complement or as a possessive : Ex: Pat QUESTIONED ["Addressee" me] about where I had been. Ex: "Do you often come here?" Kim INQUIRED ["Addressee" of the person sitting next to her]. Ex: My QUESTION ["Addressee" to you] is straightforward. Ex: ["Addressee" Kim's] INTERROGATION by the police was long.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message, or content of the question, usually takes the form of a direct quote or an embedded question with a verb target: Ex: ["Message" "What are you doing?"] Kim INQUIRED. Ex: Kim INQUIRED ["Message" what I was doing]. With noun targets, Message is not common (as Topic occurs more frequently). However, Message does occur in a PP Complement with the noun _question_: Ex: The answer to your QUESTION ["Message" of how the company makes money] is simply that it doesn't.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic occurs very frequently in this frame with both noun and verb targets. It generally occurs as a PP Complement: Ex: Pat INQUIRED ["Topic" about train times]. Ex: Pat's INQUIRY ["Topic" about train times] fell on deaf ears.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the question: Ex: Kim QUESTIONED me ["Medium" over the phone].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal Cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal Cause is expressed in a PP Complement: Ex: Kim ASKED me several questiosn ["Internal_cause" in frustration].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the questioning occurs.

frame.name: Request
frame.definition:
In this frame a Speaker asks an Addressee for something, or to carry out some action.
Ex: ["Speaker" The customer] DEMANDED ["Msg" a refund]. Ex: ["Speaker" I] BEGGED ["Addressee" my parents] ["Message" to let me stay up late.]

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The Speaker, as in other communication frames, is generally an External Argument.
Ex: ["Speaker" The judge] ORDERED the plaintiff to return the money.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
In this frame the Addressee can either occur as an NP Object (usually with a following complement clause) or as a PP Complement of verbs or nouns.
Ex: The child IMPLORED ["Addressee" her parents] to let her stay up late. Ex: I PLEADED ["Addressee" with the bus driver] to let me on without paying. Ex: I made an APPEAL ["Addressee" to the passers-by] to help me.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message is the content of the request that can be expressed as a quote, in a finite or non-finite clausal Complement, an NP Object or PP Complement. Ex: ["Message" "I'd like an extension,"] BEGGED Pat. Ex: The directors REQUESTED ["Message" that Pat resign]. Ex: Pat BEGGED them ["Message" to reconsider]. Ex: The students REQUESTED ["Message" an extension of the deadline]. Ex: The offender BEGGED ["Message" for clemency].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is rarely expressed in this frame but can occur as a PP Complement headed by _about_.
Ex: Max offered a SUGGESTION ["Topic" about completing the work].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The ["Medium" ] is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the Message. The Medium is frequently expressed as a PP Complement headed by _on_ or _in_. Ex: The parents of the missing child made an APPEAL ["Medium" on television]. Ex: The parents of the missing child made an APPEAL ["Medium" in the papers].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner indicates the manner in which the Message is delivered.
Ex: Don't stop, " he COMMANDED ["Manr" huskily]. Ex: "Maybe that was the basic problem," she TOLD him ["Manr" wearily].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An act performed by the Speaker that results in a request being made and received.
Ex: He ASKED for food ["Mns" by holding his hand out with a doleful expression].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The interval during which the Speaker makes the request.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

frame.name: Communication_response
frame.definition: This frame deals with communicating a reply or response to some prior communication or action.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the sentient entity that communicates the reply or response. It is expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of a TARGET verb or as the Genitive modifier of a TARGET noun: Ex: ["Spkr" Sue] RESPONDED to the objection convincingly. Ex: ["Spkr" Sue] gave a convincing RESPONSE. Ex: ["Spkr" Sue's] RESPONSE was convincing.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: This is the person to whom the response is communicated. When expressed, this FE occurs as the direct object of a TARGET verb, or in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to": Ex: Sue ANSWERED ["Add" Bob] immediately. Ex: Sue RESPONDED ["Add" to Bob] immediately.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a direct quote or a clause.Ex: ["Msg" "I can't help you,"] Sue ANSWERED.Ex: Sue REPLIED ["Msg" that she couldn't help].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic occurs quite rarely in this frame and usually only as a PP Complement of a noun TARGET:Ex: My boss still hasn't given me an ANSWER ["Top" about a promotion].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: As with Medium in other Communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed, usually as a PP Complement headed by "on" or "in":Ex: Sue RESPONDED to my question ["Medium" on the telephone].Ex: Sue REPLIED ["Medium" in writing].

fe.name: Trigger
fe.definition: The Trigger is the prior communication or action to which a response is given. It can occur as an NP Object or a PP Complement.Ex: Sue ANSWERED ["Trig" the question].Ex: Sue RESPONDED ["Trig" to the questionnaire].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Speaker. Ex: Her husband RESPONDED to the police officer's query, ["Depict" smoldering].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Meansby the Speaker achieves the communication of the response Message.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement: Ex: Kim RESPONDED ["ICause" out of renewed hope].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Speaker makes a verbal response.
Ex: This was how Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Jayalalithaa RESPONDED ["pla" in the Assembly] on November 5, 2003.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.
Ex: A reminder letter was sent to all nonrespondents who had not REPLIED ["tim" after 28 days].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.
Ex: We REPLIED ["pur" so as to shut you up and possibly, just possibly prevent this from happening again].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The Duration of the communication response.
Ex: He RESPONDED ["Duration" for five minutes] before letting anyone else get a word in.

frame.name: Statement
frame.definition: This frame contains verbs and nouns that communicate the act of a Speaker to address a Message to some Addressee using language. A number of the words can be used performatively, such as _declare_ and _insist_. Ex: I now DECLARE you members of this Society.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the sentient entity that produces the Message (whether spoken or written). It is normally expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of the TARGET word, or as the Genitive modifier of the noun. Ex: ["Spkr" Evelyn] SPOKE feelingly about what happened. Ex: ["Spkr" Evelyn] made a persuasive STATEMENT. Ex: ["Spkr" Evelyn's] STATEMENT was quite persuasive.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to", or as a direct object. Ex: Evelyn REPORTED ["Add" to me] about what happened. Ex: Evelyn SPOKE ["Add" to me] about what happened.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase. Ex: Evelyn SAID ["Msg" that she was not ready to leave]. Ex: Evelyn REPORTED ["Msg" the whole incident].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about", but in some cases it can appear as a direct object. Ex: Evelyn SPOKE candidly ["Top" about her past]. Ex: The teacher MENTIONED ["Top" the recent campus incidents].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Speaker makes a statement. Ex: Bilio COMMENTED on the paper ["Mns" by scrawling innumerable post-its in a range of colors and sticking them all over it].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their speaking. Ex: He COMPLAINED ["ICause" in bitterness] of the treatment the Malloreans had given him.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement. Ex: Kim PREACHED to me ["Medium" over the phone].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Speaker during the statement. Ex: Let's see if you SAY that ["Dep" sober]!

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the statement is made.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place. Ex: In some REMARKS ["Place" at the National Press Club], Mr. Keating said he would make a better prime minister tha nMr. Hawke.

fe.name: Occasion
fe.definition: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given. Ex: The ["Occasion" New Year] ADDRESS was well received.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition:
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
Ex: A further biography Shadowland by William Arnold, published in 1978, ASSERTED ["par" for the first time] that Farmer had been the subject of a transorbital lobotomy

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modified the target to indicate the legal- or "by rule" domain within which it is true or operational.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition:
The Group of Speakers or Mediums within which the statement is made.
Ex: Much would be achieved if these were more ["Group" widely] ACKNOWLEDGED.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes the Statement event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

frame.name: Volubility
frame.definition: These words describe the size of message that a Speaker is judged by a (usually unexpressed) Judge to give, either in a specific occasion or Topic or in general. As in other communication frames, Medium may also be expressed.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: This is the person who is characterized as talkative, reticent etc. It is usually the External Argument: Ex: ["Spkr" Pat] has been SILENT on this issue.

fe.name: Company
fe.definition: The Company in which the Speaker exhibits a certain communicative behavior. In this frame, Company occurs in PP Complements headed by _with_: Ex: Kim was RETICENT ["Company" with me] about her family.

fe.name: Text
fe.definition:
Text is rarely expressed because the quantity of information given is the focus of the frame, rather than the information content. Texts can occur as NP objects, but cannot be either direct quotes or complement clauses.
Ex: Kim gave a hesitant, RETICENT ["Text" account].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: This FE is the Topic on which much or little information is communicated. Topic is far more frequent than Message in this frame. Ex: Kim is very TALKATIVE ["Top" about her family and childhood].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the physical entity or channel used to communicate, as in other Communication frames. It is usually a PP Complement headed by _in_ or _on_.
Ex: Kim is TALKATIVE ["Medium" on the phone].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the Speaker withholds or does not withhold information and conversation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner in which the speaker is reticent or voluble.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

frame.name: Emotion_active
frame.definition: This frame has similarities to Experiencer_subject, but here the verbs are more 'active' in meaning. (For example, they often occur in negative imperatives, e.g. "Don't worry!''). They also differ from Experiencer_subject verbs in that they occur with Topic expressions and can be used in the present progressive: Ex: Pat is still WORRYING ["Topic" about the exam]. _*Pat is fearing the exam._ This frame can be thought of as a blend of a basic emotion frame with Cogitation.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The FE Experiencer indicates the one who is actively expressing emotion over the Topic. It usually occurs as the subject of the verb.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Kim] WORRIED about the phone bill. Ex: He WORRIES a great deal about the house.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Experiencer's emotion generally is about something. This is indicated with a Topic which usually occurs in a PP-Complement.
Ex: Kim FRETTED ["Top" over the exam]. Ex: He WORRIES a great deal ["Top" about the house].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The FE Degree indicates the degree to which the Experiencer expresses the emotion.
Ex: He WORRIES ["Degr" a great deal] about the house.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The FE Manner indicates the manner in which the active emotion is expressed.
Ex: I FRETTED ["Manr" endlessly] about the work that was needed to co-ordinate it all.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The FE Result indicates what happens due to the Experiencer actively expressing emotion.
Ex: She was WORRYING herself ["Result" sick] about Biggles.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Experiencer which brings about the active emotion.
Ex: Although she tried to distract me over that week, I still worried about them ["mea" by noticing all the little things that they left behind] .

lexunit.name: fret.v

lexunit.name: lose_sleep.v

lexunit.name: obsess.v

lexunit.name: obsession.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being obsessed.

frame.name: Emotion_directed
frame.definition:
The adjectives and nouns in this frame describe an Experiencer who is feeling or experiencing a particular emotional response to a Stimulus or about a Topic. There can also be a Circumstances under which the response occurs or a Reason that the Stimulus evokes the particular response in the Experiencer.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Mr. Whiskers] is UPSET ["Stimulus" that there are no more cat treats]. Ex: The FURIOUS ["Experiencer" parent] stormed into the office. Ex: ["Experiencer" Franz] gets INFURIATED ["Circumstances" at the thought of his ex-wife remarried]. Ex: She flashed a JUBILANT ["Expressor" smile].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
Ex: Nan Ho turned, ["Exp" his] extreme AGITATION unnoticed by the Prince.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.
Ex: I was ANGRY ["Topic" about the war]. Ex: So tell the world, and its BOREDOM ["Top" about your troubles] will heal you.

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition:
The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.
Ex: Liz's ANGER ["Stim" towards Raquel] dates back to a charity dinner this year. Ex: The feeling the bereaved find most difficult to acknowledge is their ANGER ["Stim" against the dead person] for abandoning them to face the world alone. Ex: Jack Smith openly discussed his innermost ANGUISH ["Stim" at being one of only three England players not to kick a ball during finals]. Ex: David filled her dreams; the ecstasy of their lovemaking, and the pain and BEWILDERMENT ["Stim" of his abrupt departure].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree is the degree to which the Experiencer feels the emotion.
Ex: Nan Ho turned, his ["Degr" extreme] AGITATION unnoticed by the Prince .

fe.name: Empathy_target
fe.definition:
The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.
Ex: I am HAPPY ["Empathy_target" for Sara].

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
Ex: "Can I help you?" she asked, trying not to let him see the AMUSEMENT ["Exr" in her blue eyes].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.
Ex: The feeling the bereaved find most difficult to acknowledge is their ANGER against the dead person ["Reas" for abandoning them to face the world alone].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response. In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.
Ex: One career wife spoke about her EXASPERATION ["Circumstances" when her husband listened to her with half an ear as he watched television]. Ex: Bob is INFURIATED ["Circumstances" whenever I play loud music].

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Tracy] was in an IRRITATED ["State" mood].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in.
Ex: The end of the film was filled with JUBILANT ["Event" scenes]. [Here we know that the scenes are filled with jubilant ["Experiencer" Experiencers].]

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

frame.name: Experiencer_obj
frame.definition:
Some phenomenon (the Stimulus) provokes a particular emotion in an Experiencer.
Ex: ["Stimulus" Nightmare on Elm Street] SCARED ["Experiencer" me] ["Result" silly].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer reacts emotionally or psychologically to the Stimulus. Ex: ["Stimulus" Horror films] TERRIFY ["Experiencer" Edna].

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition: The Stimulus is the event or entity which brings about the emotional or psychological state of the Experiencer. Ex: ["Stimulus" The news] ["Degree" greatly]ALARMS ["Experiencer" all the women of the village].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the degree to which the Stimulus brings about an emotion in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase which describes a state of the Experiencer.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the Stimulus affecting the Experiencer.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances is the circumstances under which the Stimulus brings about the experience. Ex: ["Stimulus" Soft music] CALMS ["Experiencer" the children] ["Circumstances" when they're wound-up].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why the Stimulus causes the emotion in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Experiencer has an emotion as caused by the Stimulus.

frame.name: Experiencer_focus
frame.definition:
The words in this frame describe an Experiencer's emotions with respect to some Content. A Reason for the emotion may also be expressed. Although the Content may refer to an actual, current state of affairs, quite often it refers to a general situation which causes the emotion.
Ex: ["Experiencer" My] ENJOYMENT ["Content" of the movie] was considerably impaired by the seven-foot guy sitting in front of me. Ex: ["Experiencer" Smithers] _takes_ ["Degree" great] PLEASURE ["Content" in collecting matchboxes]. Ex: ["Experiencer" Sergio] _derives_ ["Degree" great] PLEASURE ["Content" from smoking]. Ex: Smoking _gives_ ["Experiencer" me] ["Degree" extreme] PLEASURE. With certain verbs, the Circumstances can be expressed in a finite clausal or wh- Complement which may optionally be preceded by a Null NP Object: Ex: ["Experiencer" I] HATE it ["Circumstances" when you do that]. Note: This is not how it is currently tagged.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer experiences the emotion or other internal state.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: Content is what the Experiencer's feelings or experiences are directed towards or based upon. The Content differs from a stimulus because the Content is not construed as being direcly responsible for causing the emotion. Ex: ["Experiencer" Everyone] LOVES ["Content" compliments]. Ex: ["Experiencer" Everyone] LOVES ["Content" being complimented]. Ex: ["Experiencer" His parents] DESPAIRED ["Content" of him]. Ex: ["Experiencer" John] LIKES ["Content" that I cook him lunch]. Ex: ["Experiencer" I] am AFRAID ["Content" of spiders].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the explanation for why an Experiencer experiences the particular emotion. Ex: ["Experiencer" People] LOVE ["Content" giant pandas] ["Reason" because they look like teddy bears].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the experience occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Experiencer that reflect his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
Ex: The DELIGHT ["Expressor" on her face] was mixed with asonishment. Ex: The worshipper's JOYFUL ["Expressor" praise] rose toward the heavens.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Content.
Ex: Very few physical science students stressed the ["Parameter" intellectual] ENJOYMENT of the degree course.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the area about which the Experiencer has the particular experience. Ex: ["Experiencer" Mr. Whiskers] was UPSET ["Topic" about his cat treats].

fe.name: State
fe.definition: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer. Ex: ["Experiencer" Tracy] was in an IRRITATED ["State" mood].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The Eventis the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in. Ex: The end of the film was filled with JUBILANT ["Event" scenes]. Here we know that the scenes are filled with jubilant Experiencers.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances FE encodes the circumstances or conditions under which the Experiencer experiences the emotion. Unlike Content it does not give the specific content of the emotion, but the Content can often be inferred from the Circumstances.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Experiencer is in the specified emotional state.
Ex: ["tim" Last year], Bob was still INTERESTED in the young Republicans.

frame.name: Emotion_heat
frame.definition: This frame contains verbs that describe emotional experiences and participate in the locative alternation. For example: I was BOILING with anger. Anger was BOILING inside me. While these words might seem to be like support verbs for emotion nouns such as _anger_, the same verbs can be used in the absence of such nouns, e.g. _His remarks made me boil (inside)_. NB: Blends with communication (FE's Add, Msg, Top; part of lemmas seethe.v, fume.v) to be moved.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The Experiencer is the individual that experiences the Emotion.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Pat] SEETHED with rage.

fe.name: Emotion
fe.definition:
The Emotion experienced (usually restricted to words such as _anger, fury, rage, passion_) can occur as the External Argument or in a PP Complement. Alternatively, there may be no expression of Emotion separate from the target verb:
Ex: ["Emotion" Rage] BOILED inside him.
Ex: He BOILED ["Emotion" with rage]. Ex: Pat's behavior made me SEETHE.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause of the Emotion can be expressed in a PP Complement headed by _at_: Ex: Jo BURNED with shame ["Cause" at the criticism].

fe.name: Seat of emotion
fe.definition:
The words in this frame can occur with an overtly expressed Seat of the Emotion. This frame element occurs as a PP Complement:
Ex: Fury SEETHED ["sea" within her]. Ex: I was SEETHING ["sea" inside].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is the entity that the proposition or propositions conveyed relate to, that they are about. Had someone COMMUNICATED to the capital ["Topic" about the flagrant disregard of the religious law] ?

fe.name: Expression
fe.definition: The Expression is the words or behavior through which the Emotion is expressed. Ex: ["Emotion" Anger] BOILED ["Expression" in every word she said].

frame.name: Cure
frame.definition: This frame deals with a Healer treating and curing an Affliction (the injuries, disease, or pain) of the Patient, sometimes also mentioning the use of a particular Treatment or Medication.

fe.name: Healer
fe.definition: The Healer, anyone who treats or cures the Patient, occurs as the External Argument of verbs: Ex: ["Healer" Doctors] ALLEVIATED his suffering.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition:
This is the sufferer of the injury, disease or pain and can occur as an NP Object in this frame. However, Patient may not be expressed as a separate Frame Element but frequently occurs as the possessor of the Affliction, an example of FE Conflation: (See section on Conflation.)
Ex: Acupuncture CURED ["Patient" Pat] of his depression. Ex: Acupunture CURED ["Patient" Pat's] depression. The Patient may therefore not be tagged in a sentence although explicitly identified.

fe.name: Affliction
fe.definition: The Frame Element Affliction is generally the NP Object of a verb, frequently incorporating the Patient as a possessor, as described above: Ex: This potion HEALS ["Affliction" a broken heart]. Ex: The potion HEALED ["Affliction" Kim's broken heart].

fe.name: Treatment
fe.definition:
The FE Treatment is used for treatments and means, distinguished by separate FEs in FN-1. Ex: He emphasized treatment ["Treatment" by surgical means]. Ex: He will undergo ["Treatment" radiation] treatment.
A method used to treat the Affliction can be the External Argument of these verbs, or expressed in a PP Complement: Ex: ["Treatment" These herbs] can CURE insomnia. Ex: Insomnia can be CURED ["Treatment" with herbs].
Target nouns (e.g. therapy, treatment, etc.) will NOT be tagged with this FE.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Medication
fe.definition:
The injested, applied, injected, etc. substance designed to cure the Patient. Ex: He needs prolonged TREATMENT ["Medication" with anibiotics].
Note the tight relationship between Treatment and Medicine.

fe.name: Motivation
fe.definition: The Reason for which an intentional act is performed. Ex: We TREATED the pigeon ["Motive" for the hell of it].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. Ex: John RESUSCITATED her ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: The Body_part is the specific area of the Patient's body which is treated.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The period of time that the Patient recieves the Treatment. Ex: ["Patient" The sailor] was treated ["Affliction" for venereal disease] ["Duration" for three months].

lexunit.name: alleviate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make (pain or difficulty) less severe.

lexunit.name: cure.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a substance, treatment, or remedy that cures a disease, condition, or problem

lexunit.name: cure.v

lexunit.name: rehabilitate.v

lexunit.name: rehabilitation.n

lexunit.name: treatment.n

lexunit.name: incurable.a

lexunit.name: curative.a

lexunit.name: ease.v

lexunit.name: palliate.v

lexunit.name: palliative.n

lexunit.name: therapy.n

lexunit.name: therapeutic.a

lexunit.name: therapist.n

lexunit.name: resuscitate.v

lexunit.name: nurse.v
