frame.name: Recovery
frame.definition: These words describe the recovery or healing of a Patient from an Affliction without reference to the influence of any Treatment or Healer (see the Cure frame).

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The Patient may either be expressed as the External Argument or, as in Health.Cure, may occur as the possessor of the Affliction (an example of FE conflation): Ex: ["Patient" Pat] is CONVALESCING from surgery. Ex: Pat's wound is HEALING. In the second example, _Pat's wound_ is the Body_part, but _Pat's_ is also an instantiation of the Patient.

fe.name: Affliction
fe.definition: This FE is the injury, pain or disease experienced by the Patient. Affliction occurs either as an External Argument of verbs or as a PP Complement of nouns or verbs: Ex: ["Affliction" The wound] is HEALING well. Ex: ["Affliction" Pat's wound] is HEALING well. Ex: Pat is RECOVERING ["Affliction" from scarlet fever]. Ex: Pat's RECOVERY ["Affliction" from scarlet fever] was very rapid.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: Where Body Part is expressed as a separate constituent (rather than in phrases such as _the wound on Pat's arm_), it occurs as an External Argument: Ex: ["Body_part" Pat's arm] HEALED up quickly. Body Part is treated as a separate Frame Element although it may be viewed as metonymic for Affliction.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Patient's state diverges from their former illness.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Patient that results in their recovery. Ex: You will RECOVER more quickly ["Mns" by getting simple bed-rest].

fe.name: Company
fe.definition:
An individual or group of individuals that the Patient is generally in the presence of during convalescence.
Ex: She had confidently expected to CONVALESCE ["Company" with her brother and his wife].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the recovery takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the recovery takes place.

lexunit.name: convalesce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: gradually recover one's health after an illness or medical treatment.

lexunit.name: convalescence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of recovering from an illness or medical treatment.

lexunit.name: heal.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become sound or healthy again

lexunit.name: recover.v
lexunit.definition: COD: return to a normal state of health, mind, or strength

lexunit.name: recovery.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act or the process of recovering.

lexunit.name: recuperate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: recover from illness or exertion.

lexunit.name: recuperation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of recuperating

lexunit.name: perk up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to heal up.

frame.name: Health_response
frame.definition: A Protagonist is sensitive to a Trigger, which has the potential to cause some kind of reaction in the Protagonist.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The Protagonist occurs as the External Argument of the targets in this frame. The Protagonist represents the one exhibiting the response to the Trigger.
Ex: ["Protagonist" Pat's] ALLERGY ["Trigger" to dairy products] is severe. Ex: ["Protagonist" Young children] are very SUSCEPTIBLE ["Trigger" to infections].

fe.name: Trigger
fe.definition:
The Trigger most commonly occurs in a PP Complement headed by _to_. The Trigger is that substance or element which causes a health response in the Protagonist.
Ex: ["Protagonist" Some people] are very SENSITIVE ["Trigger" to chemicals in the environment].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner describes the way (or style) in which the Protagonist Health_response manifests itself.
Ex: Different socio-economic groups , age-groups , ethnic groups , genders have different needs for medical services because of their ["Manner" differing] SUSCEPTIBILITY and experience of morbidity and accidents.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree describes the extent to which the health response occurs.
Ex: ["Protagonist" Jake] is ["Degree" extremely] ALLERGIC ["Trigger" to codeine].
Ex: ["Protagonist" Grass and clover seeds] need fairly warm conditions for germination and are ["Degree" more] SENSITIVE ["Trigger" to drought or excessive moisture] ["Degree" than cereals.].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition:
The Body_part identifies the part of the body that is responding to the Trigger.
Ex: Diabetics may have increased ["BodP" vascular] SENSITIVITY to angiotensin II

lexunit.name: allergic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of, caused by, or relating to an allergy.

lexunit.name: allergy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a damaging immune response by the body to a substance to which it has become hypersensitive

lexunit.name: sensitive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: quick to be affected by slight changes or influences

lexunit.name: sensitivity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the quality or condition of being sensitive to slight changes or influences

lexunit.name: susceptible.a
lexunit.status: Problem: Move: see note on s
lexunit.definition: COD: likely to be influenced or harmed by a particular thing

lexunit.name: susceptibility.n
lexunit.definition: COD: likelihood of being influenced or harmed by a particular thing

frame.name: Death
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe the death of a Protagonist. A Cause of death may also be expressed obliquely.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The FE Protagonist is the being or entity that dies. With verbs in this frame, the Protagonist is the External Argument.
Ex: ["Protagonist" The goldfish] DIED.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The FE Cause expresses any object or eventuality that brings about the Protagonist's death.
Ex: The cat DIED ["Cause" of old age]. Ex: The children PERISHED ["Cause" from hunger].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Some measure of the event, generally frequency.
Ex: You know, I wouldn't want to live in a Shakespearian play; people DIE in them ["Degr" a lot].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The FE Depictivedenotes the state of the Protagonist as the death occurred.
Ex: I think he DIED ["Dep" happy].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: He DIED ["Manr" horribly]; I won't describe it.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The FE Result indicates what occurs as the result of the death of the Protagonist.
Ex: If we don't find something soon, we'll all STARVE ["Res" to death].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The FE Reason denotes the condition(s) that precede the death of the Protagonist that result in the death.
Ex: He DIED ["Reas" for his treachery]!

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The FE Place indicates where the death takes place.
Ex: Your father PASSED AWAY ["Place" in his hospital bed].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The FE Time denotes when the dying or killing occurs.
Ex: Your father PASSED AWAY ["Time" about four minutes ago]. Ex: He sadly PASSED AWAY ["Time" in 1962] because of severe cerebrovascular disease.

fe.name: Sub_event
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Sub_event in which the Protagonist dies, i.e. changes from living to dead.
Ex: The pilot DIED ["sub" in the crash]

lexunit.name: death.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or fact of dying or being killed.

lexunit.name: demise.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's death.

lexunit.name: perish.v

lexunit.name: terminator.n

lexunit.name: croak.v

lexunit.name: decease.v

lexunit.name: starve.v

lexunit.name: starvation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the fact of suffering or dying from hunger

lexunit.name: expire.v

lexunit.name: pass away.v
lexunit.definition: FN: die

lexunit.name: meet end.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: die.

lexunit.name: kick the bucket.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (s.v. kick) die.

lexunit.name: drown.v

lexunit.name: croak it.v

lexunit.name: asphyxiate.v

lexunit.name: suffocate.v

lexunit.name: suffocation.n

lexunit.name: mortality.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the death of a person or other entity

frame.name: Arriving
frame.definition: An object Theme moves in the direction of a Goal. The Goal may be expressed or it may be understood from context, but its is always implied by the verb itself.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: Theme is the object that moves. It may be an entity that moves under its own power, but it need not be. Ex: ["Theme" The officer] APPROACHED the house.Ex: I ducked as ["Theme" the baseball] APPROACHED my head.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Source expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Theme moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.Ex: The cat APPROACHED the bird ["Source" from behind].Ex: She ARRIVED ["Source" from New York] yesterday.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.Ex: The officer APPROACHED the house ["Path" through the bushes].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is any expression that tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Ex: We ARRIVED ["Goal" in Paris] before midnight. Although always conceptually present and specific, Goalmay sometimes be understood from context, rather than expressed by any separate constituent. Ex: Our visitors ARRIVED yesterday.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.Ex: The messenger ENTERED the room ["Manner" clumsily].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which a Theme arrives.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: I REACHED Canada ["Mode_of_transportation" by car]. Ex: I REACHED Mexico ["Mode_of_transportation" on foot].

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique. Ex: Pat CAME ["Cotheme" with me] down the street. Ex: The squirrel RETURNED ["Cotheme" with the nut].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when ariving occurs.

fe.name: Goal_conditions
fe.definition: The Goal_conditions are the state of the Goal when the Theme arrives. Ex: ["Theme" The senator] ARRIVED ["G_c" to a standing ovation].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Theme upon arrival. Ex: ["Theme" The Princess of Wales] ARRIVED ["Depictive" smiling].

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The time period within which the arrival repeats multiple times.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Theme arrives to the Goal.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE marks the state of affairs reported by the Arriving Event as understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the motivation or explanation for why the Theme travels to and arriv .

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Theme arrives at the Goal.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the arriving event occurs.

lexunit.name: approach.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an act of approaching

lexunit.name: approach.v

lexunit.name: arrive.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reach a destination.

lexunit.name: come.v

lexunit.name: enter.v

lexunit.name: entrance.n

lexunit.name: return.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of returning.

lexunit.name: return.v

lexunit.name: visit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of visiting

lexunit.name: visit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go to see and spend some time

lexunit.name: reach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: arrive at or attain; extend to.

lexunit.name: make.v
lexunit.definition: COD: manage to arrive at (a place) or catch (a train or other transport).

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come or go eventually or with some difficulty

lexunit.name: make it.v
lexunit.definition: FN: manage to arrive (at the planned or expected time)

lexunit.name: descend_(on).v
lexunit.definition: FN: come to a place en masse (of a temporary nuisance).

lexunit.name: crest.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reach the top of.

lexunit.name: entry.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act or the action of entering.

lexunit.name: influx.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the arrival or entry of large numbers of people or things.

frame.name: Cause_motion
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Theme to undergo directed motion. The motion may be described with respect to a Source, Path and/or Goal. In contrast with Placing, the Goal of motion is not emphasized. For many of these words (cast.v, throw.v, chuck.v, etc.), the Agent has control of the Theme only at the Source of motion, and does not experience overall motion. For others (e.g. drag.v, push.v, shove.v, etc.) the Agent has control of the Theme throughout the motion; for these words, the Theme is resistant to motion due to some friction with the surface along which they move. (They thus differ from the words of the Carrying frame in that they are supported by this surface, rather than a Carrier.)
This frame contrasts with the following frames which talk about an Agent changing a Theme's position with respect to a landmark (either Source or Goal):
In Placing, the figure (Theme) is profiled as the object, and ends up on the ground (Goal).
Ex: Joyce PLACED ["Theme" the flowers] ["Goal" onto the bed].
In Filling, the ground (Goal) is profiled as the object, and the figure (Theme) ends up on the ground (Goal).
Ex: John filled ["Goal" the box] ["Theme" with old toys].
In Removing, the figure (Theme) is profiled, and is removed from the ground (Source).
Ex: Jennifer REMOVED ["Theme" the flowers] ["Source" from the bed].
In Emptying, the ground (Source) is profiled and the figure (Theme) is removed from it.
Ex: Jason EMPTIED ["Source" the box] ["Theme" of the old toys] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The the Agent is the one whose action causes the motion of a Theme. The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.
Ex: ["Agent" Pat] THREW the china at the wall.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The FE Theme is generally an NP Object.
Ex: Pat THREW ["Theme" the china] at the wall.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The FESource is the starting point of motion.
Ex: Pat dragged the box ["Source" out of the cupboard].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.
Ex: I PUSHED the trolley ["Path" along the street].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The FE Goal is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion.
Ex: Kim THREW the cat ["Goal" into the garden].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.
Ex: Pat THREW the Javelin ["Distance" 50 meters].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.
Ex: Kim PUSHED the lawnmower ["Area" around the garden].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of a participant during the action Ex: We PUSHED the cart around, ["Depictive" gleeful].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
Subregion identifies the part of the Theme that makes contact with the resulting location. When Subregion is expressed, there usually is no Goal expressed.
Ex: The horse PITCHED the rider ["Subregion" on his head]

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes the Theme to be set in motion.
Ex: ["Cause" The storm] TOSSED the sailor from the boat

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme. It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.
Ex: When passing a basketball, you should THROW ["Ins" with bath hands].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the motion of the Theme occurs.
Ex: We SHOVED half of the cargo overboard ["Time" on the 29th].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.
Ex: The fireman DRAGGED the injured driver ["Result" clear]

fe.name: Handle
fe.definition: The Agent's manipulation of the Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Handle. The Handle is usually expressed as a PP

fe.name: Initial_State
fe.definition:
A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.
Ex: Paul PULLED Fran upright ["Initial_State" from her sitting position].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

frame.name: Cotheme
frame.definition: This frame contains words that necessarily indicate the motion of two distinct objects. The Theme is typically animate and is expressed the same way a Self-mover is expressed in the Self-motion frame--i.e. as the subject of a target verb. The Cotheme may or may not be animate and is typically expressed as a direct object or an oblique. Source, Path, Goal, and the other frame elements common to motion words also regularly occur with the words in this frame.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: This is the entity, frequently a living being, which moves in relation to the Cotheme. Normally the Theme frame element is expressed as an external argument. Ex: ["Theme" Pat] ACCOMPANIED me for five miles in a blue Toyota.Ex: ["Theme" The squirrel] CHASED the nut across the road.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
This frame element is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:
Ex: Pat ACCOMPANIED ["Cotheme" me] down the street. Ex: The squirrel CHASED ["Cotheme" after the nut ].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source marks any expression which implies a definite starting-point of the motion of the Cotheme. In prepositional phrases, the object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context. Ex: The cat CHASED the mouse ["Source" out of the house]. Ex: The cat CHASED the mouse ["Source" out].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path marks phrases that describe the Theme and Cotheme's trajectory of motion and which are neither expressions of the Source nor the Goal of motion. The notion Path also includes directional expressions. Ex: The bikers FOLLOWED the truck ["Path" west]. Ex: The bikers FOLLOWED the truck ["Path" through the desert].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Any expression which tells where the Cotheme ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal. Note that if the Cotheme is animate, the Theme need not also end up in the same place. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance. Ex: The children CHASED the ball ["Goal" into the park]. (The children end up in the park.) Ex: The children CHASED the dog ["Goal" into the park]. (The dog ends up in the park; the children may not have entered the park.)

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Phrases marked with this frame element describe a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Ex: The bikers FOLLOWED the truck ["Manner" furiously].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: Any expression which characterizes the extent of the motion of the Theme and Cotheme expresses the frame element Distance. Ex: The police TAILED the suspects ["Distance" for several miles].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: Area marks expressions which describe a general area in which the motion of Theme and Cotheme takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element. Ex: The police FOLLOWED the suspects ["Area" all around town].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This frame element marks a depictive phrase describing the Theme.
Ex: John ESCORTED his mother around ["Depictive" naked]

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
An Event in which the Cotheme is involved. Usually this is some kind of travel.
Ex: Paul Simon ACCOMPANIED the President ["Event" on his trip to Japan]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This frame element expresses the Means by which a (volitional) Theme moves in relation to the Cotheme. Ex: The policemen CHASED the suspect ["Means" by running after him].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Phrases marked with this frame element mark resultant states that the Cotheme can reach due to the motion event.Ex: The dogs HOUNDED their prey ["Result" to death].

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
This frame element denotes the means of conveyance on which the Theme is traveling. The Mode_of_Transportation can be the Theme's own body or a vehicle. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
Ex: The husband ACCOMPANIED his wife to the hospital ["Mode_of_Transportation" in the ambulance] Ex: Lily ACCOMPANIED me to the store ["Mode_of_Transportation" on foot]

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: Phrases that describe the rate of motion of the Theme are marked Speed. Ex: The detective FOLLOWED the suspect ["Speed" at a leisurely pace].

fe.name: Road
fe.definition: Phrases that denote a physical path on which the motion of Theme and Cotheme takes place are marked Road.Ex: The police FOLLOWED the suspect ["Road" on the interstate] for several miles.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which motion occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the motion occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which a Theme moves. Ex: John STALKED her every day ["Purpose" to relieve his obsessions].

fe.name: Following_distance
fe.definition: The Following_distance is the distance between the Theme and Cotheme. Ex: ["Theme" I] FOLLOWED ["Cotheme" him] ["Following_distance" at a distance of 30 yards].

fe.name: Handle
fe.definition: The Handle is active zone of the Cotheme. Ex: ["Theme" Mark ]LED ["Cotheme" Sara] ["Handle" by the hand].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location which provides a setting for a defined motion (that is one with Source, Path or Goal).

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Some event or state of affairs that leads to the Theme following the Cotheme.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction in which the Theme and Cotheme move.
Ex: The tracking dogs CHASED their target ["Direction" towards the river], where they lost it.

frame.name: Departing
frame.definition:
An object (the Theme) moves away from a Source. The Source may be expressed or it may be understood from context, but its existence is always implied by the departing word itself.
Ex: ["Theme" The plane] LEAVES ["Time" at seven].["Source" DNI].
Ex: ["Theme" His] DEPARTURE ["Source" from the dock] was delayed by hundreds of tearful farewells.
Ex: ["Theme" We all] EXITED ["Source" the room] ["Speed" slowly].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: This is the object which moves. It may be an entity which moves under its own power, but it need not be. Ex: ["Theme" The officer] LEFT the house.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: All the verbs in this frame express some change of location, away from one place and to another. Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Theme, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context. Ex: The woman LEFT. ["Source" DNI] Ex: The woman LEFT ["Source" the house].Ex: We DEPARTED ["Source" from New York] on Friday.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'. Ex: Spiderman LEFT ["Path" through the window].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE labels any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source. Ex: Our visitors LEFT ["Goal" for Los Angeles].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels. Ex: The messenger LEFT the room ["Manner" clumsily].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Theme which results in its departure. Ex: He RETREATED from his opponent ["Means" by taking a quick leap backwards].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Theme is moving. Ex: He ["Speed" quickly] EXITED the crowded terminal.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: We SET OUT ["Mode_of_transportation" by boat] for Nova Scotia. Ex: Wilbur DEPARTED ["Mode_of_transportation" on foot] for London.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a prepositional phrase generally headed by 'with' or 'along with'. Ex: He LEFT ["Cotheme" along with John].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance that the Theme has traveled. Ex: He WITHDREW ["Distance" a little] from her.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the departure takes place.Ex: We LEFT ["Time" in the morning].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency is the rate at which each Theme departs.

fe.name: Journey
fe.definition: The Journey is the trip or expedition on which the Theme embarks. Ex: ["Theme" Mr. Burns] DEPARTED ["Journey" on a hunting expedition].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase which describes the Theme at the time of departing.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the motivation or explanation for why the Theme departs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Theme departs from the Source.

fe.name: Duration_of_end_state
fe.definition: The length of time that the Theme stays away from the Source location.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes of the state of affairs denoted by the Departing event as role fillers in other frames; the state of affairs reported Departing event is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

frame.name: Emptying
frame.definition:
These are words relating to emptying containers and clearing areas of some substance or items. The area or container can appear as the direct object with all these verbs, and is designated Source because it is the source of motion of the Theme. Corresponding to its nuclear argument status, it is also affected in some crucial way, unlike Source in other frames. Some words in this frame, such as _empty_, may also occur with Path or Goal expressions, e.g.
Ex: ["Agent" The players] EMPTIED ["Source" the bucket] ["Path" over his head].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying. Ex: ["Agent" Pat] CLEARED the table of dishes.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of". Ex: Pat CLEARED the table ["Thm" of dishes].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Sourceis the region or container which is emptied of something. In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object. Ex: Pat CLEARED ["Src" the table].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. Ex: Kim EMPTIED the basin ["Path" over the edge of the balcony].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Ex: The children EMPTIED the toy box ["Goal" onto the floor].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying. Ex: ["Dep" Naked], ["Agent" Millhouse] EMPTIED ["Source" the trash can].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the Agent emptying the Source.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source. Ex: I EMPTIED the tub ["Inst" with a bucket]. Ex: I PEELED the oranges ["Inst" with a knife].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying. Ex: ["Cause" A basic washing] can DEGREASE ["Source" your workclothes].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the emptying takes place.
Ex: Don't EVISCERATE him ["pla" in the house]!

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the emptying takes place.
Ex: The prisoners were DELOUSED ["tim" in June and August].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason why the Agent empties the Source of the Theme.

frame.name: Filling
frame.definition: These are words relating to filling containers and covering areas with some thing, things or substance, the Theme. The area or container can appear as the direct object with all these verbs, and is designated Goal because it is the goal of motion of the Theme. Corresponding to its nuclear argument status, it is also affected in some crucial way, unlike goals in other frames. Ex: ["Agent" Lionel Hutz] COATED ["Goal" the wall] ["Theme" with paint].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location. Ex: ["Agent" Rev. Lovejoy] ["Manner" carefully] BRUSHED ["Goal" the rolls] ["Theme" with butter].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion. Ex: ["Agent" Josef] FILLED ["Goal" his flask] ["Source" from the whiskey bottle].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path is the trajectory of the motion. Ex: ["Agent" Jess] FILLED ["Goal" the container] ["Path" through a small hole in the lid].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goalis the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the filling occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action. Ex: ["Dep" Naked], ["Agent" Margeret] FILLED ["Goal" the tub].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the filling occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the filling occurs.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal. Ex: ["Agent" Samantha] COVERED ["Goal" the table] ["Theme" with flowers] ["Reason" because she was bored].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the filling occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the filling takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which the Agent fills the Goal. Ex: ["Agent" Samantha] COVERED ["Goal" the table] ["Theme" with flowers] ["Purpose" to please her mother].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which the filling occurs.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs. Ex: ["Agent" Mrs. Bouvier] ANOINTED ["Goal" the children] ["Theme" with oil] ["Subregion" on the forehead].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

frame.name: Motion_noise
frame.definition:
This frame pertains to noise verbs used to characterize motion. Motion_noise verbs take largely the same Source, Path and Goal expressions as other types of Motion verbs.
Ex: ["Thm" The reception doors] BANGED ["Result" open]. Ex: ["Thm" Guillemots and razor bills] WHIRRED ["Spd" rapidly] ["Goal" out to sea]. Ex: ["Thm" The limosine ]PURRED ["Path" forwards] ["Goal" into the traffic]. Ex: ["Thm" Loose guns] RUMBLED ["Area" all over the ship's deck] . Ex: ["Thm" The train] CLANGED along ["Dist" for over a thousand miles].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: TheCause describes the reason for the motion. Ex: The glasses CLINKED across the table ["Cause" during the tornado].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme is the entity that changes location. In sentences containing a Cause, the Theme is typically the NP Object. In other sentences, the Theme is normally the External Argument.
Ex: ["Theme" Pat] CRUNCHED over the fresh snow.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of Motion.
Ex: The train RUMBLED ["Source" out of the station].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.
Ex: The truck ROARED ["Path" through the tunnel].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up as a result of the Motion.
Ex: The plates CLATTERED ["Goal" to the floor].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the general Area in which motion takes place, used particularly if the motion is understood as following a complex or non-linear path.
Ex: The fly BUZZED ["Area" about the room].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
The Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of Motion. This frame element occurs very infrequently with Motion_noise verbs.
Ex: The car WHEEZED ["Dist" the two miles] into town.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs.
Ex: My Saab PURRS along easily ["Speed" at 80 miles an hour].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The Depictive indicates the state of the Theme during Motion.
Ex: The car CHUGGED across the ruts, ["Dep" unstoppable].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner is the way in which the Motion takes place.
Ex: The drone BUZZED ["Manr" curiously] across the room and vanished behind the table.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which the Theme moves in the specified way.
Ex: The autochopper WHIRRED along["Mns" by supplementing its onboard power with solar generators].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The Result is the ultimate effect of the Motion.
Ex: The door of the empty box CREAKED ["Result" open] in the wind.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Motion occurs.
Ex: Suddenly , the pole THUMPED ["Degr" really hard] into an unseen object.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place describes the location of a more specific motion (which has Source, Path or Goal).

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time for which the Theme moves under accompaniment of noise.
Ex: From there they ROARED northward ["Duration" for about 10 minutes] before turning up the beach approach onto A1.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
TheTime when the motion event takes place.
Ex: The train SCREECHED into the station ["Time" at half past seven]

frame.name: Path_shape
frame.definition:
The words in this frame describe the "fictive" motion of a stationary Road.
Some of the targets cast the scene primarily in terms of the Path_shape: Ex: ["Road" The long mountain road] MEANDERED ["Area" through the woods].
Some of the words in this frame imply a Source or Goal which is expressed by a direct object: Ex: ["Road" The path] ENTERED ["Goal" the garden] ["Place" on the west side].
Other members of the frame refer to a Direction: Ex: Then ["Road" the path] BEARS ["dir" a little to the right].
Yet others indicate a Path which requires mention of a landmark: Ex: ["Road" The otherwise arrow-straight highway] veers north and SKIRTS ["Path" the lake].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of the Road. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
Ex: The Way DESCENDS ["Source" from the City of the Peak] through a dense forest.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The trajectory that would be followed by one moving on the Road.
Ex: Valencia ANGLES ["Path" across the number streets].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Any expression which tells where the fictive mover travelling along a Road would end up.
Ex: ["Goal" Where] does Interstate 80 ENTER the city ?

fe.name: Road
fe.definition: A physical path that a virtual moving entity can be imagined to travel along. ["Road" The bike trail] ZIGZAGGED through the woods.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of the kind of motion a hypothetical mover would have (including steadiness, grace, and general comparisons) count as Manner expressions.
Ex: Drifting clouds lent a mystical touch while the narrow road TWISTED ["Manner" crazily] through ancient stone villages on the valley floor.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.
Ex: The thin line of dirt and gravel WOUND ["Distance" another ten miles] and on into the Ozarks before it petered out completely.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path.
Ex: The paths CRISSCROSSED ["Area" the desert].
Note that this FE should not be used for any locational modifier which would occur just as naturally with a non-motion predicate, like speech.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Extent to which the described configuration deviates from the norm for a Road.
Ex: The road BENT ["Degree" slightly] before resuming its long, straight march to the sea .

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An state of affairs involving the Road that allows the Road to be in the specified configuration.
Ex: As the Condell Road the route SKIRTS the northside of Limerick ["Means" by passing through Westfield's bird sanctuary on the north bank of the River Shannon].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which an imaginary traveler on the Road would move.
Ex: The road ["Speed" quickly] DROPS after passing the final turn.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive phrase describing the character of the Road.
Ex: The trail snaked down the mountainside, arduous and nearly impassable.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.
Ex: ["Place" In the mountains], Highway 60 WINDS and swerves a lot, so we lost a couple of hours from my estimate.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The configuration formed by the entire Path along the Road. Ex: The cavern DESCENDED ["PS" in a spiral].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction in which a "fictive" mover would travel along a Road.
Ex: The pass DIPS ["dir" down] about 2000 feet, and then ["dir" back up] again.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the fictive motion takes place. This may describe the time when the Road or a particular piece of the Road existed, or it may implicitly describe the time when an actual motion event occurred on the Road.
Ex: ["tim" Thousands of years ago], the Roman roads CRISS-CROSSED this landscape. Ex: ["tim" After it reached the edge of the forest], the road SLANTED upwards and grew rough.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Road brings about by being in a particular configuration.
Ex: The roadWOUND around ["Purp" in order to circumvent the house.].

frame.name: Placing
frame.definition:
Generally without overall (translational) motion, an Agent places a Theme at a location, the Goal, which is profiled. In this frame, the Theme is under the control of the Agent/Cause at the time of its arrival at the Goal. Ex: ["Agent" David] PLACED ["Theme" his briefcase] ["Goal" on the floor].
This frame differs from Filling in that it focusses on the Theme rather than the effect on the Goal entity. It differs from Removing in focussing on the Goal rather than the Source of motion for the Theme.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person (or other force) that causes the Theme to move.
Ex: ["Agent" The waiter] PLACED the food on the table.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme is the object that changes location during the Placing.
Ex: The waiter PLACED ["Theme" the food] on the table.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it changes location. Ex: Her mother SHELVED the cans ["Src" from the countertop].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a _via_-sense.
Ex: The mail carrier STUCK the letters ["Path" through the slot].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The FE Goal is the location where the Theme ends up. This FE is profiled by words in this frame. Ex: The waiter PLACED the food ["Goal" on the table].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any expression which describes a property of the placing action which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Ex: The chef PACKAGED the food ["Manner" carefully] into take-out containers.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree indicates the degree to which the placing occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme of the placing.
Ex: I PUT the dishes into the cabinet ["Depictive" unwashed].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the placing of the Theme.
Ex: The Egyptians SET it in place ["Mns" by simple levering].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of the Placing.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme is to stay in the Goal location.
Ex: If you PLACE it there ["Duration" for extended periods], your monitor may suffer permanent damage.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place indicates where the Placing occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason indicates why the Placing occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
Time is when the Placing occurs
Ex: Smithers had PLACED the table there ["Time" the night before].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
The Area is the setting into which the Theme is placed.
Ex: She emptied a wash basket full of towels and DEPOSITED them ["Area" around the house].

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.
Ex: Pat LAY the trophy on the mantle ["Cotheme" along with her portrait].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.
Ex: I PLUNGED my hands ["Distance" wrist deep] in the fragrant herbs and rubbed the dry fragments between the fingertips

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which Placing occurs.
Ex: Smithers PUT his book down ["Speed" quickly] and turned around.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: Ex: Grass , which is sown with clover , provides rich pasture for cattle in summer and the clover is ["Cause" another plant which] PUTS nitrogen into the soil .

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the placing action.
Ex: They PUT the vase in a box ["Purpose" to protect it during transportation].

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

frame.name: Removing
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Theme to move away from a location, the Source. The Sourceis profiled by the words in this frame, just as the Goal is profiled in the Placing frame.
Ex: I saw that ["Agent" several men in dark suits] had REMOVED ["Theme" all of the evidence] ["Source" from the scene]. Ex: ["Means" With your index finger] PRISE ["Theme" the meat] ["Source" out of the shell] Ex: ["Cause" The torrential winds] DISLODGED ["Theme" most of the roof tiles].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person (or other force) that causes the Theme to move.
Ex: ["Agent" The waiter] REMOVED the dishes from the table.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
Theme is the object that changes location.
Ex: The waiter REMOVED ["Theme" the dishes] from the table.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it changes location.
Ex: The waiter REMOVED the dishes ["Source" from the table].
A few of the words in this frame participate in an alternation between a Theme object and a Source object.
Ex: The waiter CLEARED ["Thm" the dishes] ["Src" from the table]. Ex: The waiter CLEARED ["Src" the table] ["Thm" of dishes]. Ex: The plumber DRAINED ["Thm" the water] ["Src" from the sink]. Ex: The plumber DRAINED ["Src" the sink] ["Thm" of water]. Ex: The gardener EMPTIED ["Thm" the soil] ["Src" from the bucket]. Ex: The gardener EMPTIED ["Src" the bucket] ["Thm" of soil]. Ex: The army EVACUATED ["Thm" the people] ["Src" from the town]. Ex: The army EVACUATED ["Src" the town].
Sentences with a Source object belong in the frame Motion_Emptying. The frames Motion_Emptying and Motion_Removing differ in terms of which frame element, the Source or the Theme, is construed as being more highly affected.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a _via_-sense.
Ex: The army EVACUATED the townspeople ["Path" through the tunnel].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is the location where the Theme ends up. This Frame Element is not profiled by words in this frame, though it may occasionally be expressed, as with the word _remove_.
Ex: Grandmother REMOVED the fine china ["Goal" to a safe place].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Ex: The army EVACUATED the townspeople ["Manner" efficiently]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the removal.
Ex: You'll have to EJECT it ["Mns" by sticking an unfolded paperclip into that little hole].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The non-Agentive cause of the removing event.
Ex: ["Cause" The raging fire] quickly EMPTIED the square of all people. Ex: ["Cause" Magnetic storms on the sun] sometimes EJECT hot gas from beneath the surface.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
The Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion. This frame element occurs throughout the motion domain but is very infrequent in Motion_Noise.
Ex: John WITHDREW the gun ["Distance" a few feet].

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The Vehicle expresses the conveyance with which the Agent effects the motion of the Theme. The Vehicle holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: WeEVACUATED the population ["Vehicle" by helicopter].

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.
Ex: Pat REMOVED the jam from the fridge ["Cotheme" along with the cheese].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the removal takes place.
Ex: ["Time" That year] they drained the swamp-water out of Higgs' bottomland.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the removal takes place.
Ex: You just take the dishes and RINSE them ["pla" in the kitchen], okay?

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The tool the Agent uses to remove the Theme from its Source.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition:
An event the punctuates the larger Removing event.
Ex: ["Subevent" With a laugh], she TORE a page from his diary.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world when the Agent or Cause removes the Theme from the Source.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: To what end the Agent or Cause removes the Theme.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

frame.name: Self_motion
frame.definition: The Self_mover, a living being, moves under its own power in a directed fashion, i.e. along what could be described as a Path, with no separate vehicle.

fe.name: Self_mover
fe.definition: Self_mover is the living being which moves under its own power. Normally it is expressed as an external argument. Ex: ["Self_mover" Fred] CRAWLED the narrow passage.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source is used for any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context. Ex: The cat RAN ["Source" out of the house]. Ex: The cat RAN ["Source" out]. Ex: The cat RAN ["Source" away]. Ex: The cat RAN ["Source" off].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path is used for any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. This includes "middle of path'' expressions.
Ex: The scouts HIKED ["Path" through the desert]. Ex: The scouts HIKED ["Path" along the river].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is used for any expression which tells where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion. Ex: The children SKIPPED ["Goal" into the park]. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance. Ex: The principal WALKED ["Goal" over] and sat down. Ex: A dog RAN ["Goal" up] and licked our hands.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory or rate of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions. Ex: We SLITHERED ["Manner" smoothly] through the crowd. Ex: They had to TREK ["Manner" on foot] through the desert.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance. Ex: I barely HOBBLED ["Distance" six feet] before collapsing. Ex: We HIKED ["Distance" a short distance] into the forest and sat down.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Note that this FE should not be used for cases when the same phrase could be used with the same meaning with a non-motion target, since these should be annotated with the Place FE.
Ex: The mouse SCURRIED ["Area" about]. Ex: Stop RUNNING ["Area" around the room] and sit down!

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the motion occurs.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
An entity whose motion is correlated with that of the Self_mover, following and tracking the Self_mover, being followed and tracked, or with both parties mutually matching Paths.
Ex: We CLOMPED down to the shore ["Cotheme" with a whole troop of younglings]. Ex: I had little hope of catching up, but I CRAWLED ["Cotheme" after her] as fast as I could. Ex: The troops MARCHING ["Cotheme" in front of him] paid no attention to the beggar by the roadside.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The rate at which the location of the Self_mover changes with respect to time.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action Ex: We WANDERED around ["Depictive" naked].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Self_mover achieves movement. Ex: He WALKED back to the village ["Mns" by dragging his mangled foot behind].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotional or mental state of the Self_mover which motivates them toward motion or the particular manner of motion.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Self_mover moves. Ex: John WALKED with her every day ["Purpose" to relieve the boredom].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is the location within which a defined motion takes place. Any specified or implied Source, Path or Goal should designate a location contained with the Place. This FE can be differentiated from Area by the fact that the annotated phrase can be used in the same meaning with non-motion targets.
Ex: The hitchhikers WALKED ["Place" in the middle of the road]. Ex:

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The state of affairs that leads to the particular motion that the Self_mover adopts.

fe.name: External_cause
fe.definition:
External_cause is something in the external environment that causes the Self_mover to move.
Ex: They DANCED ["ext" at the sound of her voice].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction that the Self_mover heads in during the motion.
Ex: You should WALK ["Direction" south] about a block .

fe.name: Coordinated_event
fe.definition: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event-it does not allow states-that the Traversing is rhythmically aligned with. The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The shape of the overall Path travelled by the Self_mover.

frame.name: Operate_vehicle
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe motion involving a Vehicle and someone who controls it, the Driver. Some words normally allow the Vehicle to be expressed as a separate constituent. Ex: ["Driver" Tim] DROVE ["Vehicle" his car] ["Path" all the way across North America]. Ex: ["Driver" Tom] PADDLED ["Vehicle" my canoe] ["Path" across the Canadian border]. Other words in this domain are based on the names of vehicles, and do not normally allow the Vehicle to be expressed as a separate constituent. Ex: ["Driver" The group] BIKED all the way across the country. However, a separate Vehicle constituent can occur if it adds information not included in the verb. Ex: ["Driver" Tim] BIKED across the country ["Vehicle" on an old 10-speed].

fe.name: Driver
fe.definition: This is the being, typically human, that controls the Vehicle as it moves. Ex: ["Driver" Kim] DROVE my old car cross-country.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: This is the means of conveyance controlled by the Driver. It may move in any way or medium. With verbs, Vehicle is usually expressed as Object: Ex: I DROVE ["Vehicle" my car] to Canada.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context. Ex: Kim DROVE ["Source" out of town]. Ex: Kim DROVE ["Source" away].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. This includes directional expressions and "middle of path'' expressions, e.g.: Ex: The bikers RODE ["Path" through the desert].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Any expression which tells where the moving object(s) ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance. Ex: Kim DROVE ["Goal" into the parking lot]. Ex: Kim DROVE ["Goal" in].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions. Ex: The bikers RODE ["Manner" recklessly] through the desert. Ex: The bikers RODE ["Manner" haltingly] over the rough terrain.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance. Ex: The bikers RODE ["Dist" hundreds of miles].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element. Ex: The bikers RODE ["Area" all over the place].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Driver or Vehicle during the Transportation. Ex: I was FLYING ["Dep" blind]. Ex: Murray DROVE the car, ["Dep" still unpainted], right through the store front.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: An event that the Driver is also participating in while directing the Vehicle. Ex: How long have you FLOWN ["Event" combat missions]?

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action performed by the Driver by which the Driver achieves directed Transportation. Ex: I managed to BIKE home ["Mns" by holding the left handlebar in my teeth]!

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of the Driver's action.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: This is a second moving object, expressed as a PP headed by _with_.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the Vehicle moves.

fe.name: Route
fe.definition: The Route is the road or path that the Vehicle regularly travels on. Ex: United Airlines FLIES ["Route" the London-New York route].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the operation of the Vehicle takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place describes the location of a more specific motion (which has Source, Path or Goal).

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of the time interval during which the Driver operates the Vehicle.
Ex: Henry would BIKE through the woods["Duration" for hours] in all kinds of weather

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Driver operates the Vehicle
Ex: ["Time" Yesterday], Smithers PADDLED his boat across the lake and back

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Vehicle crosses a boundary or the extent to which the Vehicle completes a course.
Ex: Sylvie PADDLED ["Degree" completely] around the breakwater Ex: EugeneDROVE ["Degree" completely] off the highway and turned the engine off

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Driver tries to bring about by the way that they direct the Vehicle.
Ex: I BIKE to work ["pur" to save money].

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Operate_vehicle event occurs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: "How often" the Operate_vehicle event occurs.

frame.name: Perception_active
frame.definition:
This frame contains perception words whose perceivers intentionally direct their attention to some entity or phenomenon in order to have a perceptual experience. For this reason we call the perceiver role in this frame Perceiver_agentive.
Ex: ["per" She] GAZED ["Phenomenon" upon him] ["Manner" fondly].
Comparing the Perception_active frame to the Perception_experience frame, we note that for some modalities there are different lexical items in each frame. For instance, whereas Perception_active contains the verb phrase _look at_, Perception_experience contains _see_. For other sense modalities, we find the same lexical item in both frames. To illustrate, consider the verb _smell_.
This first sentence exemplifies the Perception_active use of the verb _smell_:Ex: SMELL ["Phenomenon" this] ["Purpose" to see if it's fresh].["Perceiver_agentive" CNI] This second sentence exemplifies its Perception_experience sense: Ex: I SMELL something rotten.

fe.name: Perceiver_agentive
fe.definition: The Perceiver_agentive performs some action in order to have a perceptual experience. It is expressed as an External Argument: Ex: ["Perceiver_agentive" The waiter] SMELLED the milk to see if it was fresh.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: Phenomenon indicates the entity or phenomenon to which the Perceiver_agentive directs his or her attention in order to have a perceptual experience. Typically, it is expressed as an Object with verbs. Ex: The waiter SMELLED ["Phenomenon" the milk] to see if it was fresh. Ex: The policeman WATCHED ["Phenomenon" him] ["Phenomenon" run out the door]

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition:
Body_part identifies the part of the body used as a sensory organ of the Perceiver_agentive, typically expressed in a _with_-PP. Ex: You should FEEL the water ["Body_part" with your toes] before jumping in. This frame element occurs infrequently in this frame, because most of the target words intrinsically imply what part of the body is used (e.g. smelling must be done with the nose). However, the verb _feel_ does take this frame element, because touch is not localized on the body the same way as other modalities . Body_part may be expressed in other modalities when it adds specificity to what is implied by the target word in question.
Ex: I was now able to breathe properly and started to FEEL over my body ["BodP" with both hands]. Ex: I LOOKED at the wreckage ["Body_part" with my good eye].

fe.name: Location_of_perceiver
fe.definition: This FE is the position of the Perceiver during the act of perception. Typically, it is expressed in a _from_-PP. Ex: We WATCHED the parade ["Loc_Perc" from the roof].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
Direction is used for all path-like expressions that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception, with the exception of those indicating the location of the Perceiver_agentive (which would be marked Location_of_perceiver)
Ex: The detective LOOKED ["Direction" across the street] at the suspect. Ex: The detective LISTENED ["Direction" through the wall] to their conversation.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: State is used for predicate expressions that apply to the Phenomenon, providing some information about the state it is in while the perceiver's attention is directed to it: Ex: The detective WATCHED the suspect ["Depictive" fleeing]. Ex: Pat TASTED the cookie dough ["Depictive" raw].

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
State is the location, activity, or other characteristic of the Phenomenon.
Ex: I TASTED the soup ["State" in the fridge].
Ex: I STARED at the man ["State" running out the door].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of active perception as such: _closely_, _carefully_, etc. Ex: Dan LOOKED at the inscription ["Manr" carefully].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means indicates the tool or method the Perceiver_agentive is using to actively perceive the Phenomenon. May be confused with Direction in cases with _through_-PP, but is referring more to the instrument used than the path used.
Ex: Joann PEEKED at John ["Mns" through the binoculars] Ex: You can OBSERVE distant galaxies ["Mns" with a good telescope]. Ex: He OBSERVED babies ["Mns" using ultrasound] and discovered that each showed a preference for one or the other thumb.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the activity of attempting to perceive occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
Some action that the Perceiver_agentive is trying to accomplish by directing their own attention.
Ex: She LISTENED to the music ["Purp" to find out if it was actually written by Satan].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The general location within which the act of perception takes place.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Perception takes place.
Ex: I WATCH them ["Dur" for quite a while] .

fe.name: Expected_entity
fe.definition:
An entity or state-of-affairs that the Perceiver_agentive hopes, fears, or expects to find within the Phenomenon.
Ex: WATCH ["exp" for little errors with hand position]. Ex: While Bertha was n't looking, he carefully SMELT the soup ["exp" for any trace of the poison].

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver_agentive.
Ex: Kim LOOKED at the cloud ["Ground" against the blue sky].

fe.name: Obscuring_medium
fe.definition:
The Obscuring_medium is the medium through which the Phenomenon makes itself perceivable to the Perceiver_agentive. This is similar to the Direction, but occurs in the opposite direction and implies a movement of the Phenomenon.
Ex: I HEARD the music ["Obscuring_medium" through the wall].

frame.name: Appearance
frame.definition: In this class of perception words, a Phenomenon, typically expressed as External Argument, and its perceptual characteristics are given some description. This may be a Characterization describing purely perceptual properties, an Appraisal (i.e. positive or negative judgment) or an Inference about some non-perceptual property based on the Perceiver_passive's perception.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: The Phenomenon is typically the External Argument of the verbs in this frame.Ex: ["Phenomenon" The soup] TASTED very salty.

fe.name: Characterization
fe.definition: Characterization is the subjective description (of the Perceiver_passive ) of the Phenomenon.Ex: Kim's new furniture LOOKS ["Char" sort of bluish].Ex: The violins SOUNDED ["Char" as if they were in pain].Ex: The city SMELLED ["Char" like rotting sewage].

fe.name: Appraisal
fe.definition: Appraisal is the positive or negative judgement given to the Phenomenon.Ex: Kim's hair FEELS ["Appraisal" nice].Ex: That trumpet SOUNDS ["Appraisal" dreadful].

fe.name: Inference
fe.definition: Inference expresses some property of the Phenomenon that is not a direct feature of the particular sensory modality (if any), but rather is based on perception within that modality.Ex: Pat SOUNDS ["Inference" devestated] by the bad news. Inference may superficially look like Appraisal, as in: Ex: That idea SOUNDS ["Inference" dreadful]. However, it is not the perception of the "sound" of the idea that is "dreadful", it is the idea itself that is inferred to be dreadful based on what was heard. Ex: It LOOKS ["Infer" like Johanna is going to the ball without me]. Note the dummy-it as subject in this sense of "look" and that "appears that" could replace "looks like". Here, it is _inferrable_ that Johanna will go to the ball without the speaker.

fe.name: Perceiver_passive
fe.definition: The Perceiver_passive experiences some perception without necessarily intending to, but makes a judgment about the Phenomenon. The Perceiver_passive generally occurs in a PP Complement.Ex: The milk SMELLS bad ["Perceiver_passive" to me].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: Body_part expressions are not common in this frame, but may occur with the verb "feel" (the only verb in this frame that does not lexically encode the Body_part involved in perception) or occasionally (and redundantly) with other verbs.Ex: The fabric FELT soft ["Body_part" on my skin].Ex: The music SOUNDED beautiful ["Body_part" to my ears].

fe.name: Location_of_perceiver
fe.definition: Location_of_perceiver identifies the position of the Perceiver_passive during the act of perception. Typically it is expressed in a PP-from.Ex: The house LOOKS deceptively small ["Location_of_perceiver" from the outside].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: This frame element, usually expressed in a PP, is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the Location_of_perceiver (see above), that describe how the Perceiver_passive's attention is directed during the act of perception. Ex: His voice SOUNDED muffled ["Path" through the wall].

fe.name: State
fe.definition: This FE identifies expressions that predicate something of the Phenomenon, providing some information about its State while the Perceiver_passive experiences it.Ex: Pat LOOKS great ["State" dressed in red].Ex: The meat TASTES delicious ["State" seasoned with garlic].

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver_passive.Ex: The painting LOOKS great ["Ground" against the new wallpaper].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which a Phenomenon gives the impression that a certain Characterization or Inference holds.
Ex: John LOOKS like his father ["Degree" a bit].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The physical or abstract Circumstances that determine the appearance of the Phenomenon.
Ex: The people I work with SEEM to either hate their jobs, or like them, ["cir" depending on my mood].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Phenomenon has the Appraisal, Characterization, or Phenomenon.

frame.name: Perception_body
frame.definition: This frame contains words describing physical experiences that can affect virtually any part of the body. The body part affected is almost always mentioned with these words. It is typically expressed by the noun heading the external argument, and this noun is typically accompanied by a possessive determiner that refers to the possessor of the body part: _My head hurts!_.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer is the being who has a physical experience on some part of his or her body, or internally. Often information about this frame element is incorporated as a possessive determiner into the constituent expressing the Body Part, in which case it is not tagged separately (from Body Part), as shown below: My legs HURT! Sometimes, however, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument in its own right: ["Experiencer" I] HURT all over! Here, the phrase _all over_ can be considered a kind of generalized Body Part expression, and the pronoun _I_ expresses the Experiencer independently. With nouns and adjectives in this frame, the separate expression of the Experiencer is more common: ["Experiencer" I] have a PAIN in my leg.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: This FE is the location on the body where the physical experience takes place, typically expressed as External Argument, often as PP complement: ["Body_part" My legs] are a little SORE. I'm a little SORE ["Body_part" in my legs].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason describes the cause of the perception the body is experiencing.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion is the specific area of the Body_part which experiences the sensation. Ex: ["Body_part" My leg] ACHES ["Subregion" under the bandage].
