frame.name: Make_noise
frame.definition:
A physical entity, construed as a point-Sound_source, emits a Sound. This includes animals and people making noise with their vocal tracts. Sometimes the sound itself is referred to with a nominal expression, in which case it is called the Sound. Manner expressions may also be relevant in this frame, if they describe properties of the sound as such. A path-schema can be overlaid on the simple noise-making scene, adding a Location_of_source and/or a Path. Ex:
This frame does not cover scenarios where objects create sound by coming into forceful contact with one another or rubbing against each other. Such scenarios are covered by the Impact and Friction frames. The current frame also does not cover cases where an animate Agent or a natural Force or Cause causes a single Source or several Souces (moving or rubbing against each other) to make noise. Such scenarios are covered by the Cause_to_make_noise, Cause_impact and Cause_friction frames (the latter of which is not yet existent). Cases where the major emphasis of the portrayed scene is on the motion of a Theme, with sound emission only an accompaniment, are covered by the Motion_noise frame. Likewise, cases where the Sound itself is portrayed as moving through space are not covered in this frame but rather in Sound_movement. Finally, all nouns used to evoke Sounds have been placed in the Sounds frame. We have done this because these nouns do not denote sound emission/production events but only the Sound itself (*The siren's blare occurred right on time).

fe.name: Sound_source
fe.definition:
The frame element Sound_source is assigned to a constituent referring to a physical entity which emits a sound. Such an entity must have an appropriately complex internal structure such that it can create a sound. For example, a machine or some other thing with moving parts can create sound by itself.
Ex: ["Sound_source" The wind] HOWLED.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Reason that the Sound_source produces the sound. Generally, this is some external stimulus that prompts the Sound_source to make noise.
Ex: The planks above him CREAKED ["Reason" as Simon hoisted himself inside]

fe.name: Sound
fe.definition:
The frame element Sound is incorporated in the meaning of the verbs of this frame. Otherwise, this FE is assigned to NPs which actually refer to a sound in the presence of the target. This typically occurs when the target is a verb used as a modifier in its _-ing_ form, e.g.:
Ex: The branches made a RATTLING ["Sound" sound].
In this example, the frame element Sound is actually expressed by the word _sound_. Sometimes, Sound just occurs as an NP argument of a tensed verb form. Ex: ["Sound" Heavy music] THUNDERED from leather-curtained basements

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of a sounds as such: _loudly_, _shrilly_, etc.
Ex: Jocelyn SOBBED ["Manner" loudly].

fe.name: Location_of_source
fe.definition:
The location of the Sound_source by which the Sound is emitted.
Ex: A radio BLASTED music ["Location_of_source" from the balcony].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: State of the Sound_source during the action. Ex: Cicadas SCREECH ["Depictive" unseen from within]

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The noise-making may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the mental or emotional state of an animate Sound_source. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement:
Ex: Kim HMMMED AND HAAED ["Internal_cause" in concentration]. Ex: Kim WAILED ["Internal_cause" in despair].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion is the sulocation of the Sound_source from which the sound is emitting.
Ex: Manville WHISTLED ["Sub" through his teeth]

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
Addressee identifies the intended audience of an event of making a noise as a communicative signal.
Ex: Our new puppy has taken to GROWLING ["Addressee" at other dogs]

fe.name: Noisy_event
fe.definition:
An event in which one or more Sound_sources participate and which is accompanied by Sound.
Ex: ["Noisy_event" The conversations] DRONED on

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path along which the Sound travels away from the Sound_source.
Ex: The radio BLARED ["Path" across the room]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location of the Sound_source. This FE differs from Location_of_source only in terms of point of view; the latter FE implies a point of view that is not on the Sound_source.
Ex: A bat SQUEAKED ["Place" over our heads].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
A state or location of the Sound_source which contributes to the Sound_source's making noise.
Ex: Leaves CRUNCHED ["cir" underfoot]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Noisy_event occurs.
Ex: It's going to BEEP again ["Time" in two minutes].

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition:
The number of times the noise-making event takes place.
Ex: ["Sound_source" The raven] CAWED ["ite" twice] and flew on a short distance, then sat down again in front of her and cawed again twice.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: This FE indicates that the noise-making event is embedded within a series of similar events.

frame.name: Perception_experience
frame.definition: This frame contains perception words whose Perceivers have perceptual experiences that they do not necessarily intend to. For this reason we call the Perceiver role Perceiver_passive. Comparing the Perception-experience frame to the Perception-active frame, we note that for some modalities there are different lexical items in each frame. For instance, whereas Perception-experience has _see_, Pereception_active has _look at_. For other sense modalities, we find the same lexical items in both frames. To illustrate, consider the verb _smell_ where _I smell something rotten_ exemplifies its Perception-experience use and _Smell this to see if it's fresh_ exemplifies its Perception-active sense. This frame also includes words which are not specific to any sense modality, including _detect, perceive, perception, sense_.

fe.name: Perceiver_passive
fe.definition:
This FE is the being who has a perceptual experience, not necessarily on purpose. It is typically expressed as an External Argument.
Ex: ["Perceiver_passive" The waiter] SMELLED something foul in the kitchen.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
This FE is the entity or phenomenon that the perceiver experiences with his or her senses. It is typically expressed as Object with verbs.
Ex: The waiter SMELLED ["Phenomenon" something foul] in the kitchen.
Ex: I SAW ["Phenomenon" the baker] ["Phenomenon" prepare his special peanut butter pie].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: The Body_part is the location on the body where the perceptual experience takes place. It is typically expressed in a PP. Ex: Marlow FELT something cold and hard ["Body_part" against the back of his neck]. This Frame Element occurs less frequently than others, because many target words imply that a particular part of the body is involved (e.g. smelling must be done with the nose). However, the verb _feel_ does take this Frame Element, because touch is not localized on the body the same way other modalities are. Body_part may be expressed in other modalities when it adds specificity to what is implied by the target word in question. Ex: I HEARD a ringing ["Body_part" in my right ear].

fe.name: Location_of_perceiver
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Location_of_perceiver during the perceptual experience. It is typically expressed in a _from_-PP. Ex: The witnesses SAW the robbery ["Loc_perc" from the their car].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception. Ex: The detective could easily SEE ["Direction" into the house]. Ex: The detective HEARD their conversation ["Direction" through the wall].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The State indicates predicate expressions that apply to the Phenomenon, providing some information about the state it is in while the Perceiver_passive experiences it.
Ex: The detective SAW the suspect ["Depictive" fleeing]. Ex: Pat SAW Kim ["Depictive" naked].

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
State is the location, activity, or other characteristic of the Phenomenon.
Ex: I SAW the baker ["State" baking his special peanut butter pie].
Ex: I OVERHEARD the cat ["State" in the cupboard].
Ex: I HEARD fear ["State" in his voice].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of perception as such: _clearly_, _loudly_, etc.
Ex: Pat HEARD the shot ["Manner" clearly].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree indicates the degree to which the Perception is experienced.
Ex: A nightmare creature, ["Degr" barely] PERCEIVED in the swirling dense smoke, was beating at the flames coming from its own body. Ex: Older people PERCEIVE ["Degr" less well].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action whereby the Perceiver perceives.
Ex: He SAW it ["Mns" by looking out the window].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Perceiver_passive or the Body_part perceives the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

fe.name: Contrastive_context
fe.definition:
An element of the discourse that serves to contextualize the Phenomenon, with which it is directly related (i.e. filling a frame-element role of the Phenomenon or vice-versa). It contrasts with other contextually relevant elements that potentially (but do not actually) fill the same role.
Ex: Such a difference in note-taking accuracy can also be SEEN ["Contrastive_context" for second-year pupils] . Ex: The Scioto data fall within the range OBSERVED ["Contrastive_context" for world rivers] .

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state-of-affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state-of-affairs would be expected given the state-of-affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: A situation which pertains during the event. This frame element is primarily used to highlight the event denoted by the target against a (potentially partially) causal or concessive background state-of-affairs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: An expression of how often the event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The general location within which the act of perception takes place.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: The Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver_passive. It can be distinguished from locative postnominal modifiers of the Phenomenon in negative contexts. Ex: Pat didn't SEE Kim ["Ground" behind the bar]. In this example, it is implied that Pat looked behind the bar and did not find Kim there.

fe.name: Obscuring_medium
fe.definition:
The Obscuring_medium is the medium through which the Phenomenon makes itself perceivable to the Perceiver_passive. This is similar to the Direction, but occurs in the opposite direction and implies a movement of the Phenomenon.
Ex: My mother HEARD the scream ["Obscuring_medium" through the attic window].

frame.name: Sensation
frame.definition: This frame contains nouns that refer to sensations in different modalities. The FE Source is used for the phenomenon that gives rise to the sensation in question. The FE Percept is used for the characteristic quality of the sensation. In cases of veridical perception these are not typically distinguished from one another; we use the FE Percept as the default in these cases. With some nouns in this frame it is possible to express the being who experiences the sensation, or the part of the body of such a being. We mark such expressions with the FEs Perceiver_passive and Body_part, respectively. (The _-passive_ part of this label serves to distinguish this FE from the Perceiver-Agentive FE used in other frames.)

fe.name: Perceiver_passive
fe.definition: This FE is only expressed with certain nouns in this frame, and then only with the help of a support verb, such as _have_: Ex: ["Perceiver_passive" I] _have_ a tingling SENSATION in my hands. With most nouns in this frame, a perceiver can only be expressed as the subject of a perception verb such as _detect_ or _sense_: Ex: The dog _detected_ the SCENT of explosives. In sentences like these the perceiver-denoting expression is not annotated because it is introduced by another perception word, which is treated independently in a different frame.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: This is the entity or phenomenon which gives rise to the sensation. In cases of veridical sensation, this FE is not typically distinguished from Percept. Most of the phrases that express this FE can be paraphrased as _from_-phrases, e.g. Ex: The SMELL ["Source" of the garlic] made me hungry. Ex: The SMELL ["Source" from the garlic] made me hungry. Ex: The SMELL _of garlic_ made me hungry. Ex: *The SMELL _from garlic_ made me hungry. The first sentence, in which the object of the prepostion _of_ is a definite NP, can be roughly paraphrased by the second sentence, which replaces the _of_-PP with a _from_-PP. This shows that the phrase _of the garlic_ in the first sentence expresses Source. On the other hand, the third sentence, in which the object of the preposition _of_ is a bare noun, cannot be so paraphrased. The bare-noun _of_-PPs express Percept rather than Source. Source can be expressed as the External Argument of a support verb, e.g. Ex: ["Source" This herb] _emits_ a strong ODOUR.

fe.name: Percept
fe.definition: The FE Percept is used for phrases that express the characteristic property of a sensation. Typically this characteristic property is described with reference to the entity or phenomenon that produces the sensation---that is why this FE can be difficult to distinguish from Source. It is possible for Source and Percept to be expressed separately, however: Ex: ["Source" This herb] ["Gov" gives off] a SMELL ["Percept" of garlic]. In cases in which it is impossible to distinguish between Source and Percept, Percept is used as the default FE.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: This FE is assigned to phrases expressing the body part in which a sensation is located. Since touch is the least localized of sense modalities, words relating to haptic sensations are the ones most likely to occur with this FE: Ex: I have a tingling FEELING ["Body_part" in my hands]. Words for other sense modalities can occasionally express this FE as well: Ex: There is a bitter TASTE ["Body_part" on the back of my tongue]. Ex: The ringing SOUND ["Body_part" in my left ear] distracted me during class.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: This FE is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the sensation is perceived.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes how strong the sensation is.

frame.name: Change_of_leadership
frame.definition:
This frame concerns the appointment of a New_leader or removal from office of an Old_leader. The Selector brings about the change in leadership, for example, by electing or overthrowing a leader. Some words in the frame describe the successful removal from office of a leader (e.g. _depose_, _oust_), others simply the attempt (e.g. _uprising, rebellion_).
Ex: On March 17 , ["Selector" Mamedov] APPOINTED ["New_leader" Rakhim Gasiyev] ["Role" as Defence Minister] .

fe.name: Selector
fe.definition:
The Selector (most commonly a group of people) is responsible for a change in leadership. Typically, it occurs as the External Argument of verbs.
Ex: ["Selector" The voters] ELECTED Blair. Ex: ["Selector" The president] APPOINTS the prime minister.

fe.name: Old_leader
fe.definition:
With words denoting removal (or attempted removal) from office of a leader, the Old_leader is typically the direct object of verbs, or occurs in a PP Complement with noun targets, frequently headed by the preposition _against_.
Ex: The students OVERTHREW ["Old_leader" the president]. Ex: The UPRISING ["Old_leader" against the king] was quickly ended by the military.

fe.name: New_leader
fe.definition:
With words denoting appointment to a position, the New_leader is typically the object of verbs.
Ex: The president APPOINTS ["New_leader" the prime minister].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Frequently the Old_leader or New_leader is referred to only by his/her role. However, the Role can be expressed separately from the leader, usually as either a secondary predicate or in a PP Complement.
Ex: The board of directors APPOINTED Ashton ["Role" Acting President]. Ex: The board of directors APPOINTED Ashton ["Role" as Acting President]. Ex: The voters ELECTED Mitterand ["Role" to the presidency].

fe.name: Old_order
fe.definition: The FE Old_order identifies the political order that existed before the change of leadership occurs. Ex: The rebels OVERTHREW ["Old_order" the dictatorship].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive indicates the state of one of the participants during the action.
Ex: We DETHRONED him, ["Dep" unaware of the evil we did].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE is used for the Manner of performing an action.
Ex: The king was OUSTED ["Manr" violently].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Selector accomplishes the change of leadership. Ex: The rebels OVERTHREW the government ["Mns" by gaining the support of the military].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE is used for indicating the Result of an event.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This frame element describes the situation that brought about the change of leadership.
Ex: The king was DEPOSED ["Circumstances" in a bloody coup].

fe.name: Function
fe.definition: The Function is the purpose the New_leader will fufill.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the change takes place. Ex: The ["Time" 2000] COUP against the dictator was led by former president Smith.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the change takes place. Ex: The crew MUTINIED ["Place" out in the middle of the Atlantic], the scoundrels.

fe.name: Body
fe.definition:
A group of individuals who are elected or appointed to perform some function of governance.
Ex: His district ELECTED her ["bod" to Congress] three times.

frame.name: Leadership
frame.definition:
These are words referring to control by a Leader over a particular entity (the Governed) or an Activity. The frame contains both nouns referring to a title or position (e.g. _director, king, president_), and verbs describing the action of leadership (e.g. _rule, reign_). With verbs, it is possible to mention the Role played by the Leader (often a name of a leading position, e.g., _king_)
Ex: ["lea" Sebek em hat] _was_ a LEADER ["gov" of Priests]. ca. 1780 BC Ex: ["Time" In 1789] ["Leader" Fletcher Christian] LED ["Activity" the mutiny on HMS Bounty] Ex: ["Leader" Louis XIV] RULED ["Governed" over his people] ["Role" as king] ["Duration" for the longest period of any European monarch].

fe.name: Leader
fe.definition: The Leader is the one who has the role of leading. With verbs, and with predicate nominals linking an individual to a Role, the Leader is usually the External Argument: Ex: ["Leader" King Hussein] RULED Jordan. Ex: ["Leader" Hussein] was KING of Jordan. With leadership nouns, the frame element Leader is most frequently instantiated by the target itself. Ex: The ["Leader" QUEEN] announced her upcoming visit to Belgium.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The role played by the Leader in a given situation, often an official title; incorporated in most noun LUsin this frame. When expressed separately from the target, Role usually occurs in a PP Complement headed by _as_.
Ex: Hussein REIGNED ["Role" as King of Jordan]

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Leadership by any particular individual is frequently limited in time, which is noted here as Duration. Duration usually occurs in a PP Complement. Ex: She REIGNED ["Duration" for 3 years].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive refers to that which describes one of the participants in the leadership relationship.
Ex: He LED them for a thousand years, ["Dep" strong, bold, and deathless].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner refers to the style/way in which the leadership is asserted.
Ex: Alternative and orthodox practitioners REIGN ["Manner" harmoniously] ["Manner" side by side].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: Means identifies act(s) performed by the Leader through which leadership is maintained. Ex: He RULED ["Mns" by sheer brutality and intimidation]. Ex: Napolean REIGNED ["Mns" by the grace of God and the will of the people].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which leadership is asserted.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
Time refers to the point in time that the leadership took place.
Ex: The general LED his troops into battle ["Time" on June 22, 1883].

fe.name: Governed
fe.definition:
The entity whose actions or beliefs the Leader directs in the context of a joint activity or movement. This entity can be a political body, a person, or a group of people.
Ex: Cyprus Turks turn against ["gov" their] LEADER Ex: Naoto Kan is the new LEADER ["gov" of the Democratic Party of Japan]. Ex: King Hussein RULED ["gov" Jordan].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Leader.
Ex: A ["des" nervous] GOVERNOR stepped up to the lectern to give his speech.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Leader belongs to.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The relevant Domain within which the Leader rules.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The Leader directs the Activity.
Ex: The captain's cousin LED ["Activity" the mutiny]. Ex: John Cage is one of the LEADERS ["Activity" of the minimalist music movement].

frame.name: Sociability
frame.definition:
These words describe how outgoing or sociable a Protagonist is judged to be by a (usually implicit) Judge, often in a particular context, either with certain people (the Company), or about a particular situation, topic or event (the Content).
As opposed to the Social_interaction_evaluation frame, this frame talks about _how much_ someone interacts, not _how well_.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist is the person whose sociability is being described. Ex: ["Protagonist" Pat] is SOCIABLE. Ex: Pat was a very SHY ["Protagonist" child]. Ex: ["Protagonist" Pat] is a LONER. Ex: Everyone had heard about the RECLUSE ["Protagonist" SLF] who lived on the hill.

fe.name: Company
fe.definition: The Protagonist may be sociable, shy, outgoing, etc. when with particular Company (specific people or types of people). Company usually occurs in a PP Complement with a target adjective: Ex: Kim is SHY ["Company" of strangers]. Ex: The children are FRIENDLY ["Company" to everyone they meet].

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The Protagonist may be sociable, shy, outgoing, etc. when in a particular situation, or about performing some action. Ex: Kim is OUTGOING ["Content" when traveling alone]. Ex: Kim is TIMID ["Content" about meeting new people].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition:
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.
Ex: Pongo is very SHY, ["jud" In my opinion].

frame.name: Strictness
frame.definition:
These adjectives describe the degree of strictness or tolerance of an Agent, usually with regard to another person (the Controllee) and often with regard to a particular Issue. The strictness/lenience with respect to the Issue may be manifested in (expressed by) an Agent or by some Medium (e.g., laws), or by some behavior of the Agent, i.e., the Controlling_act.
Ex: Court says ["Agent" judge] ["Degree" too] LENIENT ["Area" in rape case].["Issue" INI] Ex: ["Agent" Sonny] _was_ INDULGENT ["Controllee" of her admirers] and allowed their attention for a time before she disappeared into the small back room. Ex: ["Medium" Some laws] _are_ just ["Degree" too] STRICT. Ex: Don't _be_ STRICT ["Issue" about cross-posting].["Agent" CNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person who is strict or liberal in his/her control over another. This FE is usually the External Argument with predicate adjectives, or the head noun if the adjective is used attributively: ["Agent" The school] is very LIBERAL in approach and curriculum. I attended a very LIBERAL ["Agent" school].

fe.name: Controllee
fe.definition: The Agent's strictness may be directed towards or limited to some particular person or group over whom he/she has control. The Controllee generally occurs in a PP Complement. Grandparents are often INDULGENT ["Controllee" with their grandchildren].

fe.name: Controlling_act
fe.definition: The Agent's strictness may be manifested in particular behavior: The judge was LENIENT ["Controlling_act" in dealing with the offender].

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition: The Agent may be strict or lenient with respect to a particular matter or situation. Issue occurs in PP Complements, usually headed by _about_: The city council is STRICT ["Issue" about pollution control].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: A Medium of control, such as rules, may also be described as strict or lenient. Medium may occur with or without the Agent who ultimately has control (i.e. the one who implements or enforces the rules). The club has STRICT ["Medium" rules] about who can become a member. ["Medium" Immigration law] is very STRICT.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The Area is the arena in which the Agent is or is not strict.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The body part or expression of the Agent that indicates their strictness.
Ex: I like to think he quaked under my AUTHORITARIAN ["exp" glare].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner is the way in which the Agent embodies the strictness associated with him or her.
Ex: These could perhaps be tied to the sometimes ["man" cruelly] AUTHORITARIAN structures of the peasant household.

lexunit.name: authoritarian.a

lexunit.name: indulgent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: readily indulging someone or overlooking their faults; tolerant or lenient.

lexunit.name: lenient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: merciful or tolerant.

lexunit.name: liberal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: respectful and accepting of behaviour or opinions different from one's own.

lexunit.name: strict.a
lexunit.definition: COD: demanding that rules concerning behaviour are obeyed.

lexunit.name: tolerant.a
lexunit.definition: FN: showing a willingness to allow or endure a disagreeable behavior or person.

frame.name: Adorning
frame.definition:
This frame involves a static (primarily spatial) relationship between a Location and a Theme. All of the verbs used statically in this frame can also occur in the frame Filling, producing pairs such as the following:
Ex: Filling: Pat COVERED the table with flowers. Ex: Adorning: Flowers COVERED the table.
Please note: adorned, covered, etc are in the Abounding_with frame because of the point of view shift.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme in this frame is the object which is described as standing in some spatial relation to a particular Location. Theme typically occurs as the External Argument or, with passives, as a PP Complement headed by "with" or "by".Ex: ["Theme" Ribbons] FESTOONED the car.Ex: The table was COVERED ["Theme" by a purple velvet cloth].

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: Location is the entity or area with respect to which the Theme's spatial arrangement is described. This frame element generally occurs as an NP Object.Ex: Thick varnish COATED ["Location" the beautiful wood].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The part of the Location which contains or is covered by the Theme. Ex: Bulletholes COVERED the windshield ["Sub" on the right side].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Theme occupies the Location.
Ex: By 1950, factories dotted the adjacent countryside.

frame.name: Cause_expansion
frame.definition:
An Agent or non-human causes an Item to change its physical size. The Size_change of an Item may be explicitly indicated or characterized in terms of Initial_size and/or Result_size. In the default case, expansion is along all dimensions, but sometimes the Dimension of expansion is incorporated or made explicit.
Ex: If the design crashes too often, then try LENGTHENING ["Item" the wings] ["Size_change" by a few centimeters], ["Result_size" to perhaps 30cm total]. ["Agent" CNI] ["Dimension" INI]
Ex: As the juice churned with natural process of changing into wine, ["Cause" the gas it created] would EXPAND ["Item" the balloon], and when the balloon eventually deflated, it was ready to drink.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
With some words in this frame, an Agent who causes the change in size of the Item may be present. The Agent typically occurs as the External Argument of a verb.
Ex: ["Agt" Management] EXPANDED the company.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The Item is frequently the External Argument of verbs or the NP Object if an Agent is expressed.
Ex: ["Item" The company] EXPANDED. Ex: Management EXPANDED ["Item" the company].

fe.name: Initial_size
fe.definition:
Initial_size is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit. Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-_from_ Complement.
Ex: The glacier SHRANK ["Initial" from 1km square] to 400 square meters.

fe.name: Result_size
fe.definition:
Result_size is typically expressed in a PP Complement headed by _to_.
Ex: I GROW vegetables ["Result" until they weigh 25 pounds].

fe.name: Size_change
fe.definition:
Size_change identifies the amount by which the size of an Item changes.
Ex: A ["Sizec" 2-3cm] EXPANSION in width is required.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition:
Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.
Ex: The image was ENLARGED ["Dim" in height]. Ex: The machinist NARROWED the tube by 6 inches ["Dim" in diameter].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent brings about the expansion of the Item.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner of performing an action.

fe.name: Co_Variable
fe.definition:
The feature that the size of the Item is varied in step with.
Ex: I NARROWED the viewport ["Co_Var" with the increasing glare].

fe.name: Group
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Group in which an Item changes size.
Ex: Tails LENGTHENED 10% ["Grp" among rats more than 3 days old].

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition:
Rate identifies the rate of change of the value.
Ex: The balloon INFLATES ["Rate" about 2 cubic cm a minute].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is a non-human entity which brings about the change in size.

fe.name: Elapsed_time
fe.definition: The Elapsed_time is the amonut of time in which the change occurs. Ex: ["Item" The sun] would SHRINK ["Result_size" to a point] ["Elapsed_time" in a matter of minutes].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent causes the Item to expand.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent cause the expansion of the Item.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Agent cause the expansion of the Item.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent causes the expansion of the Item.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent causes the expansion of the Item.

frame.name: Containers
frame.definition: This frame covers entities which are prototypically conceived of and created to fulfill the function of containing--i.e. Containers that contain objects or substances, the Contents. This can be expressed as a complement , and includes potential or intended contents. A Container may also have an Owner, a current Relative_location, Material from which it is constructed, a method of Construction, and a Type. Note the connection between words in this frame and those in the Filling, Emptying, and Fullness frames. Ex: a ["Container" BAG] ["Contents" of popcorn] Ex: ["Contents" underwear] ["Container" DRAWER] Ex: ["Owner" Chuck's] ["Container" SUITCASE] Ex: ["Container" the SUITCASE] ["Rel_loc" in Chuck's office] Ex: ["Mat" straw] ["Container" BASKET] Ex: ["Cons" woven] ["Container" BASKET] Ex: ["Type" Erlenmeyer] ["Container" FLASK]

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
Container is an object which is conventionally used as a container. Target words in this frame are tagged with this frame element.
Ex: John carried a ["Container" BUCKET].

fe.name: Contents
fe.definition: Contents is the object(s)/stuff contained in the Container.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Material identifies the material of which the Container is made.
Ex: ["Mat" straw] ["Container" BASKET]

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
Type designates the type of Container. Often the Type labels part of a multi-word or compound word target.
Ex: ["Type" Erlenmeyer] ["Container" FLASK] Ex: ["Type" TABLE]["Container" SPOON]

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
Relative_location is the location of the Container.
Ex: The ["Container" WALLET] ["Rel_loc" in his pocket] was full of photos of his family.

fe.name: Construction
fe.definition:
Construction indicates the action (or causer) which creates the Container.
Ex: ["Cons" fired] ["Container" URNS].

fe.name: Owner
fe.definition:
Owner identifies the owner of the Container.
Ex: ["Owner" Chuck's] ["Container" SUITCASE]

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: Use identifies the purpose for which an artifact is constructed and the activity with which it is associated, or the Contents protypically contained in the Container. Ex: ["Use" watering] ["Container" CAN] Ex: ["Use" wine] ["Container" GLASS]

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
This FE identifies a Part of the Container.
Ex: ["Part" screw top] ["Container" BOTTLE]

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor describes some aspect of the Container.
Ex: He put everything into a ["Descriptor" really really huge] BRIEFCASE

frame.name: Duration_attribute
frame.definition: An event or state (here termed an Eventuality) or time-Period is described in terms of the Degree to which its duration diverges from a standard. As is usual for gradable attributes, the standard of comparison is normally based on the expectated duration for the type of Eventuality or Period. (In conjunction with the comparative construction, the standard may also be based upon an explicit value.)

fe.name: Eventuality
fe.definition: A situation, action or event whose duration is being described. The Eventuality occurs as the External Argument if the adjective is used predicatively, or as the modified noun if the adjective is used attributively: ["Eventuality" The lecture] was SHORT. We had a LENGTHY ["Eventuality" conversation].

fe.name: Period
fe.definition: Sometimes these adjectives describe simply a period of time, rather than an event or state. The Period almost invariably occurs as the modified noun with an attributive adjective: We waited for only a SHORT ["Period" time]. Use of the drug over a LENGTHY ["Period" period] can cause memory loss.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

lexunit.definition: FN: permanent, enduring

lexunit.name: brief.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of short duration.

lexunit.name: chronic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an illness or problem) persisting for a long time.

lexunit.definition: FN: continuing, durable

lexunit.name: interim.a
lexunit.definition: COD: provisional.

lexunit.definition: COD: enduring or able to endure over a long period of time.

lexunit.name: lengthy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of considerable or unusual duration

lexunit.definition: FN: continuing or occuring only briefly; fleeting

lexunit.name: short.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of a small length or duration.

lexunit.name: long.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of greater temporal duration than normal.

frame.name: Frequency
frame.definition:
This frame has to do with the repetition (and especially the frequency of repetition) of an event. Many of the adjectives and adverbs in this frame are based on nouns in the Calendric_unit frame.
Ex: China will have to face a ["Degree" high] FREQUENCY ["Event" of sand storms] in the years to come.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE is used for any (bounded) Event whose frequency or iteration is described. Ex: The country has been struck by FREQUENT ["Event" economic crises]. Ex: ["Event" The symptoms] were SPORADIC.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the actually observed rate of occurrence of the Event or Salient_entity differs from the expected rate.
Ex: The Crested Lark (Galerida cristata) is ["Degree" very] FREQUENT from the coastal plain to the mountains.

fe.name: Interval
fe.definition: The Intervalis a noun modified by the target word. The target word specifies the frequency of the Interval. Ex: The meetings occurred at FORTNIGHTLY ["Interval" intervals]. Ex: The parties were held on a MONTHLY ["Interval" basis].

fe.name: Time_span
fe.definition:
The Time_span is the length of time of the Interval. This FE is incorporated by most of the lexical units in this frame.
Ex: You have to renew the license EVERY ["Time_span" year] .

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition:
The number of times per unit of real or scanning time that an Event or Salient_entity is encountered.
Ex: The state government spends its fiscal year 2006 budget of $23.4 billion at a RATE ["rat" of $742 per second].

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
An entity which the implicit cognizer encounters with the specified frequency.
Ex: It costs about US$2.50 to travel 200km (124 mi), but ["sal" buses] are INFREQUENT and only one or two buses a day service most routes.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The frequency feature of the Event or Salient_entity that is under discussion. All the lexical units in this frame incorporate this frame element.
Ex: These exposures were likely to be INTERMITTENT ["att" in frequency] occurring only when workers were participating in activities at these specific areas.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Event has a particular frequency.

lexunit.definition: COD: done, produced, or occurring every day or every weekday.

lexunit.name: fortnightly.a
lexunit.definition: COD: happening or produced every two weeks.

lexunit.name: frequent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: occurring or done many times at short intervals.

lexunit.name: infrequent.a

frame.name: Relative_time
frame.definition:
These words relate to the relative ordering of two events or times. There are two major types of relations evoked by the words of this frame. Ex: Some of the words (e.g. _follow.v, antecedent.a, previous.a_) describe the (definitively) stative relationship between two events (the Landmark_occasion and the Focal_occasion). This first type will be moved to the Time_vector frame.
Ex: AFTER ["Landmark_occasion" she arrived] , ["Focal_occasion" she laid out her papers on the desk]. Ex: The FOLLOWING ["Focal_occasion" morning], she tried to figure out what it meant . ["Landmark_occasion" DNI]
Ex: Others (e.g. _belated.a, early.a_) refer to the change or deviation of an event from the Landmark_occasion (which is expected or usual at a particular time) to the Focal_occasion (which occurs at a different time). Quite often, a Focal_participant who is saliently involved in the Focal_occasion stands in for the occasion.
Ex: ["Focal_occasion" My flight] is EARLY ["Interval" by 20 minutes]. Ex: ["Focal_participant" I] 'm LATE ["Landmark_occasion" for my departure] !

fe.name: Focal_occasion
fe.definition: The Focal_occasion is the event which is being located in time with respect to some other event: The Focal_occasion is profiled, in contrast to the Landmark_occasion, which is backgrounded. Ex: ["FEv" Hours of eating and drinking] FOLLOWED the wedding ceremony. Ex: Her BELATED ["Focal_occasion" party] was still a success. Ex: During the PREVIOUS ["Focal_occasion" week], he had eaten 5 mangoes.

fe.name: Landmark_occasion
fe.definition: The Landmark_occasion is the event with respect to which the Focal_occasion is located. Ex: Hours of eating and drinking FOLLOWED ["Landmark_occasion" the wedding ceremony].

fe.name: Interval
fe.definition: Frequently, the Interval between the Reference and Focal Occasions is expressed: The article in the Times ["Interval" closely] FOLLOWED the singer's announcement that he was retiring.

fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE is used for the Reason or explanation for the Focal_occasion being early or late.

fe.name: Focal_participant
fe.definition:
The Focal_participant is the participant in the Focal_occasion which is profiled as being in a relation of relative time to the Landmark_occasion.
Ex: ["Focal_participant" We] were LATE ["Landmark_occasion" for dinner].

frame.name: Commerce_scenario
frame.definition: Commerce is a situation in which a Buyer and a Seller have agreed upon an exchange of Money and Goods (possibly after a negotiation), and then perform the exchange, optionally carrying it out with various kinds of direct payment or financing or the giving of change. Ex: The Seller indicates their willingness to give the Goods in their possession to a Buyer who would give them some amount of Money. The Seller may have already decided on the amount of money that they would require, in which case it is called the Asking price. Ex: The Buyer also indicates their willingness to give an amount of money called an Offer to a Seller who would give them the Goods. Ex: Normally the process is begun by the Seller. The means by which the Seller indicates their wish to engage in an exchange are various, ranging from putting a price tag on an item on a store shelf, to advertizing, to communicating directly and specifically with a possible Buyer. In some cases, however, the process may be initiated by the Buyer indicating to a possible Seller that they would like to make an exchange.

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer has the Money and wants the Goods. Ex: She was considered a ["Byr" PURCHASER] of the finest things

fe.name: Seller
fe.definition: The Seller has the Goods and wants the Money. Ex: ["Slr" My local grocery store] raised PRICES on meat

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. Ex: The PRICE of the sweater _was_ ["Mny" $50].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: Goods is anything including labor or time, for example, which is exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: She was considered a PURCHASER ["Gds" of the finest things]

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: The authorities cut tomato PRICES ["Rate" to a dollar per pound].

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: The PRICE of Bob's peppers is determined ["Unit" by the pound].

fe.name: Means

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the agent intends to bring about as a result of participating in the Commercial Transaction.

frame.name: Expensiveness
frame.definition:
A Payer gives up (or potentially gives up) the use of an Asset (generally money) in order to achieve an Intended_event. This event is often more specifically described as gaining possession of some Goods or receiving a Service. In the majority of cases, the Payer is described generically (INI), and the situation depicted answers the question of how much of an Asset would have to be given up to receive the Goods or bring about the Intended_event.
Ex: It 'll COST ["Payer" Sandra's parents] ["Asset" fifty grand a year] ["Intended_event" for her to attend that school]. Ex: ["Intended_event" That book] would COST ["Payer" you] ["Asset" more than twenty dollars] ["Intended_event" to bind] ["" in a local book bindery]. Ex: ["Goods" Stamps] used to COST ["Asset" only five cents]. ["Payer" INI] Ex: The COST of a trip to a resort or spa varies by region, dependent primarily on weather, not local economic conditions. Ex: Well, ["Intended_event" it] 'll COST ["Payer" you]. Ex: ["Payer" For you], ["Asset" thirty bucks] _is_ ["Degree" practically] FREE. ["Intended_event" DNI]

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is the item(s) whose price is being assessed. Goods is usually an External Argument: Ex: ["Goods" These paintings] are very PRICEY.

fe.name: Payer
fe.definition: The person whose Asset is given up in order to achieve an Intended_event. This FE is often expressed as INI. Ex: A holiday in Europe is very EXPENSIVE ["Payer" for me]. Ex: Europe is not CHEAP. ["Payer" INI]

fe.name: Asset
fe.definition: The price of or payment made for the Goods. Ex: The painting was CHEAP ["Asset" at $600]. Ex: ["Asset" $600] is EXORBITANT for that painting!

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The place where a transaction would take place, generally where Goods and services are created or sold. Ex: Shirts are CHEAP ["Origin" at K-Mart].

fe.definition: This FE identifies theDegree to which Goods are cheap or expensive.

Ex: No, they've got a special on; it's really CHEAP there ["Time" on Tuesdays]

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: The amount of an Asset relative to some measure of the Goods

frame.name: Frugality
frame.definition:
The words of this frame describe how a Resource_controller spends money or other Resources for a particular purpose . They can be applied to the Resource_controller or to their Behavior in particular instances. These words indicate a judgment of how conservatively the Resource_controller guards their Resource.
Ex: ["Resource_controller" Margeret] has always _been_ PENNY-WISE. Ex: ["Resource_controller" Bill] SQUANDERS ["Resource" his money]. Ex: ["Behavior" To spend the surplus now] would _be_ needlessly PROFLIGATE .

fe.name: Resource_controller
fe.definition: The Resource_controller is the individual whose frugality or generosity is being described. Person typically occurs as the External Argument or, in some cases when Behavior is also expressed, in an _of_-PP: Ex: ["Resource_controller" Jo] is very FRUGAL. Ex: It was FRUGAL ["Resource_controller" of Jo] not to pay for dinner.

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: Some specific Behavior may be described as frugal or extravagant, rather than attributing the characteristic directly to the Resource_controller. Ex: It's THRIFTY of Jo ["Behavior" to re-use teabags].

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition: This FE is the resource which the Resource_controller expends. Ex: Pat is WASTEFUL ["Resource" with her time].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which a Resource_controller is frugal or profligate.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

frame.name: Attempt_suasion
frame.definition:
The Speaker expresses through language his wish to get the Addressee to act. There is no implication that the Addressee forms an intention to act, let alone acts.
Ex: ["Speaker" Mr Smithers] always ENCOURAGES ["Add" the employees] ["Content" to stay late and work harder].
Ex: ["Speaker" Dennis Rodman] advises ["Content" moderation in all things]. ["Add" INI]

fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an action is performed.

fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase that describes the actor of an action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an action is performed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the lobbying occurs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (independent of the event).

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: The Group is the set of Speakers and Mediums within which the Attempt_suasion is occuring.

fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Purpose

frame.name: Eventive_affecting
frame.definition:
An Entity undergoes some change (the Event) that is (or is construed as) punctual. (This frame exists mainly to allow common FEs to be inherited.)
Ex: ["Event" This] HAPPENS ["Entity" to me] ["Frequency" all the time].
Ex: ["Entity" The area] was STRUCK ["Event" by tragedy] ["Time" in 1996], ["Time" when an assassin killed 35 people in Port Arthur.]

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event which occurs and affects the Entity.

frame.name: Suasion
frame.definition:
A Speaker expresses through language his wish to get the Addressee to act and as a result the Addressee forms an intention do so. There is no implication that the Addressee actually acts upon the intention formed. In the case of _convince_ and _persuade_, the act that the Speaker wishes the Addressee to perform can be the adoption of a belief, which may be expressed as a that-clause or as an of-PP complement.
This frame differs from Attempt_suasion in that in Suasion, the Addressee has changed their mind in accord with the Speaker's wishes, whereas in Attempt_suasion, the only implication is that the Speaker communicates with the intent of changing the mind of the Addressee.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The person that the Speaker seeks to influence to act.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The person who intends through the use of language to get another person to act.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The wish for action on the Addressee's part that the Speaker expresses.

fe.name: Text
fe.definition: A piece of written or spoken material that changes the mind of the Addressee. Ex: ["Text" His speech] CONVINCED me to join the Peace Corps.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The general item or items that are the focus of the Content of the Speaker's message. Ex: You haven't CONVINCED me ["Top" about that yet].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Speaker that accomplishes the persuasion. Ex: I PERSUADED the committee ["Mns" by giving each member a grand].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The way in which the Speaker suades the Addressee.
Ex: The car salesman ["Manner" expertly] PERSUADED the customer to spend more than he could afford.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Speaker suades the Addressee.

lexunit.name: convince.v
lexunit.definition: COD: persuade to do something.

lexunit.name: dissuade.v

lexunit.definition: COD: provide with a motive.

lexunit.name: persuade.v

lexunit.name: sway.v

frame.name: Talking_into
frame.definition: A Speaker expresses through language his wish to get the Addressee to act. The Addressee forms an intention to act and does so.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker intends through the use of language to get another person to act.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The wish for action on the Addressee's part that the Speaker expresses.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The person that the Speaker seeks to influence to act.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: Act of the Speaker that enables them to persuade the Addressee. Ex: Mr. Mortiarty TALKED me into it ["Mns" by claiming it was the last job].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition:
An entity that the Speaker gets the Addressee to give to them.
Ex: He TALKED me ["Goods" out of five dollars].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Speaker hopes to bring about.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity that the Speaker manipulates to get the Addressee to perform the Content.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Speaker talks the Addressee into performing the Content.

frame.name: Change_position_on_a_scale
frame.definition:
This frame consists of words that indicate the change of an Item's position on a scale (the Attribute) from a starting point (Initial_value) to an end point (Final_value). The direction (Path) of the movement can be indicated as well as the magnitude of the change (Difference). The rate of change of the value (Speed) is optionally indicated. Another scale (Correlate), which the values are correlated with, is indicated if it is not the default correlate (namely, absolute time).
Ex: The distinction between Attributes and Items is not always an easy one. The clear cases involve the expression of the Attribute in an _in_-PP.
Ex: ["Item" Hawke's Bay winery] DOUBLED ["Attribute" in size] ["Time" last year].
Ex: The amount you can deduct, then, depends on whether or not ["Item" the stock] has INCREASED ["Attribute" in value] ["Time" during the period you have owned it].
Other clear cases of Attributes involve NP's like _size, quality, number, value_ that denote abstract attributes rather than events or classes of things.
Ex: The analysis is more complicated when an event-denoting noun phrase occurs as the subject and the sentence has no _in_-PP. In the simplest cases, where the Attribute is the number of occurrences of the event, the Attribute is usually left implicit, as in exx. 1 and 2, the Attribute below.
Ex: (1)["Item" Accidents] INCREASED ["Difference" 20%] ["val2" to 345]. Ex: (1--second FE layer)Accidents INCREASED 20% ["Attribute" to 345]. Ex: (2) ["Item" Attacks on civilians] DECREASED ["Time" over the last 4 months] ["Attribute" DNI].
In cases like (1), we will tag the Attribute on the second layer below the Final_value label, as that FE makes it clear that the Attribute is simply cardinality. In cases like (2), we tag it as DNI because in context the hearer has to understand a particular Attribute rather than just some or any appropriate Attribute of the Item. Note that the above pattern can be compared to cases involving tangible Items, where the Attribute may similarly be missing when the incidence or frequency of the Item is specified.
Ex: (3) ["Item" Woodland birds] INCREASED["val2" to their highest level since 1990] ["Attribute" DNI].
A more complicated case involving event-denoting subjects is when the Attribute measured is not the incidence of the type of event specified but rather an Attribute of an event-participant. In (4), it is not the _number of times_ that turbot was caught that has changed but the _amount_ of fish caught.
Ex: (4) ["Item" Turbot catches] INCREASED ["val1" from around 100 tonnes in the 1960s] ["val2" to around 1,200 tonnes in the mid 1990s]. Ex: (4-second FE layer) Turbot catches INCREASED ["att" from around 100 tonnes in the 1960s] ["att" to around 1,200 tonnes in the mid 1990s].
(Note the 2nd layer annotation of the Attribute below the Initial_value and Final_value FEs, since they indicate that the Attribute is implicitly _weight_.)
Similarly, in (5), the report is (in context) about the total monetary value of the gifts, not about the number of donations made.
Ex: (5)["Item" Overall Giving by Church Members] INCREASED from 2000 to 2001
As can be seen from the above examples, we consider the event nouns in uses such as (4) and (5) to also specify Items. Note that in cases like (4), we do not want to treat the subject NP "turbot catches" as an Attribute that includes information about the Item, since it would not make sense to restate (4) as follows:
Ex: *Turbot INCREASED in catches.
Two more complications arise. First, certain nouns that do not, by their etymology, denote abstract attributes have a second sense in which they do denote an Attribute.
Ex: (6) The population of Smallville INCREASED fourfold to 807.
Under one reading, (6a), the population could be understood as referring to "the people", in which case the Attribute _cardinality_ is understood as unexpressed, as in (1), (2), and (3). The Attribute could be overtly specified:
Ex: (6a) ["ite" The population of Smallville] INCREASED ["Diff" fourfold] ["att" in size] ["val2" to 807].
Under another reading, (6b), population is an Attribute that habitats or locations possess. In this case, the whole NP "the population of Smallville" is treated as the Attribute and on the second layer "of Smallville" is tagged as Item.
Ex: (6b) ["att" The population of Smallville] INCREASED ["Diff" fourfold] ["val2" to 807]. Ex: (6b-second FE layer) The population ["ite" of Smallville] INCREASED fourfold to 807. Support for the possibility of this second reading comes from the fact that you can also state the facts as in (6c).
Ex: (6c) ["ite" Smallville] INCREASED ["Diff" fourfold] ["att" in population] ["val2" to 807].
The last complication is that Initial_value expressions can also function as the subject, which superficially look like expressions of Attribute.
Ex: (7) ["val1" The 1999 price] had INCREASED ["val2" to $3400] ["Time" by 2001]. Ex: (7--second layer) The 1999 ["att" price] had INCREASED to $3400 by 2001.
There is no Attribute "1999 price" here (though the concept is plausible in certain special statistical contexts where prices are indexed to prices of a particular year). (7) simply reports that the value of the price-Attribute changed from whatever it was in 1999 to the new value of $3400 by 2001. For sentence (7), Attribute would only be indicated as "price" on the 2nd layer.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The Attribute is a scalar property that the Item possesses.Ex: ["Item" Oil] ROSE ["Attribute" in price] ["Diff" by 2%].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The entity that has a position on the scale.
Ex: I fear ["Item" this service] will DIMINISH in quality.

fe.name: Difference
fe.definition: The distance by which an Item changes its position on the scale.Ex: Oil ROSE in price ["Diff" by 2%].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any expression that gives information about points on the scale that the Item traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement along the scale.Ex: The price of oil MOVED ["Path" up] last month.

fe.name: Final_value
fe.definition: The position on the scale where the Item ends up. Ex: Microsoft shares FELL ["val2" to 7 5/8].

fe.name: Initial_value
fe.definition: The initial position on the scale from which the Item moves away. Ex: Microsoft shares FELL ["val1" from 12 3/8] to 7 5/8.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The rate of change of the Value.Ex: Prices are RISING ["Speed" by 2% a year].

fe.name: Correlate
fe.definition:
The Correlate is a directional path (or ordered collection of values) that the (dependent) Attribute is measured against. Note that normally, the Correlate is simply (forward-directional) time.
Ex: The amount of power INCREASES ["cor" with the frequency of the laser]. Ex: ["cor" As you travel along the Quan-duo road], the poverty level SOARS dramatically.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances under which the change of position takes place. Ex: The eggs will only INCREASE ["Circumstances" under pressure].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result. of an event

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: The Group in which an Item changes the value of a Attribute in a specified way.Ex: Colon cancer incidence FELL by 50 % ["Grp" among men over 30].Ex: Net foreign debt has more than TRIPLED ["Grp" in Africa] over this decade.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is the time-frame in which the change of position occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time over which the change takes place. Ex: The amount of troops in the war will no doubt DOUBLE ["Dur" over the next several years].

fe.name: Value_range
fe.definition:
A portion of the scale, typically identified by its end points, along which the values of the Attribute fluctuate.
Ex: The patient's temperature FLUCTUATED ["Value_range" between 28.5 and 29.5].

fe.name: Initial_correlate
fe.definition:
The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Initial_value of the Attribute.
Ex: ["cor1" From Monterrey] to southern Oregon, tree height INCREASES steadily in this species to a stunning 50 meters.

fe.name: Final_correlate
fe.definition:
The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Final_value of the Attribute.
Ex: From Monterrey ["cor2" to southern Oregon], tree height INCREASES steadily in this species to a stunning 50 meters.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: A location where Attribute is measured

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition:
A description that presents the Item's state before the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.
Ex: Diesels have INCREASED ["inis" from having a 20% market share in 1995] to just over 30% in 2004.

fe.name: Final_state
fe.definition:
A description that presents the Item's state after the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.
Ex: It was never bad (1 or 2 seizures a year), but this past decade, it has INCREASED ["finis" to having them 1 day a month] and on that 1 day I have 6 or 7 seizures.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

frame.name: Manipulate_into_doing
frame.definition: A Manipulator gets his Victim to perform a Resulting_action against what their better judgment would have been at the time. The means by which the Manipulator overcomes or bypasses the Victim's resistance to act need not be linguistic expression. In some cases, the Goods may stand in for a Resulting_action of the Victim giving the Manipulator the Goods.

fe.name: Manipulator
fe.definition: The person who gets the Victim to act against their interest.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: The person who the Manipulator gets to do something they would not have done had no pressure or deception been applied.

fe.name: Resulting_action
fe.definition: What the Manipulator intends to make the Victim do and the Victim actually does.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Manipulator that enables them to alter the action of the Victim. Ex: I BADGERED her into coming ["Mns" by calling her every five minutes].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away. Ex: Leslie BLACKMAILED ["Goods" the watch] out of John.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity that the Manipulator uses to get the Victim to perform the Resulting_action.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: A state-of-affairs that the Manipulator is hoping to bring about by manipulating the Victim.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the manipulation occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Manipulator manipulates the Victim.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including metaphorical force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Manipulator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

frame.name: Hostile_encounter
frame.definition: This frame consists of words that describe a hostile encounter between opposing forces (Side_1 and Side_2, collectively conceptualizable as Sides) over a disputed Issue and/or in order to reach a specific Purpose.

fe.name: Side_1
fe.definition: One of two participants in a hostile encounter. While ["Side_1" the U.S.'s] BATTLE with terrorist-harboring nations is far off ...

fe.name: Side_2
fe.definition: One of two participants in a hostile encounter, usually the second mentioned. Ex: While the U.S.'s BATTLE ["Side_2" with terrorist-harboring nations] is far off ...

fe.name: Sides
fe.definition: The jointly expressed sides in a hostile encounter. ["Sides" They] FOUGHT over the right to own land.

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition:
An unresolved question over which the two sides of a hostile encounter are in disagreement.
Ex: They had a DUST-UP ["Issue" over who was prettier] .
Quite often it takes the form of a covert question of various sorts. So in an example like:
Ex: They FOUGHT ["Issue" over the right to own land].
among many other possibilities, the covert question might be more explicitly phrased as follows:
Ex: They FOUGHT ["Issue" over what the right to own land means].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The desired result of the outcome of the hostile encounter for the Side_1 or for all the Sides collectively. It may either directly refer to the state of affairs that is desired, e.g.
Ex: He DUELED with his former second ["Purpose" to defend the honour of the man he had killed] .
or it the state of affairs may be implicit in an (abstract or concrete) entity that they desire, e.g.
Ex: Rival Democratic presidential candidates Mr Bill Clinton and Mr Jerry Brown taunted each other at the weekend as mudslinging in the BATTLE ["Purpose" for votes] in tomorrow's crucial New York primary reached a new low.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: Means describes the way in which a side engages in a hostile encounter. President Corazon Aquino of the Philippines is bracing herself for a ["Means" legal] BATTLE over her decision to allow the remains of the former president, Ferdinand Marcos, to be returned home from Hawaii for burial.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of the hostile encounter. Descriptions of the intensity count as Manner expressions. After Brundle's Jaguar took off like a scalded cat, it was Mass who hunted it down, an soon engaged it in a ["Manner" lurid] BATTLE.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the hostile encounter takes place.
Ex: Following the BATTLE ["Place" of Naseby] in 1645 ...

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the hostile encounter occurs.
Ex: Following the BATTLE of Naseby ["Time" in 1645] he died.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal Cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal Cause is expressed in a PP Complement: Kim FROWNED ["Internal_cause" in concentration]. Kim THREW her hands up ["Internal_cause" in despair].

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

frame.name: Theft
frame.definition:
These are words describing situations in which a Perpetrator takes Goods from a Victim or a Source. The Means by which this is accomplished may also be expressed.
Ex: I can't believe ["Perpetrator" he] PICKPOCKETED ["Goods" my gold watch] ! Ex: ["Perpetrator" I] had to PILFER ["Victim" from the office] ["Purpose" just to get by] . ["Goods" INI] Ex: SNATCHING ["Goods" purses] ["Source" from little old ladies] is not a living . ["Perpetrator" CNI]

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition:
Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) that takes the goods away.
Ex: ["Perp" Leslie] STOLE the watch from Kim.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that owns the goods before they are taken away by the perpetrator. Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch ["Victim" from Kim].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition:
Goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.
Ex: Leslie STOLE ["Goods" the watch] from Kim.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Source is the initial location of the goods, before they change location.
Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch ["Src" from the table].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the theft occurs.
Ex: Leslie ["Manner" swiftly] STOLE the watch from Kim.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which a Perpetrator takes the Victim's Goods.
Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim ["Means" by following her home after work].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the theft occurs. Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim ["Place" in the park].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which a theft occurs. Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim ["Purpose" in order to sell it on Ebay].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Reason for which a theft occurs.
Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim ["Reason" because she'd always wanted a Gucci].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the theft occurs.
Ex: Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim ["Time" at dusk].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An object used by the Perpetrator in taking possession of the Goods.
Ex: Chis STOLE it ["Instrument" with a long bamboo pole] through the fence

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that a theft occurs.
Ex: Thieves ["Frequency" twice] STOLE my Dodge Dart in the last two weeks

frame.name: Position_on_a_scale
frame.definition: This frame contains words that describe an Item's static position on a scale with respect to some property Variable.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: Item identifies the entity whose scalar property is specified. Ex: ["Item" Bacon] is HIGH ["Variable" in fat].

fe.name: Variable
fe.definition:
Variable is the scalar property that the Item possesses.
["Item" Soda] is HIGH ["Variable" in sugar].

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
The Value is the position or range of positions on the scale that the Item occupies. This is normally implicit in the LU.
Ex: This car is ["Value" HIGH] in price.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the scalar property of an Item holds with respect to some Variable. Ex: Bacon is ["Degree" very] HIGH in fat.

lexunit.name: high.a
lexunit.definition: COD: great in amount, value, size, or intensity.

lexunit.name: low.a
lexunit.definition: COD: below average in amount, extent, or intensity

lexunit.name: rich.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having (something) in large amounts.

lexunit.name: deficient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: insufficient or inadequate.

lexunit.name: lacking.a
lexunit.definition: COD: absent or deficient.

lexunit.name: advanced.a
lexunit.definition: COD: complex; not elementary.

lexunit.name: through the roof.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: extremely high

lexunit.name: medium.a
lexunit.definition: COD: between two extremes; average.

frame.name: Cause_change_of_position_on_a_scale
frame.definition: This frame consists of words that indicate that an Agent or a Cause affects the position of an Item on some scale (the Attribute) to change it from an initial value (Value_1) to an end value (Value_2). The direction of the change (Path) can be encoded as well as the magnitude of the change (Difference). The rate of change of the value (Speed) can optionally be indicated as well as a second scale (Co_Variable), which the values are correlated with.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The person who causes an entity (Item) to change its positon on a scale with respect to some property (Variable).

fe.name: Difference
fe.definition:
The distance between the orginial value (Value-1) and the final value (Value-2) of the entity on the scale (Variable).
["Agent" Coke] RAISED ["Variable" the price] ["Item" of their soda] ["Difference" by 2%].

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The scale along which the Item ranges in value. Ex: ["Agent" They] INCREASED ["Attribute" the price of oil].

fe.name: Value_1
fe.definition: The initial value of the entity (Item) along the scale.

fe.name: Value_2
fe.definition: The final position on the scale that the entity (Item) assumes.

fe.name: Co_Variable
fe.definition:
The Co-Variable is the scale that the (dependent ) Variable is measured against.
We RAISE the temperature ["Co_Variable" with the pressure]

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Item) along the scale between its initial (Value-1) and its final position (Value-2).
Ex: They MOVED ["Path" up] the price of oil.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.
["Agent" Ford] ["Speed" slowly] RAISED ["variable" the price] ["Item" of their best-selling model].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The entity whose position along a scale is being changed.
["Item" Oil] prices were RAISED yesterday.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the position of the Item on the scale. Ex: They INCREASE the price of diamonds ["Mns" by withholding a sizable portion of the supply].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. John FLATTERED her ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The force that causes the change. ["Cause" The rain] INCREASED the river's flow rate to an astonishing million gallons per second.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Agent changing the value of an Attribute which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Agent changes the value of an Attribute.
Ex: As a result, they RAISED prices ["Place" in Peoria].
