frame.name: Influence_of_event_on_cognizer
frame.definition:
A Situation or Protagonist creates conditions that push the Cognizer towards executing an Action, or which influence the Cognizer in an Activity. The words in this frame imply that the Cognizer actually does something.
Ex: ["sit" The murder of my brother] INFLUENCED ["cog" me] ["act" to study Law].
Ex: ["sit" Her interest in history] has largely INFLUENCED ["cog" her] ["tiv" in her work].
Ex: Despite this huge variety, there were ["sit" only two main factors that] ["deg" significantly] INFLUENCED ["tiv" the artist's work]. Ex: Despite this huge variety, there were only two main factors that significantly INFLUENCED ["cog" the artist's] work.
Ex: Discuss ["sit" the things that] GUIDED ["cog" you] ["tiv" in making your decision].

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition:
The Situation which motivates the Cognizer to execute the Action.
Ex: ["sit" The accident] INFLUENCED him to drive slower.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
A person or self-directed entity whose actions may potentially change the mind of the Cognizer.
Ex: ["pro" Van Gogh] INFLUENCED Cezanne

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The sentient entity whose mind is moved in the direction of change.
Ex: Had that information INFLUENCED ["cog" Fred Franz]?

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
The Action that the Cognizer is influenced to do.
Ex: Everyone in the town also enjoyed her writing, which INFLUENCED her ["act" to continue].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Cognizer is influenced.
Ex: ["tim" Today] the Koran INFLUENCES the thinking of hundreds of millions of people

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: I can't say that any single writer has INFLUENCED me ["man" directly], that I'm aware of ...

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
An activity (or domain) rather than a single, particular action that the Cognizer is influenced in.
Ex: These works had a profound effect and INFLUENCED her ["tiv" in the creation of a successful series capturing this sun-drenched region].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which a Protagonist or Situation influences the Cognizer.
Ex: Who ["deg" significantly] INFLUENCED the artist's life

lexunit.name: guide.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to influence towards a specific action

lexunit.name: influence.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have an influence on

lexunit.name: influence((mass)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the capacity to have an effect on the character or behaviour of someone or something, or the effect itself

lexunit.name: influence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: factor which has an effect on someone so that they perform an action.

lexunit.name: influential.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having great influence.

frame.name: Eventive_cognizer_affecting
frame.definition:
An Event causes the Cognizer to accept some Content. Although the Cognizer forms an intention, it is not entailed that he/she acts.
Ex: ["Event" The divorce] CONVINCED ["Cognizer" him] ["Content" to get help].
Ex: ["Event" The price of a factory reconditioned tool] DECIDED ["Content" it] ["Cognizer" for me].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The person who perceives the Event and changes his or her mind.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The new idea that the Cognizer accepts as a result of experiencing the Event.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The Event which motivates the Cognizer to change his/her mind.
Ex: ["Event" The accident] CONVINCED him to drive slower.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The degree to which the Cognizer's mind is changed.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Cognizer is affected by an outside Event.

lexunit.name: convince.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make an impression on someone so that they believe something.

lexunit.name: decide.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause someone to come to a particular conclusion.

frame.name: Robbery
frame.definition:
These are words describing situations in which a Perpetrator wrongs a Victim by taking something (Goods) from them. In some cases, the Source location from which the Goods were taken is used to metonymically refer to the Victim. The robbery can be done in a particular Manner (for example, forcefully) and via a specific Means (for example, by threatening the Victim).
Ex: ["Perpetrator" Half of the team] HELD UP ["Victim" the tellers] while the others were stationed to report the arrival of police.
As opposed to Theft, Robbery focuses on the harm to the Victim and on the Source location from which the Goods have been removed, rather than the Goods themselves.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition:
The Perpetratoris the person (or other agent) that takes the Goods away by force or threats.
Ex: ["Perpetrator" Leslie] ROBBED Kim of her watch.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition:
The Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that owns the Goods before they are taken away by the Perpetrator.
Ex: Leslie ROBBED ["Victim" Kim] of her watch.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition:
The Goods are anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.
Ex: Leslie ROBBED John ["Goods" of his watch].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source is the initial location of the goods, before they change location. Ex: Leslie and Kim ROBBED ["Source" a bank] This FE is realized in compound nouns as follows: Ex: ["Source" bank] ROBBERY

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means indicates the means by which the Robbery takes place.
Ex: John MUGGED his victim ["Means" by holding a toy gun to his head].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner describes the way in which the Robbery took place.
Ex: He was known for committing ["Manner" violent] MUGGINGS on schoolchildren

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is where the Robbery occurs.
Ex: They ROBBED a bank ["Place" in North Berkeley].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time indicates when the Robbery occurs.
Ex: They ROBBED a bank in North Berkeley ["Time" last May].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by the robbery.
Ex: They used to ROB folks ["Purp" just to see the expression on their faces].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The state of affairs that the Perpetrator has in mind which leads to the decision to commit the robbery.
Ex: Listen, I just MUG people ["Reason" 'cause I got mouths to feed] -- nothing personal.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times a robbery event occurs.
Ex: An Agoura Jills cigar store was ROBBED ["Frequency" twice] last week

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: Co_participant denotes a person that participates in a coordinated way in robbery event as the primary protagonist, the Perpetrator.

lexunit.name: rob.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take away from by force or threats

lexunit.name: robber.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A person who robs.

lexunit.name: mug.v
lexunit.definition: FN: an act of robbing

frame.name: Personal_relationship
frame.definition: The words in this frame have to do with people and the personal Relationships they are or can be a part of. Some of the words denote people engaged in a particular kind of Relationship, others denote the Relationship, yet others the events bringing about or ending the Relationships. Many of the words presuppose an understanding of states and events that must have occurred before another event takes place or before a person can be classified in a certain way.

fe.name: Partner_1
fe.definition: That partner in the Relationship who is realized as the subject of verbs in active form sentences, or of adjectives in predicative uses. Ex: ["Partner_1" John] is MARRIED ["Partner_2" to Sue]. Ex: ["Partner_1" John] is ["Partner_2" Sue's] HUSBAND. When the target word is a noun (e.g. mistress, lover, bachelor), that noun is annotated as Partner_1 and, if there is one, the other member of the Relationship is Partner_2. Ex: ["Partner_1" George] is a BACHELOR. Ex: ["Partner_2" George's] ["Partner_1" MISTRESS] left the party. Ex: ["Partner_2" George] has a ["Partner_1" MISTRESS]. When there is a word other than the target that refers to Partner_1, that word is tagged rather than the target. Ex: ["Partner_1" George] is ["Partner_2" Laura's] LOVER.

fe.name: Partner_2
fe.definition: That partner in the Relationship who is not expressed as the external argument. Ex: ["Partner_1" John] is ["Partner_2" Sue's] HUSBAND. Ex: ["Partner_1" John] is ENGAGED ["Partner_2" to Joan].

fe.name: Partners
fe.definition: The joint construal of both Partners in the Relationship. Ex: ["Partners" John and Sue] are MARRIED. Ex: ["Partners" They] are ENGAGED.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Partners.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby a focal participant achieves an action indicated by the target. Ex: He BEFRIENDED her ["Means" by staying after to talk every day].

fe.name: Relationship
fe.definition: The Relationship between Partners. Ex: His wanderings caused the BREAK-UP ["Relationship" of their marriage].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of the relationship. Ex: I'd like you to meet my ["Duration" long-time] FRIEND.

fe.name: Source_of_relationship
fe.definition: The source of the relationship. Ex: Have you seen my old ["Src" High School] BUDDY Johnathan Rich lately?

frame.name: Aggregate
frame.definition:
This frame contains nouns denoting Aggregates of Individuals. The Aggregates may be described by an AggregateProperty.
Ex: An ["Agg" ARMY] ["Individuals" of postal workers] descended on my office.

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: This FE identifies the people or things that form the Aggregate. Ex: A CROWD ["Individuals" of hoodlums] filled the plaza.

fe.name: Aggregate
fe.definition: This FE identifies the collection of entities that are the Aggregate. Ex: A ["Aggregate" CROWD] of hoodlums filled the plaza.

fe.name: AggregateProperty
fe.definition: This FE describes a property of the Aggregate rather than the Individuals and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the aggregate noun when it is unambiguous.Ex: A ["AgProp" large] CROWD of hoodlums filled the plaza.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The term used to refer to the Aggregate.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Aggregate.

frame.name: Kinship
frame.definition: This frame contains words that denote Kinship relations. In annotating the directional uses of these words, we use the standard terms from anthropology, Ego and Alter. Ex: ["Alter" Matilde] is ["Ego" Gilberto's] COUSIN ["Degree" once removed]

fe.name: Alter
fe.definition: The person who fills the role named by the Kinship term with respect to the Ego.Ex: ["Alter" John] _is_ ["Ego" my] COUSIN.Ex: I met ["Ego" his] ["Alter" BROTHER] last year.

fe.name: Ego
fe.definition: The person from whose perspective the Kinship relationship is defined.Ex: ["Alter" Bill] _is_ ["Ego" Sue's] SON.

fe.name: Relatives
fe.definition: The combination of Alter and Ego together.Ex: ["Relatives" John and I] _are_ BROTHERS.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: An expression of the closeness or distance of the relation. We do not go into full anthropological detail in measuring the distance of the relation, but simply annotate all such expressions as Degree

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describe some characteristic of the Alter or the Ego.

frame.name: Location_of_light
frame.definition:
A perceptible Figure shows up against a Ground location due to Light shining on/from it, its salience possibly dependent on a Cause_of_shine.
Ex: ["Fig" The grass] GLISTENED ["Shine" with dew]. Ex: Still GLOWING ["Shine" from the forge]... Ex: ["Fig" The oily mud] GLEAMED ["Shine" wetly] ["Grnd" under his feet]. Ex: ["Fig" Something] was SHIMMERING ["Grnd" on the shore]. Ex: ["Fig" The quartz] GLOWED ["Lit" with a fitful, internal light]. Ex: ["Fig" The walls] GLOWED ["Grnd" in the sun]. Ex:
Note that in this last example, the PP 'in the sun' is both the Ground on the primary FE layer and Light on the secondary layer.
Ex: This frame is similar to the frame Light_movement. In both, there is a very consistent metaphorical conception of emotions as shining in eyes or forth from eyes, including the associated pattern of eyes shining with an emotion. The sense in such cases is that the eyes (or the muscles and features around the eyes) are in such a configuration as to saliently convey the emotion. Such sentences should be tagged with the metaphor tag to differentiate them from literal sentences like "His eyes glistened with tears."

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the Light is emitted, usually indicating the brightness.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of a focal participant during the emission of Light . Ex: The moonlight SHONE ["Dep" cold] over the Scottish moor.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of Light emission. Ex: In the dim light the gold and strong colours GLITTERED and glowed ["Manr" intensely].

fe.name: Figure
fe.definition: The percept which is perceived at a certain Ground location. Ex: ["Fig" Candlelight] SPARKLED on the silverware.Ex: ["Fig" Her face] GLISTENED with sweat.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: The location of the phenomenon.Ex: Hot coals GLOWED ["Grnd" behind the fire grate].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the emission of the Light . Ex: The screen GLOWED ["Result" into life].

fe.name: Cause_of_shine
fe.definition: This is the cause of the shininess of the phenomenon, generally introduced by 'with'.Ex: Her face GLISTENED ["Shine" with sweat].Ex: His eyes GLEAMED ["Shine" with amusement].

fe.name: Light
fe.definition:
The Light which is emitted. In this frame, it is usually incorporated in verbs and adjectives, and is the denotation of many of the nouns. Ex: The fire ["Lit" GLOWED]. Ex: The ["Light" GLINT] of gold made me blind with greed.
Occasionally this FE shows up as a full argument:Ex: The chamber ["Lit" GLOWED] ["Lit" with brilliant light].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period for which the Figure shows up against the Ground due to Light falling on it.
Ex: ["Duration" For a few minutes] the walls GLOWED in the sun

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The spatial setting in which the Figure shows up against a Ground location.
Ex: ["Place" Outside] something was SHIMMERING on the shore.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Figure is observed against the Ground location due to Light shining on it.
Ex: ["Time" In the morning] the grass GLISTENED with dew

frame.name: Gizmo
frame.definition:
This frame contains general words denoting equipment where the Use or purpose is not specified by the lexeme but (typically) by a separate expression. The words are described with respect to the Use for which the item is used or its typical User.
Ex: ["Use" coffee] MACHINE Ex: ["User" dentist's] EQUIPMENT

Ex: DEVICE ["Use" for making soap bubbles]

frame.name: Examination
frame.definition: This frame deals with testing or examination of someone's Knowledge or skill in a particular area. An Examiner conducts an Examination to an Examinee to determine the Examinee's Knowledge and/or determine their Qualification for some priviledge; this proceeds either by the Examinee demonstrating a skill or by writing responses to questions.

fe.name: Examiner
fe.definition: One who administers a test of some kind.Ex: ["Exmr" The teacher] TESTED the students.

fe.name: Examinee
fe.definition: One who undergoes a test of some kind.Ex: ["Exmee" The students] took a TEST.

fe.name: Knowledge
fe.definition:
The ability, practice, or command of information on which an Examinee is tested.
Ex: I took my ["Knowledge" driving] TEST. Ex: Is there anything more odious than a ["kno" History] test strictly on dates ?

fe.name: Qualification
fe.definition: A credential or status that one acquires by passing an Examination.Ex: ["Exmee" He] _took_ the ["Qualification" college entrance] ["Examination" EXAM].

fe.name: Examination
fe.definition: The Examination that somebody takes.Ex: ["Examination" The examination] TESTS driving skills.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Examiner assesses the Examinee. Ex: The sarge TESTED him ["Mns" by having him take his rifle apart and put it back together].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Examiner wants to bring about by giving the Examinee the Examination.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the examination takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the examination occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Examiner that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

frame.name: Dimension
frame.definition: This frame concerns words that express an Object's position on a scale, its Measurement, with respect to some attribute , its Dimension. Location, identifying the sub-region of the Object where the Dimension is measured, may also be expressed. Ex: ["Object" The tower] is ["Measurement" 10 feet] ["Dimension" TALL]. Ex: ["Object" The new vase] is ["Measurement" 5 cm] in ["Dimension" CIRCUMFERENCE] ["Location" at the top]. Ex: Note the tagging of _six feet_ on the GF and PT layers in the following sentence. Ex: ["Object" The woman] was ["Measurement" six feet] TALL. The GF of _six feet_ is Dep and the PT is NP.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Dimension which is measured.
Ex: The new vase is 5 cm in ["Dimension" CIRCUMFERENCE] at the top.

fe.name: Object
fe.definition:
Object identifies the item which is measured along one of its Dimensions.
Ex: ["Object" The new vase] is 5 cm in CIRCUMFERENCE at the top.

fe.name: Measurement
fe.definition:
Measurement identifies the extent of the Object along the specified Dimension.
Ex: The new vase is ["Measurement" 5 cm] in CIRCUMFERENCE at the top.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: Location identifies the sub-region of the Object where the Dimension is measured. Ex: The new vase is 5 cm in CIRCUMFERENCE ["Location" at the top].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The relevant dimension of development.

frame.name: Residence
frame.definition:
This frame has to do with people (the Residents) residing in Locations, sometimes with a Co-resident.
Ex: ["Resident" Peter] LIVES ["Location" in New York]. Ex: ["Resident" Sue] _is_ an INHABITANT ["Location" of Los Angeles].

fe.definition:
The individual(s) that reside at the Location.
Ex: ["Res" Hannah] LIVES in San Francisco.

fe.definition:

Ex: ["Res" Sue] LIVES ["Location" in Berkeley].

fe.name: Co_resident

Ex: ["Res" Boris] still LIVES ["Co_resident" with his parents].

fe.name: Frequency

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE refers to the Time when the Resident resides.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

frame.name: Education_teaching
frame.definition:
This frame contains words referring to teaching and the participants in teaching. A Student comes to learn either about a Subject; a Skill; a Precept; or a Fact as a result of instruction by a Teacher.
Some of the nouns (schoolmaster, -mistress) in this frame refer to administrative positions and do not take relevant frame elements; these will be moved.
Ex: ["tea" Dad] TAUGHT ["" me] ["fac" that if you work hard, you will be OK - no matter what happens].
Ex: ["fac" What] ["tea" Our Cat] TAUGHT ["stu" Me] ["sub" About Marketing]!
Ex: For two years ["tea" she] TAUGHT ["stu" me] ["sub" French]
Ex: ["tea" Mom and Dad] TAUGHT ["stu" me] ["pre" not to bullshit], because it always came back to bite me in the ass, without fail.
Ex: ["tea" A young swiss girl up in a swiss chalet] TAUGHT ["stu" me] ["ski" how to yodel].
Ex: Young Murdock later met ["tea" a blind martial arts master known as Stick, who] taught him how to use his augmented senses and TRAINED ["stu" him] ["rol" as a fighter].
Ex: Maria, ["stu" a woman] STUDYING ["rol" to be a nun] is sent from her convent to be the governess of the seven children of a widowed naval captain
Ex: Frame-Element relations:
Several Frame element relations hold in this frame. There is a core-set {Material, Teacher} (possibly also including Institution); these FE's can fill the subject slot of the teach-type verbs. There is another core-set {Precept, Subject, Skill, Fact, Role} to do with what is learnt. In addition, the FE Qualification may occur with Subject and Role Ex: My sister is studying ["Qualification" for a maths degree ] ["Role" to be a teacher ] Ex: She's studying ["Subject" maths] ["Role" to be a teacher ].
Phrases expressing Qualification also very often include information about the Subject (see below), which is to be annotated on the second layer.
Ex: Bill is STUDYING ["Qualification" for a BS in physics/a maths degree]. Ex: Bill is STUDYING for a BS in ["Subject" physics]/a ["Subject" maths] degree.

fe.name: Teacher
fe.definition: One who instructs a Student in some area of knowledge or skill.

fe.name: Student
fe.definition: One who is instructed by a Teacher in skills or knowledge.

fe.name: Institution
fe.definition: An educational establishment, such as a school or college.

fe.name: Subject
fe.definition:
The area of knowledge or skill which is taught by a Teacher or to a Student.
Ex: She's a ["Subject" French] TEACHER

fe.name: Level
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Level of a student in his/her education. This is distinct from the goal or qualification towards which a student is working (Qualification). Ex: a ["Level" graduate] student Ex: a ["Level" fourth grade] student The above are both Levels, in contrast to: Ex: a ["Qualification" doctoral] Student Ex: an ["Qualification" MA] Student

fe.name: Qualification
fe.definition:
A formal Qualification such as an academic degree or a certificate for which a student is aiming.
Ex: She's STUDYING ["Qualification" for a Master's degree] Ex: She's an ["Qualification" MA] STUDENT

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the actor (Student or Teacher depending on the profiling of particular words) that lets them achieve the instruction or learning they are attempting.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the teaching occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location within which the teaching takes place.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Skill
fe.definition:
An action which the Student is able to perform as a result of instruction.
Ex: Taut with worry, Dad TAUGHT us ["ski" how to drive].

fe.name: Precept
fe.definition:
A guideline for correct behavior. In most cases, this concerns morally or socially desirable actions.
Ex: My brother TAUGHT me ["pre" not to be mean to guys when I'm not interested in them].

fe.name: Fact
fe.definition:
A piece of information that the Student is informed of by the Teacher.
Ex: When I was two she TAUGHT me ["fac" that a quarter was 25 cents and a dime was 10 cents].

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Educational Material, such as books, tapes, or videos, used by a Teacher or a Student to acquire skills or knowledge.
Ex: All employees have received ["mat" a booklet] INSTRUCTING them on how to report ` anything from unwanted touching and uncalled-for blue jokes to overt demands for sexual favours . "

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
A role, typically professional or vocational, that the Student is meant to be able to fill as a result of their training.
Ex: When his father died he went to live with an uncle in Ka'u who TRAINED him ["rol" as a warrior] during his teenage years

fe.name: Course
fe.definition: FN: a program of lectures or other matter dealing with a subject

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Teacher hopes to bring about by teaching.
Ex: I TEACH ["Purpose" so that I can see the little light-bulb light up].

frame.name: Cause_harm
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe situations in which an Agent or a Cause injures a Victim. The Body_part of the Victim which is most directly affected may also be mentioned in the place of the Victim. In such cases, the Victim is often indicated as a genitive modifier of the Body_part, in which case the Victim FE is indicated on a second FE layer.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
Agent is the person causing the Victim's injury.
Ex: ["Agt" Jolosa, who] BROKE a rival player 's jaw, was told to model his play on the England striker. Ex: ["Agt" Someone] BASHED him on the back of the head with a heavy smooth object. Ex: Claire McLaren, 16, was punched and KICKED senseless ["Agt" by a thug].

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition:
The Victim is the being or entity that is injured. If the Victim is included in the phrase indicating Body_part, the Victim FE is tagged on a second FE layer (see 3rd example).
Ex: Someone BASHED ["Vic" him] on the back of the head with a heavy smooth object. Ex: The farmer tied him to the fence to stop him BUTTING ["Vic" the sheep]. Ex: Jolosa, who BROKE ["Vic" a rival player 's] jaw, was told to model his play on the England striker.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.
Ex: Riot police in Nairobi CLUBBED four women ["Result" unconscious] on March 3. Ex: A battered wife who BURNED her brutal husband ["Result" to death] was freed from jail yesterday. Ex: Claire McLaren, 16, was punched and KICKED ["Result" senseless] by a thug.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree is the degree to which the Agent causes harm to the Victim.
Ex: She wanted to SLAP him ["Degr" hard] for his change of mood. Ex: Fox spun around and SLAPPED him, ["Degr" harder than necessary].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the Agent acts upon the Victim.
Ex: He ["Manner" violently] SLAPPED his assailant.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.
Ex: Rachael INJURED her friend ["Means" by closing the car door on his left hand].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
Place identifies the place where the harm causing event occurs.
Ex: Boys are PUNCHED ["Place" at school] for payback

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.
Ex: Riot police in Nairobi CLUBBED four women unconscious ["Time" on March 3].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition:
The Body_part identifies the location on the body where the bodily injury takes place.
Ex: Someone BASHED him ["BodP" on the back of the head] with a heavy smooth object. Ex: Jolosa, who BROKE ["BodP" a rival player 's jaw] , was told to model his play on the England striker.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
This FE is any object used to cause the injury.
Ex: Someone BASHED him on the back of the head ["Ins" with a heavy smooth object]. Ex: John BUTTED her in the chest ["Ins" with his head].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: Purpose identifies the purpose for which a harm-causing action is carried out.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.
Ex: Indeed, Henry V used to BURN them ["Depict" alive].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event in which the harm is caused.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A fact or action somehow related to the Victim that the Agent responds to by causing harm to the Victim.
Ex: She wanted to SLAP him hard ["Reas" for his change of mood]. Ex: She could easily have SLAPPED her ["Reas" for that remark].

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition:
Iterations refers to the number of times the Agent causes harm to the Victim.
Ex: Kim HIT Harold with the stick ["Iter" a dozen times]. Ex: he had SLAPPED his wife across the face ["Iter" a number of times].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that inflicts harm on the Victim
Ex: ["Cause" A falling rock] CRUSHED my ankle.

fe.name: Subregion_bodypart
fe.definition: The Subregion_bodypart defines the precise location on the Body_part which is harmed. Ex: ["Body_part" Martha's legs] were CHOPPED off ["Subregion_bodypart" at the knees].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Cause_harm event and any of its participants.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Cause_harm event occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_harm event to its end.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Patricular_iteration
fe.definition: This FE indicates that the Cause_harm event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_harm event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: Fenella and Caspar both knelt down , taking a gentle hold of the Tree Spirits ' maimed branches , searching for the right words to convey their gratitude .

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the Cause_harm event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

frame.name: Likelihood
frame.definition:
This frame is concerned with the likelihood of a Hypothetical_event occurring. The Hypothetical_event is its only core frame element.
Ex: It _is_ LIKELY ["Hypothetical_event" that he'll arrive late].
Notice that in the case where a noun phrase is the subject of the Support Verb, that NP is also tagged as Hypothetical_event.
Ex: ["Hypothetical_event" He] _is_ LIKELY ["Hypothetical_event" to arrive late].

fe.name: Hypothetical_event
fe.definition: The state of affairs or occurrence whose likelihood is assessed. Ex: ["Evt" Rain] is fairly UNLIKELY today, I think.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE expresses a reason the speaker has for making judgment about the likelihood of an event.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the Hypothetical_event is likely.
Ex: A positive placebo effect is more LIKELY ["cir" when both patient and physician believe that therapeutic benefit will result].

frame.name: Catastrophe
frame.definition: The words in this frame involve an Undesirable_Event which affects the Undergoer negatively. No agent need be involved.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Undesirable_Event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Undesirable_Event occurs.

fe.name: Undergoer

The entity that experiences the Undesirable_Event.
Ex: An ["Undergoer" environmental] DISASTER is just what we need. Ex: Should hair loss BEFALL ["Undergoer" you]...

fe.name: Degree

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Circumstances under which a warning applies. (Proper only to _betide_.)

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The cause of the Undesirable_Event.
Ex: Most counties are prepared for some level of ["cau" natural] DISASTER.

frame.name: Attempt
frame.definition:
An Agent attempts to achieve a Goal. The Outcome may also be mentioned explicitly.
Ex: ["Agent" John] ATTEMPTED ["Goal" to climb Mt. Everest].
Ex: The ATTEMPT ["Goal" to climb Mt. Everest] ["Outcome" failed].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: ["Agent" John] ATTEMPTED to climb Mt. Everest.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.
Ex: John ATTEMPTED ["Goal" to climb Mt. Everest GOAL].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: John's third ["Outcome" failed] ATTEMPT began propitiously.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where an attempt is made.
Ex: ["Place" On the bridge] he ATTEMPTED to put the wig on.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the Agent makes the attempt.
Ex: He _made_ his final ATTEMPT ["man" secretly].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time peiod over which the attempts take place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which the Agent attempts the Goal.

fe.name: Particular iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is independent of the the attempt of the Agent to achieve the Goal.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The area of work to which the Attempt event belongs.
Ex: This is a market society where paid work is generally valued more than any ["Domain" domestic] ENDEAVOR.

frame.name: Compliance
frame.definition: This frame concerns Acts and State_of_Affairs for which Protagonists are responsible and which either follow or violate some set of rules or Norms.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist's behavior is in or out of compliance with norms. Ex: ["Protagonist" Jo] VIOLATED the no trespassing law.

fe.name: Act
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Act that is judged to be in or out of compliance with the Norms.
Ex: Jo's ["Act" VIOLATION] of the no trespassing law came as a surprise.

fe.name: State_of_Affairs
fe.definition: A State_of_Affairs may violate a law or rule. Ex: ["soa" Their pricing policy] VIOLATED inter-governmental agreements.

fe.name: Norm
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the rules or Norms that ought to guide a person's behavior.
Ex: John VIOLATED ["Norm" the law] by not paying taxes.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the compliance ocurrs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies any description of the Actor or Undergoer.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the compliance occurs. Ex: Jo COMPLIED with the law ["Manner" willingly].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the compliance is (ro is not) accomplished. Ex: He COMPLIED with the decree ["Mns" by firing the employees].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of compliance.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the act of compliance or non-compliance occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for complying with the Norm. Ex: He SUBMITTED to the will of the king ["Reason" because he had no other choice].

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

frame.name: Possession
frame.definition: An Owner has (or lacks) a Possession.

fe.name: Owner
fe.definition: The entity that owns a posession.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: State of the Owner or Possession.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Owner possesses the Possession.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Owner has a possession.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Owner has the Possession.

frame.name: Observable_bodyparts
frame.definition: This frame covers words for Body_part(s) (BP) belonging to a Possessor (Poss), which may be characterized by a Descriptor (Desc). The location of the BP may be identified in terms of its Attachment or its Orientational_Location. A Subregion of a BP may also be indicated. The constructions in which body part words occur include the following:

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_part.
Ex: ["Poss" Kim's] arm is broken.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_part. Note that Descriptor is not an FE of the same character as other FEs. Specifically, rather than filling a slot, it identifies a modifier of its head noun.
Ex: Kim has ["Desc" beautiful] EYES. Ex: His ["Desc" trembling] HANDS....

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: This Frame Element is the Body_part. Ex: Kim's ["Body_P" arm] is broken.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
This FEidentifies the Subregion of the Body_part referred to by the target.
Ex: ["Subr" upper] ARM Ex: ["Subr" lower] BACK

fe.name: Orientational_Location
fe.definition:
This Frame Element describes the location of the Body_part with respect to the inherent orientation of the body (or the larger body part) the Body_part is attached to.
Ex: ["OrLoc" left] LEG Ex: ["OrLoc" hind] FOOT Ex: ["OrLoc" second] FINGER Ex: ["OrLoc" front] WINGS
NB: All of these (other than very productive types such as "left", "right", "front", "back", and "second") should be tagged as secondary targets.

fe.name: Attachment
fe.definition: The Attachment is the larger body part to which the BP is attached. Ex: the FINGERS ["Attachment" of her left hand] Ex: the FIN ["Attachment" on its back] Ex: the ["Attachment" dorsal] FIN

lexunit.name: heel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the back part of the foot below the ankle.

lexunit.name: incisor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a narrow-edged tooth at the front of the mouth, adapted for cutting.

lexunit.name: jaw.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of the upper and lower bony structures in vertebrates forming the framework of the mouth and containing the teeth.

lexunit.name: toe.n
lexunit.definition: COD: any of the five digits at the end of the human foot

lexunit.name: hoof.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the horny part of the foot of an ungulate, especially a horse

lexunit.name: claw.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a curved, pointed horny nail on each digit of the foot in birds, lizards, and some mammals

lexunit.name: paw.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an animal's foot having claws and pads

lexunit.name: talon.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a claw, especially one belonging to a bird of prey

lexunit.name: wing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a modified forelimb or other appendage allowing a bird, bat, insect, or other creature to fly.

lexunit.name: pelt.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the skin of an animal with the fur, wool, or hair still on it.

lexunit.name: snout.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the projecting nose and mouth of an animal, esp. a mammal

lexunit.name: maw.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the jaws or throat, esp. of a voracious animal.

lexunit.name: fang.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a dangerous tooth, large and sharp and/or capable of delivering poison

lexunit.name: mane.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a growth of long hair on the neck of a horse, lion, or other animal

lexunit.name: whisker.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long projecting hair or bristle growing from the face or snout of an animal such as a cat

lexunit.name: feeler.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an animal organ such as an antenna that is used for testing things by touch or for searching for food

lexunit.name: antler.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a branched horn on the head of an adult deer

lexunit.name: muzzle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the projecting part of the face, including the nose and mouth, of an animal such as a dog or horse

lexunit.name: beak.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a bird's horny projecting jaws; a bill

lexunit.name: trunk.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the elongated, prehensile nose of an elephant

lexunit.name: tail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the hindmost part of an animal, especially when extended beyond the rest of the body, such as the flexible extension of the backbone in a vertebrate or the feathers at the hind end of a bird

lexunit.name: eye.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the organ of sight in humans or other animals

lexunit.name: foreleg.n
lexunit.definition: FN: each of the most anterior limbs used for locomotion or standing.

lexunit.name: forefoot.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of the front feet of a four-footed animal

lexunit.name: forepaw.n
lexunit.definition: FN: each of the frontmost paws of an animal

lexunit.name: limb.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an arm, leg, or wing

lexunit.name: fin.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a flattened appendage on the body of a fish or other aquatic animal, used for propelling, steering, and balancing

lexunit.name: flipper.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a broad, flat limb without fingers, used for swimming by sea animals such as seals, whales, and turtles

lexunit.name: horn.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a hard permanent outgrowth of bone encased in hardened skin, often curved and pointed, found in pairs on the heads of cattle, sheep, and other animals

lexunit.name: nape.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the back of a person's neck. NB: not always used of people

lexunit.name: nose.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part projecting above the mouth on a person or animal, containing the nostrils and used in breathing and smelling

lexunit.name: antenna.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long, thin sensory appendage found in pairs on the heads of insects and some other arthropods.

lexunit.name: fluke.n
lexunit.definition: COD: either of the lobes of a whale's tail

lexunit.name: skin.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a thin layer of tissue forming the natural outer covering of the body of a person or animal

lexunit.name: forelimb.n
lexunit.definition: FN: any of the frontmost limbs of a creature

lexunit.name: hindlimb.n
lexunit.definition: FN: any of the rearmost limbs of a creature.

lexunit.name: hindleg.n
lexunit.definition: FN: any of the hindmost legs of a creature

lexunit.name: fingertip.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the tip of the finger

lexunit.name: brow.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's forehead

lexunit.name: lip.n
lexunit.definition: COD: either of the two fleshy parts forming the edges of the mouth opening.

lexunit.name: temple.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the flat part either side of the head between the forehead and the ear.

lexunit.name: fingernail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the nail on the upper surface of the tip of each finger.

lexunit.name: tongue.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the fleshy muscular organ in the mouth, used for tasting, licking, swallowing, and (in humans) articulating speech

lexunit.name: toenail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a nail on the upper surface of the tip of each toe

lexunit.name: thumb.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the short, thick first digit of the hand, set lower and apart from the other four and opposable to them.

lexunit.name: nostril.n
lexunit.definition: COD: either of two external openings of the nasal cavity in vertebrates that admit air to the lungs and smells to the olfactory nerves.

lexunit.name: sole.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the underside of a person's foot.

lexunit.name: midriff.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the region of the front of the body between the chest and the waist

lexunit.name: navel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a rounded knotty depression in the center of a person's belly caused by the detachment of the umbilical cord after birth; the umbilicus

lexunit.name: neck.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part of a person's or animal's body connecting the head to the rest of the body.

lexunit.name: hindquarters.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the hind legs and adjoining parts of a quadruped.

lexunit.name: forefinger.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the finger next to the thumb.

lexunit.name: thigh.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the part of the leg between the hip and the knee.

lexunit.name: mouth.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the opening and cavity in the lower part of the face, surrounded by the lips, through which food and air are taken and vocal sounds are emitted

lexunit.name: tentacle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long slender flexible appendage of an animal, used for grasping or moving about, or bearing sense organs.

lexunit.name: bill.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a. the beak of a bird, especially when it is slender, flattened, or weak, or belongs to a web-footed bird or a bird of the pigeon family

lexunit.name: appendage.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a projecting part of an organism, with a distinct appearance or function

lexunit.name: thorax.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part of the body of any living being between the neck and the abdomen, including the cavity enclosed by the ribs, breastbone, and dorsal vertebrae.

lexunit.name: rump.n
lexunit.definition: FN: .the hind part of the body of a mammal, the lower back of a bird, or humourously a person's buttocks

lexunit.name: crown.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the top part of a person's head.

lexunit.name: member.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a man's penis

lexunit.name: leg.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of the limbs on which a person or animal walks and stands.

lexunit.name: shoulder.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the joint between the upper arm or forelimb and the main part of the body.

lexunit.name: tooth.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a hard structure in the mouth of some animals often used for chewing and other purposes

frame.name: Arraignment
frame.definition: At a court hearing, a Defendant is informed of the Charges against him or her, (usually) enters a plea, and a decision is made by a Judge as to the amount of bail, if any.

fe.name: Defendant
fe.definition: The Defendant is charged with a crime by a Judge. Ex: ["Defendant" Jan] was ARRAIGNED on eight counts of treason.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the arraignment occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the arraignment occurs.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The Judge is the head of the court where the arraignment occurs. Ex: Jan was ARRAIGNED on eight counts of treason ["Judge" before Duncan Smith].

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: Charges is the crime with which the Defendant is charged. Ex: Jan was ARRAIGNED ["Charges" on eight counts of treason].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time that the arraignment takes.
Ex: Just a ["Dur" short] little ARRAIGNMENT, and then you'll walk, alright?

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the arraignment which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (openly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Judge that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: Everyone 's always ["Manner" very carefully] ARRAIGNED before they meet trial, don't you worry none.

lexunit.name: arraign.v
lexunit.definition: COD: call before a court to answer a criminal charge

lexunit.name: arraignment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the calling of a defendant before a court to answer a criminal charge

frame.name: Bail_decision
frame.definition: This frame covers a step in a criminal process in which a Judge decides whether the Accused should be released on bail, and, if so, what the amount of the bail should be.

fe.name: Accused
fe.definition: At the time of bail setting, the Accused is held without bail/bond, released on his/her own recognizance, or required to give the Court a specific amount of money for bail. Ex: Judge Duncan FIXED ["Accused" the doctor's] bail at one million dollars.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The Judge, as head of the Court, determines the Accused's bail. Ex: ["Judge" Judge Duncan] FIXED the doctor's bail at one million dollars.

fe.name: Status
fe.definition: Status idenitifies the decision made with regard to bail. The possible statuses are "without bail/bond", "on one's own recognizance", or a specific amount of money required for bail. Ex: Judge Duncan FIXED the doctor's bail ["Status" at one million dollars].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the bail setting occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the bail setting occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the bail setting which is not covered by more specific FEs, including, secondary effects (openly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Judge that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The method used by the Judge to set the bail.
Ex: It used to be that a judge would SET bail ["Means" purely by guesswork].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which the Judge sets bail.

lexunit.name: set.v
lexunit.definition: FN: To determine an amount of money for bail

lexunit.name: fix.v
lexunit.definition: FN: To determine an amount of money for bail;

lexunit.name: order.v
lexunit.definition: FN: A judge's decision with regard to confinement or bail for a defendant.

lexunit.name: bail.n
lexunit.definition: FN: Money paid to a court to guarantee one's appearance in court.

lexunit.name: bond.n
lexunit.definition: FN: Money paid to guarantee one's performance of a duty; in this frame, to appear in court at the appropriate date.

frame.name: Kidnapping
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe situations in which a Perpetrator carries off and holds the Victim against his or her will by force.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: The Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) who carries off and holds the Victim against his or her will.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: The Victim is the person who is carried off and held against his/her will.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the kidnapping takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the kidnapping occurs.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source is the initial location of the Victim before it changes location.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is the place in which the Victim ends up.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner in which the kidnapping takes place.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Perpetrator that helps them accomplish the kidnapping.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose is what the Perpetrator hopes to accomplish by kidnapping.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is why the Perpetrator commits the kidnapping.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The abduction of a Victim by a Perpetrator.

fe.name: Co_abductee
fe.definition: An additional abductee taken along with the Victim. Ex: She was ABDUCTED ["CA" with her brother].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time for which the Victim is held by the Perpetrator
Ex: Two young man ABDUCTED her ["Duration" for about two hours]

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that the Victim is kidnapped.
Ex: The prelate was KIDNAPPED ["Frequency" twice] in the last two years

lexunit.name: kidnap.v
lexunit.definition: COD: abduct and hold captive, typically to obtain a ransom.

lexunit.name: abduct.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take (someone) away illegally by force or deception.

lexunit.name: shanghai.v
lexunit.definition: COD: force to join a ship's crew by underhand means.

lexunit.name: nab.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take or grab suddenly.

lexunit.name: snatch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: steal or kidnap by seizing suddenly.

lexunit.name: kidnapping.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of taking a person against their will, typically to obtain a ransom

lexunit.name: abduction.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action or condition of being taken away illegally by force or deception.

lexunit.name: kidnapper.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who abducts and holds (someone) captive, typically to obtain a ransom.

lexunit.name: abductor.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the person who is taking away (someone) illegally by force or decption.

lexunit.name: snatcher.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who steals or kidnaps by seizing suddenly.

lexunit.name: kidnapped.a
lexunit.definition: FN: abducted and held captive, typically for ransom.

lexunit.name: abducted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: taken away illegally by force or deception.

frame.name: Piracy
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe situations in which a Perpetrator forcibly seizes control over a Victim's Vehicle to gain some end.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: This is the person (or other agent) who forcibly seizes control over a vehicle to gain some end.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: This is the means of transportation which gets under the control of the perpetrator. Example: The terrorists hijacked ["Vehicle" the plane].

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: This FE describes the people that are suffering as a result of the Perpetrator's action. Ex: The rebels skyjacked a plane ["Victim" with 89 passangers].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The unlawful seizure of a Vehicle by a Perpetrator.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Perpetrator by which the seizure of the Vehicle is accomplished.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This is the place to which the vehicle is directed.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: This is the place from which the vehicle is taken away.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by piracy.
Ex: We have HIJACKED this plane ["Purpose" just to show how easy it is].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The situation that the Perpetrator had in mind which lead to the decision to perpetrate the particular act of piracy.
Ex: He CARJACKED the Lincoln Towncar instead ["Reason" because it looked ritzier].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An object that the Perpetrator uses in taking control of the Vehicle.
Ex: The plane was HIJACKED ["Instrument" with knives]

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that the VEHICLE is seized in acts of piracy.
Ex: The ferry that Kenneth was on was HIJACKED ["Frequency" twice] in three days

lexunit.name: hijack.v
lexunit.definition: COD: illegally seize control of (an aircraft, ship, or vehicle) while in transit.

lexunit.name: hijacking.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act or instance of being illegally seized (as an aircraft, ship, or vehicle) while in transit

lexunit.name: hijacker.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who illegally seizes control of (an aircraft, ship, or vehicle) while in transit

lexunit.name: carjacking.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of stealing a car after violently ejecting its driver.

lexunit.name: hijacked.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been illegally seized (as an aircraft, ship, or vehicle) while in transit

lexunit.name: piracy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the practice of attacking and robbing ships at sea, or a similar practice in other contexts, especially hijacking.

lexunit.name: pirate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rob or plunder (a ship).

lexunit.name: carjack.v
lexunit.definition: FN: steal someone's car while they are driving it.

frame.name: Activity
frame.definition:
This is an abstract frame for durative activities, in which the Agent enters an ongoing state of the Activity, remains in this state for some Duration of Time, and leaves this state either by finishing or by stopping. The Agent's Activity should be intentional.
This frame is intended mostly for the inheritance of common FEs, and to provide the frame structure for the beginning, ongoing, finish, or stop stage of an Activity, each of which constitutes a subframe of this frame. This frame should be compared to the Process frame.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Activity in which the Agent is engaged.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of Time an Activity takes.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Activity occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Activity occurs.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is engaged in the Activity.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the activity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

frame.name: Social_event
frame.definition:
A Host provides a venue for people to gather and conduct a social function or joint activity (often a party or celebration, in which case it is possible to express the idea that the Social_event is to honor someone (Honoree) or to celebrate an Occasion, at which Attendees are present).
Ex: ["Host" Sue] _threw_ a ["Soc" PARTY] ["Occasion" for Bob's birthday].
Ex: ["Host" Who] will HOST ["Soc" the Olympic games] ["Time" in eight years]?

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Social_event is ongoing.

fe.name: Social_event
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Social_event itself.
Ex: The department ["Soc" PICNIC] was lots of fun.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Social_event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Social_event occurs.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition:
The Host is the person or organization that hosts the Social_event. In cases where an individual stands in for an organization, the host may be marked twice.
Ex: ["Host" Ron] threw a PARTY. Ex: ["Host" President Reagan] hosted a ["Host" state] BANQUET. The FE Host is also used in ambiguous cases, such as: Ex: ["Host" church] ["Soc" PICNIC].

fe.name: Honoree
fe.definition:
The person for whom the Social_event is held.
Ex: I threw a PARTY ["Hon" for Josef].

fe.name: Occasion
fe.definition: The Occasion for which the Social_event is held.

fe.name: Attendee
fe.definition:
Attendee is used for the people who come to the Social_event.
Ex: ["Att" The whole group] attended the PARTY.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which Social_event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Social_event occurs.

fe.name: Refreshment
fe.definition:
Refreshment is used for the meal, food or drinks that are served at the Social_event.
Ex: I enjoy a tasteful ["Ref" dinner] PARTY. Ex: I attended a ["Ref" cocktail] PARTY and drank myself silly. Ex: First layer: I attended a ["Soc" BANQUET] on Saturday. Ex: Second layer: I attended a ["Ref" BANQUET] on Saturday.

fe.name: Style
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Style of the Social_event and its level of formality, indicating appropriate dress for participants and/or the kind of activities in which they engage.
Ex: Lee hosted a ["Style" formal] PARTY. Ex: Abby's ["Sty" garden] PARTY was successful.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: COD: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the social_event.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The Name of the Social_event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE describes how often the Social_event occurs.

lexunit.name: party.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a social gathering of invited guests, typically involving eating, drinking, and entertainment.

lexunit.name: host.v
lexunit.definition: COD: act as host (person who receives or entertains other people as guests) at (an event)

lexunit.name: banquet.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an elaborate and formal meal for many people.

lexunit.name: shindig.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large, lively party.

lexunit.name: fete.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a party

lexunit.name: celebration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an event honoring a special occasion

lexunit.name: social.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an informal social gathering organized by the members of a particular club or group.

lexunit.name: get-together.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a social gathering of individuals

lexunit.name: picnic.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a packed meal eaten outdoors, or an occasion when such a meal is eaten.

lexunit.name: fair.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a gathering of stalls and amusements for public entertainment.

lexunit.name: reception.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal social occasion held to welcome someone or celebrate an event.

lexunit.name: dance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a social gathering at which people dance.

lexunit.name: festival.n
lexunit.definition: COD: day or period of celebration or an organized series of concerts, films.

lexunit.name: feast.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large meal, especially a celebratory one. NB: certain religious days are called "feasts" - these are not social events.

lexunit.name: dinner.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal evening meal, typically one in honour of a person or event.

lexunit.name: dinner-party.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a social occasion at which guests eat dinner together.

lexunit.name: bash.n
lexunit.definition: COD: usu. with modifier a party or social event.

lexunit.name: gala.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a festive entertainment or performance

lexunit.name: jollification.n
lexunit.definition: COD: merrymaking.

lexunit.name: rave.n
lexunit.definition: COD: lively party involving dancing and drinking

lexunit.name: soiree.n
lexunit.definition: FN: party

lexunit.name: barbecue.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an outdoor meal or gathering at which meat, fish, or other food is grilled on a rack over an open fire.

lexunit.name: ball.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal social gathering for dancing.

lexunit.name: meeting.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an assembly of people for a particular purpose, especially for formal discussion.

frame.name: Hair_configuration
frame.definition:
Temporary or permanent Styles and Configurations of Hair, as well as its inherent Nature. Note that Attachment and Body Part will generally be incorporated in the lexical meanings. Subregions (eg roots, ends) are often not specified, and sometimes incorporated (eg in 'bangs')
Ex: On either side her head gleamed ["Configuration" coiled] ["Configuration" BRAIDS] ["Hair" of dark-gold hair] , almost pale copper in the subdued light of the room .

fe.name: Hair
fe.definition: This FE is the hair itself Ex: Her ["Hair" TRESSES] were golden.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition: This FE is the Possessor of the body part. Ex: ["Possessor" Michael's] HAIR is long.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: A subregion of the body part referred to by the target, e.g. Ex: Her HAIR is dark ["Subregion" at the roots]

fe.name: Configuration
fe.definition: Temporary Configurations of hair (eg braid, bun, ponytail). Something done to the hair merely by movement. Ex: I pulled Michael's ["Configuration" ponytail].

fe.name: Hair_Property
fe.definition: A property of the hair (eg curly, fine, brown). This acts much like "Descriptor" in the Observable_bodyparts Frame. Colors, styles, natural properties are described by this frame element.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: Where the salient part of the hair is. Ex: His HAIR was ["Location" in his eyes].

fe.name: Accessory
fe.definition: Items that are put in the hair as part of a Configuration or Style Ex: She braided ["Acc" ribbons] into her hair.

lexunit.name: lock.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a) a piece of a person's hair that coils or hangs together. b) locks chiefly poetic/literary a person's hair.

lexunit.name: tress.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long lock of a woman's hair

lexunit.name: curl.n
lexunit.definition: COD: something in the shape of a spiral or coil, especially a lock of hair.

lexunit.name: curl.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form or cause to form a curved or spiral shape.

lexunit.name: blond.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of hair) fair or pale yellow. Having fair hair and a pale complexion. Usually pertaining to males.

lexunit.name: blonde.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of hair) fair or pale yellow. having fair hair and a light complexion.

lexunit.name: pigtail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a plaited lock of hair worn singly at the back or on each side of the head.

lexunit.name: curly.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of hair): the characteristic of locks to naturally twist into ringlets

lexunit.name: ponytail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a hairstyle in which the hair is drawn back and tied at the back of the head.

lexunit.name: plait.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a single length of hair, rope or other material made up of three or more interlaced strands.

lexunit.name: braid.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a length of hair made up of three or more interlaced strands.

lexunit.name: braided.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of having the configuration of a braid.

lexunit.name: topknot.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a knot of hair arranged on the top of the head.

lexunit.name: wavy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having or consisting of a series of wave-like curves.

lexunit.name: wave.n
lexunit.definition: COD: A slightly curling lock of hair. a tendency to curl in a person's hair.

lexunit.name: hairdo.n
lexunit.definition: COD: (informal) the style of a woman's hair.

lexunit.name: golden.a

frame.name: Rape
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe situations in which the Perpetrator has sexual intercourse with the Victim forcibly (or by threatening the use of force) and without his or her consent.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: This is the person who forces another person to have sexual intercourse with him or her against the other person's will.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: This is the person who is forced to engage in sexual intercourse against his or her will.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The rape of a Victim by the Perpetrator.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Perpetrator by which the sexual crime is accomplished.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the event occurs.
Ex: The lawyer said the woman was RAPED ["Time" on a night of madness]

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE is any object used to commit the crime.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that a rape event takes place.
Ex: The eleven year old told the court that she was RAPED ["Frequency" three times]

lexunit.name: rape.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a man) force (another person) to have sexual intercourse with him against their will.

lexunit.name: rape.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act or the crime of raping someone.

lexunit.name: rapist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a man who commits rape.

lexunit.name: raped.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been forced (by a man) to have sexual intercourse with (him)

lexunit.name: sexually assault.v
lexunit.definition: FN: force (another person) to have sexual intercourse with against their will.

frame.name: Type
frame.definition:
This frame has to do with nouns denoting types of entities. The Subtype refers to a collection of members of a more general Category which have certain defining characteristics; alternatively, the Subtype refers only to the type itself, i.e. a more restrictive set of characteristics than those of the more general Category. The properties of the items that are included in the collection may be specified by the Item_Property. Sometimes the Subtypes themselves are described by some Type_Property.
Ex: I don't like this ["Type_Property" newfangled] ["Subtype" KIND] ["Category" of fish]. Ex: Kleo isn't ["Item_Property" our] ["Subtype" SORT] ["Category" of people]. Ex: He argued against the ["Item_Property" formalist] ["Subtype" TYPE] ["Category" of analysis of art]. Ex: I think that she was referring to the other ["Subtype" TYPE]. ["Category" DNI]

fe.name: Subtype
fe.definition: The entity which denotes a subtype of the more general Category. Ex: I don't like this ["Subtype" KIND] of fish.

fe.name: Category
fe.definition:
The more general type that the target denotes a subtype of. This FE is obligatory and should be labeled DNI when not present.
Ex: They created a new BREED ["Category" of dog].

fe.name: Type_Property
fe.definition:
A property of the Subtype itself rather than the members of the Category.
Ex: I tried a ["Type_Property" new] TYPE of hair gel yesterday.
Many Type_Property adjectives (e.g. new, rare, traditional, modern, strange) make explicit that the type under discussion is just one of the types in the more general Category. Adjectives that denote properties of items in the category should be tagged Item_Property.

fe.name: Item_Property
fe.definition:
A property of the members of the Category that helps identify (directly or indirectly) the particular set of members that are referred to by the Subtype.
Ex: He had a ["Item_Property" Bon Jovi] KIND of guitar.

lexunit.name: ilk.n

frame.name: Notification_of_charges
frame.definition: The judge or other court officer (the Authority) informs the Accused of the Charges against him/her, i.e. the alleged actions and the relevant laws.

fe.name: Arraign_authority
fe.definition: The judge or other authority of the court in which the accused person is arraigned.

fe.name: Accused
fe.definition: The person being charged with an offense against the law.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: The crime with which the Accused is charged

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: The larger event which contains the Notification of Charges event. Ex: Seven people have been INDICTED ["CE" in the seven-year investigation].

lexunit.name: charge.n

lexunit.name: accuse.v

frame.name: Entering_of_plea
frame.definition: The Accused enters a Plea in answer to the Charges. In most jurisdictions, the possible pleas are innocent, guilty, or nolo contendere. Accused persons may stand mute, in which case, the court usually enters a plea on their behalf.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The judge of the court in which the accused enters a plea.

fe.name: Accused
fe.definition: The person entering the plea in court. Ex: ["Accused" Joy Peterson] PLEADED ["Plea" innocent] ["Charges" to the murder of his son].

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: The crime with which the Accused is charged Ex: ["Accused" Simpson] PLEADED ["Plea" not guilty] ["Charges" to the murder of his wife].

fe.name: Plea
fe.definition: The Plea that a defendant makes. Ex: ["Accused" The student] PLEADED ["Plea" guilty]["Charges" to stealing a bike].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Court
fe.definition: The Court is the institution before which the plea is entered.

lexunit.name: plead.v

lexunit.name: plea.n

frame.name: Light_movement
frame.definition: An Emitter emits a Beam of light from a Source, along a Path, and/or towards a Goal. Essentially, this frame denotes the (semi-)fictive motion of the the Beam. Ex: Avoid allowing ["Beam" light] to SHINE ["Goal" into neighbors' gardens]. Ex: ["Beam" Clear yellow sunlight] SHONE ["Path" through the window-panes]. Ex: She thinks ["Emit" the sun] SHINES ["Src" out of his backside]. Ex: ...when ["Emit" the candles] SHINE ["Src" out]. Ex: ["Beam" It] SHINES ["Goal" in my eyes]. ('It' is both Beam and Emitter, though only one will show up in the display.) Ex: ...["Beam" light] SHINES ["Path" down] ["Goal" on the world]. Ex: ["Beam" The moonlight] SHONE ["Path" off the fields]. Ex: ["Beam" The candlelight] GLINTED ["Src" from pearls and rubies].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the light movement occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the external argument. Ex: Their swords GLOWED ["Depictive" red] in the setting sun.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Emitter
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity at the Source from which the Beam originates.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location the Beam occupies initially before its change of location.

fe.name: Beam
fe.definition: The light that travels from a Source along a Path to a Goal. Ex: ["Beam" Sunlight] GLEAMED from the water of the bay. Ex: ["Beam" Lamplight] FLICKERED through the foggy air.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path refers to where the Beam travels over or to a landmark the Beam travels by.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is the location the Beam ends up in.

frame.name: Instance
frame.definition:
This frame concerns transparent nouns that denote Instances of Types of entities or events.
Ex: The survey confirmed that management interference in team operations had increased , and ["Instance" INSTANCES] ["Type" of management decisions being taken without team consultation] had also increased .

fe.name: Place

fe.name: Time

fe.name: Initial_subevent

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

fe.name: Manner

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of the Event.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time for which the Process is ongoing after it has started.
Ex: In three instances, violence ERUPTED ["Duration" for brief periods].

The number of times that the specified type of Event begins.
Ex: Clashes BROKE OUT ["Frequency" twice] because Kenneth had been arrested.

frame.name: Clothing
frame.definition:
This frame refers to clothing and its characteristics, including anything that people conventionally wear. The Wearer wears a Garment that has a certain Style, is made of a certain Material, and can be otherwise characterized by a Descriptor. In some cases, the Body_location (where the garment is worn) and Subregion of the clothing may also be specified.
Ex: Claudia dressed in a ["Descriptor" dark] ["Descriptor" green] ["Material" cotton] DRESS clasped round her slender waist with a broad yellow belt , drank a cup of coffee and opened her neglected post .

fe.name: Garment
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the clothing worn.
Ex: Mike wore a new leather ["Garment" jacket].

fe.name: Wearer
fe.definition:
The Wearer is the person wearing the clothes, or for whom the clothes are intended.
Ex: ["Wearer" Mike] wore a new leather jacket.

fe.name: Style
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the design, or cut, of the clothing.
Ex: Mike wore a ["Style" tailored] leather JACKET.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the material from which the clothing is made.
Ex: Mike wore a new ["Material" leather] jacket.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE identifes any description of the clothing besides Style and Material. Ex: Mike wore a ["Descriptor" new] ["Descriptor" black] leather JACKET. Note that each modifer of the target gets its own FE (and, hence, its own GF and PT).

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
This FE identifies a part of the clothing.
Ex: Mike wore a leather jacket ["Subregion" with fringes].

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the Use for which a Garment is worn or was made.
Ex: Mike wore a new ["Use" riding] jacket.

fe.name: Body_location
fe.definition:
Body_location identifies the place on the body where the clothing is worn.
Ex: Hannah draped a shawl elegantly ["Body_loc" over her shoulders].

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
The individual who created the Garment.
Ex: She 's wearing a ["cre" Ralph Lauren] DRESS.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which the Creator makes the Garment.
Ex: The BIKINIS ["tim" of the 1940's] are fairly similar.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The name given to a specific Garment. Note this is not the name of a general class of clothing items, but rather an individual item. This is accordingly VERY RARE.
Ex:
