frame.name: Memory
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with Cognizers remembering and forgetting mental Content.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizeris the person whose mental Content is at issue.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The Content is the mental content that a Cognizer retains or forgets.
Ex: Each student must be able to RECALL ["Content" the whole paragraph] .

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the subject the Cognizer mental Content is about.
Ex: ["Cognizer" John] FORGOT ["Content" everything] ["Topic" about his uncle].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Cognizer manages to remember or forget the Content.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result represents the consequences of the remembering or forgetting of the mental Content.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration is the amount of time for which the mental Content is remembered or forgotten.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the remembering or forgetting takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the remembering or forgetting occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the remembering or forgetting of mental Content occurs.

fe.name: Experience
fe.definition: An event (or period of time standing in for events) that the Cognizer has experienced that leads to the Cognizer remembering the Content. Ex: Then I REMEMBERED ["Exp" from our summer together] that he frowned on smoking.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The situation which surrounds a Cognizer remembering a Content or Topic.
Ex: ["cir" With the lights off], people can REMEMBER better.

lexunit.definition: COD: fail to remember

lexunit.definition: COD: something remembered

lexunit.definition: FN: bring back to mind

lexunit.definition: FN: bring back to the level of conscious awareness

lexunit.definition: COD: the action or faculty of remembering

lexunit.definition: COD: keep in one's memory

lexunit.definition: FN: remember, remind oneself

frame.name: Expertise
frame.definition: This frame concerns people's knowledge or skill in certain domains. It does not concern acquaintance or familiarity with people. With adjectives as targets in this frame, we annotate on two FE layers. Ex: FE Layer-1: He is an EXPERIENCED ["Prot" programmer]. Ex: FE Layer-2: He is an EXPERIENCED ["Skill" programmer].

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The person whose expertise is assessed.

fe.name: Skill
fe.definition: Skill identifies the Protagonist's talent or ability to do things with one's hand or body.

fe.name: Knowledge
fe.definition: The area of knowledge (as opposed to a practical skill) in which the Protagonist 's experience is assessed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Behavior_product
fe.definition:
A product of behavior that shows the Protagonist's skill or lack of skill.
Ex: A SKILLFUL ["Behavior_product" advertising campaign] persuaded voters that his opponent was soft on crime.

fe.name: Focal_participant
fe.definition:
This frame element can only occur in place of a skill expression. It refers to the prototypical patient in an action involving the Protagonist. For instance, in the following sentence the children are experts at some (contextually given) action such as rolling the hoops.
["Protagonist" Some children] _were_ ["Degree" quite] EXPERT ["Focal_participant" with wooden hoops].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
This frame element denotes a role in which the protagonist has developed his expertise.
Ex: ["Protagonist" His] PROWESS ["Role" as a surgeon] is impressive.
In many cases, the Role noun secondarily evokes the Skill that is at issue.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner give further description of the way in which the Protagonist exhibits their skill or lack of skill.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Protagonist has the expertise.

frame.name: Arson
frame.definition: A Perpetrator intentionally sets fire to his own or someone else's property, often in order to collect an insurance payment on this property.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase that describes the actor of an action.

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition: The illegal setting of fire to destroy something.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an action is performed.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which arson is committed.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish with the arson Event.
Ex: ARSON ["Purp" for insurance fraud] is quite common.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time that a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the arson occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the arson occurs.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: The Perpetrator sets fire to a building in order to gain some benefit from so doing. Ex: ["Perpetrator" The two men] were charged with ARSON when found running from the burning factory.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: Victim identifies the enity that is negatively effected by the arson. Ex: There has been an increase in the number of ARSON attacks ["Victim" on local schools].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The frequency with which an act of arson is committed.
Ex: The churches were plagued with ["Freq" frequent] ARSON.

lexunit.name: arson.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

lexunit.name: arsonist.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the criminal who deliberately set things on fire

frame.name: Giving
frame.definition: A Donor transfers a Theme from a Donorto a Recipient. This frame includes only actions that are initiated by the Donor (the one that starts out owning the Theme). Sentences (even metaphorical ones) must meet the following entailments: the Donor first has possession of the Theme. Following the transfer the Donor no longer has the Theme and the Recipient does. Ex: ["Donor" Barney] GAVE ["Theme" the beer] ["Recipient" to Moe]. Ex: ["Theme" $300] was ENDOWED ["Recipient" to the university].["Purpose" to build a new performing arts building].

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person that begins in possession of the Themeand causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The object that changes ownership.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the manner in which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Theme is given. Ex: ["Donor" I] GIVE ["Theme" my services] ["Circumstances" free of charge].

fe.name: Purpose_of_theme
fe.definition: The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme. Ex: Please GIVE this list to the secretary ["pot" for entry into the client database].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A description of the Donor, Recipient, or Theme given independently of the giving event per se.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

frame.name: Part_whole
frame.definition:
This frame is concerned with nouns denoting a part or parts of a Whole entity . The Part is not defined relative to the Whole's orientation, center, or edge and is not ordered. We also annotate properties of the Part, e.g. relating to its size.
Ex: Kim forgot a ["Part_Prop" large] ["Part" PART] ["Whole" of the story].
Ex: Abby ate only the ["Orientation" top] ["Part" HALF] ["Whole" of the cake].

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: A Part of a larger Whole.Ex: Sergey had ["Part" HALF] of the pizza for breakfast.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: An undivided entity having all its Parts. Ex: Sergey had HALF ["Whole" of the pizza] for breakfast.

fe.name: Part_Prop
fe.definition: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.Ex: Sue painted a ["Part_Prop" big] ["Part" SECTION] ["Whole" of the room].

fe.name: Orientation
fe.definition:
This is a property of the Part that determines the portion of the Part.
Ex: Abby ate only the ["Orientation" top] ["Part" HALF] ["Whole" of the cake] .

lexunit.name: part.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a piece or segment of something which combined with others makes up the whole.

lexunit.name: fragment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a small part broken off or detached.

lexunit.name: half.n
lexunit.definition: COD: either of two equal or corresponding parts into which something is or can be divided.

lexunit.name: segment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of the parts into which something is or may be divided

lexunit.name: section.n
lexunit.definition: COD: any of the more or less distinct parts into which something is or may be divided or from which it is made up.

lexunit.name: eighth.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one of eight parts.

lexunit.name: fifth.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one of five parts.

lexunit.name: hundredth.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one of one hundred parts.

lexunit.name: third.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one of three parts.

lexunit.name: quarter.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one of four parts.

lexunit.name: tenth.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one of ten parts.

lexunit.name: portion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a part or a share.

frame.name: Certainty
frame.definition:
This frame concerns a Cognizer's certainty about the correctness of beliefs or expectations. It only includes uses where a Cognizer is expressed.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Lermontov] _was_ CERTAIN ["Content" he would come to the party].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the person whose certainty or uncertainty is at issue.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Marcel] _was_ SURE that she had seen Eldridge on the balcony.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer has a certain/uncertain belief about.
Ex: She talked of quests , of finding this absurd religious character , but he _was_ UNSURE ["Topic" of her conviction]. Ex: I '_m_ DUBIOUS ["Topic" about this Mafia story].

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.
Ex: I _am_ SURE ["Content" that we'll arrive on time].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the Degree to which the Cognizer is certain or uncertain.
Ex: Charles felt ["Degr" fairly] CONFIDENT of her safety for the time being.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The FE Manner denotes the manner of the certainty or uncertainty.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the mental state of the Cognizer.
Ex: She caught sight of her mother's DUBIOUS ["Exr" expression].
Notice that we do NOT tag possessives such as 'her mother's' or 'on her face' that occur within the noun phrase of which the target adjective is a part. In sentences such as
Ex: She had a DUBIOUS ["Exr" look] on her face.
NOTE: We do NOT tag 'have' and its subject since the governor relationship is between the verb 'have' and the noun that the target adjective modifies rather than between the target adjective and the verb 'have'.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Cognizer is certain.

lexunit.definition: COD: not completely confident or sure

frame.name: Part_piece
frame.definition:
This frame is concerned with transparent nouns denoting a Piece of a Substance. Also present is Piece_prop which is a property of the Piece, e.g. relating to its size.
Ex: Kim ate a ["Piece_prop" tiny] ["Piece" MORSEL] ["Substance" of cake ].

fe.name: Piece
fe.definition: A Piece made of a substance.Ex: Sergey had a few ["Piece" MORSELS] ["Substance" of bread] for breakfast. The specific whole entity from which the Piece comes is not specified. Thus, the following sentence is not in frame: _A piece of the TV fell of the floor._

fe.name: Piece_prop
fe.definition: A property relating to the Piece.Ex: Sue had a ["Piece_prop" big] ["Piece" PIECE] ["Substance" of cake].

fe.name: Substance
fe.definition: The Substance is what the Piece is made of and may describe the type of larger whole from which it came.Ex: Sue ate a ["Piece_prop" big] ["Piece" PIECE] ["Substance" of cake].

frame.name: Part_orientational
frame.definition:
In this frame, there is a Part of a Whole in which the Part is defined with respect to the canonical or inherent orientation of the Whole. In cases where the TARGET is an adjective, it has a special relationship with the noun that it modifies such that a phrase which is a syntactic argument of the noun is semantically available to fill the argument structure of the adjective, as in
Ex: the FRONT ["Part" row] ["Whole" of the class]
Ex: The TOP ["Part" shelf] ["Whole" of the bookcase] was lying on the floor.
Ex: The ["Part" BOTTOM] was missing.
Ex: ["Whole" My] LEFT ["Part" hand] was numb.
Ex: He rested on the ["Whole" cliff]["Part" TOP]

fe.name: Part

fe.name: Part_Prop
fe.definition: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.Ex: The ["Part_Prop" white-painted] ["Part" FRONT] ["Whole" of the house] had 2 black doors.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: An undivided entity having all its Parts.Ex: The show takes place in the WEST ["Part" wing] ["Whole" of the White House].

frame.name: Process_stop
frame.definition: A Process stops at a certain Time and Place. Reason may also be specified. A Duration may be included in order to indicate the length of the persistence of the Paused-state before action resumes. NB: Refer to Process frame.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The Process which is halting.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Cause of an event occur.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of an event.

fe.name: Last_subevent
fe.definition:
The Last_subevent of an event.
Ex: The peace march STOPPED ["Last" with a prayer].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that a process remains stopped.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that the Process stops.,
Ex: Mining activities on the opal fields CEASED ["Frequency" twice] in the last two weeks due to heavy rain storms

fe.name: Depictive

fe.name: Manner

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time over which the Event is ongoing.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: Name of the Event which is continuing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Event occurs.

fe.name: Next_subevent

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

frame.name: Activity_start
frame.definition: An Agent initiates the beginning of an ongoing Activity in which he will be continuously involved.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent starts an Activity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent engages in a starting Activity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent starts an Activity.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent starts an Activity.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent starts an Activity.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Activity that an Agent starts.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: This FE identifies the being that starts the intentional Activity.

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition: This FE identifies the first Subevent of the started Activity.Ex: The peace march STARTED ["Sub" with a prayer].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases. I

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition: A consecutive event to the starting of the Activity of the Agent.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modifies the target to indicate the legal- or other domain within which it is true or operational.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

frame.name: Measure_mass
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with nouns that denote Units of measurement for masses. The Frame Elements are Unit, Count, and Stuff.Ex: Jelena bought ["Count" three] ["Unit" KILOS] ["Stuff" of apples].Ex: Add ["Count" a] ["Unit" POUND] ["Stuff" of sugar].

fe.name: Count

fe.name: Unit

fe.definition: The Stuff whose weight is being measured.Ex: Sue bought ["Count" three] ["Unit" KILOS] ["Stuff" of cat food] on sale.

lexunit.name: metric ton.n

frame.name: Process_resume
frame.definition: An event resumes at a certain Place and Time. NB: Refer to Event frame.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of Time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The Process which is being resumed.Ex: ["Process" The meeting] RESUMED after the bomb threat passed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that the Process resumes.
Ex: The tenth emergency special session RESUMED ["Frequency" twice more] to address ongoing violations against the security council resolution

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: Trading resumed ["Manner" in an orderly fashion] on Monday

lexunit.name: resume.v
lexunit.definition: COD: begin again or continue after a pause or interruption. NB: The action is not usually resumed at the beginning with this verb, but rather at the point in the Ongoing process where it was interrupted.

frame.name: State
frame.definition: An Entity persists in a stable situation called a State

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Concrete or abstract entity

fe.name: State
fe.definition: State of an Entity.

frame.name: Process_initial_state
frame.definition: The initial State of an Entity in an event; part of the Event X-schema. NB: Refer to Event frame.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The overall process which is about to begin.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The point at which the Process begins.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Process remains ready to begin.

frame.name: Process_stopped_state
frame.definition: The State of an Entity after an Event has stopped, i.e. part of an X-schema. NB: Refer to Event frame.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The overall event which is stopped.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The point at which the Process is not continuing.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Process does not resume.

frame.name: Measure_linear_extent
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with nouns that denote Units of measurement for linear extent. The Frame Elements are Unit, Count, and Stuff.Ex: The shirt is made from ["Count" 12] ["Unit" MILES] ["Stuff" of pure cotton].Ex: ["Count" 81] ["Unit" MILES] ["Stuff" of dyke] are still visible from this point.

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units of the linear extent.Ex: ["Count" Five] ["Unit" MILES] ["Stuff" of pipework] were necessary.

fe.name: Stuff
fe.definition: The Stuff whose linear extent is being measured.Ex: ["Unit" MILES] ["Stuff" of wiring] were necessary.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities of the same kind are measured.Ex: ["Unit" MILES] ["Stuff" of telephone cables] had to be replaced.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition: This FE marks constituents which express what property is being measured.

lexunit.name: inch.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of linear measure equal to one twelfth of a foot (2.54 cm)

lexunit.name: mile.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of linear measure equal to 1,760 yards (approximately 1.609 kilometres).

lexunit.name: yard.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of linear measure equal to 3 feet (0.9144 metre).

lexunit.name: foot.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of linear measure equal to 12 inches (30.48 cm).

lexunit.name: meter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the fundamental unit of length in the metric system, equal to 100 centimetres (approx. 39.37 inches).

lexunit.name: kilometer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a metric unit of measurement equal to 1,000 metres (approximately 0.62 miles).

lexunit.name: centimeter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a metric unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre

lexunit.name: millimeter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: one thousandth of a metre (0.039 in.)

lexunit.name: furlong.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an eighth of a mile, 220 yards.

lexunit.name: light-year.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of distance equivalent to the distance that light travels in one year, 9.4607E12 km (nearly 6 million million miles).

lexunit.name: block.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one city street length

frame.name: Measure_volume
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with nouns that denote Units of measurement for volumes. The Frame Elements are Unit, Count, Stuff, and Size. The frame will be split soon into container-derived volumes (box, bottle etc.) and pure volumes (gallon, quart). For the moment we tag things as follows: Ex: Greg drank ["Count" two] ["Size" 2 liter] ["Unit" BOTTLES] ["Stuff" of lemonade]. Ex: Sue drank ["Count" two] ["Unit" LITERS] ["Stuff" of beer]. This frame necessitated the introduction of the GF: Quant and the PT: Num used for expressions such as the following: Ex: two CUPS of coffee _FE: , GF: Quant, PT: Num_Ex: Note that we treat cardinal numbers and "a" (= 1) in the same way. Ex: a CUP of coffee _FE: , GF: Quant, PT: Num_Ex: For the present, we prefer not to annotate "many cups of coffee" Ex: many CUPS of coffee _FE: , GF: Quant, PT: Adj_Ex:

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units of the measured volume.Ex: Serena found ["Count" two] ["Unit" CUPS] ["Stuff" of sugar] in the freezer.

fe.name: Stuff
fe.definition: The Stuff whose volume is being measured.Ex: Sue bought ["Count" three] ["Unit" BOTTLES] ["Stuff" of milk] on sale.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities of the same kind are measured.Ex: Drink ["Count" two] ["Unit" GLASSES] ["Stuff" of wine] every day.

fe.name: Size
fe.definition: A specification of the volume of the container.Ex: Michell bought ["Count" a] ["Size" 2 liter] ["Unit" BOTTLE] ["Stuff" of Sangria].

lexunit.name: pint.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of liquid or dry capacity equal to one eighth of a gallon, in Britain equal to 0.568 litre and in the US equal to 0.473 litre (for liquid measure) or 0.551 litre (for dry measure).

lexunit.name: cup.n
lexunit.definition: COD: chiefly N. Amer. a measure of capacity used in cookery, equal to half a US pint (0.237 litre)

lexunit.name: bottle.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume of a container with a narrow neck, used for storing liquids

lexunit.name: bushel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a measure of capacity equal to 8 gallons (equivalent to 36.4 litre), or in the US a measure of capacity equal to 64 US pints (equivalent to 35.2 litres).

lexunit.name: box.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume of a container with a flat base and sides

lexunit.name: glass.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained in a drinking container made of glass

lexunit.name: gallon.n
lexunit.definition: COD: unit of volume for liquid measure equal to eight pints: in Britain also imperial gallon, equivalent to 4.55 litres; in the US, equivalent to 3.79 litres.

lexunit.name: barrel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a measure of capacity for oil and beer, equal to 36 imperial gallons for beer and 35 imperial gallons or 42 US gallons (roughly 192 litres) for oil

lexunit.name: pack.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cardboard or paper container and the items contained within it

lexunit.name: bowl.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained by a round, deep dish or basin

lexunit.name: teaspoon.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the amount held by a teaspoon, in the UK considered to be 5 millilitres when used as a measurement in cookery

lexunit.name: jug.n
lexunit.definition: FN: volume contained by a large container for liquids, with a narrow mouth

lexunit.name: spoon.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume or amount held by an implement consisting of a small, shallow oval or round bowl on a long handle, used for eating, stirring, and serving food

lexunit.name: tablespoon.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the amount held by a tablespoon, in the UK considered to be 15 millilitres when used as a measurement in cookery

lexunit.name: bag.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained by a flexible container with an opening at the top

lexunit.name: quart.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of liquid capacity equal to a quarter of a gallon or two pints, equivalent in Britain to approximately 1.13 litres and in US to approximately 0.94 litre.

lexunit.name: spoonful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained in a spoon

lexunit.name: teaspoonful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained in a teaspoon

lexunit.name: bagful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained by a bag

lexunit.name: boxful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained by a box

lexunit.name: bucketful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained by a bucket

lexunit.name: tankful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained by a tank

lexunit.name: sackful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume or amount contained by a sack

lexunit.name: packet.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the amount contained in a paper or cardboard container

lexunit.name: mug.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the amount of contents of a large cup, typically cylindrical and with a handle and used without a saucer

lexunit.name: scoop.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume or amount contained in a utensil resembling a spoon, having a short handle and a deep bowl, used for extracting liquids or substances from a container

lexunit.name: scoopful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained in a scoop

lexunit.name: platter.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a selection of food placed on a platter

lexunit.name: tray.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the contents of a flat, shallow container with a raised rim, typically used for carrying or holding.

lexunit.name: busload.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a load that fills a bus

lexunit.name: planeload.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a load that fills a plane

lexunit.name: truckload.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a load that fills a truck

lexunit.name: carload.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a load that fills a car

lexunit.name: roomful.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume or amount a room will hold

lexunit.name: trainload.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the size of load that fills a train

lexunit.name: boatload.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a load that fills a boat.

lexunit.name: litre.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a metric unit of capacity, formerly the volume of one kilogram of water under standard conditions, now equal to 1,000 cubic centimetres (about 1.75 pints)

lexunit.name: can.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the volume contained in a can

frame.name: Measure_area
frame.definition: This transparent noun frame is concerned with Units for measuring the Area of regions.Ex: Hillary lives in the middle of ["Count" 10] ["Unit" ACRES] ["Occupant" of wheat].Ex: Paul owns ["Count" 20] ["Unit" HECTARES] ["Area" of land].

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The Unit of measurement.Ex: Apollo grows ["Count" 34] ["Unit" ACRES] ["Occupant" of strawberries].Ex: Otto owns ["Count" 43] ["Unit" HECTARES] ["Area" of land].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The region whose surface is being measured. Ex: Klaas has a 10 ACRE peach ["Area" orchard]

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units.Ex: Smiley owns ["Count" fifteen] ["Unit" HECTARES] ["Area" of prime real estate].

fe.name: Occupant
fe.definition: Things that occupy the Area that is being measured.Ex: Swanson grows ["Count" 1,000] ["Unit" ACRES] ["Occupant" of vegetables].

lexunit.name: hectare.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a metric unit of square measure, equal to 10,000 square metres (2.471 acres)

lexunit.name: acre.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a unit of land area equal to 4,840 square yards (0.405 hectare)

frame.name: Body_description_holistic
frame.definition:
This frame covers descriptions of an entire human body, viewed as a gestalt (as opposed to descriptions based on salient body parts). The Frame Elements are Individual and Figure.
Ex: ["Ind" Chuck] _is_ MUSCULAR.
Ex: ["Ind" Chuck] has a MUSCULAR body.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which a body has a particular characteristic. Ex: Chuck is ["Degree" rather] MUSCULAR.

fe.name: Individual
fe.definition: This FE identifies the individual (or individuals) being described. Ex: ["Ind" Chuck] _is_ MUSCULAR. Ex: ["Ind" Chuck] has a MUSCULAR body.

fe.name: Figure
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target. Ex: Chuck has a MUSCULAR ["Figure" body].

frame.name: Accoutrements
frame.definition: A Wearer wears accessories, which are made of some Material and may have a Style. Most of the accessories are non-essential (clothing) items. Ex: ["Wearer" She] wore ["Descriptor" a black] ["Material" velvet] HAT ["Body_location" on her head].

fe.name: Wearer
fe.definition: The Wearer wears the Accoutrement. Ex: Why must you always wear ["Wearer" your] HELMET when I'm driving?

fe.name: Style
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Style of the Accoutrement. Ex: He wore ["Style" a Jacobean] WIG.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Material from which the Accoutrement is made.Ex: He wore a ["Material" gold] WATCH.

fe.name: Accoutrement
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Accoutrement. Ex: She wore a ["Acout" tiara].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Accoutrement. Ex: Kim wore ["Desc" an exquisite] TIARA.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Accoutrement is worn or made.
Ex: She was wearing ["Use" reading] GLASSES.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: This FE identifies a part of the Accoutrement. Ex: He bought a leather CAP ["Part" with sheepskin flaps].

fe.name: Body_location
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place on the body where a particular Accoutrement is located. Ex: Tess wore a single RING ["Body_loc" in her left nostril].

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
The individual or group who created the Accoutrement.
Ex: We found this ["cre" Chinese] ANKLET two layers below Tel-Wilaya 3. Ex: ["cre" De Beers] JEWELRY is justly famous.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which the Accoutrement was created.
Ex: What was a ["tim" 17th century] BROOCH doing in her attic?

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
A name given to an individual Accoutrement to distinguish it from all other objects.
Ex: The RING ["nam" Narya] was passed to Gandalf.

frame.name: Grooming
frame.definition: In this frame, an Agent engages in personal body care. An Instrument can be used in this process as well as a Medium.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The agent is the person who does the grooming. Ex: ["Agent" She] washed the baby

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The patient is the person who gets washed. Ex: She washed ["Patient" the baby].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This is an object that aids the washing process. Ex: She scrubbed her hands ["Instrument" with soap].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: This is the region of the body that gets groomed. Ex: She scrubbed ["Body_part" her hands] with soap.

fe.name: Sub_region
fe.definition: This is a region of the object, body or the body part that gets groomed. Ex: I washed ["Sub_region" from the waist up].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the substance that is the grooming agent. Bobby WASHED his hair ["Medium" with shampoo].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The frequency with which the Agent groom himself/other.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally acts.

fe.name: Time

frame.name: Wearing
frame.definition:
The words in this frame refer to what Clothing the Wearer (or a specific Body_part of the Wearer) has on.
Ex: ["Wearer" I] HAD ON ["Clothing" the most ridiculous monkey-suit you could imagine]. Ex: ["Wearer" These two losers] were WEARING ["Clothing" bras] ["BP" on their heads]!
Many targets incorporate the Clothing item, and some targets describe the state of _not_ wearing something (when it might be expected).
Ex: Do you think anyone would notice if ["Wearer" I] _went_ TOPLESS?
NB: There is a very common metonymy in which characteristics of the clothing stand for the clothing itself, such as
Ex: the ["Wearer" man] CLAD ["Clothing" in leather]. Ex: ["Wearer" She] was DRESSED ["Clothing" all in red].
Such sentences should be tagged METAPHOR on the sentence level.

fe.name: Wearer
fe.definition: The person whose clothing is under discussion. Ex: ["Wearer" Fred] was SHIRTLESS.

fe.name: Clothing
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Clothing that the Wearerwears. Ex: Fred was WEARING ["Clothing" a shirt].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition:
The body part of the Wearer which is covered by the Clothing.
Ex: She was WEARING a glove ["BP" on one hand].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A characterization of how completely the clothing status holds.
Ex: She was ["deg" scantily] CLAD -- with just a towel in strategic position.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A characterization of the impression given by the Wearer's clothing status.
Ex: She was aware that she was being closely observed by the ["man" formally] DRESSED staff .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at or during which the Wearer has the Clothing on.
Ex: ["tim" By five o'clock], he was WEARING the old holey jeans and t-shirt again.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The location that the Wearer exits while wearing the Clothing.
Ex: I just ca n't understand why he doesn't WEAR his hat ["sou" out of the house].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The location that the Wearer arrives at or enters while wearing the Clothing.
Ex: She WORE her purple dress ["goa" to the party].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Wearer wishes to bring about.
Ex: He just WORE it ["pur" to see if it would fit].

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
The location relative to the body of the Wearer that the Clothing occupies. Note that in many cases, the location is defined relative to other clothing.
Ex: She WORE shorts ["rel" outside her jeans].

frame.definition: The words in this frame refer to facial Expressions and the Possessors of those Expressions.

fe.name: Manner

fe.name: Degree

fe.definition: This is the person who exhibitis the Expression.Ex: ["Poss" Ryan] grinned.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The Expression may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause - the Possessor's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement as in: Ex: Kim made a FROWN ["ICause" in concentration].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:

fe.name: Agent

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

fe.name: Circumstances

fe.name: Duration

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason the Agent stops the Activity.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: n general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

frame.name: Activity_ready_state
frame.definition:
The Protagonist is in an initial state, before beginning to be involved in the Activity, but all pre-conditions for performance of the Activity have been satisfied. In many cases, the Protagonist is an intentional agent, but there are other uses in which the agent is deprofiled, and the Protagonist is an entity which is essential to the Activity. Alternatively, the Activity may be indicated by a Salient_entity which stands in for the Activity. This Salient_entity may also be an intentional agent, but need not be.
Ex: ["pro" She] _'s_ not READY ! ["act" DNI]. Ex: ["pro" He] _'s_ READY ["act" to talk] , I think . Ex: _Is_ ["pro" the UK government] READY ["act" to do a u-turn on passport-ID cards] ? Ex: Check and see if ["pro" Sal] _is_ READY ["sal" for the bathtub] . Ex: ["pro" The world] _is_ finally PREPARED ["sal" for him] !

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Protagonist in the initial state of an activity.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The action that the Protagonist is prepared to do.
Ex: The students were finally READY ["act" to take the exam] .

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
An entity which stands in metonymically for the Activity.
Ex: Are you READY ["sal" for a baby] ? Ex: I 'm READY ["sal" for the eggs] now .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Protagonist is ready.
Ex: He looks like he 's READY ["tim" now] .

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state or event that follows due to the ready state.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Protagonist remains capable of the Activity without beginning it.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

frame.name: Commerce_buy
frame.definition: These are words describing a basic commercial transaction involving a buyer and a seller exchanging money and goods, taking the perspecitive of the buyer. The words vary individually in the patterns of frame element realization they allow. For example, the typical pattern for the verb BUY: BUYER buys GOODS from SELLER for MONEY. Abby bought a car from Robin for $5,000.

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer wants the Goods and offers Money to a Seller in exchange for them. Ex: ["Buyer" Jess] BOUGHT a coat. Ex: Lee BOUGHT a textbook ["Buyer" from Abby].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: Only one winner PURCHASED ["Gds" the paintings]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Ex: Will they allow you to PURCHASE ["Mns" by check]?

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. Ex: Sam BOUGHT the car ["Money" for $12,000].

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: Jon RENTED a car for ["Rate" twenty dollars a day] Rate.

fe.name: Seller
fe.definition: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer. Ex: Most of my audio equipment, I PURCHASED ["Seller" from a department store near my apartment].

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Lee BUYS potatoes ["Unit" by the pound].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the purchasing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Buyerthat affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: She ["Manner" gleefully] BOUGHT the rock.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual intended by the Buyer to receive the Goods. Ex: You BOUGHT ["Recipient" me] three pairs already!

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Goods are (or have been) in the Buyer's possession. (This FE is generally only relevant for the LU's _rent.v_ and _lease.v_ which imply a temporary change of possession.) Ex: Our neighbors have been RENTING their house ["Duration" for the last ten years].

fe.name: Purpose_of_goods
fe.definition: The Buyer's intended purpose for the Goods. Ex: I PURCHASED the calculator["POG" for easier calculation of my debts].

lexunit.name: buy.v
lexunit.definition: COD: obtain in exchange for payment

lexunit.name: purchase.v
lexunit.definition: COD: buy

lexunit.name: purchase_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of buying.

frame.name: Commerce_sell
frame.definition: These are words describing basic commercial transactions involving a buyer and a seller exchanging money and goods, taking the perspective of the seller. The words vary individually in the patterns of frame element realization they allow. For example, the typical patterns for SELL: SELLER sells GOODS to BUYER for MONEY. Robin sold a car to Abby for $5,000.

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer has the Money and wants the Goods. Ex: Lee SOLD a textbook ["Buyer" to Abby].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: Kim SOLD ["Goods" the sweater].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Ex: Abby SOLD the car ["Means" for cash].

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. Ex: Sam SOLD the car ["Money" for $12,000].

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: The farmers' market SELLS apples ["Rate" for one dollar a pound]

fe.name: Seller
fe.definition: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer. Ex: So far, ["Seller" my company] has SOLD more than three million copies.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Bob SELLS peppers ["Unit" by the pound].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the selling event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Seller that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: Stuart ["Manner" reluctantly] SOLD her his last rock.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Seller after the sale has occurred. Ex: I SOLD the whole lot ["Result" at a loss].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Goods are (or have been) in the Buyer's possession. (This FE is generally only relevant for the LU's _rent.v_ and _lease.v_ which imply a temporary change of possession.) Ex: Our neighbors have RENTED their house out ["Duration" for the last ten years].

fe.name: Purpose_of_Goods
fe.definition: The Buyer's intended purpose for the Goods. Ex: He SOLD the filing robot to me ["POG" for filing all my legal documents].

fe.name: Reversive
fe.definition:
This FE indicates that the selling act reverses an earlier separate act in which the current Seller bought the Goods from the current Buyer.
Ex: There is a plan for Mercer to buy the ground and LEASE it ["Reversive" back] to the club

fe.name: Relay
fe.definition:
This FE indicates that the selling act constitues a re-selling by the current Seller of Goods that they bought earlier from a third person who is not the Buyer of the current selling act.
Ex: The Chambers villa has been SOLD ["Relay" on] to a local construction company

frame.name: Buildings
frame.definition:
This frame contains words which name permanent fixed structures forming an enclosure and providing protection from the elements.
Ex: The ["Type" baroque] CHURCH, built in 1635, has a very rich interior Ex: The city tour includes the ["toc" 16th-century] MONASTERY of the Transfiguration and Church of Elijah the Prophet Ex: An ancient ["Mat" stone] CHURCH stands amid the fields
Ex: Jack ["Gov" built] ["X" his HOUSE] in the style of the day.

fe.name: Builder
fe.definition: The Individual that created the Building.

fe.name: Building
fe.definition: The entity built by the Builder which has some Function.

fe.name: Function
fe.definition: The use for which the Building is intended.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The Name used to refer to the Building.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: Any indication of what makes up the Building, including components, ingredients, etc

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition: The time at which the Building comes into existence.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An indication of the subtype of Building, including architectural style.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characterization of some property of the Building.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The building's location.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition: A place that a Building is located with respect to.

frame.name: Smuggling
frame.definition: The words in this frame describe situations in which the Perpetrator secretly takes Goods into or out of a country or other area which are prohibited by law or on which one has not paid the required duty.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: This is the person (or other agent) that illegally takes the goods into or out of a country.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be illegally taken into our out of a country.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The source is the location the goods occupy initially before change of location.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The path refers to (a part of the) ground the Goods travel over or to a landmark the Goods travel by.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is the location the Goods end up in.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Perpetrator which allows them to smuggle the Goods.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The unlawful movement of Goods.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the Event not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In most cases, it indicates salient characteristics of a Perpetrator that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: The rebels had ["Manner" secretly] SMUGGLED in several tonnes of explosives.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by the act of smuggling.
Ex: We SMUGGLED you in here ["Purp" to try to help] but ...

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that a smuggling event occurs.
Ex: Inmates ["Frequency" frequently] SMUGGLE marijuana into the prison

fe.name: Constant_location
fe.definition:
The container, vehicle, or other entity that the Goods move with and remain stationary with respect to.
Ex: She 'll SMUGGLE them ["Constant_location" in suit cases].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance travelled by the Goods.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The amount of time per distance travelled by the Goods.
Ex: They SMUGGLED the bomb ["Speed" swiftly] through customs.

lexunit.name: smuggle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move (goods) illegally into or out of a country.

lexunit.name: smuggling.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act or instances of moving (goods) illegally into or out of a country

lexunit.name: smuggler.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who moves (goods) illegally into or out of a country

lexunit.name: contraband.a
lexunit.definition: COD: imported or exported illegally.

lexunit.name: contraband.n
lexunit.definition: COD: goods that have been imported or exported illegally.

frame.name: Commercial_transaction
frame.definition: These are words that describe basic commercial transactions involving a Buyer and a Seller who exchange Money and Goods. The individual words vary in the frame element realization patterns. For example, the typical patterns for the verbs buy and sell are: BUYER buys GOODS from the SELLER for MONEY. SELLER sells GOODS to the BUYER for MONEY.

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer wants the Goods and offers Money to a Seller in exchange for them.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: ["Goods" Kim] BOUGHT ["Goods" the sweater]. Ex: ["Goods" Kim] SOLD ["Goods" the sweater].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Ex: Abby BOUGHT the car ["Means" with cash]. Ex: Robin PAID for the car ["Means" by check].

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: Price or payment per unit of Goods. Ex: ["Rate" The manager] PAYS the paper boys ["Rate" five dollars an hour] Rate.

fe.name: Seller
fe.definition: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The Unit of measure of the Goods according to which the exchange value of the Goods (or services) is set. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Bob SELLS peppers ["Unit" by weight]. Ex: Lee BUYS potatoes ["Unit" by the pound]. Ex: She is PAID ["Unit" by the hour].

lexunit.name: transaction.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an instance of buying or selling.

frame.name: Transfer
frame.definition: This frame involves a Donor transferring a Theme to a Recipient.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The object that changes ownership.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the transfer occurs.

fe.name: Transferors
fe.definition: The Donor and Recipient conceived of as a unit.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action whereby the transfer of the Theme from the Donor to the Recipient is effected.
Ex: The South State delivery system provides for ["mea" courier] TRANSFER of documents and interlibrary loans among member libraries and the South State Office.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the transfer which is not covered by more specific FEs

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Theme is transferred

lexunit.name: transfer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of transferring

lexunit.name: transfer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move from one place to another.

frame.name: Getting
frame.definition:
A Recipient starts off without the Theme in their possession, and then comes to possess it. Although the Source from which the Theme came is logically necessary, the Recipient and its changing relationship to the Theme is profiled.
Ex: ["Recipient" I] GOT ["Theme" two whistles] ["Source" from John].

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the object that changes possession.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied. Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place denotes where the Getting takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is the action of the Recipient which results in their possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally acts.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The state that either the Recipient or the Theme end up in after the acquisition.
Ex: You should ACQUIRE it ["Result" without any publicity].

fe.name: Concessive

frame.name: Commerce_pay
frame.definition: This frame involves agents paying MONEY for GOODS. In this frame the MONEY is the direct object, and is mapped to the Theme of the Transfer.

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer has the Money and wants the Goods. Ex: ["Byr" Gem] PAID fifty dollars for a shirt

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: Kim PAID fifty dollars ["Gds" for the shirt]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Abby BOUGHT the car ["Means" with cash]. Robin PAID for the car ["Means" by check].

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. Ex: Pat PAID ["Money" 14 dollars] for a movie ticket.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: The manager PAYS the paper boys ["Rate" five dollars an hour].

fe.name: Seller
fe.definition: The Seller has the Goods and wants the Money. Ex: ["Slr" The landlord] is PAID $700 a month by the tenants for the apartment.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Bob PAYS for peppers ["Unit" by the pound].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the paying event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Buyer that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: She ["Manner" quietly] PAID the bill and left.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
Ex: Worker 's compensation PAYMENTS alone ["Circumstances" in cases involving falls] , now average more than $8500 per incident in North America .

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
Ex: A good tenant PAYS her rent ["Frequency" regularly]

frame.name: Quantity
frame.definition:
This frame contains transparent nouns (and some adjectives) denoting quantities of a Mass or of Individuals. As opposed to aggregate words such as group, set, these Quantity do not have a status as Wholes on their own. Initially, at least, we annotate both Quantity of Masses and of Individuals in this frame, though we may split the frame along these lines later on.
Ex: He found them in the ["Quantity" DELUGE] ["Individuals" of papers] on his desk.

frame.name: Natural_features
frame.definition:
The Locale is a geographical location as defined by shape. This frame includes natural geographic features, including land/ice forms and bodies of water.
Ex: We climbed up the ["Constituent_parts" rock] ["Locale" CLIFF].

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: Salient parts of the Locale. Ex: We drove through a ["Constituent_parts" mossy] DELL.

fe.definition: The location that the Locale is a part of. Ex: John spent several years wandering the ["Locale" MOUNTAINS] ["Container_possessor" of Romania].

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Locale about. Ex: There is a ["Formational_cause" glacial] ["Locale" valley] near here.Ex: There is a ["Formational_cause" impact] ["Locale" valley] near here.

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition: A stable bounded area. It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
A place that a Locale is located with respect to.
Ex: All the ["Locale" MOUNTAINS] ["Relative_location" in America] are small.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: The Type is the subtype of natural feature.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.
Ex: That 's a long way down on such a ["des" steep] CLIFF.

frame.name: Locale
frame.definition:
This frame contains general locale words, and is mostly a place-holder in the hierarchy. Words in this frame designate relatively stable bounded ares of the world which have permanent Relative_locations with respect to other locales, and thus are useful as permanent landmarks.
It is inherited by Locale_by_use, which has to do with places that are named according to their intened use, or some hibitual use, such as factory.n, dance floor.n, village.n, field.n. It is also inherited by Locale_by_event, which covers places that are names according to some event which took place there, such as concerts, battles, and meteor impacts.

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition:
A stable bounded area. It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.
Ex: There used to be a forest in that AREA.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: Salient parts that make up a Locale. Ex: This is the largest ["Cnst" live oak] AREA in the forest.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
A place that a Locale is located with respect to.
Ex: For some reason, the PLACE ["rel" next to the lamp] was damp.

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition:
Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Locale about. This FE should also include words that indicate that there was no salient formation.
Ex: In an official ["for" "Defense of the Pedestrian Act"] ZONE, all forms of wheeled transport (excluding wheelchairs) are prohibited.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The location that the Locale is a part of. Ex: John spent several years wandering the northern REGIONS ["ContP" of Europe].

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the Names of Locales.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Locale.
Ex: The day after the hurricane, the prime minister visited the ["des" devastated] AREA.

fe.name: Related_event
fe.definition: An event related to the locale in some way other than (1) Formational_cause (which is a separate FE) or an intended use (which would place the instance in Locale_by_use), or (3) a defining event (which would place the instance in Locale_by_event).

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The activity that is carried out in the Locale.

lexunit.name: area.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a region of an expanse

lexunit.name: zone.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an area distinguished on the basis of a particular characteristic, use, restriction, etc.

lexunit.name: region.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an area of a country or the world having definable characteristics but not always fixed boundaries.

lexunit.name: place.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular position or point in space; a location.

lexunit.name: spot.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular place, point, or position.

lexunit.name: location.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular place or position.

lexunit.name: locale.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a place associated with particular events.

lexunit.name: pocket.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a small. isolated or protected area.

lexunit.name: regional.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of or pertaining to a particular geographical area, territory, or district.

lexunit.name: site.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an area of ground on which something is located.

lexunit.name: point.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a particular spot or location.

lexunit.name: grounds.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the desginated property of an area

frame.name: Biological_area
frame.definition: This frame contains words that denote large ecological areas as well as smaller locations characterized by the type of life present--in other words, geography locations as defined by biota.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: Constituent_parts make up a Locale. Ex: This is the oldest ["Cnst" oak] FOREST in California.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition:
Container_possessor is the location of which the Locale is a part.
Ex: Jon explored the FORESTS ["ContP" of California].

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition: Formational_cause brings about the features of the Locale. Ex: Jon explored the ["FormC" glacial] VALLEY. This FE is also used for words that indicate no salient formation. Ex: Jon explored the ["FormC" virgin] WOODLAND.

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition: This FE identifies a stable bounded area, and is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames. Ex: There used to be a forest in that ["Locl" VALLEY].

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Names of Locales. Ex: Jon explored the FORESTS ["Name" of California]. Ex: Jon hiked around ["Name" Muir] WOODS.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
Relative_location identifies a place in respect to which a Locale is located.
Ex: All theSWAMPS ["RelLoc" in Georgia] are dry.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.
Ex: Apparently they found him at the bottom of a ["des" really deep] BOG.

lexunit.name: woodland.n

lexunit.name: mudflat.n

lexunit.name: forest.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.

lexunit.name: bog.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an area of very soft wet muddy ground

lexunit.name: wood.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a small forest.

lexunit.name: jungle.n

lexunit.name: swampland.n

lexunit.name: marshland.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a piece of land that happens to be marshy

lexunit.name: fen.n

lexunit.name: moor.n

lexunit.name: grassland.n

lexunit.name: mead.n

lexunit.name: lea.n

lexunit.name: wold.n

lexunit.name: thicket.n

lexunit.name: savanna.n

lexunit.name: mire.n

lexunit.name: bush.n

lexunit.name: greenwood.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a wood or forest in leaf, especially as a refuge for outlaws.

lexunit.name: spinney.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a small area of trees and bushes.

lexunit.name: scrub.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a natural area defined by its abundance of shrubbery.

lexunit.name: oasis.n

lexunit.name: rainforest.n
lexunit.definition: FN: Lush forest in hot, humid locales (receiving plentiful precipitation)

frame.name: Clothing_parts
frame.definition:
The Subparts of Clothing items worn by a Wearer and made of a certain Material. The Subpart may itself have parts, which we label Subregion:
Ex: The shirt features a long SLEEVE ["Subregion" with shiny gold buttons].

fe.name: Clothing
fe.definition:
This is the Clothing of which the target word is a part.
Ex: His ["clo" trouser] POCKET...

fe.name: Subpart
fe.definition:
This is a Subpart of the Clothing item.
Ex: His trouser ["Subpart" POCKET]...

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
The Material from which the Subpart is made.
Ex: He wore a jacket with a ["mat" fur] COLLAR.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
A part of the Clothing item.
Ex: a shirt ["Subregion" with long sleeves]

fe.name: Wearer
fe.definition:
The person who is wearing the clothes, or for whom the clothes are intended.
Ex: ["Wear" He] wore a filthy leather miniskirt.

fe.name: Body_location
fe.definition:
This is the part of the body were the garment is worn.
Ex: He had a stocking ["BLoc" over his head]. Ex: He put gloves ["BLoc" on his hands].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This FE identifes any description of the clothing besides Material.
Ex: He shoved his left hand into a ["Des" deep] pant POCKET.

lexunit.name: bootlace.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cord or leather strip for lacing boots.

lexunit.name: shoelace.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cord or leather strip passed through eyelets or hooks on opposite sides of a shoe and pulled tight and fastened.

lexunit.name: lace.n

lexunit.name: button.n

lexunit.name: zip.n

lexunit.name: zipper.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a zip fastener.

lexunit.name: buckle.n

lexunit.name: snap.n

lexunit.name: thong.n

lexunit.name: collar.n

lexunit.name: neck.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a narrow connecting or end part.

lexunit.name: sleeve.n

lexunit.name: cuff.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a.the end part of a sleeve, where the material of the sleeve is turned back or a separate band is sewn on

lexunit.name: waist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: part of the clothing below the ribs and above the hips.

lexunit.name: tassel.n

lexunit.name: fringe.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a border of threads, tassels, or twists, used to edge clothing or material. [Clothing] [Textiles]

lexunit.name: pocket.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a small bag sewn into or on clothing so as to form part of it, used for carrying small articles.

lexunit.name: braid.n
lexunit.definition: COD: mass noun threads of silk, cotton, etc. woven into a decorative band.

lexunit.name: seat.n
lexunit.definition: COD: clothing that covers a person's buttocks.

lexunit.name: leg.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a part of a garment covering a leg or part of a leg.

lexunit.name: sash.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long strip or loop of cloth worn over one shoulder or round the waist.

lexunit.name: strap.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strip of leather, cloth, or other flexible material, used for fastening, securing, carrying, or holding on to.

lexunit.name: hood.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a covering for the head and neck with an opening for the face, typically part of a coat or cloak. [Clothing]

lexunit.name: cowl.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large loose hood forming part of a monk's habit.

lexunit.name: skirt.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part of a coat or dress that hangs below the waist.

lexunit.name: breastplate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a piece of armour covering the chest.

lexunit.name: waist-band.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strip of cloth encircling the waist, attached to a skirt or a pair of trousers. (listed as waistband)

lexunit.name: clasp.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a small device with interlocking parts used for fastening things together.

lexunit.name: seam.n

lexunit.name: placket.n

lexunit.name: monogram.n

lexunit.name: decolletage.n

lexunit.name: cuff-link.n

lexunit.name: hem.n

lexunit.name: insole.n

lexunit.name: waistband.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strip of cloth encircling the waist, attached to a skirt or a pair of trousers.

lexunit.name: waistline.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part of a garment that is shaped or constructed to fit at or near the waist.

lexunit.name: sole.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the section forming the underside of a piece of footwear.

lexunit.name: brim.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the projecting edge around the bottom of a hat.

lexunit.name: neckband.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strip of material round the neck of a garment

frame.name: Political_locales
frame.definition: This frame covers words that name Locations as defined politically, or administratively.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up a Locale. Ex: New York is a CITY ["Constp" of glass and steel]

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The location that the Locale is a part of. Ex: John spent several years wandering the VILLAGES ["ContP" of Romania].

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition:
A stable bounded area. It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.
Ex: There used to be a forest in that ["Lcl" CITY]

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the Names of Locales.
Ex: The CITY ["Name" of Paris] Ex: The TOWN ["Name" of Smithersville]

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
A place that a Locale is located with respect to.
Ex: All the CITIES ["RelLoc" near the San Francisco bay] are large.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.
Ex: He ruled the ["des" largest] KINGDOM ["des" that ever existed].

fe.name: Population
fe.definition:
The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale.
Ex: Stawiski was a CITY ["pop" of laborers], of whom can be said ?You shall eat your bread by the sweat of your brow?

lexunit.name: barony.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the rank and estates of a baron.

lexunit.name: territory.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an area under the jurisdiction of a ruler or state.

lexunit.name: country.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the Names of Locales. Ex: The CITY ["Name" of Paris]

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition: A place that a Locale is located with respect to. Ex: The corn FIELD ["RelLoc" across from the highway] has been there for many years.

fe.definition:

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent Locale itself and any of its participants.

frame.name: Attaching
frame.definition:
The Attaching frame covers two situations: a scene in which somebody causes one thing to be physically connected to something else; or a scene in which somebody causes two things to be connected to each other. In the first, the frame includes an Agent who attaches an Item to a Goal by manipulating a Connector, creating an asymmetric relationship between the Item and the Goal. In the second, the Agent attaches two Items to each other, where each serves as a Goal for the other, creating a symmetric relationship between the two Items. In both cases, the Connector remains to bind the two entities (either Item and Goal, or two Items), without creating a new entity.
Ex: ["Agent" The robber] TIED ["Item" Harry] ["Goal" to the chair].
Ex: Make sure ["Agent" you] BIND ["Items" his wrists] ["Manner" as thightly as possible].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent manipulates an object. Agent typically refers to animate beings, but is also extended to mechanical and other inanimate objects. It is most frequently expressed as the external argument of verbs. Ex: ["Agent" The robber] TIED Harry to the chair.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Item that the Agent attaches to the Goal. Ex: The robber TIED ["Item" Harry] to the chair.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an attaching event. Ex: The robber TIED his ankles ["Result" together].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal identifies the location to which an Item is attached. Ex: The robber TIED Harry ["Goal" to the chair].

fe.name: Connector
fe.definition: The Connector forms the bond that maintains the Item or Items in a fixed position; it is usually expressed in a _with_-PP. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Connector" with a rope].

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the plural Items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment. Ex: The robber TIED ["Items" Harry's ankles] together.
Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Goal can occur.

fe.name: Handle
fe.definition: Thie Handle is the point of attachment on the Item to which the Agent attaches. Ex: The robbers TIED Harry to the chair ["Handle" by his ankle].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Means" by wrapping the rope around his chest].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Manner" with enthusiasm].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Place" in the basement].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Purpose" to stop him from leaving].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Item or Items. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Time" at midnight].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent attaches an Item or Items. Typically, it transmits the force applied by the Agent, and is not left behind as a participant in the resultant Being_attached frame. Ex: The robber TIED Harry to the chair ["Instrument" with his left hand].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up attached.
Ex: You only ["Degr" partially] ANCHORED it, and now it's torn off.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times the Attaching event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the Attaching event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time when the Attaching occurs.
