frame.name: Intentionally_act
frame.definition: This is an abstract frame for acts performed by sentient beings. It exists mostly for FE inheritance.

fe.name: Act
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Act that the Agent performs intentionally.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent performs the intentional act.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent performs an intentional act. John FLATTERED her ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent acts intentionally.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: 'Twould be best it were DONE ["Manner" quietly].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain within which the Agent acts.
Ex: No doubt he has begun to engage in ["dom" political] ACTIVITY of late

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of an act.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Event_dscription
fe.definition: This FE gives a description of the Intentionally_act event.

frame.name: Locative_relation
frame.definition:
A Figure is located relative to a Ground location. The location of the Figure may be further specified by its Distance from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) and the Direction in which the Figure lies from a reference location (generally, the deictic center).
Ex: ["Fig" The cat] _is_ ON ["Grnd" the mat]. Ex: ["Figure" The kitchen, with its breakfast / snack bar,] ADJOINS on one side while the dining area adjoins on the other side. ["Ground" DNI]

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.
Ex: The cat is ON ["Grnd" the mat].

fe.name: Figure
fe.definition:
The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location.
Ex: ["Fig" The cat] is ON the mat.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Distance between the Figure and some reference location (generally, the deictic center or the Ground). Ex: The cat is ["Dist" right] UNDERNEATH the table. Ex: The cat is ["Dist" way] back AGAINST the wall. Ex: ["Dist" Deep] UNDER the earth lurk dark things.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure. Ex: The cat is ["Dir" down] ON the mat. Ex: The book is way ["Dir" back] IN the Paleontology area.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.
Ex: He was IN Athens ["tim" on Friday].

fe.name: Figures
fe.definition: The Figures are items which mutually serve to identify the location of the other items.

frame.name: Criminal_process
frame.definition: A Suspect is arrested by an Authority on certain Charges, then is arraigned as a Defendant. If at any time the Defendant pleads guilty, then the Defendant is sentenced, otherwise the Defendant first goes to trial. If the Verdict after the trial is guilty, then the Defendant is sentenced. In the end, the Defendant is either released or is given a Sentence by a Judge at the sentencing. The core roles in this frame include Jury, Judge, Defendent, District Attorney, Defense Attorney, an Authority such as the police/sheriff. Non-core roels include Witness, Accomplice and Victim.

fe.name: Court
fe.definition: This FE identifies the court involved in a trial.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Defendant
fe.definition: The Defendant is charged with an offense.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The Judge heads the court where arraignment occurs and the case is tried.

fe.name: Prosecution
fe.definition: This FE identifies the attorney(s) prosecuting the Defendant.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Charges brought against the Defendant.

fe.name: Defense
fe.definition: The Defense represents the interests of the Defendant.

fe.name: Jury
fe.definition: This FE identifies the people who are charged by the Court to listen to the testimony, evidence, and arguments, and come to a consensus about the guilt or innocence of the Defendant.

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Offense which the Defendant is accused of committing.

frame.name: Trial
frame.definition: A trial is a process conducted in a Court before a Judge and (usually) a Jury in which the participants meet in order to decide a Case. The Prosecution attempts to prove that the Defendant is guilty of the Charges and the Defense tries to prove that the Defendant is innocent. Trials have a rich schematic structure which is only partially represented here. The Trial frame is the part of the Criminal Process frame that occurs after a crime, Arrest of a suspect, Arraignment, jury selection, etc. and before Sentencing and Punishment or release. The Trial is made up of court appearances. The beginning of the Trial generally involves Opening Arguments, in which the Prosecution and the Defense present their respective points of view. Then during the course of the Trial, both sides present evidence, some of which is provided by witnesses with testimony, and this is then drawn upon as support for their arguments. Following the presentation of evidence, testimony, and arguments, generally culminating in Closing Arguments for each side, the Jury (if present) deliberates and either comes to no sufficient concensus or produces a Verdict.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: The legal label for the crime that the Defendant is accused of.

fe.name: Court
fe.definition: The specific room where the participants in a Trial meet.

fe.name: Defense
fe.definition: The individual or group which is responsible for promoting the welfare of the Defendant during a Trial, usually involving the contention that the Defendant is innocent of the Charges.

fe.name: Jury
fe.definition: The group of individuals who observe the Trial and ultimately attempt to come to a verdict.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the trial occurs.

fe.name: Prosecution
fe.definition: The individual or group responsible for promoting the interests of the state in the Trial, prototypically including presenting arguments for the guilt of the the Defendant.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the trial occurs.

fe.name: Defendant
fe.definition: The person charged with an offence.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The official who directs and presides over the Trial.

fe.name: Case
fe.definition: The Case which a Trial is convened to decide.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Trial is conducted.

frame.name: Arrest

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: Charges identifies a category within the legal system; it is the crime with which the Suspect is charged.Ex: The police ARRESTED Harry ["Chrg" on charges of manslaughter].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the arrest occurs.Ex: The police ARRESTED Harry ["Place" in front of his house].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the arrest occurs. Ex: The police ARRESTED Harry ["Time" on Wednesday afternoon].

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition: The Authorities charge the Suspect with commiting a crime, and take him/her into custody.Ex: ["Authorities" The police] ARRESTED Harry on charges of manslaughter.

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition: The Suspect is taken into custody, under suspicion of having committed a crime.Ex: The police ARRESTED ["Suspect" Harry] on charges of manslaughter.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates the subtype of arrest under which the Suspect is placed. Ex: The police placed Harry under ["Type" house] ARREST.

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition: Offense identifies the ordinary language use of the reason for which a Suspect is arrested. Ex: They arrested Harry ["Offense" for shoplifting].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the arresting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Authorities that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which Authorities arrest a Suspect.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which Authorities arrest a Suspect. Ex: The police ARRESTED Harry ["Purpose" to get him off the street].

fe.name: Source_of_legal_authority
fe.definition: The Source_of_legal_authority describe the law which grants the power of arrest to the Authorities. Ex: ["Authorities" The policeman] ARRESTED ["Suspect" him] ["Source_of_legal_authority" under the "suspected loitering with intent" power].

fe.name: Coparticipant
fe.definition:
A person that participates in the event along with the Authorities or the Suspect.
Ex: She was ARRESTED ["Coparticipant" with the Minister of Finance, Javier Soledad] .

frame.name: Roadways
frame.definition:
This frame involves stable Roadways which connect two stable Endpoints, the Source and the Goal. Being physical objects, these Roadways may have Names and Characteristics; they are also made of a Material. They also cover ground, so they may have a Path or a Relative_location that the travel occurs in.
Ex: We crossed the ["Material" brick] ["Roadway" road]. Ex: I prefer to travel on ["Roadway" highway] ["Name" I-80]. Ex: This is the only ["Roadway" highway] ["Endpoints" between Lodi and Sonoma]. Ex: She dreaded turning onto the ["Frequency_of_use" busy] ["Roadway" street].

fe.name: Roadway
fe.definition:
The Roadway is the roadway that connects locations.
Ex: The ["Road" ROAD] runs between London and Manchester.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is one of the Endpoints treated as a source.
Ex: The ROAD ["Src" from london] to Glastonberry...

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is one of the Endpoints of the Roadway treated as a goal.
Ex: The ROAD from London ["Goal" to Glastonberry]...

fe.name: Endpoints
fe.definition:
The Endpoints are two (or more) named endpoints of the Roadway.
Ex: The ROAD ["EPs" between London and Glastonberry]...

fe.name: Characteristic
fe.definition:
The Characteristic is a characteristic(s) of the Roadway.
Ex: It was a ["Char" long], ["Char" winding], ["Char" bumpy] ROAD.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The Name is the name of the Roadway.
Ex: We went down ["Name" Abbey] ROAD.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
This is the setting through which the Roadway goes.
Ex: The TUNNEL ["Pat" through the mountains]...

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The Use is the purpose of the Roadway.
Ex: This is the main ["Use" traffic] ARTERY out of Berkeley.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The Direction is the direction or directions the Roadway runs.
Ex: I-80 is an ["Direction" east-west] HIGHWAY.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
The Relative_location is where the Roadway is located.
Ex: The HIGHWAYS ["rel" in California] are the second-worst in the nation.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: The Material is what the Roadway is constructed from.

fe.name: Frequency_of_use
fe.definition: The Frequency_of_use is the state of the Roadway with regard to the number of people who are using the Roadway or typically use it.

fe.name: Abundant_entities
fe.definition:
The Abundant_entities are the entities which occupy the space denoted by the Roadway.
Ex: We passed an ["Roadway" avenue] ["Abundant_entities" of boutiques and restaurants].

fe.name: Length
fe.definition: The Length is the distance the Roadway extends.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A subpart of the Roadway.
Ex: It was a ROAD ["Part" with too many twists and turns to count].

frame.name: Lose_possession
frame.definition: Subframe of Transfer in which the Donor begins by possessing a Theme and finishes by not possessing the Theme.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the Relinquishing occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason indicates what the Donor is trying to accomplish by the Relinquishing.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time indicates when the Relinquishing occurs.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the object that changes ownership due to the Relinquishing.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose indicates the purpose for which the intentional Relinquishing takes place.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The Recipient is the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

frame.name: Pre_lose_possession
frame.definition: Subframe of Relinquish where the Owner (=Donor) has the Possession (=Theme).

fe.name: Owner
fe.definition: The Owner is the entity that owns the Possession.

fe.name: Possession
fe.definition:
The Possession is the thing which is owned by the Owner.
Ex: ["Owner" I] HAVE ["Possession" twenty bucks]. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the possession state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_lose_posession event occurs.

frame.name: Post_lose_possession
frame.definition: The subframe of Relinquish in which the Owner (= Donor) no longer has the Possession (=Theme).

fe.name: Owner
fe.definition: The entity that no longer owns the posession.

fe.name: Possession
fe.definition: The thing which was owned by the Owner. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the possession state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_lose_possession event occurs.

frame.name: Commerce_money-transfer
frame.definition: The subframe of the Commercial_transaction frame which involves the transfer of Money from the Buyer to the Seller (in exchange for the Goods).

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer wants the Goods and offers Money to a Seller in exchange for them. Ex: ["Buyer" Jess] BOUGHT a coat. Ex: Lee SOLD a textbook ["Buyer" to Abby].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: Kim BOUGHT ["Goods" the sweater]. Ex: Kim SOLD ["Goods" the sweater].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Ex: Abby BOUGHT the car ["Means" with cash]. Ex: Robin PAID for the car ["Means" by check].

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. Ex: Pat PAID ["Money" 14 dollars] for a movie ticket. Ex: Sam SOLD the car ["Money" for $12,000].

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In isome cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: The manager PAYS the paper boys ["Rate" five dollars an hour].

fe.name: Seller
fe.definition: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Bob SELLS peppers ["Unit" by the pound]. Ex: Lee BUYS potatoes ["Unit" by the pound].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the transfer not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Buyer, Seller, or Exchangers that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Buyer, Seller, or Exchangers wish to bring about by participating in the exchange.

fe.name: Exchangers

fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Buyer, Seller, or Exchangers wish to bring about by participating in the exchange.

fe.name: Exchangers
fe.definition: The Buyer and Seller considered jointly.

frame.name: Lose_possession_scenario
frame.definition: This is the Frame which binds together the initial state of the Donor possessing the Theme, the transfer, and the final state of the Donor not possessing the Theme.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The entity that began by owning the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The thing which was originally owned by the Donor. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

frame.name: Addiction
frame.definition: This frame concerns an Addict's physiological or psychological compulsive dependence on an Addictant, the substance or behavior to which the Addict is addicted.

fe.name: Addict
fe.definition: The Addict is physiologically or psychologically dependent on a substance or a behavior.

fe.name: Addictant
fe.definition: Addictant is the substance or behavior to which the Addict is dependent.Ex: Pat defeated ["Addict" her] ["Addictant" heroin] ADDICTION.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an Addict is addicted to the Addictant.

fe.name: Compeller
fe.definition: Compeller is the part of a human's body or psyche that compels the Addict to seek out the Addictant. Ex: ["Addict" Pat] _is_ ["Compeller" emotionally] ADDICTED ["Addictant" to Kim]. Ex: ["Addict" Cyril] _is_ ["Compeller" physically] ADDICTED ["Addictant" to nicotine].

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
The feature of the Addict that is being described, namely their condition.
Ex: His ADDICTED ["sta" condition] wasn't anyone's fault, exactly, but she blamed Mom anyway.

lexunit.name: addicted.a

frame.name: Intoxication
frame.definition: This frame concerns people being in an altered mental state that is induced by an Intoxicant. Ex: ["Cognizer" Cory] _was_ DRUNK. Ex: ["Cognizer" Nutty] stormed in DRUNK ["Degree" as a fiddler].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The mental state of the Cognizeris changed by an Intoxicant.

fe.name: Intoxicant

fe.name: Degree

fe.name: Evaluation
fe.definition: Evaluation indicates the Cognizer's reaction to the intoxicatoin. Ex: ["Cognizer" Jim] had a ["Evaluation" bad] TRIP.

fe.name: Duration

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer is intoxicated. Ex: ["Cognizer" Michael] was ["Manner" aggressively] DRUNK.

frame.name: Direction
frame.definition:
A Path made up of a set of positions in some N-space Domain (often spatial) is determined as a function of a Base_position and some one-dimensional Independent_variable (often time). For many of the words of this frame, the Domain and/or the Independent_variable are incorporated in the basic definition of the target.
Ex: ["Path" EAST] ["Base_position" of Mt. Diablo] the Sierras rise majestically above the Central Valley.
In this case, the Domain and the Independent_variable are both spatial.

fe.name: Base_position
fe.definition: The point of reference from which the rest of the Path is reckoned.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The one-dimensional set of locations.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The kind of space in which the set of points of the Path is defined. Ex: Let us progess a bit FORWARD ["Dom" in time] to the Napoleonic wars.

fe.name: Independent_variable
fe.definition: The one-dimensional variable with respect to which the positions on the Path are reckoned. For normal motion, the positions on the Path are with respect to time.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: How much along the Path from the Base_position that there has been movement in the stated direction.

frame.name: Rewards_and_punishments
frame.definition:
An Agent (the punisher or rewarder) performs a Response_action on an Evaluee for a Reason, the Evaluee's actions or beliefs. Means and Instrument may also be indicated. The goal of the punishment/reward is to discourage/encourage the actions or beliefs. Words in this frame presuppose that a judgment of the Evaluee has occurred and that the Evaluee is (or becomes) aware of the judgment. This judgment was performed by a cognizer which is either the same as the Agent, or, minimally, a representative of the same institution.
Ex: ["Agt" His] PUNISHMENT ["Eval" of the prisoners] was too harsh. Ex: ["Eval" Her] PUNISHMENT was too harsh. Ex: The PENALTY ["Reas" for this crime] _is_ ["Action" death]. Ex: I believe that this behaviour should be subject to DISCIPLINARY ["Action" action].

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment has made and to whom reward/punishment is dealt. With verbs, the Evaluee is typically expressed as Object. Ex: The boss REWARDED ["Eval" you] for your diligence.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing the reward or punishment.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward. Ex: His parents DISCIPLINED him ["Mns" by taking away his toys]. Ex: The Bar Association REWARDED her ["Mns" by hosting a lunch in her honor].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for theAgent's judgment. It is usually a 'for'-PP, e.g. Ex: I PUNISHED him ["Reas" for his impudence].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of the reward or punishment.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person doing the rewarding or punishing. Ex: ["Agt" Jake's] REWARDS to his best workers were very generous.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which the reward or punishment is carried out.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose of the reward or punishment.

fe.name: Response_action
fe.definition: The reward or punishment given to the Evaluee by the Agent. Ex: If a person be guilty of impiety let him be PUNISHED ["Action" with death].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree of reward or punishment.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the reward or punishment.

frame.name: Causation_scenario
frame.definition: A Causation event (the Cause) causes a Result event (the Effect).

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes. Ex: ["Cause" John] MADE me give up smoking. Ex: ["Cause" The wind] MADE the door rattle. Ex: ["Cause" The accident] CAUSED them to be more careful the next time.

fe.name: Effect
fe.definition: The Effect is the event which results from the Cause. Ex: The eruption LED ["Effect" to the extinction of thirty separate species].

frame.name: Cardinal_numbers
frame.definition:
This is the primary frame evoked by the cardinal numbers.
Ex: Dr. Malik has confined ["Precision" almost] a ["Num" SCORE] ["Entity" of such unfortunates in his basement], you know. Ex: There were ["Num" THIRTY] ["Entity" of the little blue creatures] staring up at him. Ex: Stephen has more than ["mul" five] ["Number" HUNDRED] in his closet! ["Entity" DNI] Ex: There are ["deg" just over] ["Number" six] BILLION ["Entity" people] in the world today.

fe.name: Number
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Number. Ex: JP has almost ["Num" one million] dollars.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Entity enumerated by the Number. Ex: JP has almost one million ["Entity" dollars].

fe.name: Precision
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Precision to which an Entity approximates a Number.
Ex: JP has ["Precision" almost] two MILLION dollars. Ex: ["deg" About] THIRTY cases are known. Ex: There are ["deg" just over] six BILLION people in the world today.

fe.name: Multiplier
fe.definition:
How many times larger the group of Entitys is than the base Number.
Ex: ["mul" Four] SCORE and seven years ago, our forefathers set forth blah blah blah.

frame.name: Judgment_communication
frame.definition: A Communicator communicates a judgment of an Evaluee to an Addressee. The judgment may be positive (e.g. _praise_) or negative (e.g. _criticize_), and this is indicated by the semantic types Positve and Negative attached to the lexical units. This frame does not contain words where Evaluee and the Addressee are necessarily the same . Ex: ["Com" I] COMMENDED ["Evaluee" his handling of the crisis]. Ex: ["Com" Gaston] DENOUNCED ["Evaluee" him] ["Addressee" to the committee]. This is distinct from the Judgment frame in that it involves the communication of an evaluation, rather than merely forming and holding a particular evaluation.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee hears the judgement from the Communicator.
Ex: Jon BELITTLED Madie ["Add" to her colleagues].

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The Communicator uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey his or her evaluation of the Evalueeto another person. Ex: ["Com" Jon] BELITTLED Madie to her colleagues.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the evaluation is conveyed.
Ex: Jon BELITTLED Madie ["Medium" over the telephone]. Ex: ["Communicator" The party] DENOUNCED ["Evaluee" the General] ["Medium" in vehement terms]. Ex: ["Communicator" Mayor Quimby] CRITICIZED ["Evaluee" the townspeople] ["Medium" in his annual speech].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic identifies the entity to which the proposition or propositions conveyed relate. Ex: Jon CRITICIZED Madie ["Topic" about her managerial style].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Communicator judges the Evaluee to be good or bad.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: A judgment is made about the Evaluee With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object: Ex: Jon BELITTLED ["Eval" Madie] to her colleagues.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the judgment made by the Communicator. Ex: She viewed him with a CRITICAL ["Expressor" gaze].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the judgmental communication occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which a judgmental communication is accomplished.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the REASON for the Communicator's judgment. It is usually a _for_-PP. Ex: Jon EXTOLLED Madie ["Reason" for her efforts]. It can also sometimes be expressed as an _as_-phrase, when that phrase picks out the reason for the praise or critique. Ex: ["Evaluee" The book] was RIDICULED ["Reason" as an example of all the worst of post-modernism]. For some words, Reason is an obligatory FE. In other words, the FE may be ommitted only when the Reason for the judgment is understood from context, as when it is clear why an Evaluee is being blamed. Ex: I BLAME you.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Role is used for the capacity in which theEvaluee is judged, and is expressed in _as_-PPs. Ex: Jon BELITTLED Madie ["Role" as a nurse].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies any expression describing the state of a participant in the event.

fe.name: Grounds
fe.definition: The Grounds is the standard by which the Evaluee is judged. Ex: ["Evaluee" The proposal] was CRITIQUED ["Grounds" on this basis].

fe.name: Extent_of_acclaim
fe.definition:
The Extent_of_acclaim provides a description of the number or whereabouts of the Communicator.
Ex: The movie met with ["Extent_of_acclaim" international] ACCLAIM.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the communication of the judgment takes place. Ex: He received critical ACCLAIM ["Time" last week].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the communication of the judgment takes place. Ex: He was BELITTLED by his long-time friend ["Place" in front of his family].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotional or physical state of the Communicator that leads to their communication of a judgment. Ex: He CRITICIZED his compatriots ["IC" out of a deep hatred for all who are better than him].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE describes the frequency with which the specified communication occurs

lexunit.definition: COD: fix blame or responsibility on.

lexunit.name: rave.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to praise with energy and enthusiasm

frame.name: Name_conferral
frame.definition:
This frame contains words that talk about how Speakers name Entities.
Ex: They drove through ["Entity" an area] NICKNAMED ["Name" Sniper's Alley] Ex: ["Speaker" His parents] NAMED ["Entity" him] ["Name" Winston] ["Name_source" after the British prime minister].
In this frame we will ignore uses of words like baptize and christen that don't clearly bring out the name conferral but talk about the meaning of baptism etc. as a sacrament:
Ex: They christened the child on December 4th. Ex: Method was baptized into the church soon thereafter. Ex: Cyril was baptized as a Methodist.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The entity that Speakers refer to by using the Name.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The linguistic expression by which Speakers refer to the Entity.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The person who uses the linguistic expression (Name) to refer to the Referent.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Motivation
fe.definition: The Reason for which an intentional act is performed. We DID it ["Motivation" for the hell of it].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. John FLATTERED her ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Name_source
fe.definition:
This frame element is the person or thing whose name was chosen by the Speaker to give to the Entity.
They NAMED their daughter Carol ["Name_source" after Paul's grandmother].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action the Speaker takes in order to accomplish the name conferral.
Ex: When he was born they CHRISTENED him ["Means" by smashing a bottle of champagne against his arse]

lexunit.name: nickname.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a nickname to

lexunit.name: dub.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give an unofficial name or nickname to

lexunit.name: name.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a name to

lexunit.name: baptize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a specified name or nickname to.

lexunit.name: rename.v

lexunit.name: entitle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to name something

frame.name: Corporal_punishment
frame.definition: Blend of Rewards_and_punishments and Bodily_injury in which the Agent performs some action intended to cause Bodily harm to the Evaluee as a consequence of some action or belief of the Evaluee (the Reason).

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward. Ex: The emperor FLOGGED her ["Means" by taking one of the stays to her].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. Ex: John CANED the criminal ["Purp" to set an example].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object: Ex: ["Evaluee" You] will be FLOGGED for your actions.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a _for_-PP, e.g. Ex: The Sheriff FLOGGED him ["Reason" for his crimes].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: This FE is the location on the body where the bodily injury takes place.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Severity
fe.definition: This frame element marks a quantity related to the seriousness of the punished behavior. Ex: Mr. Devine could face ["Severity" up to 300] LASHES for the offense.

lexunit.name: flog.v

lexunit.name: flogging.n

frame.name: Fining
frame.definition: The Payer is (legally) forced to pay a Fine by an official Speaker as a punishment for some action (the Reason). The Speaker represents an entity which receives the payment. Ex: ["Payer" They] were FINED ["Fine" approximately $3.1 billion dollars] ["Reason" for their knowing, malicious injury to consumers].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the person imposes the fine upon the Payer.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which the fining is performed.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward. His parents DISCIPLINED him ["Means" by taking away his toys]. The Bar Association REWARDED her ["Means" by host a lunch in her honor].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. John FLATTERED her ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Payer
fe.definition: The Payer is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object: Ex: The mental control officer FINED ["Payer" you] for your lack of diligence.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the event (or state) not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the REASON for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a _for_-PP, e.g. I ADMIRE you ["Reason" for your intellect]. For some words in this domain, the Reason frame element is obligatory. That is to say, the overt expression of this frame element may only be omitted when the reason for the judgment is understood from context. For example, the sentence 'I BLAME you!' can only be uttered when it is clear what the addressee is being blamed for.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Fine
fe.definition: The money given to expiate some debt for transgression. Pat paid ["Money" 14 dollars] in FINES.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In isome cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. ["Rate" The manager] PAYS the paper boys ["Rate" five dollars an hour] Rate.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a BY-PP. Bob SELLS peppers ["Unit" by weight]. Lee BUYS potatoes ["Unit" by the pound].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The imposition of a debt due to culpable behavior.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree to which the Fine is punitive to the Payer.
Ex: Employers that hire foreigners without work permits are punishable by law and may be FINED ["Degree" considerably]

frame.name: Measure_duration
frame.definition:
This frame contains (transparent ) nouns that are Units of measurement for time. The frame elements are Count, Unit and Process.
Ex: The final total was 606, scored in only ["Count" 10] ["Unit" HOURS] ["Process" of excellent batsmanship].
In this frame, we will NOT annotate deictic, calendric uses of nouns like week, month, etc. as in "next week, this month, in the 21st century".

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units of the measured entity.Ex: The ads had been absorbed into her brain during ["Count" many] ["Unit" HOURS] ["Process" of television watching].

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities are measured.Ex: ["Count" Seven] ["Unit" HOURS] ["Process" of torrential rain] reduced the pitch to a lake.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The activity or state that takes place during the period of time under discussion.Ex: He had to listen to ["Count" almost two] ["Unit" HOURS] ["Process" of complaints].

frame.definition: An Executioner punishes an individual (Executed) with death as a consequence of some action of the Evaluee (the Reason).

frame.name: Calendric_unit
frame.definition: Words in this frame name the different parts of the calendric cycle, both man-made and natural. Frame elements include Whole for the whole of which the target is a part, Relative_time (RelT) for locating the time with respect to an identifiable reference point, and Name for the name of the day (month, etc.) of a specially named unit. Words in this frame figure into a variety of temporal schemas, realized as constructions. There are families of constructions in which these words occur, including ones in which weekday names combine with day part names using particular prepositions (e.g. _on Wednesday morning_, cf. _on Wednesday_, but _in the morning_) and ones in which calendric terms fill the slots in multi-word expressions such as N-after-N (e.g. _day after day_), N-by-N (e.g. _week by week_), N-to-N (e.g. _month to month_), etc. More can be found on these in Fillmore (2002). Note, also, the connection between this frame and Iteration, specifically that many iterative adjectives and adverbs are based on calendric terms (e.g. _daily_, _weekly_, _monthly_, etc.).

fe.name: Relative_time
fe.definition:
Relative_time is used for the word or words that locate the time with respect to an identifiable reference point.
Ex: Jo's mother will visit ["RelT" this coming] TUESDAY.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: Name is used for the name of a day (month, etc.). Note that only the word (or words) that is the name is (are) tagged, not the target word. Ex: ["Name" Labor] DAY is just around the corner. Ex: January is ["Name" Black History] MONTH.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
Whole is used for the larger unit of which the target word names a part.
Ex: Jo fled in the early MORNING ["Whole" of Sunday December 15].

fe.name: Count
fe.definition:
The number of intervals of the specified type.
Ex: These last ["cou" two] WEEKS, I just keep getting myself into trouble .

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The calendric unit that is denoted. LUs in this frame all denote the Unit.

fe.name: Salient_event
fe.definition:
An event saliently associated with a particular calendric unit.
Ex: Today was my school's ["sal_eve" cut] DAY.
Ex: Republicans have indicated they plan to make Kerry's positions an ["sal_eve" election] YEAR issue.

lexunit.name: spring.n

lexunit.name: summer.n

lexunit.name: minute.n

lexunit.name: second.n

lexunit.name: autumn.n

lexunit.name: quarter.n

lexunit.name: era.n

lexunit.name: age.n

lexunit.name: rush hour.n

lexunit.name: tonight.n

lexunit.name: century.n

lexunit.name: millennium.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a period of a thousand years, especially when calculated from the traditional date of the birth of Christ.

frame.name: Intentionally_affect
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Patient to be affected, sometimes by a particular Means or by use of an Instrument.
Ex: ["Agent" A professional dishwasher] doesn't DO ["Pat" dishes] ["Ins" with a rag] ["Time" anymore]!

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the act that the Agent performs intentionally.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional act that affects the Patient.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient to accomplish the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent performs the intentional act.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: Patient is the entity acted on and that may, but need not, undergo a change. Ex: A professional dishwasher DOES ["Patient" dishes] one at a time.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Patient is affected by the Event.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes the event.

lexunit.name: do.v
lexunit.definition: COD: work on (something) to bring it to completion or to a required state

lexunit.name: do_something_(with_to).v
lexunit.definition: FN: affect (an entity) by some unspecified action.

lexunit.name: do_what_(with_to).v
lexunit.definition: FN: affect (some entity) via an action that is in question.

frame.name: Process_end
frame.definition: A Process comes to an end.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: Name of the event which occurs.Ex: Let ["Process" the carnage] END.

fe.name: Last_subevent
fe.definition: The Last_subevent of an event.Ex: The peace march ENDED ["Last" with a prayer].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the event ends.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event ends.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing the event.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result for the event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that the event is repeated.
Ex: ["Frequency" Twice] the peace march ENDED with a prayer.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time it takes for the Process to end.

lexunit.name: end.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come to an end.

lexunit.name: come to a end.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to reach the conclusion of (as of a process, project, meeting)

lexunit.name: come to a close.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to reach the end of (as a process, project, meeting)

lexunit.name: conclude.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come to an end.

lexunit.name: draw to a close.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to bring to the final stage, as of a meeting or project

lexunit.name: draw to a end.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to bring to the final stage, as of an ongoing process

lexunit.name: end_cessation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a termination of a state or situation.

lexunit.name: end_final-subevent.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a final part of something. NB: especially of events. "the end of the year" "Mario led the race from beginning to end."

lexunit.name: final.a
lexunit.definition: COD: coming at the end of a series.

lexunit.name: finale.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the last part of a piece of music, an entertainment, or a public event.

lexunit.name: pass.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come to an end

lexunit.name: end.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The final point in a process.

frame.name: Process
frame.definition:
This frame describes a complex event which lasts some amount of time, consisting of a beginning stage, a stage where the process is ongoing, and a finish or end. In some cases the process may pause, and then possibly resume.
In this frame and its subframes, the distinguished argument is a Process, and there is no reference to an Entity which undergoes this Process or an Agent which initiates this Process.
In formal terms, this frame refers to an overall controller x-schema (Narayanan 1997) with subframes corresponding to parts of the x-schema.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: Name of the Process which occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

lexunit.name: process.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a natural series of changes.

frame.name: Process_completed_state
frame.definition: A Process is finished and can no longer proceed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: This FE identifies the name of the Process that occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

lexunit.name: done.a
lexunit.definition: COD: no longer happening or existing.

lexunit.name: finished.a
lexunit.definition: FN: brought to an end

lexunit.name: complete.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having run its full course; finished.

lexunit.name: over.a
lexunit.definition: COD: finished.

frame.name: Body_description_part
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with words that describe a person based on a salient part of their body. Ex: He was a BLONDE ["Individual" guy]. Ex: ["Individual" He] was a PEG-LEG.

fe.name: Individual
fe.definition:
This FE identifies theIndividual (or individuals) being described.
Ex: ["Ind" Chuck] is a REDHEAD.

fe.name: Figure
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target. Ex: The RED-HAIRED ["Fig" figure] stood in the doorway.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the body description applies.
Ex: Mort is ["Degree" extremely] FLAT-FOOTED.

lexunit.name: blonde.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person with blonde hair

lexunit.name: brunette.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person with dark brown hair

lexunit.name: blue-eyed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having blue eyes

lexunit.name: redhead.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person, especially a woman, with red hair.

lexunit.name: flat-footed.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having flat feet

lexunit.name: albino.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having a congenital absence of pigment in the skin and hair (which are white) and the eyes (which are usually pink)

lexunit.name: knock-kneed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a condition where the knees curve inward

lexunit.name: bow-legged.a
