lexunit.name: cross-eyed.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having one or both eyes turned inwards towards the nose, either temporarily or as a permanent condition (convergent strabismus)

lexunit.name: black-haired.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having black hair

lexunit.name: grey-haired.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having grey hair

lexunit.name: bearded.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a beard

lexunit.name: moustached.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a moustache

lexunit.name: pigtailed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having pigtails

lexunit.name: red-haired.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having red hair

lexunit.name: peg-leg.n
lexunit.definition: FN: having an artificial leg, especially a wooden one.

lexunit.name: fair.a
lexunit.definition: FN: light- or pale-colored; generally used in reference to hair or skin

frame.name: Apply_heat
frame.definition:
A Cook applies heat to Food, where the Temperature_setting of the heat and Duration of application may be specified. A Heating_instrument, generally indicated by a locative phrase, may also be expressed. Some cooking methods involve the use of a Medium (e.g. milk or water) by which heat is transfered to the Food. A less semantically prominent Food or Cook is marked Co_participant.
Ex: ["Cook" Sally] FRIED ["Food" an egg] ["Medium" in butter]. Ex: ["Cook" Sally] FRIED ["Food" an egg] ["Heating_instrument" in a teflon pan]. Ex: ["Cook" Ellen] FRIED ["Food" the eggs] ["Co_participant" with chopped tomatoes and garlic].
This frame differs from Cooking_creation in focussing on the process of handling the ingredients, rather than the edible entity that results from the process.

fe.name: Cook
fe.definition: The Cook applies heat to the Food.Ex: ["Cook" Drew] SAUTEED the garlic in butter.

fe.name: Heating_instrument
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the entity that directly supplies heat to the Food. Ex: Jim BROWNED the roast ["Heat_instr" in the oven].
This FE will take precedence over Container when both are expressed in the same constituent. For example:
Ex: Kate COOKED the rice ["Heat_instr" in a rice-cooker].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the heat application occurs. Ex: We BAKED the cake ["Place" in the kitchen].

fe.name: Food
fe.definition: Food is the entity to which heat is applied by the Cook.Ex: Suzy usually STEAMS ["Food" the broccoli].In instructional imperatives, this FE, which would be used for the (missing) object, is tagged CNI:Ex: COOK on low heat for two hours.["Food" CNI]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the heat application occurs. Ex: Jim ROASTED the chestnuts ["Time" in the evening].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which heat is applied to Food. Ex: Kate BLANCHEDthe broccoli ["Means" by throwing it into a pot of boiling water].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.Ex: John BAKED cookies ["Purp" to show Patti that he was sorry].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration is the amount of Time heat is applied to the Food.Ex: Jim BOILED the egg ["Duration" for three minutes].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the substance through which heat is applied to the Food. Ex: Bobby FRIED the potatoes ["Medium" in oil].

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: Co_participant is the gramatically less prominent of two foods to which heat is applied by the Cook.Ex: Kate BAKED the apples ["Co_participant" with cinnamon].Ex: Joe ROASTED potatoes ["Co_participant" with the chicken].

fe.name: Temperature_setting
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Temperature_setting of the Heating_instrument for the Food.
Ex: He BAKED the cookies ["Temp" at 350 degrees] for 11 minutes. Ex: She MICROWAVED the popcorn ["Temp" on high]. Ex: You can't COOK popcorn ["Temp" on low heat]!

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which heat application occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the cooking event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Cook that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: SAUTE the onions ["Manner" gently].

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: The Container holds the Food to which heat is applied.Ex: BOIL the potatoes ["Container" in a medium-sized pan].Things that apply the heat directly are Heating_Instruments, e.g. crock-pot, electric skillet.

lexunit.name: braise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fry lightly and then stew slowly in a closed container

lexunit.name: blanch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prepare vegetables for freezing or further cooking by immersing briefly in boiling water

lexunit.name: brown.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become brown by cooking

lexunit.name: broil.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook by exposure to direct heat

lexunit.name: parboil.v
lexunit.definition: COD: partly cook by boiling

lexunit.name: coddle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook an egg in water below boiling point

lexunit.name: scald.v
lexunit.definition: COD: heat milk or other liquid to near boiling point

lexunit.name: stew.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook or be cooked slowly in liquid in a closed dish or pan

lexunit.name: char.v
lexunit.definition: COD: partially burn so as to blacken the surface

lexunit.name: poach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook by simmering in a small amount of liquid

lexunit.name: steep.v
lexunit.definition: COD: soak or be soaked in water or other liquid

lexunit.name: toast.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook or brown by exposure to radiant heat

lexunit.name: saute.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to fry food in a fatty substance

lexunit.name: microwave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook in a microwave oven

lexunit.name: steam.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook by heating in steam from boiling water

lexunit.name: fry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook or be cooked in hot fat or oil

lexunit.name: grill.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook with a grill

lexunit.name: roast.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook or be cooked by prolonged exposure to heat in an oven or over a fire.

lexunit.name: boil.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cook by immersing in boiling water

lexunit.name: simmer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stay or cause to stay just below boiling point while bubbling gently

lexunit.name: cook.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to prepare food by applying heat

lexunit.name: bake.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook by dry heat without direct exposure to a flame, typically in an oven

lexunit.name: barbecue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cook (food) on a barbecue.

lexunit.name: deep fry.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to cook by immersion in heated fat or oil

lexunit.name: singe.v
lexunit.definition: FN: burn superficially

lexunit.name: sear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: burn or scorch with a sudden intense heat.

frame.name: Bounded_entity
frame.definition: This is an abstract frame for bounded areas, used mostly for FE inheritance.

fe.name: Bounded_area
fe.definition: This FE identifies a stable Bounded_area. It typically serves as the denotation of nouns.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: This FE identifies the salient Constituent_parts that make up a bounded area.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition: Relative_location identifies the place in respect to which a bounded area is located.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: This FE is used for the Name of a bounded area.

fe.name: Owner
fe.definition: This FE identifies theOwner, generally a person, of the bounded area.

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Formational_cause (action or agent) that brings about the features of the bounded area.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An indication of which kind of Bounded_area the entity is.

frame.name: Motion_scenario
frame.definition: This frame binds together the various parts of movement, from setting out, to travelling, to arriving.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for the movement is ongoing.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the motion occurs.
Ex: The truck MOVED ["Time" at 10 o'clock].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
The Area is the setting in which the Theme's movement takes place.
Ex: Emily rose to her feet and MOVED restlessly ["Area" around the room].

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.
Ex: Pat ACCOMPANIED ["Cotheme" me] down the street. Ex: The squirrel CHASED ["Cotheme" after the nut].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The Distanceis any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is the location the Theme ends up in.
Ex: The car accelerated and MOVED ["Goal" into the slow lane], as he passed.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path refers to (a part of the) ground that the Theme travels over or to a landmark the Theme travels past.
Ex: The door opened , and he MOVED ["Path" past Dad], into the hall.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the location the Theme initially occupies before its change of location.
Ex: The policeman MOVED ["Source" away from the door].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which motion occurs.
Ex: The car MOVED along ["Spd" at 55 miles per hour].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme is the entity that changes location.
Ex: The explosion made ["Thm" me] MOVE in a hurry.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

frame.name: Medical_conditions
frame.definition:
Words in this frame name medical conditions or diseases that a patient suffers from, is being treated for, may be cured of, or die of. The condition or disease may be described in a variety of ways, including the part or area of the body (Body_Part) affected by the condition (e.g. liver cancer, cardiovascular disease), the Cause of the condition (e.g. bacterial meningities, viral pneumonia), a prominent Symptom of the condition (e.g. asymptomatic stenosis, blue ear disease), the Patient or population (originally) affected by the condition (e.g. bovine turberculosis, juvenile diabetes), or the (proper) Name used to identify the condition (e.g. Munchausen Syndrome, Lou Gehrig's Disease). Annotation in this frame is done in respect to the name of the condition or disease.
Ex: John died of ["Body_P" pancreatic] CANCER.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition:
This FE is used for the patient, entity, or population (originally) affected by the condition or illness.
Ex: ["Patient" juvenile] DIABETES Ex: ["Patient" Dutch Elm] DISEASE Ex: ["Patient" Legionnaire's] DISEASE

fe.name: Body_Part
fe.definition: Body_Part is used for the part or area of the body affected by the condition or disease. Ex: ["Body_P" cardiovascular] DISEASE Ex: ["Body_P" liver] DISEASE

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: This FE is used for the cause of a condition or disease. Ex: ["Cause" bacterial] MENINGITIS

fe.name: Symptom
fe.definition:
This FE is used for a prominent symptom of the condition or disease.
Ex: ["Symptom" asymptomatic] STENOSIS Ex: I have a COLD ["Symptom" with a really bad cough].

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
This FE is used for the Name that identifies the condition or disease.
Ex: ["Name" Munchausen] SYNDROME

fe.name: Ailment
fe.definition: FN: Any medical problem.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Ailment diverges from the norm.
Ex: I am ["Degree" very] SICK.
Since the degree of involvement with an Ailment is equivalent to how negative the experience of the Patient is, in many cases, Degree is expressed by a negative descriptor.
Ex: It seems that he does have ["Degree" very severe] ECZEMA.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Ailment is effecting the Patients.

lexunit.name: acromegaly.n
lexunit.definition: COD: abnormal growth of the hands, feet, and face, caused by overproduction of growth hormone by the pituitary gland

lexunit.name: amnesia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a partial or total loss of memory

lexunit.name: arthritis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disease causing painful inflammation and stiffness of the joints

lexunit.name: anorexia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: lack of appetite for food, in particular also anorexia nervosa an emotional disorder characterized by an obsessive desire to lose weight by refusing to eat

lexunit.name: asphyxia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a condition arising when the body is deprived of oxygen, causing unconsciousness or death

lexunit.name: asthma.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a respiratory condition marked by attacks of spasm in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing and usually associated with allergic reaction

lexunit.name: bronchitis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: inflammation of the mucous membrane in the bronchial tubes, typically with spasm of bronchial muscle and coughing

lexunit.name: cancer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disease caused by an uncontrolled division of abnormal cells in a part of the body.

lexunit.name: candida.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a yeast-like parasitic fungus that sometimes causes thrush

lexunit.name: cataract.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a medical condition in which the lens of the eye becomes progressively opaque, resulting in blurred vision

lexunit.name: cholangitis.n
lexunit.definition: FN: inflammation of the bile ducts.

lexunit.name: cholecystitis.n
lexunit.definition: FN: inflammation of the gallbladder, usually caused by the presence of gallstones.

lexunit.name: cholera.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an infectious and often fatal bacterial disease of the small intestine, typically contracted from infected water supplies and causing severe vomiting and diarrhoea

lexunit.name: cirrhosis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a chronic liver disease marked by degeneration of cells, inflammation, and thickening of tissue

lexunit.name: cold.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a common infection in which the mucous membrane of the nose and throat becomes inflamed, causing running at the nose and sneezing

lexunit.name: colitis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: inflammation of the lining of the colon

lexunit.name: conjunctivitis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: inflammation of the conjunctiva

lexunit.name: cryptosporidiosis.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a diarrheal disease caused by a microscopic parasite (Cryptosporidium parvum).

lexunit.name: diarrhea.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a condition in which faeces are discharged from the bowels frequently and in a liquid form

lexunit.name: depression.n
lexunit.definition: COD: severe despondency and dejection, especially when long-lasting

lexunit.name: dermatitis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: inflammation of the skin as a result of irritation by or allergic reaction to an external agent

lexunit.name: diabetes.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disorder of the metabolism causing excessive thirst and the production of large amounts of urine

lexunit.name: diphtheria.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a serious bacterial disease causing inflammation of the mucous membranes and formation of a false membrane in the throat which hinders breathing and swallowing

lexunit.name: diverticulosis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a condition in which diverticula are present in the intestine without signs of inflammation

lexunit.name: dysmenorrhoea.n
lexunit.definition: COD: painful menstruation

lexunit.name: eczema.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a medical condition in which patches of skin become rough and inflamed with blisters which cause itching and bleeding

lexunit.name: flu.n
lexunit.definition: COD: influenza or any similar, milder infection

lexunit.name: influenza.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a highly contagious viral infection of the respiratory passages causing fever, severe aching, and coughing

lexunit.name: hepatitis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disease characterized by inflammation of the liver

lexunit.name: hernia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a condition in which part of an organ (most commonly, the intestine) is displaced and protrudes through the wall of the cavity containing it

lexunit.name: hypertension.n
lexunit.definition: COD: abnormally high blood pressure

lexunit.name: hypoglycaemia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: deficiency of glucose in the bloodstream

lexunit.name: illness.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disease or period of sickness

lexunit.name: disease.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disorder of structure or function in a human, animal, or plant, especially one that produces specific symptoms or that affects a specific part

lexunit.name: sickness.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being ill

lexunit.name: infection.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an infectious disease

lexunit.name: jaundice.n
lexunit.definition: COD: yellowing of the skin due to an excess of bile pigments in the blood

lexunit.name: leprosy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a contagious bacterial disease that affects the skin, mucous membranes, and nerves, causing discoloration and lumps on the skin and, in severe cases, disfigurement and deformities

lexunit.name: leukemia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a malignant progressive disease in which the bone marrow and other blood-forming organs produce increased numbers of immature or abnormal leucocytes, suppressing the production of normal blood cells

lexunit.name: malaria.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a mosquito-borne intermittent and remittent fever endemic to warmer regions and caused by a protozoan parasite (genus Plasmodium)

lexunit.name: measles.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an infectious viral disease causing fever and a red rash, typically occurring in childhood

lexunit.name: meningitis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disease in which there is inflammation of the meninges, caused by viral or bacterial infection

lexunit.name: menorrhagia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: abnormally heavy bleeding at menstruation

lexunit.name: polio.n
lexunit.definition: COD: short for poliomyelitis

lexunit.name: psoriasis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a skin disease marked by red, itchy, scaly patches

lexunit.name: pyelonephritis.n
lexunit.definition: FN: infection of the kidneys.

lexunit.name: rosacea.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a condition in which certain facial blood vessels enlarge, giving the cheeks and nose a flushed appearance

lexunit.name: schizophrenia.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long-term mental disorder of a type involving a breakdown in the relation between thought, emotion, and behaviour, leading to faulty perception, inappropriate actions and feelings, and withdrawal from reality into fantasy and delusion

lexunit.name: sciatica.n
lexunit.definition: COD: pain affecting the back, hip, and outer side of the leg, caused by compression of a spinal nerve root in the lower back

lexunit.name: shock.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an acute medical condition associated with a fall in blood pressure, caused by loss of blood, severe burns, sudden emotional stress, etc.

lexunit.name: stress.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a state of mental, emotional, or other strain

lexunit.name: strongylosis.n
lexunit.definition: FN: infestation of strongyle worms.

lexunit.name: syphilis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a sexually transmitted bacterial disease, progressing if untreated from infection of the genitals via the skin and mucous membranes to the bones, muscles, and brain

lexunit.name: tetanus.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a bacterial disease causing rigidity and spasms of the voluntary muscles

lexunit.name: tuberculosis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an infectious bacterial disease characterized by the growth of nodules (tubercles) in the tissues, especially the lungs

lexunit.name: tumor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a swelling of a part of the body, generally without inflammation, caused by an abnormal growth of tissue, whether benign or malignant

lexunit.name: ulcer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an open sore on an external or internal surface of the body, caused by a break in the skin or mucous membrane which fails to heal

lexunit.name: rubella.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a contagious viral disease, with symptoms like mild measles; German measles

lexunit.name: mumps.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a viral disease mainly affecting children, causing swelling of the parotid salivary glands of the face

lexunit.name: bacterial meningitis.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an infection of the fluid of a person's spinal cord and the fluid that surrounds the brain caused by a bacteria (as opposed to a virus)

lexunit.name: German measles.n
lexunit.definition: COD: another term for rubella.

lexunit.name: ailment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a minor illness.

lexunit.name: wound.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an injury to living tissue caused by a cut, blow, or other impact.

lexunit.name: affliction.n
lexunit.definition: FN: ailment.

lexunit.name: condition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an illness or medical problem.

lexunit.name: syndrome.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an illness characterized by a group of symptoms occurring together.

lexunit.name: stenosis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the abnormal narrowing of a passage in the body.

lexunit.name: sick.a
lexunit.definition: COD: affected by physical or mental illness.

lexunit.name: ill.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not in full health; unwell.

lexunit.name: unwell.a
lexunit.definition: COD: ill.

lexunit.name: health.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being free from illness or injury.

lexunit.name: plague.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a contagious bacterial disease characterized by fever and delirium, typically with the formation of buboes (see bubonic plague) and sometimes infection of the lungs (pneumonic plague).

lexunit.name: malnourishment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of not being poorly nourished becuase of lack of food.

lexunit.name: malnutrition.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the affliction of being undernourished

lexunit.name: paraplegic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being paralyzed from the waist down

lexunit.name: healthy.a
lexunit.definition: FN: in good health; not ill

lexunit.name: AIDS.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disease, caused by a virus transmitted in body fluids, in which there is a severe loss of cellular immunity leaving the sufferer susceptible to infection and malignancy

lexunit.name: Alzheimer's.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a form of progressive mental deterioration due to generalized degeneration of the brain, occurring in middle or old age.

lexunit.name: disorder.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disruption of normal physical or mental functions

frame.name: Bringing
frame.definition:
This frame concerns the movement of a Theme and an Agent and/or Carrier. The Agent, a person or other sentient entity, controls the shared Path by moving the Theme during the motion. In other words, the Agent has overall motion in directing the motion of the Theme. The Carrier may be a separate entity, or it may be the Agent's body. The Constant_location may be a subregion of the Agent's body or (a subregion of) a vehicle that the Agent uses.
Ex: ["Agent" Karl] CARRIED ["Theme" the books] ["Path" across campus] ["goa" to the library] ["CL" on his head]. Ex: ["Agent" Karl] CARRIED ["Theme" the books] ["Path" across campus] ["goa" to the library] ["CL" in his truck]. Ex: ["Agent" Karl] CARRIED ["Theme" the books] ["Path" across campus] ["goa" to the library] ["Carrier" by truck]. Ex: ["Carrier" The truck] CARRIED ["Theme" the books] ["Path" across campus] ["goa" to the library] ["CL" in specially designed boxes]. The FEs include Path, Goal, and Source. Area is an area that contains the motion when the path is understood as irregular. This frame empasizes the path of movement as opposed to the FEs Source or Goal as in Filling or Placing.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is a sentient being who physically controls the movement of the Theme via the carrier, accompanying the Theme. Ex: ["Agent" Karl] CARRIED the books across the campus to the library.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal identifies the endpoint of the path.
Ex: Karl CARRIED the books ["goa" to the library].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Source indicates the beginning of the path along which the Theme travels.
Ex: Karl HAULED the books ["sou" from the library] to the office.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path along which carrying occurs. Ex: Karl CARRIED the books ["Path" across the campus].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The objects being carried. Ex: Karl TOTED ["Theme" the books] to the car.

fe.name: Constant_location
fe.definition:
The Constant_location expresses the location of the Theme relative to the Carrier. This relationship holds for the entire length of the carrying event.
Ex: Karl TOOK the books to the library ["CL" in his car]. Ex: Karl CARRIED the books to the library ["CL" in his arms].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: Area is used for descriprion of a general area in which the carrying action takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase describing the Carrier, Agent or Theme.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Distance the Theme is carried.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Carrier or Agentcarries the Theme.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the carrying or transporting occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Carrier or Agentcarries the Theme. Ex: We had to CARRY the heavy weights all the way to the top of the hill["Pps" to show our strength].

fe.name: Carrier
fe.definition: The Carrier provides support for the Theme. Movement of the Carrier results in movement of the Theme. Ex: ["Car" The boat] FERRIED the troops across the river.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The actions the Agent takes to move the Theme. Ex: The books were TAKEN to the library ["Mns" by helicopter deliveries]. Ex: I HAUL books ["Mns" by putting them on top of my head].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the general area that serves as a setting for the specific motion of the Agent and Theme (with Source, Path, or Goal). Ex: ["Place" Even in such a small port], these boats would TRANSPORT many tons of trade-goods in to shore annually.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time in which the carrying event takes place.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This FE describes the particpant for whom the bringing is beneficial.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co_participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative.

lexunit.name: lug.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry or drag with great effort

lexunit.name: haul.v
lexunit.definition: COD: transport in a truck or cart

lexunit.name: wheel.v
lexunit.definition: FN: carry in or on a vehicle with wheels

lexunit.name: cart.v
lexunit.definition: FN: carry, sometimes in a cart

lexunit.name: carry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move or transport from one place to another.

lexunit.name: hump.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. and adverbial of direction informal lift or carry (a heavy object) with difficulty.

lexunit.name: fly.v
lexunit.definition: FN: transport by air.

lexunit.name: transport.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take or carry from one place to another by means of a vehicle, aircraft, or ship.

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry or bring with one; convey or guide.

lexunit.name: drive.v
lexunit.definition: COD: convey in a car.

lexunit.name: schlep.v
lexunit.definition: COD: haul or carry with difficulty.

lexunit.name: truck.v
lexunit.definition: COD: convey by truck.

lexunit.name: tote.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry.

lexunit.name: trundle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to move (s.t. with wheels).

lexunit.name: ferry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: convey by ferry or other transport, especially on short, regular trips.

lexunit.name: jet.v
lexunit.definition: FN: transport by means of jet aircraft

lexunit.name: paddle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: transport by non-motorized watercraft

lexunit.name: motor.v
lexunit.definition: FN: transport by means of motor vehicle

lexunit.name: row.v
lexunit.definition: FN: transport by means of non-motorized watercraft

lexunit.name: convey.v
lexunit.definition: COD: transport or carry to a place.

lexunit.name: bike.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to convey by bicycle.

lexunit.name: bring.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry or accompany to a place.

lexunit.name: bear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry.

lexunit.name: fetch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go for and bring back.

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: FN: bring

lexunit.name: portable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be easily carried or moved.

lexunit.name: mobile.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to move or be moved freely or easily.

lexunit.name: transport.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of bringing something from one place to another by some carrier.

frame.name: Competition
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with the idea that people (Participant_1, Participant_2, or Participants) participate in an organized rule governed activity (the Competition) in order to achieve some advantageous outcome (often the Prize). Rank and Score are different criteria by which the degree of achievement of the advantageous outcome is judged.

fe.name: Participant_1
fe.definition: This FE identifies the first (or only) participant in a competition. Ex: ["Participant_1" Jo] PLAYED the lottery every day.

fe.name: Participant_2
fe.definition: This FE identifies the second participant in a competition. Ex: Jo PLAYED ["Participant_2" Leslie] at tennis.

fe.name: Participants
fe.definition: This FE is used for plural NP participants in a competition. Ex: ["Participants" The Yankees] PLAYED in the World Series.

fe.name: Competition
fe.definition: This FE is used for the name of the competition. Ex: Jo PLAYED ["Comp" in the foosball tournament]

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: This FE is used for the score in a game. Ex: The Yankees won the game ["Score" 2 to 0]. EX: The Yankees won the game ["Score" by two points].

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: This FE is used for the ranked results of a competition, and is translatable into a numerical value. Ex: Jo came in ["Rank" third].

fe.name: Prize
fe.definition: This FE indicates a prize won in a competition. Ex: John was COMPETING ["Prize" for a bronze medal].

fe.name: Venue
fe.definition: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition. Ex: The Mets will play ["Venue" at the ball park] on Sunday. Ex: The Mets will play ["Venue" at Shea Stadium] tonight.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place. A constituent tagged as Place may require annotation on a secondary FE-layer. Ex: First layer: John's first COMPETITION ["Place" at Wimbledon] astonished the crowd. Ex: Second layer: John's first COMPETITION ["Competition" at Wimbledon] astonished the crowd.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way the Participants compete.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action the Participants (or Participant_1) is involved in that constitutes a Competition.
Ex: They PLAYED ["Means" by seeing who could get the ball to the far side of the parking lot].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The period of time when the Competition occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE is used to describe the length of time over which competition occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE is used to describe the intended outcome of the competition.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes the intensity of competition.

lexunit.name: competition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the activity or condition of competing against others

lexunit.name: competitive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: relating to or characterized by competition.

lexunit.name: competitor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who takes part in a sporting contest

lexunit.name: compete.v
lexunit.definition: COD: strive to gain or win something by defeating or establishing superiority over others.

lexunit.name: play.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take part in (a sport or contest).

lexunit.name: challenge.n
lexunit.definition: FN: competition against a favored opponent

lexunit.name: rivalry.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a semi-permanent or long-term state of being in competition (with).

lexunit.name: rival.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing competing with another for superiority or the same objective.

frame.name: Communication_means
frame.definition: This frame concerns Communicators communicating with each other with the aid of a Means of communication such as a telephone.

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: This FE is the person who uses the Means of communication to deliver the Message to the Addressee. The Speaker is normally expressed as the External Argument of target verbs, or as the Genitive modifier of nouns. Ex: ["Com" The President] CABLED his assistant to cancel all of his appointments.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by to, or as the direct object, or as the first object in a double object construction. Ex: The President CABLED ["Addressee" his assistant] to cancel all other engagements.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: This is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by about.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which an action is carried out. Ex: Jo FAXED the document ["Manner" speedily].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This Frame Element refers to the Instrument of Communication that is used by the Speaker (and Addressee).

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for using the means of communication. Ex: Pat PHONED ["Reason" to talk about the party]. Note that this FE does not inheret from Intentional_act.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Communicator or Messageduring the communication. Ex: ["Dep" Worried about mail delays], Stephen FAXED the agreement. Ex: Since the general had died in the midst of writing them, the operator TELEGRAPHED Andrea's orders ["Dep" incomplete].

lexunit.name: cable.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send a cablegram to

lexunit.name: wire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send a telegram or cablegram to.

lexunit.name: phone.v
lexunit.definition: COD: telephone.

lexunit.name: semaphore.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send by semaphore or by signals resembling semaphore.

lexunit.name: telegraph.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (someone) a message by telegraph

lexunit.name: telex.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (a message) by telex

lexunit.name: radio.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send a message by radio

lexunit.name: telephone.v
lexunit.definition: FN: send a message via the telephone

lexunit.name: fax.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (a document) by fax.

frame.name: Sending
frame.definition:
A Sender plans the Path (along with Source and Goal) of a Theme and places it in circumstances such that it travels along this Path under the power of some entity other than the Sender. This frame also has a Recipient distinct from the Goal, as both can be present: Ex: I SENT the manuscript ["Goal" to England] ["Recipient" to Bill]. Ex: I FORWARDED the grain ["Recipient" to a dealer] ["Goal" in Frankfurt].
This frame contains verbs that participate in the ditransitive construction, with a recipient as the direct object, as in the following: Ex: I SENT ["Recipient" Bill] the manuscript. Certain Verbs in this Frame focus on the initial sending act, while others do not. For example, _I sent it rapidly_ can either mean the act of sending was initiated quickly or that it moved quickly. However, the in following sentence: _I exported/dispatched it rapidly_, meaning that the act was begun quickly, both types of verbs are included.

fe.name: Sender
fe.definition: This is the person who initiates the movement of the Theme and, unlike Carrying, does not accompany it.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path along which movement occurs. I shipped the books ["Path" along Interstate 65].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The end of the path and intended goal of the sending. I SENT the logs ["Goal" to the shed].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The beginning of the path, similar to source except that it serves to define the path. I sent wood ["Source" from Illinois] ["Goal" to California].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The objects being sent. I mailed ["Theme" the books] ["Goal" to Alaska]. Note that Theme may be multiply instantiated. They MAILED["Theme" a questionnaire] ["Theme" with a return envelope].

fe.name: Transport_means
fe.definition: The mode of sending employed. I SHIPPED ["Theme" the crops] ["Transport_means" by bigrig ].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Sender or Theme Ex: He FAXED his order ["dep" while brushing his teeth]

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme. Pat THREW the Javelin ["Distance" 50 meters].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: This is the recipient of the sent Theme. ["Sender" Tess] MAILED ["Theme" a letter] ["Recipient" to Abby]

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose of the sending. Ex: Rachel SENT the letter to her mother ["Purpose" to let her know about the marriage].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for the sending. Ex: Letters are generally FORWARDED for several months ["Reason" because people are lazy about telling people their new location].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the sending takes place Ex: I SENT the letter to you ["Time" last week].

fe.name: Co_theme
fe.definition: An additional theme sent along with the main Theme.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: A container in which the Theme is sent. Ex: Please send in the request ["Cont" in a self-addressed stamped envelope].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A spatial setting encomnpassing the Source location, where the Sending event takes place.
Ex: Barney POSTED the letter on Monday ["Place" in Athens]

lexunit.name: send.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. cause to go or be taken or delivered to a particular destination.

lexunit.name: mail.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. send (a letter or parcel) by post.

lexunit.name: ship.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to be transported (esp. on a ship).

lexunit.name: post.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. chiefly Brit. send via the postal system.

lexunit.name: export.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (goods or services) to another country for sale.

lexunit.name: forward.v
lexunit.definition: COD: dispatch; send.

lexunit.name: route.v
lexunit.definition: COD: v.1.routeing or routing with obj. and adverbial of direction send or direct along a specified course.

lexunit.name: dispatch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send off promptly to a destination or for a purpose.

lexunit.name: fax.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (a document) by fax.

lexunit.name: telex.v
lexunit.definition: FN: send via telex

lexunit.name: shipment_((items)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: a consignment of goods shipped.

lexunit.name: shipment_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of shipping goods.

lexunit.name: express.v
lexunit.definition: FN: send in the post with a short delivery time

lexunit.name: barge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: send via a vessell that travels through the water

lexunit.name: wire.v
lexunit.definition: FN: send by telegram or electronically

frame.name: Fullness
frame.definition: A Container is in a state of fullness/emptiness with respect to some Contents. Note the connection between words in this frame and those in the Containers, Emptying, and Filling frames. Ex: John carried ["Container" a bucket] FULL ["Contents" of water].

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: Containeris used for the entity whose fullness is being described. Ex: John carried an EMPTY ["Container" bucket].

fe.name: Contents
fe.definition: Contents is used for the stuff that is present/absent in the Container. Ex: The bucket is FULL ["Contents" of water].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the amount of Contents in the Container diverges from the maximal expected amount for the Container.
Ex: Be careful, because the glass is ["deg" very] FULL .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Container is full.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The amount of times the Container is empty per unit of time.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Container's fullness to the end.

lexunit.name: full.a
lexunit.definition: COD: containing or holding as much or as many as possible; having no empty space.

lexunit.name: empty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: containing nothing; not filled or occupied.

lexunit.name: emptiness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of containing nothing

lexunit.name: fullness.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being full.

frame.name: Inhibit_movement
frame.definition:
An Agent restricts the movement of a Theme to within the vicinity of the Holding_location, despite the Theme's desire, plan, or tendency towards motion; the Agent may also use an Instrument. For many of these targets, the means is incorporated. For some LUs, the Theme is required to be a sentient entity. Several of these LUs may be used to describe punishment situations when the Theme is a sentient entity.
Ex: ["Agent" They] HELD ["Theme" the package] ["Duration" for two months] ["Holding_location" in the border-patrol locker room] .

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The entity which is confined.
Ex: He CONFINED ["Thm" 340 mutineers] in Burford Church for the next three days under general sentence of death.

fe.name: Holding_location
fe.definition:
The area within which the Theme comes to be confined.
Ex: He CONFINED 340 mutineers ["Holding_location" in Burford Church] for the next three days under general sentence of death.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.
Ex: ["Agt" He] CONFINED 340 mutineers in Burford Church for the next three days under general sentence of death.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which the confinement is carried out.

fe.name: Motivation
fe.definition:
The reason for the confinement.
Ex: He was LOCKED in his room ["Motive" for disobeying his mother].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose the confinement.
Ex: John was LOCKED in his room ["Purpose" so he could think about what he had done wrong].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target. Ex: The Lilliputians TIED him down ["Mns" by catching him unconscious and traversing his body with their thickest ropes].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Agent maintains the confinement of the Theme.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-sentient entity which is responsible for restricting the movement or location of the Theme.

lexunit.name: confine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep or restrict someone or something within certain limits of (space, scope, or time).

lexunit.name: lock.v
lexunit.definition: FN: enclose someone or something by locking a door

lexunit.name: tie.v
lexunit.definition: FN: confine by making a knot in or around the opening of a container.

lexunit.name: shut up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confine or exclude by closing something such as a door.

lexunit.name: restrict.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deprive of freedom of movement or action.

lexunit.name: imprison.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put or keep in prison.

lexunit.name: prisoner.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: a person who is held confined

lexunit.name: confinement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of forcing or keeping withing a contained area.

lexunit.name: detain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep (someone) in official custody.

lexunit.name: hold.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep in a specified position.

lexunit.name: immure.v

frame.name: Rope_manipulation
frame.definition:
An Agent manipulates a linear entity (the Rope) to form a Knot.
Ex: ["Agent" Harry] TIED ["Rope" the rope] ["Knot" into a slipknot]. Ex: ["Agent" Patty and Selma] KNOTTED ["Rope" the ties of their aprons].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the sentient being who manipulates the Rope.
Ex: ["Agent" Melissa] BRAIDED Jessica's hair.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which the Rope is manipulated.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Prof. Frink BRAIDED my hair ["Purpose" to make me look beautiful].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Terri TIED the rope around her waist ["Time" before scrambling up the side of the mountain].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Kelly TIED her laces around the back of her heel ["Reason" to combat loose shoes].

fe.name: Rope
fe.definition:
The basically linear object which is manipulated by the Agent to produce a Knot.
Ex: He TIED ["Rope" an electrical cable] around the trunk and his neck before hanging himself .

fe.name: Knot
fe.definition:
The stable configuration of a Rope which results from tying.
Ex: Jake TIED the cravat ["Knot" into an acceptable knot].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner in which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: John KNOTTED the tie ["Manr" tightly] around his neck.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Kelly TIED her laces ["Loc" around the back of her heel] to combat loose shoes.

lexunit.name: tie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form into a knot or bow.

lexunit.name: knot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tangle.

lexunit.name: tangle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: twist (strands) together into a confused mass.

lexunit.name: braid.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form a braid with three or more strands

frame.name: Knot_creation
frame.definition: An Agent creates a Knot (possibly in a Place and/or with an Instrument).Ex: ["Agent" Loretta] TIES ["Knot" the most beautiful bowline I've ever seen].Ex: If ["Agent" you] can TIE ["Knot" a half-hitch] ["Place" around the table leg] ["Instrument" with only that much string]...

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which a Knot is produced..

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. John FLATTERED her ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent by which the creation of the Knot is accomplished.

fe.name: Knot
fe.definition: The stable configuration of a String which results from tying.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action. We WANDERED around ["Depictive" naked]. Cicadas SCREECH ["Depictive" unseen from within].

lexunit.name: tie.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to form (a knot)

frame.name: Relation
frame.definition: A relation holds between Entity1 and Entity2

fe.name: Entity1
fe.definition: An entity with a relationship to Entity1

fe.name: Entity2
fe.definition: The entity with a relationship to Entity2.

fe.name: Relation_type
fe.definition:
A characterization of the relation that determines what model is active for further reasoning.
Ex: There is a ["Relation_type" kinship] RELATION between them .

lexunit.name: relation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the way in which two or more people or things are connected or related.

frame.name: Immobilization
frame.definition:
The Agent immobilizes a Patient optionally, to an Anchor.
Ex: ["Agent" The junior officer] HANDCUFFED ["Patient" his commanding officer] ["Anchor" to his desk].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent immobilizes the Patient. Ex: ["Agent" Lisa] HANDCUFFED Mike to the refridgerator.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The Patient is immobilized by the Agent, optionally to an Anchor.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the immobilization.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent immobilizes a Patient.
Ex: Lisa HANDCUFFED Mike to the refridgerator ["Purp" to reduce the mess].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Anchor
fe.definition: The Agent attaches the Patient to an Anchor, generally, an immobile object. Lisa HANDCUFFED Mike ["Anchor" to the refridgerator].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Patient is immobilized as a result.
Ex: The policman TIED UP the burglar ["Degree" completely]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the immobilizing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). This FE also covers expressions that indicate salient characteristics of the Agent which also affect the action (carefully, eagerly).
Ex: Brian grabbed Kim's arm and HANDCUFFED him ["Manner" quickly].

lexunit.name: tie up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: immobilize someone or something

lexunit.name: lock up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make or become rigidly fixed or immovable by locking

lexunit.name: handcuff.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put handcuffs on.

lexunit.name: shackle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: chain with shackles.

frame.name: Entity
frame.definition: This frame is for words that denote highly schematic entities.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: Salient parts that make up a Locale. This is the oldest ["Constituent_parts" oak] FOREST in Dorsetshire.

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition: Formational_causeindicates the action that brings about the features of an Entity. ["Formational_cause" glacial] VALLEY ["Formational_cause" impact] CRATER

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: This FE is used for the Name of an Entity. Ex: LAKE ["Name" Constance]

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: A thing (either abstract or physical) that exists with some degree of permanence.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Entity belongs to.

lexunit.name: item.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an individual article or unit.

lexunit.name: entity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: Something that exists as a particular and discrete unit.

frame.name: Make_cognitive_connection
frame.definition: Using Evidence, which may or may not be expressed, a Cognizer recognizes or proves that Concept1 is associated causally or collocationally with another concept, Concept2. These may be expressed collectively as associated Concepts.

fe.name: Concept_1
fe.definition: Concept1 is the phenomenon which is believed to be related to Concept2.

fe.name: Concept_2
fe.definition: The phenomenon which is believed to be linked to Concept1.

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: The phenomenon which proves the causal connection.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The sentient entity that recognizes the causal connection.

fe.name: Concepts
fe.definition: The phenomena which are believed to be related.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
This FE describes how often the connection is made
Ex: People ["Frequency" often] LINK brand names with Hollywood celebrities

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Cognizer make the connection.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Cognizer makes the connection.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: tie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: connect; link.

lexunit.name: connection.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a link or relationship between people or things.

lexunit.name: connect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be related in some respect.

lexunit.name: link.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make, form, or suggest a link with or between.

lexunit.name: link.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a conceptual relationship between people or things.

lexunit.name: tie.n
lexunit.definition: FN: connection; link

lexunit.name: linked.a
lexunit.definition: FN: The conceptual connectedness between people or things made by a cognizer.

frame.name: Social_connection
frame.definition:
A mutual social and personal relationship that keeps people involved in each other's lives comprises a Connection of Individual1 to Individual2 or between Individuals.
Ex: They wanted to strengthen ["Individuals" their] ["Typ" family] ["Connection" TIES].

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: Individuals have a Connection with each other.

fe.name: Individual1
fe.definition: Individual1 has a social Connection to Individual2.

fe.name: Individual2
fe.definition: Individual2 has a relationship to Individual1.

fe.name: Connection
fe.definition: Connection is the personal relationship between Individuals that keeps them involved in each other's lives.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type is the sub-category to which the Connection belongs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree (strength or closeness) of the Connection.

lexunit.name: tie.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something that serves as a connecting link in a relationship (as a bond of kinship or affection)

lexunit.name: connection.n
lexunit.definition: COD: link or relationship between people or things.

lexunit.name: connected.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a social relationship with

lexunit.name: link.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: a force, feeling, or experience that unites people

lexunit.name: bond.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a force or feeling that unites people.

lexunit.name: close.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a relationship or the people conducting it) very affectionate or intimate.

lexunit.name: closeness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: degree of mutual concern and fondness in a relationship.

lexunit.name: linked.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a social connection

lexunit.name: intimate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: closely acquainted; familiar.

lexunit.name: intimate_((setting)).a
lexunit.definition: FN: promoting or having a friendly atmosphere.

frame.name: Closure
frame.definition:
An Agent manipulates a Fastener to open or close a Containing_object (e.g. coat, jar). Sometimes an Enclosed_region or a Container_portal may be expressed. Since the Manipulator is syntactically omissible, many verbs in this frame incorporate the Fastener.
Ex: ["Agent" Mary] CLOSED ["Containing_object" her coat] ["Fastener" with a belt]. Ex: ["Agent" Mary] CLOSED ["Containing_object" her coat] ["Manipulator" with one hand]. Ex: ["Agent" Mary] BUTTONED ["Containing_object" her coat .]

fe.name: Containing_object
fe.definition: This FE identifies the item that is closed by the agent with the fastener. ["Agent" Lee] BUTTONED ["Containing_object" his coat].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent opens/closes the Containing-object. Ex: ["Agent" Harry] UNCORKED the champagne.

fe.name: Fastener
fe.definition: This FE identifies the fastener that the agent manipulates. Ex: Marcus TIED his shoe ["Fastener" with the neon-green shoelaces].

fe.name: Enclosed_region
fe.definition: This FE identifies the region enclosed by the container-object that is closed. Ex: Harry BUCKLED his belt ["Enclosed_region" around his ample waist]. Ex: Jeremy BUTTONED the shirt ["Enclosed_region" around her hypothermic body].

fe.name: Manipulator
fe.definition: This FE identifies the instrument or part of the body that manipulates the Fastener. Ex: Lee UNBUCKLED his belt ["Manipulator" with one hand]. Note that this FE is syntactically omissible.

fe.name: Container_portal
fe.definition: This FE identifies the active zone of the container that may be expressed as the direct object of the target verb. Ex: We ZIPPED ["Container_portal" the tent flap]. The sentence refers to the closure of the tent, hence is different from sentences where the action involves the manipulation of a fastener, e.g. We unscrewed the lid.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Container_portal/Containing_object ends up closed.
Ex: Why did you only LACE it up ["Degr" partway]?

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity manipulated by the Agent that accomplishes the closure of the Containing_object or the Container_portal.
Ex: He SEALED the lid ["Ins" with wax].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the closing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action of the Agent that accomplishes the closure of the Container_portal or Containing_object.
Ex: He had to BUTTON his sleeve ["Mns" by holding the cuff in his mouth].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the closing event takes place.
Ex: Shouldn't you have BUTTONED that ["Place" in the bathroom]?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Agent closes the Container_portal or the Containing_object.
Ex: They CLOSE the bank vault ["Time" at precisely 5:35PM].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The resultant state of the Closure action.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: The person for whom the Closure event occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE describes the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Closure event and any of its participants.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

lexunit.name: fasten.v

frame.name: Medical_professionals
frame.definition:
This frame includes words that name medical professionals and is closely related to the Medical_specialties frame. The FE Type characterizing a Professional's sub-specialty may also be expressed.
Ex: Ralph is a ["Prof" PAEDIATRICIAN]. Ex: ["X" ["Type" Paediatric] ["Prof" ONCOLOGISTS]] ["Gov" treat] children with leukemia.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Type of medical professional. Ex: ["X" ["Type" Paediatric] ONCOLOGISTS] ["Gov" treat] children with leukemia.

fe.name: Professional
fe.definition: This FE identifies the medical Professional. Ex: ["X" Paediatric ["Prof" ONCOLOGISTS]] ["Gov" treat] children with leukemia.

fe.name: Affliction
fe.definition:
The particular disorder that the medical Professional treats. Most words in the frame inherently indicate this information.
Ex: ["aff" Cardiac] GERONTOLOGISTS can make more money in a year than I 'll see in my life !

fe.name: Body_system
fe.definition:
The part of the body that the medical Professional treats. This is usually indicated by the Lexical Unit itself.
Ex:

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: The length of time the Professional has been alive.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: The payment that the Professional recieves for working.

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The Employer gives compensation to the Professional for working.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Professional belongs.

fe.name: Place_of_employment
fe.definition: The place where the Professional works.

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: Rank is the position in a hierarchy that the Professional occupies within an organization.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The Origin is the place where the Professional was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Instrument is used.
Ex: Use the STETHOSCOPE ["Purpose" to check his lungs]

frame.name: Accompaniment
frame.definition: A Coparticipant fills the same role as the Participant in an event or relation.

fe.name: Participant

fe.name: Coparticipant
fe.definition: In this frame, Coparticipant is the accompanying entity (person or object).Ex: Charlie played the piano WITH ["Coparticipant" Lily].

frame.name: Building
frame.definition:
This frame describes assembly or construction actions, where an Agent joins Components together to form a Created_entity, which is profiled, and hence the object of the verb.
Ex: ["Agent" Jack] BUILT ["CrEnt" a new house] ["Cmpnt" out of bricks]. Ex: We GLUED the airplanes ["Result" together].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent builds a Created_entity. Ex: ["Agent" Jack] BUILT a new house.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument(s) with which an Agent builds a Created_entity. Ex: Jack built a new house ["Ins" with hammer and nails].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the building occurs.
Ex: Jack BUILT a new house ["Place" in a glade].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed. Ex: Jack BUILT a new house ["Purp" to have more living space].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the building occurs.
Ex: Jack BUILT a new house ["Time" early in the morning].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent builds a Created_entity. Ex: Jack BUILT a new house ["Means" by enlisting the help of his friends].

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Components that form the Created_entity. Ex: Jack built a new house ["Cmpnt" out of old bricks].

fe.name: Created_entity
fe.definition: Created_entity identifies the entity that is created in the act of building. Ex: Jack BUILT ["CrEnt" a new house].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies theResult of the act of building. Ex: We GLUED the airplanes ["Result" together].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifes the phrase describing the participant in the act of building. Ex: Jack BUILT the new house ["Depict" naked].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE idenitifies the Manner in which an Agent builds a Created_entity.
Ex: Jack BUILT a new house ["Manner" lovingly].

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Created_entity.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

frame.name: Gathering_up
frame.definition: This frame describes an Agent's gathering of Individuals (people or entities) into a group, the Aggregate, defined by relative proximity. Ex: ["Agent" The police] GATHERED ["Individuals" the suspects] ["Aggregate" into a line-up]. Compare this frame with Congregating, and contrast it with Amalgamating.

fe.name: Aggregate
fe.definition: This FE identifies the aggregate that results from the gathering. It may be expressed either as an adjunct result phrase or as a direct object of a target verb. Ex: The police GATHERED the suspects ["Aggregate" into a line-up]. Ex: He AMASSED ["Aggregate" a collection of shiny bits of tin foil].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: Agent is the person who gathers Individuals. Ex: ["Agent" The police] GATHERED the suspects into a lineup.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the gathering event occurs, if specified. The crowd assembled ["Time" at dawn].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the gathering.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the gathering event occurs. He ASSEMBLED the children ["Place" in the hall].

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entities that come together to form an Aggregate. Ex: The police GATHERED ["Individuals" the suspects] into a line-up.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The way in which the Individuals are gathered up.
Ex: Sue ASSEMBLED the team ["Manner" quickly]

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An Instrument that the Agent uses to gather the Individuals together.
Ex: Native Americans GATHERED these bulbs ["Instrument" with specially whittled and fired digging sticks]

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Agent is attempting to bring about by gathering.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times the Gathering_up event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the Gathering_up event occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal designates the location where the Individuals might end up.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: The Co_participant participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path is the trajectory of motion that the Individuals take.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location where the Individuals are at the beginning of the gathering event.

frame.name: Commemorative
frame.definition:
This frame describes a particular compounding construction (a pattern of coinage) by which more complex words can be created by joining an Honored_entity to a Dedicated_type to describe a particular Dedicated_entity which has been officially named for the Honored_entity. The Dedicated_type and Honored_entity FEs each form part of the Lexical Units (annotated on the second FE layer), and the Dedicated_entity is the denotation of the whole. Since each of the FEs is a part of the Lexical Unit, there is no assignment of Grammatical Function or Phrase Type. The Dedicated_type should (in principle) also be annotated as a LU in a separate frame. Targets are added opportunistically to this frame in the course of annotating other frames. For example, the Day of ARMISTICE DAY should also be annotated in the Calendric_unit frame.
Ex: 1st layer: Turn right at the ["ded" JEFFERSON BUILDING]. Ex: 2nd layer: Turn right at the ["Honored_entity" Jefferson] ["Dedicated_type" Building].

fe.name: Honored_entity
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the person, subject, or event that is being honored.
Ex: We have a picnic every year on ["Honored_entity" VETERANS'] day.

fe.name: Dedicated_type
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the type of entity that had been dedicated to honor the Honored_entity.
Ex: Is Armistice ["Ded_typ" DAY] a national holiday?

fe.name: Dedicated_entity
fe.definition:
The entity which has been dedicated to the Honored_entity.
Ex: The ["ded" JIMMY HOFFA BUILDING] hasn't opened yet.

frame.name: Abounding_with
frame.definition:
A Location is filled or covered with the Theme. The Location is realized as the External Argument, and the Theme either as PP complement headed by _with_, _in_ or _of_.
NB: This frame does not include uses of adjectives like _paved_ when they merely specify the Type of some location, as in "paved and unpaved roads".
Ex: ["Location" The waters of the bay] TEEMED ["Theme" with fish]. Ex: ["Location" The waters of the bay] _were_ TEEMING ["Theme" with fish]. Ex: ["Location" The road] _was_ ["Degree" completely] COVERED ["Theme" in mud].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme covers or fills the Location. This FE most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with or in.
Ex: The waters of the bay TEEMED ["Theme" with fish].

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: Location is the object or area that the Theme fills or covers. This frame element generally occurs as the External Argument.Ex: ["Location" The walls] CRAWLED ["Theme" with nanite surveillance probes]. Ex: ["Location" The picture frame] _was_ ["Degree" thickly] COATED ["Theme" with dust].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree of abundance with which the Theme covers or fills the Location.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Location.Ex: She had ["Location" a closet] CRAMMED ["Depictive" full of clothes].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The period of time during which the the Abounding_with event occurs.

frame.name: Ingestion
frame.definition: An Ingestor consumes food or drink (Ingestibles), which entails putting the Ingestibles in the mouth for delivery to the digestive system. This may include the use of an Instrument. Sentences that describe the provision of food to others are NOT included in this frame.

fe.name: Ingestor
fe.definition: The Ingestor is the person eating or drinking.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Ingestibles
fe.definition: The Ingestibles are the entities that are being consumed by the Ingestor.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Place from which the Ingestor takes the Ingestibles

fe.definition: An act performed by the Ingestor that enables them to accomplishes the whole act of ingestion. Ex: The thing ATE ["Mns" by snaking its long tongue out and grabbing with it].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Ingestibles are consumed by the Ingestor.
Ex: The wolves DEVOURED the carcass ["Degree" completely]

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:

frame.name: Sleep
frame.definition: The Sleeper stays in an altered state of consciousness with greatly reduced external awareness.

lexunit.name: nap.n
lexunit.definition: COD: 1. a short sleep of this [light, brief, or diurnal] type.

lexunit.name: sleep_event.n

lexunit.name: slumber.n
lexunit.definition: COD: 1. a sleep.

lexunit.name: snooze.n

lexunit.name: asleep.a
lexunit.definition: COD: in or into a state of sleep.

lexunit.name: out like a light.a

lexunit.name: out.a
lexunit.definition: FN: asleep or unconscious.

lexunit.name: unconscious.a

frame.name: Cutting
frame.definition:
An Agent cuts a Item into Pieces using an Instrument (which may or may not be expressed).
Ex: At the ceremony, ["Agent" the CEO] CUT ["Item" the red ribbon hanging across the main entrance] ["Pieces" into a glorious confetti].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person cutting the Item into Pieces.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which the Item is being cut into Pieces.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the slicing takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which the Item is being sliced into Pieces.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the slicing occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Agent that accomplishes the slicing. Ex: I SLICED the cucumber in 1/8th inch slices ["Mns" by marking intervals with a ruler].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The item which is being cut into Pieces. Ex: People back then had to CHOP ["Item" firewood] all day long.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the Item being sliced into Pieces.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner in which the Item is being cut into Pieces.

fe.name: Pieces
fe.definition: The Pieces are the parts of the original Item which are the result of the slicing.

lexunit.name: slice.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cut into slices.

lexunit.name: dice.v
lexunit.definition: COD: Cut (food) into small cubes.

lexunit.name: mince.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cut up or shred (meat) into very small pieces.

lexunit.name: cube.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cut (food) into small cubes.

lexunit.name: chop.v

lexunit.name: fillet.v

lexunit.name: pare.v
