lexunit.name: juice.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the liquid present in fruit or vegetables, often used for drinks

lexunit.name: beer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: mass noun an alcoholic drink made from yeast-fermented malt flavoured with hops.

lexunit.name: soup.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a savoury liquid dish made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in stock or water.

lexunit.name: stew.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid in a closed dish or pan.

lexunit.name: sauce.n
lexunit.definition: COD: thick liquid served with food to add moistness and flavour.

lexunit.name: dressing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: also salad dressing mass noun a sauce for salads, usually consisting of oil and vinegar with herbs or other flavourings.

lexunit.name: vinaigrette.n
lexunit.definition: COD: salad dressing of oil, wine vinegar, and seasoning.

lexunit.name: ketchup.n
lexunit.definition: COD: mass noun a spicy sauce made chiefly from tomatoes and vinegar, used as a relish.

lexunit.name: mayonnaise.n
lexunit.definition: COD: mass noun a thick creamy dressing consisting of egg yolks beaten with oil and vinegar.

lexunit.name: lasagne.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an Italian dish consisting of [pasta in wide sheets or strips] baked with meat or vegetables in a cheese sauce

lexunit.name: food.n
lexunit.definition: COD: any nutritious substance that people or animals eat or drink or that plants absorb in order to maintain life and growth.

lexunit.name: tea.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a hot drink made by infusing the dried, crushed leaves of the tea plant in boiling water.

frame.name: Text_creation
frame.definition:
An Author creates a Text, either written, such as a letter, or spoken, such as a speech, that contains meaningful linguistic tokens, and may have a particular Addressee in mind. The Text may include information about its topic, although the latter is not an FE in this frame.
Ex: ["Author" I] PENNED ["Text" a letter concerning racism] ["Addressee" to Congress]. Ex: ["Author" The brothers] SAID ["Text" not two words] ["Addressee" to each other]. Ex: JOT ["Text" any notes you need] ["Place" below the line] ["Manner" in red pen only].

fe.name: Author
fe.definition: The Author produces a particular Text.

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: The Components are the parts that the Author uses to construct the Text. Ex: Caitlin WROTE the book ["Components" from memoirs she collected].

fe.name: Text
fe.definition: The entity which results from the act of writing or speaking. Ex: Michael WROTE ["Text" a frame description]. Ex: Cybil wanted to SPEAK ["Text" those three words].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action Ex: I WROTE everything in that decade ["Depict" on drugs].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action. This frame includes some peculiar examples of manner phrases. WRITE it ["Manner" in pen]. WRITE it ["Manner" in ink].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which a Text is created.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the text is created.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: This is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by to, or as the direct object, or as the first object in a double object construction.

fe.name: Honoree
fe.definition: Honoree identifies the person in whose honor or for whose benefit the Text is created.

fe.name: Form
fe.definition:
This FE describes the form in which the text is presented.
Ex: ["Author" Yeats] WROTE OUT his poems ["Form" in prose].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for creating the text. Ex: I WROTE the article ["Reason" because I would have lost my teaching post otherwise].

lexunit.name: pen.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write or compose

lexunit.name: author.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be the author or the originator of.

lexunit.name: write.v
lexunit.definition: FN: compose a text in writing

lexunit.name: compose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write or create (a work of art, especially music or poetry).

lexunit.name: draft.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prepare a preliminary version of (a text).

lexunit.name: jot down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: write quickly on paper or other receptive medium.

lexunit.name: jot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write quickly.

lexunit.name: speak.v
lexunit.definition: FN: say (a verbal formula).

lexunit.name: say.v
lexunit.definition: FN: recite or create a speech, formula, or other meaningful text

lexunit.name: utter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make (a sound) or say (something).

lexunit.name: write up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: write a full account of something

lexunit.name: write down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: physically write (a mark or symbol) on paper or another receptive medium.

lexunit.name: write in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to write (e.g., a letter) to a central letter-receiving location (e.g., as a letter to the editor)

lexunit.name: write out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: write carefully, generally to avoid omitting necessary parts of a message (or other sequence of symbols) which is already formed in the mind

lexunit.name: print.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write clearly without joining the letters.

lexunit.name: type.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write using a typewriter or computer.

lexunit.name: type out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: type completely, expressing all parts of a message already formed in the mind.

lexunit.name: type up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: create a message by typing

lexunit.name: type in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: input by typing.

lexunit.name: print_out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce a paper copy of (information stored on a computer).

lexunit.name: print_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce (books, newspapers, etc.) by a mechanical process involving the transfer of text or designs to paper.

lexunit.name: get down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: write down

lexunit.name: chronicle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: record (a series of events) in a factual and detailed way.

lexunit.name: sign.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write one's name on (something) for the purposes of identification or authorization.

lexunit.name: dash off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to write down quickly .

frame.name: Reading
frame.definition: The Reader attends to a Text to process its information. Sometimes a particular kind of Phenomenon is sought in the Text.

fe.name: Reader
fe.definition: The one who examines a Text to understand it.

fe.name: Text
fe.definition: The entity that contains linguistic symbols.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: A particular characteristic or thing that the Reader intends to process. READ ["Text" Chapter 7] ["Phenomenon" only for the major concepts.].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act that allows the Reader to read in the specified manner. Ex: I SKIMMED the book ["Mns" by reading just the section headings and the first sentences after].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose is the reason for which the Reader reads the Text.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the reading event takes place. Ex: Charlie often READS the newspaper ["Time" at night].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the reading event takes place. Ex: Surprisingly, few of the students READ much at all ["Place" in the designated reading rooms].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: read.v
lexunit.definition: COD: look at and comprehend the meaning of (written or printed matter) by interpreting the characters or symbols of which it is composed.

lexunit.name: pore.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be absorbed in the reading or study of.

lexunit.name: scan.v
lexunit.definition: COD: look at quickly in order to identify relevant features or information.

lexunit.name: skim.v
lexunit.definition: COD: read (something) quickly, noting only the important points.

lexunit.name: peruse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: read or examine thoroughly or carefully.

lexunit.name: devour.v
lexunit.definition: COD: read quickly and eagerly.

lexunit.name: reader.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who reads.

frame.name: Intentionally_create
frame.definition: The Creator creates a new entity, the Created_entity, possibly out of Components.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: The Creator creates a created entity.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place ehere the Agent intentionally creates the new entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifes the Time when an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Components that are attached together to form a Created_entity. Ex: He MADE a jungle gym ["Components" out of iron bars].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

fe.name: Created_entity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity that the Agent intentionally creates. Ex: They were GENERATING ["Created_entity" grenades] for export.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the creation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Creator that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the instrument with which an Agent intentionally creates a Created_entitiy.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The role of Created_entity.
Ex: This particular book was CREATED ["Role" as an introductory text].

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
A secondary agent with whom the Creator intentionally creates the Created_entity.
Ex: Emily SET UP the business ["Co_participant" with the former president of Intersoft, Inc].

lexunit.name: make.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form by putting parts together or combining substances, or cause to exist or come about; bring about or perform.

lexunit.name: create.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring into existence.

lexunit.name: creation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of creating

lexunit.name: establish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set up on a firm or permanent basis.

lexunit.name: set up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: establish a business, institution, etc.

lexunit.name: generate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to arise or come about.

lexunit.name: establishment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of establishing or being established.

lexunit.name: generation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of producing or generating.

lexunit.name: produce.v
lexunit.definition: FN: create

lexunit.name: found.v
lexunit.definition: COD: establish (an institution or organization)

lexunit.name: production.n
lexunit.definition: FN: creation

lexunit.name: synthesise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make by synthesis.

lexunit.name: synthesis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the production of chemical compounds by reaction from simpler materials.

frame.name: Birth
frame.definition: A Mother and Father produce a Child or an Egg. Ex: ["Mother" Betty] BORE ["Father" Gerry] ["Child" three intelligent daughters].

fe.name: Mother
fe.definition: Mother is the female creature that produces the Child. Ex: ["Mother" Betty] BORE Gerry three intelligent daughters.

fe.name: Child
fe.definition: Child identifies the new self-motile creature produced from the Mother and Father. Ex: Betty BORE Gerry ["Child" three intelligent daughters].

fe.name: Father
fe.definition:
Father is the male creature that copulates with the Mother, thus leading to the birth of the Child.
Ex: Betty BORE ["Father" Gerry] three intelligent daughters.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive identifies the phrase describing a participant of an action
Ex: Demons are SPAWNED ["Depict" fully formed].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Circumstances under which a Mother and Father produce produce a Child.
Ex: Star fish can be SPAWNED ["Circumstances" under the right conditions].

fe.name: Egg
fe.definition:
Egg is an immobile object containing an organism that may hatch as a mobile, infant organism.
Ex: Female clownfish LAY ["Egg" their eggs] around sea anemones

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the event occurs.

fe.name: Parents
fe.definition: The Mother and Father expressed together. Ex: ["Parents" We] are going to be HAVING twins!

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of the birth. Ex: John's mother BORE him ["Result" into a wealthy family].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Parents (or a Father or Mother) that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: They ["Manner" eagerly] SPAWNED more of their kind until there was no room for more.

lexunit.name: bear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give birth to (a child).

lexunit.name: birth.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the emergence of a baby or other young from the body of its mother; the start of life as a physically separate being.

lexunit.name: whelp.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give birth to (a puppy).

lexunit.name: father.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to beget, ie be the father of.

lexunit.name: beget.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce (a child).

lexunit.name: sire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be the sire of.

lexunit.name: spawn.v
lexunit.definition: FN: produce young, particularly in large numbers

lexunit.name: have.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give birth to or be due to give birth to.

lexunit.name: drop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an animal) give birth to. [Vet]

lexunit.name: calve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give birth to a calf.

lexunit.name: kid.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a goat) give birth.

lexunit.name: lay.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a female bird, reptile, etc.) produce (an egg) from inside the body.

lexunit.name: calving.n
lexunit.definition: FN: bearing of calves

lexunit.name: lambing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: bearing of lambs.

lexunit.name: carry_to_term.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be pregnant with and give birth to

lexunit.name: birth.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give birth to

lexunit.name: mother.v
lexunit.definition: FN: give birth

lexunit.name: bring_forth.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give birth to something.

lexunit.name: generate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: produce offspring.

lexunit.name: propagate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: breed by natural processes from the parent stock.

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: FN: produce (offspring)

frame.name: Being_employed
frame.definition:
An Employee has a Position doing work in a particular Field, or doing work on a particular Task, for which an Employer gives Compensation to the Employee.
Ex: ["Employee" Undocumented foreigners] are WORKING ["Position" as building contractors] ["Employer" for Laing Builders].

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition:
The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
Ex: Louise WORKS as an engineer ["Compens" for $1,000]

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The Employee is obligated to perform a Task in order to receive Compensation.
Ex: ["Empee" My Mom] WORKS for the Michigan Department of Agriculture.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The Employer gives Compensation to an Employee.
Ex: My mom WORKS ["Emper" for an Eye Doctor].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee works for an Employee.
Ex: Last weekend, the commercial TV station Nova broadcast testimonies of young Czechs who have WORKED ["Mnr" illegally] for America's largest retailer, Wal-Mart.

fe.name: Place_of_employment
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place_of_employment of the Employee.
Ex: The undocumented foreigners were WORKING ["Place_of_employment" at the organic farm].

fe.name: Position
fe.definition:
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Ex: Louise WORKS ["Posit" as an engineer].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employer is in employment.
Ex: He WAITED TABLES ["Purp" to finance his education at St. Lawrence University, where he was a top-notch wrestler].

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
The Employee is obligated to perform the Task to recieve Compensationfrom the Employer.
Ex: My dad WORKS ["Task" building houses]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time period during which an Employee works for an Employer.
Ex: ["Time" From 2000-2001], Mr. Eckhardt CLERKED for The Honorable Jerry A. Funk, United States Bankruptcy Judge, Middle District of Florida.

fe.name: Field
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Field in which one works.
Ex: Undocumented foreigners WORK ["Field" in construction] for years.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the amount of Time for which the Employee continues being employed.
Ex: She WORKED ["Dur" for 10 years] in private and hospital practice and 19 years in teaching and administration.

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition:
Rank is the position in a hierarchy that an Employee occupies within the organization of the Employer.
Ex: Sue has the ["Rank" top] JOB in the company.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Type of the profession.
Ex: He's harkening back to a time before Bush became president and he had a ["Type" white collar] JOB and wore a suit.

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition:
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.
Ex: As much as possible, however, do not attempt to run a full-time business in addition to holding a ["CB" full-time] JOB .

fe.name: Amount_of_work
fe.definition:
The amount of work the Employee is doing for the Employer.
Ex: Harold is WORKING ["harold" overtime] this week.
This FE needs to be deleted once the LU work is moved.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Employee works.
Ex: Most people WORK ["pla" in the city].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Employee works.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE gives a description of the Being_employed event.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: work.v
lexunit.definition: COD: do work, especially as one's job.

lexunit.name: work.n
lexunit.definition: FN: activity as a means of earning income.

lexunit.name: workplace.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a place where one does work or job

lexunit.name: employ.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being employed; employment.

lexunit.name: wait tables.v
lexunit.definition: COD: act as a waiter or waitress

lexunit.name: position.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: a role as a paid employee

lexunit.name: job.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a paid position of regular employment.

lexunit.name: clerk.v
lexunit.definition: COD: work as a clerk.

lexunit.name: temp.v
lexunit.definition: COD: no obj. work as a temp.

lexunit.name: stint.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an allotted period of work.

lexunit.name: employed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a job

lexunit.name: subcontract.v
lexunit.definition: COD: employ a firm or person outside one's company to do (work).

lexunit.name: farm_(out).v
lexunit.definition: COD: send out or subcontract work to others

lexunit.name: employment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: being employed.

lexunit.name: unemployment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being unemployed.

lexunit.name: unemployed.a
lexunit.definition: COD: without a paid job but available to work.

lexunit.name: jobless.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having no job

lexunit.name: joblessness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of having no job

frame.name: Setting_fire
frame.definition:
This frame describes either the creation of a Flame by a Kindler or the igniting of Flammables by a Kindler.
Ex: ["Kindler" Taliban militants] recently SET FIRE ["Flammables" to several schools].
Ex: ["Flame" The fire] IGNITED.

fe.name: Kindler
fe.definition: The Kindler is the person performing the intentional act. Ex: ["Kindler" Mark] STARTED ["Flame" the fire] with a magnifying glass.

fe.name: Flame
fe.definition: The Flame is what is created by the Kindler. Ex: ["Kindler" Oscar] STARTED ["Flame" the fire].

fe.name: Flammables
fe.definition: The Flamables is the the object that is set on fire by the Kindler. Ex: ["Kindler" Tracy] SET ["Flammables" the couch] ON FIRE.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The cause of the fire. Ex: ["Cause" A spark] IGNITED ["Flammables" the curtains].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Kindler that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An event brought about by the Cause or the Kindler that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes the Kindler as being in some state during the action.

lexunit.name: start fire.v
lexunit.definition: FN: ignite

lexunit.name: light.v
lexunit.definition: FN: ignite something. "Alan gathered sticks and lit a fire."

lexunit.name: ignite.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to catch fire

lexunit.name: torch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set fire to. "The shops had been looted and torched."

lexunit.name: kindle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: light (a flame); set on fire.

lexunit.name: combust.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. consume or be consumed by fire.

lexunit.name: spark.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. ignite.

lexunit.name: alight.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (set) on fire

lexunit.name: ablaze.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (set) on fire

lexunit.name: on fire.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being burnt by flames; must occur with support verb 'set' in this frame

lexunit.name: set fire to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: ignite

frame.name: Mass_motion
frame.definition: A Mass_theme, generally made up of many individuals, moves from a Source to a Goal with some Path.

fe.name: Mass_theme
fe.definition: The mass of entities which moves.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree of abundance.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The place where the overall motion event takes place, thus including Source, Path, and Goal locations. Letters STREAMED in ["Area" all over the country].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which motion occurs.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the location the Theme occupies initially before its change of location.
Ex: Afterwards, the crowd FLOODED ["Source" away from the ceremony].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path refers to (a part of the) ground the Mass_theme travels over or to a landmark the Mass_theme travels by.
Ex: The door opened , and a crowd of people FLOODED ["Path" past me], into the hall.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal is the location the Mass_theme ends up in.
Ex: Eager spectators CROWDED ["Goal" into the auditorium]

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion. This frame element occurs throughout the motion domain but is very infrequent in Motion.Noise. The engine SPLUTTERED forward ["Distance" a short way] and stopped.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Mass_theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Mass_theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: Fans POURED in ["Mode_of_transportation" by boat and train].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the motion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Mass_theme that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully)
Ex: Children CROWDED ["Manner" eagerly] around us

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The spatial setting in which the Mass_motion takes place.
Ex: ["Place" In the main auditorium] people CROWDED around Orange's newest computer

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the Goal of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body. Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Mass_theme, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.

lexunit.name: swarm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move somewhere in large numbers.

lexunit.name: teem.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move as a large, flowing group

lexunit.name: throng.v
lexunit.definition: COD: flock or be present in great numbers.

lexunit.name: stream.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a mass of people or things) move in a continuous flow.

lexunit.name: crowd.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move or come together as a crowd.

lexunit.name: flood.v
lexunit.definition: COD: arrive in or overwhelm with very large numbers.

lexunit.name: pour.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of people or things) come or go in a steady stream.

lexunit.name: flock.v
lexunit.definition: COD: congregate or move in a flock.

lexunit.name: roll.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come by the score

lexunit.name: troop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come or go together or in large numbers.

lexunit.name: parade.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move as a groop (as if) on display

lexunit.name: rain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fall or cause to fall in large quantities.

lexunit.name: hail.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fall destructively in copious quantities.

lexunit.name: shower.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fall, throw, or be thrown in a shower

lexunit.name: pelt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of rain, hail, or snow) fall very heavily.

frame.name: Silencing
frame.definition: An Agent causes a Speaker to become silent, sometimes about a particular Topic.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. Ex: John QUIETED the crowd ["Purpose" to reassert his authority].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Agent silences the Speaker.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The sentient entity that is not communicating.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: This is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by about.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which an intentional act is performed. Ex: I HUSHED him ["Reason" because quiet hours were in effect].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result is the final state of the Speaker.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: The Expressor is theSpeaker's voice or other communicative noise emitted by the Speaker. Ex: ["Agent" The teacher] QUIETED ["Expressor" the children's laughter].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the silencing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: Kim SHUSHED Pat ["Manner" rather haughtily].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Agent succeeds in creating silence.
Ex: Valois SILENCED the crowd ["Degree" completely] with one commanding gesture

lexunit.name: silence.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make silent.

lexunit.name: shush.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tell or signal to be silent

lexunit.name: hush.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become quiet.

lexunit.name: hush_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: suppress public mention of something.

lexunit.name: shut_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop or cause someone to stop talking.

lexunit.name: quiet.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become quiet.

lexunit.name: quiet_down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become quiet

frame.name: Contacting
frame.definition: A Communicator (whose Location may be indicated) directs a Communication to an Addressee at a particular Address. Note that no actual successful communicative act is implied, only the successful completion of acts which would establish the communication. (In other words, Mari can e-mail Jon without Jon ever reading it.) NB: The Address or Location_of_communicator may be a virtual address, such as an e-mail or telephone number.Ex: ["Com" Disgruntled voters] PHONED ["Add" Congressman Neil] ["Address" at his Washington residence] ["Communication" with complaints about the recent increases in corporate welfare].Ex: ["Com" She] tried to CALL ["Src" from the payphone down the street].

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a message to another person.Ex: ["Com" He] WROTE ["Addressee" to John].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The physical or abstract setting in which the message is conveyed.Ex: Opinions are usually CALLED IN ["Medium" over the telephone] and are often given within 24 hours.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The person that receives the message from the Communicator.Ex: ["Communicator" The company] must be able to CALL ["Add" potential customers].

fe.name: Address
fe.definition: This FE is used for a (metaphorical) place in a system of communication where Communicators and Addressees can access the system. Ex: ["Communicator" You] can TELEPHONE ["Addressee" your senator] ["Address" at 555-5555].

fe.name: Communication
fe.definition: The information that the Communicator wishes to impart to the Addressee, often to get a particular response. In this frame the Communication is not necessarily received by the Addressee. Ex: ["Communicator" Patients] continually CALL IN ["Communication" with questions].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for the Communicator contacting the Addressee. Often, this FE is used to identify a PP-for which indicates what the Communicator is attempting to obtain.Ex: Pat PHONED ["Reas" to talk about the party].Ex: ["Reason" For more information], call ["Address" 1-EVANGELIST]. Note that this FE does not inherit from Intentional_act.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: This is the subject matter to which the message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about". Ex: CALL ["Addressee" John] ["Topic" about the party].

fe.name: Location_of_communicator
fe.definition: The location occupied by the Communicator.Ex: Does anyone E-MAIL the office ["Src" from a phone booth]?

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

fe.name: Intermediary
fe.definition: The Intermediary is the person who facilitates the contact. Ex: We CONTACTED her ["Intermediary" through her employer ] .

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive notes the state of one of the participants in the contacting event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times a Communicator contacts the Addressee per unit of time.

lexunit.name: reach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make contact with.

lexunit.name: contact.v
lexunit.definition: COD: get in touch or communication with.

lexunit.name: contact.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state or condition of communicating or meeting

lexunit.name: write in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact by letter

lexunit.name: write.v
lexunit.definition: COD: write and send (a letter) to someone.

lexunit.name: e-mail.v
lexunit.definition: COD: mail or send using email.

lexunit.name: call.v
lexunit.definition: COD: telephone.

lexunit.name: call up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact personally by phone

lexunit.name: phone.v
lexunit.definition: COD: telephone.

lexunit.name: phone in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact by phone

lexunit.name: ring.v
lexunit.definition: COD: call by telephone

lexunit.name: ring up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact personally by phone.

lexunit.name: get in touch.v
lexunit.definition: FN: manage to start communication with someone

lexunit.name: telephone.v
lexunit.definition: COD: ring or speak to (someone) using the telephone.

lexunit.name: call.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a telephone communication.

lexunit.name: mail.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact with information via the postal service

lexunit.name: telex.v
lexunit.definition: COD: communicate with by telex.

lexunit.name: fax.v
lexunit.definition: COD: contact by fax

lexunit.name: cable.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact via cablegram

lexunit.name: page.v
lexunit.definition: COD: contact by means of a pager.

lexunit.name: radio.v
lexunit.definition: COD: communicate with by radio.

lexunit.name: telegraph.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (someone) a message by telegraph.

lexunit.name: call in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contact by telephone

frame.name: Prevarication
frame.definition: A Speaker communicates about a Topic in such a way as to mislead an Addressee, either by telling outright lies or by presenting a message in a misleading form.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a deceptive Message to the Addressee. Ex: ["Speaker" Politicians] do nothing but _tell_ LIES about money.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The person that receives a Message from the Speaker. Ex: You're KIDDING ["Addressee" me]! Ex: Satan LIES ["Addressee" to everyone, including himself].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is the entity to which the proposition or propositions relate, that they are about. Ex: You DECEIVED me ["Topic" about the location of the diamonds].

lexunit.name: lie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tell a lie or lies

lexunit.name: prevaricate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak or act evasively.

lexunit.name: lie.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an intentionally false statement

lexunit.name: mislead.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to have a wrong impression about someone or something.

lexunit.name: kid.v
lexunit.definition: FN: deceive playfully

lexunit.name: misrepresent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a false or misleading account of.

lexunit.name: deception.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of deceiving.

lexunit.name: misrepresentation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: act of deception or misleading

lexunit.name: prevarication.n
lexunit.definition: FN: act of speaking evasively

lexunit.name: shit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: jokingly deceive.

lexunit.name: joke.v
lexunit.definition: FN: say something untrue to be funny.

lexunit.name: equivocate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: use ambiguous or evasive language.

lexunit.name: fool.v
lexunit.definition: COD: trick, deceive, or dupe.

lexunit.name: equivocation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: act of producing ambiguous or evasive language.

lexunit.name: fib.n
lexunit.definition: COD: 1. a trivial lie.

lexunit.name: bullshit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk nonsense in an attempt to deceive.

lexunit.name: pull_leg.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deceive someone playfully

lexunit.name: deceive.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deliberately mislead or misrepresent the truth to.

lexunit.name: fib.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tell a fib.

lexunit.name: pull the wool over (someone's) eyes.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to deceive

lexunit.name: hoodwink.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deceive or trick.

lexunit.name: bullshit artist.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person known to deceive.

lexunit.name: dissemble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hide or disguise one's true motives or feelings.

lexunit.name: dissembler.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who misrepresents him or herself.

lexunit.name: deceptive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: to not be revealing the truth

lexunit.name: tell.v
lexunit.definition: FN: communicate the truth, a lie, etc (support only)

frame.name: Cause_to_experience
frame.definition: An Agent intentionally seeks to bring about an internal mental or emotional state in the Experiencer. This frame in closely related to Experiencer_obj. Ex: ["Agent" Samantha] TERRORIZED ["Experiencer" the children] ["Resulting_action" into screaming].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally tries to bring about an internal mental or emotional state.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is an External Argument of the target word and purposefully arouses an emotional state.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer is the person the Agent causes to have a particular emotional state.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which the Agent affects the Experiencer.

fe.name: Resulting_action
fe.definition: What the Agent intends to make the Experiencer do by causing a certain experience and the Experiencer actually does.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent affects the Experiencer.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where theAgent affects the Experiencer

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent brings about the emotional state.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent brings about the emotional state in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree to which the Experiencer ends up feeling an emotion.
Ex: He ["Degr" completely] TERRORIZED her.

lexunit.name: terrorize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: create and maintain a feeling of terror in.

lexunit.name: torment.v
lexunit.definition: COD: annoy or tease unkindly.

lexunit.name: entertain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide with amusement or enjoyment.

lexunit.name: amuse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to find something funny.

lexunit.name: divert.v
lexunit.definition: FN: entertain

frame.name: Shoot_projectiles
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Firearm to discharge which induces the rapid motion of the Projectile.
Ex: ["Agent" The bankrobber] SHOT ["Goal" at the clerks] ["Firearm" with an AK-47]. Ex: SHOOTING ["Projectile" a cannonball] isn't as easy as it looks. ["Agent" CNI]
Note that usages with the Firearm as object are out of frame, belonging to Use_firearm.

fe.name: Firearm
fe.definition: The device used by the Agent to cause the motion of the Projectile.

fe.name: Projectile
fe.definition: The entity whose rapid, dangerous motion is caused by the Agent and/or Firearm.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the motion of the Projectile.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme. Pat THREW the Javelin ["Distance" 50 meters].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion. Kim THREW the cat ["Goal" into the garden].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Agent whereby the rapid motion of the Projectile is achieved.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: This FE is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal. I PUSHED the trolley ["Path" along the street].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: This FE is the starting point of motion. Pat dragged the box ["Source" out of the cupboard].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A description of the state of the Agent or Projectile during the event.
Ex: He SHOT three arrows at the target, ["dep" all unsuspecting as to why Harold had done so well].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element. Kim PUSHED the lawnmower ["Area" around the garden].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the shooting event takes place.
Ex: The bankrobbers were crazy enough to SHOOT at the clerks with an AK-47 ["Place" inside the bank]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the shooting event takes place.
Ex: The robbers SHOT at the clerks ["Time" as they ran out of the bank]

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Agent's purpose in launching the Projectile
Ex: We mistook a satellite LAUNCHED ["pur" to study earthquakes] to be a missile, so we shot it down over the Pacific.

lexunit.name: shoot.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause an object to be projected forcefully from a device (esp. a weapon, e.g., gun, bow). "He shot the bullet into the air."

lexunit.name: fire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: propel (a bullet or projectile) from a gun or other weapon.

lexunit.name: fire off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: discharge, shoot, launch (a gun, rocket, etc)

lexunit.name: launch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send out or hurl forcefully

lexunit.name: launch.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act or instance of launching something.

frame.name: Use_firearm
frame.definition: An Agent causes a Firearm to discharge, usually directing the projectile from the barrel of the Firearm (the Source), along a Path, and to a Goal. Ex: ["Agent" The Germans] wouldn't stop SHOOTING ["Firearm" cannons] ["Goal" at them]. Ex: ["Agent" Oswald] FIRED ["Iteration" twice] ["Path" through the window].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The self-directed entity that uses and activates the Firearm.

fe.name: Firearm
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Firearm that an Agent activates so that it rapidly propels a projectile.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the means by which an Agent uses the Firearm.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the manner in which an Agent uses the Firearm.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent uses the firearm. Ex: FIRING cannons ["Purp" to have a good time] is not my idea of prudence!

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent fires the Firearm.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is the location the Theme ends up in, or is intended to end up in. Ex: Who FIRED a pistol ["Goal" at my client]?

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: This is the path along which the projectiles travel.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location of the Firearm from which projectiles originate.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: Area is the setting in which the projectile's movement takes place. Ex: Sometimes they got together and FIRED off M-16 ["Area" in the park].

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the number of times a firearm is used.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depicitive phrase describing the state of a participant in the action.

lexunit.name: shoot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause (a gun) to fire.

lexunit.name: fire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: discharge (a gun or other weapon).

lexunit.name: discharge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fire (a gun or missile).

frame.name: Fall_asleep
frame.definition: A Sleeper goes from wakefulness to an altered state of consciousness where they are largely unaware of their environment. The LUs of this frame are differentiated by how quickly and deeply the state is entered and what causes the change (especially whether it comes about naturally as a result of sleepiness or is brought about by injury).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

fe.name: Sleeper
fe.definition: The Sleeper is the entity that falls asleep.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time where the event occurs.

lexunit.name: konk out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lose consciousness suddenly (as if hit on the head)

lexunit.name: black out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lose consciousness suddenly

lexunit.name: doze off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: drift off into a light sleep.

lexunit.name: pass out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: suddenly lose consciousness as a result of being overcome by pain, lethargy, intoxication, heat-exhaustion or the like.

lexunit.name: faint.v
lexunit.definition: FN: suddenly lose consciousness (often resulting in falling down) as a result of emotional shock, pain, or some other internal cause.

lexunit.name: nod off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fall into a light sleep as a result of sleepiness or fatigue.

lexunit.name: zonk out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: quickly fall deeply asleep.

lexunit.name: drift off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: slowly fall asleep.

frame.name: Cause_to_wake
frame.definition: An Agent or Cause causes a Sleeper to transition from the Sleep_state to wakeful conciousness.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Sleeper
fe.definition: The person or being that is sleeping.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent wakes the Sleeper. Ex: John ROUSED her ["Purpose" to irritate her].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which an intentional act is performed. Mary WOKE him ["Reason" because he looked troubled].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes. Ex: ["Cause" The rain] WOKE me. Ex: ["Cause" The smell of cooking] WOKE the children.

fe.name: Sleep_state
fe.definition: This describes the state out of which the Sleeper is awakened.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Sleeper ends up awake.
Ex: I couldn't manage to ROUSE him ["Degr" completely], he could only mumble.

lexunit.name: wake_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to emerge from a state of sleep

lexunit.name: wake.v
lexunit.definition: COD: emerge or cause to emerge from a state of sleep; stop sleeping.

lexunit.name: awaken.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop or cause to stop sleeping.

lexunit.name: rouse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring out of sleep; awaken.

lexunit.name: get_up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to rise from bed after sleeping

frame.name: Sleep_wake_cycle
frame.definition: A Sleeper enters a state of consciousness of reduced external awareness, remains in this state for some amount of time, and (normally) returns to full wakeful conciousness.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

fe.name: Sleeper
fe.definition: The Sleeper is the entity that is sleeping.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

frame.name: Waking_up
frame.definition: A Sleeper transitions from a state of consciousness where they are largely unaware of their environment to a wakeful state.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

fe.name: Sleeper
fe.definition: This FE identifies the sleeping entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Sleep_state
fe.definition: This describes the state out of which the Sleeper awakens. Ex: He AWOKE ["Sleep_state" out of a deep dream].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Sleeper awakens.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Sleeper upon waking up. Ex: Well, sometimes she just WAKES UP ["Dep" angry].

fe.name: World_state
fe.definition: The World_state is the situation the Sleeper finds him or herself in upon awaking. Ex: I AWOKE ["World_state" to the sound of the coffeegrinder].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: This FE indicates an instance of the Waking_up event within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Sleeper awakes from the Sleep_state.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

lexunit.name: come to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: wake up

lexunit.name: awake.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop sleeping.

lexunit.name: wake.v
lexunit.definition: COD: emerge from a state of sleep

lexunit.name: wake up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: emerge from a state of sleep

lexunit.name: get up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to wake up

lexunit.name: revive.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to return to consciousness

lexunit.name: come back around.v
lexunit.definition: FN: return to consciousness with difficulty.

frame.name: Jury_deliberation
frame.definition: The Jury discuss the Case and its Charges in order to evaluate the Possible_sentence of the Accused.

fe.name: Jury
fe.definition: The group that debates the case.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the deliberation is ongoing.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: The legal label for the crime that the defendant is accused of.

fe.name: Case
fe.definition: The Case which a Trial is convened to decide.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the deliberation takes place. Ex: The jury DELIBERATED for three hours ["Time" last Tuesday.].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the deliberation takes place. Ex: The jury DELIBERATED for several hours ["Place" in the Oakland courhouse].

fe.name: Possible_sentence
fe.definition: A sentence that the jury considers during deliberation. Ex: The jury DELIBERATED ["PS" his guilt].

lexunit.name: judgment.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: the activity of the jury after the presentation of all the evidence and statement in a trial, as they try to decide about the guilt or innocence of the defendant

lexunit.name: deliberation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the activity of the jury after the presentation of all the evidence and statement in a trial, as they try to decide about the guilt or innocence of the defendant

lexunit.name: deliberate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: a jury engaging in careful consideration to reach a verdict

frame.name: Sentencing
frame.definition: During a court appearance, a Sentence, generally a punishment, is imposed on the Convict by a Court, usually represented by a judge.

fe.name: Convict
fe.definition: The Convict is given a Sentence by the Court. Ex: Judge Duncan SENTENCED ["Convict" Marty] to five years under house detention.

fe.name: Court
fe.definition: The Court imposes a Sentence on a Convict. Ex: ["Court" Judge Duncan] SENTENCED Marty to five years under house detention.

fe.name: Sentence
fe.definition: The Sentence is imposed on the Convict by the Court. Ex: Judge Duncan SENTENCED Marty ["Sentence" to five years under house detention].

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE denotes the type of sentence. Ex: ["Convict" He] will receive a ["Type" prison] ["Sentence" SENTENCE] if convicted.

fe.name: Term_of_sentence
fe.definition: This FE denotes the duration of the sentence. Ex: ["Convict" Tom] will recieve a ["Sentence" SENTENCE] ["Term_of_sentence" of five years].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Convict is sentenced.
Ex: He will be SENTENCED ["tim" at a later date].

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition:
The illegal action of which the Convict has been found guilty and for which they are punished.
Ex: A pet store owner was SENTENCED ["off" for illegaly smuggling protected reptiles].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location of the sentencing Court.
Ex: Biancaniello will be SENTENCED ["pla" in San Francisco] later this summer.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state that the Convict is in at the time of their sentencing.
Ex: He was SENTENCED ["dep" in absentia] during the mass trials.

lexunit.name: sentence.v
lexunit.definition: COD: declare the punishment decided for (an offender).

lexunit.name: sentence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the punishment assigned to a defendant found guilty by a court.

lexunit.name: order.v
lexunit.definition: FN: force the convict to pay or serve in the prison as punishment

lexunit.name: send up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sentence someone to imprisonment

lexunit.name: condemn.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sentence to a punishment, especially death.

frame.name: Text
frame.definition: A Text is an entity that contains linguistic, symbolic information on a Topic, created by an Author at the Time_of_creation. It may be a physical entity that is made of a certain Material etc. It may be constructed for an Honoree.

fe.name: Author
fe.definition:
The Author is the person who produced a particular Text.
Ex: I'm glad I bought and read ["Author" Robbins's] BOOK.

fe.name: Text
fe.definition:
The Text is the entity that contains linguistic information.
Ex: I'm glad I bought and read Robbins's ["Text" BOOK].

fe.name: Honoree
fe.definition: The person for whom the Text is produced. Ex: The ["Text" POEM] ["Hon" for Caitlin] was included in an anthology .

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Text was created.
Ex: Jackson's new story is based on a ["Time_of_creation" 1980] NOVEL by his father. Ex: POEMS ["Time_of_creation" from the end of that dynasty] are known to contain many novel metric structures.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: What a Text is made of (if applicable). Ex: The library was so old, it was filled with ["Mat" vellum] ["Text" TOMES], not a paperback in sight.

fe.name: Containing_text
fe.definition: This is a text in which the Text is located. Ex: The last ["Text" POEM] ["Cont_text" in the anthology] was horrid.

fe.name: Genre
fe.definition:
The Genre or sub-Genre of the Text.
Ex: She writes only ["Genre" historical] ["Text" FICTION].
Ex: I've got three ["Genre" comedic] ["Text" SCREENPLAYS] on my desk right now!

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The use for which the text was produced; its purpose.
Ex: She read through the bicycle's ["Use" construction] ["Text" MANUAL].

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: The smaller texts that make up the Text. Ex: He found it in a ["Text" BOOK] ["Cmpnt" of spells].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is what the Text is about.Ex: I read a ["Text" BOOK] ["Topic" about knitting].

fe.name: Title
fe.definition:
The Title of a Text.
Ex: She read ["Title" Sassy] ["Text" MAGAZINE]. Ex: Current NOW President Kim Gandy said Friedan's ["Title" Feminine Mystique] BOOK opened women's eyes.
NOTE: when the Title is expressed in an appositive clause, it is labeled as Text on the first layer and Title on the second.
Ex: She read the MAGAZINE ["Text" Sassy].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The Medium is the language in which a text is composed, or the physical medium (radio, ink) in which it is distributed.
Ex: Science ["Text" ARTICLES] ["Medium" in Greek] are difficult to understand for me.
Ex: It's prudent to pay attention to ["Medium" radio] BULLETINS.

lexunit.name: fanzine.n

lexunit.name: imprecation.n

lexunit.name: eulogy.n

lexunit.name: autobiography.n

lexunit.name: ballad.n

lexunit.name: biography.n

lexunit.name: drama.n

lexunit.name: elegy.n

lexunit.name: epic.n

lexunit.name: epigram.n

lexunit.name: epistle.n

lexunit.name: essay.n

lexunit.name: exemplum.n

lexunit.name: fable.n

lexunit.name: festschrift.n

lexunit.name: haiku.n

lexunit.name: letter.n

lexunit.name: limerick.n

lexunit.name: lyric.n

lexunit.name: memoir.n

lexunit.name: monograph.n

lexunit.name: mystery.n

lexunit.name: novel.n

lexunit.name: novelette.n

lexunit.name: novella.n

lexunit.name: ode.n

lexunit.name: poetry.n

lexunit.name: poem.n

lexunit.name: rhyme.n

lexunit.name: song.n

lexunit.name: manual.n

lexunit.name: handbook.n

lexunit.name: paperback.n

lexunit.name: hardback.n

lexunit.name: grimoire.n

lexunit.name: spellbook.n

lexunit.name: lay.n

lexunit.name: book.n

lexunit.name: magazine.n

lexunit.name: account.n

lexunit.name: sermon.n

lexunit.name: screenplay.n

lexunit.name: script.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the written text of a play, film, or broadcast.

lexunit.name: article.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a piece of writing included with others in a newspaper or magazin

lexunit.name: obituary.n

lexunit.name: volume.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a book forming part of a work or series

lexunit.name: mag.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a magazine.

lexunit.name: edition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular form or version of a published text.

lexunit.name: treatise.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a written work dealing formally and systematically with a subject.

lexunit.name: report.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an account given of a matter after investigation or consideration.

lexunit.name: bulletin.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a short official statement or summary of news.

lexunit.name: tractate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a treatise.

lexunit.name: hagiography.n

lexunit.name: journal.n

lexunit.name: periodical.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a periodical magazine or newspaper.

lexunit.name: editorial.n

lexunit.name: meditation.n

lexunit.name: booklet.n

lexunit.name: fiction.n

lexunit.name: writings.n

lexunit.name: missive.n

lexunit.name: newspaper.n

lexunit.name: list.n

lexunit.name: manuscript.n

lexunit.name: literature.n

lexunit.name: history.n

lexunit.name: brochure.n

lexunit.name: material.n
lexunit.definition: FN: literature on a topic

lexunit.name: pamphlet.n

lexunit.name: issue.n

lexunit.name: paper (newspaper).n
lexunit.definition: FN: a newspaper or other regular publication

lexunit.name: paper (article).n
lexunit.definition: FN: a (typically scholarly) written work that is usually intended for a class or publication in a journal

lexunit.name: epic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of or relating to poetry of the epic tradition.

frame.name: Body_decoration
frame.definition: This frame concerns the decorations that human beings have on or apply to their bodies. Ex: ["Dec_ind" Abby] rarely wears ["Decoration" LIPSTICK].

fe.name: Body_location
fe.definition: This FE identifies the location on the body where the decoration takes place. Ex: Abby has a TATTOO ["BodP" on her lower-back].

fe.name: Decorated_individual
fe.definition: This is the individual whose body is decorated. Ex: ["Dec_ind" Abby] rarely wears LIPSTICK.

fe.name: Decoration
fe.definition: Decoration is the decorative item that adorns the body. Ex: Abby has a ["Dec" TATTOO] on her thigh.

fe.name: Decoration_desriptor
fe.definition: Dec_desc identifies a descriptor of the Decoration. Ex: Abby wears ["Dec_desc" red] LIPSTICK.

fe.name: Picture
fe.definition: This is the frame element that describes what shape the Decoration represents. Ex: Abby has a TATTOO ["Pic" of a rose] on her thigh.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Use to which a body decoration is put. Ex: Abby is wearing ["Use" stage] MAKE-UP.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type designates different kinds of body decorations. Often this FE will label part of a multi-word or compound word target. Ex: Abby wore ["Type" SPF 15] MAKE-UP to work, everyday.

lexunit.name: tattoo.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a design made by inserting pigment into punctures in the skin

lexunit.name: make-up.n
lexunit.definition: COD: cosmetics such as lipstick or powder applied to the face

lexunit.name: mascara.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cosmetic for darkening and thickening the eyelashes

lexunit.name: eyeliner.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cosmetic applied as a line round the eyes.

lexunit.name: rouge.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a red powder or cream used as a cosmetic for colouring the cheeks or lips

lexunit.name: blusher.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cosmetic used to give a warm reddish tinge to the cheeks

lexunit.name: concealer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a flesh-toned cosmetic used to cover spots and blemishes.

lexunit.name: lipstick.n
lexunit.definition: COD: coloured cosmetic applied to the lips from a small solid stick

lexunit.name: foundation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cream or powder applied to the face as a base for other make-up

lexunit.name: eyeshadow.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a coloured cosmetic applied to the eyelids or to the skin around the eyes

lexunit.name: kohl.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a black powder, usually antimony sulphide or lead sulphide, used as eye make-up, especially in Eastern countries

frame.name: Predicament
frame.definition:
An Experiencer is in an undesirable Situation, whose Cause may also be expressed.
Ex: ["Exp" The insurers] _ended up_ _in_ the BIND ["Sit" of having to pay 15 years' taxes].
Ex: ["Exp" He] _was_ _in_ a bit of a ["Situation" PICKLE] and make no mistake!
Ex: What a ["Situation" MESS] ["Exp" we] _'re_ _in_ ["Time" now]!

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The Experiencer is in an undesirable Situation.
Ex: ["Exp" The insurers] _ended up_ _in_ a BIND.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition: This FE identifies the undesirable Situation the Experiencer is in. Ex: They found themselves _in_ a quite ["Situation" a fix]. Ex: The company _was_ definitely _in_ ["Situation" dire straits] from the dollar's inflation.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Cause of the Situation.
Ex: We 're in this MESS ["Cause" from paying too little attention to quality control].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
Thiis FE identifies the Time when the Situation is in effect.
Ex: ["Time" Yesterday's] PREDICAMENT was a little too exciting.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Situation occurs.
Ex: The TROUBLE ["pla" in America] is only going to get worse.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The Domain in which the Experiencer has the problem.

lexunit.name: pickle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: 2. a pickle informal a difficult situation.

lexunit.name: scrape.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an embarrassing or difficult predicament.

lexunit.name: pinch.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a difficult situation

lexunit.name: predicament.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a difficult situation.

lexunit.name: bind.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a problematical situation.

lexunit.name: fix.n
lexunit.definition: COD: in sing. informal a difficult or awkward situation. How on earth did you get into such a fix?

lexunit.name: jam.n
lexunit.definition: COD: informal an awkward situation or predicament: I'm in a jam.

lexunit.name: mess.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a confused and problematic situation.

lexunit.name: plight.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a dangerous, difficult, or otherwise unfortunate situation.

lexunit.name: misfortune.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an unfortunate event.

lexunit.name: problem.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an unwelcome or harmful matter needing to be dealt with and overcome.

lexunit.name: trouble.n
lexunit.definition: COD: difficulty or problems.

frame.name: Rite
frame.definition:
This frame concerns rituals performed in line with religious beliefs or tradition.
Ex: In certain ["Desired_state" fertility] RITES ["Place" in Burma] , a woman desirous of offspring is required not only to approach the King Cobra but to plant a kiss on its mouth .
Ex: ["Member" He] was ORDERED ["New_Status" a priest] ["Time" in 1944]. ["Leader" CNI]

fe.name: Leader
fe.definition:
This is the religious or cultural leader who performs and/or leads the rite.
Ex: ["Ldr" The medicine man] performs this RITUAL

fe.name: Member
fe.definition:
The FE Member describes the member of the religious or cultural group who participates in/undergoes the rite.
Ex: ["Mbr" Joe] received COMMUNION.

fe.name: Organization
fe.definition:
Organization identifies the institution in which the rite is prescribed.
Ex: His BAPTISM ["Org" into the Catholic Church] is scheduled for next Sunday.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action that is taken to perform the ritual.
Ex: A building is CONSECRATED ["Mns" by anointing the doorposts with special oil and saying certain prayers]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing the rite

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the rite is performed

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the rite takes place.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Instrument used to perform a particular rite.
Ex: We BAPTISE children ["Instrument" with holy water]

fe.name: Desired_state
fe.definition: This FE identifies the state which the rite is hoped or intended to bring about. Ex: They performed a ["DesS" fertility] RITUAL.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
The type of ritual or ceremony being performed.
Ex: We performed the traditional ["Type" marriage] RITES

fe.name: Object
fe.definition:
This FE indicates an object on which a rite is performed.
Ex: The priest BLESSED ["Obj" the wine]

fe.name: New_Status
fe.definition:
Rites may confer a New_Status on a participant (e.g. rank, membership).
Ex: Elliott was almost ORDAINED ["NStat" as a priest]

fe.name: Guardian
fe.definition:
The Guardian is the member of the Organization who instigates the rite for someone of which they are a guardian.
Ex: ["Guardian" Mr. and Mrs. Wilson] BAPTIZED their son.

lexunit.name: christen.v

lexunit.name: baptism.n

lexunit.name: eucharist.n

lexunit.name: confirmation.n

lexunit.name: pray.v
lexunit.definition: COD: address a prayer to God or another deity

lexunit.name: prayer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a solemn request for help or expression of thanks addressed to God or another deity

lexunit.name: mass.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the Christian Eucharist or Holy Communion, especially in the Roman Catholic Church.

lexunit.name: communion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the service of Christian worship at which bread and wine are consecrated and shared; the Eucharist

lexunit.name: bless.v

lexunit.name: blessing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a prayer asking for God's favour and protection

lexunit.name: consecrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or declare sacred

lexunit.name: anoint.v
lexunit.definition: COD: smear or rub with oil, especially as part of a religious ceremony

lexunit.name: unction.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of anointing someone with oil or ointment as a religious rite

lexunit.name: rite.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a religious or other solemn ceremony or act

lexunit.name: ritual.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a religious or solemn ceremony involving a series of actions performed according to a prescribed order.

lexunit.name: confirm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: administer the religious rite of confirmation to

lexunit.name: circumcise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cut off the foreskin of (a young boy or man) as a Jewish or Islamic rite or cut off the clitoris, and sometimes the labia, of (a girl or young woman) as a traditional practice in some cultures

lexunit.name: circumcision.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or practice of circumcising

lexunit.name: service.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a ceremony of religious worship according to a prescribed form

lexunit.name: ordination.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of ordaining someone in holy orders

lexunit.name: vigil.n
lexunit.definition: COD: (in the Christian Church) the eve of a festival or holy day as an occasion of religious observance. [Eccl]

lexunit.name: confession.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal admission of one's sins privately to a priest.

lexunit.name: baptize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: administer baptism to

lexunit.name: sacrament.n
lexunit.definition: COD: (in the Christian Church) a religious ceremony or ritual regarded as imparting divine grace, such as baptism, the Eucharist, and (in the Catholic and many Orthodox Churches) penance and the anointing of the sick.

lexunit.name: ordain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confer holy orders on.

lexunit.name: christening.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the ritual of giving a name at baptism in a Christian Church

lexunit.name: consecration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the performing of a ritual which makes or declares an object to be sacred; ordination to a sacred office

lexunit.name: bar mitzvah.n

lexunit.name: sacrifice.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the practice or an act of killing an animal or person or surrendering a possession as an offering to a deity.

lexunit.name: initiation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: formal admission into a group, usually by means a ritual

lexunit.name: initiate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: admit formally into a society or group, typically with a ritual.

lexunit.name: rite of passage.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a ceremony or event, e.g. marriage, marking an important stage in someone's life

lexunit.name: evensong.n
lexunit.definition: COD: (especially in the Anglican Church) a service of evening prayers, psalms, and canticles

lexunit.name: worship.n
lexunit.definition: COD: religious rites and ceremonies.

lexunit.name: vesper.n
lexunit.definition: COD: evening prayer.

lexunit.name: sacrifice.v
lexunit.definition: COD: offer or give up as a sacrifice.

lexunit.name: order.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to ordain (passive only - archaic)

lexunit.name: exercise.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a ceremony or procession

frame.name: Physical_entity
frame.definition: An Entity exists in some Place at some time.

fe.name: Constituents
fe.definition:
Salient parts that make up a locale.
Ex: This is the oldest ["Constituents" oak] FOREST in Dorsetshire.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: A thing (either abstract or physical) that exists with some degree of permanence.

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the locale about. Ex: ["Formational_cause" glacial] VALLEY Ex: ["Formational_cause" impact] CRATER Should also include words that indicate that there was no salient formation: Ex: ["Formational_cause" virgin] WOODLAND

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: ULTIMATELY TO BE _replaced_ BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the names of locales. Ex: LAKE ["Name" Constance] Ex: ["Name" Pike's] PEAK Ex: The CITY ["Name" of Paris] Ex: The ["Name" Indonesian] ARCHIPELAGO

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Entity belongs to.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A place that a physical Entity is located with respect to.
Ex: All the THINGS ["Place" on the bureau] are small.

lexunit.name: object.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: a tangible, visible entity

lexunit.name: thing.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: a tangible, visible entity

frame.name: Weather
frame.definition: Ambient conditions of temperature, precipitation, windiness, and sunniness pertain at a certain Place and Time. Further Specification of the conditions that pertain may also be indicated. Ex: ["X" A ["Specification" blustery] STORM] ["Gov" blew] ["Gov" in]. Ex: _There_ _was_ a ["Spec" thick] BLIZZARD ["Time" last night]. Ex: ["X" An armada of HAILSTORMS] ["Gov" swept] through the region.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the weather occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the weather occurs.

fe.name: Specification
fe.definition: This FE identifies a further Specification of the weather conditions. Ex: An ["Spec" icy] STORM hit the Northeast last night.

lexunit.name: stormy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: affected or disturbed by a storm.

lexunit.name: snowy.a
lexunit.definition: FN: marked by or covered by snow or looking as if it were

lexunit.name: blizzard.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a severe snowstorm with high winds.

lexunit.name: storm.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a violent disturbance of the atmosphere with strong winds and usually rain, thunder, lightning, or snow.

lexunit.name: storm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be stormy.

lexunit.name: hailstorm.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an event where large pellets of frozen water fall amidst modest to high winds and possibly other precipitation.

lexunit.name: rainstorm.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a storm with heavy rain.

lexunit.name: snowstorm.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a heavy fall of snow accompanied by a high wind.

lexunit.name: weather.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of the atmosphere at a place and time as regards temperature, wind, rain, etc.

lexunit.name: thunderstorm.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a storm with thunder and lightning and typically also heavy rain or hail.

lexunit.name: climate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the general weather conditions prevailing in an area over a long period.

lexunit.name: lowering sky.n
lexunit.definition: FN: weather in which dark, low clouds presage a storm.

lexunit.name: sunshine.n

frame.name: People
frame.definition: This frame contains general words for Individuals, i.e. humans. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have an Age, Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. Ex: A ["Person" man] ["Origin" from Phoenix] was shot yesterday. Ex: She gave birth to a ["Descriptor" screaming] ["Person" baby]yesterday. Ex: I study ["Age" 16-year-old] ["Persistent_characteristic" female] ["Person" adolescents]. Ex: I am dating an ["Ethnicity" African-American] ["Person" man]. Ex: She comforted the ["Descriptor" terrified] ["Person" child]. Ex: I always thought of him as a ["Persistent_characteristic" stupid] ["Person" man].

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition: The Person is the human being.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

fe.name: Context_of_acquaintance
fe.definition:
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
Ex: Hey, where'd that ["coa" museum] GUY go? Ex: Is that the WOMAN ["coa" from the rally]?

frame.name: Attention_getting
frame.definition:
This frame covers terms used to get someone's attention, including Interjections (e.g. _hey_, _yo_) and certain terms of address (Address_term), the latter of which may serve the function of attention getting.
Ex: ["Interj" HEY]. Ex: ["Interj" Hey], ["Add_t" boy]. Ex: ["Interj" Hey], ["Add_t" boy], come over here now!

fe.name: Address_term
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Address_term as used to get someone's attention, and may be a proper name. Ex: ["Add_t" Boy], come over here right now! Ex: ["Add_t" Billy], come over here right now!
Tag this constiuent with the FE Interjection on a secondary FE layer.

fe.name: Interjection
fe.definition: Interjection identifies the attention getting element. Ex: ["Interj" Hey], boy, come over here now!

frame.name: Inchoative_attaching
frame.definition:
An Item comes to be attached to a Goal, with a Connector forming a bond between the Handle of the Item and the Goal (or some part of it). Alternatively, multiple Items may form a bond between each other.
Ex: According to plan, ["Item" the front part of the hull] ["Manner" quietly] ATTACHED ["Goal" to the docking gear].
Ex: ["Items" The cells] BIND ["Result" together].

fe.name: Connector
fe.definition:
Connector identifies the instrument used to attach, usually in a _with_-PP.
Ex: The remoras ATTACH to the whale ["Connector" with their strong jaws].

fe.name: Handle
fe.definition:
Handle identifies the point of attachment on the Goal to which the Item attaches.
Ex: The remoras ATTACH ["Handle" by the mouth].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
Item identifies the entity that comes to be attached to the Goal.
Ex: ["Item" Remoras] ATTACHED to the dolphins.

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
Items identifies the plural items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment.
Ex: ["Items" The cells] BIND together.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal identifies the location to which the first Item is attached.
Ex: The remoras ATTACH ["Goal" to the underside of the whale].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Result of an attaching event.
Ex: The cells BIND ["Result" together].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item comes to be attached to a Goal.
