frame.name: Being_attached
frame.definition:
An Item is attached by a Handle, via a Connector, to a Goal, or Items are attached to each other. There may be a Dependent_state, which depends crucially on Item(s) being attached.
Ex: ["Item" My thumb] _was_ STUCK ["Goal" to the tube of glue].
Ex: ["Items" The prisoner's legs] were SHACKLED.

fe.name: Connector
fe.definition:
Connector identifies the instrument used to attach and is usually expressed in a _with_-PP.
Ex: The tarp is TIED down ["Conn" with a rope].

fe.name: Handle
fe.definition:
Handle identifies the point of attachment on the Item.
Ex: Harry was TIED ["Handle" by the neck] to the tree.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
Item identifies the entity that comes to be attached to the Goal.
Ex: ["Item" A handle] was AFFIXED to the door.

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
Items identifies the plural items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment.
Ex: ["Items" The boats] remained TIED together.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal identifies the location to which the Item(s) is attached.
Ex: The boat remained ANCHORED ["Goal" to the coastline].

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition:
Dependent_state identifies the state of the Item or Itemswhich depends on the existence of the attachment.
Ex: The tarp is TIED ["State" down] with a cord. Ex: Harry's hands are TIED ["State" down]with cords.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item is in an attached state to a Goal, or two Items are attached to each other.
Ex: The tiny stick was FASTENED ["Manner" tightly] to his wrist.

frame.name: Reasoning
frame.definition: An Arguer presents a Content, along with Support, to an Addressee. The Content may refer elliptically to a course of action or it may refer to a proposition that the Addressee is to believe. Some lexical units (e.g. "prove") indicate the speaker's belief about the Content.Ex: Jan ARGUED ["Content" that the evidence was inadmissable].Ex: Jan ARGUED ["Content" against the admissability of the evidence].Ex: Jan PROVED ["Content" that the evidence was inadmissable].

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The Arguer wants the Addressee to entertain the Content, which can be a proposition to be believed or a course of action to be taken, based on the Support presented.Ex: Jan ARGUED ["Content" that the evidence was inadmissable].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This FE identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the Content is conveyed.Ex: Jan ARGUED ["Medium" in writing] that the evidence was inadmissable.

fe.name: Arguer
fe.definition: The Arguer presents the Content before the Addressee.Ex: ["Arguer" Jan] ARGUED that the evidence was inadmissable.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: Addressee is the entity before whom the Arguer presents a Content. Ex: Jan ARGUED ["Addressee" to the court] that the evidence was inadmissable.

fe.name: Support
fe.definition: Support lends epistemic support to a claim, or provides a reason for a course of action.Ex: Jan ARGUED that gun was inadmissable as evidence ["Support" because the police didn't have a search warrant].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifes the Manner in which an Arguer argues.Ex: Jan ARGUED ["Manner" convincingly] that the evidence was inadmissable.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Arguer presents Content to an Addressee.Ex: Jan ARGUED the evidence was admissable ["Means" by waving the warrant in the air].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase describing a participant in an action.Ex: Jan ARGUED that the evidence was inadmissable ["Depictive" in a tuxedo].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an arguing event.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an arguing event occurs.Ex: Jan ARGUED the defendant's innocence ["Degree" beyond a shadow of a doubt].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which an Arguer makes an argument for the Content.
Ex: The government ARGUED ["Time" in August] that the prisoners should not be released

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the location where an argument is made by an Arguer.
Ex: The young men will be ARGUING their policies ["Place" in the school auditorium].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time for which the Arguer presents his or her reasoning to the Addressee.
Ex: He ARGUED ["Duration" for hours] that chess is a sport

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: An entity related to the Content.

lexunit.definition: COD: demonstrate by evidence or argument the truth or existence of

frame.name: Cause_to_be_wet
frame.definition:
An Agent causes an Undergoer to be wet with a Liquid. In this frame, the Liquid can be a liquid or gas. Undergoers are porous objects, but not hollow (like containers).
Ex: ["Agent" Jo] SOAKED ["Undergoer" the dog] ["Liquid" with water]. Ex: ["Agent" Ellen] WET ["Undergoer" the sponge] ["Liquid" with water].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the Undergoer to become wet.
Ex: ["Agt" Hannah] DRENCHED the cat with anti-flea ointment.

fe.name: Liquid
fe.definition:
The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates or covers the Undergoer. It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with.
Ex: ["Agent" Jo] SOAKED ["Undergoer" the dog] ["Liquid" with water].

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
The Undergoer takes up the Liquid through its pores or has the Liquid covering its surface.
Ex: Ellen WET ["Undergoer" the sponge] with water.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner or way in which the Agent wets the Undergoer.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an the Agent wets the Undergoer

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent wets the Undergoer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent wets the Undergoer and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent wets the Undergoer.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally wets the Undergoer.
Ex: Colin DOUSED the burning pot ["Ins" with a fire extinguisher].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of wetness.
Ex: ["Cause" The sprinklers] DRENCHED me.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree to which the Agent wets the Undergoer.
Ex: Ryan DOUSED the fire with water ["Degr" until it stopped smoldering].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The cloth was WETTED ["sub" around the edges].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE describes the reason for the state of the Cause_to_be_wet event.

frame.name: Impact
frame.definition: While in motion, an Impactor makes sudden, forcible contact with the Impactee, or two Impactors both move, mutually making forcible contact. Ex: ["Impactor" The massive metal foot] HIT ["Impactee" the ground] ["Result" with a huge thud].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The reason for which an Impact occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Impactor

fe.name: Impactee

fe.name: Impactors

fe.name: Speed

fe.name: Force

fe.name: Period_of_Iterations
fe.definition: The Time throughout which the impact repeatedly takes place.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Impactors or the Impactor during the impact.

frame.name: Scalars
frame.definition: An Item has a specified Value for some property. (Which property is determined by the target.)

fe.name: Item

frame.name: Detaining
frame.definition: The Authorities hold a Suspect under suspicion of having commited a crime (Charges). The Holding_Location and period of detention (Duration) may also be specified. Ex: ["Authorities" The police] HELD ["Suspect" Mr. Smith] ["Holding_Location" in the slammer] ["Charges" on charges of killing his lawyer].

fe.name: Authorities

fe.definition: This FE identifies the person who is taken into custody and held, under suspicion of having committed a crime.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the detaining occurs.

fe.name: Holding_Location
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Suspect is confined. Ex: ["Suspect" Marge] was under ARREST ["Hold_L" in the county jail].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the length of time that the Suspect spends in confinement.

fe.name: Legal_basis
fe.definition: This FE identifies the law, act, or precedent that allows the Authorities to detain the Suspect. Ex: ["Authorities" The government] HELD ["Suspect" him] ["Basis" under the Why Not Act].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Authorities detain a Suspect.

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition: This FE identifies the state of the Suspect being held. Ex: ["Suspect" Snake] was HELD ["Dependent_state" in communicado].

lexunit.name: custody.n
lexunit.definition: FN: imprisonment before a trial

lexunit.name: under_arrest.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: having been taken into custody

lexunit.name: hold.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep or detain.

lexunit.name: detain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep (someone) in official custody.

lexunit.name: intern.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confine as a prisoner.

lexunit.name: internment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of confining, especially during war

lexunit.name: on the loose.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: having escaped from confinement.

lexunit.name: at large.a
lexunit.definition: COD: escaped or not yet captured.

frame.name: Precipitation
frame.definition: Water in some solid or liquid form (the Precipitation) falls from the sky at a particular Place and Time, lasting for a particular Duration. The Rate or Quantity of precipitation may also be indicated.

fe.name: Precipitation
fe.definition: The water in liquid or solid form that falls from the sky is the Precipitation. Ex: ["Precipitation" Rain] pelted him for an hour.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: The Quantity of Precipitation that falls within a certain Duration. Ex: It RAINS ["Rate" only half an inch per year] around here.

fe.name: Quantity
fe.definition: The Quantity is the amount of Precipitation that has fallen in a precipitation event or events. It is usually measured as the height that the Precipitation attains if prevented from further movement. Ex: It RAINED ["Quantity" six inches] last night.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The area which experiences precipitation.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the precipitation event lasts.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs. Ex: It will probably be RAINING ["Time" at five o'clock].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the reason for the precipitation event. Ex: It RAINS ["Cause" because of high humidity].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the precipitation falls. Ex: It DRIZZLED ["Manner" softly].

fe.name: Temperature
fe.definition: This FE identifies the temperature of the precipitation. Ex: I was standing in the ["Temperature" cool] DRIZZLE.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

lexunit.name: rain.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the condensed moisture of the atmosphere falling visibly in separate drops.

lexunit.name: rain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rain falls.

lexunit.name: rain_event.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the overall event (e.g., storm) in which rain is falling to the ground

lexunit.name: snow.v
lexunit.definition: COD: snow falls.

lexunit.name: snow.n
lexunit.definition: COD: atmospheric water vapour frozen into ice crystals and falling in light white flakes or lying on the ground as a white layer.

lexunit.name: snowfall.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a fall of snow.

lexunit.name: rainfall.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the fall of rain.

lexunit.name: drizzle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rain lightly.

lexunit.name: drizzle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: light rain falling in very fine drops.

lexunit.name: sleet.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sleet falls.

lexunit.name: sleet.n
lexunit.definition: COD: rain containing some ice, or snow melting as it falls.

lexunit.name: downpour.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a heavy fall of rain.

lexunit.name: hail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: pellets of frozen rain falling in showers from cumulonimbus clouds.

lexunit.name: hail.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hail falls.

lexunit.name: precipitation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: rain, snow, sleet, or hail that falls to or condenses on the ground.

lexunit.name: precipitation_event.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the overall event (e.g., storm) in which rain, snow, sleet, or hail is falling to the ground

lexunit.name: shower.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a brief and usually light fall of rain or snow.

lexunit.name: torrent.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strong and fast-moving stream of water or other liquid

lexunit.name: sprinkle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rain very lightly.

lexunit.name: torrential.a
lexunit.definition: FN: strong, plentiful and fast-moving, as a torrent

lexunit.name: shower.v
lexunit.definition: FN: rain briefly and lightly

lexunit.name: snow_event.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the overall event in which snow falls from the sky

frame.name: Coming_to_be
frame.definition:
An Entity comes into existence at a particular Place and Time which may take a certain Duration_of_endstate, have a Cause, or be formed from Components.
Ex: ["Entity" Problems] may ARISE ["Time" whenever an S1 sophont enters the game]. Ex: ["Entity" Mountains] ["Time" sometimes] FORM ["Period_of_Iterations" in as little as a million years]. Ex: ["Entity" A new paradigm] EMERGED ["Cause" from the discussion of nuclear weapons]. Ex: ["Entity" New Plants] FORM ["Components" from the cut veins] ["Period_of_Iterations" in two weeks].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Concrete or abstract entity that did not exist before the Time of the event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This is the Place where the new Entity comes into being.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifes the Time when a new Entity comes into existence.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: This FE labels the Cause of the formation of the Entity. Ex: New clarity COALESCED ["Cause" out of the hours spent simulating the climate].

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: This FE identifies the components out of which the Entity forms. Ex: New plants FORM ["Components" from cut veins] in two weeks.

fe.name: Duration_of_endstate
fe.definition: This FE identifies the length of time that the Entity exists after coming to be.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The form in which the Entity comes to be. Ex: Vishnu MATERIALIZED ["Role" in the form of a half man, half beast]. Ex: The megacorps stranglehold on property EMERGED ["Role" as a problem].

fe.name: Period_of_Iterations
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Period_of_Iterations during which habitual or iterative actions are performed.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Entity comes to be.

lexunit.name: form.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to develop

lexunit.name: come to be.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come into existence

lexunit.name: appear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come into existence

lexunit.name: arise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: originate

lexunit.name: emerge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become gradually visible or apparent.

lexunit.name: take shape.v

lexunit.name: develop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: start to exist

lexunit.name: coalesce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come or bring together to form one mass or whole.

lexunit.name: materialize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: appear

lexunit.name: spring up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: suddenly develop or appear

lexunit.name: come into existence.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (an entity) start to exist

lexunit.name: evolve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: develop gradually.

lexunit.name: evolution.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: gradual development

frame.name: Releasing
frame.definition: An Agent ends the captivity or inhibition of the motion of a Theme.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the individual who ends the confinement or captivity of the Theme.
Ex: ["Age" The police] RELEASED the suspect.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme is the person or object in motion released by the Agent.
Ex: The police RELEASED ["Theme" the suspect].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the release which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: The police RELEASED the suspect ["Manner" carefully].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action of the Agent which brings about the release.
Ex: He SET the entire convoy of prisoners FREE ["Means" by bribing the guards].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason identifies the reason for which the Agent are releasing the Theme.
Ex: The police RELEASED the suspect ["Reason" because he had a good alibi].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Agent release the Theme.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Theme ceases to be confined.
Ex: "Aren't you going to RELEASE us ["Place" here]?" she asked.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Timeidentifies when the Agent release the Theme.

fe.name: Location_of_confinement
fe.definition:
The location to which the Theme's motion was formerly inhibited.
Ex: She petitioned unsuccessfully for their RELEASE ["Loc" from Chateau D'If].

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world when the Releasing event occurs.

lexunit.name: release.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set free

lexunit.name: let go.v
lexunit.definition: COD: allow someone or something to go free

lexunit.name: set free.v
lexunit.definition: FN: allow to leave custody

lexunit.name: release.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of setting free

frame.name: Verdict
frame.definition: In this frame, which is a part of the Trial sequence, a Judge gives a Finding with respect to the Charges against the Defendant in a particular Case.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The Judge (which may be the jury, judge, magistrate or court) decides on the Finding.

fe.name: Finding
fe.definition: This FE identifies the outcome of the Judge's deliberation or consideration.

fe.name: Defendant
fe.definition: The person who stands accused of a crime and is subject to the verdict.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: This FE refers to the Charges with respect to which the verdict is being given.

fe.name: Case
fe.definition: The Case on which the verdict is being given.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Legal_Basis
fe.definition: This FE indicates the basis in law of a verdict. Ex: He was found GUILTY ["LBasis" under section 28 article 5].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances under which the verdict was reached. Ex: He was CONVICTED ["cir" on a four to three vote].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Judge acts.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Judge returns a particular verdict. Ex: Did you ACQUIT him ["Purp" just to get the publicity]?

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies an action that the Judge performs in order to return the verdict.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for the verdict given. Ex: The jury CONVICTED him on all charges ["Reason" because of the overwhelming evidence against him].

lexunit.name: pronounce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: declare or announce

lexunit.name: find.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a court) officially declare to be the case; (with against or for) make a decision against (or in favour of); judge to be guilty (or innocent).

lexunit.name: finding.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a conclusion reached as a result of an inquiry, investigation or trial

lexunit.name: ruling.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an authoritative decision or pronouncement

lexunit.name: convict.v
lexunit.definition: COD: declare to be guilty of a criminal offence by the verdict of a jury or the decision of a judge in a court of law.

lexunit.name: conviction.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the act or process of convicting someone; an instance of being convicted

lexunit.name: acquit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally declare not guilty of a criminal charge

lexunit.name: acquittal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a formal declaration that someone is not guilty of a criminal charge

lexunit.name: verdict.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a decision on an issue of fact in a civil or criminal case or inquest

lexunit.name: clear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: show or declare officially to be innocent

lexunit.name: guilty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: culpable of a specified wrongdoing.

lexunit.name: not_guilty.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not culpable of a specified wrongdoing.

frame.name: Creating
frame.definition: A Cause leads to the formation of a Created_entity.

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Components that are attached together to form a Created_entity. Ex: The force of the rock above FORMED diamond ["Components" out of the carbon].

fe.name: Created_entity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity that the Agent intentionally creates. Ex: They were ASSEMBLING ["Created_entity" grenades] for export.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action. We WANDERED around ["Depictive" naked]. Cicadas SCREECH ["Depictive" unseen from within].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place ehere the Agent intentionally creates the new entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifes the Time when an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the instrument with which an Agent intentionally creates a Created_entitiy.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: A secondary agent with whom the Creator intentionally creates the Created_entity.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: The Creator creates a created entity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

fe.name: Purpose_of_created_entity
fe.definition: The Creator's intended purpose for the Created_entity.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: The Beneficiary benefits in some way from the creation of the Created_entity.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The Role that the Created_entity takes (or is intended to take, if there is a Creator).

fe.name: Period of iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: create.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring into existence.

lexunit.name: form.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring together parts to create

lexunit.name: assemble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fit together the component parts of.

lexunit.name: produce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: create or form as part of a physical, biological, or chemical process.

lexunit.name: production.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of producing as part of a physical, biological, or chemical process.

lexunit.name: formation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of creating by gathering components

lexunit.name: generate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to arise or come about.

lexunit.name: yield.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce or deliver (a result or gain).

lexunit.name: issue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally send out or make known.

lexunit.name: issuance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an instance of making a provision known or accepted.

frame.name: Try_defendant
frame.definition: A Defendant is tried by a Jury or Judge in a Court for Charges. This frame perspectivalizes the general Trial frame.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The Judge heads the court where the case is tried. An expression referring to the court may also stand in for the Judge. Ex: ["Judge" Judge Murphy] will TRY the defendant for murder. Ex: ["Judge" The court] is currently TRYING several South American militants on charges of vehicular manslaughter.

fe.name: Court
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Court in which a case is tried.

fe.name: Defendant
fe.definition: The Defendant is being tried for the Charges in Court.

fe.name: Jury
fe.definition: This FE identifies the people who are charged by the Court to listen to the testimony, evidence, and arguments, and come to a consensus about the guilt or innocence of the Defendant.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the case is tried.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the case is tried.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Charges brought against the Defendant.

fe.name: Governing_authority
fe.definition: The Defendant is tried under the laws of the Governing_authority. Ex: ["GA" The United States] will TRY the accused bomber in a federal courthouse.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner of the trial of the Defendant. Ex: Thomas Klein was TRIED ["Manner" in absentia].

lexunit.name: try.v
lexunit.definition: COD: subject (someone) to trial, or investigate and decide (a case or issue) in a formal trial.

frame.name: Employment_scenario
frame.definition: An Employee and Employer enter into an employment relation, wherein the Employee remains employed for some Duration of time, and finally the relationship ends either by the Employee leaving the job or the Employer letting go (or firing) the Employee. To each of these events there are concomitants, such as agreeing to/signing a contract for entering employment, compensation and performance of a service for the employment period itself, and severance for the dissolution of the relationship. There are several other events involved, including preparatory actions on the part of the Employer (posting the Position), the prospective Employee's part (looking for a job), or both (job interviews). In addition, there is the possibility of change in the relationship of Employer and Employee during the employment period, such as a change in Position (e.g. promotion, demotion) and a change in Compensation (e.g. raise, paycut).

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
Ex: ["Empee" I] was just HIRED yesterday!

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition: The label given to a particular type of employment. Ex: Look, I wasn't HIRED ["Position" as your waitress]!

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
Ex: I was HIRED ["Task" just to empty the trash cans].

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Field in which one works. Ex: He has been WORKING ["Field" in finance] for years.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

frame.name: Hiring
frame.definition:
An Employer hires an Employee, promising the Employee a certain Compensation in exchange for the performance of a job. The job may be described either in terms of a Task or a Position. In some cases, the Employee FE will also indicate the Position (see fourth example below).
Ex: ["Empee" John] was HIRED ["Task" to clean up the file system]. Ex: ["Emper" IBM] HIRED ["Empee" Gates] ["Posit" as chief janitor]. Ex: ["Empee" I] was RETAINED ["Compense" at $500 an hour]. Ex: ["Emper" The A's] SIGNED ["Empee" a new third baseman] ["Compense" for $30M]. The same sentence (above) should also have the FE Position on the second layer: Ex: The A's SIGNED ["Posit" a new third baseman] for $30M.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person whom the Employer takes on as an Employee, obligating them to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
Ex: ["Employee" I] was just HIRED yesterday!

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The person (or institution) that takes on an Employee, giving them Compensation in return for the performance of an assigned Task.
Ex: Last month, ["Emper" IBM] HIRED Mike Zisman to head up its storage software group.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition:
The Compensation is the payment that the Employee is set to receive for performing an assigned Task.
Ex: They fired our management, HIRED him ["Compense" for 20% more] and gave him a free office to set up his own company.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employer hires an Employee.
Ex: The three young men were given medals and ["Manner" hastily] COMMISSIONED.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: Actually, he HIRED me ["Place" in a bordello].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when an Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: Guess who just got HIRED ["Time" today]!

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: John HIRED her ["Purp" to make his wife jealous].

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
The action that the Employee is taken on by the Employer to do.
Ex: I was HIRED ["Task" just to empty the trash cans].

fe.name: Position
fe.definition:
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Ex: Look, I wasn't HIRED ["Posit" as your waitress]!

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: The Field that the Employee is going to work in for their Employer.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity that the Employer uses to hire the Employee.
Ex: The congressman HIRED him ["Instrument" with personal funds] as an aide

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action by the Employer whereby the hire is brought about.
Ex: The manager HIRED me ["Means" with a handshake].

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition:
The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.
Ex: She couldn't figure it out but suggested that I'd be good for the job, so they HIRED me ["cb" part time] at first.

lexunit.name: hire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: employ for wages.

lexunit.name: sign.v
lexunit.definition: COD: engage for or commit oneself to work by signing a contract.

lexunit.name: retain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep engaged in one's service.

lexunit.name: commission.v
lexunit.definition: COD: order or authorize (someone) to do or produce something.

lexunit.name: take on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: hire

lexunit.name: hire.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of hiring.

lexunit.name: give job.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take somebody on as an employee

lexunit.name: commission.n
lexunit.definition: FN: act of commissioning

frame.name: Employing
frame.definition:
An Employer employs an Employee whose Position entails that the Employee perform certain Tasks in exchange for Compensation.
Ex: ["Emper" I] EMPLOYED ["Empee" him] ["Posit" as Chief Gardener] ["Dur" for ten years].

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The FE Employee denotes the person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
Ex: ["Empee" I] was EMPLOYED by an international corporation.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The Employer is the person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.
Ex: ["Emper" I] EMPLOYED him as Chief Gardener for ten years.

fe.name: Field
fe.definition:
The FE Field identifies the field in which the Employee is employed.
Ex: He was EMPLOYED["Field" in finance] fourteen years ago.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The FE Manner identifies the way in which an Employer hires an Employee.
Ex: The three young men were given medals and ["Manner" hastily] COMMISSIONED.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The FE Place identifies the location where the Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: Actually, he EMPLOYED me ["Place" at the downtown office ].

fe.name: Position
fe.definition:
The FE Position indicates a particular type of employment.
Ex: I'm not EMPLOYED ["Position" as your waitress]!

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The FE Purpose identifies what the Employer intends to accomplish through the hiring of the Employee.
Ex: John EMPLOYS bodyguards ["Purpose" to protect him from previous clients].

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
The Task indicates the action/duty that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
Ex: I am EMPLOYED ["Task" to collect the trash].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The FE Time identifies the time at whcih the Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: Charles has been an EMPLOYEE of Microsoft ["Time" since 1998]!

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The FE Duration identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.
Ex: I EMPLOYED him as Chief Gardener ["Dur" for ten years].

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition:
The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.
Ex: Chrysler EMPLOYS 1000 skilled worker ["Contract_basis" full-time].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describes a characteristic or the entity in question.

lexunit.name: employ.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give work to (someone) and pay them for it.

lexunit.name: employer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person that employs people

lexunit.name: employee.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person that is employed for wage or salary

lexunit.name: commission.v
lexunit.definition: COD: order or authorize (someone) to do or produce something

lexunit.name: personnel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: people employed in an organization or engaged in an organized undertaking

lexunit.name: staff.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the employees of a particular organization

lexunit.name: employment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of employing

lexunit.name: worker.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who works.

frame.name: Get_a_job
frame.definition: A new Employee obtains a Position with an Employer, with which there are certain Tasks associated; in exchange for the performance of these Tasks, the Employee receives Compensation from the Employer.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition:
The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
Ex: He said he wanted to play for a contender, and then he SIGNED ON ["Compense" for a lot of money] with a team that is not a contender.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person who enters an employment relation with an Employer.
Ex: In spring of 1983, ["Empee" Tom] SIGNED ON at the historic Wawona Hotel in Yosemite National Park, and continues to perform there nightly in the hotel?s piano parlor. .

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The person (or institution) that the Employee enters an employment relationship with.
Ex: He later played for the Scottish Claymores of the NFL Europe League in the spring of 2001, then SIGNED ON ["Emper" with Baltimore] in July of 2001

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee enters an employment relationship with an Employer.
Ex: Van Auken ["Mnr" eagerly] SIGNED ON with Pennsylvania.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the Employee enteres an employment relationship with an Employer.
Ex: I had SIGNED ON ["Place" right there] with the rest of the freaks.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition:
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Ex: In 1973 Franco Acerbis SIGNED ON ["Posit" as a mechanic for the Italian enduro team].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Employee enters an employment relationship.
Ex: Aengaela SIGNED ON with the Company ["Purp" to learn the family business].

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
The action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
Ex: In the end, however, Gaskill opted to remain out West and SIGNED ON ["Task" to play Oscar Marone on CBS's The Bold and the Beautiful].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when an Employee signs on with an Employer.
Ex: Things have been very busy with the new job since I SIGNED ON ["Time" in June, 2001].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action by which the Employee enters an employment relationship.
Ex: After interviewing, he SIGNED ON ["Means" with a handshake] in 1988.

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition:
The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.
Ex: In addition, Kellie Anngotell and Emil Fredette have HIRED ON ["cb" part-time].

lexunit.name: sign on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: commit oneself to employment

lexunit.name: hire on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take a job

frame.name: Quitting
frame.definition:
An Employee voluntarily leaves the service of an Employer.
Ex: ["Empee" Leah] QUIT ["Position" her job] ["Time" after one month] ["Reason" because of an evil force].
Ex: It's Time for ["Empee" Glenn Hubbard] to QUIT ["Position" as CEA Chair] Ex: ["Emper" Its chief executive officer] has RESIGNED ["Reason" amid a reorganization that will also eliminate about 20 percent of its work force]. Ex: ["Position" Its chief executive officer] has RESIGNED amid a reorganization that will also eliminate about 20 percent of its work force. Ex: You should fill in your name, the defendant's name, and ["Time" the date and time] ["Emper" you] GAVE NOTICE. ["Position" DNI]

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person who is obligated to perform some task in order to receive compensation.
Ex: ["Empee" I] just QUIT yesterday!

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The person (or institution) in whose employ the Employee stood.
Ex: He replaces Michael Lawrie, 50, who QUIT ["Emper" IBM] to run Siebel.

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: The Field that one works in. Ex: He might QUIT ["Field" showbusiness] for years.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee leaves the job.
Ex: Los Angeles junior high school teacher named Patricia Ann Carruthers QUIT her job ["Mnr" in a huff].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: Actually IQUIT ["Place" in the lobby] before I got to my office.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition: The label given to a particular type of service that the employer quits. Ex: I QUIT ["Position" as a professional player]!

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Employer hires the Employee. Ex: John RESIGNED ["Purpose" to join the private sector].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when an Employer hires the Employee.
Ex: Guess who just QUIT ["Time" today]!

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for which the Employee quits.
Ex: North QUIT ["Reason" over the mismanagement scandal].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means whereby the act of quitting is accomplished Ex: ["Time" Lately,] ["Employee" many workers] have been QUITTING ["Means" by simply not showing up for work].

lexunit.name: quit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: resign from (a job).

lexunit.name: resign.v
lexunit.definition: COD: voluntarily leave a job or position of office.

lexunit.name: retire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: leave one's job and cease to work, especially because one has reached a particular age.

lexunit.name: stand down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to resign from (a job) due to pressure

lexunit.name: resignation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of resigning.

lexunit.name: retirement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or fact of retiring.

lexunit.name: give notice.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to notify one's employer of a resignation

lexunit.name: step down.v
lexunit.definition: COD: withdraw or resign from a position or office.

lexunit.name: leave.v
lexunit.definition: FN: quit a job

frame.name: Firing
frame.definition: An Employer ends an employment relationship with an Employee. There is often a Reason given for the action.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person who is let go by their Employer.
Ex: ["Empee" I] was just FIRED yesterday!

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The person (or institution) that end an employment relationship with an Employee.
Ex: Dominic Mallozzi claims ["Emper" United Trust Bank] FIRED him from a job at the bank's Palmer Township branch because of he's HIV positive.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employer fires an Employee.
Ex: Five were ["Mnr" hastily] FIRED, and the federal government is investigating possible insider trading violations

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the Employer fires the Employee.
Ex: The phone in his small apartment in the town of Milan rang and he dreaded it. He was going to be FIRED ["Place" right there].

fe.name: Position
fe.definition:
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Ex: Doc Rivers was FIRED ["Posit" as coach of the Orlando Magic].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employer fires the Employee.
Ex: John FIRED her ["Purpose" to make his the other employees nervous].

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
The action that the Employee is relieved from doing for the Employer
.Ex: I was FIRED ["Task" from training the new actors].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when an Employer fires the Employee.
Ex: Guess who just got FIRED ["Time" today]!

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for which the Employee is terminated.
Ex: North was DISMISSED ["Reason" for gross mismanagement of funds].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The means whereby the Employer fires the Employee
Ex: ["Employer" Pat] fired ["Employee" Jan] ["Means" by leaving a letter of dismissal on his desk]

lexunit.name: discharge.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: dismiss from employment.

lexunit.name: dismiss.v
lexunit.definition: COD: discharge from employment.

lexunit.name: can.v
lexunit.definition: COD: dismiss from a job or reject as inadequate.

lexunit.name: fire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: dismiss from a job.

lexunit.name: shitcan.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (informally) fire

lexunit.name: sack.v
lexunit.definition: COD: dismiss from employment.

lexunit.name: terminate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: end the employment of.

lexunit.name: let go.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (euhpemistically) discharge from a job

lexunit.name: lay off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: temporarily or permanently discharge worker(s)

lexunit.name: dismissal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an instance of discharging from employment

lexunit.name: firing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: cease to employ.

lexunit.name: give the boot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: dismiss from job

lexunit.name: lay-off.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a temporary or permanent discharge of a worker or workers.

lexunit.name: the sack.n
lexunit.definition: COD: dismissal from employment.

lexunit.name: termination.n
lexunit.definition: FN: ending the employment of a person

lexunit.name: downsize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a company) shed staff.

frame.name: Part_inner_outer
frame.definition:
This frame concerns Parts of objects that are defined relative to the center or edge of the object. The Part is a part of the Whole and the Part_Prop describes a property of the Part.
Ex: She discarded the ["Part" EXTERIOR] ["Whole" of the walnut]. Ex: She preferred a sparse ["Whole" church] ["Part" INTERIOR] . .
In cases where the TARGET is an adjective, it has a special relationship with the noun that it modifies such that a phrase which is a syntactic argument of the noun is semantically available to fill the argument structure of the adjective, as in "the OUTSIDE ["Part" row] ["Whole" of the class]"Ex: The INNER ["Part" shelf] ["Whole" of the bookcase] was lying on the floor.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: This element describes the Part of the larger Whole.Ex: She only ate the ["Part" SKIN] ["Whole" of the apple].

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: An undivided entity having all its Parts.Ex: She eats only the ["Part_Prop" thick] ["Part" SKIN] ["Whole" of the banana].

fe.name: Part_Prop
fe.definition: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.Ex: Sue ate the ["Part_Prop" thick] ["Part" SHELL] ["Whole" of the pistachio].

lexunit.name: outside.a
lexunit.definition: COD: situated on or near the outside.

lexunit.name: outer.a
lexunit.definition: COD: outside; external.

lexunit.name: inside.a
lexunit.definition: COD: situated on or in, or derived from, the inside.

lexunit.name: exterior.a
lexunit.definition: COD: forming, situated on, or relating to the outside.

lexunit.name: inner.a
lexunit.definition: COD: situated inside; close to the centre.

lexunit.name: outside.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the external side or surface of something.

lexunit.name: skin.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the peel or outer layer of a fruit or vegetable or a thin outermost layer

lexunit.name: lining.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a layer of different material covering or attached to the inside of something

lexunit.name: perimeter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the outermost parts or boundary of an area or object

lexunit.name: centre.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a point in the middle of something that is equally distant from all of its sides, ends, or surfaces

lexunit.name: exterior.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the outer surface or structure of something.

lexunit.name: inside.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the inner side or surface of a thing

lexunit.name: interior.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the interior part of something

lexunit.name: interior.a
lexunit.definition: COD: situated within or inside; inner.

lexunit.name: middle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a middle point or position.

lexunit.name: shell.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the hard protective outer case of a mollusc or crustacean, turtle, egg, seed, kernel, etc.

lexunit.name: surface.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the outside part or uppermost layer of something.

frame.name: Shapes
frame.definition:
This frame contains words which describe the dimensional extent and Shape of a Substance. These words do not make reference to a Part-whole relationship. There can also be a descriptor of the Shape, Shape_prop.
Ex: She held a ["Shape" SQUARE] ["Substance" of cloth ].

fe.name: Substance
fe.definition: A Substance of which pieces can be extracted.Ex: Sue ate a ["Shape_prop" big] ["Shape" SQUARE] ["Substance" of cake].

fe.name: Shape
fe.definition: This is the Shape that the Substance is in.Ex: I ate a ["Shape" STICK] ["Substance" of butter].

fe.name: Shape_prop
fe.definition: This describes a property of the Shape, e.g. it's size.Ex: Sue ate a ["Shape_prop" big] ["Shape" SQUARE] ["Substance" of cake].

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of units of the measured Substance. Ex: Serena found ["Count" two] ["Shape" SQUARES] ["Substance" of coth] in the cabinet.

lexunit.name: square.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a plane figure with four equal straight sides and four right angles.

lexunit.name: sheet.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a flat , frequently rectangular portion of a substance

lexunit.name: coil.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a length of something wound in a joined sequence of concentric rings.

lexunit.name: cube.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a symmetrical three-dimensional shape contained by six equal squares.

lexunit.name: stick.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long, thin object or piece of something

lexunit.name: strip.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long, narrow piece of cloth, paper, etc.

lexunit.name: stretch.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a continuous expanse

lexunit.name: ribbon.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long, narrow strip of something.

lexunit.name: expanse.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a wide continuous area of something, typically land or sea.

lexunit.name: circle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: round plane figure whose boundary consists of points equidistant from the centre.

lexunit.name: ball.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a solid or hollow sphere.

lexunit.name: length.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a stretch or piece of something.

lexunit.name: shape.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the external form or appearance of someone or something; the outline of an area or figure.

lexunit.name: curve.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a line or outline which gradually deviates from being straight for some or all of its length.

lexunit.name: circular.a
lexunit.definition: FN: Being in the shape of a circle.

lexunit.name: line.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a one-dimensional shape of some substance

lexunit.name: row.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a line (often occurring adjacent to other rows)

lexunit.name: triangle.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a three-sided geometric shape

lexunit.name: wedge.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a subpart of a circular whole

lexunit.name: v.n
lexunit.definition: FN: shaped like the letter 'V'

lexunit.name: oval.n
lexunit.definition: FN: egg-shaped; elliptical

lexunit.name: round.a
lexunit.definition: FN: circular

lexunit.name: ellipse.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the shape that occurs from slicing a cone with an oblique plane (that is not a parabola or hyperbola)

frame.name: Boundary
frame.definition: This frame contains words that describe a Boundary between two Entities. In many cases, the Boundary is the border between an Entity and some unnamed space, generally conceived of as empty.

fe.name: Boundary
fe.definition: The region which is between the Entities or between the Entity and empty space.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The entity that has a Boundary.

fe.name: Entities
fe.definition: The joint construal of both Entities next to the Boundary.

lexunit.name: border.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a line separating two countries or other areas.

lexunit.name: boundary.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a line marking the limits of an area.

lexunit.name: edge.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the outside limit of an object, area, or surface.

lexunit.name: line.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a boundary (between)

frame.name: Part_edge
frame.definition:
This describes a part_whole relationship where the Part provides the boundary between the Whole and what is not that object. The Part can exist along a continuum of width. It can be modified by an Orientation that specifies the particular portion of the edge of a Part_prop which describes a property of the Part.
Ex: We came to the ["Orientation" southern] ["Part" EDGE] ["Whole" of the town ] .

fe.name: Orientation
fe.definition: This is a property of the Part that determines the portion of the Part.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: An undivided entity having all its Parts.Ex: The show takes place on the ["Part_prop" western] ["Part" EDGE] ["Whole" of town].

fe.name: Part_prop
fe.definition: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.Ex: Sue painted the ["Part_prop" longer] ["Part" EDGES] ["Whole" of the dollhouse].

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: Part is that which forms a boundary between the Whole and what is not the object.

lexunit.name: edge.n
lexunit.definition: COD:.the outside limit of an object, area, or surface.

frame.name: Part_ordered_segments
frame.definition: In this frame a Part is part of a larger Whole comprised of parts that are ordered. The Part can be modified by the Part_prop or the number of the part can be given by Ordinality.Ex: I sat through the ["Ordinality" first] ["Part_prop" interminable] ["Part" ACT] ["Whole" of the play ] . Ex: Tess finished a ["Whole" dissertation] ["Part" CHAPTER] .

fe.name: Ordinality
fe.definition: This is the number of the sequence of Parts.Ex: I sat through the ["Ordinality" first] ["Part_prop" interminable] ["Part" ACT] ["Whole" of the play] .

fe.name: Part_prop
fe.definition: A property relating to the Part of a Whole. Ex: I sat through the ["Ordinality" first] ["Part_prop" interminable] ["Part" ACT] ["Whole" of the play] .

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: A part of a larger Whole. Ex: I sat through the ["Ordinality" first] ["Part_prop" interminable] ["Part" ACT] ["Whole" of the play] .

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: An undivided entity having all its Parts. Ex: I sat through the ["Ordinality" first] ["Part_prop" interminable] ["Part" ACT] ["Whole" of the play] .

lexunit.name: inning.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each division of a game during which both sides have a turn at batting

lexunit.name: chapter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a main division of a book.

lexunit.name: act.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a main division of a play, ballet, or opera.

lexunit.name: book.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a main division of a literary work or of the Bible.

frame.name: Being_wet
frame.definition: An Item is in a state of wetness with the possibility of the wetting Liquid being mentioned, along with the Degree of wetness. Ex: ["Item" The mop] is DRENCHED ["Liquid" with water] ["Cause" from last night's rain].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The Item takes up the Liquid through its pores. Ex: ["Item" The mop] is DRENCHED with water.

fe.name: Liquid
fe.definition: The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates the Item. It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with. Ex: The mop was DRENCHED ["Liquid" with water].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item is wet. Ex: The mop is ["Degree" absolutely] DRENCHED.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause brings about the state of wetness, and is usually expressed in a _from_-prepositional phrase. Ex: The mop is DRENCHED ["Cause" from the rain].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected. Ex: The mop was DRENCHED ["Subregion" on the fringes].

lexunit.name: drenched.a
lexunit.definition: FN: to be wet throroughly, soaked

lexunit.name: damp.a
lexunit.definition: COD: slightly wet.

lexunit.name: moist.a
lexunit.definition: COD: slightly wet

lexunit.name: wet.a
lexunit.definition: COD: covered or saturated with liquid.

lexunit.name: soaked.a
lexunit.definition: FN: to be thoroughly wet

lexunit.name: saturated.a
lexunit.definition: FN: thoroughly soaked

lexunit.name: soggy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: very wet and soft

lexunit.name: sopping.a
lexunit.definition: COD: wet through

lexunit.name: sodden.a
lexunit.definition: COD: soaked through.

lexunit.name: soaking.a
lexunit.definition: FN: to be very wet

lexunit.name: waterlogged.a
lexunit.definition: COD: saturated with or full of water.

lexunit.name: humid.a
lexunit.definition: FN: damp

lexunit.name: dewy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: wet with dew.

lexunit.name: clammy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unpleasantly damp and sticky or slimy

lexunit.name: moistened.a
lexunit.definition: FN: wet

lexunit.name: sweaty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: soaked in sweat.

frame.name: Soaking
frame.definition: In this frame, an Agent places the Theme in the Medium for an extended period of time, with the intent that the Theme will be affected by and absorb some of the Medium. Ex: ["Agent" Ellen] SOAKED ["Theme" the beans] ["Medium" in the water] ["Duration" for 30 seconds].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the soaking.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the entity that changes location. Ex: Ellen SOAKED ["Theme" the beans] ["Medium" in the water] ["Duration" for 30 seconds] .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Theme is soaked.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent soaks the Theme.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the substance in which the Theme is submerged.Ex: Bobby SOAKED the potatoes ["Medium" in water] overnight.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Container that holds the Theme which is submerged and the Medium that it is in. Ex: SOAK the potatoes ["Container" in a medium-sized pan].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the submerging occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Agent soaks the Theme.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action of the Agent that brings about the soaking.
Ex: SOAK the beans ["Means" by placing the entire package, unopened, in the water].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The situation that the Agent hopes to bring about by soaking the Theme.

lexunit.name: soak.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become thoroughly wet by immersion in liquid.

lexunit.name: marinate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj. soak in a marinade.

frame.name: Cause_temperature_change
frame.definition:
In this frame, an Agent changes the temperature of an Item. A Temperature_goal can specify the desired temperature. A Temperature_change can also be indicated. The Temperature_start indicates the initial temperature.
Ex: ["Agent" Margaret Anne] CHILLED ["Item" the salad] ["Temperature_goal" to 30 degrees]. Ex: HEAT ["Item" the water] ["Temperature_change" 30 degrees].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent performs the intentional act which changes the temperature of the Item.
Ex: ["Agt" Ryan] REHEATED the pasta in the microwave.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The Item undergoes the temperature change.
Ex: Ryan REHEATED ["Item" the pasta] in the microwave.

fe.name: Temperature_goal
fe.definition:
The Temperature_goal is the temperature to which the Agent is heating or cooling the Item.
Ex: HEAT the syrup ["Temperature_goal" to 180 degrees].

fe.name: Temperature_change
fe.definition: The Temperature_change is the amount of difference between the intial and goal temperatures.

fe.name: Temperature_start
fe.definition:
Temperature_start is the initial temperature of the Item.
Ex: HEAT the sugar water mixture ["Temperature_start" from room temperature] until it reaches 180 degrees.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result is the resultant state of the Agent changing the temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that changes the temperature. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
Ex: ["Cause" The sun] WARMED the house.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.
Ex: REFRIGERATE the cookie dough ["Dur" for an hour] before baking.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The mousse was CHILLED ["Subregion" around the edges].

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Container that holds the Item whose temperature is being changed.
Ex: HEAT the potatoes ["Container" in a medium-sized pan].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Item.

fe.name: Hot_Cold_source
fe.definition:
The Hot_Cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.
Ex: We CHILLED the drinks ["Hot_Cold_source" on ice].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the temperature change occurs.
Ex: Bill COOLED the jello ["Circumstances" at room temperature].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Item approaches (an implicit) Temperature_goal, which is often construed to be the ambient temperature.
Ex: You'll probably have to wait a while to WARM your legs UP ["Degr" completely].

lexunit.name: heat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make hot or warm

lexunit.name: warm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make warm

lexunit.name: cool.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become at a fairly low temperature

lexunit.name: refrigerate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: subject (food or drink) to cold in order to chill or preserve it.

lexunit.name: heat up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make hot or warm

lexunit.name: cool down.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to become at a fairly low temperature

lexunit.name: warm up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make at a higher temperature

lexunit.name: reheat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: heat again.

lexunit.name: chill.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make cold.

lexunit.name: overheat.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become too hot

frame.name: Cause_change_of_phase
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Undergoer to undergo a change of phase. The Result of the change may be given, along with the Initial_state and the Circumstances under which the change can occur.
Ex: ["Agent" Bob] MELTED ["Undergoer" the butter].
Ex: ["Agent" Sally] DEFROSTED ["Undergoer" the chicken] ["Purpose" to eat for dinner].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent causes the Undergoer to change phase.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent intentionally affects the Undergoer.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent intentionally affects the Undergoer.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally affects the Undergoer

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer undergoes a change of phase brought about by the Agent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where change of phase occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent affects the Undergoer,

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the change of phase occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the phase change occurs

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the Agent changes the phase of the Undergoer

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition: This is the original state of the Undergoer.Ex: ["Undergoer" The rock ] was SOLIDIFIED ["Initial_state" from its molten state ] .

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result is the result of the change of phase. Ex: ["Undergoer" the butter ] was MELTED ["Result" to a runny consistency]

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: These bottles MELTED ["sub" at the top] and stuck together

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-Agent which brings about the change in the Undergoer. Ex: ["Cause" The sun] MELTED ["Undergoer" the ice].

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Container that holds the Undergoer whose phase is being changed .Ex: MELT the butter["Container" in a medium-sized pan].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time for which the Agent changes the phase of the Undergoer.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Agent or Undergoer at the time of phase change.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The Medium is the substance which surrounds the Undergoer and facilitates its phase change.

fe.name: Hot/Cold_source
fe.definition: The Hot/Cold_source is the source of the heat or cool. Ex: ["Agent" We ] FROZE ["Undergoer" the fish] ["Hot/Cold_source" on ice ] .

lexunit.name: freeze.v
lexunit.definition: COD: turn into ice or another solid as a result of extreme cold.

lexunit.name: thaw.v

lexunit.name: melt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make liquefied by heating.

lexunit.name: defrost.v

lexunit.name: evaporate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: turn from liquid into vapour.

lexunit.name: liquefy.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become a liquid

lexunit.name: solidify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become hard or solid.

lexunit.name: flux.v

lexunit.name: unfreeze.v
lexunit.definition: COD: thaw.

lexunit.name: boil.v

frame.name: Change_of_phase
frame.definition:
In this frame an Undergoer undergoes a change of phase.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The water] FROZE. Ex: ["Undergoer" The rock] SOLIDIFIES ["Initial_state" from its molten state]. Ex: ["Undergoer" The lake] FROZE ["Result" solid]. Ex: ["Undergoer" The lake] FROZE ["Result" into ice]. Ex: ["Undergoer" The lake] FROZE ["Degree" to depths of 30 feet].

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
Undergoer is the entity that undergoes a change of phase.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The water] FROZE.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The FE Result indicates the result of the change of phase.
Ex: The lake FROZE ["Result" solid].

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition:
This is the original state of the Undergoer.
Ex: The rock SOLIDIFIED ["Initial_state" from its molten state].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree to which the Undergoer changes phase.
Ex: The lake FROZE ["Degree" to depths of 30 feet].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Undergoer changes phase.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Undergoer changes phase.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the Undergoer changes phase.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the phase change occurs.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The cloth FROZE ["sub" around the edges].

lexunit.name: sublimation.n

frame.name: Cause_to_be_dry
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Dryee (either a surface or an entire entity, inside and out) to become dry. This should not include examples like "drying tears" or "drying spills" as these are in the Removing frame.
Ex: ["Agent" Michael] DRIED ["Dryee" the clothes]. Ex: ["Agent" Abby] DRIED OUT ["Dryee" the room] ["Instrument" with a dehumidifier].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the Dryee to become dry. Ex: ["Agent" Michael] DEHYDRATED ["Dryee" the apples]. Ex: ["Agent" Abby] DRIED OUT ["Dryee" the room] ["Instrument" with a dehumidifier].

fe.name: Dryee
fe.definition: The Dryee is the entity which has the water removed from it. Ex: ["Agent" Michael] DEHYDRATED ["Dryee" the apples]. Ex: ["Agent" Abby] DRIED OUT ["Dryee" the room] ["Instrument" with a dehumidifier].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.
Ex: ["Agent" Abby] DRIED OUT ["Dryee" the room] ["Instrument" with a dehumidifier].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies theManner in which an the Agent dries the Dryee.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which Agent intentionally affects the Dryee and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of dryness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
Ex: ["Cause" The wind] DRIED ["Dryee" the porch].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The cloth was DRIED ["sub" around the edges].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the length of Time that the drying takes.

fe.name: Temperature
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Temperature at which heat is applied to the Dryee.
Ex: He DRIED the apples in the oven for a day ["Temp" at 350 degrees].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Dryee ends up dry.
Ex: First, the remains should be ["Degr" completely] DESICCATED before you begin the extraction.

lexunit.name: desiccate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remove the moisture from.

lexunit.name: dry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become or cause to become dry.

frame.name: Being_dry

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The Item exists in a state of dryness. Ex: ["Item" The mop] is DRY.

fe.name: Degree

fe.name: Subregion

frame.name: Preserving
frame.definition:
In this frame an Agent preserves an Undergoer in order to prevent it from decaying. A Medium may be used.
Ex: ["Agent" Bill] MUMMIFIED ["Undergoer" John].
Ex: ["Agent" Tess] PICKLED ["Undergoer" the beets] ["Medium" in vinegar].
Ex: ["Agent" The Smiths] DRIED ["Undergoer" the apples].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act that leads to the preservation.Ex: ["Agt" Arlene] PICKLED the cucumbers.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the substance in which the Undergoer might be submerged to be preserved. Ex: Tess PICKLED the beets ["Medium" in vinegar].

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer is organic matter that undergoes the preservation.Ex: Tess PICKLED ["Undergoer" the beets] in vinegar.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which an an Agent performs the Preserving.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Agent preserves the Undergoer.Ex: Hannah CURED the shrimp ["Means" by injecting them with brine].Ex: This salami was CURED naturally ["Means" in salt].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent preserves the Undergoer.Ex: Jake ["Manner" painstakingly] EMBALMED the next body.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the preserving occurs.Ex: Mr. Amber EMBALMED the woman's body ["Place" in Turkey] in 1922.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Agent preserves the Undergoer.Ex: Mr. Amber EMBALMED the woman in Turkey ["Time" in 1922].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Agent preserves the Undergoer.Ex: Jude PICKLED the onions ["Purpose" to increase their potency].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an action.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of Time for which the process of Preserving is ongoing.Ex: ...oak CURED ["Dur" for eight years].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive phrase describing one of the participants.Ex: The herring was CURED ["Depict" with its innards still inside it].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Undergoer is preserved from decaying.
Ex: The corpse had been MUMMIFIED ["Degree" completely].

lexunit.name: mummify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (especially in ancient Egypt) preserve (a body) as a mummy

lexunit.name: pickle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: preserve (food) in pickle.

lexunit.name: embalm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: preserve (a corpse) from decay, originally with spices and now usually by injection of a preservative.

lexunit.name: salt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: preserve with salt.

lexunit.name: cure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: preserve (meat, fish, tobacco, or an animal skin) by salting, drying, or smoking.

lexunit.name: mummification.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of preserving s.t., usually a body, from decomposition.

lexunit.name: preservation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of preventing (food) from decomposing.

lexunit.name: can.v
lexunit.definition: COD: preserve in a can.

lexunit.name: preserve.v

lexunit.name: embalming.n
