lexunit.name: dry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: preserve by evaporating the moisture from

frame.name: Rotting
frame.definition:
In this frame an Undergoer, which is an organic substance, undergoes the natural process of decaying from an I_state to a Result.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The leaves] ROTTED ["Result" into a mass of slime]. Ex: ["Undergoer" The dresses] DECAYED ["I_state" from their former beauty].

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
The Undergoer is the entity that undergoes a change.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The leaves] ROTTED into a mass of slime. Ex: ["Undergoer" The dresses] DECAYED from their former beauty.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is where the rotting occurs.
Ex: Any traces of uneaten food will DECOMPOSE ["Place" in your tank] and foul the water.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time indicates when the rotting occurs.
Ex: ["Time" Before he could get to the specimen] , its entrails had DECOMPOSED so badly that they had to be thrown away.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason indicates the reason for which the Undergoer rots.
Ex: Typically, the front top six teeth will DECAY ["Reas" because of the way the child has sucked on its bottle].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The Result is the result of the change of phase of the Undergoer.
Ex: The leaves ROTTED ["Result" into a mass of slime]. Ex: A dead snail DECOMPOSES very rapidly, ["Result" fouling the water badly].

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition:
The Initial_state is the original state of the Undergoer.
Ex: The dresses DECAYED ["I_state" from their former beauty].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The Duration indicates the amount of time for which the Undergoer rots.
Ex: That thorn had been there , FESTERING, ["Dur" for months].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which the Undergoer changes.
Ex: A dead snail DECOMPOSES ["Spd" very rapidly], fouling the water badly.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The cloth was ROTTING ["sub" around the edges].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree expressions that indicate to what degree the Undergoer has changed.
Ex: Its entrails had ["Degree" totally] DECOMPOSED. Ex: Before he could get to the specimen , its entrails had DECOMPOSED ["Deg" so badly that they had to be thrown away].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that a rotting event takes place.
Ex: ["Frequency" Often], the food would PERISH because there was no refrigeration.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Rotting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (horribly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: The soldiers' wounds FESTERED ["Manner" slowly]

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that entails the Undergoer decaying.
Ex: And I've got a piece of ham that 'll SPOIL ["cir" if we don't eat it tonight].

lexunit.name: putrefy.v
lexunit.definition: COD: decay or rot and produce a fetid smell.

lexunit.name: rot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: decompose by the action of bacteria and fungi; decay or cause to decay

lexunit.name: decompose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of organic matter) decay; become rotten.

lexunit.name: decay.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rot or cause to rot through the action of bacteria and fungi; decompose.

lexunit.name: fester.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become rotten

lexunit.name: moulder.v
lexunit.definition: COD: slowly decay

lexunit.name: perish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rot or decay.

lexunit.name: spoil.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of food) become unfit for eating.

lexunit.name: decay.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state or process of decaying.

lexunit.name: rot.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process of decaying.

frame.name: Change_of_consistency
frame.definition:
In this frame an Undergoer changes its consistency. There may be a Initial_state and a Result.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The blood] CONGEALED. Ex: ["Undergoer" The liquid] GELLED ["Result" into a semi-solid mass].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the Result of the change of consistency of the Undergoer
Ex: The liquid GELLED ["Result" into a semi-solid mass].

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition:
This is the original state of the Undergoer.
Ex: The cheesecake finally HARDENED ["Initial_state" from its runny state].

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
Undergoer is the entity that undergoes a change.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The blood] CONGEALED. Ex: ["Undergoer" The liquid] GELLED into a semi-solid mass.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed at which the change of consistency occurs.
Ex: The jello SET ["Spd" in 30 minutes].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the consistency change occurs.
Ex: The jello SETS ["Circumstances" at room temperature].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The jello SET ["sub" around the edges].

lexunit.name: congeal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become semi-solid, especially on cooling.

lexunit.name: coagulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a fluid, especially blood) change to a solid or semi-solid state.

lexunit.name: jell.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set or become firmer

lexunit.name: clot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form or cause to form into clots

lexunit.name: soften.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become soft or softer

lexunit.name: harden.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become hard or harder

lexunit.name: curdle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: separate into curds or lumps

lexunit.name: thicken.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become thick or thicker

lexunit.name: set.v
lexunit.definition: COD: harden into a solid, semi-solid, or fixed state

lexunit.name: coagulation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of coagulating

lexunit.name: indurate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: harden

frame.name: Sufficiency
frame.definition:
An Item is located on a Scale relative to a critical value which is determined by some Enabled_situation. Generally, when the Enabled_situation is left unexpressed the Enabled_situation is interpreted to be the desirability of the Item being located within a particular range on the Scale. With many of the adjectives of this frame, the Scale is not explicitly mentioned; in such cases, the Scale is usually the quantity, incorporated in the meaning of the targets themselves, though in the case of ADEQUACY, etc. the Scale referred to is quality.
Ex: I probably have ENOUGH. ["Item" DNI] ["Enabled_situation" DNI]
Ex: ["Item" I] was ["Scale" mad] ENOUGH ["Enabled_situation" to scream].
Ex: ["Item" I] was TOO ["Scale" mad] ["Enabled_situation" to keep myself from screaming].
Ex: ["Item" I] was ["Degree" way] TOO ["Scale" hot]. ["Enabled_situation" DNI]
Ex: ["Item" The particles] are SUFFICIENTLY ["Scale" small] in diameter ["Enabled_situation" that they may be considered points].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The entity whose scalar property is specified.Ex: ["Item" The light] is probably bright ENOUGH.Ex: I have SUFFICIENT ["Item" paper] for the purpose.

fe.name: Scale
fe.definition: The Scale is the attribute of theItem that is being described.Ex: It was ["Scale" hot] ENOUGH to ignite the iron.Ex: The workforce is SUFFICIENT ["Scale" in number and proficiency] to finish the building in minimum time.

fe.name: Enabled_situation
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Enabled_situation by which the critical value is judged. Ex: Can He make a rock TOO heavy ["Enabled_situation" for Him to lift]? Ex: There's almost ENOUGH ["Enabled_situation" for thirty people]. Ex: That information SUFFICED ["Enabled_situation" to convince me]. Ex: Finding a parking spot is SUFFICIENTLY difficult ["Enabled_situation" that you'd do better to walk]. Ex: This legislation was INADEQUATE ["Enabled_situation" in that it allowed many obvious delinquents to escape prosecution].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree frame element indicates a modification of the value indicated by the target.Ex: The spell was ["Degree" almost] powerful ENOUGH to destroy the demonic pumpkin.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: enough.n
lexunit.definition: COD: as much or as many as is necessary or desirable

lexunit.name: enough.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: to the required degree or extent.

lexunit.name: enough.a
lexunit.definition: COD: as much or as many as is necessary or desirable

lexunit.name: suffice.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be enough or adequate.

lexunit.name: sufficient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: enough; adequate.

lexunit.name: sufficiently.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: adequately; with enough to meet the needs of

lexunit.name: insufficient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not enough.

lexunit.name: insufficiently.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: without adequate power, capacity, or competence

lexunit.name: adequate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: satisfactory or acceptable.

lexunit.name: adequately.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: satisfactorily or acceptably

lexunit.name: insufficiency.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the condition of being insufficient.

lexunit.name: adequacy.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality of being just satisfactory or adequate

lexunit.name: inadequacy.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a lack of the quality or quantity required; insufficiency

lexunit.name: inadequate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: lacking the quality or quantity required; insufficient for a purpose.

lexunit.name: inadequately.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: with a lack of the quality or quantity required; insufficienly for a purpose

lexunit.name: plenty.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large or sufficient amount or quantity; more than enough.

lexunit.name: plenty.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: fully; sufficiently.

lexunit.name: plenty.a
lexunit.definition: FN: more than adequate amount or supply

lexunit.name: ample.a
lexunit.definition: COD: enough or more than enough; plentiful.

lexunit.name: too.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: to a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible.

lexunit.name: so.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: to such a great extent.

frame.name: Travel
frame.definition: In this frame a Traveler goes on a journey, an activity, generally planned in advance, in which the Traveler moves from a Source location to a Goal along a Path or within an Area. The journey can be accompanied by Co_participants and Baggage. The Duration or Distance of the journey, both generally long, may also be described as may be the Mode_of_transportation. Words in this frame emphasize the whole process of getting from one place to another, rather than profiling merely the beginning or the end of the journey. Ex: ["Traveler" Ellen] JOURNEYED ["Goal" to Europe] ["Baggage" with five suitcases]. Ex: ["Traveler" Samantha] JOURNEYED ["Distance" 2500 miles] ["Co_participant" with her family] ["Path" by sea] ["Goal" to China].Ex: ["Traveler" The Osbournes] _took_ a TRIP ["Source" from Beverly Hills] ["Goal" to London] ["Mode_of_transportation" on the Concorde].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: This is the Area in which the traveling takes place. This frame element describes the enclosed area inside which travelling, of unspecified Source, Path or Goal takes place. Ex: We TRAVELLED in Europe.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: The Co_participant is the person or persons who accompany the Traveler on the journey.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE dientifies the Distance traveled.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time during which the trip occurs.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is the location where the travelers end up.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the traveling takes place. Ex: The Brownie troop TRAVELLED ["Manner" hurriedly].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action done by the Traveler by which the traveling is accomplished. Ex: I TRAVELED to London ["Mns" by hitchhiking and walking].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path is the route along which the travel takes place.

fe.name: Traveler
fe.definition: This is the living being which travels. Normally, the Traveler is expressed as an external argument.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the starting point of the trip.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the travel takes place. Ex: The Simpsons TRAVELLED ["Speed" at 60 km per hour].

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Traveler is effected, by their body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Traveler. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: Barney used to TRAVEL ["Mode_of_transportation" by bus ] a lot Ex: Strom TRAVELLED ["Mode_of_transportation" on foot ] to see the Pope

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the traveling occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the travel is undertaken.

fe.name: Baggage
fe.definition: The Baggage are the items necessary for travel that accompany the Traveler. Ex: Ellen JOURNEYED to Europe ["Baggage" with five suitcases].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency with which the Traveler makes the journey.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Traveler travels, i.e. the future state of affairs that will hopefully come about.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of times the trip is traveled by the Travelers.

fe.name: Period_of_Iterations
fe.definition: The Time throughout which the traveling repeatedly takes place.

fe.name: Travel_means
fe.definition: This FE applies to expressions that indicate documents, money, tickets, etc. which allow people to engage in travel. Ex: He TRAVELED to San Diego ["Travel_means" on a standby ticket].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Traveler during the journey. Ex: We TRAVELED around ["Depictive" unencumbered].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The affect of travel on a Traveler. Ex: We JOURNEYED ["Res" to exhaustion].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location of the motion. It describes the area in which motion (with a specified Source, Path or Goal) takes place.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction in which the Traveler goes.
Ex: They began their ODYSSEY ["Direction" north].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characterisitic of the traveling event.

frame.name: Reshaping
frame.definition:
In this frame an Deformer deforms an Undergoer possibly against a Resistant_surface such that it undergoes a shape-change from its canonical or original shape into the Result, a new shape. Some of these words indicate that the Result is an undesirable alteration of the norm, and in such cases the lexical unit is marked with the semantic type Negative. This frame does not include senses that specifically indicate causing harm to a living being.
Ex: ["Def" Ellen] CRUMPLED ["Undergoer" the paper] ["Result" into a ball]. Ex: ["Def" Michael] FLATTENED ["Undergoer" the can] ["Resistant_surface" against his head]. Ex: Mix butter and sardines very thoroughly , MASHING ["Und" them] ["Ins" with a fork] ["Result" until you have a smooth paste]. ["Def" CNI] Ex: ["Cause" A killer hurricane] ["Mnr" nearly] FLATTENED ["Und" Sylvester Stallone's five luxury homes in Hawaii].

fe.name: Deformer
fe.definition:
The Deformer is the one who does the reshaping.
Ex: ["Def" The lieutenant] CRUSHED it angrily with his boot before looking back at Hencke.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Deformer affects the Undergoer.
Ex: The lieutenant CRUSHED it angrily ["Ins" with his boot] before looking back at Hencke.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Deformer intentionally affects the Undergoer.
Ex: The lieutenant CRUSHED it ["Mnr" angrily] with his boot before looking back at Hencke.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The FE Means identifies the means by which the Deformer intentionally affects the Undergoer.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
The Undergoer is the entity acted on and that undergoes a change.
Ex: Jack plucked the flower out of his morning coat and closed his fist slowly over it , CRUSHING ["Und" it] into a pulp.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place indicates where the Deformer intentionally affects the Undergoer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Deformer intentionally affects the Undergoer.
Ex: What 's more , when you 've finished with it simply wipe it clean and then FOLD it flat["Purp" for easy storage].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The FE Time identifies when the Deformer intentionally affects the Undergoer.
Ex: The lieutenant CRUSHED it angrily with his boot ["Time" before looking back at Hencke].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The Result is the shape the Undergoer becomes.
Ex: Jack plucked the flower out of his morning coat and closed his fist slowly over it , CRUSHING it ["Result" into a pulp].

fe.name: Resistant_surface
fe.definition:
The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Deformer presses the Undergoer.
Ex: Michael FLATTENED the can ["Res_surf" against his head] . Ex: She CRUSHED her cigarette ["Res_surf" in the ashtray] and stood up to go.

fe.name: Locus
fe.definition:
The Locus is the locus of the reshaping action; it is essentially a simultaneous Instrument and Resistant_surface.
Ex: Russell CRUMPLED the paper cups ["Locus" in his fist].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The Cause is an animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
Ex: ["Cause" The strong winds] DEFORMED the structure of the outhouse. Ex: ["Cause" The rockslide] SQUASHED our summer villa.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The FE Iterations indicates the number of times the reshaping has occurred.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason indicates a state of affairs that the Deformer is responding to in performing the reshaping.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The degree to which the Undergoer is reshaped. Ex: The steamroller FLATTENED my shoes ["Degr" completely].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The part of the Undergoer which is directly affected by the reshaping. Ex: He WARPED the steering rack ["Subr" on the left side].

frame.name: Fluidic_motion
frame.definition: In this frame a Fluid moves from a Source to a Goal along a Path or within an Area. Ex: ["Fluid" The blood] SPURTED ["Source" from the wound]. Ex: ["Fluid" The water] GUSHED ["Goal" into the house] .

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: Area is the setting in which the Fluid's movement takes place on an unspecified Path. Ex: The Thames River FLOWS ["Area" throughout England].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE describes the phsyical extent of the motion of the Fluid.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Fluid moves.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is the location the Fluid ends up.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path is the trajectory along which the Fluid moves.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location the Fluid occupies initially.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This is the rate at which the Fluid flows.

fe.name: Fluid
fe.definition: The Fluid is the entity that changes location and moves in a fluidic way.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Fluid flows.

fe.name: Configuration
fe.definition: The Configuration encodes information about the amount, arrangement, and unitization of the flow. Ex: ["Fluid" The water] CASCADED ["Configuration" in torrents] . Ex: ["Fluid" The water] CASCADES ["Configuration" in large volumes].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Fluid flows.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the reason for the fluidic motion. Ex: It FLOWED ["Cause" from the sheer weight of water above it].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Fluid throughout the action.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the result of the Fluid moving.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place describes the location of the motion which has a specified Source, Path or Goal. Ex: ["Place" At Oregon Caves], a stream RUNS through the dining room.

frame.name: Being_rotted
frame.definition: An organic item, the Undergoer, has undergone the natural process of rotting and decaying with a possible expression of the Degree to which the rotting has occurred. Ex: ["Undergoer" The coconut milk] became RANCID.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer is the organic matter that has decayed. Ex: ["Undergoer" The coconut milk] became RANCID.

fe.name: Degree

frame.name: Revenge
frame.definition:
This frame concerns the infliction of punishment in return for a wrong suffered. An Avenger performs a Punishment on a Offender as a consequence of an earlier action by the Offender, the Injury. The Avenger inflicting thePunishment need not be the same as the Injured_Party who suffered the Injury, but the Avenger does have to share the judgment that the Offender's action was wrong. The judgment that the Offender had inflicted an Injury is made without regard to the law.
Ex: (1) ["Avenger" They] took REVENGE ["Injury" for the deaths of two loyalist prisoners]. Ex: (2) ["Avenger" Lachlan] went out to AVENGE ["Injured_Party" them]. Ex: (3) The next day, the Roman forces took REVENGE ["Offender" on their enemies.].

fe.name: Avenger
fe.definition:
The Avenger exacts revenge from the Offender for the Injury.
Ex: ["Avenger" We] want to AVENGE her.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs. Ex: Marie took ["Degree" terrible] REVENGE on Trevor.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive identifies a phrase describing the actor of an action.

fe.name: Offender
fe.definition:
The Offender has committed the earlier Injury for which the Avenger seeks revenge.
Ex: Jo had the affair as a kind of REVENGE ["Offender" against Pat]. Ex: Marie took terrible REVENGE ["Offender" on Trevor].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the revenge is performed.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This frame element refers to the Manner in which the Avenger exacts their revenge from the Offender.
Ex: They took ["Manner" brutal] REVENGE on the criminal.

fe.name: Punishment
fe.definition:
The Avenger carries out a Punishment in order to exact revenge on the Offender.
Ex: The team took REVENGE ["Punishment" with a resounding victory].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the revenge occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the revenge is performed.

fe.name: Injury
fe.definition:
The Injury is the injurious action committed by the Offender against the Injured_Party. This Frame Element need not always be realized, although it is conceptually necessary.
Ex: The team sought REVENGE ["Injury" for their 4-1 defeat last month].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of inflicting punishment for a wrong suffered.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the revenge occurs.

fe.name: Injured_Party
fe.definition:
This frame element identifies the constituent that encodes who or what suffered the Injury at the hands of the Offender. Sometimes, an abstract concept such a person's honour or their blood is presented as the element that has suffered the Injury. These also constitute instances of Injured_Party
Ex: Sam's brothers AVENGED ["Injured_Party" him]. Ex: We will decide later how to AVENGE ["Injured_Party" the blood of the fallen].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Avenger seeks revenge for the Injury.

frame.name: Corroding
frame.definition: In this frame the Undergoer, an inorganic item, undergoes a chemical process which renders it less useful, desirable or stable. Ex: Ex: ["Undergoer" The bike] RUSTED. Ex: ["Undergoer" The metal] CORRODED ["Result" into a mass of slime]. Ex: ["Undergoer" The bikes] RUSTED ["I-state" from their former beauty].

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition: Initial_state is the original state of the Undergoer. Ex: The bikes RUSTED ["I-state" from their former beauty].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifes the Duration of time for which the Undergoer corrodes.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the Undergoer corrodes.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Undergoer corrodes.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of the change of phase. Ex: The metal CORRODED ["Result" into a mass of slime ] .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Undergoer corrodes.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer undergoes a change. Ex: ["Undergoer" The bikes] RUSTED from their former beauty.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Undergoer corrodes.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected. Ex: The metal RUSTED ["sub" around the edges ].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Speed at which the Undergoer corrodes.

lexunit.name: rust.v

lexunit.name: corrode.v

frame.name: Partiality
frame.definition: This frame has to do with the bias or lack of bias of a Judge making an assessment concerning two or more Sides. The Sides may stand opposed to each other in a dispute or be alternatives in a situation of choice. The Domain in which the Judge is partial or impartial may be expressed as well as the Degree of bias or lack thereof. In sentences in this frame one may also find expressions of Manifestation_of_bias, i.e. expressions that tell us how the Judge's bias is realized.

fe.name: Decision_maker
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks the person whose objectivity in making assesment is being evaluated.
Ex: ["Decision_maker" The referee] was totally BIASED against our team.

fe.name: Side_1
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks one of the Sides in a dispute or one of the alternatives in a situation of choice.Ex: The umpire was PARTIAL ["Side_1" to the home team].

fe.name: Sides
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks phrases jointly expressing both Sides in a dispute or all of the alternatives in a situation of choice.Ex: The judge was NEUTRAL ["Sides" between the parties].

fe.name: Side_2
fe.definition: The second-mentioned of the Sides to a dispute or alternatives in a situation of choice.Ex: The judge FAVORED the defendant ["Side_2" over the plaintiff].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks expressions of a Domain or parameter with respect to which the Judge exhibits bias or lack thereof.Ex: The judge was ["Domain" politically] BIASED against the defendant.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks expressions that tell to what extent the Judge exhibited or lacked bias.Ex: The referee was ["Degree" totally] BIASED against the Giants.

fe.name: Manifestation_of_bias
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how the bias of the Judge expresses itself in their behavior or actions.Ex: The judge made a BIASED ["Manifestation_of_bias" decision].Ex: The referee was PARTIAL ["Manifestation_of_bias" when he called all those fouls].

fe.name: Dispute
fe.definition: The Dispute is the situation in which there is some conflict between two sides. Ex: ["Judge" My sister] remained NEUTRAL ["Dispute" in our disputes].

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for the partiality.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE denotes the time when the partiality occurs.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Decision_maker.
Ex: He had a NEUTRAL ["exp" smile] on his face.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner is the way in which the Decision_maker embodies the bias associated with him or her.
Ex: He was ["man" cooly] IMPARTIAL towards the matter.

lexunit.name: bias.n
lexunit.definition: COD: inclination or prejudice for or against one thing or person

lexunit.name: partial.a
lexunit.definition: COD: favouring one side in a dispute above the other;

lexunit.name: impartial.a
lexunit.definition: COD: treating all rivals or disputants equally.

lexunit.name: partiality.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality or state of being partial to one side in a dispute

lexunit.name: prejudge.v

frame.name: Corroding_caused
frame.definition:
In this frame, the Undergoer, an inorganic item, undergoes a chemical process caused by another entity, which renders it less useful, desirable or stable. The process may or may not be under the control of an Agent. Ex: Ex: ["Undergoer" The metal] was CORRODED ["Cause" by the water].
Ex: ["Cause" Acid rain] CORRODED ["Undergoer" the metal] ["Result" into a mass of slime].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Initial_state of the Undergoer. Ex: Acid rain CORRODED the metal ["I_state" from its former shininess].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Undergoer is corroded.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of the caused corrosion. Ex: ["Undergoer" The metal] was CORRODED ["Result" into a mass of slime].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer is corroded by the Cause. Ex: ["Und" The metal] was CORRODED by the water.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Speed at which the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion identifies the part of a larger whole that is affected. Ex: Acid rain CORRODED the metal ["sub" around the edges].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Cause corrodes the Undergoer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Undergoer is corroded.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
Cause identifies an animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that corrodes the Undergoer. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Cause.
Ex: ["Cause" Acid rain] CORRODED the metal.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that corrodes the Undergoer.

frame.name: Grinding
frame.definition: In this frame a Grinder or Grinding_cause causes an Undergoer to be broken into smaller pieces. A Result or Goal can be present.Ex: ["Grinder" Bill] GROUND ["Undergoer" the coffee beans] ["Result" into a fine powder].

fe.name: Grinding_cause
fe.definition: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that grinds. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic. Ex: ["Grinding_cause" The wind] GROUND ["Undergoer" the leaves] ["Result" into a fine powder].

fe.name: Grinder
fe.definition: The Grinder breaks the Undergoer into smaller pieces.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Locus
fe.definition:
The Locus is a description of the active zone of the Grinder, where the grinding most saliently takes place.
Ex: ["Grinder" Russell] GROUND ["Undergoer" the paper cups] ["Locus" under his foot].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result is the shape the Undergoer becomes.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer is the entity which undergoes the change brought about by the Grinder or Grinding_cause.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time for which the Grinder grinds the Undergoer.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This is where the Undergoer might end up, after undergoing the grinding process.

frame.name: Choosing
frame.definition:
A Cognizer decides upon the Chosen (either an item or a course of action) out of a set of Possibilities . The Cognizer may have an Intended_purpose for the Chosen. Often a Reason, which serves as the basis of the choice, is given.
Ex: ["Cognizer" The council] PICKED ["Chosen" you] ["Possibilities" out of all the pilots available] ["Intended_purpose" to head this mission]. Ex: ["Cognizer" No one] would CHOOSE ["Chosen" to live in such squalor]. Ex: If ["Chosen" no judge] was ["Manner" unanimously] SELECTED ["Time" in the previous round], play rock-paper-scissors pairwise.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive labels an independent descriptor of a Cognizer in a choosing event.
Ex: I could PICK you out of a crowd ["Depictive" blindfolded].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer chooses the Chosen out of the Possibilities. Ex: ["Cog" We]have to PICK a colour for the living room.

fe.name: Chosen
fe.definition: Chosen identifies the entity or course of action which is selected from among the Possibilities. Ex: I DECIDED ["Chosen" to give it another try]. Ex: We have to PICK ["Chosen" a colour for the living room].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Cognizer chooses the Chosen. Ex: He CHOSE her ["Reason" for her beauty].

fe.name: Possibilities
fe.definition: A Cognizer makes a choice from among a set of Possibilities. Possibilities are commonly expressed via an oblique phrase which indicates the alternative or alternatives, or by a subordinate clause (choosing to do it or choosing not to do it), typically headed by "whether or "if". Ex: They CHOSE their new guitarist ["Possib" out of more than 300 auditioners].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which bthe Cognizer accomplishes the choosing. Ex: He PICKED a name ["Means" by pointing to one in the phone book].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies thePlace where the choosing occurs. Ex: The winner was SELECTED ["Place" in the secret meeting room].

fe.name: Larger_purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Larger_purpose for which the Cognizer chooses. It exemplifies what the Cognizer hopes to accomplish by choosing the particular Chosen. Ex: Mr. Smith CHOSE Lord Rollins to be his running mate ["Larger_purpose" in order to further irritate all his critics].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer chooses the Chosen. Ex: I was n't CHOSEN ["Time" in the last round]. Ex: SELECT the jury ["Time" by 3 PM].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the selecting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). Ex: She ["Manner" wisely] CHOSE the plain-looking cup.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic occurs quite rarely in this frame and usually only as a PP Complement of a noun target: Ex: There is no CHOICE ["Top" about the way through]. Ex: If there is any CHOICE ["Topic" in hue] at all, choose the darkest.

fe.name: Intended_purpose
fe.definition: The Cognizerintends the Chosen to fulfill an Intended_purpose. Ex: SamsonCHOSE Delilah["Intended_purpose" as a wife].

fe.name: Contrast
fe.definition: The hypothetical Chosen that is less desirable for the Cognizer.

frame.name: Evaluative_comparison
frame.definition:
This frame is about the static comparison of an Profiled_item to a Standard_item, often with respect to some Attribute. In this frame, there is an inherent asymmetry between Profiled_item and Standard_item in that the two cannot be expressed jointly as a subject. Degree expressions are also found that indicate how close the items are to each other on the scale evoked by the Attribute. Furthermore, the particular value of the standard or item on a certain scale may be given by the Standard_attribute of the Profiled_attribute respectively.
Ex: The Sun is putting on ["Profiled_item" a show that] RIVALS ["Standard_item" the most sizzling Hollywood thrillers]. Ex: ["Profiled_item" Mexico's Copper Canyon] RIVALS ["Standard_item" the Grand Canyon] ["Attribute" in sheer beauty and drama]. Ex: ["Standard_attribute" Peyton Manning's passing yards] are EQUALLED ["Comparison_set" among NFL quarterbacks] ["Profiled_item" by only a select few]. Ex: ["Profiled_item" Few pianists] have ever EQUALLED ["Standard_attribute" the lightness and vivacity of his rhythm] . Ex: ["Profiled_attribute" The current price] MATCHES ["Standard_attribute" the price last year] .

fe.name: Profiled_item
fe.definition:
In active sentences, the Profiled_item is the grammatically more prominent one of the items that are compared and realized as the subject. .
Ex: ["Profiled_item" This PC] STACKS UP well against its competitors

fe.name: Standard_item
fe.definition:
In active setnnces, the Standard_item is the grammatically less prominent element, i.e. the object or an oblique.
Ex: This PC STACKS UP well ["Standard_item" against its competitors]

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
This Frame Elements marks constituents that indicate in which respect Item-1 and Item-2 are equal to each other.
Ex: The Tri-Cities STACK UP well against the competition ["Attribute" in the area of innovation]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how close the Profiled_item and the Standard_item are to each other on the scale evoked by the Attribute.
Ex: A peanut butter and jelly sandwich STACKS UP ["Degree" well] against other popular food items

fe.name: Standard_attribute
fe.definition: The Standard_attribute is used when the standard is a specific value on a scale. Ex: ["Profiled_item" We] EQUALLED ["Standard_attribute" father's skills] .

fe.name: Profiled_attribute
fe.definition: The Profiled_attribute is a particular value on a scale which is being compared to a Standard_item or Profiled_attribute.

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition: The Comparison_set includes the Standard_item and is what the Profiled_itemis judged with respect to.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Profiled_item rivals the Standard_item.
Ex: ["Place" In Africa], the level of drug resistance RIVALS even Noatirtin's vaunted efficacy.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Profiled_item rivals the Standard_item.
Ex: American caviar ["Time" now] RIVALS Russia's in quality.

frame.name: Desirability
frame.definition: This frame concerns an Evaluee being judged for its quality, i.e. how much it would probably be liked. In many cases, the Evaluee is implicitly judged good or bad relative to other instances of its type. The Evaluee's desirability is determined by one or more Parameters, which are scalar properties of the Evaluee. The evaluation may also explicitly be relativized to a set of Circumstances, a Comparison_set of entities that belong to the same class as the Evaluee, or an Affected_party. The Degree of goodness or badness may also be expressed. Ex: ["Evaluee" The view] was ASTONISHING. Ex: ["Circumstances" On clear days], ["Evaluee" the view] was EXCELLENT. Ex: The book is ASTOUNDING ["Parameter" in its scope]. Ex: The games have been AWFUL ["Affected_party" for the team].

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition:
The Evaluee is being judged for its quality.
Ex: He gave me another LAME ["Evaluee" excuse].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Evaluee is judged good or bad.
Ex: Smithers was doing an ["Degree" absolutely] SPLENDID job.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the quality of the Evaluee is being judged.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that denote a scalar property of the Evaluee with respect to which the Evaluee is judged.
Ex: The Beaujolais Nouveau is dazzling ["Parameter" in freshness].

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition: This FE marks expressions that indicate what class of things or events the Evaluee is being judged against.

fe.name: Affected_party
fe.definition:
The Affected_party indicates entities that benefit or suffer from the good or bad quality of the Evaluee.
Ex: The season was SPLENDID ["Affected_party" for the team].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Depictive encodes a state that the Evaluee is in and which does not represent a temporary or hypothetical set of Circumstances.
Ex: The aerial view is SUPERB ["Depictive" with its view of the harbour].

frame.name: Sole_instance
frame.definition: An Item is the only instance of its Type. Ex: ["Item" Steven] is the SOLE ["Type" survivor] in his family.

fe.name: Item

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type specifies a category which in principle could apply to multiple items, but which is limited to the Item.

frame.name: Beyond_compare
frame.definition:
Compared to its Competitors, a Standard is at the high end of a scale with respect to some Variable. The Competitors are frequently not realized syntactically. Ex: The taxpayer is supporting ["Standard" a system] UNMATCHED ["Variable" in wastefulness ]. Ex: The drawing room was a place of UNMATCHED ["Variable" squalor]. Ex: She was envious of her mother's MATCHLESS ["Variable" beauty].
Ex: When there is no overt Variable it must be understood from the context. Ex: ["Standard" He] was UNMATCHED ["Competitors" by any other politician of his time].
Ex: When the target occurs as the modifier of a predicate nominal, it is tagged as Standard, rather than Variable. Ex: They were MATCHLESS ["Standard" needlers of each other].

fe.name: Standard
fe.definition: The Standard is the entity that is located closest to the end of the scale evoked by some Variable. Ex: ["Standard" Hilary] was UNMATCHED by any politician in the country.

fe.name: Variable
fe.definition: The Variable is a property that evokes a scale along which the Standard is located closest to one extreme in comparison to its Competitors. Ex: Hilary possessed MATCHLESS ["Variable" integrity].

fe.name: Competitors
fe.definition:
The FE Competitors denotes the entities that are exceeded by the Standard with regard to the Variable.
Ex: Hilary was UNMATCHED ["Competitors" by any politician in the country]. Ex: He is UNRIVALLED ["Compet" even among tennis players] for his temper.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The spatial or temporal context in which the Standard is not matched by any Competitors.
Ex: Our commitment to service and quality is legendary and UNMATCHED ["dom" in Pakistan].

frame.name: Surpassing
frame.definition:
In this frame a Profiled_item is higher that its Standard_item on a scale with respect to some Attribute. The Extent of the difference between the Standard_item and the Profiled_item may also be mentioned. Futhermore, the particular value of the standard or profiled item on a certain scale may be given by the Standard_attribute of the Profiled_attribute respectively.
Ex: ["Profiled_item" Notices for the Shield Theater's production of Macbeth] SURPASSED ["Standard_item" all previous reviews] .
Ex: ["Profiled_item" Radio WKRR] ["Extent" far] SURPASSES ["Standard_item" all radio stations] ["Comparison_set" among rural radio stations] ["Attribute" as the leading source of regional news ] .
Ex: ["Profiled_item" We] SURPASSED ["Standard_attribute" father's skills] ["Time" before we were 12 ] .
Ex: ["Profiled_attribute" The current price] SURPASSES ["Standard_attribute" the price this time last year].

fe.name: Standard_item
fe.definition:
The FE Standard_item denotes the entities that are exceeded by the Item with regard to the Attribute.
Ex: In her time, she OUTSTRIPPED ["Standard" most politician in the country].

fe.name: Profiled_item
fe.definition:
The Profiled_item is the entity that is located closest to the end of the scale evoked by some Attribute.
Ex: ["Item" The buildings] were OUTSTRIPPED in beauty and grace many years ago.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The Attribute is a property that evokes a scale along which the Item is located closer to one extreme in comparison to the Standard_item.

fe.name: Extent
fe.definition: The Extent is the degree to which the Item surpasses the Standard.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Item is higher on the scale than the Standard.

fe.name: Standard_attribute
fe.definition: The Standard_attribute is used when the standard is a specific value on a scale. Ex: We SURPASSED ["Standard_attribute" our father's skills] .

fe.name: Profiled_attribute
fe.definition: The Profiled_attribute is a particular value on a scale which is being compared to an Attribute or Standard_item.

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition: The Comparison_set includes the Standard and is what the Item is judged with respect to.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

frame.name: Emitting
frame.definition: In this frame a Source_emitter discharges its Emission along a Path or to a Goal. Ex: (1) ["Source_emitter" The factory] EXUDES ["Emission" toxic fumes] ["Sub_source" from three large chimneys]. The Sub_source is only present when the actual Source_emitter is also given or is present in a possessive. Ex: (2) ["Emission" Light] is EMITTED ["Source_emitter" rom the tower] . Ex: (3) ["Emission" Noxious odors] are EMITTED ["Sub_source" from his feet] . In (3) we would tag 'his' as Source_emitter on a second layer because the inalienable possession on the Sub_source indicates the Source_emitter

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Source_emitter emits the Emission

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Source_emitter emits the Emission.

fe.name: Source_emitter
fe.definition: The Source_emitter is the item from which the Emission are discharged.

fe.name: Emission
fe.definition: The Emissions are discharged out of the Source_emitter.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which emission takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which emission occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Emission or Source_emitter.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE is an expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Emission

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE is the point at which the Emission ends up as a result of the motion.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Source_emitter emits.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: This FE is a description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source_emitter or Sub_source nor Goal.

fe.name: Sub_source
fe.definition: The Sub_source is the subregion of the Source_emitter which emits the Emission.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The rate at which emission occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Source_emitter emits the Emission

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Source_emitter emits the Emission.

fe.name: Carrier
fe.definition: This is the means of conveyance of the Emission. Ex: ["Emission" The acorn seeds] are EXCRETED ["Carrier" in the feces of squirrels] .

fe.name: Form
fe.definition: The Form is the state in which the Emission is emitted. Ex: ["Emission" The signal ] is EMITTED ["Form" as radio waves] .

lexunit.name: exude.v

frame.name: Compatibility
frame.definition: Item-1 and Item-2 are compatible with each other if they can exist or function together in some context without problems, conflict, or other undesirable situation. The set of Item-1 and Item-2 may be expressed jointly as Items. The Degree to which the Items are compatible may also be indicated, as may be a Parameter along whose lines the Items are compatible. Ex: Make sure ["Item-1" your site] is COMPATIBLE ["Item-2" with any browser]. Ex: ["Items" Our software applications] are COMPATIBLE.

fe.name: Item_1
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Item_1 marks the grammatically more prominent of the two entities, i.e.the subject in active clauses, when they are expressed separately.
Ex: ["Item_1" That technology] turned out not to be COMPATIBLE with the existing devices

fe.name: Item_2
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Item_2marks the grammatically less prominent of the Items when they are expressed separately.
Ex: My computer is not COMPATIBLE ["Item_2" with my new printer].

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
This FE is used when the Items are expressed jointly in a phrase, either a plural or a coordinated NP.
Ex: ["Items" Your socks] don't MATCH. Ex: ["Items" Creationism and Evolutionary Theory] don't JIBE.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate the extent to which two Items are compatible. Ex: These devices are ["Degree" absolutely] COMPATIBLE.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate a Parameter or respect in which the Items are said to be compatible, not in conflict.
Ex: The two applications are COMPATIBLE ["Parameter" in their essential features].

frame.name: Emanating
frame.definition: In this frame an Emission emanates from a Source along a Path or to a Goal. Ex: ["Emission" The light] EMANATES ["Source" from the tower]. Ex: ["Emission" The uranium particles] RADIATE ["Source" from the nuclear plant] .

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which the emanating takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the emanation occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Emission.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE is an expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Emission

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which emanation occurs.

fe.name: Emission
fe.definition: The Emissions are discharged out of the Source.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE is the point at which the Emission ends up as a result of the motion.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the emanating occurs.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: This FE is a description of a trajectory of emanation which is neither a Source nor Goal.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The rate at which emanation occurs

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the emanation occurs.

fe.name: Carrier
fe.definition: This is the means of conveyance of the Emission .

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location from which the Emission emanates.

fe.name: Form
fe.definition: The Form is the state in which the Emission is emitted. Ex: ["Emission" The signal] EMANATED ["Form" as radio waves] .

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the result of the emanating.

lexunit.definition: COD: flow out from.

frame.name: Motion_directional
frame.definition:
In this frame a Theme moves in a certain Direction which is often determined by gravity or other natural, physical forces. The Theme is not necessarily a self-mover.
Ex: ["Theme" The paper] FELL ["Path" to the floor]. Ex: ["Theme" The girl] DROPPED ["Distance" 13 stories] ["Result" to her death].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the general Area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.
Ex: Soot-contaminated snow FALLS ["Area" in Slovakia's mountainous regions].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Theme during the motion.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
Distance identifies a phrase that characterizes the extent of motion of the Theme.
Ex: The student PLUNGED from a road bridge ["Dist" more than 100 feet] to his death.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
Duration is used for the length of time for which the Motion takes place.
Ex: In one storm , 46 inches of rain FELL ["Dur" in 24 hours] .

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is the location the Theme ends up in (often unintentionally).
Ex: The rivals both FELL backwards ["Goal" into empty space].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Motion takes place.
Ex: A few heavy spots of rain FELL on the pavement ["Mnr" like coins].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Theme travels or to a landmark past which the Theme travels.
Ex: The boys PLUMMETED ["Path" down the stairs] into the basement.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Speed at which the motion occurs.
Ex: Michelle TOPPLED ["Spd" slowly] to the floor.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Motion occurs.
Ex: ["Time" In 1977] Nigel PLUNGED to his death in his car on a mountain road in southern France.

fe.name: Carrier
fe.definition:
The Carrier is the means of conveyance of the Theme.
Ex: Nigel PLUNGED to his death ["Car" in his car] on a mountain road in southern France.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme is the entity that changes location.
Ex: In 1977, ["Thm" Nigel] PLUNGED to his death in his car on a mountain road in southern France.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the location the Themeoccupies before the Motion occurs.
Ex: The man TOPPLED ["Src" from the passenger seat] into the road.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Result of the motion.
Ex: Marie shoved Simon, and he TOPPLED ["Result" over].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where motion specified by Source, Path or Goal occurs. Ex: ["Place" In the kitchen], the towel DROPPED onto the floor.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Theme crosses boundary as it enters a Goal region or exits a Source region.
Ex: Sucking in a deep breath, he PLUNGED ["Degree" fully] into the cold water

fe.name: Point_of_contact
fe.definition:
This FE is used for expressing some part of the Theme participant that makes contact with a horizontal surface.
Ex: With a loud thump, the monster FELL ["poi" on its back], the earth trembling as he hit the ground.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The shape formed by the path followed by the Theme.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An event whereby the motion of the Theme comes about.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction of motion of the Theme. Direction characterizes the Path of motion according to some system of orientation, most often that imposed by gravity.
Ex: I hope your egg does n't FALL ["dir" down] .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Any state of affairs or event from which the particular direction motion logically follows.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the agentive Theme hopes to bring about by moving in a particular direction.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world as the action occurs.

frame.name: Deciding
frame.definition:
A Cognizer makes a Decision, which may be about an entity or a course of action.
How (and whether) this frame is distinct from Choosing is currently up for debate.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer decides on a course of action.
Ex: ["Cog" Mo] DECIDED to quit the program.

fe.name: Decision
fe.definition: Decision identifies the entity or course of upon which the Cognizer decides. Ex: Mo DECIDED ["Dec" to quit the program].

fe.name: Possibilities
fe.definition:
A Cognizer makes a Decision from among a set of Possibilities.
Ex: Mo DECIDED on the blue sweater ["Poss" from the pile on the counter].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time or time period over which the Cognizer makes the decision.
Ex: The State Cabinet ["tim" today] DECIDED to file an appeal in the Supreme Court seeking an extension of six months for implementation of its judgment

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where the Cognizer makes the decision.
Ex: ["pla" At the first] crossroad we DECIDED to wait.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Cognizer makes a Decision

lexunit.definition: SMV: decide upon an option

frame.name: Stimulus_focus
frame.definition: In this frame either a Stimulus brings about a particular emotion or experience in the Experiencer or saliently fails to bring about a particular experience. Some words indicate that the Stimulus is characterized by the experience it is likely to evoke in an Experiencer and for these, the Experiencer may rarely be present. There may also be a Degree to which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer and Circumstances under which the experience occurs. There may also be a Comparison_set to which the Stimulus is compared and a Parameter that indicates the area in which the Stimulus has its effect. Ex: ["Stimulus" The view] is BREATHTAKING ["Circumstances" in January]. Ex: ["Stimulus" That movie] was ["Degree" quite] FASCINATING. Ex: That was certainly a GRATIFYING ["Stimulus" experience]. Ex: ["Stimulus" The report] was ["Degree" very] ALARMING ["Experiencer" to me].

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition: The Stimulus is the object or event which brings about the emotion in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer experiences the emotion brought about by the Stimulus

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the Stimulus evokes the emotion in the Experiencer

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Stimulus is able to bring about the emotion.
Ex: ["Circumstances" When sunny] the view is IMPRESSIVE.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
The Parameter is the area in which the Stimulus brings about an effect on the Experiencer.
Ex: This art work is ["Parameter" aesthetically] PLEASING. Ex: The book is ["Parameter" emotionally] DISTURBING.

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition: The Comparison_set is the set of individuals the Stimulus is compared to when determining the Degree of the emotional reaction. Ex: Randy is very STIMULATING ["Comparison_set" for a curator].

fe.name: Property
fe.definition: This FE indicates a Property of the Stimulus which causes a particular experience. Ex: The movie is TERRIFYING ["Property" in its realism] Ex: The movie is TERRIFYING ["Property" in its use of violence] Ex: The move was DISAPPOINTING ["Property" in every respect ].

frame.name: Businesses
frame.definition: A Proprietor owns or runs a Business which provides a Product (which may be goods or services).

fe.name: Product
fe.definition: Product identifies the product or service provided by the business. Ex: Josh runs a ["Product" copier toner] BUSINESS.

fe.name: Proprietor
fe.definition: Proprietor is the owner or chief participant in the business. Ex: I worked in ["Pptr" Goldberg's] legal PRACTICE . Ex: I didn't want to go into the ["Pptr" family] BUSINESS.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Descriptor indicates other characteristics of the business besides its Product and Proprietor. Ex: Chris runs a ["Desc" small] COMPANY in Idaho. Ex: I work for a ["Desc" non-profit] arts COMPANY.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place in which the business is located. Ex: Chris's BUSINESS ["Place" in Idaho] is thriving. Ex: ["Place" Local] COMPANIES are looking for more and more Spanish-speaking employees.

fe.name: Business
fe.definition: Business identifies the company or establishment. This may be the target itself or the Business_Name if it is an appositive not set off with commas (i.e. restrictive): Ex: The electronics ["Busn" FIRM] went bankrupt. In the appositive case, the name may also be tagged Business_Name on a second annotation layer. Ex: ["Gov" 1st Layer:] The Japanese electronics FIRM ["Busn" Sony] is growing rapidly. Ex: ["Gov" 2nd Layer:] The Japanese electronics FIRM ["BName" Sony] is growing rapidly.

fe.name: Business_Name
fe.definition: The name of the Business when it appears in an appositive set off by commas (non-restrictive): Ex: My clothing COMPANY, ["BName" Togs], is doing well.

fe.name: Service_provider
fe.definition: When a Business is described in terms of the professionals who work to produce the product or service, use Service_provider. Ex: John works as an office assistant for a FIRM ["ServP" of accountants].

frame.name: Desiring
frame.definition: An Experiencer desires that an Event occur. (Note that commonly a resultant state of the Event will stand in for the Event.) In some cases, the Experiencer is an active participant in the Event, and in such cases theEvent itself is often not mentioned, but rather some Focal_participant which is subordinately involved in the Event. Ex: Generally, the use of a word in this frame implies that the specific Event has not yet happened, but that the Experiencer believes that they would be happier if it did. Sometimes the Time_of_Event, Purpose_of_Event, or the Location_of_Event are mentioned without the explicit mention of the Event. Ex: ["Experiencer" I] only WANTED ["Foc" one piece of candy]. Ex: ["Exp" The company] _was_ EAGER ["Foc" for him] ["Event" to leave as soon as possible]. Ex: ["Exp" Susan] ["Degr" really] WISHES ["Event" that you 'd listen to her].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the Event to occur.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The change that the Experiencer would like to see.

fe.name: Focal_participant
fe.definition: This is the entity that the Experiencer wishes to be affected by some Event.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is a the extent of the Experiencer's Desiring.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The way in which the Experiencer desires something.
Ex: I WANTED more of her ["Manner" like a junkie wants his next fix].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason shows why the Experiencer wants the Event to occur. This FE occurs frequently as a PP complement headed by _for_.
Ex: She thinks people only WANT her on the project ["Reas" for the money she will contribute].
Ex: Pat YEARNS for power ["Reas" since that is the only thing he has ever known].

fe.name: Purpose_of_Event
fe.definition:
The Purpose_of_Event is the purpose pertaining to the desired Event.
Ex: I WANT that book ["Purp" for my test tomorrow].

fe.name: Time_of_Event
fe.definition: The time that the Event would ideally occur. Ex: I WANT porridge ["EvT" tomorrow].

fe.name: Location_of_Event
fe.definition:
The Location_of_Event is the place involved in the desired Event.
Ex: I WANT that box ["PEv" on top of the other one]. Ex: The prince WISHES you ["PEv" here] before matins.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Experiencer desires something. Ex: Oh, so ["Time" now] you WANT to go to the zoo!

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place. Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame. Ex: ["Place" In the car] I had DESIRED nothing more than to get here, but now that I'm here...

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Experiencer has desired something. Ex: His ["Dur" lifelong] YEARNING for success had finally been fulfilled. Ex: I've WANTED them to fix the sidewalk ["Dur" for years]!

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An aspect of the Experiencer that causes a desire. Ex: Do Italians have a ["Cause" genetic] YEARNING for pizza? Ex: ["Cause" Intellectually] he LONGED for success, but really he just wanted love.

fe.name: Role_of_focal_participant
fe.definition:
The Role is a role filled by a Focal_participant in the Event that the Experiencer desires.
Ex: Michaels originally WANTED Smith ["rol" as the new Late Night producer].

frame.name: Suitability
frame.definition:
This Frame is concerned with evaluating an Evaluee as being suitable for a Purpose or a User, presupposing some choice that is being made about which Evaluee to use for the Purpose or User. An LU like suitable.a thus implies that, given a particular Purpose or User, the Evaluee is one which could be or ought to be chosen. The Evaluee may be deemed suitable to a greater or lesser Degree. This frame has some similarity to the compatibility frame where two Items are evaluated with respect to their compatibility with each other against some background.
Ex: (1) We need to build ["Evaluee" more houses] SUITABLE ["User" for local residents]. Ex: (2) ["Evaluee" These chips] are not ["Degree" very]SUITABLE ["Purpose" for parallel processing]. Ex: (3) We are not sure about ["Evaluee" the Cathedral's] SUITABILITY ["Purpose" for Philharmonic concerts].

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks constituents expressing the entity that is judged to be more or less suitable for some Purpose or User.
Ex: Being a project leader is not a job for which ["Evaluee" everybody] is SUITED.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks constituents that express the Degree to which the Evaluee is suitable for the Context.
Ex: Please advise on the ["Degree" most] SUITABLE design

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks constituents that express the Purpose for which the Evaluee is judged to be suitable or unsuitable.
Ex: We need to plan more buildings SUITABLE ["Purpose" for disabled people].

fe.name: User
fe.definition: This FE marks expressions that indicate a User to whom

frame.name: Social_behavior_evaluation
frame.definition: In this frame the Behavior is judged by the speaker (or, in some cases, a separate Judge) against pre-existing social standards for that type of behavior. An Individual who is involved in the Behavior is assigned the same evaluation as the Behavior. This is an abstract frame that encodes the relationship between such frames as Mental_property, Sociability, Social_interaction_evaluation, Stinginess, and Volubility.

fe.definition: The Behavior is the action of the Individual on which the evaluation of the Individual's character is based.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the described Behavior deviates from the norm.

frame.name: Social_interaction_evaluation
frame.definition:
In this frame an Evaluee is judged by a (usually implicit) Judge to be of a certain character based on her or his Behavior towards other human beings; a specific Affected_party may be overtly mentioned along with the Degree to which the Evaluee behaves appropriately towards others. TheBehavior alone may be mentioned with the understanding that these behaviors characterize a property of the unmentioned Evaluee. The Evaluee's Behavior may be in the context of a Topic.
Ex: It was NICE ["Evaluee" of you] ["Behavior" to send a card].
Ex: ["Evaluee" Jim] was THOUGHTFUL ["Behavior" to email the directions].
Ex: ["Behavior" For Martha to smoke in the car] was ["Degree" extremely] INCONSIDERATE.
Ex: It was CRUEL ["Behavior" that he continued to call her].
Ex: ["Evaluee" Mary] was CRUEL ["Affected_party" to her friends].
Ex: Samson was a THOUGHTLESS ["Evaluee" person].
Ex: ["Evaluee" Mrs. Robinson] was always CONSIDERATE ["Affected_party" of her students].
Ex: ["Evaluee" The press] was always KIND ["Topic" about Madonna].
Ex: ["Evaluee" Lee] was NICE ["Topic" about my car accident].
Ex: I appreciated his KIND ["Behavior" offer of the car].

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: The Evaluee is the person whose Behavior towards other human beings is being evaluated.

fe.name: Affected_party
fe.definition: The Affected_party is the entity which is positively or negatively treated by the Evaluee.

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior is the action of the Evaluee on which the evaluation of the Evaluee's character is based.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the extent to which the Evaluee exhibits the particular Behavior towards others.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the situation or person that the Evaluee's Behavior responds to or is related to.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Evaluee.
Ex: She flashed me a KIND ["Expressor" smile].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner is the way in which the Evaluee embodies the characteristic ascribed to her or him.
Ex: ["Evaluee" Lester] was ["Manner" coldly] POLITE.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition:
The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the evaluation denoted by the target.
Ex: ["jud" In my book], that wasn't very GRACIOUS.

lexunit.definition: COD: tactful.

lexunit.name: barbaric.a
lexunit.definition: COD: savagely cruel.

lexunit.name: spiteful.a
lexunit.definition: FN: showing a desire to hurt, annoy or offend others

lexunit.name: pleasant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a person) friendly and considerate; likeable.

lexunit.name: horrible.a
lexunit.definition: FN: very disagreeable or unpleasant

lexunit.name: good.a
lexunit.definition: FN: kind, benevolent or socially correct.

lexunit.name: good-natured.a
lexunit.definition: FN: Having an easygoing, cheerful disposition.

lexunit.name: good-humored.a
lexunit.definition: FN: without ill-will.

lexunit.name: warm.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having or showing enthusiasm, affection, or kindness.

frame.name: Topic
frame.definition:
A stretch of linguistic discourse or a Text that a Communicator produces has a Topic that it is about.
Ex: ["Text" Chapter 5] DISCUSSES ["Topic" the issue of transsubstantiation]. Ex: ["Text" Smither's essay] is ABOUT ["Topic" plane spotting]. Ex: ["Communicator" Ostrovsky] ADDRESSES ["Topic" monetary policy] ["Text" in Chapter 5]. Ex: ["Text" This book] is ["Degree" mostly] ABOUT ["Topic" particle physics].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is what a Text is about.

fe.name: Text
fe.definition:
A set of propositions that is coherent in being about a Topic
Ex: Sue bought a ["Text" book] ABOUT Pennsylvania

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition:
The Communicator is the person who has produced a Text on a Topic.
Ex: In his book, ["Communicator" Smithers] DISCUSSES cotton production.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate to which Degree the Text is about the Topic
Ex: The article is ["Degree" mostly] ABOUT yoga techniques

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions in which Manner the Topic is treated.
Ex: The book ["Manner" carefully] DISCUSSES the events leading up to the war

fe.name: Status
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Status is used for expressions that indicate the relative importance of a Topic with respect to the other topics that a Text is about.
Ex: The book is ["Status" mainly] ABOUT 19th century sewage systems Ex: A ["Status" peripheral] TOPIC of Chapter 3 is Appalachian coal-mining.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Communicator produces Text on a Topic.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Text or Communicator presents the Topic.

lexunit.name: about.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: on the subject of; concerning

lexunit.name: concern.v
lexunit.definition: COD: relate to; be about.

lexunit.name: discuss.v
lexunit.definition: FN: provide a discussion of a topic

lexunit.name: topic.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a subject of a text, speech, conversation, etc.

lexunit.name: subject.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing that is being discussed or dealt with or that gives rise to something.

lexunit.name: cover.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deal with (a subject).

lexunit.name: regarding.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: about; concerning

lexunit.name: treat.v
lexunit.definition: FN: deal with some topic

lexunit.name: address.v
lexunit.definition: FN: deal with a topic

lexunit.name: concerning.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: about.

lexunit.name: theme.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a subject or topic on which a person speaks, writes, or thinks.

lexunit.name: dwell_(on).v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak, or write at length about.

lexunit.name: on.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: about, concerning

lexunit.name: regard.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take as topic.

lexunit.name: regard.n
lexunit.definition: FN: relation, connection.

frame.name: Daring
frame.definition:
An Agent performs some Action which is considered imprudent. This frame is distinct from Attempt in that the danger that the Agent puts themself in by performing the Action is profiled. The danger is not spelled out, but generally the Action has a possibility or likelihood of causing social or physical harm to the Agent.
Ex: ["Agent" I] RISKED ["Action" taking another look].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individual that performs the Action, resulting in danger to themself.
Ex: I do n't think ["age" you] should HAZARD the ascent in the dark , that 's all .

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: This FE denotes the Action taken by the Agent.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which the Action is performed. Ex: He RISKED a look back ["Purpose" to check for pursuit].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason the Agent takes the risk. Ex: She RISKED a disguise ["Reason" since they already had a photo of her].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Agent dares to perform the Action.
Ex: ["Time" At dawn], the Captain CHANCED opening the hatch.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Agent risks doing the Action.
Ex: ["Place" Back in his room], he RISKED peeking inside.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the risking action which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: If you ["Manner" carelessly] CHANCE going back there, you deserve what you get.

lexunit.name: chance.v
lexunit.definition: COD: risk.

lexunit.name: hazard.v
lexunit.definition: COD: risk to chance.

lexunit.name: dare.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take the risk of.

lexunit.name: venture.v
lexunit.definition: COD: undertake a risky or daring journey or course of action.

lexunit.name: risk.v
lexunit.definition: COD: act in such a way as to incur the risk of.

lexunit.name: risk.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the possibility that something unpleasant will happen.

lexunit.name: audaciousness.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: fearless daring

lexunit.name: chance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a possibility of something happening.

frame.name: Difficulty
frame.definition:
An Experiencer has an easy or difficult time carrying out an Activity. The ease or difficulty associated with the Activity seems to often be associated with a prominent participant. However, we consider this impression to be due to the syntax and pragmatics of the relevant sentence constructions and employ no specal FE for such participants. The Degree of ease or difficulty is often specified as well as a set of Circumstances. A Parameter may be mentioned that indicates in which respect the Activity is judged to be easy or difficult.
Ex: (1) ["Activity" John] _is_ EASY ["Activity" to please]. Ex: (2) It _is_ EASY ["Activity" to get Alex annoyed]. Ex: (3) ["Activity" Smithers] is ["Degree" very] TOUGH ["Experiencer" for me] ["Activity" to please]. Ex: (4) ["Activity" VWs] are EASY ["Activity" to repair]. Ex: (5) ["Activity" The dating of western sculpture] is DIFFICULT. Ex: (6) ["Circumstances" In that kind of wind] ["Activity" the course] is ["Parameter" physically] ["Degree" very] TRICKY. Ex: (7) ["Activity" The last question on the exam] _was_ HARD. Ex: (8) The last one was a HARD ["Activity" question] ["Activity" to answer].

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions indicating the Activity that the Experiencer finds difficult or easy. In many cases, the relevant Activity has to be inferred from the context.
Ex: ["Activity" The climb] was DIFFICULT. Ex: ["Activity" That question] was DIFFICULT. Ex: ["Activity" That question] was DIFFICULT ["Activity" to answer].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Degree of difficulty that the Experiencer has in carrying out the Activity.
Ex: Charlie is ["Degree" very] TOUGH for Lulu to please.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions in which the Activity is being experienced and which influence the Experiencer's perception of how easy or difficult the Activity is.
Ex: ["Circumstances" In this weather] the climb turned out to be very DIFFICULT.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate which person judges carrying out the Activity to be easy or difficult.
Ex: The geology question on the exam was HARD ["Experiencer" for me].

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a respect in which the Activity is judged easy or difficult to carry out by the Experiencer.
Ex: The problem involves a ["Parameter" mathematically] DIFFICULT Fourier transformation.

fe.name: Standard
fe.definition:
The experience of the Activity by the Experiencer may be compared to a Standard situation, which may be evoked either as an event or state, or by reference to a salient participant.
Ex: Man, running on hilly bike paths of Calgary was TOUGH ["sta" compared to my routes in flat southwestern Ontario].
Ex: Elsewhere, expert rider Kris Leeson was finding the going TOUGH ["sta" compared to the previous rounds].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Activity takes place.

lexunit.name: difficult.a
lexunit.definition: COD: needing much effort or skill to accomplish, deal with, or understand

lexunit.name: easy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: achieved without great effort; presenting few difficulties

lexunit.name: hard.a
