lexunit.name: tough.a
lexunit.definition: COD: nvolving considerable difficulty or hardship

lexunit.name: tricky.a
lexunit.definition: COD: requiring care and skill because difficult or awkward

lexunit.name: challenging.a
lexunit.definition: FN: requiring a person's full abilities and effort

lexunit.name: a breeze.n
lexunit.definition: FN: very easy

lexunit.name: a pain.n

lexunit.name: a bitch.n
lexunit.definition: FN: very difficult

lexunit.name: impossible.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not able to be accomplished

lexunit.name: trivial.a
lexunit.definition: FN: very easy

lexunit.name: a snap.n
lexunit.definition: FN: very easy

lexunit.name: no picnic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: difficult

lexunit.name: arduous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: difficult and tiring

lexunit.name: a pain in the neck.n
lexunit.definition: FN: difficult and unpleasant

lexunit.name: child's_play.n
lexunit.definition: FN: very easy, trivial

lexunit.name: a piece of cake.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something easily achieved

lexunit.name: a cinch.n
lexunit.definition: FN: very easy

lexunit.name: a bastard.n
lexunit.definition: FN: very difficult

lexunit.name: near thing.a
lexunit.definition: FN: an event which occurs despite fears that it might not occur

lexunit.name: difficulty.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: the attribute of being difficult

lexunit.name: challenge.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a demanding task or situation.

lexunit.name: a doddle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a very easy task.

frame.name: Fairness_evaluation
frame.definition:
In this frame an Action is evaluated with respect to how fairly, justly or equitably the Action affects the Affected_party. An Actor may also be identified, who performs the Action and may be characterized as fair, unfair, etc. based on how these actions affect the Affected_party. Grounds may also be identified.
Ex: ["Actor" Smithers] was being ["Degree" very] FAIR ["Grounds" about the distribution of supplies]. Ex: ["Actor" Smithers] was being ["Degree" very] FAIR ["Action" about distributing the supplies]. Ex: ["Action" The decision] was FAIR ["Affected_party" to all involved]. Ex: It was not FAIR ["Action" for the warning to remain in place]. Ex: ["Actor" The company] was UNFAIR ["Affected_party" to its loyal employees]. Ex: Smith received a FAIR ["Action" trial]. Ex: ["Action" The student loan system] is ["Parameter" socially] UNJUST.

fe.name: Actor
fe.definition: The Actor is the individual who performs the Action and can thus be characterized with repsect to how that Action affects the Affected_party.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action is judged based on how just and appopriate it is to the Affected_party in a particular situation.

fe.name: Grounds
fe.definition: The Grounds is the event or state that requires some decision or action in response to it for which the Actor is judged.

fe.name: Affected_party
fe.definition: The Affected_party's treatment is what determines the evaluation of the Actor's Action.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the extent to which the Action or Actor is evaluated as being fair or unfair.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition: The Parameter is the area in which the Action is judged.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A holistic characterization of the description of the Actor, including depictions of the Actor's state in terms of how it affects the entire description.
Ex: You have been ["Manner" cruelly] UNFAIR to me !

lexunit.name: fair.a
lexunit.definition: COD: just or appropriate in the circumstances.

lexunit.name: unfair.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not based on or showing fairness; unjust.

lexunit.name: unjust.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not just; unfair.

lexunit.name: inequitable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unfair; unjust.

lexunit.name: fairly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: (do something) so as to have a fair outcome.

lexunit.name: unfairly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: (do something) so as to have an unfair outcome.

lexunit.name: unjustly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: (do something) so as to have an unfair outcome.

frame.name: Inclination
frame.definition:
Due to internal forces/properties, an Entity is inclined towards a particular Behavior, which may be to perform an action or a to maintain a state. The underlying force is seen as being beyond the Entity's control. The Degree to which the Entity is inclined towards the Behavior may also be specified as well as the Basis for the inclincation.
Ex: ["Entity" My grandmother] _has_ ["Behavior" criminal] TENDENCIES. Ex: "["Entity" Smithers] has always _had_ a deplorable TENDENCY ["Behavior" to exhibitionism]. Ex: ["Entity" Chuck] _was_ not ["Degree" very] INCLINED ["Behavior" to believe me]. Ex: ["Entity" Smithers] _has_ a ["Basis" genetic] PREDISPOSITION ["Behavior" for neural tube defects].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
TheFrame Element Entity identifies the person or thing that has a tendency towards some Behaviour.
Ex: ["Entity" Lubomir] was not INCLINED to believe me

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition:
The FE Behavior marks expressions that indicate which state or action the Entity tends towards.
Ex: Martha has a TENDENCY ["Behavior" to overdo the housekeeping].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how great the inclination of an Entity towards a Behavior is.
Ex: We're ["Degree" very] INCLINED ["Behavior" to doubt it].

fe.name: Basis
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate why the Entity has the propensity for some Behavior.
Ex: Smurphs have a ["Basis" natural] PROPENSITY to hide in caves

fe.name: Containing_Event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

lexunit.name: tendency.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an inclination towards a particular characteristic or type of behaviour

lexunit.name: inclined.a
lexunit.definition: COD: have a specified tendency, disposition, or talent.

lexunit.name: prone.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a tendency or inclination

lexunit.name: proclivity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an inclination or predisposition.

lexunit.name: propensity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an inclination or tendency.

lexunit.name: predisposition.n
lexunit.definition: FN: liable or inclined to a specified attitude, action, or condition.

lexunit.name: penchant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strong liking or inclination

lexunit.name: predisposed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being disposed in advance

frame.name: Run_risk
frame.definition:
A Protagonist is described as being exposed to a potentially dangerous situation that may end in a Bad_outcome for him- or herself. An Asset which is in danger of loss may stand in for the Bad_outcome. There is no implication that the Protagonist intentionally exposes themself to the risky situation. The Protagonist may be attempting to achieve some Purpose, which involves being in a dangerous situation. The Severity of risk involved may also be expressed.
Ex: There was a RISK ["Bad_outcome" of fire]. Ex: ["Protagonist" Original thinkers] _incur_ ["Severity" greater] RISKS ["Asset" to their careers] ["Severity" than their pedestrian colleagues].
NOTE: This Frame is currently in the process of being changed so that some instances of _at risk.n_ will be moved to the Being_at_risk frame, and some will be moved to the Risky_situation frame. In the Being_at_risk frame, _risk_ is almost always supported with _at_, and its external argument is the Asset. Risky_situation uses of _risk_ include the following:
Ex: Smoking poses a risk to your health. Ex: Smoking is a health RISK. Ex: The most imminent RISK is to our infrastructure.
but (possibly ; still under discussion) not: _The most imminent RISK is that our infrastructure may not be able to handle the load._
In the Risky_situation frame, the external argument is the Situation, and the Bad_outcome in not expressible.
The verb risk.v will remain in the Run_risk frame, in the sense of . The construction _run risk_ also will remain in the Run_risk frame.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The person who is at risk of some Bad_outcome

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where there is risk. Ex: There is always some DANGER to rich men ["Place" in a bar like this].

fe.name: Severity
fe.definition: The probability of something bad happening to the Protagonist. Ex: If he is uncertain of right and wrong, he is in ["Sev" dire] PERIL of losing his immortal soul.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the risk pertains. Ex: ["Time" Even after the end of Apartheit] we still run the RISK of letting racism continue forever.

fe.name: Bad_outcome
fe.definition: A situation that the Protagonist would like to avoid. Ex: There was no DANGER ["Bad" of his returning].

fe.name: Asset
fe.definition: Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Protagonist which might be lost or damaged. Ex: The RISK ["Asset" to his reputation] was significant.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action that creates the risk. Ex: ["Action" Implementing this program] the RISK of offending our core constituents.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The Frequency with which the Protagonist runs risks.
Ex: Some people have no problem with RISKING their hides ["fre" every day].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The desired action or goal that the Protagonist hopes to bring about.
Ex: They all RISKED being caught ["Pur" in order to come to the United States].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: An Explanation for why the Protagonist has put the Assetis in a dangerous situation.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The number of times that the Protagonist risks an Asset.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances indicates the state of affairs under which the risky situation holds.
Ex: Putting forward new ideas RISKS sparking controversy ["cir" if you don't frame your argument properly].

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition:
The Protagonist intends for his/her actions to benefit Beneficiary in some way.
Ex: They would RISK all ["ben" for their closest friends].

lexunit.name: risk.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a situation involving exposure to danger.

lexunit.name: endangered.a
lexunit.definition: COD: at risk, especially of extinction.

lexunit.name: peril.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a situation of serious and immediate danger.

lexunit.name: risk.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (of a situation or action) inviting risk or danger.

frame.name: Time_vector
frame.definition:
An Event is identified as occurring at a particular Distance and in a particular Direction from a Landmark_event. The lexical units incorporate the Direction and, in some cases, the Landmark_event. This frame builds on the Direction frame, further specifying the Domain as Time. This frame will receive some of the lexical units currently found in Relative_time.
Ex: ["Event" Tell me that] ["Distance" a week] ["Direction" FROM] ["Landmark_event" now]. Ex: ["Distance" Some twelve months] ["Direction" AFTER] ["Landmark_event" I had graduated], ["Event" I had my first job interview]

fe.name: Landmark_event
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the reference point in which the Event is anchored.
Ex: Sue is going to pick me up again two days FROM ["Landmark_event" tomorrow].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate the amount of time that lies between the Target and the Landmark_event.
Ex: Peter will meet me ["Distance" a week] FROM today

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate whether the Target is prior or subsequent to the Landmark_event on the time line.
Ex: Mom last called me a week ["Direction" AGO].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Event temporally located with respect to the Landmark_event. Ex: ["Event" The incident] _was_ several years AGO.

lexunit.name: from.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: indicating the point in space or time at which a journey, process, or action starts.

lexunit.name: hence.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: from now; in the future

lexunit.name: after.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: in the time following

lexunit.name: before.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: during the period of time preceding.

lexunit.name: in time.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: at the usual or proper time

lexunit.name: ago.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: before the present (used with a measurement of time).

lexunit.name: since.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: from the time mentioned until the present or the time under consideration.

lexunit.name: down the road.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: later than a specified point of time

lexunit.name: previously.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: before

lexunit.name: prior.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: before

lexunit.name: beforehand.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: in advance.

lexunit.name: afterward.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: at a later or future time

lexunit.name: afterwards.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: at a later or future time.

lexunit.name: right away.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: immediately

lexunit.name: sooner rather than later.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: (of inevitable occurrences) quite soon (as opposed to later)

lexunit.name: later.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: At a time in the near future; afterwards

lexunit.name: thereafter.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: after that time

lexunit.name: through.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: from beginning to end of (an experience or activity).

lexunit.name: former.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having been previously.

lexunit.name: formerly.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: in the past.

lexunit.name: eventually.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: after a long period of time.

lexunit.name: previous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: existing or occurring before in time or order.

lexunit.name: pre.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: before (in time, place, order, degree, or importance)

lexunit.name: post.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: after in time or order.

lexunit.name: ante.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: before; preceding.

lexunit.name: finally.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: at last

lexunit.name: then.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being (something) at an earlier time

lexunit.name: already.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: having done so in the past

lexunit.name: until.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: at which point something happens that will effect the course of something else.

frame.name: Custom
frame.definition:
A Behavior is classified as entrenched for a Protagonist or a Society. The Behavior may be associated with a particular Domain of experience and described with a Descriptor. This indicates that the Behavior is commonly performed by the Protagonist or members of the Society.
Ex: It is an ["Descriptor" old] ["Society" Jewish] CUSTOM. Ex: He was unaware of the ["Society" Japanese] CUSTOM ["Behavior" of waiting until the giver had departed]. Ex: The ["Descriptor" ancient] TRADITION ["Behavior" of swan-upping] has been taking place on the river Thames. Ex: Smithers thought that ["Behavior" hunting lions] was just another ["Society" native] CUSTOM Ex: Marko showed great respect for the ["Domain" social] CUSTOMS ["Society" of his people]. Ex: When I reply to debates , it is ["Protagonist" my] CUSTOM ["Behavior" to have heard all the speeches that have been made].

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the entrenched Behavior.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate whose entrenched Behavior is at issue.
Ex: ["Protagonist" His] CUSTOM was to come here for the 10 o'clock service.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the area of human experience to which the Behavior belongs.
Ex: Witali tried to understand their ["Domain" religious] CUSTOMS.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate attributes, traits, or evaluations of the entrenched Behavior.
Ex: In the year 2100, a historian will undertake a study of that ["Descriptor" quaint] CUSTOM of preserving public footpaths across private land .

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a region where the Behavior is entrenched.
Ex: They found that a loca CUSTOM ["Place" in the country] was to walk around barefoot at all times of the year and in all weathers .

fe.name: Society
fe.definition: Ex: We can help , you to meet Egyptian people and learn about ["Society" Egyptian] CUSTOMS.

lexunit.name: ways.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: customs of life, esp. with regard to morality

lexunit.name: custom.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something that is specific to a particular society, place, or time.

lexunit.name: practice.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the customary or expected procedure or way of doing something.

lexunit.name: ritual.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a series of actions habitually and invariably followed by someone.

lexunit.name: tradition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long-established custom or belief passed on in this way.

lexunit.name: habit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a settled or regular tendency or practice

lexunit.name: convention.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a settled or regular tendency or practice

lexunit.name: traditional.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of, relating to, or following tradition.

lexunit.name: ritualistic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being related with regular observance or practice of ritual, especially when excessive or without regard to its function.

lexunit.name: habitual.a
lexunit.definition: COD: done constantly or as a habit.

lexunit.name: customary.a
lexunit.definition: COD: in accordance with custom; usual.

lexunit.name: traditionally.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: (of an action) according to tradition.

frame.name: Cause_to_start
frame.definition:
A Cause, animate or inanimate, causes a process, the Effect, to begin.
Ex: ["Cause" The murder of Sergei Kirov] SET OFF ["Effect" a chain of events that culminated in the Great Terror of the 1930s].
Ex: ["Cause" Ressam] planned to SET ["Effect" a bomb] OFF at the Los Angeles International Airport.
Ex: ["Cause" Space email] SPARKED ["Effect" astronaut jealousy].
Ex: ["Cause" A crime surge in a former coal town] PROMPTED ["Effect" a crackdown on illegal immigrants].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
Ex: ["Cause" The programme] SPARKED a public outcry.

fe.name: Effect
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the process that the Cause initiates.
Ex: Few things SPARK ["Effect" the wrath of the British] like food additives.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the Effect occurs.
Ex: ["Place" In Obscurania], the release of the movie SPARKED protests.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is the way in which the Cause causes the process to begin.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE is for the Time when causing to start occurs

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Cause results in the Effect.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the actor responsible for creating the Effect.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: To what end the Agent or Cause caused the Effect.

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition: This FE identifies the first Subevent of the started Effect.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Agent causes the Effect.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modifies the target to indicate the legal- or "by rule" domain within which it is true or operational.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why or the way in which the Agent or Cause causes the Effect.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world at the time when the Agent or Cause produces the Effect.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition: A consecutive event to the starting of the Effect of the Agent.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness

lexunit.name: spark.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide the stimulus for.

lexunit.name: generate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to arise or come about.

lexunit.name: arouse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: evoke (a feeling or response).

lexunit.name: bring about.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause something to happen

lexunit.name: set off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put in motion or trigger.

lexunit.name: produce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to happen or exist.

lexunit.name: create.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring into existence

lexunit.name: engender.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring into existence

lexunit.name: actuate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to operate.

lexunit.name: call forth.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to occur

lexunit.name: elicit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: draw forth into existence.

lexunit.name: kindle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: arouse

lexunit.name: excite.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: elicit an emotional response

lexunit.name: incite.v
lexunit.definition: COD: encourage or stir up (violent or unlawful behaviour).

lexunit.name: instigate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring about or initiate.

lexunit.name: motivate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause activity to start

lexunit.name: prompt.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause an activity to start

lexunit.name: stir up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause activity or state

lexunit.name: stimulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: apply or act as a stimulus to.

lexunit.name: provoke.v
lexunit.definition: COD: incite to do or feel something, especially by arousing anger.

frame.name: Contrition
frame.definition:
An Experiencer feels bad about a choice, an Action, or a failure to do something, which they now consider to have been a mistake or wrong. The emotional state of the Experiencer may be showing in gestures or facial expressions, viz. an Expressor.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Smithers] did not REPENT ["Action" of his crime]. Ex: It is God who rejoices at the REPENTANCE ["Experiencer" of his sinner].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The FE Experiencer indicates the person who experiences the emotion about their prior action.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Smithers] was contrite about his wrongdoings.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
The FE Action marks expressions that indicate a prior action that the Experiencer has come to feel bad about.
Ex: They confessed and REPENTED ["Action" their actions against the Soviet Union].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The FE Degree marks expressions that indicate how badly the Experiencer feels about their prior action.
Ex: Smithers was ["Degree" very] CONTRITE.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The FE Expressor marks expressions that indicate a gesture or body part which is displaying the Emotional_state of the Experiencer.
Ex: REPENTANT ["Expressor" tears] welled to his eyes.

fe.name: Authenticity
fe.definition:
The FE Authenticitymarks expressions that indicate whether the Experiencer genuinely feels contrite or just acts as if they did.
Ex: The defendant showed no ["Authenticity" real] REMORSE.

fe.name: Emotional_state
fe.definition:
The FE Emotional_state is modified by an adjective that indicates the Experiencer is contrite.
Ex: Martha had a GUILTY ["Emotional_state" conscience] after selling inferior merchandise.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Experiencer or the Expressor is contrite.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Experiencer or Expressor has contrition.

lexunit.name: contrite.a
lexunit.definition: COD: feeling or expressing remorse.

lexunit.name: contrition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of feeling contrite

lexunit.name: rue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bitterly regret (a past event or action) and wish it undone.

lexunit.name: rueful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: expressing regret, especially in a wry or humorous way.

lexunit.name: repent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: feel or express sincere regret or remorse

lexunit.name: repentant.a
lexunit.definition: FN: feeling or expressing contrition

lexunit.name: repentance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a feeling or expression of sincere regret

lexunit.name: penitent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong.

lexunit.name: penitence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of feeling regret or remorse over a past action or omission

lexunit.name: remorse.n
lexunit.definition: COD: deep regret or guilt for a wrong committed

lexunit.name: remorseful.a
lexunit.definition: FN: full of deep regret or guilt for a wrong committed.

lexunit.name: sorry.a
lexunit.definition: COD: feeling regret or penitence.

lexunit.name: guilty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having or showing a feeling of guilt

lexunit.name: remorseless.a
lexunit.definition: COD: without remorse.

lexunit.name: unrepentant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: showing no regret for one's wrongdoings.

lexunit.name: guilt.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a feeling of having committed wrong or failed in an obligation

frame.name: Cause_change_of_consistency
frame.definition:
In this frame an Agent or Cause changes the consistency of an Undergoer from its Initial_state to a Result. This may take place under certain Circumstances for a Purpose or Reason in a certain Manner. A Change_agent can also be used.
Ex: ["Agent" Donna] THINNED ["Undergoer" the soup] ["Change_agent" with chicken broth]. Ex: ["Cause" The high temperatures] CURDLED ["Undergoer" the milk].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the consistency change occurs. Ex: Tom THICKENED the soup ["Circumstances" at 300 degrees].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition: This is the original state of the Undergoer. Ex: ["Agent" Marcus] THICKENED ["Undergoer" the soup] ["Initial_state" from its runny state].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Undergoer's consistency is changed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies theReason for which the Undergoer's consistency is changed.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result is the result of the change of consistency. Ex: ["Agent" Samson] THINNED ["Undergoer" the soup] ["Result" into a thin broth].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed at which the change of consistency occurs.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected. Ex: ["Undergoer" The bread] was HARDENED ["sub" around the edges].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Undergoer changes consistency.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: Undergoer is the entity that undergoes a change.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent causes the change of consistency in the Undergoer.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent changes the consistency of the Undergoer.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the consistency of the Undergoer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent changes the consistency of the Undergoer.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-Agent which brings about the change in the Undergoer. Ex: ["Cause" The hot water] JELLED ["Undergoer" the jello].

fe.name: Change_agent
fe.definition: The Change_agent is the substance used to change the consistency of the Undergoer.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a Container in which the Undergoer is changing consistency.
Ex: Smithers SOFTENED the butter ["Container" in a cup].

fe.name: HotCold_source
fe.definition:
The HotCold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.
Ex: ["Agent" We] THICKENED ["Undergoer" the soup] ["HotCold_source" over an open flame].

lexunit.name: thicken.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become thicker

lexunit.name: thin.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to have a thinner consistency

lexunit.name: curdle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to separate into curds or lumps

lexunit.name: soften.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become easier to mould, cut, compress, or fold.

lexunit.name: harden.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become solid, firm, and rigid; not easily broken, bent, or pierced.

lexunit.name: jell.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of jelly or a similar substance) set or become firmer.

lexunit.name: coagulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a fluid, especially blood) change to a solid or semi-solid state.

lexunit.name: congeal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become semi-solid, especially on cooling.

lexunit.name: clot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form or cause to form into clots.

lexunit.name: indurate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: harden.

lexunit.name: inspissate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: thicken or congeal.

lexunit.name: set.v
lexunit.definition: COD: harden into a solid, semi-solid, or fixed state.

frame.name: Experience_bodily_harm
frame.definition: An Experiencer is involved in a bodily injury to a Body_part. (In some cases, no Body_part need be indicated.) Often an Injuring_entity on which the Experiencer injures themself is mentioned. Ex: I think that ["Exp" I] HURT ["Exp" myself] ["Sev" pretty bad] ["Place" back there]. Ex: ["Exp" He] SMACKED ["Body_part" his head] ["Inj_ent" on the mantel] ["con" getting up from poking at the fire].

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: The location on the body of the Experiencer where the bodily injury takes place. Ex: I CUT ["BodP" my finger] on the envelope.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: The event in which the bodily injury takes place. Ex: I BROKE my arm ["con" in the accident].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner in which the injury takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the harming event occurs. Ex: She fell and HIT her head ["Place" out in the playground].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The being or entity that is injured. Ex: ["Exp" The squirrel] ABRADED ["Exp" its] tail as it twitched nervously in the confined space. Ex: Then ["Exp" I] CUT ["Exp" myself] on an envelope.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the harming event occurs. Ex: So you CUT your leg on the window frame ["Time" at six o'clock], correct?

fe.name: Injuring_entity
fe.definition:
The Experiencer injures him/herself on an Injuring_entity.
Ex: He punched me, but he HURT his fist ["Inj_ent" on my nose].

fe.name: Severity
fe.definition: The extent to which the Experiencer is affected by the injury. Ex: The suspect INJURED his leg ["Sev" severely] climbing the fence.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of times that the injury happens to the Experiencer. Ex: I JAMMED my pinky on these juggling clubs ["Iter" three times] in the last hour.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time during which the Experiencer repeatedly receives bodily injuries.
Ex: Smithers STUBBED his toe on the couch ["Duration" for several months] before he got used to its new location.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that the Experiencer has an experience of bodily harm.
Ex: Sue STUBBED her toe ["Frequency" three times] today

lexunit.name: stub.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accidentally strike (one's toe) against something.

lexunit.name: jam.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to strike one's finger or toe resulting in injury to the joints

lexunit.name: hit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accidentally strike (part of one's body) against something.

lexunit.name: hurt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause physical pain or injury to.

lexunit.name: injure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: do or undergo physical harm to; wound.

lexunit.name: break.v
lexunit.definition: COD: separate or cause to separate into pieces as a result of a blow, shock, or strain.

lexunit.name: sprain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: wrench the ligaments of (an ankle, wrist, or other joint) violently so as to cause pain and swelling but not dislocation.

lexunit.name: strain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: injure (a limb, muscle, or organ) by overexertion.

lexunit.name: twist.v
lexunit.definition: COD: force or be forced out of the natural position by a twisting action

lexunit.name: pull.v
lexunit.definition: COD: damage (a muscle, ligament, etc.) by abnormal strain.

lexunit.name: tear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: damage (a muscle or ligament) by overstretching it.

lexunit.name: cut.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make an opening, incision, or wound in (something) with a sharp tool or object.

lexunit.name: burn.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be or cause to be harmed or destroyed by fire.

lexunit.name: smack.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hit with a smack.

lexunit.name: abrade.v
lexunit.definition: COD: scrape or wear away by friction or erosion

lexunit.name: graze.v
lexunit.definition: COD: scrape and break the skin on (part of the body).

lexunit.name: bruise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: sustain a bruise on a specified body part

frame.name: Altered_phase
frame.definition: In this frame an Undergoer is in a phase brought about after a change of phase. This can be its inherent phase or indicate that it is returned to its inherent state. Ex: Collect up the THAWED ["Undergoer" water] from the freezer section. Ex: Put under the broiler until ["Undergoer" the cheese] becomes MELTED. Ex: Major companies are switching to LIQUEFIED ["Undergoer" natural gas].

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition: The Undergoer is the entity which has had its phase altered.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The part of the Undergoer that is in an altered state. Ex: The turkey was only DEFROSTED ["Sub" on the top].

lexunit.name: thawed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been caused to become liquid as a result of warming up from a frozen state

lexunit.name: melted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been caused to become liquid

lexunit.name: liquefied.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been caused to become liquid

lexunit.name: frozen.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been turned into ice or another solid as a result of extreme cold.

lexunit.name: defrosted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been thawed

lexunit.name: solidified.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been turned into solid form

frame.name: Ingest_substance
frame.definition:
In this frame an Ingestor takes a Substance into his or her body. The Delivery_device can appear as a direct object.
Ex: ["Ingestor" You] should refrain from TAKING ["Substance" vodka] ["Entry_path" up the nose].
Ex: SMOKING ["Delivery_device" a cigarette] only takes a couple of minutes . ["Ingestor" CNI]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

fe.name: Delivery_device
fe.definition: The Delivery_device is the means by which the substance is ingested. Ex: ["Ingestor" Tabitha] SMOKED ["Delivery_device" a pipe]. Ex: ["Ingestor" Simon ]SMOKED ["Substance" pot] ["Delivery_device" with a bong].

fe.name: Ingestor
fe.definition: The Ingestor ingests the Substance

fe.name: Substance
fe.definition: The Substance is the drug or other substance that is ingested by the Ingestor.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency with which the Ingestor ingests.

fe.name: Entry_path
fe.definition: The Entry_path is the path along which the Substance enters the Ingestor's body. Ex: ["Ingestor" Rick] SNORTED ["Substance" cocaine] ["Entry_path" up his nose].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration is the length of time for which the Ingestor ingests.

lexunit.name: smoke.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inhale and exhale the smoke of tobacco or a drug.

lexunit.name: snort.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inhale

lexunit.name: drag.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inhale the smoke from (a cigarette).

lexunit.name: drag.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of inhaling smoke from a cigarette.

lexunit.name: toke.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a pull on a cigarette or pipe, typically one containing cannabis.

lexunit.name: pull.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inhale deeply while drawing on (a cigarette).

lexunit.name: pop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take or inject (a drug).

lexunit.name: inject.v
lexunit.definition: FN: introduce a liquid, especially a drug, into the body with a syringe

lexunit.name: shoot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inject oneself with a narcotic drug.

lexunit.name: sniff.v
lexunit.definition: FN: draw intoxicating fumes or other substance through the nose

lexunit.name: do.v
lexunit.definition: COD: regularly take (a narcotic drug).

lexunit.name: use.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take (an illegal drug).

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: FN: consume drugs or medicine

lexunit.name: puff.v
lexunit.definition: quickly suck in smoke of tobacco or a drug

frame.name: Prison
frame.definition: This Frame deals with Penal_institutions. They are run by an Operator and may be intended to hold certain kinds of Inmates. Penal_institutions may have a special Name and their Location may also be indicated.

fe.name: Operator
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Operator marks expressions that indicate which level of government operates the Penal Institution.
Ex: Smithers had to serve time in ["Operator" prison].

fe.name: Inmates
fe.definition:
Inmates marks expressions that indicate the group of people a Penal Institution is intended to hold.
Ex: Monica served time in the Tennessee PRISON ["Inmates" for Women].

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that are the Name of a Penal Institution.
Ex: Kolimov visited the ["Name" Willy C. Peterson] State PRISON.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate the Location of the Penal Institution.
Ex: Carruthers spent three years in ["Location" Fort Pulaski] State PRISON.

fe.name: Security
fe.definition: The level of security maintained at the prison. Ex: He was held in a ["Sec" maximum security] PRISON.

fe.name: Penal_institution
fe.definition: The locale which serves to confine individuals, generally for the purpose of punishment.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A subpart of the Penal_institution.
Ex: You really expect me to run a PRISON ["Part" with only ten cells]?

lexunit.name: penitentiary.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a prison for people convicted of serious crimes.

lexunit.name: jail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a place for the confinement of people accused or convicted of a crime.

lexunit.name: prison.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a building for the confinement of criminals or those awaiting trial.

lexunit.name: jailhouse.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a prison.

lexunit.name: slammer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: prison.

lexunit.name: stockade.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a military prison.

lexunit.name: pen.n
lexunit.definition: COD: short for penitentiary

lexunit.name: joint.n
lexunit.definition: COD: prison.

lexunit.name: correctional institution.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a prison

lexunit.name: brig.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a prison, especially on a warship [Mil]

frame.name: Atonement
frame.definition: An Agent has committed a Wrong in the past and is making Amends for it. The Degree to which the Amends are adequate may also be expressed.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent has committed a Wrong and is making Amends.
Ex: ["Agent" Syria] has ATONED for its support of Iraq.

fe.name: Wrong
fe.definition:
Wrong identifies the act committed by the Agent for which Amends are made.
Ex: Smithers is ATONING ["Wrong" for his misspent youth].

fe.name: Amends
fe.definition:
Amends marks expressions that indicate what the Agent does to compensate for the Wrong that was committed.
Ex: He ATONED for his sin ["Amends" with good works].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which Amends made are adequate for atoning the Wrong.
Ex: The sacrifice ["Degree" fully] ATONED for his sin.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The situation that the Agent hopes to bring about by atoning.
Ex: He ATONED for his sins ["pur" so that he could be inducted into the society].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the atonement which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Agent atones for the Wrong.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Agent expiates the Wrong.

lexunit.name: atone.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make amends or reparation for

lexunit.name: atonement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: reparation for a wrong or injury.

lexunit.name: expiate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: atone for (guilt or sin).

lexunit.name: expiation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of atoning for (guilt or sin).

lexunit.name: expiatory.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of an act) done in atonement

lexunit.name: expiator.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who atones for guilt or sin

lexunit.name: atoner.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who atones for a sin or guilt

frame.name: Intoxicants
frame.definition: An Intoxicant is ingested in order to achieve an altered state of consciousness. A Type or Descriptor may be indicated as well. Ex: We ["Gov" smoked] ["X" some ["Descriptor" high-grade] ["Intoxicant" MARIJUANA]]. Ex: They ["Gov" smoked] ["X" ["Type" freebase] ["Intoxicant" COCAINE]].

fe.name: Intoxicant
fe.definition: The Intoxicant is ingested. Ex: We ["Gov" smoke] ["X" ["Intoxicant" MARIJUANA]] every day.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type identifies the kind or sort of Intoxicant. Ex: They smoked ["Type" freebase] ["Intoxicant" cocaine].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Descriptor describes a quality of the Intoxicant. Ex: We smoked some ["Descriptor" fine] ["Intoxicant" marijuana].

fe.name: Country_of_origin
fe.definition:
Country_of_origin identifies where the Intoxicant is grown or originates.
Ex: The British enjoy ["Country_of_origin" Afghanistan's] ["Intoxicant" opium].

lexunit.name: marijuana.n
lexunit.definition: COD: cannabis, especially as smoked in cigarettes.

lexunit.name: heroin.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a highly addictive analgesic drug derived from morphine, often used illicitly as a narcotic

lexunit.name: cocaine.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a highly addictive analgesic drug derived from morphine, often used illicitly as a narcotic

lexunit.name: opium.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an addictive drug prepared from the juice of a poppy (Papaver somniferum), used illicitly as a narcotic and occasionally in medicine as an analgesic

lexunit.name: LSD.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a synthetic crystalline compound, lysergic acid diethylamide, which is a powerful hallucinogenic drug.

lexunit.name: mescaline.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a hallucinogenic compound present in the peyote cactus.

lexunit.name: ecstasy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an illegal amphetamine-based synthetic drug with euphoric effects

lexunit.name: methamphetamine.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a synthetic drug with more rapid and lasting effects than amphetamine, used illegally as a stimulant.

lexunit.name: cannabis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a dried preparation or resinous extract made from a plant, used (generally illegally) as a psychotropic drug (chiefly in cigarettes)

lexunit.name: amphetamine.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a synthetic mood-altering drug, used illegally as a stimulant

lexunit.name: barbiturate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: any of a class of sedative drugs derived from barbituric acid.

lexunit.name: sedative.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a drug that promotes calm

lexunit.name: tranquillizer.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a drug with a sedative effect

lexunit.name: dope.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an illegal drug, especially cannabis or (US) heroin

lexunit.name: coke.n
lexunit.definition: COD: informal term for cocaine.

lexunit.name: upper.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a stimulating drug, especially amphetamine.

lexunit.name: downer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a depressant or tranquillizing drug

lexunit.name: speed.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an amphetamine drug, especially methamphetamine.

lexunit.name: crack.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a potent hard crystalline form of cocaine broken into small pieces.

lexunit.name: freebase.n
lexunit.definition: COD: cocaine that has been purified by heating with ether, taken by inhaling the fumes or smoking the residue.

lexunit.name: pot.n

frame.name: Assistance
frame.definition:
A Helper benefits a Benefitted_party by enabling the culmination of a Goal that the Benefitted_party has. A Focal_entity that is involved in reaching the Goal may stand in for it.
Ex: Will ["Helper" you] HELP ["Benefitted_party" the Government] ["Goal" find your brother]? Ex: Maybe ["Helper" Stephen] should ASSIST ["Benefitted_party" him] ["Focal_entity" with the last manuscript]. Ex: ["Helper" They] HELPED ["Benefitted_party" me] ["dom" psychologically] ["Goal" to overcome the physical loss I had suffered]. Ex: ["Helper" You] have HELPED ["Benefitted_party" him] ["deg" tremendously] ["Means" by showing him how to stand up for himself and by being his friend]. Ex: ["Means" By bringing assistance to his troops wherever they were in trouble] ["Helper" he] AIDED ["Benefitted_party" them] ["deg" greatly].

fe.name: Benefitted_party
fe.definition: The Benefitted_party receives a benefit from the action of the Helper.

fe.name: Helper
fe.definition: The Helper performs some action that benefits the Benefitted_party.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The desirable state of affairs that the Benefitted_party is involved in and which is enabled by the Helper.
Ex: JackHELPED Jill ["Goal" climb Mt. Everest].

fe.name: Focal_entity
fe.definition: This FE identifies a Focal_entity involved in achieving the Goal. Ex: Whoever didn't cook has to HELP ["Focal_e" with the dishes].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Assistance occurs. Ex: The police ASSISTED Harry in finding his cat ["tim" on Wednesday afternoon].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Assistance occurs. Ex: The police ASSISTED Harry in finding his cat ["Place" in front of his house].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which a Helper assists a Benefitted_party.
Ex: The doorman ASSISTED Harry into the car ["Manner" with enthusiasm].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action that the Helper undertakes in service of the Benefitted_party's Goal.
Ex: Her teachers and her parents HELPED her ["mea" by reading sections to her and by outlining some of the chapters].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity used by the Helper in service of the Benefitted_party's accomplishing their Goal.
Ex: Actually, he was born in his parents' Dodge Durango, with Sheree Benefield beginning to give birth as his dad, Jon Benefield, held the wheel with his left hand, HELPED her ["ins" with his right] and maneuvered the sport utility vehicle up the I-65 exit ramp at Warrior.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The aspect of accomplishing the Goal to which the Helper's assistance is relevant.
Ex: How can you be HELPED ["dom" spiritually] by his music, when he is defying God?s Word with his very appearance?

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The measure to which the Helper's assistance brings the Benefitted_party closer to accomplishing their Goal.
Ex: The Algebra Buster software HELPED my daughter ["deg" very much].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Helper gives assistence to the Benefitted_party.
Ex: Several nations HELPED ours ["dur" during our most difficult years].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The situation that the Helper wishes to bring about by helping the Benefitted_party to acheive the Goal. Note that this FE should normally be used only when this situation is separate from the Goal.
Ex: I HELPED her with the problem ["pur" just to show her that it could be done].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the questions how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs; Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.
Ex: ["Explanation" Since the earthquake did so much damage], even the federal government AIDED in the recovery process.

frame.name: Being_obligated
frame.definition:
Under some Condition, usually left implicit, a Responsible_party is required to perform some Duty. If they do not perform the Duty, there may be some undesirable Consequence, which may or may not be stated overtly.
NB: Contrast this frame with Likelihood and Preconditions frames, which involve many of the same lemmas.
Ex: ["Resp" This country] MUST ["Duty" support its citizens' right to express themselves]. Ex: ["Resp" I] GOTTA ["Duty" get going] ["Con" or I'll be late for the concert].

fe.name: Responsible_party
fe.definition: The person who must perform the Duty. Ex: ["Resp" Everyone] SHOULD vote.

fe.name: Duty
fe.definition: The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform. Ex: I 'VE GOT TO["Duty" get to the other side of the bridge].

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty. Ex: ["Condition" If you want to succeed at chess ], you HAVE to practice.

fe.name: Consequence
fe.definition: The Consequence will result if the Duty is not performed.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the Responsibly_party is obligated to fulfill the Duty.
Ex: ["Time" At that time] men were OBLIGATED to marry women from their own community.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .
Ex: I almost forgot to tell you that ["pla" in Sweden] we are OBLIGATED to spend atleast 7.5 months in the army for training.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

frame.name: Body_mark
frame.definition:
In this frame a Body_mark is present on a Possessor's body. It may be located at an Attachment and have a Descriptor. A Cause may also be indicated. It may be a temporary condition or a permanent one.
Ex: ["Possessor" Mark] has a ["Descriptor" cancerous] ["Body_mark" MOLE] ["Attachment" on his back].

fe.name: Attachment
fe.definition: The Attachment is the larger body part to which the Body_mark is attached, or of which it is a part. Ex: Mark has a cancerous MOLE ["Attachment" on his back]. Ex: The WARTS ["Attachment" of her left hand] shocked everyone.

fe.name: Body_mark
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Body_mark.
Ex: Mark has a cancerous ["Body_mark" MOLE] on his back.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_mark. it identifies a modifier of its head noun.
Ex: Mark has a ["Desc" cancerous] MOLE on his back.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_mark.
Ex: ["Poss" Mark] has a cancerous MOLE on his back.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the event that brings about the presence of the Body_mark.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
A specific kind of the particular Body_mark.
Ex: Well, looks like you got a ["typ" plantar] WART on your palm there.

fe.name: Constituents
fe.definition: Salient constituents that make up the Body_mark.

frame.name: Biological_urge
frame.definition:
An Experiencer is in a State where a biological urge is signalling the need to perform a certain action such as eating, drinking, stopping exertion, sleeping, regurgitating, or having sex. The Duration, Time, Place, or Degree of intensity associated with the occurrence of the urge may also be indicated. In this frame, the Experiencer does not necessarily want to perform the action that would fulfill the urge, and there is no specific focus associated with the urge.
Ex: ["Experiencer" Mike] _feels_ HUNGRY. Ex: ["Experiencer" Sam] _was_ THIRSTY ["Time" after dinner].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree identifies the extent to which the Experiencer receives the biological signal.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer receives the biological signal and possesses the internal experience which is a reaction to the phsyical signal. Ex: ["Exp" Mr. Burns] _was_ sexually AROUSED.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Experiencer feels the biological signal. Time may also allow inference about the Reason for the biological urge. Ex: ["Experiencer" I] _am_ EXHAUSTED ["Time" when I babysit]. In such cases, we tag Reason on the second layer.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place is where the Experiencer feels the biological signal.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
Expressor is used for a gesture, expression, or body part indicating that the Experiencer is feeling a certain urge.
Ex: He gave me a TIRED ["Expressor" shrug] and then looked down again.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration identifies the amount of time for which the Experiencer feels the urge.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Experiencer has the biological urge. Ex: ["Experiencer" Jen] _is_ TIRED ["Reason" because she gave birth last night.].

fe.name: State
fe.definition: State identifies the Experiencer's state of being. Ex: She was alarmed by John's HUNGRY ["State" state].

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition: Parameter is the particular biological realm in which the Experiencer feels the urge. Ex: Mr. Burns _was_ ["Parameter" sexually] AROUSED.

frame.name: Cause_impact
frame.definition:
An Agent causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee, or manipulates two (or more) Impactors so that they make mutual forcible contact.
Ex: ["Agent" He] SLAMMED ["Impactor" his fist] ["Result" down] ["Impactee" on the table] and bellowed something unintelligible.

fe.name: Force
fe.definition:
The Force is the amount of force in the course of the impact.
Ex: He SMACKED the bat ["Frc" hard] against the wall.

fe.name: Impactee
fe.definition:
The Impactee is the entity which is hit by the Impactor.
Ex: What I want to know is who SMACKED ["Imp2" my head] with a 10-ton truck? Ex: He SLAMMED the lid down ["Imp2" on the top of the jar] so hard that it broke.

fe.name: Impactor
fe.definition:
The Impactor is the entity that hits the Impactee because of the Agent's efforts.
Ex: Those hoodlums STRIKE my car ["Imp1" with water balloons] every day! Ex: Well, then he just RAN ["Imp1" the car] right into the wall.

fe.name: Impactors
fe.definition:
The Impactors are the multiple entities that collide.
Ex: Mr. Addams likes to COLLIDE ["Imps" toy trains] at high speed.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.
Ex: They ` hot-wired " a prison van and ["Manr" repeatedly] RAMMED it into a security gate.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
Where the event takes place.
Ex: Father Shanahan , of Rushey Mead , Leicester , RAMMED his Datsun into another car ["Place" on the way to the city 's Gilroes cemetery].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Result of the impact.
Ex: I SLAMMED the door ["Result" shut].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the Speed of the Impactor (or Impactors at impact.
Ex: The statue was RAMMED into the wall ["Speed" at 30 mph]--a bit faster than John could have hurled it.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
Subregion identifies the part of the larger whole which was hit.
Ex: The gunman GRAZED him ["Sub_l" on his left temple]. Ex: She STRUCK him hard ["Sub_l" across the left cheek] with the flat of her hand.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the impact occurs.
Ex: A postman RAMMED his Fiat Panda into a getaway car ["Time" after spotting the burglars ] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent causes an impact.
Ex: ["Agent" One juggler] was HITTING the ceiling with every other ball.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects an Impactee.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The FE Means identifies the means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The FE Purpose identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects the Impactee.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Period_of_iterations during which the Agent repeatedly causes impacts.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes an Impactor to make sudden, forcible contact with an Impactee.
Ex: ["Cause" A violent explosion]RATTLED the windows.

frame.name: Feeling
frame.definition: In this frame an Experiencer experiences an Emotion or is in an Emotional_state. There can also be an Evaluation of the internal experiential state. Ex: ["Experiencer" John] FEELS ["Emotion" anger towards his mother]. Ex: ["Experiencer" Martha] FEELS ["Emotional_state" angry]. Ex: ["Experiencer" Dr. Hibbert] FEELS ["Evaluation" good]. Inalienably possessed aspects of the Experiencer frequently stand in for the Experiencer. Ex: ["Experiencer" Her heart] FELT ["Emotional_state" angry].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer experiences the Emotion or is in the Emotional_state. Ex: After two pints, ["Exp" he] FELT ["Eval" a bit better] and Ted arrived.

fe.name: Emotion
fe.definition: The Emotion is the feeling that the Experiencer experiences. Ex: ["Exp" Patients] EXPERIENCE ["Emot" high anxiety levels] at time of admission to hospital.

fe.name: Emotional_state
fe.definition: The Emotional_state is the state the Experiencer is in. Ex: Her heart was galloping so fast that ["Exp" she] FELT ["Emo_s" quite giddy with happiness].

fe.name: Evaluation
fe.definition: The Evaluation is a negative or positive assessment of the Experiencer regarding his or her Emotional_state. Ex: ["Exp" Max] was FEELING ["Eval" worse than he'd ever felt in his life].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The thing or state-of-affairs that leads to the Experiencer feeling the Emotion or Emotional_state.
