lexunit.name: feelings.n
lexunit.definition: COD: emotional responses or tendencies to respond.

lexunit.name: emotion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strong feeling, such as joy, anger, or sadness.

frame.name: Containing
frame.definition: In this frame a Container holds within its physical boudaries the Contents. Ex: ["Container" The box] HOLDS ["Contents" three hundred pictures].

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
The Container is the physical object which holds within its boundaries the Contents
Ex: ["Container" The box] HOLDS three hundred pictures.

fe.name: Contents
fe.definition: The Contents is the substance or objects contained within the physical bounds of the Container. Ex: The box HOLDS ["Contents" three hundred pictures].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Container holds the Contents.

lexunit.name: contain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have or hold within.

lexunit.name: hold.v
lexunit.definition: COD: contain or be capable of containing.

lexunit.name: house.v
lexunit.definition: COD: enclose or encase.

frame.name: Praiseworthiness
frame.definition: The Behavior of an Evaluee is described in terms of the reaction it deserves from somebody, such as praise, blame or admiration.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: The Behavior of the Evaluee is being judged as worthy of a particular reaction. Ex: It was COMMENDABLE ["Eval" of Lisa] ["Beh" to give so much to charity].

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Behavior on which the assessment of praiseworthiness is based. Ex: ["Beh" Your behavior] is COMMENDABLE Ex: The children made a COMMENDABLE ["Beh" effort].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the judgement or reaction is deserved. Ex: ["Beh" Your actions] were ["Deg" very] COMMENDABLE

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

lexunit.name: praiseworthy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving of praise

lexunit.name: commendable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving praise

lexunit.name: reprehensible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving censure or condemnation

lexunit.name: blameworthy.a
lexunit.definition: FN: deserving reproach or blame

lexunit.name: deplorable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving strong condemnation; shockingly bad

lexunit.name: lamentable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deplorable or regrettable

lexunit.name: laudable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving praise and commendation

lexunit.name: admirable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving respect and approval

lexunit.name: pitiable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving or arousing pity

lexunit.name: estimable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: worthy of great respect

lexunit.name: creditable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving public acknowledgement and praise but not necessarily outstanding or successful.

lexunit.name: detestable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving intense dislike

lexunit.name: abominable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: deserving of revulsion or disgust

lexunit.name: execrable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: detestable; worthy of execration

lexunit.name: honorable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: bringing or worthy of honour

lexunit.name: dishonorable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: worthy of or causing dishonor

lexunit.name: meritorious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving reward or praise

lexunit.name: despicable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving hatred and contempt.

frame.name: Reparation
frame.definition:
The words in this frame describe the process of making amends for some (wrongful) action (the Injury) committed by the Wrongdoer. In this process, in order to appease the Injured_party or to follow laws or customs, the Wrongdoer performs some Benefitting_Action for the Injured_party or gives the Injured_party some Gift.
Ex: ["Wrongdoer" I] will MAKE ["Injury" it] UP ["Injured_party" to you]. Ex: Sinn Fein said that ["Wrongdoer" the marchers] had to _make_ RESTITUTION ["Injured_party" to the Catholics] ["Injury" for the disruption and violence]. Ex: ["Wrongdoer" The tribesmen] tried to _make_ AMENDS ["Injured_party" to us] ["Gift" with handfuls of their most precious seashells].

fe.name: Injured_party
fe.definition: The Injured_party was affected by some previous wrongful act of the Wrongdoer and who should benefit from the reparations. Ex: You can never make AMENDS ["Injrd_prty" to Susan] for standing her up.

fe.name: Injury
fe.definition: The Injury is the injurious action that the Wrongdoer committed against the Injured_party. Although conceptually present, this FE need not always be realized. Ex: Wyelander sought REPARATIONS ["Injury" for the brutal murder of his nephew].

fe.name: Wrongdoer
fe.definition: The Wrongdoer makes amends to the Injured_party for the Injury. Ex: How can ["Wrongdoer" I] MAKE it UP to you?

fe.name: Benefitting_Action
fe.definition: The Benefitting_Action is performed by the Wrongdoer to make amends. Ex: Between friends, AMENDS can be made ["Bene" by apologizing].

fe.name: Gift
fe.definition: Gift identifies the entity that the Wrongdoer gives to the Injured_party. Ex: He MADE it UP to her ["Gift" with a bouquet of flowers].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner marks any description of the Wrongdoer's making of reparations not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification, (e.g. _probably_), and general descriptions comparing events (e.g. _the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Wrongdoer that also affect the action ( e.g. _presumptuously_). Ex: Smeagol ["Mnr" humbly] made AMENDS for his earlier bad behavior.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Wrongdoer makes amends. Ex: RESTITUTION was given ["Place" in Milan] with the Treaty of Abiselle.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when amends are made. Ex: He made AMENDS to her ["Time" that very afternoon].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Wrongdoer makes restitution to the Injured_party. Ex: He thinks that Japan made RESTITUTION for the incident ["Purp" to lull Americans into complacency].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Wrongdoer makes amends for the Injury .
Ex: Of course, they won't be able to MAKE it UP to you ["Degree" completely].

lexunit.name: reparation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the making of amends for a wrong

lexunit.name: restitution.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the restoration of something to its original state

lexunit.name: amends.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an action or actions performed to benefit someone whom one has injured; reparation

lexunit.name: make up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make reparation (for), to compensate (for)

frame.name: Forgiveness
frame.definition: A Judge refrains from imposing, or demanding a punishment for an Evaluee who has committed an Offense. Ex: ["Judge" God] FORGIVES ["Evaluee" repentant sinners]. Ex: Won't ["Judge" you] FORGIVE ["Evaluee" me] ["Offense" for keeping it a secret]?

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The Judge holds the Evaluee responsible for the Offense.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: The Evaluee is subject to the judgment of the Judge for having committed the Offense. Ex: ["Judge" God] FORGIVES ["Evaluee" repentant sinners].

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition: The Offense is the illicit or unpleasant act committed by the Evaluee. Ex: Won't ["Judge" you] FORGIVE ["Evaluee" me] ["Offense" for keeping it a secret]?

lexunit.name: forgive.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop feeling angry or resentful towards (someone) for an offence or mistake.

lexunit.name: forgiveness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of forgiving

lexunit.name: excuse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: forgive (a fault or offence, or a person committing one).

lexunit.name: pardon.v
lexunit.definition: COD: forgive or excuse (a person, error, or offence).

lexunit.name: condone.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accept or forgive (behaviour considered wrong or offensive)

frame.name: First_rank
frame.definition:
An Item is located at the top end of a scale of importance or social rank (or some other Attribute) in comparison to other members of a Contrast_set (usually, implicit) that is otherwise similar in kind to the Item. Oftentimes, the limits of the Contrast_set are determined by an expression of the Limits_of_consideration.
Ex: The MAIN ["Item" problem] is that the administration has not yet clarified "Regime change." ["Contrast_set" INI] Ex: Oh, he had a great many concerns -- CHIEF ["Contrast_set" among them] ["Item" his own boredom]. Ex: Their PRIMARY ["Item" objective] ["Limits_of_consideration" in Bosnia] was bringing about a lasting peace. ["Contrast_set" INI]

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: An Item is the foremost thing in the Contrast_set.

fe.name: Limits_of_consideration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the domain (usually temporally or spatially defined) within which the Item is primary among its kind. Ex: The FOREMOST band ["Limits_of_consideration" in the world of the 1960's] was clearly the Beatles.

fe.name: Contrast_set
fe.definition: The Contrast_set is a group of entities similar to the Item out of which the Item is the most preeminent. Ex: Our discussion has raised a number of issues, FOREMOST ["Cos" among them] time.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The Attribute of the Item which is under consideration.
Ex: The FOREMOST ski lodge ["Attribute" in size] is Lassen.

lexunit.name: primary.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of chief importance; principal.

lexunit.name: main.a
lexunit.definition: COD: chief in size or importance.

lexunit.name: chief.a
lexunit.definition: COD: most important:

lexunit.name: principal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: first in order of importance; main.

lexunit.name: foremost.a
lexunit.definition: COD: the most prominent in rank, importance, or position.

lexunit.name: lead.n
lexunit.definition: FN: most important or noticeable

lexunit.name: leading.a
lexunit.definition: COD: most important or in first place.

lexunit.name: lead.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the highest ranked

lexunit.name: leader.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The highest ranked

frame.name: Achieving_first
frame.definition:
A Cognizer introduces a New_idea into society.
Ex: It is difficult to imagine how different our lives would be without ["Cognizer" Edison's] INVENTION ["New_idea" of the light bulb.]

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer comes up with or conceptualizes the New_idea. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: Ex: ["Cognizer" Kim Sung] INVENTED cinnamon cheez fries in 1988.

fe.name: New_idea
fe.definition: The New_idea is a concept not previously present in society which the Cognizer introduces.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer comes up with the New_idea. Ex: The strong gravitic shield was DISCOVERED ["Time" in 2162].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Cognizer comes up with the New_idea. Ex: Was the light bulb INVENTED ["Place" in Austria]?

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Cognizer accomplishes the innovative achievement. Ex: Jo INVENTED 550 different electronic devices ["Mns" by tinkering with old cables].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purposefor which the Cognizer creates the New_idea. Ex: He INVENTED the holographic charge-distributor ["Purp" to protect office buildings].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Reason for which the Cognizer created the New_idea.
Ex: Wildcom PIONEERED the use of short wire segments ["Reas" because of rising wire costs].

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: The Field is the general domain of endeavor to which the Cognizer is contributing and of which the New_idea is a part. Ex: These photochemical techniques were PIONEERED ["Fld" in broadcasting].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity used by the Cognizer to achieve the introduction of the New_idea into society.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the creative event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Basis
fe.definition:
The conceptual material from which the Cognizer invents the New_idea.
Ex: Galen INVENTED the term 'gonorrhea' ["Basis" from the words for genital and flow].

fe.name: Location_of_appearance
fe.definition:
The Location_of_appearance is where the Invention is first discovered by others.
Ex: This term was COINED by James Joyce ["Location_of_appearance" in his second novel].

lexunit.name: originate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: create or initiate.

lexunit.name: pioneer.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be the first to do something that becomes thereafter adopted as a common, accepted technique.

lexunit.name: invent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: create or design (a new device, process, etc.).

lexunit.name: discover.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be the first to find or observe (a place, substance, or scientific phenomenon).

lexunit.name: coin.v
lexunit.definition: COD: invent or devise (a new word or phrase).

lexunit.name: coinage.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of inventing new words

lexunit.name: discovery.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of finding something new to the world or one's social group

lexunit.name: discoverer.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who discovers something new to the world or his or her social group

lexunit.name: originator.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who creates a new practice or social institution

lexunit.name: inventor.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who creates a new and useful device or process

lexunit.name: invention.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of creating a new device or process for some useful end

lexunit.name: pioneer.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who goes first into unknown territory or who is the first to develop a process or product in a new field of thought

lexunit.name: pioneering.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the activity of being a pioneer

frame.name: Word_relations
frame.definition:
One linguistic unit, Sign_1, has a relation to another linguistic unit, Sign_2. This relation may be semantic, phonological, orthographic, or distributional in nature. The parameter along which the two signs are set in relation to each other is incorporated in the meaning of the target words in this frame. When the relation is symmetrical, the two linguistic units can be expressed jointly, Signs. Otherwise they have to be expressed disjointly. Ordinarily it is assumed that one linguistic unit has exactly one meaning but in cases where this is not so, a set of Circumstances may be specified that helps pick out the relevant sense.
Ex: ["Signs" Happy and sad] are ANTONYMS. Ex: ["Circumstances" In one sense], ["Sign_1" dog] is a HYPONYM of ["Sign_2" itself].

fe.name: Sign_1
fe.definition: FN: a linguistic unit that carries semantic, phonological or syntactic information. Ex: In one sense, ["Sign_1" dog] is a HYPONYM of itself.

fe.name: Sign_2
fe.definition:
FN: a linguistic unit
Ex: In one sense, dog is a HYPONYM of ["Sign_2" itself].

fe.name: Signs
fe.definition: FN: Linguistic units Ex: ["Signs" Happy and sad] are ANTONYMS.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are conditions under which the relationship holds between Sign_1 and Sign_2.

lexunit.name: synonym.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a word or phrase that means the same as another word or phrase in the same language, e.g. shut and close.

lexunit.name: antonym.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a word opposite in meaning to another

lexunit.name: contrary.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a gradable antonym

lexunit.name: hyponym.n
lexunit.definition: FN: denoting a subtype of what another lexical unit denotes

lexunit.name: hypernym.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a linguistic expression denoting a superordinate concept

lexunit.name: synonymous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a word or phrase) having the same meaning as another word or phrase in the same language.

lexunit.name: meronym.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a linguistic expression that names a part of a larger whole

lexunit.name: holonym.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a linguistic expressions that names the whole of which a given linguistic expression is a part

lexunit.name: homophone.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of two or more words having the same pronunciation but different meanings, origins, or spelling (e.g. new and knew).

lexunit.name: homograph.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of two or more words spelled the same but having different meanings and origins.

lexunit.name: collocate.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a linguistic expression that fequently co-occurs with another linguistic expression

lexunit.name: collocate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to frequently co-occur with another linguistic expression

lexunit.name: homonym.n
lexunit.definition: COD: each of two or more words having the same spelling and pronunciation but different meanings and origins (e.g. pole #1 and pole #2 ).

lexunit.name: homophonous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a word or words) having the same pronunciation as another but different meaning, origin, or spelling

frame.name: Performing_arts
frame.definition: The Performers, together with behind the scenes Personnel, execute a Performance according to a Script and/or Score. The purpose of the Performance is to create an experience for an Audience, who then judge its merits. Performances may be in many different Mediums and be of various Types. This frame is very elaborate in modern society and there are a number of traditions and practices typically (but not necessarily) related to Performances: The Performance is preceded by many practice sessions in which the Performers and other Personnel attempt to improve the quality and/or fidelity of their individual and collective performances to the Script and/or Score. The Audience members pay a fee to experience the Performance. The Performers (and Personnel) receive payment for contributing to the Performance. Often there are other individuals involved in the specifically financial aspects of the Performance and Performers. Critics act as part of the Audience and then write reviews that evaluate the merits of the Performance, describing the Performance to other potential Audience members. Due to the high quality of previous Performances, Performers can become famous, i.e. well known and liked. Those who like them particularly well become fans of the Performer. (Shared with writers...)

fe.name: Performer
fe.definition: The Performer provides an experience for the Audience.

fe.name: Personnel
fe.definition: The Personnel, including writers, producers, stage hands, key grips, etc., contribute to the Performance without actually being directly perceived by the Audience.

fe.name: Audience
fe.definition: The Audience experiences the Performance.

fe.name: Performance
fe.definition: The experience generated by the Performers and perceived by the Audience.

fe.name: Script
fe.definition: The (usually written) directions which instruct the Performers on what actions to perform, when, and how. It has many different names depending on the Type of Performance including _script_, _screenplay_, _libretto_, _book_, and _choreography_.

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: The Score may be performed in the Performance, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Type of Performance, including _dance_, _theater_, _film_, etc.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Performer to transmit the Performance to the Audience.

lexunit.name: music.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the art or science of combining vocal or instrumental sounds (or both) to produce beauty of form, harmony, and expression of emotion.

lexunit.name: performance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of performing a play, concert, or other form of entertainment.

lexunit.name: play.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a dramatic work for the stage or to be broadcast.

frame.name: Linguistic_meaning
frame.definition: A linguistic Form has a particular Meaning, possibly restricted to a particular Context. Some linguistic Forms, nouns and nominal expressions, also can refer to an object in the real or an imagined world, a Referent.

fe.name: Form
fe.definition: Form is the formal pole of a linguistic sign.

fe.name: Meaning
fe.definition: Meaning is the sense of a linguistic Form.

fe.name: Context
fe.definition: The FE Context is used for expressions that indicate under which semantic, collocational, pragmatic or other circumstances a Form has a particular Meaning.

fe.name: Referent
fe.definition: Referent identifies an object in the real (or a hypothetical) world that a linguistic expression is used to talk about.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Form and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: denote.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to function as a linguistic expression of the concept of

lexunit.name: denotation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a directly conveyed meaning of a linguistic expression (as opposed to implied or associated idea)

lexunit.name: ambiguous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of language) having more than one meaning

lexunit.name: polysemous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of a linguistic expression) having more than one meaning

lexunit.name: monosemous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of linguistic expressions) having only one meaning

lexunit.name: vague.a
lexunit.definition: FN: uncertain or indefinite in meaning

lexunit.name: designate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (of linguistic expressions) to denote

lexunit.name: intension.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the internal content of a concept

lexunit.name: extension.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the range of a term or concept as measured by the objects which it denotes or contains

lexunit.name: meaning.n
lexunit.definition: FN: what is meant by a linguistic expression

lexunit.name: mean.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a word) have as its signification in the same language or its equivalent in another language

lexunit.name: referential.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (for linguistic expressions) to have a referent

lexunit.name: non-referential.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of linguistic expressions) lacking a referent

lexunit.name: sense.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a way in which an expression or situation can be interpreted; a meaning

lexunit.name: reading.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an interpretation or understanding of a word that is considered a separate sense

frame.name: Importance
frame.definition:
A Factor affects the outcome of an Undertaking, which can be a goal-oriented activity or the maintenance of a desirable state, the work in a Field, or something portrayed as affecting an Interested_party. A Reason may be given for the importance of the Factor. The Degree of importance may also be specified.
Ex: Temperature is the ["Degree" most] CRITICAL ["Factor" factor] ["Undertaking" in successful storage]. Ex: ["Factor" Timing] will be CRITICAL. Ex: ["Factor" Heathcliff] _is_ ["Degree" more] IMPORTANT ["Interested_party" to me] ["Degree" than myself] . Ex: ["Factor" 1992] _was_ _of_ ["Degree" great] IMPORTANCE ["Interested_party" to the business community].

fe.name: Factor
fe.definition: Factor is used for the concrete or abstract entity whose importance is assessed. Ex: ["Factor" Being sure they are buying fresh food] _is_ IMPORTANT ["Interested_party" to most people].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which the Factor is important to the Undertaking. Ex: ["Factor" 1992] _is_ _of_ ["Degree" great] IMPORTANCE ["Interested_party" to the business community].

fe.name: Undertaking
fe.definition: The Undertaking is a process or state or field of activity in which the Interested_party has a stake. Ex: Temperature is the ["Degree" most] CRITICAL ["Factor" factor] ["Undertaking" in successful storage].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Factor is important to the Undertaking. Ex: It 's CRITICAL to get it right ["Reason" because there are situations where if you don't, they will withhold some commission.].

fe.name: Interested_party
fe.definition:
Interested_party identifies the people who are affected by a particular Factor.
Ex: ["Factor" Being sure they are buying fresh food] _is_ IMPORTANT ["Interested_party" to most people].

fe.name: Field
fe.definition:
A Factor may be generally important to the people or the activities in a field of endeavour.
Ex: ["Factor" A successful GATT round] _is_ IMPORTANT ["Field" for the world economy].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Factor is important to the Undertaking.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Factor is important.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

lexunit.name: crucial.a
lexunit.definition: COD: decisive or critical, especially in the success or failure of something

lexunit.name: critical.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having a decisive importance in the success or failure of something.

lexunit.name: key.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of crucial importance

lexunit.name: decisive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: acting to settle an issue quickly and effectively

lexunit.name: pivotal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of crucial or central importance

lexunit.name: important.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of great significance or value

lexunit.name: significant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extensive or important enough to merit attention

lexunit.name: importance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state or quality of being important

lexunit.name: significance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the quality of being significant; importance.

lexunit.name: import.n
lexunit.definition: COD: importance

lexunit.name: major.a
lexunit.definition: COD: important, serious, or significant.

lexunit.name: instrumental.a
lexunit.definition: FN: important or serving as a principle means in some undertaking.

lexunit.name: vital.a
lexunit.definition: COD: absolutely necessary; essential.

lexunit.name: considerable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having merit or distinction.

lexunit.name: fundamental.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of or serving as a foundation or core; of central importance.

lexunit.name: main.a
lexunit.definition: FN: chief in importance.

lexunit.name: serious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: significant or worrying in terms of danger or risk.

lexunit.name: seriously.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: to a grave degree.

lexunit.name: acute.a
lexunit.definition: FN: critically important

lexunit.name: landmark.n
lexunit.definition: FN: of pivotal or decisive importance

lexunit.name: epic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: impressive or major; hypothetically deserving of legendary status

lexunit.name: count.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be important

frame.name: Manufacturing
frame.definition: A Manufacturer produces a Product from a Resource for commercial purposes. Ex: They PRODUCED ["Product" only half of the units] ["Circumstances" after an injunction to follow the environmental policy].

fe.name: Manufacturer
fe.definition: The person or company that produces the Product. Ex: ["Manufacturer" General Electric] MANUFACTURES ["Product" electronic appliances].

fe.name: Product
fe.definition: The Product is produced by the Manufacturer. Ex: ["Manufacturer" The company] MANUFACTURED ["Product" T-shirts].

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition: Resource is the material that the product is made from. Ex: ["Product" Copal varnishes] are MANUFACTURED ["Resource" from fossilised resins].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Product is manufactured. Ex: ["Product" Those leather shoes] were MADE ["Place" in Italy].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This Fe identifies the Time when the product was produced. Ex: ["Product" Those cars] were PRODUCED ["Time" in 1997].

fe.name: Factory
fe.definition: Factory identifies the particular plant where the Product is manufactured. Ex: ["Product" Those machines] were MANUFACTURED ["Factory" in the Miami plant].

fe.name: Consumer
fe.definition: The Manufacturer produces the Product for the Consumer. Ex: ["Product" The toys] are MADE ["Consumer" for children].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A phrase that describes the state of the Manufacturer or the Product during the manufacturing process. Ex: They MANUFACTURED the goods ["Depictive" naked].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Instrument with which a Manufacturer produces a Product. Ex: ["Product" Those lamps] were MADE ["Instrument" by machines].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which a Manufacturer creates a Product. Ex: ["Product" Fine furniture] is usually MADE ["Manner" slowly].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which a Manufacturer creates a Product. Ex: ["Product" Cars] are MANUFACTURED ["Means" by mass production].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Manufacturer produces a Product. Ex: ["Manufacturer" The company] will PRODUCE more ["Depictive" high-tech] ["Product" gadgets] ["Purpose" to meet the demand of the market].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the the product was produced. Ex: ["Manufacturer" They] PRODUCED ["Product" only half of the units] ["Circumstances" after an injunction to follow the environmental policy].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of manufacturing events in a given time period.
Ex: We PRODUCE 90 million units ["fre" every month].

fe.name: Locus
fe.definition: The Locus is a description of the active zone of the Manufacturer, where the manufacturing most saliently takes place.

lexunit.name: manufacture.v

lexunit.name: produce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make, manufacture, or create.

lexunit.name: manufacture.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process of manufacturing

lexunit.name: make.v

lexunit.name: manufacturing.n

lexunit.name: manufacturer.n

lexunit.name: production.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of producing or being produced.

lexunit.name: producer.n

lexunit.name: industrial.a
lexunit.definition: FN: related to economic activity concerned with the processing of raw materials and manufacture of goods in factories.

lexunit.name: fabricate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: construct or manufacture (an industrial product), especially from prepared components

lexunit.name: fabrication.n
lexunit.definition: FN: construction or manufacturing of an industrial product, especially from prepared components

lexunit.name: maker.n
lexunit.definition: FN: party responsible for manufacturing.

frame.name: Behind_the_scenes
frame.definition: Artists work at various tasks that further the completion of a film, play, television show, or other similar Production. Artists never appear on stage or in front of a camera. Some (e.g., a director) may interact with the actors (on-screen participants) of the Production. Often times a particular Production is made for distribution by a Distributor, by a particular Studio, or in a specific Medium. The Artists may be categorized into Type or work in specific Medium. Ex: ["Artist" Steven Spielberg] DIRECTED ["Production" several films] ["Studio" for Universal Pictures]. Ex: ["Studio" Universal Pictures and Amblin Entertainment] PRODUCED ["Production" Jurassic Park] ["Distributor" for MCA]. Ex: Surprisingly, this ["Medium" film] ["Artist" PRODUCER] was willing to work for a cable company. Ex: ["Type" Independent] ["Artist" PRODUCERS] often win big at smaller film festivals.

fe.name: Artist
fe.definition: The Artist works off-stage to help make the Production. Ex: ["Artist" John Williams] COMPOSED the soundtrack to Star Wars.

fe.name: Production
fe.definition: The Production is the final product put out by the off-stage (and on-stage) participants. Ex: Ralph Smith PRODUCED ["Prod" the off-Broadway hit "Why Is My Name Ralph?"].

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An Artist may be categorizedy by Type. Ex: ["Type" Hollywood] DIRECTOR Ex: ["Type" independent] FILM-MAKER

fe.name: Distributor
fe.definition: Often (especially with film or television) the Production is advertised and transmitted to the audience by the Distributor. Ex: Even desperate producers would never PRODUCE a film ["Dist" for that television station].

fe.name: Studio
fe.definition: This FE indicates the particular orgainzaion that makes the Production. Ex: The latest performance PRODUCED ["Studio" by The Umbrella Thesbians] was a major hit in France. Ex: First layer: ["Studio" New Line Cinema] PRODUCES several films each year. Ex: Second layer: ["Artist" New Line Cinema] PRODUCES several films each year.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Medium in which a particular Artist works or a Production is made. Ex: He PRODUCES ["Medium" for television] Ex: She is a ["Medium" theatre] DIRECTOR.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the time when the Production is made. Ex: Silence of the Lambs was FILMED ["Time" in 1991].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE indicates the location of production. Ex: The documentary was SHOT ["Place" on location].

fe.name: Nationality
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Nationality, ethnicity, or primary working location of the Artist. Ex: Several ["Nationality" Canadian] DIRECTORS have received attention from critics in recent years. Ex: ["Nationality" Local] FILM-MAKERS often collaborate for larger efforts.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which an Artist works on a Production. Ex: I PRODUCED this film ["Purpose" to let people know what I went through as a child].

fe.name: Performer
fe.definition: In screen performances, the Performer is filmed as he or she acts out a role with respect to the larger Production Ex: This particular scene was SHOT ["Perf" with a local choir and dancers].

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: The music which may be performed in the performance of the Production, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

fe.name: Scene
fe.definition: A Scene is a sub-part of a larger production. In film, scenes are sometimes recorded independently, and later edited into the final movie.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Artist creates the Production.

frame.name: Taking
frame.definition: An Agent removes a Theme from a Source so that the it is in the Agent's possession.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The person who takes possession of the Theme. Ex: ["Agent" Milton] TOOK the can of beer out of the refrigerator.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Agent takes possession of the Theme. Ex: Milton TOOK ["Theme" the can of beer] out of the refrigerator.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The location of the Theme prior to the taking. Ex: Milton TOOK the can of beer ["Source" out of the refrigerator].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the taking takes place. Ex: Police SEIZED several tons of marijuana ["Place" in Berkeley] last weekend.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the taking takes place. Ex: The government SEIZURE of a suspected dissident's computer ["Time" last November] has increased the tension between citizens and law enforcement.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner of the taking. Ex: Milton ["Mnr" stealthily] TOOK the can of beer out of the refrigerator.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The intermediate action taken by the Agent to take the Theme. Ex: Milton TOOK the can of beer from John ["Mns" by distracting him with a shiny nickel].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for the taking. Ex: Milton TOOK the can of beer out of the refrigerator ["Pur" to make sure no one else took it].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for the taking. Ex: Milton TOOK the champagne out of the ice ["Rsn" because it was getting too cold].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: The larger event which contains the Taking event. Ex: These weapons were SEIZED ["CE" in a police raid].

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to act so as to acquire

lexunit.name: seize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to take by force, esp. despite the resistance of the current possessor or contrary to law

lexunit.name: seizure.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of seizing.

lexunit.name: grab.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take something from a source

frame.name: Receiving
frame.definition: A Recipient comes into possession of the Theme as a result of the joint action of the Donor and the Recipient. The Receiving frame like the Giving frame requires that the Donor first has possession of the Theme and that following the transfer, the Donorno longer has the Theme and the Recipient does.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person who gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

fe.name: Purpose_of_donor
fe.definition:
The aim of the Donor, which they believe will be accomplished by giving the Theme.
Ex: Rural communities RECEIVED government subsidies["pur" to ensure their continued viability.].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The act that the Recipient performs which brings about their reception of the Theme.
Ex: She received the package ["mea" by signing her name on the delivery certification].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.
Ex: She received the package ["tim" before the month was out].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Mode_of_transfer
fe.definition:
The system whereby the Theme travels (literally or metaphorically) so that the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.
Ex: I RECEIVED it ["mod" by e-mail].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Recipient or Theme during the action.
Ex: I didn't expect to RECEIVE this steak ["dep" absolutely raw]!

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The character of the Recipient which saliently affects the action, or a general description of the action itself.
Ex: He ["man" slyly] RECEIVED the package without signing for it.

fe.name: Countertransfer
fe.definition:
A good given or a service rendered by the Recipient, in return for wich the Theme is given to the Recipient by the Donor.
Ex: Shelley Walker of Washoe County?s Information Technology Department RECEIVED $100 ["cou" for her suggestion to create an electronic employee evaluation form].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: When the Theme is received physically by the Recipient from the Donor, the Path of motion of the Theme may be specified.

fe.name: Purpose_of_theme
fe.definition:
What the Recipient intends to do with the Theme.
Ex: James Madison Memorial High School RECEIVED $1,000 ["pot" to purchase instruments for school orchestra and band programs].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
A role that the Theme is intended to fill by the Donor.
Ex: He RECEIVED the book ["rol" as a gift] from his uncle.

lexunit.name: receive.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to take something that is given

lexunit.name: accept.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to consciously receive something given

lexunit.name: receipt.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of receiving something or the fact of its being received

frame.name: Omen
frame.definition:
One phenomenon, Phenomenon_1 is an indication of the current or future existence of another phenomenon, Phenomenon_2. There is no Cognizer present on the scene, in distinction to the Expectation frame where a Cognizer takes (the equivalent of) Phenomenon_1 as evidence for (the equivalent of) Phenomenon_2. Many words in this frame also allow a slightly different understanding, whereby Phenomenon_1 provides clues as to the good or bad Outcome of an expected Phenomenon_2. Instead of Phenomenon_2 an Interested_party that will be involved in the event or state that is Phenomenon_2 may be mentioned. In both construals, the two phenomena are asymmetrical and consequently they have no joint syntactic realization.
Ex: ["Phenomenon_1" Such potential] AUGURS ["Outcome" well] ["Phenomenon_2" for the 1990s] Ex: ["Phenomenon_1" Its appearance] _was_ an ["Outcome" ill] OMEN. Ex: ["Phenomenon_1" Cold-blooded words] do not necessarily BETOKEN ["Phenomenon_2" a callous nature]. Ex: I wish I could say ["Phenomenon_1" my success] BODES ["Outcome" well] ["Interested_party" for him].

fe.name: Phenomenon_1
fe.definition:
Phenomenon_1 provides evidence for the existence or the nature of the Outcome of Phenomenon_2.
Ex: ["Phenomenon_1" To achieve so much this year] AUGURS well for the future.

fe.name: Phenomenon_2
fe.definition:
Phenomenon_2 is that phenomenon whose existence or quality is at issue.
Ex: This move PRESAGES ["Phenomenon_2" a freeze on the granting of new concessions].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition:
The FE Outcome identifies those expressions that indicate how Phenomenon_2 is expected to turn out based on the evidence of Phenomenon_1.
Ex: It all BODES ["Outcome" well] for the future.

fe.name: Interested_party
fe.definition:
Interested_party marks expressions that indicate people who are interested in the Outcome of Phenomenon_2.
Ex: That Meisel speaks so highly of Kate BODES well ["Interested_party" for her].

fe.name: Strength
fe.definition: The degree to which the Phenomenon_1 predicts the occurrence of Phenomenon_2.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the omen is occuring.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which Phenomenon_1 is an omen for Phenomenon_2 or the Outcome.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.definition: COD: be a sign or warning that (something momentous or calamitous) is likely to happen

lexunit.name: portent.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a sign or warning that a momentous or calamitous event is likely to happen

lexunit.definition: COD: be a sign of

lexunit.definition: COD: be an early indication or version of

lexunit.definition: COD: give good grounds for expecting

lexunit.name: herald.v
lexunit.definition: COD: signal the imminence of

frame.name: Performers_and_roles
frame.definition:
A Performer has a certain Role in a Performance and plays their part by following the directions in the Script for that particular Role.
Ex: ["Performer" Margaret Thatcher] PLAYED ["Role" Juliet] ["Performance" in a school play]. Ex: ["Performance" "Pulp Fiction"] STARRED ["Performer" John Travolta and a lot of other big names]. Ex: ["Performer" Mel Gibson] STARRED ["Performance" in "Braveheart"] ["Role" as the leader of a Scottish rebellion]. Ex: I play the CHARACTER ["Role" of Yusuf] in this film.

fe.name: Audience
fe.definition: The Audience experiences the Performance.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Performer to transmit the Performance to the Audience.

fe.name: Performance
fe.definition: The Performers generates the Performance which the Audience perceives.

fe.name: Performer
fe.definition: The Performer provides an experience for the Audience.

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: The music which may be performed in the Performance, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

fe.name: Script
fe.definition: The (usually written) directions which instruct the Performers on what actions to perform, when, and how. It has many different names depending on the Type of Performance including _script_, _screenplay_, _libretto_, _book_, and _choreography_.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates the subtype of Performance, including _dance_, _theater_, _film_, etc.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Role identifies one of the possible relations that the Performer can have to the Performance. The Role(s) a Performer has in the Performance will determine which parts of the Script should be performed by the Performer, as the Script is written in terms of which Role(s) each set of instructions applies to. In the fields of theater, movies, ballet, and opera, a Role generally corresponds to a character in the story of the Script, while other types of performance may use more general Roles like _lead violinist_.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when an event occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place an event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing.

fe.name: Performer1
fe.definition: The person that performs alongside Performer2. Ex: He CO-STARRED ["Perf1" with Matt Perry] in Tool 3.

fe.name: Performer2
fe.definition: The person that is also in the Performance, alongside Performer1. Ex: Who CO-STARRED ["Perf2" with Glen Close] in that space opera thingy?

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: How long the Performer is in the Performance. Ex: She STARRED in Cats ["Dur" for several years].

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This is an appraisal or description of the performance event.

lexunit.name: as.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: playing in the role of

lexunit.name: feature.v

frame.name: Cause_to_fragment
frame.definition:
An Agent suddenly and often violently separates the Whole_patient into two or more smaller Pieces, resulting in the Whole_patient no longer existing as such. Several lexical items are marked with the semantic type Negative, which indicates that the fragmentation is necessarily judged as injurious to the original Whole_patient.
Compare this frame with Damaging, Render_non-functional, and Removing.
Ex: ["Agent" He] RIPPED UP ["Pat" the letter] ["Manner" faster than you can say "Jack Robbins"]. ["Pieces" INI] Ex: Don't go in there or ["Pat" you] 'll be TORN ["Pieces" to bits]! ["Agent" CNI] Ex: ["Agent" She] SHATTERED ["Pat" the vase] ["Means" with a casual backhand blow] ["Purp" to make it look like there had been a struggle]. ["Pieces" INI] Ex: TEAR ["Pieces" into 6" strips, each about one inch wide], then bake at 400. ["Agent" CNI] ["Pat" CNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Whole_patient being broken into Pieces. Ex: ["Agt" I and I alone] can SHATTER the gem and break the curse.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Whole_patient to accomplish its fracture.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the fracturing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the breakage.

fe.name: Whole_patient
fe.definition: The entity which is destroyed by the Agent and that ends up broken into Pieces. Ex: Shattering someone's confidence is a little different than SHATTERING ["Pat" a dish].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent breaks the Whole_patient into pieces.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the break-up of the Whole_patient. Ex: The window cleaners SHATTERED every other pane ["Purp" to protest their working conditions].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action. Ex: He TORE the treaty UP ["Reason" out of frustration].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent breaks up the Whole_patient.

fe.name: Pieces
fe.definition: The fragments of the Whole_patient that result from the Agent's action. Ex: I SMASHED the toy boat ["Pieces" to flinders].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The degree to which the fracturing is completed. Ex: I SHATTERED the vase ["Degr" completely].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The part of the Whole_patient which is directly affected by the breakage. Ex: With a swing of his broadsword, he SHATTERED the goblet["Subr" all the way to the stem].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event. Ex: I BROKE it ["Result" open].

fe.name: Resistant_surface
fe.definition:
The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Agent presses the Whole_patient.
Ex: Michael BROKE the bottle ["Res_surf" against his head] . Ex: She did her best to RIP her shirt ["Res_surf" on the fence].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event which leads to the fragmentation of the Whole_patient.

frame.name: Damaging
frame.definition:
An Agent affects a Patient in such a way that the Patient (or some Subregion of the Patient) ends up in a non-canonical state. Often this non-canonical state is undesirable, and some lexical units (marked with the Negative semantic type) specifically indicate that the Patient is negatively affected.
Compare this frame with Destroying, Cause_to_fragment, and Render_nonfunctional.
Ex: ["Agent" That idiot] just DENTED ["Patient" my car]! Ex: ["Agent" Some ne'er-do-wells] DEFACED ["Patient" the Park's wall] ["Instrument" with spray paint] ["Purpose" to show their anger at local natural resources allocation policy]. Ex: Please don't DAMAGE ["Patient" the goods].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the damage to the Patient.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The degree to which the Patient is damaged. Ex:

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Patient to accomplish the damage.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the action of damaging which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the damage.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent damages the Patient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the damage to the Patient. Ex: The dock workers KEYED their manager's car ["Purp" to protest their working conditions].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action. Ex: He RENT his garment ["Reason" out of the despair that only biblical character can feel].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the damaging. Ex: The dog TORE his pants ["Subr" just below the seat].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent damages the Patient.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The entity which is affected by the Agent so that it is damaged. Ex:

fe.name: Character_of_end_state
fe.definition:
A description of the state of the Patient after the damaging has taken place, including descriptions of the severity and the permanence of the damaged condition.
Ex: To a all appearances, she had ["cha" permanently] DAMAGED her right clavicle.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
Result of the Agent's action.
Ex: She TORE the sugar packet ["Result" open]

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event which leads to the damage of the Patient.
Ex: ["Cause" The crash] DENTED my car pretty bad.

lexunit.definition: FN: to cause harm to an object

lexunit.name: mar.v

lexunit.name: deface.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to damage the front surface of

lexunit.name: nick.v

lexunit.name: dent.v

lexunit.name: vandalise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to deliberately damage or deface

lexunit.name: scratch.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to create small grooves in the surface of something by sliding contact

lexunit.name: chip.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to strike in such a way that a small chip is detached from a larger object

lexunit.name: score.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to scratch or cut, often repeatedly

lexunit.name: sabotage.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to deliberately damage something in order to impede some activity

lexunit.name: key.v
lexunit.definition: FN: damage (esp. a car) by scraping (with a key or other metal object).

lexunit.name: vandalism.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of vandalising

lexunit.name: rend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tear to pieces.

lexunit.name: tear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rip a hole or split in.

lexunit.name: rip.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tear.

lexunit.name: damage.n
lexunit.definition: FN: harm or direpair inflicted upon something; the result of the act of damaging something

frame.name: Render_nonfunctional
frame.definition: An Agent affects an Artifact so that it is no longer capable of performing its inherent function.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity causes the Artifact to not function.

fe.name: Artifact
fe.definition: The device that no longer works.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An event that the Agent hopes to bring about by breaking an Artifact. Ex: I TOTALED my car ["Purp" so I wouldn't have to renew the tags].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action that the Agent performs which results in the Artifact being inoperable.
Ex: I guess I BROKE the doorknob ["Mns" by twisting it too hard].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An inanimate entity or force that renders the Artifact non-functional.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the event takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place at which the event takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A holistic description of the event (e.g. _the same way_), including depictions of the Agent in terms of how the state of the Agent affects the overall action (e.g _maliciously_).

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: Meaning: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs--Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Artifact is (or has been) rendered nonfunctional.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of particpant while lack of functionality is being rendered.

lexunit.name: total.v
lexunit.definition: COD: destroy or kill.

lexunit.name: break.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make non-functional

lexunit.name: hose.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to render completely useless.

lexunit.name: knock out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: destroy or disable equipment.

lexunit.name: disable.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put out of action.

lexunit.name: incapacitate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to cause something to stop functioning

frame.name: Destroying
frame.definition: A Destroyer (a conscious entity) or Cause (an event, or an entity involved in such an event) affects the Undergoer negatively so that the Undergoer no longer exists.

fe.name: Destroyer
fe.definition:
The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Undergoer's destruction.
Ex: ["Agt" Who] can UNMAKE the ring?

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The degree to which the destruction is completed. Ex: I DESTROYED all signs of our presence ["Degr" completely].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity directed by the Destroyer that interacts with an Undergoer to accomplish the Undergoer's destruction.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the process of destruction which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Destroyer that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Destroyer that accomplishes the destruction. Ex: Samptu OBLITERATED the land of Abde ["Mns" with a great flood], leaving only the sea.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Destroyer destroys the Undergoer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Destroyer causes the destruction of the Undergoer. Ex: We LAID WASTE to Hattusas ["Purp" to subjugate them, not to vex them].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Destroyer is responding to in destroying the Undergoer. Ex: He RAZED the goddess's temple ["Reason" out of sheer anger].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event on the Undergoer. This FE is very rare in this frame, and since the Undergoeris destroyed by this process, the Result is generally constrained to indicate the Undergoer's resulting inexistence. Ex: All of the buildings had been RAZED ["Result" to nothing].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The part of the Undergoer which is directly affected by the destruction. Ex: The village was DEVASTATED ["Subr" from the north end to the banks of the Neva].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Destroyer destroys the Undergoer.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
The entity which is destroyed by the Destroyer.
Ex: Who can UNMAKE ["Und" the ring]?

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The event or entity which is responsible for the destruction of the Undergoer. Ex: ["Cause" The subsequent explosions] LEVELED most downtown office buildings. Ex: ["Cause" Tornados] VAPORIZED this town a few decades back.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The category in which the Undergoer is destroyed.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Cause or Destroyer destroys the Undergoer.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

lexunit.name: raze.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to destroy (buildings, etc.), esp. by fire

lexunit.name: unmake.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to undo the action of making (as of a law); to destroy the structure of something

lexunit.name: level.v
lexunit.definition: COD: demolish (a building or town).

lexunit.name: destroy.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to exert force so as to cause something to cease to exist

lexunit.name: obliterate.v

lexunit.name: destruction.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an event of destroying

lexunit.name: devastate.v

lexunit.name: devastation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the destruction of large parts of "Floods caused the devastation of most of the fall crops."

lexunit.name: vaporize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: destroy utterly (as if) by turning into vapor.

lexunit.name: annihilate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: destroy utterly.

lexunit.name: annihilation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: to destroy completely

lexunit.name: lay_waste.v
lexunit.definition: FN: the deliberate destruction of buildings, farms, etc., as by an army or force of nature

lexunit.name: demolish.v
lexunit.definition: FN: destroy a fixed structure by crushing

lexunit.name: demolition.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of destroying or dismantling, esp. of buildings

lexunit.name: dismantle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take to pieces.

lexunit.name: dismantlement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of taking something apart.

lexunit.name: destructive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: causing destruction.

lexunit.name: blow up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to destroy with explosives

frame.name: Collaboration
frame.definition:
Partner_1 and Partner_2 or a group of Partners work together in some Undertaking. The Partners are taken to be of equal status even when expressed disjointly.
Ex: ["Partner_1" CSTR] ["Manner" actively] COLLABORATES ["Partner_2" with the Departments of Artificial Intelligence and Physics]. Ex: ["Partners" Tom and the American composer Steve Riche] have ["Time" recently] COLLABORATED ["Undertaking" on a piece of elevator music].

fe.name: Partner_1
fe.definition:
When the parties in a collaboration are expressed separately, this Frame Element marks constituents that express the one that is grammatically more prominent, i.e., the one that is the subject of an active clause.
Ex: ["Partner_1" Smithers] COLLABORATED with Chief Wiggum

fe.name: Partner_2
fe.definition:
This Frame element marks constituents expressing the grammatically less prominent, typically oblique, party in a collaboration.
Ex: Britain is COLLABORATING ["Partner_2" with France and West Germany] in the development of anti-tank missiles

fe.name: Undertaking
fe.definition:
This frame element marks constituents that express the project in which the Partners are collaborating.
Ex: The two artists COLLABORATED ["Undertaking" on a mosaic].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which Partner_1 collaborates with Partner_2 or in which the Partners collaborate.

fe.name: Partners
fe.definition:
This frame element marks expressions that express the parties that work together in an Undertaking.
Ex: ["Partners" Smithers and Chief Wiggum] COLLABORATED well

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the Partners are engaged in their collaboration.
Ex: ["Time" Last year] some of my colleagues collaborated in the design of a theme-park.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the collaboration occurs.
Ex: ["Place" In New Braunfels] Paul and John COLLABORATED in the design of a new Guggenheim

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of time the Partners collaborate.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate to what extent the Partners are cooperating.
Ex: The French government COOPERATED ["Degree" fully] with the New Zealand police.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action taken by the Partners that lets them accomplish the collaboration.

lexunit.name: collaborate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: work jointly on an activity or project

lexunit.name: partner.v
lexunit.definition: COD: associate as partners

lexunit.name: collaborator.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person whith whom someone works on a joint project

lexunit.name: partner.n
lexunit.definition: FN: somebody who takes part in an undertaking with one or more other people

lexunit.name: in_cahoots.a
lexunit.definition: COD: colluding or conspiring together secretly

lexunit.name: conspire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make secret plans jointly to commit an unlawful or harmful act

lexunit.name: collaboration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of working together with someone

lexunit.name: associate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a partner or companion in business or at work

lexunit.name: confederate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an accomplice or fellow worker

lexunit.name: conspiracy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of conspiring

lexunit.name: collude.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come to a secret understanding; conspire

lexunit.name: collusion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: secret or illegal cooperation in order to cheat or deceive others

lexunit.name: team_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come together as a team to achieve a common goal

lexunit.name: cooperate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: work jointly towards the same end.

lexunit.name: cooperation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of cooperating.

lexunit.name: affiliated.a
lexunit.definition: FN: connected to an organization or entity.

lexunit.name: in league.a
lexunit.definition: FN: to be collaborating with another

lexunit.name: jointly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: done in collaboration or conjunction with another entity

lexunit.name: work together.v
lexunit.definition: FN: endeavor to complete a task in a partnered relationship.

lexunit.name: together.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: with the combined efforts of one another

frame.name: Connectors
frame.definition: The Connector is an artifact created to affix a Connected_item or to bind onto a Fixed_location and is primarily so used. A more specific Use may also be specified. Certain words in this frame (e.g. _bond, chain_ in the phrase _in chains_) indicate specifically that the Connector is being used to immobilize something. Connectors have a wide variety of physical forms: long, thin, and flexible for tying (_ropes, bonds, withies_); solid, with a shape corresponding to holes in the entities to be connected (_bolts, nails, pegs_); and liquid (_glues, adhesives, pastes_). Ex: A waterproof ["Connector" ADHESIVE] should be used for this exterior job. Ex: ["X" ["Item" His] ["Connector" BONDS]] had to be ["Gov" loosened] before they could be cut. Ex: She ["Gov" jerked] ["X" on ["Connected_item" His] ["Loc" neck] ["Connector" ROPE]] again, to keep his attention. Ex: I think they ["Gov" cut] ["X" his ["Use" bike] ["Connector" CHAIN]] with bolt cutters.

fe.name: Connector
fe.definition: Connector identifies the entity or substance that forms the bond that maintains the Item in a fixed position; it is usually expressed in a "with"-PP. Ex: The robber tied Harry to the chair with a ["Connector" ROPE].

fe.name: Connected_item
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity that is attached to the Connector in such a way as to stabilize their position or to immobilize them. Ex: The robber tied ["Item" Harry 's] BONDS very tight. Ex: ["Item" Her] ROPE was stuck between two rocks and she couldn't move far.

fe.name: Fixed_location
fe.definition: This FE identifies the location to which the Connector is attached. Ex: The ROPE ["Loc" around his neck] was like a noose, but it hung down as if it were a macabre necktie.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The items that a Connector usually attaches or the type of activity the attaching is generally for. Ex: If the ["Use" safety] ROPE snaps, you're done for.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Material identifies the material of which the Connector is made.
Ex: ["Mat" Silk] ROPE is surprisingly strong for its diameter.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type designates the type of Connector. Often the Type labels part of a multi-word or compound word target.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The term used to refer to a Connector.
Ex: Remove PEG ["nam" 3-B], if possible.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
The individual or group that creates a Connector.
Ex: I tried to find the ["cre" DuPont] ADHESIVE , but they did n't have any .

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which the Connector comes to be.
Ex: The BOLTS ["tim" of the 19th century] had non-standardized thread widths.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Connector.

lexunit.name: ribbon.n

lexunit.name: rope.n

lexunit.name: thread.n

lexunit.name: string.n
lexunit.definition: COD: material consisting of threads of cotton, hemp, etc. twisted together to form a thin leng

lexunit.name: cord.n
lexunit.definition: COD: long thin string or rope made from several twisted strands.

lexunit.name: chain.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a connected flexible series of metal links used for fastening, pulling, etc., or in jewellery.

lexunit.name: bond.n
lexunit.definition: COD: physical restraints used to hold someone prisoner.

lexunit.name: adhesive.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a malleable or liquid substance which can be applied to points of contact between objects to join them.

lexunit.name: tape.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strip of paper or plastic coated with adhesive, used to stick things together.

lexunit.name: glue.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an adhesive substance used for sticking objects or materials together.

lexunit.name: bolt.n

lexunit.name: nut.n

lexunit.name: nail.n

lexunit.name: peg.n

lexunit.name: strap.n

lexunit.name: tack.n

lexunit.name: staple.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a U-shaped piece of wire or metal, usually sharpened at both ends, used to attach objects (with the help of a device) by piercing and immobilizing them at some point(s).

lexunit.name: withy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a tough flexible branch of an osier or other willow, used for tying, binding, or basketry.

lexunit.name: tie.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a thing that ties.

lexunit.name: lace.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cord or leather strip passed through eyelets or hooks to fasten a shoe or garment.

lexunit.name: shoelace.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cord or leather strip passed through eyelets or hooks on opposite sides of a shoe and pulled tight and fastened.

lexunit.name: wire.n
lexunit.definition: COD: metal drawn out into a thin flexible thread or rod.

lexunit.name: screw.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a short, slender, sharp-pointed metal pin with a raised helical thread running around it and a slotted head, used to join things together by being rotated in under pressure.

lexunit.name: link.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something that connects.

lexunit.name: connector.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something that serves to connect items together.

frame.name: Isolated_places
frame.definition: A Place is located far off from centers of population, culture, and/or trade.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The town or area that is in a remote location.
Ex: He lives in the ["Place" BACKWOODS] of Canada.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
A place with respect to which the Place is located.
Ex: I live in BUMBLEFUCK, ["Relative_location" Kansas].

lexunit.definition: COD: rough or isolated country.

lexunit.name: boonies.n

lexunit.name: backwater.n

lexunit.name: backwoods.n

lexunit.name: middle_of_nowhere.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a remote or isolated area

lexunit.name: back_of_beyond.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an isolated area

lexunit.name: Bumblefuck.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a fictitious place name for an isolated town or area

lexunit.name: Podunk.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a small isolated town, area, or place that is considered unimportant.

lexunit.name: godforsaken.a
lexunit.definition: COD: lacking any merit or attraction

lexunit.name: out-of-the-way.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a place) remote

lexunit.name: outback.n

lexunit.name: the_sticks.n

frame.name: Artifact
frame.definition: An Artifact is deliberately made or modified by an intelligent entity to be put to a certain kind of Use. Various properties of the Artifact may be specified, such as its Creator, Time_of_creation, Name, Type, and the Material of which it is composed. The Artifact may or may not be a physical entity.

fe.name: Artifact
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The use for which an artifact is intended.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: An individual or individuals that bring the Artifact into existence.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition: The time at which an Artifact comes into existence.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The term used to refer to an Artifact.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An indication of the subtype of Artifact.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: Any indication of what makes up the Artifact, including components, ingredients, etc.

lexunit.name: wheel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a circular object that revolves on an axle, fixed below a vehicle to enable it to move over the ground or forming part of a machine.

lexunit.name: technology.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an abstract or physical product of human ingenuity focused on solving a problem

lexunit.name: biotechnology.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the results of the exploitation of biological processes for industrial and other purposes, especially the genetic manipulation of micro-organisms for the production of antibiotics, hormones, etc.

lexunit.name: artifact.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an object made by a human being.

frame.name: Import_export
frame.definition: An Agent moves Goods (or some other useful item) from an Exporting_area, across a boundary or border to a different area, the Importing_area. The Path along which the Goods pass may also be indicated. Depending on the lexical unit, the Agent 's point of view may be centered on the Exporting_area at the beginning of the process (e.g. _export_) or on the Importing_area and the end of the process (e.g. _import_) or on the Path (e.g. _transship_). In some sentences, a constituent which encodes the Agent FE also encodes information about the Exporting_area, Path, or Importing_area.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that moves the Goods. Ex: ["Agent" Bath and Bodyworks] IMPORTS all of its soaps from Scotland. Very often, an Exporting_area, Importing_area, or Path will metonymically stand in for the person or persons directly responsible for the movement of the Goods. In such cases the constituent should be labeled Agent on the first layer and with the appropriate locational FE on the second layer. Ex: ["Agent" The U.S.] EXPORTS most of its peanut products.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: An mobile entity directed by the Agent that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The items of value whose location is changing.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent moves the Goods.
Ex: Some department stores IMPORT expensive items ["Purpose" to please their higher-paying customers].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent moves the Goods.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action Ex: Kazakhstan EXPORTED the petroleum, ["Depictive" gleeful].

fe.name: Importing_area
fe.definition: The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.
Ex: The EXPORTATION of goods ["Path" across state lines] is strictly prohibited.

fe.name: Exporting_area
fe.definition: The place where the Goods are initially, before the action.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Goods. Note that Descriptor is not an FE of the same character as other FEs. Specifically, rather than filling a slot, it identifies a modifier of its head noun.

lexunit.name: transship.v

lexunit.name: import.v

lexunit.name: exporter.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person or (metonymically) a place that moves goods to another region.

lexunit.name: importer.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person or (metonymically) a place that moves goods into a region.

lexunit.name: import_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: an imported commodity, article, or service.

lexunit.name: export_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: an exported commodity, article, or service.

lexunit.name: import_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of importing.

lexunit.name: export_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the exporting of goods or services.

lexunit.name: exportation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of moving goods out of an area for purposes of sale.

lexunit.name: importation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of moving goods into an area.

lexunit.name: trans-shipping.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of transferring cargo to move it towards its ultimate destination.
