frame.name: Color
frame.definition: A Color serves as a landmark in color-space, either a point-like landmark (e.g. _burnt sienna_) or a broader region (e.g. _blue_). Especially when the Color designates a broad region in color-space, it may be defined with a specific Type, further specified by comparison to the color of a Comparand, modified by a Color_qualifier, or evaluated with a Descriptor. All color words are generally used to specify the color of some (physical) Entity. Ex: I really like that shade of ["Color" BLUE]. Ex: ["Entity" The welts on his side] had already _turned_ an ["Descriptor" angry] ["Color" RED]. Ex: The room was bathed in a soft ["Color" PINK] ["Entity" light]. Ex: They promptly set up a zillion ["Color_qualifier" bright] ["Color" VERMILION] ["Entity" pavilions]. Ex: ["Entity" His face and hands] _were_ ["Color" BROWN] ["Cause" from a life spent in the bright sun of the fields].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Entity described by the Color. Ex: ["Entity" His jacket] was absolutely GREEN.

fe.name: Color
fe.definition: A position in color-space, generally used to describe the quality of some Entity.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category of a Color is indicated. Ex: It is said that the eyes of the prophet will be of the deepest ["Type" azure] BLUE.

fe.name: Comparand
fe.definition: A physical entity (or type of physical entity) whose color is similar to the designated color. When this FE occurs with adjective targets, (a relatively rare circumstance) the Comparand also serves to specify a Type, which should be labeled on the second FE layer. Ex: Her lips looked ["Comp" sunset] RED in the light of the single lamp. Ex: The ents stared out at us with eyes the deep GREEN ["Comp" of the forest].

fe.name: Color_qualifier
fe.definition: A phrase that indicates the direction in color-space from the center of the region designated by the Color. Ex: Its gill-flaps turn a sort of ["Qual" reddish] ORANGE when it has the disease. Ex: I told him not to use the ["Qual" dark] BROWN, but he didn't listen. Ex: For a moment the whole sky turned ["Qual" bright] PINK.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Some characteristic or judgment of a Color implicitly imposed by a speaker. Ex: Her feathers were dyed a ["Desc" lovely] PURPLE for the occasion.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Color is dependent on. Ex: His face was RED ["Cause" with anger].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The closeness of the Entity 's color to the center of a Color prototype.
Ex: The plums are ["Degr" very] RED, and very ripe.

fe.name: Sub-region
fe.definition: The part of the Entity that has the indicated Color.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The aspect of the Entity which is under discussion, namely color.
Ex: The wine is bright RED ["att" in color] with aromas of red fruits, toasted almond, clove and orange peel.

frame.name: Attack
frame.definition:
An Assailant physically attacks a Victim (which is usually but not always sentient), causing or intending to cause the Victim physical damage. A Weapon used by the Assailant may also be mentioned, in addition to the usual Place, Time, Purpose, Reason, etc. Sometimes a location is used metonymically to stand for the Assailant or the Victim, and in such cases the Place FE will be annotated on a second FE layer.
Ex: ["Time" As soon as he stepped out of the bar] ["Victim" he] was SET ["Victim" upon] ["Assailant" by four men in ski-masks]. Ex: Is ["Asl" he] INVADING ["Victim" Iraq] ["Purp" just to cover other shortcomings]? Ex: ["Time" Then] ["Assailant" Jon-O's forces] AMBUSHED ["Victim" them] ["Place" on the left flank] ["Source" from a line of low hills].

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: This FE is the being or entity that is injured by the Assailant's attack. Ex: The mysterious fighter ATTACKED ["Victim" the guardsmen] with a sabre.

fe.name: Weapon
fe.definition: An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim. Ex: The mysterious fighter ATTACKED the guardsmen ["Weapon" with a sabre].

fe.name: Assailant
fe.definition: The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim. Ex: ["Assailant" The mysterious fighter] ATTACKED the guardsmen with a sabre.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault. Ex: ["Assailant" Japanese] AMBUSHED ["Victim" Americans] ["Means" by bombing Pearl Harbor].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim. Ex: ["Time" Then] ["Assailant" Jon-O's forces] AMBUSHED ["Victim" them] ["Place" on the left flank] ["Source" from a line of low hills].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim. Ex: John ASSAULTED Thibault ["Purpose" to prove his manhood].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Assailant is responding to that leads them to make an assault on the Victim. Ex: ["Assailant" Gloria] ATTACKED ["Victim" Michael] ["Reason" for the cause of Justice].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim. Ex: ["Time" As soon as he stepped out of the bar] ["Victim" he] was SET ["Victim" upon] ["Assailant" by four men in ski-masks].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describeing the state of the Assailant or Victim while the Attack occurs. Ex: They ATTACKED us ["Depictive" in large numbers].

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the attack on the Victim by the Assailant.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Particular iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held. Form: once, twice, Cardinal expression + /it times, /it lots/a lot

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

frame.name: Predicting
frame.definition:
A Speaker states or makes known a future Eventuality on the basis of some Evidence.
Ex: ["Speaker" The Weather Centre] PREDICTED ["Eventuality" that it would be warmer but wet for the weekend]. Ex: ["Speaker" The OECD] FORECAST ["Eventuality" that UK interest rates would be 13 per cent by the end of 1989]. Ex: ["Speaker" Another seer who] FORECAST ["Eventuality" a Tory majority] -- without compromising his impartiality -- was Sir Robin Day . Ex: ["Eventuality" The European market] is FORECAST ["Eventuality" to grow 18.1% by the end of next fiscal year].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The Speaker makes a prediction.
Ex: The institute FORECAST an increase in leisure spending of 15 per cent.

fe.name: Eventuality
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate an event or state that is predicted to occur or hold at a future time. A single Eventuality may be expressed discontinuously in a raising construction. This FE is also used for expressions that denote entities with variable attributes about which the Speaker makes predictions.
Ex: PREDICTING ["Eventuality" the weather] is risky business. Ex: PREDICTING ["Eventuality" the numbers of disabled elderly] into the future is problematic as it depends upon the projection forward of current patterns of disability . Ex: WangFORECASTS ["Eventuality" a 9 per cent increase in state revenue] Ex: ["Eventuality" The European market] is FORECAST ["Eventuality" to grow 18.1%].

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that denote a set of facts on the basis of which the Speaker makes the prediction.
Ex: Violence was PREDICTED ["Evidence" on the basis of disorder at demonstrations in Paris].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the prediction is made.
Ex: John PREDICTED ["Time" last year] that he would be finished by October.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place where the Speaker makes the prediction.
Ex: Greenman PREDICTED ["Place" at a small dinner party] that the market would rise again.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner marks any description of the Speaker's prediction making that is not covered by more specific FEs.
Ex: Smeagol ["Mnr" confidently] PREDICTED that he would win the race. Ex: One commentator ["Manner" rashly] PREDICTED that the fad for adaptions wouldn't last much longer
Note that this FE does not cover modifiers such as 'correctly' or 'accurately'.

fe.name: Time_of_Eventuality
fe.definition:
This frame element marks expressions that indicate forwhat future time an Eventuality is predicted.
Ex: Cocoa stocks reached a record 1.2m tonnes and a seventh year of surplus is FORECAST ["Time_of_Eventuality" for the year to September 1991].

fe.name: Accuracy
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Accuracy of the prediction. Ex: Compary president Randall Johnson PREDICTED ["Accuracy" correctly] that a major reworking of infrastructure would be necessary. Ex: It is hard to FORECAST ["Accuracy" with a high degree of certainty] what the weather will be like past two or three days.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describes a characteristic of the Eventuality.

frame.name: Weapon
frame.definition: A Weapon is an artifact created specifically to cause harm or damage. In some cases, a Use, Material of construction, Part or Type may be more narrowly specified. Ex: Did you, or did you not, ["Gov" fire] ["X" this ["Weapon" GUN]] with intent to harm my client? Ex: Cyra tried to ["Gov" swing] ["X" ["Wld" her] ["Weapon" SWORD]] to parry, but it was to heavy. Ex: I investigated a specialist ["X" ["Mat" precious metal] ["Weapon" FIREARMS]] ["Gov" manufacturer]. Ex: My neighbor, a member of the NRA since birth, has got an ["Type" AK-47] ["Type" fully automatic] ["Use" assault] ["Weapon" RIFLE]. Ex: Let 's just say that he 's the kind of guy who likes ["Wep" GUNS] ["Part" with hair triggers].

fe.name: Weapon
fe.definition: An entity prototypically used by a Wielder to cause damage. Ex: They used to shoot these long-range ["Wep" RIFLES] with scopes and hit targets a mile away.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The type of activity that the Weapon is generally involved in. Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also. Ex: a ["Use" dueling] PISTOL Ex: ["Use" anti-personnell] MINES Ex: ["Use" deer] RIFLE

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Weapon belongs to. Ex: Most people don't keep ["Typ" bastard] SWORDS in their livingrooms.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: The substance that makes up the Weapon.

fe.name: Wielder
fe.definition: The person (or other sentient entity) that is using the Weapon. Ex: Reluctantly, he slid ["Wld" his] GUNS back into their holsters.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: This FE identifies a part of the Weapon. This includes permanent, obligatory parts and mere attachments. Ex: I bought a RIFLE ["Part" with a 2000-yard scope]. Ex: They practiced on SWORDS ["Part" with wooden blades] first.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The term used to refer to an Weapon.
Ex: The SWORD ["nam" Wirikidor] was inadvertently cursed.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which a Weapon comes into existence.
Ex: The ["tim" fourth millennium BC] SPEAR has stimulated a lot of controversy.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Weapon.
Ex: ["cre" Colt] PISTOLS are, for some reason, considerably more likely to be missold in this fashion.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A description or characteristic of the Weapon.
Ex: He prefers to use a ["Descriptor" heavy] BOW for long-distance combat.

frame.name: Sign
frame.definition: A phenomenon, the Indicator, exists as an indication of another phenomenon, the Indicated. The relationship is asymmetric: the Indicated is not necessarily a sign for the existence or presence of an Indicator. The Indicated can be a past, present, or future entity or eventuality. The relationship between Indicator and Indicated is not one of symbolization or iconicity. Rather the Indicator is an index of the Indicated.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Degree to which the Indicator is a sign of the Indicated.

lexunit.name: sign.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an object, quality, or event whose presence or occurrence indicates the probable presence, occurrence, or advent of something else

lexunit.name: indication.n

frame.name: Vehicle
frame.definition: The frame concerns the vehicles that human beings use for the purpose of transportation.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Vehicle. Ex: Kim drove a ["Desc" used] CAR.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: Vehicle is the transportation device that the human beings use to travel. Ex: To get to the island, you need to take a ["Vehicle" FERRY].

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition: This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Vehicle. Ex: ["Poss" His] CAR crashed into a tree.

fe.name: Itinerary
fe.definition: The frame element tells about the time and route of the service of the transportation device. Ex: You must take the ["Itinerary" midnight] TRAIN to get there by tomorrow noon.

fe.name: Means_of_propulsion
fe.definition: The Means_of_propulsion designates how the vehicle is moved. Ex: They rode in a ["Means_of_propulsion" horse-drawn] CARRIAGE.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The task which the Vehicle is put to. Normally, this includes the transportation of some kind.

frame.name: Domain
frame.definition:
A Predicate is said to apply in a particular Domain. The understanding of the relation between Domain and Predicate depends on the nature of the Predicate. When the Predicate is a complete proposition, then a Domain adverbial also functions as a topic restrictor. Sentences with topic restrictors often come in pairs. When the Predicate is a simple predicate, there is no notion of topic restriction on the sentence level.
Ex: The Normal College is ["Domain" GEOGRAPHICALLY] ["Predicate" adjacent to the University of North Wales]. Ex: ["Domain" GEOGRAPHICALLY], ["Predicate" Britain is a group of island off the mainland of Europe]. ["Domain" CULTURALLY] , ["Predicate" it has always been linked to the continent] . Ex: ["Domain" SOCIALLY] and demographically ["Predicate" the period has been dominated by two factors -- the fall in the size of families and the increase in the expectation of survival to retirement , the effects of which are still far from having exhausted themselves ].

fe.name: Predicate
fe.definition:
This Frame Element denotes the Predicate which is applied to the Domain.
Ex: This policy is not ECONOMICALLY ["Predicate" sound].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
This Frame Element applies to the Domain in which the Predicate is said to apply.
Ex: Britain and France are close , not only ["Domain" GEOGRAPHICALLY] , but also strategically .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

frame.name: Offenses
frame.definition: Words in this frame describe acts in violation of a legal code.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE broadly picks out the degree of offense. Ex: She faces conviction on three counts of ["Degree" first-degree] ["Off" MURDER]. Ex: ["Degree" Aggravated]["Off" ASSAULT] is usually considered a felony.

fe.name: Specification
fe.definition: The Specification is an additional aspect of the main crime being commited. Ex: He was charged with ["Off" ASSAULT] ["Spec" causing actual bodily harm]. Ex: The prosecutors decided to go with ["Off" ARSON] ["Spec" with intent to harm].

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition: The illegal act. Ex: He was charged with ["Off" ASSAULT].

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: This FE denotes the person or entity that is badly affected by the Offense. Ex: The police is investigating the HOMICIDE _of Dr. Johnson_.

fe.name: Punishment
fe.definition: This FE denotes the Punishment that is specified by the statute in which the offense is defined. Ex: Suicide is a ["Offense" felony] ["Punishment" punishable by four years in prison].

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: The individual who commits the Offense

frame.name: Bearing_arms
frame.definition:
A Protagonist has (or does not have) a Weapon. The Degree to which the Protagonist is armed may also be described. The Protagonist is normally a human but may be a device that has subsidiary weapons. Ex: Apparently, ["Protagonist" the suspect] _is_ ARMED ["Weapon" with a shotgun]. Ex: After she pulled the .45 from her sock drawer, ["Protagonist" she] _felt_ ["Degree" well enough] ARMED ["Degree" to face anyone coming in]. Ex: ["Protagonist" The Tomahawk missile] PACKS a lot of heat .
Ex: ["Protagonist" An individual with a right-to-carry license] may continue to CARRY in a "school zone" in compliance with existing state and local laws. ["Weapon" INI]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The amount of Weapons that the Protagonist has (relative to some standard). Ex: He is very ["Degree" well] ARMED.

fe.name: Weapon
fe.definition: The destructive device that the Protagonist has with them.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The individual that possesses a Weapon.

lexunit.name: armed.a

lexunit.name: unarmed.a

frame.name: Hindering
frame.definition:
In this frame a Hindrance makes it more difficult for a Protagonist to complete their intended Action or a Hindrance directly affects an Action where the Action can be a natural act or the actions of many individuals in a collective endeavor. Crucially, these lexical units do not entail that the Protagonist was unable to complete the Action or that the Action did not occur. The Hindrance may indicate a lack of enablement or an obstacle on the natural progression of the Protagonist or Action
Ex: ["Protagonist" Malcolm] was HINDERED ["Hindrance" by his drinking problem] . Ex: ["Hindrance" A lack of money] HAMPERED ["Action" our plans] . Ex: ["Action" Many candidates' progress] is ["Degree" severely] IMPEDED ["Hindrance" because they have to resit for the exam]. Ex: ["Hindrance" The new dam] IMPEDED ["Action" the flow of water] .

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist is the entity that tends towards or plans some Action which the Hindrance causes to be more difficult.

fe.name: Hindrance
fe.definition: The Hindrance is the force which makes the Action more difficult or less likely to be successfully completed. The Hindrance may be a lack of enabling force: Ex: ["Action" The project] was HAMPERED ["Hindrance" by a lack of funds]. or the Hindrance may be an obstacle in the natural progression of the Protagonist or Action. Ex: ["Protagonist" Burns] was HINDERED ["Hindrance" by Smither's violent attack].

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action is what the Protagonist desires to do, which is made more difficult by the Hindrance. It can also be a natural act or collective endeavor, not linked to an overt Protagonist.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Hindrance affects the Protagonist or Action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location where he Hindrance affects the Protagonist or Action.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the extent to which the Hindrance affects the Protagonist or Action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE describes the means by which hindering occurs

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE label is used for the cause of the HINDRANCE

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which hindering occurs

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time over which the hindering takes place.
Ex: The exporting of goods from the United States was IMPEDED ["dur" for several months] while negotiations continued.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause. In other words, given only the facts of the *Concessive, one would expect them to cause the world to be the opposite of what is protrayed in the main clause.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

frame.name: Similarity
frame.definition:
Two or more distinct entities, which may be concrete or abstract objects or types, are characterized as being similar to each other. Depending on figure/ground relations, the entities may be expressed in two distinct frame elements and constituents , Entity_1 and Entity_2, or jointly as a single frame element and constituent, Entities. The similarity may be based on appearance, physical properties, or other characteristics of the two entities. However, no such Dimension has to be specified explicitly. The Entities may be like each other to a greater or lesser Degree. Rather than specifying the Dimension of difference, a Differentiating_fact may be mentioned. Ex: Notice that, although similarity presupposes the notion of a judge who assesses similarity, that judge is not part of the frame of similarity.
Ex: ["Entity_1" A mulberry] _is_ ["Degree" very] SIMILAR ["Dimension" in shape] ["Entity_2" to a loganberry] Ex: ["Entity_1" Recovering it afterwards] can also _be_ SIMILAR ["Entity_2" to collecting an unsecured loan] Ex: ["Entities" Great Britain and Germany] _were_ only ALIKE ["Dimension" in one respect]. Ex: ["Entity_1" Lothlorien] _is_ ["Degree" quite] LIKE ["Entity_2" most of their other war games] really.

fe.name: Entities
fe.definition:
This FE marks constituents that express the set of objects or types whose similarity is at issue.
Ex: ["Entities" The two painters] _were_ ALIKE in being unable to draw acceptably . Ex: Agbenugba confirms the RESEMBLANCES ["Entities" between his own experience and that of his protagonist].

fe.name: Entity_1
fe.definition:
When there is an asymmetry, Entity_1 is the entity characterized by its similarity to Entity_2, whose characteristics are assumed to be known. Entity_1 is often an external argument.
Ex: In the first phase ["Entity_1" Barthes's approach] _has_ SIMILARITIES to that of Levi-Strauss. Ex: ["Entity_1" Our economy] _is_ LIKE a healthy plant after a long drought Ex: I found a SIMILAR ["ent1" passage] in Tolkien.

fe.name: Entity_2
fe.definition:
When the Entities are expressed separately, Entity_2 is the one whose characteristics are assumed to be known; it serves as a basis for establishing characteristics of Entity_1.
Ex: The results of Method 2 _show _remarkable SIMILARITY ["Entity_2" to those obtained by Method 1] Ex: Leadbelly's recordings are not DISSIMILAR ["Entity_2" to those of Jimmie Rodgers]. Ex: This is a problem DIFFERENT ["ent2" from meltdown] only in degree. Ex: Here we see a SIMILAR case. ["ent2" DNI]

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition:
This FE marks constituents which express a property in respect to which the similarity of the entities is assessed.
Ex: The disc announced Friday is ["Dimension" physically] SIMILAR to current music CDs

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which entities are similar to each other, in general or with respect to some Dimension(s)
Ex: The twins are ["Degree" very] SIMILAR.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the similarity occurs or exists.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the general area in which similarity occurs or exists

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which Dimension is similar or different

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An inanimate entity or process that causes the similarity.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Entities

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Differentiating_fact
fe.definition:
A fact about Entity_1 or the Entities that reveals how Entity_1 is the same or different from other entities. (Note the contrast with 'as to'.)
Ex: His presidency was DIFFERENT ["Differentiating_fact" in that it offered a way forward for the common man] . Ex: Banks primarily DIFFER ["Differentiating_fact" in offering different rates for different risks] . Ex: We are all SIMILAR ["Differentiating_fact" in having two arms , two legs , a mind , and a heart to feel with] .

frame.name: Abusing
frame.definition: In this frame an Abuser repeatedly treats the Victim in a cruel and violent way, including physically harming or forcing the Victim to engage in sexual activity against their will. The Victim usually lacks the power to resist or fight back. A Type of abuse may be indicated. There may also be a Degree. Ex: ["Abuser" Her father] ["Type" verbally] ABUSED ["Victim" her mother].

fe.name: Abuser
fe.definition: The Abuser subjects the Victim to repeated verbal, physical, emotional or sexual attacks. Ex: ["Abuser" Fred] ABUSED Martha by locking her into a closet .

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: The Victim is the recipient of the Abuser's actions. Ex: Fred ABUSED ["Victim" Martha] by locking her into a closet .

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type is used for the domain in which the Abuser mistreats the Victim. Ex: Fred is known for his ["Type" emotional] ABUSE of women.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree is the extent to which the abuse occurs.
Ex: ["Abuser" Fred] ABUSED Martha ["Degree" alot].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the abuse occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the abuse occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner is used for any description of the abuse event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Abuser that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: It is fair to say that it was ["Man" malicious] ABUSE.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which the Abuser accomplishes the abuse.
Ex: Fred ABUSED Martha ["Means" by locking her into a closet].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity used by the Abuser to accomplish the abuse.
Ex: Look, being BATTERED ["Instrument" with a mallet] is no one's idea of a good time.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Abuser intends to accomplish by performing the abuse.
Ex: They are ABUSIVE ["Purp" in order to get back at those who abused them].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Abuser abuses others. Ex: They ABUSE ["Rsn" because they were themselves abused].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The amount of time that abuse occurs.
Ex: She had been BATTERED ["Dur" for years] before she even knew there was anything serious wrong.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
How often abuse occurs.
Ex: She had been abused ["Freq" too much] as a child ["Freq" to let it happen again].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Circumstnaces
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the Abusing event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

lexunit.name: abuse.n
lexunit.definition: COD: cruel and violent treatment

lexunit.name: abuse.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to cruelly mistreat, esp. physically or sexually

lexunit.name: abusive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: characterized by repeated mistreatment.

lexunit.name: batter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: subject (one's spouse, partner, or child) to repeated violence and assault

lexunit.name: domestic violence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: violence that occurs inside a family

lexunit.name: maltreat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: treat cruelly or with violence.

lexunit.name: maltreatment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: cruel, improper actions taken upon someone.

frame.name: Reporting
frame.definition: In this frame an Informer informs the Authorities of the illegal or otherwise improper Behavior of the Wrongdoer. Ex: ["Informer" Tony] REPORTED ["Wrongdoer" Michael] ["Authorities" to the police] ["Behavior" for breaking into his car] . Ex: ["Informer" The teacher] REPORTED ["Behavior" the bathroom vandalism] .

fe.name: Informer
fe.definition: The Informer reports the activities of the Wrongdoer to the Authorities.

fe.name: Wrongdoer
fe.definition: The Wrongdoer has his or her activities reported to the Authorities.

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition: The Authorities are the officials, government or otherwise, who handle misbehavior.

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior is the action or actions for which the Wrongdoer is reported.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Informer reports the Behavior of the Wrongdoer.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location where the reporting occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose is the purpose for which the Informer reports the Wrongdoer.

lexunit.name: report.v
lexunit.definition: FN: inform the authorities of the wrongful actions of someone

lexunit.name: finger.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on to the police.

lexunit.name: rat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on someone.

lexunit.name: inform.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give incriminating information about (someone) to the police or other authority.

lexunit.name: tell.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on.

lexunit.name: rat out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on

lexunit.name: squeal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on someone.

lexunit.name: snitch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on someone.

lexunit.name: peach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on.

lexunit.name: fink.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an informer.

lexunit.name: informer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who informs on another person to the police or other authority.

lexunit.name: snitch.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an informer.

lexunit.name: nark.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a police informer.

lexunit.name: fink.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform on.

frame.name: Hit_target
frame.definition:
An Agent causes the ballistic motion of a projectile and its subsequent impact on a Target.
Ex: It looks like ["Agent" he] HIT ["Target" the bull's-eye] ["ins" with his first arrow]!
Ex: If ["Agent" he] SHOT ["Target" her], he is fully culpable whether he meant to or not.

fe.name: Target
fe.definition: The entity which is hit by a Projectile directed by the Agent.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that directs the Projectile such that it impacts the Target.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about by hitting the Target

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Agent hits the Target.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the event happens.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The part of the Target hit by the Agent.
Ex: He SHOT me ["Subregion" in the arm]!

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action performed by the Agent that accomplishes hitting the Target.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The entity, most often ammunition or a firearm, which the Agent manipulates to hit the Target.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

lexunit.name: shoot.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to fire a gun such that another object is impacted by a bullet.

lexunit.name: hit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: strike (a target).

lexunit.name: pick off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: shoot

frame.name: Conduct
frame.definition:
An Agent acts in a certain Manner either generally or under some particular Circumstances. The conduct may also be directed specifically towards an Affected_Party.
Ex: ["Agent" He] pledges to CONDUCT himself ["Manner" with honesty and humility]. Ex: This year ["Agent" they] have BEHAVED themselves ["Manner" particularly impudently]. Ex: His appearance was as immaculate as ever and ["Agent" his] BEARING ["Manner" composed and dignified].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that denote the person whose conduct is being evaluated.
Ex: ["Agent" Douglas Hurd] CARRIED HIMSELF well

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that characterize the way that the Agent behaves.
Ex: They stood together and posed for the pass, Alleyne relaxed and smiling , a tall , angular man who CARRIED HIMSELF ["Manner" with natural elegance] .

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of Circumstances under which the Agent acts in a particular way.
Ex: But Garvey did not care what Gabriel believed , so long as he CONDUCTED himself ["Circumstances" on stage] like the Angel Gabriel .

fe.name: Affected_Party
fe.definition:
A person to whom behavior is directed by the Agent.
Ex: ["Agent" Smithers] BEHAVED himself ["Manner" shamefully] ["Affected_Party" towards me].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate why an Agent behaved in a certain way.
Ex: People BEHAVE in the way they do ["Reason" because of their past learning experiences]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Agent behaves in a certain way.
Ex: She knew that she had BEHAVED badly ["tim" last night]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the Agent exhibits their behavior.
Ex: Sometimes an offender may be placed at a Probation hostel because they have committed a serious offence or have BEHAVED badly ["pla" at an independent hostel]

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The Domain of human behavior in which the Agent acts in a certain Manner

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the (usually 'good' or 'bad') conduct of the Agent deviates from some standard or norm

fe.name: Standard
fe.definition: An explicit point to which the conduct of the Agent is compared

lexunit.name: conduct.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the manner in which a person behaves

lexunit.name: deportment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's behaviour or manners

lexunit.name: behavior.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the way in which someone behaves

lexunit.name: comportment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: behaviour or bearing

lexunit.name: misbehave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: behave badly

lexunit.name: misbehavior.n
lexunit.definition: FN: bad behavior

lexunit.name: behave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: act or conduct oneself in a specified way

lexunit.name: act.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to behave in a certain way.

lexunit.name: act up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to behave badly.

lexunit.name: bearing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's way of standing, moving, or behaving.

lexunit.name: conduct.v
lexunit.definition: COD: the manner in which a person behaves.

lexunit.name: carry oneself.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stand and move in a specified way.

lexunit.name: demeanor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: outward behaviour or bearing.

lexunit.name: manner.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's outward bearing or way of behaving towards others.

frame.name: Criminal_investigation
frame.definition:
This frame describes the process that involves the determination by an authority, the Investigator, of the circumstances surrounding an Incident by means of inquiry.
Ex: ["Investigator" The police] are INVESTIGATING ["Inc" the bank's reported loss of several thousand dollars from their downtown branch's top security vault]. Ex: ["Investigator" Authorites] are INVESTIGATING ["Inc" several murders].

fe.name: Investigator
fe.definition: The Investigator is the person or agency that investigates a person of a crime.

fe.name: Incident
fe.definition: The Investigator attempts to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the Incident, which is typically a criminal act (murder, robbery) or the result of such an act (death, loss of money).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Investigator investigates the Incident. Ex: Our guys are ["Time" currently] INVESTIGATING her disappearance.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of the investigation. Ex: The police carried out a ["Dur" two-year] INVESTIGATION into terrorist kidnappings.

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition: This FE denotes the Suspect that is investigated by the Investigator. Ex: ["Investigator" The police] are INVESTIGATING ["Suspect" Dr. Phil].

lexunit.name: inquiry.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official investigation.

lexunit.name: probe.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an investigation.

lexunit.name: investigate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry out a systematic or formal inquiry into (an incident, person or allegation) so as to establish the truth of a criminal event.

lexunit.name: inquire.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to ask questions and gather evidence about a possible crime "The police began to inquire into the circumstances of his death."

lexunit.name: probe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: enquire into closely.

lexunit.name: investigation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a systematic search or inquiry into an incident

lexunit.name: lead.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a clue to be followed in the resolution of a problem.

lexunit.name: clue.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a fact or piece of evidence serving to reveal a hidden truth or solve a problem.

lexunit.name: under investigation.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: be the subject of a (criminal) investigation.

frame.name: Legality
frame.definition:
Words in this frame describe the status of an Action with respect to a Code of laws or rules. An Object may also be in violation or compliance of the Code by virtue of its existence, location or possession.
Ex: ILLEGAL ["Action" drug use] is on the rise.
Ex: Scores of ILLEGAL ["Object" immigrants] cross the border every year.
Ex: ["Action" Feeding the buffalo] _is_ PROHIBITED ["Code" according to Code 138] .

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action is the behavior which complies with or violates the Code.Ex: ILLEGAL ["Action" drug use] is on the rise.

fe.name: Code
fe.definition: The Code is the set of rules, laws or regulations that determine whether the Action is allowed or prohibited.

fe.name: Object
fe.definition: The Object complies with or violates the Code by virtue of its existence, location or possession.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

lexunit.name: illegal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: contrary to or forbidden by law.

lexunit.name: legal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: permitted by law.

lexunit.name: lawful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: conforming to, permitted by, or recognized by law or rules.

lexunit.name: unlawful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not conforming to or permitted by the law or rules.

lexunit.name: wrongful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an act) not fair, just, or legal.

lexunit.name: illicit.a
lexunit.definition: COD: forbidden by law, rules, or custom.

lexunit.name: licit.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not forbidden; lawful.

lexunit.name: permissible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: allowable; permitted.

lexunit.name: wrongly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: in a manner characterized by an abuse of power.

lexunit.name: wrong.a
lexunit.definition: FN: in violation of the law (due to abuse of power)

lexunit.name: prohibited.a
lexunit.definition: FN: forbidden by law

lexunit.name: legitimate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: conforming to the law or to rules.

lexunit.name: fair.a
lexunit.definition: FN: legal (esp. in the domain of sports)

frame.name: Surrendering
frame.definition: In this frame a Fugitive presents himself or herself to the Authorities to be subject to the criminal process. Ex: ["Fugitive" The bank robber] SURRENDERED ["Authorities" to Berkeley police]. Ex: ["Fugitive" Norte] is expected to SURRENDER ["Authorities" to police] ["Time" tomorrow] ["Charges" on tax fraud charges] .

fe.name: Fugitive
fe.definition: The Fugitive is wanted by the Authorities and turns himself or herself in to the Authorities.

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition: The Authorities are the officials, government or otherwise, who are in charge of initiating the criminal process.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location where the surrendering occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Fugitive surrenders.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: The Charges is the offense for which the Fugitive is wanted.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Fugitive surrenders to the Authorities.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE denotes a proposition from which the surrendering event logically follows.

lexunit.name: surrender.v
lexunit.definition: FN: turn oneself into the authorities

lexunit.name: turn in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to surrender oneself to the authorities

lexunit.name: give up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: turn oneself in to the authorities

lexunit.name: surrender.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the event of surrendering

frame.name: Suspicion
frame.definition:
A person or group, the Authority, believes that another person, the Suspect is a participant in a criminal Incident.
Ex: ["Authority" The police] SUSPECT ["Suspect" Noah Rogers] ["Incident" of aiding the robbery last night at Shop-n-drive].

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition: The Authority is the group or person who suspects the Suspect of criminal activity.

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition: The Suspect is the target of the Authority's suspicion.

fe.name: Incident
fe.definition: The (typically criminal) Incident in which the Suspect is suspected of being involved.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the suspecting takes place. Ex: Jakobson was placed UNDER SUSPICION ["Time" last week] . Ex: ["Time" At that time], the police SUSPECTED no one.

lexunit.name: suspect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: believe (someone) to be guilty of a crime or offence, without certain proof.

lexunit.name: under suspicion.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: be (of a person) suspected of involvement in a crime.

lexunit.name: suspicion.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: the state of being suspected

lexunit.name: suspect.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person suspected of a crime or offence.

frame.name: Appeal
frame.definition: In the Appeal stage of the criminal process the Convict or his or her Representative applies to a higher Court to reverse the Decision of the lower court on certain Grounds. Ex: ["Representative" The defense] plans to APPEAL ["Decision" the court's decision] ["Grounds" on the grounds that the judge violated Code 81.b] . Ex: ["Convict" John Michaels] will APPEAL ["Decision" his conviction] .

fe.name: Convict
fe.definition: The Convict is the individual convicted of the crime who may make an appeal on her or his behalf.

fe.name: Representative
fe.definition: The Representative applies to a higher court on behalf of the Convict.

fe.name: Decision
fe.definition: The Decision is the ruling handed down by the first court.

fe.name: Grounds
fe.definition: The Grounds is the legal basis on which the appeal rests.

fe.name: Court
fe.definition: The Court is the judicial establishment to which the Convict appeals.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which a Convict or Representative appeals.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

lexunit.name: appeal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an application to a higher court for a decision to be reversed.

lexunit.name: appeal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: apply to a higher court for a reversal of the decision of a lower court.

lexunit.name: appellate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a court) dealing with appeals.

lexunit.name: appellant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who appeals against a court ruling.

lexunit.name: plead.v
lexunit.definition: FN: present (a case) on appeal.

frame.name: Want_suspect
frame.definition: A Suspect has been investigated and has a warrant issued for his or her arrest on certain Charges. Ex: ["Suspect" Bill] _is_ WANTED ["Charges" on murder charges].

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition: The Suspect is suspected of having committed a crime by the authorities who want the Suspect to enter the criminal process.

fe.name: Charges
fe.definition: The Charges are the offenses the Suspect will be accused of committing.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: wanted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: hunted or seeked by the police for a crime.

frame.name: Grant_permission
frame.definition:
In this frame a Grantor (either a person or an institution) grants permission for a Grantee to perform an Action or for an Action to occur. This frame does not include situations where there is a state of permission granted by authority or rule of law. The permission for the Action may be limited to certain Circumstances.
Ex: ["Grantor" My mother] LET ["Grantee" me] ["Action" go to the movies with Simon] .
Ex: ["Grantor" The teacher] _gave_ ["Grantee" the children] PERMISSION ["Action" to eat their lunch outside].
Ex: ["Grantor" The Church] had SANCTIONED ["Action" for recital after Mass] ["Action" a special prayer to St. Michael].

fe.name: Grantor
fe.definition: The Grantor is the individual or group of individuals vested with the authority to grant permission with respect to a specific domain and who grant permission to the Grantee.

fe.name: Grantee
fe.definition: The Grantee is the individual who is given permission to engage in a certain Action.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action is the activitiy of the Grantee that the Grantor permits.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the conditions under which an Action is permissible, according to the Grantor.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Grantor gives permission.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the Grantor gives permission.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose is the goal of the Grantor in granting permission.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the cognitive cause of the Grantor's granting of permission.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the allowing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Grantor that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Allowed_category
fe.definition:
A category that the Action fits into, which dictates the Action's being permitted (in accord with some implicit Principle.)
Ex: The transfer was SANCTIONED ["all" as a "necessary precaution"].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action of the Grantor whereby they communicate or enact the granting.
Ex:

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Grant_permission event occurs.

lexunit.name: permit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give permission to (someone) or for (something).

lexunit.name: allow.v
lexunit.definition: COD: permit to do something.

lexunit.name: let.v
lexunit.definition: COD: not prevent or forbid; allow.

lexunit.name: permission.n
lexunit.definition: COD: authorization

lexunit.name: leave.n
lexunit.definition: COD: permission

lexunit.name: suffer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: allow (someone) to do something.

lexunit.name: the go-ahead.n
lexunit.definition: FN: permission

lexunit.name: the okay.n
lexunit.definition: FN: permission

lexunit.name: the green light.n
lexunit.definition: FN: permission

lexunit.name: sanction.v
lexunit.definition: FN: give permission

lexunit.name: okay.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give approval to

lexunit.name: greenlight.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give permission to go ahead with.

lexunit.name: approve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: officially accept as satisfactory.

lexunit.name: approval.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of approving of something.

lexunit.name: mandate.n
lexunit.definition: FN: authorization to carry out a policy, usually granted by an organization or by the electorate in an election, e.g. a U.N. mandate, re-election with a mandate to improve public schools.

lexunit.name: restrict.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deprive of freedom of movement or action.

lexunit.name: clear.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to allow by deeming fit

lexunit.name: authorize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: grant clearance for something to occur

lexunit.name: accept.v
lexunit.definition: FN: allow

frame.name: Court_examination
frame.definition: A Questioner asks a Witness (or defendant) questions in the context of a court procedure. Ex: ["Questioner" We] 'd like to CROSS-EXAMINE ["Witness" the witness] if we can.

fe.name: Questioner
fe.definition: The individual that asks a Witness questions.

fe.name: Witness
fe.definition: A person who is present in a courtroom in order to give some form of evidence, has been sworn in, and is being examined by a Questioner. Ex: You have leave to EXAMINE ["Wit" the witness.]

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The subject matter to which the examination pertains.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the examination occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the examination takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which the questioner examines the witness. Ex: The defense attorneys CROSS-EXAMINED the prosecution's witnesses ["Manner" harshly].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose of the examination. Ex: The defense EXAMINED their own client ["Purpose" in order to show the jury her compassionate side].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which the Questioner examines the Witness. Ex: Many attorneys CROSS-EXAMINE witnesses ["Means" by asking misleading and often confrontational questions].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: How long the examination takes place. Ex: The gruelling ["Dur" two-hour] CROSS-EXAMINATION revealed much new information regarding the murder.

lexunit.name: examine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally question (a defendant or witness) in court.

lexunit.name: cross-examine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: question (a witness called by the other party) in a court of law to check or extend testimony already given

lexunit.name: cross.n
lexunit.definition: FN: short for cross-examination.

lexunit.name: cross-examination.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an event in court procedure in which a witness is questioned to further examine statements that they made when they were questioned by the other party.

lexunit.name: examination.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the formal questioning of a defendant or witness in court.

frame.name: Justifying
frame.definition: An Agent has done or omitted to do an Act or is responsible for the obtaining of a State_of_affairs, which a Judge deems to constitute a violation of an obligation or a moral guideline. The Agent gives a Reason why the Act or omission or State_of_affairs was licit despite appearances.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The person or organization that is held responsible for a prior Act or for a State_of_affairs.
Ex: ["Agent" Smithers] DEFENDED his decision by insisting that he had used his best judgment

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The set of facts or circumstances that the Agent offers in explanation of their earlierAct or of the State_of_affairs
Ex: Mr De Klerk JUSTIFIED his decision ["Reason" on the curious grounds that an inquiry would take too long]

fe.name: Act
fe.definition:
An action for which the Agent is held responsible, frequently one that the Agent has taken themself.
Ex: Kim failed to fully JUSTIFY ["Act" his decision].

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
A State_of_affairs that the Agent is held responsible for.
Ex: The lawyers tried to JUSTIFY ["State_of_affairs" enormous punitive damages being paid to victims on a first-past-the-post system] .

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition:
The person or institution that holds the Agent responsible for an Act or State_of_affairs.
Ex: Any decision that preparation and presentation should be separate would have to be JUSTIFIED ["Judge" to the public] and be open in the last resort to judicial review

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action, typically an act of speaking, which the Agent performs in order to justify an Act or State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE denotes the number of times the Act or State_of_affairs are justified.

lexunit.name: justify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prove to be right or reasonable

lexunit.name: justification.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of proving something to be right or reasonable

lexunit.name: defend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: attempt to justify

lexunit.name: defence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: attempted justification or vindication

lexunit.name: account.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a satisfactory record or explanation of.

lexunit.name: explain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: excuse or justify one's motives or conduct

lexunit.name: rationalize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: attempt to justify (an action or attitude) with logical reasoning

frame.name: Purpose
frame.definition:
An Agent wants to achieve a Goal, or an object, a Means , has been created or is used to allow the creator or a user to achieve a Goal. The Goal is an state of the world that does not currently obtain but which the Agent wants to realize and is planning and/or working towards. In some cases, it is difficult to decide whether a noun phrase metonymically stands for the Agent or the Means (e.g. The goal [of this paper/seminar/project] is to determine ...). We mark these phrases as Agent on the first layer but also annotate them as Means on a second annotation layer.
In some cases a Restrictor on the Goal state of affairs can be given prominence as a separate constituent. Talk about Goals frequently includes the mention of a Domain to which the Agent's Goal is relevant.
Ex: The modest ["Agent" American] GOAL ["Goal" of a threefold increase in capacity] recognises this fact . Ex: The OBJECT ["Means" of the tutorial] _is_ ["Goal" to help a student concentrate on his writing skills] Ex: The prime GOAL ["Means" of the programme] _was_ ["Goal" to help develop processes of scientific thinking in children] . Ex: ["Agent" My] GOAL ["Means" in this book] _is_ ["Goal" to introduce the reader to Web programming applications]. Ex: ["Agent" The president's] ["Domain" economic] GOAL ["Restrictor" for the country ]_was_ ["Goal" to overcome the recession].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The volitional actor who intends to achieve a goal. Ex: ["Agent" Microsoft 's] GOAL of delivering a million copies in the first year is trifling compared to the 25 million copies of Windows it has shipped since May 1990.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The action or state of affairs that the Agent wants to achieve.
Ex: The company missed its GOAL ["Goal" of getting a thousand third-party software packages shipped].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
A Means is an object that is used or designed to achieve a particular Goal.
Ex: The GOAL ["Means" of treatment] _was_ ["Goal" to lower diastolic blood pressure below 85 mm Hg] .

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
This frame element expresses a sphere of activity within which an Agent has a Goal.
Ex: His ["Domain" political] GOAL is the restoration of the monarchy

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This Frame Element expresses a time period during which an Agent had a particular Goal.
Ex: But the main GOAL ["Time" of the 1990s] could be to transform a big , heavily armed standing army into a more flexible force

fe.name: Restrictor
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a spatial or temporal or individual framework relative to which the Goal is said to hold. More than one Restrictor can be mentioned.
Ex: Our GOAL ["Restrictor" for Japan] ["Restrictor" for next year]is to sell 2000 units Ex: Our sales TARGET ["Restrictor" for that week] was 200 units

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate an Attribute for which it is the Agent's goal that it have or reach a particular Value .
Ex: We exceeded our ["Attribute" production] TARGET of 2000 units

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate which Value the Agent wants the Attribute to reach.
Ex: GM has a production TARGET ["Value" of 2,000,000 units]

lexunit.name: in_order.adv

lexunit.name: bent.a

lexunit.name: intent.a

lexunit.name: mean.v

frame.name: Reason
frame.definition:
A volitional Agent is responding to a State_of_Affairs by performing some Action.
Ex: And _was_ ["State_of_Affairs" that] ["Agent" your] REASON ["Action" for becoming an actor] ? Ex: But ["State_of_Affairs" Giles] _is_ the REASON ["Action" that I am here] . Ex: Oh ["Agent" my] REASON ["Action" for including it] _was_ ["State_of_Affairs" Section fifty four A].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The person who responds to a State_of_Affairs by performing some Action.
Ex: Those are ["Agent" my] REASONS , " said Toby .

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
The action that the Agent performs in response to a State_of_Affairs.
Ex: I find that all my REASONS ["Action" for postponing giving birth] still apply

fe.name: State_of_Affairs
fe.definition:
The eventuality that motivates the Agent"s performing a particular Action in response to it.
Ex: My REASON _is_ ["State_of_Affairs" that our cities are now designed round the motor car]

lexunit.name: reason.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cause, explanation, or justification

lexunit.name: why.n
lexunit.definition: COD: reason or explanation

lexunit.name: motive.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a factor inducing a person to act in a particular way

lexunit.name: motivation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a motive

lexunit.name: basis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the underlying support for an idea, argument, or process.

frame.name: Permitting
frame.definition:
In this frame a State_of_affairs is permitted by a Principle. Raising constructions are common in this frame. In this frame the Principle which sanctions the State_of_affairs is not an agent who grants permission to a specific individual or group of individuals, and thus differs from the Grantor in the Grant_permission frame.
Ex: ["State_of_affairs" Children] were not PERMITTED ["State_of_affairs" in the office] . Ex: ["Principle" Code 1425] ALLOWS ["State_of_affairs" us] ["State_of_affairs" to deduct interest payments].
Ex: ["Principle" No religion] ACCEPTS ["State_of_affairs" discrimination against women].

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition: The State_of_affairs is the situation that is permitted by the Principle.

fe.name: Principle
fe.definition: The Principle is the code or authority which permits the State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the State_of_affairs is sanctioned.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Principle permits the State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the State_of_affairs is permitted.

lexunit.name: allow.v
lexunit.definition: COD: admit as legal or acceptable.

lexunit.name: permit.n
lexunit.definition: FN: admit as acceptable or legal

lexunit.name: sanction.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to permit

lexunit.name: permit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: admit as acceptable or legal.

lexunit.name: accept.v
lexunit.definition: FN: allow

lexunit.name: entitle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: allow some state of affairs

frame.name: Preventing
frame.definition:
A Preventing_cause keeps an Event from taking place. Unlike in the Thwarting frame, the Preventing_cause does not directly prevent the actions of an individual, but rather affects the world in such a way that an Event cannot occur. Some lexical units, like AVERT and AVOID indicate that the Preventing_cause would have been affected if the Event occurred. Ex: ["Preventing_cause" Rain] PREVENTED ["Event" the ball game] ["Event" from taking place].
Ex: ["Preventing_cause" He] could have STOPPED ["Event" the riot] .
Ex: ["Preventing_cause" The government] narrowly AVERTED ["Event" a coup] .

fe.name: Preventing_cause
fe.definition: The Preventing_cause is the force which keeps the Event from happening.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The Event is prevented from occurring by the Preventing_cause.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Preventing_cause keeps the Event from taking place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the Preventing_cause keeps the Event from taking place.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the agent which keeps the Event from happening.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: prevent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep from happening or arising.

lexunit.name: avert.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent or ward off (an undesirable occurrence).

lexunit.name: frustrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent (a plan or action) from progressing, succeeding, or being fulfilled.

lexunit.name: nip in the bud.v
lexunit.definition: FN: prevent something from progressing to completion, by taking action early in the process

lexunit.name: obviate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: avoid; prevent.

lexunit.name: stave off.v

lexunit.name: check.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stop the progress of something.

lexunit.name: pre-empt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take action in order to prevent (an attack or other anticipated event) happening; forestall.

lexunit.name: avoid.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent from doing or happening.

lexunit.name: prevention.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of preventing

lexunit.name: pre-emption.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of pre-empting.

lexunit.name: stopping.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of stopping

lexunit.name: prohibit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent.

lexunit.name: stop.v
lexunit.definition: FN: prevent an event from occurring.

lexunit.name: upset.v

frame.name: Severity_of_offense
frame.definition: In this frame an Offense is described in terms of the legal or other punishing action that can be taken in response to the offense. Ex: He committed an INDICTABLE ["Offense" crime] .

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition: The Offense is the action, crime, or event which is described in terms of what legal or punishing action can be taken against the offender.

fe.name: Code
fe.definition: The legal Code under which the severity of the offense is determined. Ex: That crime is INDICTABLE ["Cd" under British law].

lexunit.name: actionable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: giving sufficient reason to take legal action.

lexunit.name: capital.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an offence or charge) liable to the death penalty.

lexunit.name: indictable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an offence) rendering a person who commits it liable to be charged with a serious crime that warrants a trial by jury.

lexunit.name: felonious.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of an offense, severe enough to be charged as a felony

frame.name: Thwarting
frame.definition:
In this frame a Preventing_cause interferes with the ability of a Protagonist to complete an intended Action. The Protagonist may not be mentioned in the sentence, in which case the Action is an endeavor that an individual or group of individuals hopes to accomplish. In this frame it is necessary that the Protagonist is unable to successfully complete the Action.
Ex: ["Preventing_cause" Noriega's troops] FOILED ["Action" a coup attempt]. Ex: ["Preventing_cause" He] PREVENTED ["Protagonist" her] ["Action" from running away]. Ex: ["Protagonist" He] was FOILED ["Action" in his attempt to overthrow the government].

fe.name: Preventing_cause
fe.definition: The Preventing_cause is the agent or force who keeps the Protagonist from completing her or his planned Action.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist is the individual or group of individuals who have a planned Action which is prevented by the Preventing_cause

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action is the action or event certain individuals desire to bring about which is prevented by the Preventing_cause.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the thwarting occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the thwarting occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Preventing_cause thwarts the Action of the Protagonist. Ex: He ["Mnr" easily] THWARTED my plans.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Action is thwarted.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation for why or how the Protagonist and/or Action was thwarted by the Preventing_cause.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

lexunit.name: thwart.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent from succeeding in or accomplishing something.

lexunit.name: foil.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent the success of.

lexunit.name: stymie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent or hinder the progress of.

lexunit.name: hamstring.v
lexunit.definition: COD: severely restrict; thwart:

lexunit.name: prevent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make unable to do something. (Different from Preventing.prevent.v)

lexunit.name: stop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent from doing something

lexunit.name: forestall.v
lexunit.definition: COD: anticipate and prevent the action of.

lexunit.name: derail.v
