lexunit.name: frustrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prevent (someone) from doing or achieving something.

lexunit.name: preclude.v
lexunit.definition: FN: prevent someone from successfully doing something

lexunit.name: counter.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take action to prevent an opponent's action from succeeding; stop some SOA (either in progress or anticipated)

frame.name: Assessing
frame.definition:
An Assessor examines a Phenomenon to figure out its Value according to some Feature of the Phenomenon. This Value is a factor in determining the acceptability of the Phenomenon. In some cases, a Method (implicitly involving an Assessor) is used to determine the Phenomenon's Value.
Ex: ["Phenomenon" Each company] is then EVALUATED ["Feature" for their earning potential]. ["Assessor" CNI] Ex: ["Evidence" From the evidence of the pilot studies] ["Phenomenon" the risk of damage to the test subjects] was RATED ["Value" too high to continue]. ["Assessor" CNI] Ex: ["Assessor" He] WEIGHED ["Phenomenon" his options] ["Manner" carefully].

fe.name: Assessor
fe.definition: The sentient entity that evaluates the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: The entity whose Value according to a Feature is being measured.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition: The value (according to some scale) that the Phenomenon is deemed to have. The Value is taken to indicate the Phenomenon's acceptability.

fe.name: Feature
fe.definition:
The type of property or feature that the Phenomenon is being judged on.
Ex: You will also be GRADED ["fea" on your speed of response] .

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: Some fact perceived by the Assessor which leads to their evaluation of the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any secondary effect of the action or characterization of the Assessor which saliently affects the character of the assessment.
Ex: He ["Manner" quietly] GRADED the papers.

fe.name: Method
fe.definition:
An event or procedure that allows the Assessor to evaluate the Phenomenon.
Ex: ["met" The study] EVALUATED the risk of a major quake.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which assessment occurs

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Assessor makes the assessment.
Ex: The committee RATED Smithers " most loyal servant " ["tim" about a week ago] .

fe.name: Standard
fe.definition:
An entity that the Phenomenon is compared to in the assessment.
Ex: Smiter WEIGHED his chances in the snow ["sta" against the danger posed by the troop of sycophants hurtling towards him].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The goal that the Assessor hopes to accomplish by assessing the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the assessing takes place.
Ex: They 'll EVALUATE you ["pla" in that room over there] , and then you 're free to go .

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Assessor to make the assessment.
Ex: ["Medium" This chapter] EVALUATES the far-left's contribution to the environmentalism debate since the '70's .

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
A person who participates along with the Assessor in the assessing event.
Ex: In order to find the best suited, targeted form of activity, the prisoner?s work and functioning capability is ASSESSED together ["cop" with him/her].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
This frame element is defined as the number of times assessing occurs per some unit of time.
Ex: Brown 's chapter on geodemographics discusses an application field where primary data collected for operational purposes are ["Fre" typically] EVALUATED in relation to secondary data derived from sources such as the Census of Population .

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

fe.name: Depicitive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world at a partiicular time and place.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The result of the assessing.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE denotes the length of time during which a continuous event occurs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

lexunit.name: assess.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to evaluate or judge some quality of an object or situation "How would you assess her performance on the job?"

lexunit.name: rate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to evaluate something on a scale depending on some quality, esp. when the number of outcomes is limited "Travelers rated Japan Air Lines "Excellent" with regard to in-flight service."

lexunit.name: evaluate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to judge something against a standard, as to its merit or suitability

lexunit.name: grade.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to decide on the basis of some quality where to place something along an established scale "Geologists grade rocks according to their hardness."

lexunit.name: assessment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of assessing; evaluating, judging

lexunit.name: evaluation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of judging the value or worth of something

lexunit.name: weigh.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to determine the weight of something

lexunit.name: judge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: decide the value or significance of some feature

lexunit.name: value.v
lexunit.definition: FN: declare the value or significance of some feature

lexunit.name: rank.v
lexunit.definition: FN: rate with respect to other members of a category.

lexunit.name: reappraise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: appraise again or differently.

lexunit.name: appraise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: assess the value, quality, or performance of.

lexunit.name: appraisal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an assessment of someone or something, especially the performance of an employee.

lexunit.name: reappraisal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an examination of the quality of for a second time.

frame.name: Deny_permission
frame.definition:
In this frame, an Authority orders a Protagonist not to engage in an Action.
Ex: ["Authority" The police officer] FORBID ["Protagonist" me] ["Action" from turning around] .

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition: The Authority orders the Protagonist to not engage in a particular Action.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist wants to engage in an Action, but is ordered not to by the Authority.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: The Action is what the Protagonist seeks to do, but is ordered not to.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the denying of permission occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the denial of permission occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose is what the Authority hopes to accomplish by denying permission.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition:
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.
First, it applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. The second subgroup consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier. What that role is depends only on the predicate heading the modifier phrase.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: forbid.v
lexunit.definition: COD: order not to do.

lexunit.name: prohibit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally forbid by law, rule, etc.

lexunit.name: outlaw.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make illegal to do something.

frame.name: Prohibiting
frame.definition:
In this frame a State_of_affairs is prohibited by a Principle. Raising constructions are common in this frame. In this frame the Principle which prohibits the State_of_affairs is not an agent who denies permission to a specific individual or group of individuals, and thus differs from the Authority in the Deny_permission frame.
Ex: ["State_of_affairs" Guns] were PROHIBITED ["State_of_affairs" in the airport] . Ex: ["Principle" Code 1425] BANS ["State_of_affairs" large trucks] ["State_of_affairs" in the tunnel].

fe.name: Principle
fe.definition:
A moral, legal, or social norm which rules a State_of_affairs to be inadmissible behavior or an outcome of behavior.
Ex: ["Prin" The Establishment Clause of the First Amendment] plainly PROHIBITS the establishment of a national religion by Congress.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the prohibiting occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the prohibiting occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the State_of_affairs is prohibited.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the State_of_affairs is prohibited.

lexunit.name: ban.v
lexunit.definition: COD: officially or legally prohibit.

lexunit.name: forbid.v
lexunit.definition: COD: refuse to allow.

lexunit.name: prohibit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally forbid by law, rule, etc.

lexunit.name: proscribe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: forbid, especially by law.

lexunit.name: outlaw.v
lexunit.definition: COD: ban.

lexunit.name: ban.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official or legal prohibition.

lexunit.name: prohibition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of prohibiting.

lexunit.name: control.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the restriction of an activity, tendency, or phenomenon.

lexunit.name: bar.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to prohibit something from happening

frame.name: Speak_on_topic
frame.definition: A Speaker addresses an Audience on a particular Topic. The Audience is generally passive, although for many types of address (including academic talks and press conferences), a discussion or question-answer period is virtually always required.

fe.name: Audience
fe.definition:
The person or persons to whom the Speaker delivers their text.
Ex: He LECTURED ["Audience" to the officers of the Scots Guard] in 1929.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The person who orally delivers a text about a Topic to a passive Audience.
Ex: ["Speaker" You] have to SERMONIZE about the good times

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
What the text that the Speaker produces is about.
Ex: He was the Director: he could LECTURE ["Topic" on whomever he liked].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is a description of the Speaker's speech.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This frame element is the Medium through which the Speaker communicates.

fe.name: Occasion
fe.definition: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given. Ex: The ["Occasion" New Year] ADDRESS was well received. Ex: ["Speaker" Professor Frink]_gave_ the ["Occasion" Macarthur]LECTURE ["Time" in 1978].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time describes when the speaking occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place describes the location where the speaking occurs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes. This often means that the Explanation causes the complaint, but not in all cases. In particular, there are cases when the connection is a bit weaker than normal for causation. In these instances, cause is mediated by some actor responding in a complex way to the situation. Such cases are not paraphrasable in the language of direct causation.

lexunit.name: lecture.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deliver an educational lecture or lectures

lexunit.name: sermonize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: a talk on a religious or moral subject, especially one given during a church service and based on a passage from the Bible

lexunit.name: expound.v
lexunit.definition: COD: present and explain (a theory or idea) systematically.

lexunit.name: preach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deliver a religious address to an assembled group of people

lexunit.name: hold forth.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to talk about something at length

lexunit.name: expatiate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak or write at length or in detail

lexunit.name: ramble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk or write at length in a confused or inconsequential way

lexunit.name: go on.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk at great or excessive length

lexunit.name: discuss.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk or write about (a topic) in detail.

lexunit.name: address.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak formally to.

lexunit.name: address.n
lexunit.definition: FN: talk

lexunit.name: lecture.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an educational talk to an audience, especially one of students in a university.

lexunit.name: pontificate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express one's opinions in a pompous and dogmatic way.

lexunit.name: deal.v
lexunit.definition: FN: speak on a particular topic.

lexunit.name: tell.v
lexunit.definition: FN: speak on a given topic (used almost or entirely exclusively with the word 'of')

frame.name: Subordinates_and_Superiors
frame.definition:
Two individuals, the Subordinate and the Superior have a relationship such that the Subordinate generally follows orders given by the Superior and has the best interests of the Superior in mind.
Ex: The archduke and several of ["Superior" his] ["Subordinate" HENCHMEN] got out of the carriage, looking around nervously.

fe.name: Superior
fe.definition: The individual in charge of the Subordinate.

fe.name: Subordinate
fe.definition: The individual under the command of the Superior.

lexunit.name: henchman.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a faithful follower or political supporter, especially one prepared to engage in crime or dishonest practices.

lexunit.name: minion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a follower or underling of a powerful person, especially a servile or unimportant one.

lexunit.name: underling.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a subordinate.

lexunit.name: lackey.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a servant, especially a liveried footman or manservant.

lexunit.name: subordinate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person under the authority or control of another

lexunit.name: master.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a man who has people working for him, especially servants or slaves.

lexunit.name: servant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a devoted and helpful follower or supporter.

lexunit.name: superior.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person of superior rank.

lexunit.name: assistant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who ranks below a senior person.

lexunit.name: hireling.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who is hired, especially for morally dubious or illegal work.

lexunit.name: goon.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a ruffian employed to harm or threaten people

lexunit.name: paxman.n
lexunit.definition: FN: type of personal guard of a lord that enjoys an extremely close personal relationship with his charge.

lexunit.name: stooge.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a subordinate used by another to do routine or unpleasant work.

lexunit.name: senior.a
lexunit.definition: COD: high or higher in rank or status.

lexunit.name: junior.a
lexunit.definition: COD: low or lower in rank or status.

frame.name: Suspiciousness
frame.definition: In this frame, a Behavior is suspicious or otherwise subject to question. The general implication is that the Behavior provides evidence for some (as yet unproven) socially undesirable conclusion about a (usually implicit) Social_actor. (Such conclusions often include the idea that some individual is lying, or that a crime was committed.) Ex: ["Behavior" That he took out a life insurance in his wife's name without informing her] _is_ SUSPICIOUS. Ex: ["Behavior" His motives] _are_ SUSPECT. Ex: It _was_ rather SUSPICIOUS ["soc" of you] ["Behavior" to leave the party just before the police arrived].

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior which is regarded as suspicious.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Behavior is suspicious. Ex: That looks like ["Degree" very] SUSPICIOUS activity.

fe.name: Social_actor
fe.definition: An individual that is suspected of wrongdoing because of the Behavior.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

lexunit.name: suspect.a
lexunit.definition: COD: possibly dangerous or false.

lexunit.name: suspicious.a
lexunit.definition: FN: arousing a feeling that something may be dangerous or may indicate criminal or unlawful behavior

lexunit.name: questionable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of suspect morality, honesty, value, etc.

lexunit.name: fishy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: arousing feelings of doubt or suspicion.

lexunit.name: dubious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not to be relied upon.

frame.name: Deserving
frame.definition:
The existence of a State_of_Affairs is sufficient reason for taking an Action . The agent who is justified in taking the suggested Action is not part of the immediate scene, however.
Ex: ["State_of_Affairs" The underwater sequences] WARRANT ["Action" the price of the admission alone].
Ex: '["State_of_Affairs" Desperate situations] CALL ["Action" for desperate measures] ," said Mr Eames grandly.

fe.name: State_of_Affairs
fe.definition:
An Eventuality or an Entity that is taken to constitute sufficient reason for taking another Action.
Ex: ["State_of_Affairs" A heavy contact to the opponent 's face] may not MERIT just a verbal warning

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
An Action that is taken to be justifiable given the State_of_Affairs.
Ex: The end JUSTIFIES ["Action" the means].

lexunit.name: merit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deserve or be worthy of

lexunit.name: warrant.v
lexunit.definition: COD: justify or necessitate

lexunit.name: warrant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: justification or authority

lexunit.name: grounds.n
lexunit.definition: COD: factors forming a basis for action or the justification for a belief

lexunit.name: worth.a
lexunit.definition: COD: deserving to be treated or regarded in the way specified

lexunit.name: deserve.v
lexunit.definition: FN: merit

lexunit.name: call.v
lexunit.definition: COD: require; demand

lexunit.name: justify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be a good reason for.

frame.name: Claim_ownership
frame.definition: A Claimant asserts his or her right to possession of a piece of Property (either real, such as land, or private). The Claimant may be acting on the behalf of a Beneficiary. Ex: ["Claimant" The King] CLAIMS ["Property" this land and surrounding waters]. Ex: Hoping to strike it rich, Thaddeus Gulch staked ["Claimant" his] CLAIM by the river bed. Ex: ["Claimant" I] DIBS ["Property" on the last piece of cake].

fe.name: Claimant
fe.definition: The Claimant asserts rights or priviliges, typically ownership, over some Property. Ex: The king ordered ["Clm" the envoy] to CLAIM the land accross the river.

fe.name: Property
fe.definition: The Property is declared to be under the ownership of the Claimant. Ex: I CLAIM ["Prp" this forest and environs] in the name of the Queen.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: The Beneficiary is declared the owner of the Property by the Claimant, or the person or group in whose name or favor the Claimant is acting. Ex: I CLAIM this forest and environs ["Ben" in the name of the Queen].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The Role of the land claimed. Ex: The French government CLAIMED this string of islands ["Role" as their own]. Ex: As of yet, no one has CLAIMED this hill ["Role" as belonging to anyone].

lexunit.name: claim.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something claimed as property, particularly a piece of land.

lexunit.name: claim.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take or declare rightful ownership of.

lexunit.name: call.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lay claim on something as one's right.

lexunit.name: dibs.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the right to share or choose something.

frame.name: Documents
frame.definition: Words in the frame refer to any Document that has a legal status. Some Document empowers the Bearer of the Document to execute the Right. Others indicate the Obligation of the Bearer. Still others show the identity or Status of the Bearer.

fe.name: Bearer
fe.definition: The holder of the document. Ex: ["Bearer" My]VISA will expire next month.

fe.name: Issuer
fe.definition: The authority that issues the document. Ex: ["Issuer" US consulate] issued a VISA to Ms. Yang to travel to San Francisco.

fe.name: Obligation
fe.definition: Obligation is the obligation that is imposed on the Bearer of the Document. Ex: They were all under SUBPOENA ["Obligation" to appear in court.]

fe.name: Right
fe.definition: Right is the right of the Bearer of the Document that is authorized by the Document. Ex: ["Bearer" Raymond] has a ["Right" fishing] LICENCE.

fe.name: Status
fe.definition: Status is the state of the Bearer of the Document indicated by the Document. Ex: The couple just got ["Bearer" their] ["Status" marriage] CERTIFICATE.

fe.name: Specification
fe.definition: Specification is the condiontion that has to do with the Right and Obligation of the Document. Ex: Before you get your driver's liscense, you need to carry your ["Specification" temporary] driving PERMIT when you drive.

fe.name: Document
fe.definition: Document is the piece of paper that has the legal status. Ex: The police need a ["Right" search] ["Document" WARRANT] to enter his house.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The language the Document is written in, or a specification of the kind of object that instantiates it.
Ex: We only need an ["Medium" electronic] CONFIRMATION.

lexunit.name: visa.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an endorsement on a passport indicating that the holder is allowed to enter, leave, or stay for a specified period of time in a country.

lexunit.name: passport.n
lexunit.definition: cOD: an official document issued by a government, certifying the holder's identity and citizenship and entitling them to travel abroad under its protection.

lexunit.name: subpoena.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a writ ordering a person to attend a court.

lexunit.name: warrant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official authorization enabling the police or some other body to make an arrest, search premises, etc.

lexunit.name: certificate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official document attesting or recording a particular fact or event, a level of achievement, the fulfilment of a legal requirement, etc.

lexunit.name: papers.n
lexunit.definition: COD: sheets of paper covered with writing or printing; documents.

lexunit.name: licence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a permit from an authority to own or use something, do a particular thing, or carry on a trade (especially in alcoholic liquor).

lexunit.name: summons.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an order to appear in a law court.

lexunit.name: diploma.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a certificate awarded by an educational establishment for passing an examination or completing a course of study.

lexunit.name: deed.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a legal document, especially one relating to property ownership or legal rights.

lexunit.name: lease.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a contract by which one party conveys land, property, services, etc. to another for a specified time.

lexunit.name: agreement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a contract by which one party conveys land, property, services, etc. to another for a specified time.

lexunit.name: treaty.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formally concluded and ratified agreement between states.

lexunit.name: charter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a written grant by a sovereign or legislature, by which a body such as a university is created or its rights and privileges defined.

lexunit.name: authorization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a legal document that gives official permission for or approval to something

lexunit.name: deposition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a statement to be used as evidence.

lexunit.name: brief.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a summary of the facts and legal points in a case given to a barrister to argue in court

lexunit.name: writ.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a form of written command in the name of a court or other legal authority to do or abstain from doing a specified act

lexunit.name: affidavit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, for use as evidence in court.

lexunit.name: will.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a legal document containing instructions for the disposition of one's money and property after one's death

lexunit.name: testimony.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal statement, especially one given in a court of law

lexunit.name: testament.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's will.

lexunit.name: ruling.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a decision made by court

lexunit.name: finding.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a conclusion reached as a result of a trial

lexunit.name: opinion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal statement of reasons for a judgement given

lexunit.name: title.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a right or claim to the ownership of property or to a rank or throne

lexunit.name: orders.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a legal written document that specifies the rules to be followed

lexunit.name: contract.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a written or spoken agreement intended to be enforceable by law

lexunit.name: permit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official document giving permission to do something.

lexunit.name: document.n
lexunit.definition: COD: A written or printed paper that bears the original, official, or legal form of something and can be used to furnish decisive evidence or information.

lexunit.name: contractual.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of or relating to a legally binding document, i.e., a contract.

lexunit.name: accord.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official agreement or treaty.

frame.name: Fighting_activity
frame.definition: A generally large group of people, the Combatants, are engaged in a chaotic, violent, and usually protracted Fight amongst themselves. There are no distinct sides, and generally no particular goal (compare Hostile_encounter). The Fight may be described as having a Manner or Degree of violence. Time and Place may also be expressed.

fe.name: Combatants
fe.definition: The Combatants participate as fighters in the Fight. Ex: The football referee's controversial call led to a bloody FREE-FOR-ALL ["Com" among the fans].

fe.name: Fight
fe.definition: The violent activity. Ex: I couldn't help but watch as several bruised people reentered the ["Fight" MELEE].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Fight takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Fight takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner of the Fight. Ex: Officers said they were stunned upon arrival at the scene of the ["Mnr" raucous] FRAY.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This is the Degree of violence of the Fight. Ex: The townspeople engaged in a ["Deg" full-scale] FREE-FOR-ALL.

fe.name: Salient_activity
fe.definition: An activity that engaged in by the Combatants while fighting. Ex: ["SA" stabbing] AFFRAY

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition: The Issue over which Fight happens.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Fight takes place.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which the Combatants engage in the Fight.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The weapon or other instrument used by the Combatants.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that (some of) he Combatants wish to acheive by fighting.

lexunit.name: melee.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a confused crowd or scuffle.

lexunit.name: free-for-all.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disorganized or unrestricted situation or event in which everyone may take part, especially a fight or discussion.

lexunit.name: affray.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a breach of the peace by fighting in a public place.

lexunit.name: fray.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a battle or fight

lexunit.name: donnybrook.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a heated argument.

lexunit.name: fracas.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a noisy disturbance or quarrel.

frame.name: Killing
frame.definition: A Killer or Cause causes the death of the Victim. Ex: ["Killer" John] DROWNED ["Victim" Martha].

fe.name: Killer
fe.definition: The person or sentient entity that causes the death of theVictim.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: The living entity that dies as a result of the killing.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An inanimate entity or process that causes the death of the Victim.
Ex: ["Cause" The rockslide] KILLED nearly half of the climbers.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state of affairs that the Killer is trying to bring about by killing.
Ex: It's simple: he KILLED her ["Purp" to get the inheritance].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The method or action that the Killer or Cause performs resulting in the death of the Victim.
Ex: The flood EXTERMINATED the rats ["Means" by cutting off access to food].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The preexisting state of affairs that the Killer is responding to.
Ex: She DROWNED him ["Reason" for lying].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the death took place.
Ex: Apparently there were two MURDERS ["Place" in Atherton] in one week.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The point or period of time within which the Victim is killed.
Ex: There is no evidence that the royal family was KILLED ["Time" during the destruction] at this site.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Killer or Victim during the killing.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The state of the Victim that results from being killed. (Normally this is somewhat redundant.)
Ex: Two men ... SMOTHERED her ["Result" to death].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The device used by the Killer to bring about the death of the Victim. Ex: It's difficult to SUICIDE ["Instr" with only a pocketknife].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Killer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). Ex: KILL them ["Manner" quietly]. Ex: A true professional , he BEHEADED his victims ["Man" with unhurried expertise], a credit to his calling. Ex: A gunman SLAUGHTERED six people ["Man" in cold blood] because he had been evicted.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree appears with adjectives to describe the killing potential of an object or with nouns to describe how widespread the killing is. Ex: The Nazis engaged in ["Degree" mass] GENOCIDE.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

lexunit.name: suicide.n

lexunit.name: annihilation.n

lexunit.name: liquidation.n

lexunit.definition: COD: cut off the head of

lexunit.name: killing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of causing death.

lexunit.name: murder.n

lexunit.name: slaughter.n

lexunit.name: killer.n

lexunit.name: massacre.n

lexunit.name: infanticide.n

lexunit.name: shooting.n

lexunit.name: matricide.n

lexunit.name: butcher.v

lexunit.name: beheading.n

lexunit.name: assassination.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the fact of murdering (a political or religious leader)

lexunit.name: butchery.n

lexunit.name: carnage.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the killing of a large number of people.

lexunit.name: suffocation.n

lexunit.name: assassin.n

lexunit.name: blood-bath.n

frame.name: Amounting_to
frame.definition:
The absolute Value of a quantifiable Attribute of an item is determined by adding up the values for the Attribute of the individuals or parts that make up the item. The item is not expressed as a separate constituent but it is presupposed by the concept of Attribute. Alternatively, the Numbers form an implicit set whose sum is the Value associated with the set. In some cases what is reported is just the cardinality of the individuals that make up the item so that in effect the Value is a count. In other cases the identity of the Attribute can only be inferred from the Value.
There is no cognizer on the scene in this frame. Instead, the frame focuses on the relationship between the Attribute or Numbers and the Value, which is stable and unchanging regardless of who performs the calculation.
Ex: Defence is provided in West Germany by ["Attribute" armed forces whose number] TOTALS ["Value" close to half a million men and women] . Ex: ["Attribute" Revenues] TOTALLED ["Value" 568.86m pounds] Ex: The WHO estimated that the cumulative TOTAL ["Attribute" of AIDS cases] was ["Value" more than 1,500,000].

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
The value of an attribute.
Ex: The final TALLY for 1990 _was_ ["Value" 199,000] .

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The scalar property of a concrete or abstract entity.
Ex: During the first three years of drug squad work, ["Attribute" arrests] TOTALED some sixty-four persons.

fe.name: Time_span
fe.definition: The span of time when the Attribute has the Value. Ex: The TOTAL ["TS" for last month] far exceeded expectations. Ex: The ["TS" April] TOTAL is 20,000.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE indicates the time span during which the total of the Attribute is the Value, with the added information that it is (somehow) calculated at a regular interval coinciding with the transition between spans of time.

fe.name: Numbers
fe.definition:
A set of numbers that add up to the Value.
Ex: Look, you turn those into numbers, and then ["num" 592 and 74] TOTAL 666, right?

lexunit.name: total.v
lexunit.definition: COD: amount in number to

lexunit.name: amount.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come to be (a total) when added together

lexunit.name: total.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a total number or amount

lexunit.name: tally.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a current score or amount.

lexunit.name: total.a
lexunit.definition: COD: comprising the whole number or amount.

lexunit.name: number.v
lexunit.definition: COD: amount to.

frame.name: Processing_materials
frame.definition: An Agent alters some Material in some useful way by means of some chemical or physical Alterant. Typically, this involves placing a reagent in contact with the Material, or applying heat, pressure, etc. Often a specific Agent and/or Result is mentioned. The Alterant is often incorporated in the target, as in _tin.v, galvanize_. (The Preserving frame is a special case of Processing_materials, in which the Material is immersed in the Alterant for the Purpose of preventing decay.) Processing_materials is distinguished from Filling in that the Material in Processing_materials is fundamentally altered (often chemically), rather than simply being covered with a different substance. Ex: ["Agent" Native Americans] DYED ["Material" textiles] ["Alterant" with dyes made from cedar strips]. Ex: ["Material" Watering cans] are often ["Alterant" GALVANIZED] ["Purpose" to prevent rust].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is a person who applies the Process to the Material.

fe.name: Alterant
fe.definition: The Alterant causes a change in the Material.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: The Material is altered by the Agent in some useful way. Ex: Stu TREATED ["Mat" the lumber] with magical waterproofing fairydust.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which the Agent processes the Material. Ex: He TREATED the exterior of the house with waterproofing ["Pur" to protect his valuable peanut butter collection.].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The result of the processing action, whether intended or not.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time during which the application of the Alterant is applied to the Material

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location in which the Materials are processed, often a purpose-built facility such as a tannery or water treatment plant.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The point in time or period during which the treatment of the Material takes place.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The part of the Material which is affected by the process.
Ex: You have to GALVANIZE the pipes ["Subregion" only in the interior].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in processing the Material.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition:
The dimension or aspect of the Material that is processed.
Ex: This supernatant was used for neasurement of ["dim" isotopic] ENRICHMENT of free leucine.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A holistic description encompassing all the details of an act of processing, often indicated by giving a characteristic of the Agent that affects the action.
Ex: Botulinum can not be WEAPONIZED ["Manner" the same way] .

lexunit.name: dye.v
lexunit.definition: FN: apply a liquid to a solid (especially fabric) in order to color it (darker than it originally was)

lexunit.name: etch.v
lexunit.definition: FN: apply a chemical (usually an acid) to a surface to make it rougher.

lexunit.name: treat.v
lexunit.definition: FN: To apply a chemical to or otherwise process (e.g. with heat or pressure) a material for a particular purpose.

lexunit.name: galvanize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: coat (iron or steel) with a protective layer of zinc.

lexunit.name: enrich.v
lexunit.definition: COD: increase the proportion of a particular isotope in (an element), especially that of the fissile isotope U-235 in uranium.

lexunit.name: enrichment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of increasing the proportion of a particular isotope in (an element), especially that of the fissile isotope U-235 in uranium.

lexunit.name: process.v
lexunit.definition: COD: perform a series of operations to change or preserve.

lexunit.name: reprocess.v
lexunit.definition: COD: process (something, especially spent nuclear fuel) again or differently, in order to reuse it.

lexunit.name: reprocessing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of taking an industrial product (often spent nuclear fuel rods) and making it useful again or in a different way.

lexunit.name: weaponize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: process (a pathogen or chemical) so as to make more deadly and/or virulent

lexunit.name: weaponization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: processing (of pathogens or chemicals) so as to make more virulent and/or deadly

frame.name: Adding_up
frame.definition:
A Cognizer computes a Result on the basis of input Numbers by addition.
Ex: ADD UP ["Numbers" your savings]. Ex: This is a cumulative figure obtained by ADDING UP ["Numbers" the cost of treating a given volume of specific diseases]. Ex: When ["Cognizer" he] later took the trouble to ADD UP ["Numbers" the bill] he discovered that the actual cost was Fr 1,481 , around 140 pounds : an overcharge of 40 pounds Ex: ["Cognizer" Chaperones] TALLIED ["Numbers" the number of tickets sold at the school dance] ["Result" at more than 1000].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The person doing the calculation.

fe.name: Numbers
fe.definition: The Numbers that are used in the calculation.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The outcome of the Cognizer's calculcations.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Cognizer operates on the Numbers.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Cognizer performs their calculation

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by calculating.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action performed by the Cognizer that brings about their calculation of the Result.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A holistic description of the event (e.g. "the same way"), including depictions of the Cognizer in terms of how the Cognizer's state affects the entire action.
Ex: This week the top brass again ["man" grimly] TALLIED the number of dead .

lexunit.name: add up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: calculate the total of

lexunit.name: tally.v

frame.name: Endangering
frame.definition:
An Agent or Cause is responsible for placing a Valued_entity at risk. Endangering_act, Place, Time, Reason, and Circumstance may also be specified.
Ex: ["Cause" His actions] have IMPERILED ["Valued" his immortal soul]!
Ex: I admit that ["Agent" I] ENDANGERED ["Valued_entity" you all] ["Endangering_act" by attracting the killer's notice].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An (non-sentient) entity or state of affairs that leads to the peril to the Valued_entity.

fe.name: Valued_entity
fe.definition: The entity which may be negatively impacted as a result of the emperilment.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity which causes the risk to the Valued_entity.

fe.name: Endangering_act
fe.definition:
The specific event or state of affairs brought about by the Agent or Cause which endangers the Valued_entity.
Ex: The snow ENDANGERED not only the mission but also our lives ["Mns" by slowing us down].
Ex: His actions IMPERILED his immortal soul ["Mns" by exposing him to demonic influence].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes an aspect of the endangering act that is not directly related to the cause, intermediate action, or entity involved. Ex: Members of the underground club would frequently ENDANGER the lives of others ["Manner" with reckless abandon].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Valued_entity is put in danger.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the Valued_entity is put in danger.

lexunit.name: imperil.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put into danger

lexunit.name: endanger.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put at risk or in danger.

lexunit.name: endangerment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of putting at risk.

lexunit.name: jeopardise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: endanger

frame.name: Eclipse
frame.definition:
An Obstruction blocks an Eclipsed entity partially or completely from view. The positions of the Obstruction and the Eclipsed entity are often reported relative to a Vantage_point.
Ex: ["Eclipsed" A small green bulb] CONCEALED ["Obstruction" behind the panel] flashed on momentarily .

fe.name: Obstruction
fe.definition:
The entity which blocks the Eclipsed entity from view.
Ex: ["Obstruction" Wispy clouds] SHROUDED the treetops.

fe.name: Eclipsed
fe.definition:
The entity which is blocked from view.
Ex: The mists OBSCURED ["Eclipsed" the top of the tower].

fe.name: Vantage_point
fe.definition:
The position from which an observer, if an observer were present, would have their view of the Eclipsed entity blocked by the Obstruction.
Ex: The gate SCREENED the house ["VP" from the road].
Phrases such as "from view" and "from sight" are assumed to indicate that the Eclipsed entity is not visible from any Vantage_point.
Ex: The telescope is BLOCKED ["VP" from view] by a big map of Europe.
This frame element includes direct reference to observers.
Ex: A fence SCREENS the garden ["VP" from passersby]..

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Eclipsed entity is blocked from view.
Ex: The bungalow is ["Degree" completely] OBSCURED by thick foliage.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The part of the ["Eclipsed" Eclipsed] entity which is blocked from view.
Ex: The gazebo was SCREENED by a hedge ["sub" on one side].

frame.name: Existence
frame.definition:
An Entity is declared to exist, generally irrespective of its position or even the possibility of its position being specified. Time, Duration, Inherent_purpose, and State may also be mentioned.
This frame is to be contrasted with Presence, which describes the existence of an Entity in a particular (and salient) spacio-temporal context, and which also entails the presense of an observer who can detect the existence of the Entity in that context.
Ex: ["Time" Finally], ["Ent" Poland] ceased to EXIST ["State" as a state] ["Duration" for hundreds of years]. Ex: ["Ent" Such laws] EXIST ["Use" to prevent exactly this kind of fraud]. Ex: THERE IS ["Ent" a Santa Claus]!

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Some entity, abstract or concrete, which is stated to exist.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: A time at which the entity is in existence.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The period during which the Entity exists.

fe.name: Inherent_purpose
fe.definition: The reason why the Entity exists. Generally, this is more specifically the reason why the Entity was made.

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
The condition that the Entity exists in.
Ex: Natural electricity EXISTS ["State" in many forms]: in storms, solar wind, and nerve impulses.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: A situation, force, or entity which brings about the existence of the Entity.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Entity exists.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Entity is declared to exist

fe.name: Point_of_view
fe.definition:
The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Entity (or further state of affairs) to exist or not.
Ex: ["pov" For him], THERE 'S just too much drink in the world.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

lexunit.name: exist.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be real, directly or indirectly perceptible.

lexunit.name: existence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the fact or state of existing.

lexunit.name: real.a
lexunit.definition: COD: actually existing or occurring in fact; not imagined or supposed.

lexunit.name: there be.v
lexunit.definition: COD: exist; be present

lexunit.name: remain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be in the same place or condition during further time.

frame.name: Moving_in_place
frame.definition: A Theme moves with respect to a Fixed_location, generally with a certain Periodicity, without undergoing unbounded translational motion or significant alteration of configuration/shape.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: A physical entity that is participating in non-translational motion.

fe.name: Fixed_location
fe.definition: The point or set of points that define the limits of motion for the Theme. For spinning motions, it is the axis, for vibrating it is a boundary, for swinging it is a point. Ex: Balls SPIN ["Fix_loc" on their axes ]. Ex: The window VIBRATED ["Fix_loc" in the frame].

fe.name: Periodicity
fe.definition: The number of times the Theme returns to a state in a given duration. Ex: They SPUN it ["Per" at 1000 rpms].

fe.name: Angle
fe.definition: The amount of rotation that the Theme undergoes.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Theme is in bounded motion.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the bounded motion happens.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: The direction of rotation of the Theme. Ex: The dial ROTATED ["Dir" clockwise] one revolution, then the vault opened.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: TheManner describes the way in which the Theme moves in place.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result describes the end state brought about by the motion in place.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause_external describes the force which sets into motion the motion. Ex: The strings VIBRATED ["Cause" with the impact of the wind].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A description of the Theme during the action.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the agentive Theme hopes to bring about by moving.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The shape formed by the path that the Theme follows.

lexunit.name: judder.v
lexunit.definition: COD: shake and vibrate rapidly and forcefully.

lexunit.name: rotate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move in a circle around a fixed axis

lexunit.name: shake.v
lexunit.definition: FN: vibrate or tremble

lexunit.name: twirl.v
lexunit.definition: FN: spin around

lexunit.name: vibrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move with small movements rapidly to and fro.

lexunit.name: swing.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to move back and forth or from side to side while or as if suspended.

lexunit.name: flop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fall, hang, or collapse in a heavy, loose, and ungainly way

lexunit.name: quiver.v
lexunit.definition: COD: shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion

lexunit.name: quiver.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a slight trembling movement

lexunit.name: wave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move to and fro with a swaying motion while remaining fixed to one point

lexunit.name: rock.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move gently from side to side

lexunit.name: roll.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move by turning over and over on an axis

lexunit.name: swing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of swinging.

lexunit.name: spin.v
lexunit.definition: COD: turn or cause to turn round quickly.

lexunit.name: turn.v
lexunit.definition: FN: rotate

lexunit.name: earthquake.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a sudden violent shaking of the ground as a result of movements within the earth's crust.

lexunit.name: temblor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an earthquake.

lexunit.name: quake.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an earthquake.

frame.name: Pardon
frame.definition:
An Authority excuses an Offense that an Offender has committed, with the effect of ending or preventing any punishment.
Ex: President Ford PARDONED ["off" her] ["tim" after it came to light she was being held in Japan as an "enemy alien" and was secretly working to subvert the broadcasts] ["fen" DNI]
Ex: ["aut" President John Quincy Adams] _granted_ ["off" them] a PARDON and remission of the fine. ["fen" DNI]

fe.name: Offender
fe.definition:
This FE denotes the offender that seeks or gets the pardon.
Ex: Defense minister Ivanov rules out PARDON ["off" for Chechen rebel leader Maskhadov].

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition:
Authority is the organization or person taht grants the pardon.
Ex: ["Authority" The governement] issued a PARDON ["off" to the two convicts].

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition:
This FE denotes the the illegal act that the Offender is pardoned for.
Ex: They demanded a PARDON ["off" to John] ["Offense" for inadverdent manslaughter].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: Reason is the cause for pardoning an Offender. Ex: He appealed for a PARDON ["Reason" on the grounds such as ill-health].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE denotes the time when the pardon is given
Ex: The families demanded a ["Time" posthumous] PARDON for the executed soldiers.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Authority that accomplishes the pardon.
Ex: But Queen Mary, pitied his youth and PARDONED him ["mea" by a bill addressed to her chancellor, Stephen Gardener from St.James's, on 18th March 1554].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the act of pardon which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Authority that also affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the pardoning takes place.
Ex: On 1 March 2002, Andreyev was found guilty of libel and conditionally sentenced to two years in prison and then PARDONED ["pla" in the courtroom].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Authority intends to accomplish by pardoning
Ex: U.S. research on biologicals started in World War II and was greatly augmented by captured Japanese research and scientists, who were PARDONED ["pur" to help the U.S. efforts].

lexunit.name: pardon.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a remission of the legal consequences of an offence or conviction.

lexunit.name: pardon.v
lexunit.definition: COD: a remission of the legal consequences of an offence or conviction.

frame.name: Cause_change
frame.definition:
An Agent or Cause causes an Entity to change, either in its category membership or in terms of the value of an Attribute. In the former case, an Initial_category and a Final_category may be expressed, in the latter case an Initial_value and a Final_value can be specified.
Ex: Our storylines follows the saga outlined by the Ultima Series, but ["age" we] have MODIFIED ["ent" it] ["pur" in order to make our writing more cohesive].
Ex: I don't think ["Agent" you] can TURN ["ent" that rabbit] ["finc" into a hat].
Ex: How can ["age" a guy that] CHANGED ["att" his name] ["iniv" from Bob Craft] ["finv" to Jack Ass] declare anyone defamed his character?
Ex: ["tim" At this juncture], ["cau" a new development] CHANGED ["ent" the political situation on the island].
Ex: ["age" She] had ["tim" at some time earlier] ["deg" completely] CHANGED ["att" her clothing and appearance] and now stood in front of me dressed like a garden gnome.
Ex: Hence, when ["ent" (Hg 0 )] is CONVERTED ["finc" to Hg 2+] , it can be rapidly taken up in rain water, snow, or adsorbed onto small particles Ex: Hence, when ["inic" (Hg 0 )] is CONVERTED to Hg 2+ , it can be rapidly taken up in rain water, snow, or adsorbed onto small particles

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The sentient entity that effects a change in the Entity.
Ex: ["age" The system administrator] CHANGED the value from 'KDE' to 'GNOME', and then restarted the system.

fe.name: Initial_category
fe.definition:
The category of which the Entity is a member before the Agent causes a change.
Ex: Her time with the Healer Craft has CHANGED her ["inic" from a shy, nervous young girl] into a confident (almost) young woman

fe.name: Final_category
fe.definition:
The category that the Entity belongs to after it has undergone the change.
Ex: The radical message of the cross transformed Saul of Tarsus and CHANGED him from a persecutor of Christians ["finc" to a tender believer].

fe.name: Final_value
fe.definition:
The value that the Attribute assumes as a result of the change that the Entity is caused to undergo.
Ex: We CHANGED the size from 8 1/2x11 ["finv" to a larger 11 x 17] and gave it a complete graphical makeover.

fe.name: Initial_value
fe.definition:
The value that the Attribute has before the change takes place.
Ex: My dad CHANGED his hair color ["iniv" from red] to blue today.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the change of the Entity is caused.
Ex: He CHANGED it ["tim" after David Bowie told him that only twerps have the same first and last name].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the initial and final categories or values differ from each other.
Ex: We ["deg" significantly] CHANGED its appearance during this time.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event causing the change of the Entity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: Taking out his Driver's Ed pass certificate, Blair ["man" carefully] CHANGED the '6' of 1969 to an '8' making it read 23rd February 1989.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change in the Entity.
Ex: I didn't CHANGE its name ["rea" because I think it has already got used to it].

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
A characteristic of the Entity for which a value can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement , or observation.
Ex: We CHANGED ["att" the price] from $1.26 to $1.27 per pint.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The abstract or concrete thing or situation that the Agent causes to change.
Ex: The recent terrorist attacks had CHANGED ["ent" the political climate].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event that causes a change in the Entity.
Ex: ["cau" Major technological innovations] CHANGED the social and economic conditions.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by effecting a change in the Entity.
Ex: His real name is Jerry Rivers, but he CHANGED it ["pur" in order to sound more ethnic and appealing]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Entity.
Ex: Ling said he had TRANSFORMED the car ["Means" by putting slicks on].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the change of the Entity is caused.
Ex: ["pla" In his own room] he had MODIFIED nothing.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The particular role that the Agent plays in the Cause_change event.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

lexunit.definition: COD:

lexunit.name: turn.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to change into a different kind of entity.

lexunit.name: change.v
lexunit.definition: FN: alter into a different forms.

lexunit.name: convert.v
lexunit.definition: FN: modify to become.

lexunit.name: transform.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to have an altered nature.

lexunit.name: modify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make partial changes to (something) in order to improve it or lessen its severity

lexunit.name: alter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: change in character, appearance, direction, etc.

lexunit.name: modification.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of modifying.

lexunit.name: alteration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of making something different without changing its category

lexunit.name: conversion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process or action of converting or of being converted

lexunit.name: transformation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a marked change in nature, form, or appearance.

lexunit.name: vary.v
lexunit.definition: COD: modify or change (something) to make it less uniform.

lexunit.name: variation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a change or slight difference in condition, amount, or level.

lexunit.name: reshape.v
lexunit.definition: COD: shape or form (something) differently or again.

frame.name: Ride_vehicle
frame.definition:
In this frame a Theme is moved by a Vehicle which is not directly under their power. The Source, Path, Goal, or Area of the motion may be indicated. The Distance travelled or the Speed of motion may also be indicated. A Route or Roadmay be present and the Manner in which the Theme moves may be given. Ex: ["Theme" Mrs. Smith] RODE ["Vehicle" on the train]. Ex: ["Theme" Sally] FLEW ["Distance" 3000 miles] ["Source" from San Francisco] ["Goal" to New York]. Ex: Every day, ["Theme" Martin] RODE ["Vehicle" the bus] ["Road" on highway 880]. Ex: ["Theme" Mr. Bigglesworth] RIDES ["Route" route 51].
There is shared vocabulary between this frame and Carrying and Operate_vehicle. It is differentiated from Operate_vehicle in that the vehicle is not under the subject's control. It is differentiated from Carrying because the vehicle is not being used to transport goods.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the entity which moves by means of the Vehicle. Ex: ["Theme" Margeret] FLEW to Cabo San Lucas.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: The Vehicle is the means of conveyance of the Theme. It is usually expressed in a _PP_-complement or the direct object. Ex: Professor Frink SAILED to Italy ["Vehicle" on an oceanliner].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. Ex: We FLEW ["Source" from Atlanta].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory. Ex: Samantha always RODE ["Manner" gracefully] on the back of a motorcycle.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path describes the trajectory of the motion. Ex: The caravan RODE ["Path" through the desert].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is the endpoint of the trajectory of motion. Ex: We SAILED ["Goal" to Morocco].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The Distance is the extent of the motion. Ex: We FLEW ["Distance" 300 miles] in 40 minutes.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration is the amount of time the motion takes. Ex: We RODE in the van ["Duration" for 45 minutes].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs. Ex: WeFLEW["Speed" at nearly 600 miles per hour].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The Area is the location where the motion takes place. Ex: We RODE ["Area" around the state].

fe.name: Road
fe.definition: The Road is the thoroughfare on which the Vehicle travels. Ex: We RIDE the bus ["Road" on highway 580].

fe.name: Route
fe.definition: The Route is the usual path that the Vehicle travles. Ex: I RIDE ["Route" the London-Birmingham route] almost everyday.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Theme or Vehicle during the motion. Ex: We FLEW to New Orleans ["Depictive" naked].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the riding takes place. Ex: We will FLY back to New York ["Time" in September].

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Theme. Ex: My family always FLIES to New York ["CT" with our good friends, the Jacksons].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Theme rides a vehicle. Ex: Jennifer HITCHHIKED to the island ["Pur" to see her long lost friend, Mr. Moreau].

lexunit.name: ride.v
lexunit.definition: COD: travel in or on (a vehicle or horse).

lexunit.name: sail.v
lexunit.definition: COD: travel in a sailing boat as a sport or for recreation or travel in a ship or boat using sails or engine power or travel by ship on or across (a sea) or on (a route).

lexunit.name: fly.v
lexunit.definition: FN: travel by means of aircraft

lexunit.name: taxi.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move within an aircraft along the ground before take-off or after landing.

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: COD: use as a means of transport

lexunit.name: cruise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sail, travel, or move slowly around without a precise destination, especially for pleasure.

lexunit.name: coast.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move by means of a vehicle without using power

lexunit.name: jet.v
lexunit.definition: FN: travel by means of an jet aircraft

lexunit.name: hitchhike.v
lexunit.definition: COD: travel by getting free lifts in passing vehicles.

lexunit.name: ride.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of riding.

lexunit.name: cruise.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an instance of cruising.

lexunit.name: flight.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the ride one takes on something that flies

frame.name: Change_event_time
frame.definition: In this frame, an Agent or Cause changes the timing of an Event. The Event will then take place at the Destination_time or with respect to a Destination_event. This can be done with by certain Means, in a certain Manner or to a certain Degree.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the animate entity which brings about the change in time of the Event. Ex: ["Agent" The umpire] POSTPONED ["Event" the game].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-sentient force which brings about the change of time for the Event. Ex: ["Cause" The rain] DELAYED ["Event" the baseball game].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: TheEvent is the occurrence which changes time. Ex: ["Event" The opening of the musical] was DELAYED.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the way in which the time change takes place. Ex: ["Agent" My mother] ["Manner" thoughtlessly] DELAYED ["Event" my salon appointment].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means describe the way in which the time change is accomplished. Ex: ["Agent" The mayor] DELAYED ["Event" the ribbon-cutting ceremony] ["Means" by pretending to be ill].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the extent to which the time change takes place.

fe.name: Destination_event
fe.definition:
The Destination_event is the occasion which the timing of the Event occurs with respect to.
Ex: ["Agent" Consumers] should POSTPONE ["Event" purchasing a new car] ["Destination_event" until their credit rating is acceptable].

fe.name: Destination_time
fe.definition: The Destination_time is the time at which the Event actually occurs. Ex: ["Agent" The king] is POSTPONING ["Event" the festival] ["Destination_time" until July].

fe.name: Interval
fe.definition: The Interval between the Landmark_time and the Destination_time may be expressed. Ex: ["Event" The lanch] will be DELAYED ["Interval" for two months].

fe.name: Landmark_time
fe.definition: The Landmark_time is when the Event was originally intended to take place. Ex: ["Event" The driving test] was POSTPONED ["Landmark_time" from July] ["Destination_time" to September].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the reason or explanation for why the Event occurs at a different time.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Agent intends to bring about by changing the time the Event will take place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the delay occurred.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the expected time of the Event changes.

lexunit.name: delay.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to become late or slow or postpone or defer.

lexunit.name: postpone.v
lexunit.definition: COD: arrange for (something) to take place at a time later than that first scheduled.

lexunit.name: defer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put off to a later time; postpone.

lexunit.name: advance.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to occur at an earlier date than planned.

lexunit.name: move up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to cause to advance in time.

lexunit.name: move back.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to reschedule to an earlier time.

lexunit.name: put off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: delay an event until a later time.

lexunit.name: hold over.v
lexunit.definition: FN: reschedule for a later time.

lexunit.name: put over.v
lexunit.definition: COD: postpone something.

lexunit.name: delay.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a period of time by which something is late or postponed.

lexunit.name: hold up.a
lexunit.definition: FN: to delay

frame.name: Crime_scenario
frame.definition: A (putative) Crime is committed and comes to the attention of the Authorities. In response, there is a Criminal_investigation and (often) Arrest and criminal court proceedings. The Investigation, Arrest, and other parts of the Criminal_Process are pursued in order to find a Suspect (who then may enter the Criminal_process to become the Defendant) and determine if this Suspect matches the Perpetrator of the Crime, and also to determine if the Charges match the Crime. If the Suspect is deemed to have committed the Crime, then they are generally given some punishment commensurate with the Charges.

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition: The individual which is under suspicion of having committed the Crime.

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition: The individual that commits a Crime.

fe.name: Crime
fe.definition: An act, generally intentional, that matches the description that belongs to an official Charge.

fe.name: Charge
fe.definition: A description of a type of act that is not permissable according to the law of society.

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition: The group which is responsible for the maintenance of law and order, and as such have been given the power to investigate Crimes, find Suspects and determine if a Suspect should be submitted to the Criminal_process.

frame.name: Committing_crime
frame.definition:
A Perpetrator (generally intentionally) commits a Crime, i.e. does something not permitted by the laws of society.
Ex: ["Perp" They] PERPETRATED ["Cr" a felony] ["Means" by substituting a lie for negotiations].
Ex: ["Perp" The suspect] had allegedly COMMITTED ["Cr" the crime] ["Purpose" to gain the attention of a female celebrity].

fe.name: Perpetrator
fe.definition:
The individual that commits a Crime.
Ex: How can ["Perp" he] COMMIT treason against the King of England in a foreign country , if he is not English?
Ex: ["Perp" He] PERPETRATED a crime against mother nature.

fe.name: Crime
fe.definition:
An act, generally intentional, that has been formally forbidden by law.
Ex: How can he COMMIT ["Crime" treason] against the King of England in a foreign country , if he is not English?
Ex: He PERPETRATED ["Cr" a crime] against mother nature.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The action that the Perpetrator was trying to accomplish in the Crime.
Ex: People don't generally PERPETRATE a felony ["Purp" in order to go to jail].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Perpetrator that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: He COMMITTED each crime ["Manner" coldly and deliberately].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Perpetrator in order to accomplish the Crime.
Ex: He PERPETRATED each heinous act ["Mns" by calculating what would do the most damage and then finding a patsy to do it].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that the Perpetrator is responding to in their Crime.
Ex: Many of the poor COMMIT petty crimes ["Rsn" because they have no recourse].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the Crime was committed.
Ex: A murder PERPETRATED ["Time" at 1:08AM this morning] was not investigated until noon today.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Crime occurs.
Ex: We have jurisdiction over crimes COMMITTED ["Place" in Woodside County].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument used in committing the crime. Ex: Most crimes are COMMITTED ["Inst" with a firearm].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The frequency with which a Crime is committed.
Ex: The average serial killer COMMITS a crime ["Freq" every five years].

lexunit.name: commit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: perpetrate or carry out (a mistake, crime, or immoral act)

lexunit.name: perpetrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry out or commit (a harmful, illegal, or immoral action).

lexunit.name: crime.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an action which constitutes a serious offence against an individual or the state and is punishable by law.

lexunit.name: commission.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of committing a crime or offence.

frame.name: Quarreling
frame.definition: A group of Arguers (also expressible as Arguer1 and Arguer2) express incompatible opinions or beliefs about an Issue.

fe.name: Arguers
fe.definition: A group of people in an argument.

fe.name: Arguer1
fe.definition: A person who is arguing with Arguer2.

fe.name: Arguer2
fe.definition:
The person who is being argued with by Arguer1.
Ex: Why are you ARGUING ["Arg2" with us].

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition: The the thing the the Arguers are arguing over or about.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The frequency with which the Arguers have a disagreement.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A state of the Arguers, Arguer1, or Arguer2 which saliently affects the perception of the action.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that the Arguers spend in the altercation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the dispute which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Arguers that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: They SQUABBLED ["Manner" heatedly] long into the night.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action that the Arguers perform in order to quarrel with each other.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The equipment, language, or other entity that the Arguers use to pursue their argument.
Ex: When they couldn't get together, they BICKERED ["Med" over the phone].
Ex: Having them SQUABBLE ["Med" in french] is better than if I understood it.

fe.name: Amount_of_discussion
fe.definition:
The degree to which the argument has been finished.
Ex: If you don't believe me now, we'll just have to ARGUE it ["amo" out].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Arguers or Arguer1 hope to bring about.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Arguers quarrel

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the argument takes place.

lexunit.name: argue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: exchange diverging or opposite views heatedly.

lexunit.name: quarrel.v
lexunit.definition: COD: an angry argument or disagreement.

lexunit.name: bicker.v
lexunit.definition: COD: argue about petty and trivial matters.

lexunit.name: altercation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a noisy argument or disagreement.

lexunit.name: argument.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a heated exchange of diverging or opposite views.

lexunit.name: bickering.n
lexunit.definition: FN: pointless argument.

lexunit.name: disagreement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a quarrel.

lexunit.name: dispute.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a disagreement or argument

lexunit.name: disputation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: debate or argument.

lexunit.name: fight.v
lexunit.definition: COD: quarrel or argue

lexunit.name: fight.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an argument.

lexunit.name: quarrel.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an angry argument or disagreement.

lexunit.name: quibble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: argue about a trivial matter.

lexunit.name: row.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an acrimonious quarrel.

lexunit.name: row.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have a row.

lexunit.name: spat.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a petty quarrel.

lexunit.name: squabble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: engage in a squabble.

lexunit.name: squabble.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a trivial noisy quarrel.

lexunit.name: tiff.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a quarrel.

lexunit.name: wrangle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: engage in a wrangle.

lexunit.name: wrangling.n
lexunit.definition: FN: intense indecisive disagreement.

lexunit.name: wrangle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long and complicated dispute or argument.

frame.name: Judgment_direct_address
frame.definition: In this frame, a Communicator judges the Addressee and then communicates that appraisal directly to the Addressee. The judgment is given for a particular Reason or about a particular Topic.

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The Communicator communicates a judgment to the Addressee.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee is jduged by the Communicator and receives the message of approval or disapproval.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the subject on which the Addressee is being judged. Ex: ["Communicator" The teacher] SCOLDED ["Addressee" the children] ["Topic" about their meessy cookie eating].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is why the Communicator forms the type of judgment they form. Ex: ["Communicator" The principal] REBUKED ["Addressee" the student] ["Reason" for cheating on the exam].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The Medium identifies the physical or abstract entity in which the judgment is conveyed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the severity of the judgment.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator or Addressee.

fe.name: Grounds
fe.definition: The Grounds describes the basis for the judgment.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the way in which the judgment is communicated.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is the method employed to communicate the judgment.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Communicator admonishes the Addressee.
Ex: We were scolded ["Place" in the kitchen] by the biggest cook you've ever seen.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The point in time at which the Communicator berates or compliments the Addressee.
Ex: She complimented me ["Time" almost every morning] on my smart starched shirts.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The laudable or reprimandable status held by the Addressee.
Ex: He REBUKED them ["Role" as heathens and blasphemers].

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
An action or entity under the control of the Communicator that expresses the criticism or praise directed towards the Addressee.
Ex: Though she had killed him so long ago, she could still see his JEERING ["Expressor" smile].

lexunit.name: congratulate.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: say something to someone expressing praise

lexunit.name: scold.v
lexunit.definition: COD: angrily remonstrate with or rebuke.

lexunit.name: upbraid.v
lexunit.definition: COD: scold or reproach.

lexunit.name: thank.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express gratitude to.

lexunit.name: thanks.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an expression of gratitude.

lexunit.name: rebuke.v
lexunit.definition: COD: criticize or reprimand sharply.

lexunit.name: rebuke.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a sharp criticism.

lexunit.name: jeer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make rude and mocking remarks at someone.

lexunit.name: jeer.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a rude and mocking remark.

lexunit.name: compliment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a polite expression of praise or admiration.

lexunit.name: compliment.v
lexunit.definition: COD: politely congratulate or praise (someone)
