lexunit.name: chide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: scold or rebuke.

lexunit.name: chastise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reprimand severely.

lexunit.name: chastisement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: severe reprimand.

lexunit.name: castigation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a severe reprimand

lexunit.name: berate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: scold or criticize angrily.

lexunit.name: admonish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reprimand firmly

lexunit.name: admonishment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: reprimand.

lexunit.name: admonition.n
lexunit.definition: FN: warning about something that (the addressed individual) will probably do wrong.

lexunit.name: reprimand.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal expression of disapproval.

lexunit.name: reprimand.v
lexunit.definition: COD: address a reprimand to.

lexunit.name: castigatory.a
lexunit.definition: FN: serving to reprimand severely

lexunit.name: reproach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express to (someone) one's disapproval of or disappointment in their actions.

lexunit.name: harangue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: criticize at length in an aggressive and hectoring manner

lexunit.name: reprove.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rebuke or reprimand.

lexunit.name: reproof.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a rebuke or reprimand.

lexunit.name: take to task.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reprimand or criticize someone

lexunit.name: tell off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reprimand someone

lexunit.name: telling off.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an event of chastizement.

lexunit.name: tongue-lashing.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a loud or severe scolding.

frame.name: Cognitive_connection
frame.definition: A concept, Concept_1, is related causally or collocationally to another concept, Concept_2, by means of some Evidence. They may be related only under certain Circumstances or from a certain Point_of_view. The two concepts may be expressed collectively as associated Concepts. Any cognizer is deprofiled.

fe.name: Concept_1
fe.definition: The concept which is linked to Concept_2. Generally expressed as the external argument. Ex: ["C1" Smoking] is TIED to cancer.

fe.name: Concept_2
fe.definition: The concept which is tied to Concept_1. Generally expressed as a PP complement. Ex: Smoking is TIED ["C2" Cancer]..

fe.name: Point_of_view
fe.definition: The point of view from which the connection exists. Ex: Smoking is LINKED to cancer ["POV" in his mind].

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: The phenomenon that points to or proves the connection between Concept_1 and Concept_2. Ex: Eating long life noodles is CONNECTED to a long, healty life ["evi" by lab experiments conducted in Vietnam].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the connection exists.
Ex: ["Circumstances" In the lab], a person's weight and life expectancy are strongly CONNECTED.

fe.name: Concepts
fe.definition: The two concepts expressed jointly. Ex: ["Cs" Smoking and weight gain] are CONNECTED.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree of connection between the Concepts. Ex: These two incidents are ["Deg" closely] LINKED.

fe.name: Specification
fe.definition: A further specification on the linkage. Ex: These two concepts are ["Spec" innately] CONNECTED. Ex: Smoking and lung cancer are LINKED ["Spec" in some unknown way].

lexunit.name: linked.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a relationship or connection between people or things

lexunit.name: tied.a
lexunit.definition: FN: related to in some respect.

lexunit.name: connected.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being related in some respect

lexunit.name: related.a
lexunit.definition: FN: connotated or connected; reminding of

lexunit.name: associated.a
lexunit.definition: COD: closely related in the mind

lexunit.name: relationship.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the way in which two or more people or things are connected, or the state of being connected.

lexunit.name: identify with.v
lexunit.definition: FN: Experience a mental connection with something.

frame.name: Forming_relationships
frame.definition:
Partner_1 interacts with Partner_2 (also collectively expressable as Partners) to change their social relationship.
Ex: ["Partner_1" I] BEFRIENDED ["Partner_2" the little pony] by giving him a piece of apple.

fe.name: Partner_1
fe.definition: The individual who comes to form a relationship with Partner_2.

fe.name: Partner_2
fe.definition: The individual whose relationship with Partner_1 changes.

fe.name: Partners
fe.definition: The individuals whose relationship is changing.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action that Partner_1 or the Partners take in order to bring about the change in the relationship.
Ex: In the old days, a man could DIVORCE his wife ["Means" just by saying "I divorce you" three times].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the relationship changes.
Ex: She MARRIED Stephen ["Time" last summer].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Partner_1 or Partners that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A salient state of Partner_1, Partner_2, or Partners which affects the perception of the formation of relationship.
Ex: I BEFRIENDED her ["Dep" unaware of her past].

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
The length of time that the changed relationship status lasts.
Ex: Ekaterina BEFRIENDED him ["Dur" for a short while].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the relationship is formed. Ex: We MARRIED ["Place" in a gazebo].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Partners or Partner_1 hope to bring about by changing their status.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: ?Formally? and ?officially? plus maybe ?technically? and ?in law.? This FE indicates the legal- or "by rule" domain within which the Forming_relationship event is true or operational.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Forming_relationship event occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

lexunit.name: befriend.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make into a friend.

lexunit.name: woo.v
lexunit.definition: COD: try to gain the love of (a woman).

lexunit.name: betrothal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the promising of one person to wed another.

lexunit.name: betroth.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to promise someone in marriage to someone else.

lexunit.name: divorce.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the legal dissolution of a marriage.

lexunit.name: divorce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: legally dissolve one's marriage with.

lexunit.name: leave.v
lexunit.definition: COD: abandon (a spouse or partner).

lexunit.name: marriage.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the formal union of a man and a woman, typically as recognized by law, by which they become husband and wife.

lexunit.name: marry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take as one's wife or husband in marriage.

lexunit.name: marry_(into).v
lexunit.definition: COD: become a member of (a family) by marriage.

lexunit.name: separate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop living together as a couple.

lexunit.name: separation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: act in which a couple (generally married) ceases to cohabitate.

lexunit.name: tie the knot.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to get married

lexunit.name: wed.v
lexunit.definition: COD: marry.

lexunit.name: wedding.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a marriage ceremony, especially one including the associated celebrations.

lexunit.name: marriage_(into).n
lexunit.definition: FN: establishing a family relationship with by means of wedding the kin of.

lexunit.name: engagement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal agreement to get married.

frame.name: Stinginess
frame.definition:
In this frame, a Resource_controller is judged by a Judge (who is usually implicit) according to how freely they allow the Recipient access to their Resource. The Resource_controller may exhibit this attitude with an Expressor.
Ex: ["Resource_controller" John] is MEAN ["Resource" with money]. Ex: ["Resource_controller" Sally] has always been GENEROUS ["Recipient" to her children].

fe.name: Resource_controller
fe.definition: The Resource_Controller is the individual who controls access to the Resource. Ex: ["Resource_controller" Stampy] was STINGY with his peanuts.

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition: The Resource_controller controls the Recipient's access to the Resource. Ex: Surprising, Dad was STINGY ["Resource" with his inheritance]. Ex: Dragons often HOARD ["Resource" gold].

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The Recipient is the individual or individuals who receive or should receive the Resource from the Resource_controller. Ex: Mr. Burns is extremely MISERLY ["Recipient" towards his employees].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is how generous or stingy the Resource_controller is judged to be. Ex: John is ["Degree" very] GENEROUS.

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior is an action of the Resource_controller which is judged to be generous or stingy. Ex: It was GENEROUS of Jim ["Behavior" to have us over for dinner]. Ex: ["Behavior" Jim's dinner invitation] was very GENEROUS.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Resource_controller.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A characterization of the way in which the Resource_controller exhibits stinginess.
Ex: She was always ["Manner" sensitively] GENEROUS to me.

lexunit.name: generous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: freely giving more of something, especially money, than is strictly necessary or expected.

lexunit.name: stingy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: mean; ungenerous.

lexunit.name: mean.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unwilling to give or share money.

lexunit.name: lavish.a
lexunit.definition: COD: giving or given in profusion.

lexunit.name: lavish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bestow or cover in generous or extravagant quantities.

lexunit.name: miserliness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality characteristic of a miser; the state of being a miser

lexunit.name: miser.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who hoards wealth and spends very little.

lexunit.name: hoard.v
lexunit.definition: COD: amass and hide or store away.

lexunit.name: miserly.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of or characteristic of a miser.

lexunit.name: niggardliness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality or state of being niggardly

lexunit.name: niggardly.a
lexunit.definition: COD: ungenerous.

lexunit.name: ungenerous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not generous; mean.

frame.name: Expansion
frame.definition:
An Item changes its physical size. The Size_change of an Item may be explicitly indicated or characterized in terms of Initial_size and/or Result_size. In the default case, expansion is along all dimensions, but sometimes the Dimension of expansion is incorporated or made explicit.
Ex: ["Item" The pile of leaves] had SHRUNK ["Size_change" by about half] ["Time" after the first haul].
Ex: ["Item" The jeans] STRETCHED ["Size_change" a little].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Item whose size changes. Ex: ["Item" Joan's new sweater] SHRANK to a size that might fit a doll.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition:
Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.
Ex: The wall GREW ["Dim" in height]. Ex: The piglet had GROWN 6 inches ["Dim" in length].

fe.name: Group
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Group in which an Item changes size.
Ex: Tails LENGTHENED 10% ["Group" among rats more than 3 days old].

fe.name: Initial_size
fe.definition:
Initial_size is used for the size of the ITEM before any change occurs. It is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit. Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-_from_ Complement.
Ex: The glacier SHRANK ["Initial_size" from 1km square] to 400 square meters.

fe.name: Result_size
fe.definition:
Result_size is the size that the Item has after the event. It is typically expressed in a PP Complement headed by _to_.
Ex: The trees GROW ["Result_size" to 25 feet].

fe.name: Size_change
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Size_change of an Item.
Ex: A ["Size_change" 2-3cm] EXPANSION in width is required.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Rate of change of the value.
Ex: The balloon INFLATES ["Rate" about 2 cubic cm a minute].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Duration of time that the expansion takes.
Ex: The piglet had GROWN 6 inches ["Dur" over two months].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the expansion occurs.

fe.name: Co_variable
fe.definition:
Co_variable is the quantity that varies commensurately with the size of the Item, usually construed to be causally linked to the size.
Ex: The snake's belly EXPANDED ["Co_variable" with each mouse it ate].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE is used for any description of the Manner of the expansion including force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the expansion occurs. Ex: Joan's new sweater had SHRUNK ["Deg" completely].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is used for any expression that gives information about points on the scale of size that the Item traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement. Ex: The muscle tissue CONTRACTS ["Path" down] to less than half its original length.

lexunit.name: contract.v
lexunit.definition: COD: decrease in size, number, or range.

lexunit.name: contraction.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of an entity becoming smaller.

lexunit.name: enlarge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become larger.

lexunit.name: dilate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become wider, larger, or more open.

lexunit.name: enlargement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or state of enlarging or being enlarged.

lexunit.name: expand.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become larger or more extensive.

lexunit.name: shrink.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become or make smaller in size or amount; contract

lexunit.name: stretch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be made or be able to be made longer or wider without tearing or breaking.

lexunit.name: grow.v
lexunit.definition: FN: increase in size

lexunit.name: lengthen.v
lexunit.definition: FN: increase in size lengthwise

lexunit.name: expansion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or an instance of expanding.

lexunit.name: inflate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: expand because of being filled with air or gas

lexunit.name: swell.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become larger or rounder in size, especially as a result of an accumulation of fluid.

lexunit.name: explosive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an increase) sudden and dramatic.

frame.name: Usefulness
frame.definition: An Entity aids in the successful completion of a Purpose. Its Degree of utility may also be expressed. Some of the lexical units in this frame (e.g. _great, good_) can only express permanent, generic states of the Entity.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The item which is useful for some purpose.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The kind of task which is promoted by the use or presence of the Entity.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The amount that the presence of the Entity aids in the completion of the (desirable) Purpose.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: This Frame Element marks expressions of a DOMAIN or parameter with respect to which the ENTITY is useful.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Entity is useful for a Purpose.

lexunit.name: good.a
lexunit.definition: COD: appropriate.

lexunit.name: effective.a
lexunit.definition: COD: producing a desired or intended result.

lexunit.name: excellent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extremely good; outstanding

lexunit.name: outstanding.a
lexunit.definition: COD: exceptionally good

lexunit.name: superb.a
lexunit.definition: COD: excellent

lexunit.name: wonderful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extremely good, pleasant, or remarkable.

lexunit.name: fantastic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extraordinarily good or attractive

lexunit.name: fine.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of very high quality.

lexunit.name: tremendous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extremely good or impressive; excellent.

lexunit.name: terrific.a
lexunit.definition: COD: excellent.

lexunit.name: marvellous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extremely good or pleasing.

lexunit.name: great.a
lexunit.definition: COD: excellent.

lexunit.name: super.a
lexunit.definition: COD: excellent.

lexunit.name: splendid.a
lexunit.definition: COD: excellent.

lexunit.name: useful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be used for a practical purpose or in several ways.

lexunit.name: utility.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being useful, profitable, or beneficial.

lexunit.name: use.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: the usefulness of an Entity with respect to some Purpose.

lexunit.name: value.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the usefulness of an Entity with respect to some Purpose.

lexunit.name: valuable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: extremely useful or important.

lexunit.name: perfect.a
lexunit.definition: FE: absolutely suited (for a purpose).

lexunit.name: ideal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: most suitable; perfect.

lexunit.name: ineffective.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not producing a desired or intended result.

lexunit.name: work.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be effective in performing as it is designed to is expected to do.

frame.name: Congregating
frame.definition: In this frame a group of Individuals come together to form a Configuration. The Individuals or the Configuration may be expressed as the external argument of the predicates in this frame. In an alternative construal, a grammatically more prominent Party_1 congregates with a Party_2, expressed as an oblique phrase. If this asymmetric construal is chosen, Purpose relates only to Party_1. Ex: The congregating happens in a certain Place and at a certain Time. Ex: Ex: ["Configuration" The crowd] ASSEMBLED ["Place" in the courtyard]. Ex: ["Individuals" The architects] CONGREGATED ["Place" in the lobby].

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: The Individuals are self-movers who come together.

fe.name: Configuration
fe.definition: The Configuration describes the resulting formation of the individuals. Ex: ["con" The crowd] ASSEMBLED ["Place" on the streets of Paris].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means descibes the way in which the Individuals accomplish the congregating.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the congregating occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the congregating occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Configuration plans to engage in upon assembly.
Ex: Chaucer's pligrims ASSEMBLED ["Pur" for their journey to Canterbury].

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition:
The position in a series of iterations that the current congregating event occupies .
Ex: The group CAME TOGETHER ["iter" the first time] in 1984. Ex: The crowd ASSEMBLED ["iter" again] the next day

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Individuals come together to form an Configuration.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of congregating which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Individuals or Configuration that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: Retired Sainsbury employees CAME TOGETHER ["Manner" in grand style] in March and April to reminisce and share afternoon tea in the sumptuous surroundings of the Royal Lancaster Hotel .

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: A Topic of a discussion that may occur between the Individuals.

fe.name: Party_1
fe.definition:
Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the congregating event.
Ex: ["pa1" Our group] MET with theirs in the plaza.

fe.name: Party_2
fe.definition:
A grammatically less prominent participant in the congregating event.
Ex: Our group MET ["pa2" with theirs] in the plaza.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

lexunit.name: congregate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (of people or autonomously moving objects) gather into a crowd or mass

lexunit.name: assemble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come or bring together.

lexunit.name: gang together.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form a group or gang

lexunit.name: band.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: people get together to form a group with a single identity

lexunit.name: band together.v
lexunit.definition: FN: people get together to form a group with a single identity

lexunit.name: come together.v
lexunit.definition: FN: converge

lexunit.name: convene.v
lexunit.definition: COD: assemble for a common purpose

lexunit.name: gather.v
lexunit.definition: FN: assemble; come together

lexunit.name: throng.v
lexunit.definition: COD: flock or be present in great numbers.

lexunit.name: meet.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to come into the company of, come together with

frame.name: Become_silent
frame.definition:
In this frame a Speaker ceases speaking, sometimes about a particular Topic. An Expressor may also be indicated. Ex: The words of this frame are very frequently used imperatively, to the extent that certain words and phrases (_not another word, silence, shhh_) can only be used this way.
Ex: Finally, ["Speaker" Jan] SHUT UP ["Topic" about his car accident]. Ex: ["Expressor" The children's laughter] QUIETED DOWN. Ex: Somehow, ["Speaker" he] managed to HOLD ["Speaker" his] TONGUE.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker has previously been speaking but has now stopped. Ex: ["Speaker" The children] finally QUIETED DOWN.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the subject which the Speaker had been speaking about. Ex: Mark SHUT UP ["Topic" about the book].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location where the becoming silent occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the becoming silent occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reasonis why the Speaker ceases speaking.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: The Expressor is theSpeaker's voice or other communicative noise emitted by the Speaker. Ex: ["Expressor" The excited chatter] HUSHED.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which the quietening occurs.

lexunit.name: button_lip.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stop speaking and remain silent

lexunit.name: hold_tongue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remain silent

lexunit.name: hush.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become quiet.

lexunit.name: hush_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: suppress public mention of something.

lexunit.name: quiet.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become quiet.

lexunit.name: quiet_down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become quiet

lexunit.name: shush.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be quiet.

lexunit.name: shut_up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop or cause someone to stop talking.

lexunit.name: stow_it.v
lexunit.definition: FN: refrain from speaking any further

lexunit.name: not_another_word.v
lexunit.definition: FN: refrain from saying anything else

lexunit.name: seal_lips.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: refrain from speaking on a topic

lexunit.name: silence.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (adjective used imperatively) be quiet.

lexunit.name: sh.intj
lexunit.definition: COD: used to call for silence.

lexunit.name: quieten.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cease making noise

lexunit.name: pipe_down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lower one's volume

lexunit.name: quiet.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being silent. Often occurs with verbs (keeping, remaining, staying).

frame.name: Telling
frame.definition: A Speaker addresses an Addressee with a Message, which may be indirectly referred to as a Topic.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the sentient entity that produces the Message. Ex: ["Speaker" Bill] TOLD me that he would come to the party.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee receives the Message from the Speaker.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition: The Message is the communication produced by the Speaker. Ex: The authorities INFORMED me ["Message" that my brother had been arrested]. Ex: I TOLD him ["Message" a bedtime story].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is a general description of the content of the Message. Ex: Leroy TOLD his mother ["Topic" about his arrest].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes the way in which the Speaker delivers the Message.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means describes the way the Speaker accomplishes the task of giving the Addressee the Message.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This frame element is the Medium in which the Message is expressed.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Speaker informs the Addressee of the Message.
Ex: Even when we had a size problem they INFORMED me ["Time" right away] and everything worked out great.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Speaker informs the Addressee of the Message.
Ex: She looked at it for a few moments, thinking of Mark Smeaton and what he had TOLD her ["Place" on the steps of City Hall].

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: ?Formally? and ?officially? plus maybe ?technically? and ?in law.?

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the telling event.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

lexunit.name: tell.v
lexunit.definition: COD: communicate information to.

lexunit.name: inform.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give facts or information to

lexunit.name: advise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: recommend, inform

lexunit.name: apprise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform; tell

lexunit.name: assure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tell someone something positively in order to dispel potential doubts.

lexunit.name: confide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tell someone about a secret or private matter in confidence

lexunit.name: notify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inform, typically in a formal or official manner.

lexunit.name: notification.n
lexunit.definition: FN: notifying, informing, typically in a formal or official manner

lexunit.name: assurance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a positive declaration intended to give confidence

frame.name: Change_posture
frame.definition: A Protagonist changes the overall postion and posture of the body.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the change in posture which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Protagonist that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The individual whose posture changes.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Protagonist's state throughout the time they are changing posture.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
The place or setting in which the Protagonist's change of posture takes place.
Ex: The supplicant SAT down ["Location" outside the office] and waited for the mayor.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Protagonist changes posture.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The final state of the Protagonist after the change of posture.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path is used for expressions that indicate the trajectory of motion without referring to the Source or the Goal of motion.
Ex: She LEANED ["Path" through the service door] Ex: Tim Thomas LEANED ["Path" forwards]

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
This FE is used for any expressions that indicate the endpoint of the posture change. Often this is the place that provides support for the posture.
Ex: John LEANED ["Goal" against the wall] and closed his eyes

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Source is used for expressions that indicate the starting point of the change of posture.
Ex: Charles STOOD UP ["Source" from his armchair]

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
This FE is used for expressions that indicate a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the Goal of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body. Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Protagonist, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.
Ex: Smithers LEANED ["Direction" forward] to grab the folder on the far side.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which a Protagonist assumes a posture.
Ex: Sunil BENT down ["Purpose" to pick up the newspaper]

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
This FE is used for expressions that indicate the extent to which the body (part) moves during the change of posture.
Ex: BEND back ["Distance" as far as you can]

fe.name: Point_of_contact
fe.definition:
The part of the body that provides support to the Protagonist in holding the posture.
Ex: Smithers CROUCHED down ["Point_of_contact" on his haunces]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Protagonist whereby they achieve the change of posture.

lexunit.name: bend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: incline the body downwards; stoop.

lexunit.name: stoop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bend one's head or body forwards and downwards, or have the head and shoulders habitually bent forwards.

lexunit.name: stand.v
lexunit.definition: FN: rise to an upright position on one's feet.

lexunit.name: stand up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: assume a standing position, typically from lying or sitting

lexunit.name: kneel.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fall or rest on a knee or the knees.

lexunit.name: kneel down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fall or come to rest on one's knees

lexunit.name: lie down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: assume a horizontal position on a supporting surface

lexunit.name: lie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be in or assume a horizontal or resting position on a supporting surface.

lexunit.name: sit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be or cause to be in a position in which one's weight is supported by one's buttocks rather than one's feet and one's back is upright.

lexunit.name: sit down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: assume a position in which one's weight is supported by one's buttocks rather than one's feet or back

lexunit.name: sit up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move from a lying or slouching to a sitting position

lexunit.name: squat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: crouch or sit with the knees bent and the heels close to or touching the buttocks or thighs.

lexunit.name: squat down.v
lexunit.definition: COD: crouch or sit with the knees bent and the heels close to or touching the buttocks or thighs

lexunit.name: lean.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be in or move into a sloping position.

lexunit.name: sprawl.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sit, lie, or fall with one's limbs spread out in an ungainly way.

lexunit.name: sprawl out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lie, or fall down with arms and legs spread out in an ungainly way

lexunit.name: crouch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: adopt a position where the knees are bent and the upper body is brought forward and down.

lexunit.name: crouch down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: assume from a standing position a posture where the knees are bent and the upper body is brought forward and down

lexunit.name: huddle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: curl one's body into a small space.

lexunit.name: hunch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: raise (one's shoulders) and bend the top of one's body forward, or sit or stand in such a position.

lexunit.name: slouch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stand, move, or sit in a lazy, drooping way.

lexunit.name: kneel up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: get on one's knees from a sitting or lying position

lexunit.name: hunch up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: assume a posture of sitting or standing with one's shoulders raised and the top of one's body bent forward

lexunit.name: rise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: get up from lying, sitting, or kneeling

lexunit.name: drop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sink to or towards the ground.

frame.name: Amalgamation
frame.definition:
These words refer to Parts merging to form a Whole. (The Parts may also be encoded as Part_1 and Part_2.) There is a symmetrical relationship between the components that undergo the process, and afterwards the Parts are consumed and are no longer distinct entities that are easily discernable or separable in the Whole.
Ex: ["Parts" The two droplets] MERGE, and then travel down the windowpane even faster.

fe.name: Parts
fe.definition: The entities that merge to form a single Whole.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
The single, undifferentiated entity that is the result of the amalgamation.
Ex: They had all just MERGED ["Whole" into one big file].

fe.name: Part_1
fe.definition:
The prominent entity that combines withPart_2 to form a Whole.
Ex: ["Part_1" The single smaller soul] MERGES with the Ur-soul.

fe.name: Part_2
fe.definition:
The less focussed-upon entity that the Part_1 merges with.
Ex: The single smaller soul MERGES ["Part_2" with the Ur-soul].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the thoroughness of the mixing job, i.e. to what degree the resulting Whole is undifferentiated.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In this frame, it is also deemed to include modification indicating the speed of the event.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Parts after the amalgamation.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Parts become amalgamated into a Whole

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the amalgamation occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of Part_1 or Parts.

lexunit.name: merger.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the combining of two things, especially companies, into one.

lexunit.name: amalgamate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: combine or unite to form one organization or structure.

lexunit.name: blend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: mix and combine (something) with something else.

lexunit.name: combine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: unite; merge; unite to form a compound

lexunit.name: commingle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: poetic/literary mix; blend

lexunit.name: fuse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: join, blend, or coalesce to form a single entity.

lexunit.name: intermix.v
lexunit.definition: COD: mix together. with obj.

lexunit.name: meld.v
lexunit.definition: COD: blend

lexunit.name: merge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: combine or be combined to form one.

lexunit.name: unify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or become united or uniform.

lexunit.name: unite.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come or bring together for a common purpose or to form a whole.

lexunit.name: band_together.v
lexunit.definition: FN: people forming a group, usually for some specific purpose

lexunit.name: come together.v
lexunit.definition: FN: coalesce to make a whole

frame.name: Attention
frame.definition:
This frame concerns a Perceiver's state of readiness to process and consider impressions of a Figure within a Ground. It is often unknown to the Perceiver whether or not the Figure exists within the Ground. Alternatively, the Expressor may be expressed as showing signs of the Perceiver's state of attentiveness.
Ex: Legislator tells ["Perceiver" consumers] to _be_ ALERT ["Figure" to dioxin levels].
Ex: They demand an ATTENTIVE ["Expressor" gaze], a careful accounting of parts.

fe.name: Perceiver
fe.definition: The individual that pays attention to the Ground.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: The sensory field or subset of a sensory field that the Perceiver is attending to.

fe.name: Figure
fe.definition: The entity that the Perceiver is specifically focussing on within the Ground.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The amount of attention that the Perceiver is paying to the Figure or Ground.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The situation within which the Perceiver is alert.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Perceiver that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: An entity (or event) associated with a Perceiver that gives evidence for a Perceiver's attentiveness.

lexunit.name: alert.a
lexunit.definition: FN: quick to notice and respond

lexunit.name: attend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pay attention to.

lexunit.name: attention.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the mental faculty of considering or taking notice

lexunit.name: attentive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: paying close attention.

lexunit.name: closely.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: with full attention.

lexunit.name: close.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of observation or examination) done in a careful and thorough way

lexunit.name: keep_a_eye_(on).a
lexunit.definition: FN: closely watch.

frame.name: Locating
frame.definition:
A Perceiver determines the Location of a Sought_entity within a Ground.
Ex: ["Perceiver" Kim] FOUND ["Sought_entity" his hat] ["Location" on the far side].

fe.name: Perceiver
fe.definition:
The individual that determines the Location of the Sought_entity.
Ex: ["Perceiver" I] finally FOUND the peanut underneath the couch cusion.

fe.name: Sought_entity
fe.definition: The entity that the Perceiver succeeds in finding.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
The position of the Sought_entity.
Ex: I FOUND him ["Loc" under the bed].

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The general set of entities that the Perceiver examined in order to find the Sought_entity.
Ex: Sam LOCATED the Imperial regal ["Ground" among the coins in his pocket] and passed it to the boy.

lexunit.name: locate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: discover the exact place or position of.

lexunit.name: find.v
lexunit.definition: COD: discover by chance or deliberately.

frame.name: Being_born
frame.definition: This frame concerns the inception of the life of a Child, generally human, at a particular Time and Place. The Relatives may also be mentioned.

fe.name: Child
fe.definition: Child identifies the new self-motile creature.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the birth occurs, generally expressed as a date or a year.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Child enters the world.

fe.name: Relatives
fe.definition: The individuals that the Child is related to, including the male and female individuals that come together to produce a Child (the parents), as well those who are related to them by birth or marriage.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Child as it enters the world.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The way in which the Child leaves the womb; this FE is typically only filled by phrases such as _by natural birth_ or _by Caesarian_.

lexunit.name: come into the world.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be born.

lexunit.name: born.v
lexunit.definition: FN: existing as a result of birth.

frame.name: Making_faces
frame.definition: An Agent makes a particular facial expression, generally in response to some Internal_cause (generally an emotional state). Sometimes the Body_part involved in the expression is mentioned in lieu of the Agent.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that assumes a particular facial expression.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotion or other mental state that leads the Agent to assume a facial expression.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition: The particular part of the face that the Agent moves into a facial expression.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The amount to which the expression on the face of the Agent matches the prototypical image for the indicated facial expression.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Intended_perceiver
fe.definition:
The individual that the Agent intends to see the facial expression; often the Intended_perceiver is also the focus of the emotional Internal_cause of the Agent.
Ex: Why don't you SMILE ["Intended_perceiver" at me] more often?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The point in time at which the change in facial_expression takes place.

fe.name: Location_of_expressor
fe.definition:
The location relative to some viewer (often the Intended_perceiver) at which the Agent makes an expression.
Ex: He SMILED up at me ["Location_of_expressor" from the bottom of the well].

fe.name: Path_of_gaze
fe.definition: A path expression that describes a line from the Agent to the Intended_perceiver.

fe.name: Cognate_event
fe.definition: The facial expression of the Agent.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Agent during the event.

fe.name: External_cause
fe.definition: An event experienced by the Agent that leads them to make an expression.

lexunit.name: frown.v
lexunit.definition: COD: furrow one's brows in an expression indicating disapproval, displeasure, or concentration.

lexunit.name: grimace.v
lexunit.definition: FN: contort one's face in an expressive way

lexunit.name: grin.v
lexunit.definition: COD: smile broadly

lexunit.name: pout.v
lexunit.definition: COD: push one's lips or bottom lip forward as an expression of petulant annoyance or in order to make oneself look sexually attractive.

lexunit.name: scowl.v
lexunit.definition: COD: frown in an angry or bad-tempered way.

lexunit.name: smile.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form one's features into a pleased, friendly, or amused expression, with the corners of the mouth turned up.

lexunit.name: smirk.v
lexunit.definition: COD: smile in an irritatingly smug or silly way.

frame.name: Communicate_categorization
frame.definition:
A Speaker communicates a message stating an Item's membership in a Category, i.e., asserts that the Item has the defining characteristics of the Category. Alternatively, the message is conceived as communicated by a Medium.
Ex: ["Speaker" He] DEPICTED ["Item" his involvement] ["Category" as merely peripheral].
Ex: ["Medium" The first half of the book] PORTRAYS ["Item" Bragg's mother] ["Category" as a beautiful and heartbroken woman].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The individual that communates the message concerning the Category of an Item.

fe.name: Category
fe.definition: The class of entities with characteristics that match those of the Item according to the portrayal of the Speaker.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The entity that the Speaker portrays as belonging to a Category.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action taken by the Speaker through which they communicate that the Item fits into a particular Category.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The piece of text in which a Speaker communicates their categorization of the Item.
Ex: However, ["Medium" "A Brief History of Medicine"] CHARACTERIZES influenza as the most deadly plague, overall.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The point in time at which the Speaker makes a characterization of the Item.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Speaker characterizes the Item

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances under which the categorization is made.

fe.name: Criteria
fe.definition: The characteristics of an Item that fit the defining characteristics of a Category, and thus serve as the basis of the Speakers characterization of the Item.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Speaker that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

lexunit.name: make out.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: to describe or represent as

lexunit.name: characterize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: describe the distinctive character of

lexunit.name: depict.v
lexunit.definition: FN: characterize pictorally

lexunit.name: depiction.n
lexunit.definition: COD: depiction is a derivative of depict

lexunit.name: describe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a detailed account in words of.

lexunit.name: description.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a spoken or written account of a person, object, or event.

lexunit.name: portray.v
lexunit.definition: COD: describe in a particular way.

lexunit.name: represent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: portray in a particular way

lexunit.name: representation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an image, model, or other depiction of something.

lexunit.name: define.v
lexunit.definition: COD: state or describe exactly the nature, scope, or meaning of.

lexunit.name: definition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal statement of the exact nature, scope, or meaning of something.

lexunit.name: redefine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: define again or differently.

lexunit.name: redefinition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: redefinition is a derivative of redefine

lexunit.name: characterization.n
lexunit.definition: COD: characterization is a derivative of characterize

lexunit.name: treat.v
lexunit.definition: FN: consider or regard in a certain way

lexunit.name: paint.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a description of (something).

lexunit.name: hail.v
lexunit.definition: FN: describe with praise

lexunit.name: cast.v
lexunit.definition: FN: portray

frame.name: Inchoative_change_of_temperature
frame.definition:
In this frame, the temperature of an Item changes. An Initial_temperature, Final_temperature, or Temperature_change can also be indicated.
Ex: The house had COOLED OFF by a few more degrees by midnight, and we finally managed to eat a bite.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The entity whose temperature changes.

fe.name: Initial_temperature
fe.definition: The temperature that the Item has prior to the event.

fe.name: Final_temperature
fe.definition: The temperature of the Item after the event.

fe.name: Temperature_change
fe.definition: The amount of difference between the Initial_temperature and the Final_temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Hot_cold_source
fe.definition: The Hot_cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event or state-of-affairs that leads to the change in temperature of the Item.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Container that holds the Item whose temperature is being changed.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Item during the temperature change.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The span of time in which the Item is changing temperature.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the change in temperature occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Item changes temperature.

fe.name: Sub_region
fe.definition: A portion of the Item which is affected by the temperature change.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which the Item changes temperature.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the temperature change occurs

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Item that results from being chilled.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: chill.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make cold.

lexunit.name: cool.v
lexunit.definition: FN: reach or approach a fairly low temperature

lexunit.name: heat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make hot or warm

lexunit.name: refrigerate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: subject (food or drink) to cold in order to chill or preserve it.

lexunit.name: reheat.v
lexunit.definition: COD: heat again.

lexunit.name: warm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make warm

lexunit.name: cool off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause a relative decrease in temperature

frame.name: Finish_competition
frame.definition:
A Competition comes to an end, with a Competitor tying, winning, or losing against an Opponent (or opponents) according to their Score. (In the symmetrical situation of a tie, the Competitor and Opponent may be jointly mentioned as Competitors.) According to the Score that the Competitor and Opponent have acheived, they may receive a Rank or a Prize. The Margin may also be mentioned.
Ex: Unbelievable--["Competitor" he] LOST ["Prize" the gold medal] ["Margin" by just .02 points]! Ex: Looks like it will came to a DRAW ["Competitors" between Woods and Stephenson].

fe.name: Competitor
fe.definition: The individual involved in the Competition.

fe.name: Opponent
fe.definition: The individual that the Competitor has been competing against.

fe.name: Competitors
fe.definition: The individuals who compete against each other.

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Competitors afterward.

fe.name: Margin
fe.definition: The amount by which the Competitor's and Opponent's Scores differ.

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: The rank (according to Score) that a Competitor acheives.

fe.name: Prize
fe.definition: A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Competitor according to Score or Rank.

fe.name: Competition
fe.definition: The event in which the Competitors compete with each other.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Competitor that results in the outcome of the Competition.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Competition which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Competitor that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Competition takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Competition takes place.

fe.name: Venue
fe.definition: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition. Ex: The Mets WON against the Yankees ["Venue" at Shea Stadium].

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: win.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a victory, especially in a game or contest

lexunit.name: victorious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having won a victory; triumphant

lexunit.name: winner.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing that wins.

lexunit.name: victory.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of defeating an enemy or opponent in a battle, game, or competition.

lexunit.name: lose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fail to win.

lexunit.name: loss.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a defeat in sport.

lexunit.name: tie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: achieve the same score or ranking as another competitor.

lexunit.name: tie.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a result in a game or match in which two or more competitors have tied

lexunit.name: victor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who defeats an enemy or opponent in a battle, game, or competition

lexunit.name: draw.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a game or match that ends with the scores even.

lexunit.name: show.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to finish third in a race

frame.name: Cause_to_make_noise
frame.definition: An Agent manipulates a Sound_maker or a Cause causes the Sound_maker to emit a sound. Ex: ["Agent" The monks] would RING ["Sound_maker" the bell] until sundown.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individual that manipulates a Sound_maker so that it makes Noise.
Ex: ["Agent" You] can RING the bell as often as you'd like.

fe.name: Sound_maker
fe.definition: The entity that produces the Noise, as a result of the action of the Agent.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: The Subregion is the sublocation of the Sound_maker from which the sound is emitting.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The location from which the noise emanates toward an (implicit) perceiver.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of one of the primary participants (either Agent or Sound_maker) during the course of the sound-making event.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action directly due to the Agent or Cause that results in the Sound_maker emitting noise..

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The inanimate force of nature that causes the Sound_maker to produce noise.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The change or state of affairs preceding the event, deemed to have caused the event.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs or action that the Agent wishes to bring about by performing the action.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the noise is produced.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the sound is produced.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times the Sound_maker makes noise per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: Used for expressions that indicate the number of times Sound_maker makes noise.

lexunit.name: blare.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to make a loud harsh sound

lexunit.name: blast.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce loud continuous music or noise.

lexunit.name: clang.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to make a resonant metallic sound

lexunit.name: creak.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to make a harsh high-pitched sound when moving or applying pressure

lexunit.name: peep.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make a peep.

lexunit.name: tinkle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to make a light, clear ringing sound.

lexunit.name: play.v
lexunit.definition: FN: manipulate (a device, generally an instrument or storage medium) so as to produce musical sounds.

lexunit.name: ringer.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who rings something.

lexunit.name: ring.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to make a clear resonant or vibrating sound

lexunit.name: honk.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to emit a honk.

lexunit.name: toot.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to make a toot.

frame.name: Measure_by_action
frame.definition:
This frame involves words that provide a measure for some undelimited (mass) Entity by referring to an Event that a prototypical quantity (or duration) of the Entity stereotypically participates in. The Entity is not necessarily a physical entity, but may instead be an undelimited type of event (such as a noise, or an activity).
Ex: He put two ["Event" SPLASHES] ["Entity" of cologne] on his face. Ex: Sorry--there's only ["Count" two] ["Event" BITES] ["Entity" of cake] left. Ex: Add a ["Event" PINCH] ["Entity" of salt].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: An abstract or concrete undelimited entity that is measured by the Event.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The event that a delimitable quantity or duration of an Entity participates in.

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of iterations of the Event.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: splash.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a small quantity of liquid that has splashed on to a surface

lexunit.name: bite.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a piece cut off by biting.

lexunit.name: pinch.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an amount of an ingredient that can be held between fingers and thumb.

frame.name: Friction
frame.definition:
A Theme moves on or against the surface of a Static_object. (Alternatively, Themes moves against each other simultaneously). The Theme exerts pressure on the surface and experiences resistance to its movement.
Ex: ["Theme" Smithers' boots] SCRAPED ["Static_object" on the floor].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The physical entity which moves over the suface of the Static_object
Ex: ["Theme" His backpack] GRATED against the wall.

fe.name: Static_object
fe.definition:
A non-moving physical object over a surface of which the Theme moves.
Ex: The spout GRATES ["Static_object" against the tap]

fe.name: Themes
fe.definition:
Two moving entities whose surfaces move against each other.
Ex: He felt ["Themes" his teeth] SCRAPE against the plaster

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The way in which the Theme moves against the Static_object
Ex: is steel helmet GRATED ["Manner" gently] against the top of the door

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The setting in which the motion of the Theme happens
Ex: ["Place" In the hallway] a key GRATED in the lock

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The amount of friction produced in the Theme's motion.
Ex: The steel helment GRATED ["Degree" faintly] against the top of the

lexunit.name: grate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make an unpleasant rasping sound.

lexunit.name: squeal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to make or utter a long, high-pitched cry or noise

lexunit.name: scrunch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: a loud crunching noise.

lexunit.name: screech.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make a high-pitched, shrill sound

lexunit.name: scrape.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rub or cause to rub against a rough or hard surface.

lexunit.name: rasp.v
lexunit.definition: FN: scrape harshly over or against a surface or object

frame.name: Absorb_heat
frame.definition:
An Entity (generally food) is exposed to a Heat_source whose Temperature may also be specified. Generally, the Entity undergoes some sort of change as a result of this process.
Ex: ["ent" Bacon] was FRYING ["Container" in the pan], and a great heap of eggs already lay steaming on a plate. Ex: If ["ent" it] COOKS ["tem" at 400] ["dur" for an hour], it 'll be nothing but a pile of ash!

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity (often a food item) that absorbs heat.
Ex: ["Entity" Bacon] FRYING in the pan and scenting the air

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
The Container that holds the Entity that absorbs the heat.
Ex: Five fat sausages were FRYING ["Container" in the pan]

fe.name: Heat_source
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the object that directly supplies heat to theEntity.
Ex: Food was placed to SIZZLE ["Heat_source" on the barbecue ].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the heat application occurs.
Ex: ["Place" In the kitchen] the meat SIZZLED in the oven and a big pan of potatoes stood on the hob

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is a substance through which heat is absorbed by the Entity.
Ex: The golden meat was SIMMERING ["Medium" in a sauce that seemed lifted straight out of a French coq au vin rouge]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the cooking event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: Get them FRYING ["Manner" slowly], iin a spoonful of olive oil.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the heat absorption takes place.
Ex: ["Time" Five minutes ago]the eggs weren't BOILING yet.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The thing or state-of-affairs that leads to the Entity being heated and undergoing change.
Ex: The liquid nitrogen was SIMMERING ["cau" from the heat].

fe.name: Temperature
fe.definition:
The temperature that the Entity stays at, resulting in change.
Ex: No, that kind of batter should BAKE ["tem" at a lower temperature].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Entity is exposed to heat.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason why a state of affairs is caused or maintained by an (implicit) agent.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes the Entity as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The final state of affairs after the absorbing heat event has finished.
Ex: The lobster BOILED ["Result" to death].

lexunit.name: sizzle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make a hissing sound in or as if in roasting or frying

lexunit.name: fry.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be cooked in hot fat or oil, or get very hot by exposure to a heat source

lexunit.name: bake.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to be cooked by dry heat, especially in an oven and as food

lexunit.name: simmer.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to cook slowly in a liquid just below the boiling point in a closed dish or pan

lexunit.name: cook.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of food) be heated so as to reach an edible state.

lexunit.name: stew.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to become boiled slowly or by simmering heat

lexunit.name: boil.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to be cooked by immersing in a boiling liquid

lexunit.name: scorch.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become burnt and crispy on the surface or edges.

lexunit.name: sear.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become burned by intense heat, usually from a metal Heat_source

lexunit.name: singe.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be burnt lightly or superficially, usually by a flame.

frame.name: Sounds
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with the percepts that vibrations which travel through the air or another medium produce in hearing organs. Sounds are a subtype of sensation. In talking about sounds, speakers often provide information about how the sound was produced. A Noisy_event may be mentioned which gives rise to the sound. Alternatively, the sound may be attributed to a Sound_source, which is construed as a point source emitting the sound. A further possible specification of what gives rise to the sound is for speakers to talk about two physical entities coming into contact by motion, resulting in either friction or impact.

fe.name: Noisy_event
fe.definition: An event during which sound is produced.

fe.name: Sound_source
fe.definition:
An entity that is construed as a single point source emitting sound.
Ex: He woke up because of the BLARE ["Sound_source" of a car horn].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
One of two entities which is construed as moving relative to the other, resulting in either friction or impact. This entity is given greater syntactic prominence--it is either a possessor or an of-complement of the noun phrase head.
Ex: He heard the CLANG ["Theme" of metal] on metal , and a ricochet whined viciously past his head

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
An entity construed as stationary on or against which the Theme moves, resulting in either friction or impact. This entity is given less grammatical prominence compared to the Theme and is usually encoded in a spatial prepositional phrase.
Ex: He heard the CLANG of metal ["Ground" on metal] , and a ricochet whined viciously past his head .

fe.name: Themes
fe.definition:
Two entities that are both moving against each other, resulting in either friction or impact.
Ex: The sound of voices and the CLINK ["Themes" of glasses] was like music to her ears

fe.name: Location_of_sound_source
fe.definition:
The place from which the sound emanates.
Ex: There followed a small silence that was interrupted by a distant CLATTERof metal["" from the ward].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which sound is produced. This FE differs from Location_of_sound_source in that it does not highlight the sound's spreading from its source to the perceiver's location, which is usually indicated by the preposition "from".
Ex: There was a CLATTER of running feet ["Place" in the street outside].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The noise-making may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, that is the mental or emotional state of an animate Sound_source.
Ex: She checked a GIGGLE ["Internal_cause" of hysteria]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Certain properties of the sound relating to its production, loudness, etc may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of a sounds as such: loudly, shrilly, etc.
Ex: The Brigadier had heard the ["Manner" faint] TINKLE of sheepbells

fe.name: Component_sound
fe.definition:
The sound percept may be characterized in terms of Component_sounds.
Ex: The lunch itself was held in a huge room and there was a constant BABBLE ["Component_sound" of noise]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Expressions that indicate the loudness of the sound.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE idntifies the Reason that the Sound_source produces the sound. Generally, this is some external stimulus that prompts the Sound_source to make noise.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path along which the sound travels away from the Sound_source.
Ex: As he opened the throttle, the roar of the BMW's engine bit into the moan and HOWL of the wind ["Path" across the culvert's mouth]

lexunit.name: babble.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the sound of babbling.

lexunit.name: bark.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the sharp explosive cry of a dog, fox, or seal.

lexunit.name: beep.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a short, high-pitched sound emitted by electronic equipment or a vehicle horn.

lexunit.name: bellow.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a loud, deep shout or sound.

lexunit.name: blare.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a loud, harsh sound.

lexunit.name: blast.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a single loud note of a horn or whistle.

lexunit.name: bleat.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a weak, wavering cry made by, or similar to that made by a sheep or goat

lexunit.name: boom.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a loud, deep, resonant sound.

lexunit.name: bray.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the loud, harsh cry of a donkey.

lexunit.name: burble.n
lexunit.definition: FN: continuous murmuring noise

lexunit.name: buzz.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a low, continuous humming or murmuring sound, made by or similar to that made by an insect

lexunit.name: cackle.n

frame.name: Sound_movement
frame.definition: A Sound emitted by a Sound_source, which construed as a single point, moves along a Path. Rather than the Sound_source itself, the Location_of_sound_source may be mentioned. Essentially, this frame denotes the (semi-)fictive motion of the the Sound. Given the spreading nature of sound vibrations, it is not surprising that there usually is no expression of any particular goal.

fe.name: Sound
fe.definition:
A percept produced in hearing organs by vibrations which travel through the air or another medium.
Ex: ["Sound" Laughter] ECHOED through the halls

fe.name: Location_of_sound_source
fe.definition:
The location of the Sound_source from which the Sound travels
Ex: The Prince 's laugh ECHOED ["Location_of_sound_source" from the corridor].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path of the Sound's movement is any description of its trajectory of motion which is neither a Location_of_sound_source or a Goal.
Ex: A loud bang ECHOED ["Path" through the valley].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A setting in which Sound movement happens.
Ex: I heard their footsteps ECHO ["Place" in the hollow cavern].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Sound movement occurs.
Ex: ["Time" In the mornings] the harsh , squawking voices of the gulls ECHO between the channel walls

fe.name: Sound_source
fe.definition:
The point-like entity which produces the Sound.
Ex: There was muzak ECHOING ["Sound_source" from cheap speakers].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the Sound moves.
Ex: The scream REVERBERATED around the house ["Manner" like the scream of a soul in pain]

lexunit.name: echo.v

lexunit.name: roll.v

lexunit.name: blast.v
