frame.name: Employment_start
frame.definition: This is an unperspectivized frame representing the initial stage of the Employment_scenario: the formation of the employment relationship between the Employer and the Employee.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition: The person who enters an employment relationship with an Employer, thereby obligating themself to perform assigned Tasks in order to receive Compensation.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The person (or institution) that enters an employment relationship with an Employee.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing assigned Tasks in the course of their employment.

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Field which the Employee enters as they take up employment with the Employer.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the employment relationship between an Employer and an Employee comes about.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Employer and the Employee enter into the employment relationship.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition: The label given to a particular type of employment.

fe.name: Task
fe.definition: Task identifies the assignment that the Employee is obligated to do when she enters the employment relationship with the Employer.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when an Employer and an Employee establish an employment relationship.

frame.name: Employment_continue
frame.definition: This is an unperspectivized frame representing the middle stage of the Employment_scenario, in which there is a stable employment relationship between the Employee and the Employer.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition: The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Field in which one works.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the relationship between an Employer and an Employee develops.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Employee works for the Employer.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition: The label given to a particular type of employment.

fe.name: Task
fe.definition: Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when an Employer employs the Employee.

frame.name: Employment_end
frame.definition: This is an unperspectivized frame representing the final stage of the Employment_scenario, in which the relationship between the Employer and the Employee comes to an end. There are two different ways in which the relation ends, represented in the Firing frame (in which the Employer is agentive) and the Quitting frame (in which the Employee is agentive).

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition: The person whose employment relationship with an Employer ends.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The person (or institution) whose employ the Employee leaves.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an employment relationship between an Employer and an Employee ends.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Employer/Employee relationship is ended.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition: The label given to a particular type of employment.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Employer/Employee relationship ceases.

frame.name: Being_in_operation
frame.definition:
A Device or machine is in (or out of) service. Note that being broken or functional is a separate issue from being turned on or off. This latter notion is what the present frame is concerned with. The Time when and the Place where the Device is in use may be specified, as may be the Purpose a backgrounded human User had in turning the Device on or off.
Ex: ["Device" The TV] is ON Ex: ["Device" The lights] were OFF ["Time" when I came by].

fe.name: Device
fe.definition:
The Device or machine that is in or out of operation.
Ex: ["Device" Lights] _were_ ON in the primary school

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when a Device is in or out of operation.
Ex: I do n't want to turn round cos the lights _are_ ON ["Time" at the moment]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place in which the Device is or is not operating.
Ex: Lights _were_ ON ["Place" on the Kingston road bridge].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

lexunit.name: on.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: (of an electrical appliance or system): being functioning

lexunit.name: off.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an electrical appliance or power supply) not functioning or so as to cease to function.

lexunit.name: operate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (of an artifact or machine) be active.

lexunit.name: operational.a
lexunit.definition: FN: be in use, active.

frame.name: Contingency
frame.definition:
The answer to one open question, the Outcome, is dictated (partially or completely) by the answer to another open question, the Determinant, i.e. if the answer to the Determinant is known, the answer to the Outcome can be predicted. The Degree of predictive power and the Circumstances under which the dependency holds can also be expressed.
Ex: ["Outcome" Economic policy] is ["Degree" partially] a FUNCTION ["Determinant" of cultural values]. Ex: Well, ["Outcome" THAT] DEPENDS ... ["Determinant" DNI] Ex: ["Circumstances" In Mediaeval times], ["Outcome" status] was DEPENDENT ["Determinant" on birth].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: An open question that is (to some degree) predictable from the Determinant.

fe.name: Determinant
fe.definition:
An open question that determines the Outcome.
Ex: Price, in such a case, DEPENDS ["Determinant" only on the whim of the supplier].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The amount of predictive power supplied by the Determinant with respect to the Outcome.
Ex: His decision was ["Degree" somewhat] DEPENDENT on who won the game

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the Determinant dictates the Outcome. Oftentimes it is expressed in a fashion similar to Time and Place in other frames, but such cases are actually metonymic for the prevailing conditions of the Time and/or Place.
Ex: ["Circumstances" In London], how long it took to cross the city depended on how many state dinners were being served that night.

lexunit.name: in_hand.prep
lexunit.definition: SMV: dependent on somebody's choices

lexunit.name: depend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be controlled or determined by.

lexunit.name: function.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a variable quantity regarded as depending on another variable; a consequence

lexunit.name: dependent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: contingent on or determined by.

lexunit.name: depends.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (something said in the immediate discourse) depends (on)

lexunit.name: dependence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being dependent

lexunit.name: hang_((on)).v
lexunit.definition: COD: be contingent or dependent on

lexunit.name: turn.v
lexunit.definition: FN: depend on

lexunit.name: determine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to occur in a particular way; be the decisive factor in

lexunit.name: independent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: free from outside control; not subject to another's authority.

lexunit.name: independence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: freedom from outside control

lexunit.name: hinge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: depend entirely on.

lexunit.name: factor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a circumstance, fact, or influence that contributes to a result.

lexunit.name: variable.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an uncertain fact that something else depends on.

frame.name: Reliance
frame.definition:
A Protagonist needs a Means action performed for their Benefit. The relevant Means action is often evoked only by reference to an Intermediary who performs it. Also, if the Protagonist performs the Means action themself, the Instrument that they use may be referred to in place of the Means Note that when one of the three interrelated FEs Means, Instrument and Intermediary is realized overtly, the other two are blocked from overt realization as clause-level arguments of the target.Ex:
When the Protagonist is a sentient being, it is implied that they put their trust in the Intermediary to help in the achievement of the Benefit.
The extent to which the Protagonist is dependent on an Intermediary or Instrument can be indicated in a Degree phrase.Ex:
A set of Circumstances in which the Protagonist's need for the Benefit arises, may also be specified. Ex:
The difference between the Benefit that the Means action provides and the Purpose that the Protagonist has is very subtle. For our purposes we will assume that one can form a predication from Benefit and Means on the one hand, and Protagonist and Purpose on the other, but that they cannot be intermingled (cf. examples (7) and (8) below). With for-PPs such as in (6) it is not clear which FE they instantiate, Benefit or Purpose. We will arbitrarily call them BenefitEx:
Ex: (1) ["Protagonist" I] RELY ["Intermediary" on you] ["Benefit" to see that my name is not sullied].
Ex: (2) ["Protagonist" The system] can RELY ["Degree" entirely] ["Instrument" on coaxial cable] or entirely on optical fibre, just as a tree and branch network can be based on either technology .
Ex: (3) The Tories had got him into this and ["Protagonist" he] RELIED ["Intermediary" on them] ["Benefit" to get him out].
Ex: (4) I knew ["Protagonist" we] could RELY ["Intermediary" on you]. ["Benefit" DNI]
Ex: (5) ["Benefit" To get the economy moving] ["Protagonist" he] will RELY ["Means" on repairing the infrastructure of America]
Ex: (6) Later , when the Northern Ireland Office was established , ["Protagonist" it] RELIED ["Degree" heavily] ["Intermediary" on it] ["Benefit" for the information on which it based security and political activities].
Ex: (7) ["Protagonist" She] would have to RELY ["Means" on his help] ["Purpose" to get through the fight in one piece]. -- She got through the fight in one piece/*His help got through the fight in one piece
Ex: (8) ["Protagonist" I] RELY ["Means" on his help] ["Benefit" to get me through a long season] -- His help got me through a long season/*I got me through a long season
Ex: (9) ["Protagonist" We] RELY ["Means" on your helping us]
Ex: (10) You can RELY on him ["Circumstances" when the chips are down] to inspire the troops

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The person or thing whose needs are served by the Means action.
Ex: ["Protagonist" I] RELY on this walking stick to get me around

fe.name: Benefit
fe.definition:
An action or state that the Means action brings about and from which the Protagonist profits.
Ex: He still RELIES on me ["Benefit" to do the head work]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the achievement of the Benefit depends on the Means action.
Ex: He knows I RELY ["Degree" entirely] on him to point out all my blunders and spelling mistakes.

fe.name: Intermediary
fe.definition:
The person or thing that performs a Means action to the Benefit of the Protagonist.
Ex: We RELY ["Intermediary" on you] for feedback and input

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An object that the Protagonist uses to realize a Benefit.
Ex: I hate having to RELY ["Instrument" on my car] to get where I want to go

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action or state that the Protagonist wants to bring about. It is more or less the Benefit viewed in relation to the Protagonist rather than the Means.
Ex: The user will quickly begin to RELY on the pills ["Purpose" to cope with life pressures].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed either by the Protagonist or an Intermediary that has a Benefit for the Protagonist attached to it.
Ex: We RELY ["Means" on your response]

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The conditions when the Protagonist needs to rely on an Instrument or Intermediary.
Ex: We have to fully rely on him ["Circumstances" when times get a little rough]

lexunit.name: rely.v
lexunit.definition: COD: depend on with full trust.

lexunit.name: depend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rely on

lexunit.name: count.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rely on

lexunit.name: reliance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: dependence on or trust in someone or something

lexunit.name: dependence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of relying on someone or something for financial or other support.

lexunit.name: dependency.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of relying on someone or something for financial or other support.

frame.name: Reliance_on_expectation
frame.definition: A Cognizer takes a certain Expectation to be a reliable fact, such that their plans can be based on it.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: An individual that considers the Expectation certain.

fe.name: Expectation
fe.definition:
The fact which the Cognizer depends on in planning for the future.
Ex: I think you should COUNT ["Expectation" on getting a paycut].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The situation in which the Cognizer can count on the Expectation.
Ex: ["Circum" When investing in such a volatile area], you can BANK on getting burned a few times.

lexunit.name: bank (on).v
lexunit.definition: COD: base one's hopes or confidence on.

lexunit.name: count (on).v
lexunit.definition: FN: confidently expect to occur, such that plans can be made.

frame.name: Chatting
frame.definition:
A group of people (the Interlocutors or Interlocutor_1 and Interlocutor_2 together) have a conversation. No person is construed as only a speaker or only an addressee. Rather, it is understood that both (or all) participants do some speaking and some listening--the process is understood to be symmetrical or reciprocal. In this frame, the purpose of the conversation is generally social, rather than specifically to decide something or exchange information, or to quarrel (see Discussion and Quarrelling).
Ex: If you ain't got nothin' better to do, ["Interlocutor_1" I] 'd like to SHOOT THE BREEZE ["Interlocutor_2" with you] ["Duration" for a couple]. Ex: ["Interlocutors" We] used to CHAT ["Topic" about everything].

fe.name: Interlocutors
fe.definition: The group of individuals involved in chatting.

fe.name: Interlocutor_1
fe.definition:
The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of a conversation, as compared with Interlocutor_2. That is, Interlocutor_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Interlocutor_1. Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Interlocutor_1, not necessarily that of Interlocutor_2 or the group of Interlocutors as a whole.
Ex: ["Interlocutor_1" We] CHATTED with the guards to distract them from the heist going on right behind them.

fe.name: Interlocutor_2
fe.definition:
The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent group of participants in a conversation. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by _with_).
Ex: I gossiped ["Interlocutor_2" with the rest of the choir] for a little while.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time that the chatting goes on.
Ex: They YAKKED ["Duration" for hours]!

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The general subject that the statements of the Interlocutors in the conversation pertain to.
Ex: Oh, we GOSSIPED ["Topic" about the management shakedown] a bit.

fe.name: Language
fe.definition:
The language(s) or dialect(s) that a conversation is conducted in.
Ex: They exchanged GOSSIP ["Language" in French] while I sat by, completely ignored.

fe.name: Means_of_communication
fe.definition:
The device used by the Interlocutors to communicate.
Ex: Don't get excited--after a short ["MOC" telephone] CHAT with a broker, you 'll have your money.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
What the Interlocutors (or Interlocutor_1) hope to accomplish by chatting.
Ex: We SHOT THE BREEZE for a couple of hours ["Purpose" just to pass the time].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which a chat takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where a chat takes place.
Ex: A bit of lunch-time CONVERSATION ["Place" on the veranda] would not be amiss, I hope?

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The way that the Interlocutors succeed in having a conversation.
Ex: Though some of the fellas couldn't hear anymore, we CHATTED with them ["Means" by sharing a typewriter].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the conversation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Interlocutors (or Interlocutor_1) that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A description of the state of the Interlocutors (or Interlocutor_1) during the conversation.
Ex: We TALKED for a few minutes, ["Depictive" uncertain about why we were bothering].

lexunit.name: banter.n

lexunit.name: chat.n

lexunit.name: chit-chat.n

lexunit.name: colloquy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a formal conference or conversation.

lexunit.name: conversation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an informal spoken exchange of news and ideas between two or more people.

lexunit.name: converse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: engage in conversation.

lexunit.name: speak.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say something

lexunit.name: talk.v
lexunit.definition: COD: speak in order to give information or express ideas or feelings; converse or communicate by speech.

lexunit.name: joke.v
lexunit.definition: COD: say something to cause amusement

lexunit.name: gossip.n
lexunit.definition: COD: casual conversation or unsubstantiated reports about other people

lexunit.name: gossip.v
lexunit.definition: COD: engage in gossip.

lexunit.name: gab.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk at length.

lexunit.name: shoot the breeze.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have a casual conversation

lexunit.name: yak.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk at length about trivial or boring subjects.

frame.name: Cause_fluidic_motion
frame.definition: An Agent or a Cause causes a Fluid to move from a Source to a Goal along a Path or within an Area.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The animate protagonist who causes the Fluid to move.
Ex: What happens if ["Agent" we] DRIP acid on this compound?

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event or force that causes the Fluid to move.
Ex:

fe.name: Fluid
fe.definition: The entity that changes location and moves in a fluidic way. It is not necessarily in a liquid state but is construed that way.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The location that the Fluid occupies initially.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal is the location the Fluid ends up in as a result of the motion
Ex: Why did you SQUIRT juice ["Goal" onto my chair]?

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The trajectory along which the Fluid moves, exclusive of the Source and Goal.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
The setting in which the Fluid's movement takes place along an unspecified Path.
Ex: I SPLATTERED red paint ["Area" nearby].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex:

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the fluidic motion event is caused.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in causing the Fluid to move.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: A state of the Fluid that results from the motion event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the motion takes place.
Ex: I SPATTERED the egg all over the floor ["pla" in the kitchen].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The entity manipulated by the Agent which causes the Fluid to move.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Agent which brings about the motion of the Fluid.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Agent is attempting to bring about by causing motion.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance travelled by the Fluid.

lexunit.name: spatter.v
lexunit.definition: FN: splash liquid in drops

lexunit.name: splatter.v
lexunit.definition: FN: splash (a sticky or viscous liquid) in a messy fashion.

lexunit.name: splash.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make (liquid) strike or fall on something in drops

lexunit.name: spray.v
lexunit.definition: COD: apply (liquid) in a spray

lexunit.name: squirt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (with reference to a liquid) be or cause to be ejected in a thin jet from a small opening.

lexunit.name: pump.v
lexunit.definition: COD: force (liquid, gas, etc.) to move by or as if by means of a pump.

lexunit.name: drip.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fall in small drops

lexunit.name: sprinkle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: shoot or drip in drops

frame.name: Arranging
frame.definition:
An Agent puts a complex Theme into a particular Configuration, which can be a proper order, a correct or suitable sequence, or a spatial position.
Ex: ["Agent" He] ARRANGED ["Theme" the elements] ["Configuration" in the pattern that we now call the periodic table].
Ex: Try to order ["Theme" them] ["Configuration" by importance]. ["Agent" CNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The person who causes the Theme to be in a particular Configuration.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: An entity that consists of parts which can be put into a configuration relative to each other and/or relative to their environment.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the arranging takes place.

fe.name: Configuration
fe.definition: A state that holds of the Theme or a relation that holds among the constituent parts of the Theme as a result of the arranging action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the arranging action which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive use, it may indicate salient characteristics of anAgent that also affect the action ( eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: The place in which the Theme is put into a Configuration.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances identifies the situation in which an Agent arranges a Theme.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent is trying to bring about by changing the Configuration of the Theme.
Ex: ARRANGE the stones in a circle ["pur" to acheive maximal effect].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity used by the Agent to change the Theme's Configuration.
Ex: ARRANGE the floats into a line ["ins" with your oar].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Agent in order to arrange the Theme.
Ex: You must ARRAY them in a circle ["mea" by concentration alone].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Arranging act has occured.

lexunit.name: arrange.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put in a neat, attractive, or required order.

lexunit.name: arrangement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action, process, or result of arranging.

lexunit.name: array.v
lexunit.definition: COD: display or arrange in a neat or impressive way.

lexunit.name: deploy.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring or move into position for military action.

lexunit.name: deployment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the arrangement (of troops or materiel) to make ready (for military action).

lexunit.name: format.v
lexunit.definition: COD: arrange or put into a format.

lexunit.name: set up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: arrange

lexunit.name: order.v
lexunit.definition: FN: arrange methodically

lexunit.name: justify.v
lexunit.definition: FN: align text to both the left and right margins

frame.name: Law
frame.definition: A Law regulates activities or states of affairs within a Jurisdiction, dictating what Required states should be the case and what Forbidden states should not. Often it also indicates negative consequences for individuals that violate it, and these negative consequences are generally enforced by some official authority. They may or may not be created by some official legislative body.

fe.name: Law
fe.definition: This FE identifies the rule designed to guide activity, deprecating some types of activity and/or requiring other types of activity.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The use for which a law is intended.
Ex: We brought back a LAW ["Use" to forbid the use of profanity].

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
An individual or individuals that bring the Law into existence.
Ex: But this was forbidden by the ["Creator" King's] LAW of 1665.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which a Law comes into existence.
Ex: The ["Time" 1996] welfare reform ACT was a sham.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The term used to refer to a Law.
Ex: Well, they're still in violation of the ["Name" Sarbanes-Oxley] ACT.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
An indication of the subtype of Law.
Ex: According to ["Type" Canon] LAW, priests may not marry.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
Any indication of what makes up the Law.
Ex: We don't need another LAW ["Part" with 300 subsections].

fe.name: Forbidden
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs which is disallowed by the Law.
Ex: I think we need a LAW ["for" against all firearms within city limits].

fe.name: Required
fe.definition:
A state-of-affairs which the Law declares must be maintained.
Ex: The LAW ["req" that all minors must be accompanied by an adult] is a laughingstock.

fe.name: Jurisdiction
fe.definition:
The location where a given Law is in force.
Ex: According to ["jur" Fijian] LAW, no-one may enter the park after sunset.

lexunit.name: law.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a rule recognized by a country or community as regulating the actions of its members and enforced by the imposition of penalties

lexunit.name: code.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a systematic collection of laws or statutes

lexunit.name: protocol.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the official procedure or system of rules governing affairs of state or diplomatic occasions

lexunit.name: act.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a written ordinance of Parliament, Congress, etc.

lexunit.name: statute.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a written law passed by a legislative body.

lexunit.name: regulation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a rule or directive made and maintained by an authority.

lexunit.name: regime.n
lexunit.definition: FN: treaty.

lexunit.name: policy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a course or principle of action adopted or proposed by an organization or individual.

frame.name: Being_located
frame.definition:
A Theme is in a stable position with respect to a Location.
Ex: ["Theme" Our offices] are LOCATED ["Location" about two miles south of I-85] .

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: An entity which is at a particular Location

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location (generally presumed to be known to the interlocutor) with respect to which the location of the Theme can be understood.

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition:
A state (of the Theme) that results as a consequence of the Theme being situated at the Location.
Ex: The inn was ["Dep" well] SITUATED ["Dep" to take advantage of the visiting tourists].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Theme is at the Location.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: A salient entity that the Theme is located with respect to.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: This frame element is used to denote phrases that specifically entail an entity which is conceived as moving relative to another entity.

lexunit.name: located.a
lexunit.definition: FN: situated at a particular location.

lexunit.name: situated.a
lexunit.definition: FN: located in a place.

lexunit.name: lie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be situated in a specified position or direction.

lexunit.name: stand.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be situated in a particular position.

lexunit.name: sit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be or remain in a particular position or state.

frame.name: Practice
frame.definition: An Agent enacts an Action that is intended to be performed again at one or more later Occasions. The goal of practicing is to ensure that the action at the later Occasion(s) comes off flawlessly.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Action that the Agent performs intentionally in order to prepare for a later Occasion.
Ex: Little Dieter PRACTICED ["Action" playing the piano] all day.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent performs the Action in preparation for later performances of the same type.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the practicing occurs.
Ex: Our band PRACTICES ["Place" on the football field].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent performs an intentional act. Ex: John PRACTICED typing ["Purpose" to receive a raise].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the Agent practices.
Ex: We PRACTICED the play ["Time" on Tuesday].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent practices.
Ex: We PRACTICED the slam dunk ["Means" by bouncing on a trampoline].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the practicing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the Action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: We RAN through the song ["Manner" at quarter speed].

fe.name: Occasion
fe.definition:
The later enactment or enactments that the Agent expects to perform. Note that the Agent does not have to have specific Occasions in mind.
Ex: ["Occasion" For our brother's wedding] we had to REHEARSE the dinner twenty times.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time during which an Action is repeatedly practiced.
Ex: The troupe REHEARSED the ballet ["dur" for 4 months] before going on tour.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition:
The number of times that the Action is practiced.
Ex: We PRACTICE this scene ["iter" daily]

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
A person who participates in a practice event along with the Agent.
Ex: Then I went back to REHEARSING ["cop" with the band] while she sat around listening

lexunit.name: practice.v
lexunit.definition: COD: perform (an activity) or exercise (a skill) repeatedly or regularly in order to acquire, maintain, or improve proficiency in it

lexunit.name: practice.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a session of practising

lexunit.name: practice_((mass)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of practising

lexunit.name: rehearse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: practise (a play, piece of music, or other work) for later public performance

lexunit.name: rehearsal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a trial performance of a play or other work for later public performance

lexunit.name: rehearsal_((mass)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of rehearsing.

lexunit.name: run_through.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to discuss and/or enact the pieces of a performance in order

lexunit.name: run-through.n
lexunit.definition: FN: discussing or enacting the pieces of a performance in order

lexunit.name: dry run.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a rehearsal of a performance or procedure

lexunit.name: exercise.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a task set to practise or test a skill.

lexunit.name: drill.n
lexunit.definition: COD: instruction by means of repeated exercises.

lexunit.name: mock.a
lexunit.definition: COD: imitation; pretended.

frame.name: Attributes
frame.definition: An Entity has a particular Attribute with some Value. This frame is primarily for inheritance.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which a particular Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.

frame.name: Measurable_attributes
frame.definition: An Entity has a particular scalar Attribute with some Value. An absolute Value may be specified or the Value pertaining to the Entity may be implicitly compared to other possible Value(s). This frame is primarily for inheritance

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Value from the norm.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

lexunit.name: long.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of a greater than normal distance.

frame.name: Speed
frame.definition:
An Entity is capable of motion at a particular Speed or actually in motion at a particular Speed.
Ex: ["Entity" The car] went by ["Degree" real] FAST.
Ex: ["Entity" The car] _is_ ["Degree" really] FAST.
Ex: Oh yeah, ["Entity" Maseratis] _are_ FAST! ["Degree" INI]
Ex: The SPEED ["Entity" of the car] was ["Speed" 25 mph] ["Time" when it ran into the obstacle].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity whose Speed is under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is a function of the distance that the Entity moves in a given duration. With the adjectives of this frame this Frame Element is generally incorporated.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's speed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Speed from the norm.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Speed.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Speed.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why the Entity or Attribute is ata certain speed.

lexunit.name: fast.a
lexunit.definition: COD: moving or capable of moving at high speed

lexunit.name: quick.a
lexunit.definition: FN: moving fast

lexunit.name: speedy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: moving quickly

lexunit.name: speed.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the rate at which someone or something moves or operates or is able to move or operate

lexunit.name: breakneck.a
lexunit.definition: COD: dangerously or extremely fast

lexunit.name: rate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the speed with which something moves, happens, or changes.

lexunit.name: pace.n
lexunit.definition: COD: speed or rate of motion, development, or change.

lexunit.name: quickly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: in a fast manner

lexunit.name: rapid.a
lexunit.definition: FN: moving at a high speed

lexunit.name: rapidly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: quickly

lexunit.name: speedily.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: in a rapid manner

frame.name: Taking_time
frame.definition:
An Activity takes some Time_length to complete. If an Agent is involved they may stand in metonymically for the Activity. For some LUs (e.g., _fast_, _speedy_) the Degree to which the Activity is conceived of as taking less time than usual can be expressed.
Ex: ["Time_length" How long] will ["Activity" this] TAKE?
Ex: ["Activity" The ride] _was_ SPEEDY and often bumpy.
Ex: Under high-pressure situations, ["Agent" police officers] _are_ ["Degree" very] FAST ["Activity" at reacting to danger].

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The event which requires some Time_length for completion.
Ex: Mona had a SPEEDY ["Activity" recovery].

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The durational feature of the Activity.
Ex: ["att" In actual experiential time], sorting the beads TAKES an extremely long time.

fe.name: Time_length
fe.definition:
The amount of time required for the Activity.
Ex: It'll only TAKE ["Time_length" 20 seconds].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Time_length from the norm.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Activity takes place.
Ex: That TOOK an hour ["Time" last week].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Activity takes a particular amount of time.
Ex: ["Circumstances" In the rain], biking to work TAKES me a lot longer

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual who performs the Activity.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration is the length of time from the beginning of the Activity to its end.

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: COD: require or use up (a specified amount of time)

lexunit.name: in.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: expressing the length of time it takes for an event to complete

lexunit.name: fast.a
lexunit.definition: COD: taking place or acting rapidly

lexunit.name: quick.a
lexunit.definition: COD: lasting a short time

lexunit.name: rapid.a
lexunit.definition: COD: happening in a short time or at great speed

lexunit.name: swift.a
lexunit.definition: FN: happening quickly

lexunit.name: speedy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: done or occurring quickly.

lexunit.name: slowly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: being done or happening at a slow pace.

lexunit.name: slow.a
lexunit.definition: FN: characterized by taking a lot of time to do something; the opposite of fast

lexunit.name: gradually.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: being or happening in slow-paced, small increments

frame.name: Shaped_part
frame.definition:
An entity is a shaped Part of a larger Whole. The Part may correspond in form and function to a part of another entity. For instance, the leg of a table supports the weight of a table like the leg of an animal or person supports their weight. The Orientation of the Part relative to the Whole may be expressed.
Ex: I removed the ["Part" BRIM] ["Whole" of the hat]
Ex: Bill likes to chew the ["Part_Prop" waxy] ["Part" RIND] ["Whole" of the cheese]

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A shaped Part of a larger Whole.
Ex: Sergey put his arm on the ["Part" ARM] of his armchair.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
A Whole which has a shaped Part.
Ex: The LEG ["Whole" of the table] came off when we moved it.

fe.name: Part_Prop
fe.definition:
A property relating to the shaped Part of a Whole.
Ex: Sue fixed the ["Part_Prop" broken] ["Part" LEG] ["Whole" of the table].

fe.name: Orientation
fe.definition:
This is a property of the shaped Part that situates the Part within the Whole.
Ex: Abby broke the ["Orientation" top] ["Part" HANDLE] ["Whole" of the suitcase] .

lexunit.name: arm.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something considered to resemble an arm in appearance, position, or function

lexunit.name: mouth.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an opening or entrance to a structure that is hollow, concave, or almost completely enclosed

lexunit.name: leg.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long, thin support or prop, especially of a chair or table.

lexunit.name: rind.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a tough outer layer or covering, especially of fruit, cheese, or bacon.

lexunit.name: brim.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the (sometimes projecting) edge or rim of a hollow vessel.

lexunit.name: handle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part by which a thing is held, carried, or controlled.

frame.name: Architectural_part
frame.definition:
An entity is integrated into a building as a Part of a (possibly unexpressed) Whole which may refer to the whole building or merely to a sub-part of the building.
Ex: We need ["Dsc" new] ["Part" COUNTERS] for the kitchen
Ex: The storm ripped off the ["Whole" bathroom's] ["Part" ROOF]

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A Part of a larger architectural unit, the Whole.
Ex: Marty leaned against the ["Part" FIREPLACE].

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
An architectural unit which includes the Part.
Ex: The ["Whole" living-room] FIREPLACE is just for show.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A property relating to the Part.
Ex: The building had a ["Dsc" dilapidated] FACADE.

fe.name: Orientation
fe.definition:
This is a property of the Part that situates the Part within the Whole.
Ex: Looks like he fell through the ["Orientation" side] WALL, innit?

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Any indication of what makes up the Part, including components, ingredients, etc.
Ex: The house has a ["Material" marble] FLOOR

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
The Individual who creates the Part.
Ex: If ["Creator" a mason's] WALL collapses, is it always his fault?

lexunit.name: fireplace.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a partially enclosed space at the base of a chimney for a domestic fire

lexunit.name: floor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the lower surface of a room, on which one may walk

lexunit.name: ceiling.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the upper interior surface of a room

lexunit.name: mantel.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a structure of wood, marble, or stone around a fireplace

lexunit.name: roof.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the structure covering the top of a building or vehicle (as seen from outside)

lexunit.name: rail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a bar or series of bars fixed on upright supports or attached to a wall or ceiling, serving as part of a fence or barrier or used to hang things on

lexunit.name: wall.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a side of a building or room

lexunit.name: counter.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a flat-topped, level surface usually in the kitchen

lexunit.name: facade.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the face of a building, especially its principal front.

lexunit.name: staircase.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a set of stairs and its surrounding structure.

lexunit.name: foundation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the base upon which a building is built

frame.name: Age
frame.definition:
An Entity has existed for a length of time, the Age. The Age can be characterized as a value of the age Attribute, or a Degree modifier may express the deviation of the Age from the norm. The Expressor exhibits qualities of the age of the Entity.
Ex: ["Entity" This building] _is_ ["Age" twenty thousand years] OLD.
Ex: ["Entity" My grandpa] _is_ ["Degree" really] OLD
Ex: ["Entity" Junior] _is_ ["Age" only five weeks] OLD.
Ex: A cunning OLDISH ["Expressor" voice] called out from the crowd.
Ex: ["Entity" His] ["Attribute" AGE] was ["Age" 23] ["Time" at the time].
Ex: ["Entity" People] _of_ ["Attribute" AGE] ["Age" 55] or older should consult their physician.
Ex: I have a ["Age" 13-year]-OLD ["Entity" cousin]
Ex: ["Entity" My grandma] _is_ OLD
There are addtional patterns that the LUs in this frame occur in which are not licensed by a particular lexical head but by a construction. Additionally, there are patterns that evoke this frame without any overt lexical head that is part of this frame.
Ex: She is 45 years of AGE. _Billy is 13._

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which a particular age is under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is a function of the amount of time that the Entity has existed.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's age.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Age from the norm.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is at a particular Age.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Age.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Entity that reflect its age.
Ex: "Who's there?" she barked. "Ensign Kim, ma'me," the YOUNGISH ["exp" voice] of Voyager's young Harry Kim came over the comm line. "

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Entity.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

lexunit.name: old.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having existed for a long time or of a specified age

lexunit.name: ancient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: very old

lexunit.name: young.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having lived or existed for only a short time; not far advanced in life

lexunit.name: youngish.a
lexunit.definition: FN: somewhat young

lexunit.name: oldish.a
lexunit.definition: FN: somewhat old

lexunit.name: age.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the length of time that a person or thing has existed.

lexunit.name: new.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not existing before

lexunit.name: fresh.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not previously used; new.

frame.name: People_by_age
frame.definition: This frame contains words for individuals as viewed in terms of their age. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have a Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. A specific Age may sometimes be specified as well.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition: The human being of a certain age.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

fe.name: Ethnicity

frame.name: People_by_origin
frame.definition: This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, with respect to their Origin. The Origin is generally incorporated, but may occasionally be specified separately. The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have an Age, Descriptor, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition:
The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life. In this frame, it is generally incorporated in the lexical item, but may be separately specified as in the following:
Ex: FOREIGNERS ["Ori" from Japan] get short shrift around here.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition: The Person is the human being whose Origin is specified.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition:
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.
Ex: The ["Pers_char" swarthy] FRENCHMAN appeared at his elbow, smiling.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

fe.name: Age

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

fe.name: Context_of_acquaintance
fe.definition:
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
Ex: Would you believe it? That FRENCHMAN ["coa" from the subway] is back again!
