frame.name: Losing_it
frame.definition:
An Protagonist goes from a default state of mental and emotional equilibrium into a temporary state of disequilibrium, often a state of anger. A Reason for the change of state may be given. Likewise, Actions that the Experiencer takes as a result of their new emotional state may be expressed. Both Reasons and Actions may be introduced just as coordinated clauses. The lexical units also are frequently accompanied by expressions of an Affected_party.
This frame is populated by many lexical units that are based on the emotion-heat/pressure metaphor. Note also that many phrases with equivalent meaning to targets of this frame are compositional, e.g. 'go insane', which we treat as the LU insane.a (of the Mental_property frame) plus the inchoative support go.v.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
This is the person (or people) whose mental state changes.
Ex: ["Protagonist" Kim] WENT BALLISTIC.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
Something done by the Protagonist as a result of losing mental equilibrium.
Ex: You totally LOST IT ["act" with that speech you just gave to the Principal].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree marks the extent to which the Protagonist's mental state changes.
Ex: John ["Degree" totally] LOST IT

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, especially general descriptions comparing events.
Ex: He FLIPPED OUT ["Manner" like my dad did last year].

fe.name: Affected_party
fe.definition:
A person (or persons) who is saliently affected by the Protagonist's Actions.
Ex: I'm sorry, but every time I try to sneak out she GOES APESHIT ["Aff_par" on me].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The cause for the Protagonist to go crazy.
Ex: She WENT BALLISTIC ["rea" because of the pizzas], man.

lexunit.name: go apeshit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (slang) lose control and move (or speak) wildly and violently, usually due to a perceived intolerable situation.

lexunit.name: lose it.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lose control, generally due to frustration and anger or fear.

lexunit.name: go ballistic.v
lexunit.definition: FN: act in a fashion indicating extreme frustration.

lexunit.name: flip out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: suddenly become visibly deranged..

lexunit.name: blow cool.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lose one's detachment out of anger, resulting in confrontational interaction.

lexunit.name: freak out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: behave in an irrational fashion due to excessive fear

frame.name: Grasp
frame.definition:
A Cognizer possesses knowledge about the workings, significance, or meaning of an idea or object, which we call Phenomenon, and is able to make predictions about the behavior or occurrence of the Phenomenon. The Phenomenon may be incorporated into the wider knowledge structure via categorization, which can be indicated by the mention of a Category. The Cognizer may possess knowledge only in part and this may be expressed in a Completeness expression. The Cognizer may also be realized as a cognitive-emotional Faculty that is conceived of as having understanding. Note that the knowledge may have been acquired either from instruction or from the Cognizer's own experimentation, observation, or mental operations.
Words in this frame are frequently used metonymically to denote the transition into the state described above.
Ex: I figured this out last week and now ["Cog" I] ["Completeness" really] UNDERSTAND ["Phen" it].
Ex: ["Cognizer" My father] failed to COMPREHEND ["Phenomenon" that his explanations were based as much upon faith as mine]
Ex: ["Cognizer" The draughtsman] must ["Completeness" fully] COMPREHEND ["Phenomenon" what he is drawing]
Ex: Nobody seems to have explained this to her, but ["Time" finally] ["Cognizer" she] UNDERSTANDS ["Phenomenon" DNI]
Ex: I realized ["Cognizer" I] had not ["Manner" properly] UNDERSTOOD ["Phen" my own needs]
Ex: ["Faculty" The mind] is often unable to COMPREHEND ["Phenomenon" the significance of what it perceives].
Ex: ["Phenomenon" Our sensations] are in some sense to be UNDERSTOOD ["Reference_point" in terms of a set of stimulation levels (spiking frequencies) in the appropriate sensory pathways]. ["Cognizer" CNI]

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The sentient animate being who acquires new knowledge.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Sue] GRASPED the essentials right away

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
A state of affairs or dynamic system whose internal make-up and working the Cognizer comes to assimilate into their knowledge structure.
Ex: You must GRASP ["Phen" the complex relationship of all these subjects to each other]

fe.name: Completeness
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Cognizer has incorporated the workings and significance of a Phenomenon into their knowledge structure.
Ex: To COMPREHEND ["Completeness" fully] the distinction between task and process it is necessary to appreciate the evolutionary stages that groups go through.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate the relative ease of the Cognizer in acquiring new knowledge (readily, easily).
Ex: Its appeal rests on a simple logic that those inside and outside schools can ["Manner" readily] COMPREHEND

fe.name: Reference_point
fe.definition:
A mental concept or domain to which the Cognizer relates their new knowledge.
Ex: Unless one posits an inherent human tendency to COMPREHEND the world ["Reference_point" in binary terms], one has to look for more sociological explanations.

fe.name: Category
fe.definition:
This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Phenomenon is considered an instance by the Cognizer, allowing them to make predictions about the qualities, occurrence, or behavior of the Phenomenon.
Ex: Dooling argued that if an individual sentence is COMPREHENDED ["Category" as part of a larger semantic unit], part of the meaning of the sentence is likely to be redundant

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the when the Cognizer asssimilates the new knowledge.
Ex: ["Time" Yesterday] the students finally GRASPED the meaning of the equation

fe.name: Faculty
fe.definition:
A part of a person's cognitive-emotional faculties that is said to acquire knowledge.
Ex: ["fac" My heart] GRASPED that reality immediately. Ex: Man has understood something only when he has GRASPED it ["fac" with his heart]

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
Evidence marks expressions that indicate the source of the Cognizer's knowledge.
Ex: The reason for this effect is easiest to UNDERSTAND ["evi" from a picture].

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

lexunit.name: grasp.v
lexunit.definition: COD: comprehend fully

lexunit.name: comprehend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: grasp mentally; understand

lexunit.name: understand.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to perceive the nature and/or significance of an object or situation

lexunit.name: grasp.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's understanding.

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: COD: understand (an argument or the person making it)

lexunit.name: see.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to comprehend

lexunit.name: unintelligible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: impossible to understand

lexunit.name: intelligible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be understood.

lexunit.name: comprehensible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be understood; intelligible

lexunit.name: incomprehensible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not able to be understood

lexunit.name: graspable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: comprehensible

lexunit.name: apprehend.v
lexunit.definition: FN: understand

lexunit.name: fathom.v
lexunit.definition: COD: understand (something) after much thought.

lexunit.name: follow.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: understand an exposition or a line of reasoning.

frame.name: Craft
frame.definition:
A particular Activity, performed conventionally or habitually by more than one Practitioner within a Culture, is described in terms of its method.
Ex: One lived-in cabin also had a grassy roof, as if the CRAFT ["Act" of thatching] had died out locally

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Activity that is being performed habitually or conventionally.
Ex: Restrop was built at the very height of the great Elizabethan age, when the CRAFT ["Act" of building] began to turn into an art.

fe.name: Practitioner
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate whose Activity is at issue.
Ex: The development and the elaboration of metal armour for protection in warfare and jousting gave considerable impetus to the CRAFT ["Prac" of the blacksmith]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Place in which the Activity is performed.
Ex: So, by application of the sacred ["Plc" northern] ART of fettling, here are a few tips on how to provide your steed with an almost Zen-like ride quality

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate attributes, traits, or evaluations of the Activity.
Ex: Once upon a time people indulged in the ["Desc" ages-old] CRAFT of telling stories to each other

fe.name: Culture
fe.definition:
A Culture within which the Activity is performed.
Ex: Origami is an ancient ["Culture" Japanese] CRAFT of paper folding

lexunit.name: art.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an activity with an aesthetic component requiring knowledge and skill

lexunit.name: craft.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an activity involving skill in making things by hand.

lexunit.name: science.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a procedurally complex activity requiring methodical attention to detail

frame.name: Idiosyncrasy
frame.definition:
A certain Idiosyncrasy belongs to an Entity distinguishing it from other entities.
Ex: If you have 32 ["Deg" totally] IDIOSYNCRATIC ["Id" meanings for a term] in a class, everyone will be very confused when they talk! ["Entity" DNI]
Ex: ["Idiosyncrasy" The art of change-ringing] _is_ PECULIAR ["Entity" to the English]

fe.name: Idiosyncrasy
fe.definition:
An entity or characteristic belonging to the Entity.
Ex: Paul has an IDIOSYNCRATIC ["Id" tendency to go barefoot at all times].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity that has a certain distinguishing Idiosyncrasy.
Ex: This bird is UNIQUE ["Entity" to England]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Idiosyncrasy differs from the norm.
Ex: Was this behavior ["Degree" completely] IDIOSYNCRATIC?

lexunit.name: idiosyncratic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: peculiar to a particular entity

lexunit.name: peculiar.a
lexunit.definition: COD: belonging exclusively to

lexunit.name: peculiarity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an unusual or distinctive feature or habit

lexunit.name: unique.a
lexunit.definition: COD: belonging or connected to (one particular person, group, or place)

lexunit.name: idiosyncrasy.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a behavior peculiar to an entity

lexunit.name: particular.a
lexunit.definition: FN: restricted to a particular entity

lexunit.name: certain.a
lexunit.definition: COD: some but not all.

lexunit.name: oddity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the quality of being strange.

lexunit.name: weird.a
lexunit.definition: COD: very strange; bizarre.

lexunit.name: uncanny.a
lexunit.definition: COD: strange or mysterious.

frame.name: Capability
frame.definition:
An Entity meets the pre-conditions for participating in an Event. A Degree modifier may be included to indicate by how much the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements.
Ex: Conductor software gives ["Entity" us] the hands-on CAPABILITY ["Evt" to provide updates immediately]
Ex: The GOP is afraid that ["Ent" it] might not _be_ ABLE ["Evt" to keep the seat vacated by Dunn.]
Ex: ["Ent" NASA] _is_ UNABLE ["Evt" to communicate with Mars rover].
Ex: ["Ent" He] CAN ["Evt" fly a kite].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.
Ex: ["Entity" Little Tommy] CA n't read

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The Event that the Entity may participate in.
Ex: White House voices doubts about Aristide's ABILITY ["Evt" to govern]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Event.
Ex: Blind parents are ["Deg" very] CAPABLE of raising children

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.
Ex: ["Circumstances" In this weather], an experienced pilot can still manage to fly 500 miles.
Ex: The new car has a cruising CAPACITY ["Circumstances" in excess of 150 kph].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Event.
Ex: They were not ABLE to go outside ["cau" because of the rain].

fe.name: Relevant_feature
fe.definition:
The characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Event.
Ex: These computers have the ["rel" processing] CAPACITY to compute the precise date of the end of the world.

fe.name: Status
fe.definition:
The status of the capability.
Ex: This machine has many ["Status" new] CAPABILITIES.
Ex: He has an ["Status" innate] POTENTIAL.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The particular role that the Entity plays in the Event.
Ex: His ABILITY ["rol" as a leader] to get things done is unparalleled.

lexunit.name: able.a
lexunit.definition: FN: meeting the pre-conditions for

lexunit.name: unable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not able to

lexunit.name: can.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be able to

lexunit.name: capable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having the ability or quality necessary to do something.

lexunit.name: ability.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the capacity to do something.

lexunit.name: potential.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something that can develop or become actual

lexunit.name: capability.n
lexunit.definition: COD: power or ability to do something

lexunit.name: capacity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the ability or power to do something.

lexunit.name: potential.a
lexunit.definition: FN: something characterized as having the ability to develop into something else

frame.name: Rest
frame.definition:
One Part of a larger Whole has been mentioned, is inferrable, or is available in the discourse setting and the previously unmentioned part, the Rest, is now mentioned.
Ex: The lenses , like the ["Rest" REST] ["Whole" of the exoskeleton], are made of calcite Ex: They see social policy work as a natural COMPLEMENT ["Part" to bureau work]

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A Part of a larger Whole that has been mentioned in prior discourse or is available in the discourse setting.
Ex: the GP had stipulated counselling as a COMPLEMENT ["Part" to medication]

fe.name: Rest
fe.definition:
The previously unmentioned part of the Whole.
Ex: You should try to persuade the ["Rest" REST] of the family to do so whatever their personal opinions

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The larger entitiy or group that is fully made up of the Part and the Rest.

lexunit.name: rest.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the previously unmentioned part of a contextually accessible whole

lexunit.name: complement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the thing that goes together with the given part to form an implicit whole

lexunit.name: complement.v
lexunit.definition: COD: serve as a complement to

frame.name: Increment
frame.definition:
A member or members of a Class have just been mentioned or are present in the discourse setting and now a different instance (or group of instances) of the same class is referred to.
Ex: My husband left me for ANOTHER ["Class" woman] -- and now wants to get back together again!
Ex: My husband left me for ["Added_set" ANOTHER]["Added_set" woman] -- and now wants to get back together again!

fe.name: Class
fe.definition:
The general category of entity which has been referred to.
Ex: My Husband left me for ANOTHER ["Class" man]!

fe.name: Added_set
fe.definition:
The instance of the Class that is added to the Initial_set of entities in the Class.
Ex: There was ["as" ANOTHER] today.

fe.name: Initial_set
fe.definition:
The previously mentioned group of entities of the Class.
Ex: A FURTHER five incursions ["is" over and above those noted for 1995] took place in the first three months of 1996.

fe.name: Increment
fe.definition:
The number of entities within the Added_set.
Ex: ["ncr" Four] MORE years of misguided leadership appeared to be in the offing.

lexunit.name: other.a
lexunit.definition: COD: used to refer to a person or thing that is different from one already mentioned or known

lexunit.name: another.a
lexunit.definition: COD: used to refer to a different person or thing from one already referred to

lexunit.name: other.n
lexunit.definition: COD: used to refer to a person or thing that is different from one already mentioned or known

lexunit.name: another.n
lexunit.definition: COD: used to refer to a different person or thing from one already referred to.

lexunit.name: further.a
lexunit.definition: COD: additional

lexunit.name: more.a
lexunit.definition: FN: an additional amount

lexunit.name: more.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an additional quantity

lexunit.name: additional.a
lexunit.definition: FN: in addition to existing instances

frame.name: Partitive
frame.definition:
A Subset is profiled against the Group it belongs to. The Subset may consist of a single member. Frequently, the Group is actually a generic sample of a full population, and the Subset is representative of the relative proportion.
Ex: OF ["Group" all scenes that evoke rural England], ["Subset" this] is one of the loveliest.
Ex: As of 5:30 p.m. Moscow time, ["Subset" 23] OUT OF ["Group" 46 miners stranded in the Zapadnaya-Kapitalnaya mine] have been rescued
Ex: ["Subset" 1.5] OUT OF ["Group" 10 respondents] preferred Shrub over Ferry

fe.name: Subset
fe.definition: A Subset belonging to the Group.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: The Group of entities which includes the Subset.

lexunit.name: of.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: expressing the relationship between a subset and a group

lexunit.name: out of.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: expressing the relationship between some members and a group

frame.name: Evoking
frame.definition:
Some Stimulus causes a Cognizer to think of a prior Phenomenon due to its perceived similarity.
Ex: I burned down the malt shop where we used to go just because ["Stim" it] REMINDS me ["Phen" of you]

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizeris the person who remembers the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
The Phenomenon is the mental content that a Cognizer remembers.
Ex: You REMIND me ["Phen" of my uncle Jerry]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which Cognizer perceives the Stimulus to match the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including speed (quickly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Other expressions involving how the experience affects the Cognizer may also be expressed (painfully).

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Stimulus continues to remind the Cognizer of the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Stimulus evokes the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Cognizer remembers the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition:
The entity or situation that causes the Cognizer to think of the Phenomenon.
Ex: ["Stimulus" Internationalization] CONJURES up a world of diplomatic exchanges and international agencies in which the interests of ex-colonial and great powers still linger

fe.name: Feature
fe.definition:
A characteristic of the Stimulus that contributes to the perception of similarity to the Phenomenon.
Ex: She REMINDS me of your mother ["fea" with her darting beady eyes].

lexunit.name: remind.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause someone to think of (something) because of a resemblance

lexunit.name: bring to mind.v
lexunit.definition: FN: evoke

lexunit.name: evoke.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring or recall to the conscious mind

lexunit.name: call to mind.v
lexunit.definition: FN: evoke

lexunit.name: put in mind_(of).v
lexunit.definition: FN: remind one of

lexunit.name: conjure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: call to the mind

lexunit.name: ring a bell.v
lexunit.definition: FN: remind (of something specific)

lexunit.name: recall.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause one to remember or think of

lexunit.name: reminder.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a thing that causes someone to remember something.

lexunit.name: evocative.a
lexunit.definition: COD: evoking strong images, memories, or feelings.

lexunit.name: evocation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the event of causing to come to mind.

frame.name: Gradable_attributes
frame.definition: An Entity has an implicit Value for an Attribute. Degree expresses either explicit comparison or the deviation of the Value when compared with other entities of similar kind. The Value may hold only relative to a particular Time or in particular Circumstances.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Value from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition: The generally implicit Value of the Attribute.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Entity is has the Attribute to a given Degree.

frame.name: Aesthetics
frame.definition:
An Entity is judged to be sensually pleasing or intellectually interesting to a (generally implicit) Judge.
Ex: . We saw this BEAUTIFUL ["Ent" boat] with the red sails several times Ex: We camped here on the beach and had an ["Deg" absolutely] LOVELY ["Entity" early morning walk through farm fields]

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the implicit value either from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular implicit value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular implicit value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition:
The individual who judges the Entity's aesthetics.
Ex: She has always been BEAUTIFUL ["Jdg" to me].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Entity is in the state of having a particular implicit value for the Attribute.

lexunit.name: beautiful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically

lexunit.name: hideous.a
lexunit.definition: SMV: ugly to a disturbing degree

lexunit.name: lovely.a
lexunit.definition: COD: exquisitely beautiful

lexunit.name: smart.a
lexunit.definition: COD: clean, tidy, and stylish

lexunit.name: ugly.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unpleasant or repulsive in appearance

lexunit.name: tasty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of food) having a pleasant, distinct flavour.

lexunit.name: elegant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: graceful and stylish.

lexunit.name: fair.a
lexunit.definition: FN: pleasurable to the aesthetic senses

frame.name: Noise_makers
frame.definition:
The Noise_maker is an artifact used to produce sound, especially for musical effect.
Ex: The ["Grnd" church] ["nm" BELLS] rang Ex: The ["Grnd" car] ["nm" ALARM] went off again Ex: I have never played an ["tp" acoustic] ["nm" GUITAR]. Ex: Each artist personally owns a Steinway and has chosen to perform on the ["Creator" Steinway] PIANO professionally

fe.name: Noise_maker
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to produce sound.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The use for which an Noise_maker is intended.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: An individual or individuals that bring the Noise_maker into existence.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition: The time at which a Noise_maker comes into existence.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The term used to refer to an Noise_maker.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An indication of the subtype of Noise_maker.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: Any indication of what makes up the Noise_maker, including components, etc.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: The location with which the Noise_maker is associated.

lexunit.name: guitar.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a stringed musical instrument with a fretted fingerboard and six or twelve strings, played by plucking or strumming with the fingers or a plectrum

lexunit.name: bell.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a hollow object, typically made of metal and in the shape of a deep inverted cup, that sounds a clear musical note when struck

lexunit.name: siren.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a device that makes a loud prolonged signal or warning sound

lexunit.name: piano.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large keyboard musical instrument with a wooden case enclosing a soundboard and metal strings, which are struck by hammers when the keys are depressed.

lexunit.name: rattle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a thing that makes a rattling sound, in particular a baby's toy consisting of a container filled with small pellets

lexunit.name: xylophone.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a musical instrument played by striking a row of wooden bars of graduated length with small beaters

lexunit.name: drum.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a percussion instrument sounded by being struck with sticks or the hands, typically cylindrical, barrel-shaped, or bowl-shaped with a taut membrane over one or both ends.

lexunit.name: cello.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a bass instrument of the violin family, held upright on the floor between the legs of the seated player.

lexunit.name: saxophone.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a member of a family of metal wind instruments with a reed like a clarinet, used especially in jazz and dance music

lexunit.name: alarm.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a warning sound or device.

frame.name: Religious_belief
frame.definition:
A Believer has faith in a piece of Content or an Element which fits into a religious belief system made up of many articles of faith. The Content is not necessarily tied to direct sensory experience. The system of beliefs may be enshrined by the members of a social group
Ex: Do ["Believer" Muslims] BELIEVE ["el" in the virgin birth of Jesus?] Ex: ["Believer" Muslims] BELIEVE ["el" in only One God, the same God that Jews and Christians believe in], but some of the ideas about the nature of God are different Ex: ["Believer" Muslims] BELIEVE ["Content" that the month of Ramadan is the holiest month of the year]

fe.name: Believer
fe.definition: The Believer is the person whose religious beliefs are in question.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The Content is the object of the Believer's religious conviction. Content can be expressed as a finite clause or in a in-PP Complement.
Ex: A Christian BELIEVES ["Cont" that Jesus of Nazareth was a prophet].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Believer is convinced of the usefulness and validity of their religious beliefs .
Ex: Christ the King Presbyterian Church therefore BELIEVES ["Degr" fervently] in Christian civilization

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Believer knows or thinks something.
Ex: All we have to do is BELIEVE in Jesus ["Manr" like a child] and confess him

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role is a function that an Element of the faith is believed to serve.
Ex: If a person BELIEVES in Jesus ["Role" as his Saviour], he can he baptized.

fe.name: Element
fe.definition:
A predefined, fixed idea to which reference is made throughout the belief system.
Ex: I believe ["Element" in Jesus] Ex: To Clark, who infinitely BELIEVES ["el" in angels] and celebrating the holidays with loved ones, Christmas means kids and family.

lexunit.name: believe.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have religious faith (in the truth or existence of)

lexunit.name: subscribe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: feel agreement with (an idea or proposal).

lexunit.name: subscriber.n
lexunit.definition: FN: someone who believes in a particular religion's ideals.

frame.name: People_by_religion
frame.definition:
This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, with respect to their Religion. The Religion is generally incorporated, but with some lexical units it is specified separately.
Ex: The bells call the ["Person" FAITHFUL] to evensong ["Religion" DNI] Ex: A ["Age" 90-year-old] ["Person" BAPTIST] claims to have seen God personally in his backyard.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition: The Person is the human being.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is conceived of as persisting over time.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

fe.name: Religion
fe.definition: The religious belief system that the Person follows.

lexunit.name: muslim.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a follower of Islam

lexunit.name: christian.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who has received Christian baptism or is a believer in Christianity

lexunit.name: faithful.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the believers in a particular religion, especially Islam

lexunit.name: baptist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a member of a Protestant Christian denomination advocating baptism only of adult believers by total immersion.

lexunit.name: buddhist.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a follower of Buddhism.

lexunit.name: pagan.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person holding religious beliefs other than those of the main world religions.

lexunit.name: mormon.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, a religion founded in the US in 1830 by Joseph Smith Jr.

lexunit.name: infidel.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who does not follow the common religion, or any religion at all

lexunit.name: zealot.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who fervently, and often militaristically, believes in a religion

lexunit.name: jew.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a follower of Judaism

frame.name: People_by_jurisdiction
frame.definition: This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, who are governed by virtue of being registered in a certain Jurisdiction. Alternatively, they may be conceptualized with respect to their governance by a political or religious Authority They may have an Age, Descriptor, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity.

fe.name: Jurisdiction
fe.definition: The Jurisdiction is the place where the Person typically resides and by whose Authority he is governed.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition: The Person is the human being.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition: The politically or religiously legitimated persons who govern the Jurisdiction.

lexunit.name: citizen.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a legally recognized subject of a political jurisdiction, typically a nation

lexunit.name: parishioner.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who belongs to a particular Church parish

lexunit.name: national.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a citizen of a particular country.

lexunit.name: subject.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a member of a state owing allegiance to its monarch or supreme ruler

lexunit.name: citizenry.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a whole body of citizens

frame.name: Halt
frame.definition:
A Theme ceases motion.
Ex: ["Theme" Peter] STOPPED ["Time" immediately] and span to see Aeryn frozen where she stood.
Ex: ["Theme" He] STOPPED ["Place" at the door], not wanting to see what he knew must be on the other side
Ex: As Lynn walked through the bedroom on her way to the shower ["Theme" she] STOPPED ["Purpose" to look at her sleeping husband]

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which a Theme stops the motion.
Ex: When the kitty was standing beside the slayer's pillow, she STOPPED ["Purpose" to make sure everything was quiet]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the Theme's motion stops.
Ex: She STOPPED ["Place" on the threshold] with a sinking heart

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Theme stops.
Ex: John STOPPED ["Time" suddenly], whirled around and spread out his arms

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE is used for a Depictive phrase describing the Theme.
Ex: Once she reached the end she STOPPED ["Dep" with her nostrils flaring]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Theme stops motion.
Ex: Martha STOPPED ["Manner" abruptly] and stared at her only son

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
This FE identifies Theme whose motion ceases.
Ex: When the kitty was standing beside the slayer's pillow, ["Theme" she] STOPPED to make sure everything was quiet

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the length of Time during which the motion is stopped.
Ex: She STOPPED ["Duration" for a minute] and listened, but the wind came back empty handed as she stared down the desolate road

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which the Theme stops motion.
Ex: She weaved back and forth on her feet, then piroetted. She STOPPED ["Means" by putting her hand to the ground and crouching]

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the last Subevent of the stopped motion.
Ex: The bus STOPPED ["Sub" with a shudder]

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Containing_Event
fe.definition: Containing event is an event that is occuring at a time during which the Theme ceases motion.

lexunit.name: stop.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cease moving

lexunit.name: halt.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cease moving

lexunit.name: to a halt.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: ending up in a resting state

lexunit.name: to a stop.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: ending up stationary

frame.name: Connecting_architecture
frame.definition:
An entity is integrated into a building as a Part of a (possibly unexpressed) Whole which may refer to the whole building or merely to a sub-part of the building. The Part itself connects locations within the building to each other, Connected_locations. If a particular point of view is adopted in the context of real or imagined motion, then one of the locations can be construed as Goal and the other as Source.
Ex: It was of great interest to me to see the star signs of Taurus the Bull and Leo the Lion on the ["Part" STAIRCASE] ["Goal" to the upper Palace].
Ex: All visitors may use the ["Part" ELEVATOR] ["cl" between the Main Level and the Upper Level] instead of the main staircase
Ex: The ["Part" WINDOW] ["Goal" into the garden] was open.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A Part of a larger architectural unit, the Whole.
Ex: Could you open the ["Part" DOOR] for me, please?

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
An architectural unit which includes the Part.
Ex: The ["Whole" kitchen] DOOR came off its hinges

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A property relating to the Part.
Ex: People may give you weird looks as you struggle up the steps with your suitcase instead of using the ["Dsc" slow] ESCALATOR.

fe.name: Orientation
fe.definition:
This is a property of the Part that situates the Part within the Whole.
Ex: We can let you in through the ["Orientation" back] DOOR.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Any indication of what makes up the Part, including components, ingredients, etc.
Ex: The house has an ["Material" oak] DOOR

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
The Individual who creates the Part.
Ex: If ["Creator" a caprenter's] DOOR is shoddy, is it always his fault?

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is one of the Connected_locations treated as source.
Ex: Does DOOR ["src" from basement] to living quarters have an adequate lock operated from living quarters side?

fe.name: Connected_locations
fe.definition:
Two or more named locations that are connected by the architectural Part.
Ex: Security in the HALLWAY ["cl" between the jail and the Court Building] needs to be improved.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The Direction is the direction or directions the Part of connecting architecture runs.
Ex: Please take the ["" east west] STAIRS down to the lower floor

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is one of the Connected_locations treated as a goal
Ex: Finally they corner us as we reach the ESCALATOR ["Goal" to the first floor].

lexunit.name: door.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a usually swinging or sliding barrier by which an entry is closed and opened

lexunit.name: elevator.n
lexunit.definition: COD: lift

lexunit.name: lift.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a platform or compartment housed in a shaft for raising and lowering people or things

lexunit.name: escalator.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a moving staircase consisting of a circulating belt of steps driven by a motor

lexunit.name: corridor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long passage from which doors lead into room

lexunit.name: hallway.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a corridor or passage in a building

lexunit.name: window.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an opening in a wall or roof, fitted with glass in a frame to admit light or air and allow people to see out

lexunit.name: staircase.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a set of stairs and its surrounding structure.

lexunit.name: stairs.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a set of such steps leading from one floor of a building to another

lexunit.name: step.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a flat surface, especially one in a series, on which to place one's foot when moving from one level to another.

frame.name: Membership
frame.definition:
A Member is semi-permanently part of a socially constructed Group.
Ex: ["mm" Victor] _is_ PART ["Group" of the Red Crescent]

fe.name: Member
fe.definition:
The person who belongs to a Group.
Ex: Two ["Member" MEMBERS] of the Red Cross were here about a donation

fe.name: Group
fe.definition:
A set of people standing in a semi-permanent relationship together.
Ex: Giles was EXPELLED ["Group" from the Future Farmers of America]

fe.name: Standing
fe.definition:
An indication of the Member's status within the Group.
Ex: Bill is a ["std" full] MEMBER of the Elks.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Member is a member of the Group.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the membership relationship holds.

lexunit.name: member.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person, country, or organization belonging to a group, society, or team

lexunit.name: belong.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be a member of.

lexunit.name: part.n
lexunit.definition: FN: belonging to (a group or organization)

lexunit.name: membership_(status).n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being a member

lexunit.name: membership.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the body of members

lexunit.name: associated.a
lexunit.definition: FN: be a member of an organization.

frame.name: First_experience
frame.definition:
An implicit experiencer has an Experience for the first time. Some LU's may specifically imply an agentive activity.
Ex: ["cxt" In Italy] ["exp" the term was] FIRST ["exp" used by the Venetians in 1546]
Ex: ["cxt" This time], ["exp" the comet was] FIRST ["exp" seen on the night of 19th October, 1805 by European observers Jean Louis Pons, Johann Sigismund Huth, and Alexis Bouvard]

fe.name: Experience
fe.definition:
An event happens for the first time within the Context.
Ex: ["exp" Made from flax, linen was] FIRST ["exp" used by the ancient Egyptians].
Ex: ["exp" The Cobra was] FIRST ["exp" deployed to Vietnam in September 1967].

fe.name: Context
fe.definition:
A spatial, cultural, or personal delimitation within which the Experience occurs for the first time.
Ex: ["cxt" In Germany] the pamphlet was FIRST used by the leaders of the Protestant Reformation to inflame popular opinion against the pope

lexunit.name: first.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: for the first time

frame.name: Identicality
frame.definition:
A Current_instance of a certain Type is under discussion. This instance is evaluated as being the same instance or a different instance from a Previous_instance encountered in a Previous_context.
Ex: Kim has a DIFFERENT ["tp" hair color] every week Ex: Kim has ["ci" a different hair color] every week
Ex: Is this the SAME ["tp" sofa] ["pi" as the one that used to be in the lobby]? Ex: Is this ["ci" the same sofa as the one that used to be in the lobby]?
Ex: Dracula and your neighbor are DIFFERENT ["Type" people] Ex: Dracula and your neighbor are DIFFERENT ["soi" people]

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
The kind of thing of which instances are under discussion.
Ex: Smithers works in a DIFFERENT ["tp" office] now

fe.name: Current_instance
fe.definition: The instance of the Type that is currently under discussion.

fe.name: Previous_instance
fe.definition: An instance of the Type that was encountered previously and which is now compared for identity with the Current_instance.

fe.name: Previous_context
fe.definition:
The situation in which another instance of the Type was encountered earlier.
Ex: This is a DIFFERENT car ["pc" than last week]

fe.name: Set_of_instances
fe.definition:
The complete set of instances of the Type involved in the mentioned contexts.
Ex: Kent Clark and Superman are the SAME ["Type" person] Ex: Kent Clark and Superman are the SAME ["soi" person]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Current_instance is the same or different.

lexunit.name: same.a
lexunit.definition: COD: referring to a person or thing just mentioned

lexunit.name: different.a
lexunit.definition: COD: distinct; separate.

lexunit.name: identical.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the very same (instance) (often accompanied by "same" or " very")

lexunit.name: distinct.a
lexunit.definition: FN: individual or separate of identity

lexunit.name: identity.n
lexunit.definition: FN: characteristics determining what something is.

frame.name: Remainder
frame.definition:
A Resource is depleted by some process, resulting in there being only a Remainder in existence some time into or after the process. The original Resource may be indicated metonymically via reference to an Original_owner. The Location where the Resource is found may be expressed.
Ex: There are only ["rem" two poems] LEFT ["oo" from Quayle] Ex: After the storm, ["Remainder" only two houses] were LEFT ["res" DNI] Ex: ["rem" Not much] was LEFT ["loc" in the till] Ex: ["rem" Nothing] REMAINED ["ben" for the youngest brother] ["res" from the inheritance] Ex: ["rem" Only this school] is LEFT ["oc" from the 1970]s; all the other ones are newer.

fe.name: Remainder
fe.definition: The part of the Resource that the Process has not yet applied to.

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition: The original set of items to which the Depletive_process applies one after the other.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
The place where the Resource is found.
Ex: How much is LEFT ["loc" in the treasury]?

fe.name: Original_owner
fe.definition:
The individual who owned the Resource that is being depleted.
Ex: Only two poems are LEFT ["oo" from Virgil Smithers]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the amount of the Resource that is let is assessed.
Ex: ["tm" In 1910], only two of the Renaissance buildings REMAINED

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition:
An individual who may use the Remainder for his benefit.
Ex: Is there any food LEFT ["ben" for me]?

fe.name: Original_context
fe.definition:
A temporal setting or event which metonymically stands for the entities that were in existence then. The Remainder is part of the Original_context. This FE occurs especially when abstract entities such as social institutions are seen as Resources.
Ex: Only the Beaux Arts cinema is LEFT ["oc" from the golden era of the 1940s]

lexunit.name: remnant.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a usually small remaining part of a larger original set of entities that has been much depleted

lexunit.name: left.a
lexunit.definition: FN: remaining after a process of depletion

lexunit.name: remain.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be left over after others or other parts have been used up or destroyed

lexunit.name: remains.n
lexunit.definition: COD: things remaining.

frame.name: Temporal_pattern
frame.definition:
A salient Subevent has a Pattern of recurrence within a larger Process.
Ex: Tony's fingers tapped RHYTHMICALLY on the keyboard

fe.name: Process
fe.definition:
The larger event that is characterized by the recurring Subevents.
Ex: The RHYTHM ["pr" of the rain falling on the roof] kept me awake

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition:
The salient, punctual event that is construed as part of a Process.
Ex: His RHYTHMIC ["se" tapping] irritated her

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of the Pattern in which the Subevents recur.
Ex: I could feel the ["dsc" steady] RHYTHM of his breathing

fe.name: Pattern
fe.definition:
The Pattern that can be detected in the recurrence of the Subevents of the Process.
Ex: The music had a driving RHYTHM Ex: The music had a driving ["pt" rhythm]

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
An indication of a conventionally recognized subtype that the Pattern belongs to.
Ex: Herminio illustrated a ["tp" rhumba] RHYTHM on the congas

lexunit.name: rhythm.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a recurrent pattern, especially of sound or movement

lexunit.name: rhythmically.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: with regular, patterned repetition

lexunit.name: beat.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a regular, strongly punctuated pattern in music

lexunit.name: rhythmic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: characterized by regular recurrence

lexunit.name: time.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the rhythm of a song

frame.name: Left_to_do
frame.definition:
A Process of using or modifiying is scheduled to be applied to a group or mass. At a certain Time, the Remainder that is still left to be processed can be identified. The Agent who is in line to work on the Remainder is usually deprofiled but may sometimes be expressed.
Ex: ["rem" Three more cars] REMAIN ["Process" to be fixed]. Ex: We have done the first twenty so there are ["rem" only five more letters] REMAINING ["pro" DNI]

fe.name: Process
fe.definition:
The activity that is being applied to the mass or the set of entities.
Ex: An additional eighty-three invitations REMAIN ["pro" to be sent]

fe.name: Remainder
fe.definition:
The mass or group that has not yet been processed.
Ex: In this case everyone should be informed by word of mouth to contact the person holding the list to find out ["rem" which gifts] still REMAIN to be bought.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Remainder is assessed.
Ex: ["tm" Now] only three more items REMAIN to be sold

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individuals who are scheduled to apply the Process to the Remainder. The Agent may be the same or a different individual who applied the process to the part that has already undergone the Process.
Ex: To insure my appointment, much will REMAIN ["agt" for you] to do

lexunit.name: left.a
lexunit.definition: FN: remaining to be processed

lexunit.name: remain.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be left after others or other parts have been dealt with

lexunit.name: remainder.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a part, number, or quantity that is left over to process

frame.name: Temperature
frame.definition:
An Entity has a Temperature characterized by the target. The Temperature is a value of the temperature Attribute.
Ex: Note that in this frame, the Entity does not experience the temperature, but is merely described as being in a certain externally verifiable state. Thus Ex: Open a window; I'm too HOT. is not in frame.
Ex: ["Entity" The pan] is already ["Degree" too] HOT ["Degree" to touch].
Ex: ["Entity" The walk-in] was FREEZING, but it was better than hanging out in the kitchen.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity for which the temperature Attribute is under consideration.
Ex: ["ent" The soup]'s too HOT.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Temperature
fe.definition:
A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the temperature Attribute.
Ex: The skillet had a TEMPERATURE ["tem" of 230 F]

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Temperature from the norm.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Degree for the temperature Attribute.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Temperature.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
A part of the Entity that has the specified Temperature value.
Ex: The pan is HOT ["sub" on the handle]

lexunit.name: temperature.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the degree or intensity of heat present in a substance or object

lexunit.name: hot.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having a high temperature

lexunit.name: cool.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of or at a fairly low temperature

lexunit.name: freezing.a
lexunit.definition: COD: very cold.

lexunit.name: cold.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of or at a low or relatively low temperature.

lexunit.name: lukewarm.a
lexunit.definition: FN: moderately warm.

lexunit.name: tepid.a
lexunit.definition: FN: moderately warm.

lexunit.name: frigid.a
lexunit.definition: FN: extremely cold.

lexunit.name: scalding.a
lexunit.definition: FN: hot, often enough to burn.

frame.name: Ambient_temperature
frame.definition:
The Temperature in a certain environment, determined by Time and Place, is specified.
Ex: It's ["deg" too] HOT ["deg" to do anything] ["tim" today].
Ex: ["pl" Nome] _is_ ["deg" pretty] COLD ["tim" this time of year]
Ex: ["tim" Last Tuesday] _was_ a ["deg" real] SCORCHER.
Ex: ["tim" Tomorrow] is gonna _be_ CHILLY.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place where it is a certain Temperature .
Ex: ["Place" Chicago] is HOT today .

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The temperature feature of the weather.

fe.name: Temperature
fe.definition:
A quantity or other characterization of the Temperature of the environment.
Ex: The TEMPERATURE was ["tem" 85 F] in the shade today

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Temperature from the norm.
Ex: It's like ["deg" totally] CHILLY, dude, like, totally.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which an ambient environment has a particular Temperature.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Some specification of the circumstances under which the ambient Temperature is as specified.
Ex: It's plenty COOL ["con" in the shade]

lexunit.name: cool.a
lexunit.status: Finished_Initial: I was not able to f
lexunit.definition: FN: having an environment with a fairly low temperature

lexunit.name: cold.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having an environment with a low temperature

lexunit.name: hot.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having an environment with a high temperature

lexunit.name: warm.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having an environment with a fairly or comfortably high temperature

lexunit.name: scorcher.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a day or period of very hot weather

lexunit.name: chilly.a
lexunit.definition: FN: Colder than is comfortable

lexunit.name: temperature.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the degree of heat of outside air

frame.name: Heralding
frame.definition:
A Communicator announces (linguistically or non-linguistically) the imminent arrival of an Individual or the occurrence of an Event. Generally, the Communicator is attempting to inform the public.
Ex: ["evt" The unveiling of Alinghi's keel] was HERALDED ["com" by alp horns]
Ex: ["com" A brass band] HERALDED ["evt" his arrival] and he was flanked by secret service agents
Ex: ["med" The telegram] HERALDED ["Ind" him], but with boundless miles for hiding he had stolen in under the cover of night

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The Communicator greets the arrival of an Individual or occurrence of an Event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Communicator heralds.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Communicator heralds.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Communicator heralds.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which a Communicator heralds.
Ex: The town HERALDED his arrival ["mns" with a peal of church bells].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Communicator that also affect the heralding (_ eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Individual
fe.definition: The person who is greeted at their arrival by the Communicator.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The occurrence which is greeted by the Communicator.
Ex: Sheep scattered from the road as trumpets HERALDED ["evt" his arrival at the castle gates]

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The symbol-containing artifact whereby a Communicator heralds.

lexunit.name: herald.v
lexunit.definition: FN: signal the imminence of (linguistically or non-linguistically)

frame.name: Cause_to_continue
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Process or State to continue.
Ex: ["agt" The goaltenders] KEPT ["pro" the game] going ["mns" with terrific saves].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individual who causes the Process to continue or the State to be maintained.
Ex: ["agt" Smithers] KEPT the food warm

fe.name: Process
fe.definition:
A Process that is maintained by the Agent.
Ex: The soot in the air KEPT ["pro" it] ["pro" raining] for weeks

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
The State that the Agent maintains.
Ex: We need to KEEP ["sta" China] ["sta" British].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time for which the Agent maintain the State or Process.
Ex: I responded quickly to the relaxed, calm atmosphere and found answers to questions that had KEPT me on edge ["dur" for years].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The event by which an Agent or Cause maintains the State or Process.
Ex: The car did not break down, though it KEPT me on edge ["mns" by making a funny noise all the way]

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event that causes the Process or State to be maintained.
Ex: ["cau" The storm] KEPT us in all the next day.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by maintaining the State or Process.
Ex: On my Toshiba I had shrunk the Windows partition and KEPT it there ["pur" for use via the dual boot].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Agent that maintain the State or Process.
Ex: The third time I KEPT the engine going ["ins" with the accelerator pedal]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Process continues.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Process continues.

lexunit.name: keep.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to continue in a specificied state or process

frame.name: Employee's_scenario
frame.definition: The sequence of events in which the Employee hires on with an Employer, holds a Position, and finally leaves the Position.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task. It often varies over the lifetime of employment.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
Ex: ["Empee" I] just STARTED yesterday!

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition:
The label given to a particular type of employment.
Ex: Look, I didn't HIRE on ["Position" as your waitress]!

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
Ex: I have a JOB ["Task" emptying the trash cans].

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Field in which one works. Ex: He has been WORKING ["Field" in finance] for years.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

frame.name: Employer's_scenario
frame.definition: The sequence of events in which the Employer hires an Employee, employs them in a Position for some Duration, and finally lets them go from the Position.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition:
Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.
Ex: I think you should HIRE him ["Compense" at $15 an hour], not a penny more.

fe.name: Employee
fe.definition:
The person who is obligated to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.
Ex: ["Empee" I] was just HIRED yesterday!

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The person (or institution) that gives Compensation to an Employee.

fe.name: Position
fe.definition: The label given to a particular type of employment. Ex: Look, I wasn't HIRED ["Position" as your waitress]!

fe.name: Task
fe.definition:
Task identifies the action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.
Ex: I was HIRED ["Task" just to empty the trash cans].

fe.name: Field
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Field in which one works. Ex: We HIRED only five ["Field" in finance].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of time for which the Employee continues in employ.

frame.name: Becoming
frame.definition:
An Entity ends up in a Final_state or Final_category which it was not in before.
Ex: ["rea" Why] ["ent" I] BECAME ["finc" an Emacs user]
Ex: ["ent" I] Left The Ministry And BECAME ["finc" An Atheist]
Ex: Surprisingly, ["ent" various veteran organizations] also TURNED ["fins" vehemently antiwar].
Ex: ["trp" Over the years] ["ent" she] BECAME ["finc" very much a part of the Sturtevant family].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the change takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that an intentional Entity is responding to by changing.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the change occurs.
Ex: ["tim" By 1945] he had BECOME uncertain of the advisability of anyone having such a weapon.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
For how long the Entity remains in the Final_state or Final_category.
Ex: He BECAME ["dur" for the next three years] the prophetic voice of the Salvadoran people until his assassination on March 24, 1980

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: The majority ["man" slowly] BECAME more and more disenchanted with him.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity which undergoes a change, ending up in the Final_state or Final_category.
Ex: ["ent" I] GROW impatient with your insolence.

fe.name: Final_state
fe.definition:
The state of the Entity after the event.
Ex: Everything 's GOING ["fins" wrong]!

fe.name: Final_category
fe.definition:
The category that the Entity ends up in after the event.
Ex: He never could understand how she ENDED UP ["finc" an evangelist].

fe.name: Transitional_period
fe.definition:
The period during which the Entity is in transition.
Ex: ["trp" Over the last 5 years], I've BECOME sick and tired of your tomfoolery.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.
Ex: Smithers BECAME tired ["cau" from all the work he'd been doing].

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition: This FE describes the state of the Entity before becoming occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity enters the Final_state or Final_category

fe.name: Initial_category
fe.definition: This FE describes the category of the Entity before becoming occurs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation for the occurance of the Becoming event.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: The individual entities related to the Entity which are saliently affected by its change.

lexunit.definition: FN: end up being

lexunit.name: grow.v
lexunit.definition: COD: become gradually or increasingly

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come into a specified state

lexunit.name: go.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pass into or be in a specified state, especially an undesirable one:

lexunit.name: end up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become (as the result of a process).

lexunit.name: turn.v

lexunit.name: form.v
lexunit.definition: FN: turn into.

frame.name: People_by_vocation
frame.definition:
This frame contains words for Individuals as viewed in terms of their vocation.
The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships and independent of their participation in any particular activity. They may have a Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. A specific Age may sometimes be specified as well.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition: The Person is the human being.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

fe.name: Context_of_acquaintance
fe.definition:
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
Ex: Is she the ACTRESS ["coa" from the movie we saw last night]?

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition:
Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Person occupies within an organization.
Ex: Robin is the ["rnk" head] WAITRESS at La Notte.

fe.name: Place_of_employment
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Person works.

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition: The Employer gives compensation to an Person for their work.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Type of the vocation that the Person practices.

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition: The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing a task.

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition:
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.
Ex: Smithers is a ["cb" half-time] CLERK for Procteur et Gamble

frame.name: Performers
frame.definition:
This frame contains words for Individuals as viewed in terms of their participation in artistic performances.
The Person is conceived of as independent of other specific individuals with whom they have relationships. They may have a Descriptor, Origin, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity. A specific Age may sometimes be specified as well.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition:
The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
Ex: Sir Alec Guiness was a ["Ori" British] ACTOR until his death.

fe.name: Person
fe.definition:
The Person is the human being.
Ex: Smithers is a brilliant ACTOR.
(Note that the Person FE is incorporated in the LU actor.n.)

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition:
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is conceived of as persisting over time.
Ex: Billy Throb is a ["psc" swarthy] ACTOR who frequently plays in scary movies.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.
Ex: Hundreds of ["desc" angry] ACTORS were protesting against the new contract

fe.name: Age
fe.definition:
The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.
Ex: I need help with the name of an ["age" old] ACTOR

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition:
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.
Ex: She's one of the most famous ["eth" black] ACTRESSES around today

fe.name: Context_of_acquaintance
fe.definition:
An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.
Ex: Is she the ACTRESS ["coa" from the movie we saw last night]?

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition:
Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Person occupies within a performance.
Ex: Robin is the ["rnk" lead] ACTRESS in La Notte.

fe.name: Place_of_employment
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the Person works.
Ex: ACTORS ["poe" at the Theater on the Square] went on strike

fe.name: Employer
fe.definition:
The Employer gives compensation to an Person for their work.
Ex: Margaret's fortunes improved in 1949 when she joined a host of young ["emp" MGM] ACTRESSES

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Type of performer the Person is.
Ex: Smithers is a ["typ" stage] ACTOR

fe.name: Compensation
fe.definition:
The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing a task.
Ex: Barney Smith is a ["com" highly-paid] ACTOR

fe.name: Contract_basis
fe.definition:
The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.
Ex: Smithers is a ["cb" part-time] ACTOR at the National Theater

lexunit.name: musician.n

frame.name: Spelling_and_pronouncing
frame.definition:
A Speaker realizes a Sign, usually a linguistic one, in some Formal_realization. The Formal_realization may be described as correct or incorrect in a Judgment expression, or it may be partially indicated as a Part_of_form. Manner may be used as a more general indication of the Formal_realization
Ex: ["spe" A person] doesn't always PRONOUNCE ["sig" a word] ["man" the way they say it in context]
Ex: ["spe" I] can't SPELL. ["sig" INI] ["jud" INI]
Ex: ["spe" Stephanopolous] SPELLS ["sig" his name] ["pof" with a "ph"].
Ex: ["cxt" On page 87465], ["spe" you] SPELLED ["sig" the name of my dog] ["jud" incorrectly] ["for" as "Checquers"].
Ex: ["cxt" In German], ["sig" the word for 'peace'] is WRITTEN ["for" "Friede"] ["spe" CNI]

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The language user who produces a Sign in some modality.
Ex: ["spe" He] insists on MISPRONOUNCING my name every time, the bastard!

fe.name: Sign
fe.definition:
An abstract form-meaning pairing.
Ex: My little nephew can't SAY ["sig" prestidigitation]

fe.name: Judgment
fe.definition:
An evaluation of whether the Formal_realization that the Speaker produced matches the standard or standard range.
Ex: Finally, I would pay more attention to your "oppinion" if you SPELLED it ["jud" correctly].

fe.name: Formal_realization
fe.definition:
The written string, gesture, or vocalized sound sequence that the Speaker produces.
Ex: The old uncensored editions of the Talmud referred to Jesus as Yeshua censored versions SPELLED it ["for" as Yeshu]

fe.name: Part_of_form
fe.definition:
A constituent part of the Formal_realization.
Ex: You spelled it ["pof" with a "t"].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The way that the Speaker produces the Formal_realization.
Ex: You SPELLED it ["man" the way it sounds].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Speaker produces the Formal_realization.
Ex: ["zeit" Today] you SPELLED it "pjuok".

fe.name: Context
fe.definition:
The context wherein the Speaker produces a particular Formal_realization.
Ex: ["cxt" On page 1223], you SPELLED her name wrong.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The person that the Speaker is producing the Formal_realization for.
Ex: So I asked the ladies down in the kitchen if they could maybe PRONOUNCE your name ["add" for me].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The amount of times the Sign is spelled or pronounced per some unit of time.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE marks any state that the Speaker is in while spelling or pronouncing.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

lexunit.name: spell.v
lexunit.definition: FN: write or name the letters that form (a word)

lexunit.name: misspell.v
lexunit.definition: COD: spell wrongly

lexunit.name: pronounce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make the sound of (a word or part of a word).

lexunit.name: mispronounce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pronounce wrongly.

lexunit.name: say.v
lexunit.definition: FN: pronounce

lexunit.name: write.v
lexunit.definition: FN: create a linguistic form by writing.

frame.name: Subjective_influence
frame.definition:
An Agent, Situation or Entity has an influence on a Cognizer. The influence may be general; or it may be manifested in the Cognizer's engaging in an Action as a consequence of the influence; or the Cognizer may be influenced in how they carry out a Behavior that they are engaged in already. Alternatively, a Product may be specified whose production or design was influenced by the Cognizer's experience of the Situation or Entity. Ex:
The mediation of the Cognizer's psyche distinguishes this frame from the Objective_influence frame, where dependent events occur automatically given the appropriate kind of influencing force. In this frame, by contrast, a Cognizer may perceive an influence yet not respond to it in any way.
Ex: ["ent" These works] had a profound effect and INFLUENCED ["cog" her] ["beh" in the creation of a successful series capturing this sun-drenched region]. Ex: I'm sure if I asked Mattel ["sit" what] INSPIRED ["pro" this car] I would be told it's an original design, and not supposed to represent any actual car.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The person who is influenced by the Situation or Entity.
Ex: George Gilder would run with this idea later in writing the New Testament of supply-side economics that INFLUENCED ["cog" Reagan].

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition:
A state of affairs--- which can be an event, state or conditions---that has an influence on the Cognizer.
Ex: ["sit" The balmy temperatures] INSPIRED me to write a poem on the advent of spring. Ex: Hecker said that although ["sit" the sheer age of the building] INSPIRED him to preserve its heritage aspects he also designed its interiors around the ·clean and fresh· mood of Queensland.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
A person or thing that has an influence on the Cognizer.
Ex: ["ent" The painting] INSPIRED me to take a risk and use the intense green for the sky.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
An Action that the Cognizer decides to carry out as a consequence of the influence of a Situation or Entity.
Ex: What factors INFLUENCED Nixon ["act" to issue the doctrine]?

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition:
A Behavior that the Cognizer is engaged in independently but whose execution is subsequently influenced by the Situation or Entity.
Ex: Attention will also be paid to St. Paul , what INFLUENCED him ["beh" in his thinking] and what he wrote in his letters about sex, sexuality, men and women

fe.name: Product
fe.definition:
An entity that stands metonymically for the actions and considerations that produced it.
Ex: Does anyone know what INSPIRED ["pro" this song]?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Subjective_influencing event occurs.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the Subjective_influence event.

fe.name: Agent

frame.name: Objective_influence
frame.definition:
An Influencing_variable, an Influencing_situation, or an Influencing_entity has an influence on a Dependent_entity, Dependent_variable, or a Dependent_situation.
Ex: More and more doctors realise that ["infs" diet] can INFLUENCE ["deps" disease].
Ex: Our subject is the body clock; how ["infs" it] INFLUENCES ["deps" our physiology and behaviour] and how it interacts with the rhythms in our environment.
Ex: But it is more likely that ["infe" a physical restraint] INFLUENCED ["depe" the swirling liquids].
Ex: It claimed, perhaps hollowly, that ["infe" NT] had yet to IMPACT ["deps" its business].
Ex: ["infs" This kind of elementary boo-boo] would certainly IMPACT ["depv" video speed].

fe.name: Influencing_entity
fe.definition:
A thing or person whose behavior has an effect on an Dependent_situation, Dependent_variable, or Dependent_entity.
Ex: Much of the acreage in this round is closer to the coastline, and as such has many implications in terms of how ["infe" it] could IMPACT upon fish spawning, local bird life, and even the Ministry of Defence in some cases

fe.name: Dependent_entity
fe.definition:
An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by an Influencing_entity or an Influencing_situation.
Ex: The Committee is responsible for making recommendations to the Board regarding the group's activities as they IMPACT ["depe" on the environment].

fe.name: Influencing_variable
fe.definition:
A scalar variable (with unspecified value) which has an effect on the Dependent_entity, Dependent_variable, or Dependent_situation.
Ex: ["infv" Factors which] INFLUENCE the stability of the combination include the softness of the car and the trailer's suspension, plus the balance of the trailer.

fe.name: Dependent_situation
fe.definition:
A situation that whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by an Influencing_entity, Influencing_event, or Influencing_variable.
Ex: The new network file system server line supports database or backup applications running alongside NFS input/output operations without one activity IMPACTING ["deps" another].

fe.name: Dependent_variable
fe.definition:
A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of an Influencing_entity, a Influencing_variable, or an Influencing_situation.
Ex: This kind of elementary boo-boo would certainly IMPACT ["depv" video speed].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Influencing_entity effects the Dependent_entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the influence occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the influencing occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Influencing_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
