frame.name: Make_acquaintance
frame.definition:
Individuals first encounter each other and make introductions at a particular Time, Place, or Context. The Individuals may have known of each other before making introductions. The Individuals may be separately construed as Individual_1 and Individual_2. In some cases, there is a Explanation of the circumstances which lead to the Individuals' meeting.
Ex: Impressed when ["ind1" he] first MET ["ind2" Nixon], he had always thought of him as an intelligent man, and believed that Nixon would take a stand for civil rights
Ex: ["ind1" We] MET ["ind2" each other] ["pla" in the university], worked in the same city and came to KSU together!
Ex: ["inds" Horatio Nelson and Emma Hamilton] first MET ["pla" in Naples] ["tim" in September 1793]
Ex: Her name was Jenny and ["ind1" I] MET ["ind2" her] ["int" through an online dating service].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Individuals make each other's acquaintance.
Ex: I MET my wife ["tim" 2 yrs ago].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Individuals make each others acquaintance.
Ex: Bill MET his wife ["pla" in Poltava, Ukraine].

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition:
The persons (or in rare cases animals) that make each other's acquaintance.
Ex: ["inds" My wife and I] MET in college working in the theatre and we will have been married for 30 years in June 2000.

fe.name: Context
fe.definition:
The Event, frequently a social occasion, during which the Individuals make each other's acquaintance.
Ex: The two first MET ["con" at a lecture] in 1851.

fe.name: Individual_1
fe.definition:
The semantically more prominent one of the two parties when the Individuals are realized separately.
Ex: ["ind1" Melissa Hurley] had never MET her neighbor, Richard Congdon ? the dog owner ? until recently, when she and a reporter knocked on his door.

fe.name: Individual_2
fe.definition:
The semantically less prominent of the two parties when the Individuals are expressed separately.
Ex: Gossip reports say she either MET ["ind2" Kennedy] while helping him shop for suits at Calvin Klein, or was contacted by him after he saw her jogging in a New York park

fe.name: Intermediary
fe.definition:
A person or social group that connects both of the Individuals, with a group member typically introducing the Individuals to each other.
Ex: Let's call her Gretchen. I "MET" her ["int" through a mutual friend (the same fellow who has wanted me to write this column for the past couple years)].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The state of affairs that leads to the Individuals' making each other's acquaintance.
Ex: No, I MET him ["exp" because he was also the teacher for the special science fiction class].

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Depicitve
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

frame.name: Clemency
frame.definition:
An Executive_authority exercises their power to reduce or remove negative consequences for someone who has been labeled an Offender who participated in an Crime.
Ex: ["off" A Fort Worth man convicted of a robbery his brother later confessed to committing] was _granted_ CLEMENCY ["zei" on December 20, 2002], ["exe" by Governor Rick Perry]. Ex: A Fort Worth man convicted ["cri" of a robbery his brother later confessed to committing] was _granted_ CLEMENCY on December 20, 2002, by Governor Rick Perry.
Ex: Engel represented Robert Bacon, ["off" the first man] ["exe" Easley] _gave_ CLEMENCY ["zei" in 2001]. ["cri" INI]
Ex: Ohioans will receive a blow-by-blow account of arguments before the Ohio Parole Board on whether ["off" Cincinnatian John Byrd Jr.] should be executed or _granted_ CLEMENCY ["cri" for a 1983 murder]. ["exe" CNI]

fe.name: Offender
fe.definition:
The individual who is accused or convicted of a Crime.
Ex: Since 1976, ["off" 225 death row inmates] have been _granted_ CLEMENCY for humanitarian reasons.

fe.name: Crime
fe.definition:
An action deemed criminal by law.
Ex: I never saw a legal case where a person was given CLEMENCY ["cri" for murder].

fe.name: Executive_authority
fe.definition:
The constitutionally specified authority who has the power to grant clemency.
Ex: Mr. Papa was _granted_ CLEMENCY for a drug conviction ["exe" by Mr. Pataki], and released in 1997

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that the Executive_authority is responding to in granting clemency.
Ex: Since 1976, 224 death row inmates have been granted CLEMENCY ["rea" for humanitarian reasons].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which clemency is granted.
Ex: In addition to Ms. White, 55, Mr. Pataki granted CLEMENCY ["zei" yesterday] to three men serving long prison terms for offenses under the stern Rockefeller-era drug laws that mandate long sentences for some relatively low-level drug crimes.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Executive_authority that accomplishes the granting of clemency.
Ex: Write, call, e-mail, or fax Governor Frank O'Bannon as soon as possible and urge him to grant CLEMENCY ["mea" by giving Gary Burris a sentence of life without parole]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the act of clemency which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Executive_authority that also affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Executive_authority intends to accomplish by granting clemency.
Ex: And so he _granted_ CLEMENCY ["pur" so that all who surrendered would be received as freedmen into his own army].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the Executive_authority grants clemency.
Ex: Apparently, no woman has ever been _granted_ CLEMENCY ["pla" there].

lexunit.name: clemency.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an act wherein an executive authority reduces a sentence or pardons an offender

frame.name: Commutation
frame.definition:
An Executive_authority exchanges one penalty, the Original_punishment, for another less severe one, the New_punishment. The Offender is who received the Original_punishment is usually expressed as a modifier.
Ex: ["zei" On December 15, 1971], ["exe" Governor Winfield Dunn] conditionally COMMUTED ["ori" his sentence] ["new" to twenty years].
Ex: On December 15, 1971, Governor Winfield Dunn conditionally COMMUTED ["off" his] sentence to twenty years.
Ex: She served about two years before ["exe" President Carter] COMMUTED ["ori" her sentence]. Ex: She served about two years before President Carter COMMUTED ["off" her] sentence.

fe.name: Offender
fe.definition:
The individual who was convicted of a crime and given a sentence (the Original_punishment).
Ex: Some of the more interesting points to me include the description of Thomas More's original sentence before it was COMMUTED to beheading Ex: Some of the more interesting points to me include the description of ["off" Thomas More's] original sentence before it was COMMUTED to beheading

fe.name: Executive_authority
fe.definition:
The constitutionally specified authority who has the power to commute punishments.
Ex: Hearst was sentenced to seven years in prison. 1979, ["exe" President Jimmy Carter] COMMUTED Hearst's prison sentence after she served nearly two years.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that the Executive_authority is responding to in commuting the Original_punishment.
Ex: His defence was a good one; but he was convicted and sentenced to death, COMMUTED ["rea" on account of his influence at court] to having his sword broken over his head .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Original_punishment is commuted.
Ex: Israel ["zei" yesterday] COMMUTED the lengthy prison terms of seven Jews convicted of murdering or plotting to kill Arabs.

fe.name: Original_punishment
fe.definition:
The punishment the Offender was originally sentenced to.
Ex: I had learned after all of this period of time has passed the court was about to let (Bush) pay a sum of money and COMMUTE ["ori" her sentence] to time served.

fe.name: New_punishment
fe.definition:
The new reduced form of punishment that the Executive_authority orders for the Offender.
Ex: he bench comprising Justice Tariq Pervez and Justice Ijazul Hassan COMMUTED his sentence ["new" to 10-year rigorous imprisonment].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the commutation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Executive_authority that also affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Executive_authority commutes the Original_punishment.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Executive_authority that accomplishes the commutation.
Ex: The governor may COMMUTE the sentence ["mea" by committing the person who may benefit from programs offered at a youth correctional facility to the department of corrections until the youth is 18 years of age or until sooner placed or discharged].

lexunit.definition: COD: reduce (a judicial sentence, especially a sentence of death) to a less severe one

lexunit.definition: COD: he action or process of commuting a judicial sentence or a legal obligation or entitlement

frame.name: Subversion
frame.definition:
A Counter_actor or Cause impedes an Agent in an Activity or impedes the unfolding or continuation of a State_of_affairs. The opposing force applies without first being noticed, often in a secret or an underhanded fashion.
Ex: However, as this story goes on the Queen of Sodom has ["cou" a brother who] plans to UNDERMINE ["age" his sister] and take the throne of Sodom.
Ex: Diotrephes withstood John's words, and would not submit to his authority; in fact, ["cou" he] UNDERMINED ["soa" John's authority].
Ex: I don't want to get a reputation for punishing disagreement. On the other hand, ["cou" he] UNDERCUT ["age" me] ["deg" pretty badly] and I can't just let it slide.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event or state_of_Affairs that successfully impedes an Agent or a State_of_affairs.
Ex: ["cau" This failure] UNDERMINES governmental authority

fe.name: Counter_actor
fe.definition:
A person who intentionally or not acts in such a way that an Agent or State_of_affairs is impeded.
Ex: Tory rebels queued to warn that ["cou" they] wouldSABOTAGE efforts to put the treaty through Parliament .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
A person who is intentionally engaged in some Activity and who is impeded in that Activity.
Ex: If he is really UNDERMINING ["age" me], then he is a fine friend.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
An Activity that is being impeded.
Ex: The Dominican Republic was widely held to have UNDERMINED ["act" its own efforts to become a full member of CARICOM]

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
A state or event that is ongoing and whose continuance or unfolding is impeded.
Ex: Whenever I try to quit they all try to SABOTAGE ["soa" my efforts].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Cause or Counter_actor impede the Agent or the State_of_affairs.
Ex: The so-called advantage of a Premier being able to determine an election date is ["deg" totally] UNDERMINED by speculation surrounding the date for the next election.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Counter_actor hopes will result from his undermining.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Counter_actor subverts an Activity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Counter_actor or Cause works agains the Agent.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Counter_actor that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE denotes the number of times the Counter_actor or Cause subverts the Agent per unit of time.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: This FE denotes the number of times the subversion event has occurred.

Ex: Note that this frame is not limited to technical, legal uses. The use of guilty in this frame is also to be distinguished from that in the Contrition frame by not referring to an emotional state. Innocent has several other meanings that are distinct from the one it has in this frame. It can mean 'ignorant of'; 'innocuous'; 'pure and unsullied by experience'.

fe.name: Accused
fe.definition:
This is the person who is accused of a Misdeed.
Ex: ["acc" Frank Quattrone] is found GUILTY of obstructing federal investigations

fe.name: Misdeed
fe.definition:
The wrongful act which the Accused was purportedly involved in.
Ex: Cambridge woman says she's INNOCENT ["mis" of fraud].

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in connecting the Accused to the Misdeed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Accused is involved in the Misdeed.
Ex: Sammy Sosa was ["deg" completely] GUILTY of corking. Ex: For his part, the writer is ["deg" somewhat] GUILTY of his usual charges: undue casual talk of nudity.

lexunit.name: guilty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: justly chargeable with a particular fault or error

lexunit.name: innocent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not guilty of a crime or offence

lexunit.name: guilt.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the fact of having committed an offence or crime

lexunit.name: innocence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: freedom from willful involvement in a particular crime or offense

lexunit.name: blood on hands.n
lexunit.definition: FN: guilt, especially for having caused death or injury.

frame.name: Imprisonment
frame.definition:
The Authorities put a Prisoner in Prison as punishment for an Offense.
Ex: ["pri" US Drug Researcher] IMPRISONED ["off" for FDA Fraud]. Ex: Men will be more likely to be PUT AWAY ["con" for murder rather than manslaughter] ["off" for killing their wives]. Ex: However, any treatments may be years in the future and in the meantime, ["pri" criminals] will continue to be IMPRISONED ["pur" for public safety].
Ex: ["aut" The government] wrongfully IMPRISONED ["pri" them] ["jai" in ?detention centers?] (a nice term for concentration camps), tortured them mentally and physically

fe.name: Prisoner
fe.definition:
The person who is confined in a penal institution.
Ex: ["pri" Man] Falsely IMPRISONED for 24 Years Seeks Damages

fe.name: Prison
fe.definition: The Prison within which the Prisoner comes to be confined.

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition:
The Authorities are the institution or actors carrying out the imprisonment.
Ex: When she returned, ["aut" the Chaoyang Town government authorities] IMPRISONED her for 5 days.

fe.name: Offense
fe.definition:
The action that the Prisoner is being punished for.
Ex: After all, Dowdy was not IMPRISONED ["off" for taking a bribe or even thinking about taking a bribe, but rather for committing perjury against two government witnesses who themselves eventually were imprisoned for defrauding the government].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Prisoner is kept.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the imprisonment happens.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose of the imprisonment.
Ex: City officials later release the blacks and say they IMPRISONED them ["pur" in order to protect them from rioters].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Authorities that brings about the imprisonment.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the imprisoning event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Authorities that affect the action (_ruthlessly_).

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The act or state of affairs that the Authorities respond to by imprisoning the Prisoner.
Ex: Though both of my grandparents were born in Canada and grew up speaking English and never had been to Japan, during the Second World War, the Canadian government IMPRISONED them ["rea" because of their Japanese genes].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Authorities maintains the confinement of the Prisoner.
Ex: Enforcement officers caught up with Irma and IMPRISONED her ["dur" for two weeks].

fe.name: Conviction
fe.definition:
The legal classification which characterizes the Offense.
Ex: Alf leader is IMPRISONED ["con" for Arson and Burglary].

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: Iteration marks expressions that indicate the number of times the Prisoner was imprisoned.

lexunit.name: imprison.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put or keep in prison

lexunit.name: imprisonment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of confining, or the state of being confined or confining

lexunit.name: put away.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confine someone in a prison

lexunit.name: jail.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put (someone) in jail.

lexunit.name: incarcerate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: imprison or confine.

lexunit.name: incarceration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of putting (a criminal) in prison.

frame.name: Replacing
frame.definition:
An Agent changes the filler of a Role by placing a New filler in the position after the Old filler ceases to occupy the position. Often this entails the Agent removing the Old filler. In most cases the Role is implicit.
Ex: If ["Agent" you] REPLACE ["Old" me] ["New" with a robot], who's gonna make excuses to your wife for you?
Ex: ["Time" Following Keating 's resignation from the Cabinet] ["Agent" Hawke] ["Time" immediately] REPLACED ["Old" him] as Deputy Prime Minister ["New" with Brian Howe , Minister for Community Services and Health].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the replacement.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs actions resulting in the New entity occupying the position.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an New entity so that it ends up in the position.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies where the Agent installs the New entity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent places the New entity in a position.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent installs the New entity.

fe.name: New
fe.definition:
The New entity is the person or thing that the Agent sets to fill a Role.
Ex: I don't know; perhaps you could SUBSTITUTE ["New" regular sugar].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics or states of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in placing the New filler in a position.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the New entity is affected by the Agent. Degrees of replacement are generally only possible when there are multiple New and Old entities.
Ex: He REPLACED the 6761 models ["deg" entirely] with about half as many 6800s.

fe.name: Old
fe.definition:
The entity that formerly occupied the position.
Ex: If you SUBSTITUTE a 15" arm ["old" for the 50cm one], it works pretty well. Ex: Please REPLACE ["old" the broken fixture] as soon as possible.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The category that the New and Old entities fit into as a result of the function they serve.
Ex: AN AUSTRALIAN state has proposed the country adopt a bill of rights and REPLACE the Queen ["rol" as head of state] with an Australian president .

lexunit.name: replace.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to put something new in the place of something

lexunit.name: substitute.v
lexunit.definition: COD: replace with another

lexunit.name: replacement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action or process of replacing

lexunit.name: substitution.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of substituting one thing for another

lexunit.name: swap out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to remove and immediately replace

lexunit.name: exchange.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to part with for a substitute

lexunit.name: change.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remove (something dirty or faulty) and replace it with another of the same kind.

lexunit.name: switch.v
lexunit.definition: FN: replace with

frame.name: Studying
frame.definition:
A Student enrolls and then remains at an Institution for the purposes of education within a Subject. They may receive instruction from a particular Teacher at the Institution. The Place, Time, and Duration of the study may also be specified.
Ex: ["Student" He] spent ten years STUDYING ["Subject" physics] ["Institution" at the lycee] before he flunked out.

fe.name: Teacher
fe.definition:
One who instructs a Student in some area of knowledge or skill.
Ex: She STUDIED ["tea" from him] for years.

fe.name: Student
fe.definition: One who receives instruction from a Teacher or Institution.

fe.name: Institution
fe.definition: An educational establishment, such as a school or college.

fe.name: Subject
fe.definition:
The area of knowledge or skill which is taught to a Student.
Ex: She STUDIES ["Subject" astrophysics].

fe.name: Level
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Level of a student in his/her education. Ex: a ["Level" graduate] student Ex: a ["Level" fourth grade] student

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A state which describes the Student during the process of study.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner of studying that the Student has.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the student is studying.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is the location within which the studying takes place.
NOTE: Consider whether a possible Place phrase is really where the training took place or is rather part of a description of the Institution.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the process of study is ongoing.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Student studies the Subject.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the Studying event.

fe.name: Motivation
fe.definition:
The Student's motivation for studying.
Ex: He is STUDYING ["Motivation" for his Master's] .

lexunit.name: study.v
lexunit.definition: COD: apply oneself to study.

frame.name: Exclude_member
frame.definition: A former Member of a Group ceases to be a member as a result of the action of an Authority within the Group. (In directly democratic Groups, the Authority may consist of the Group itself as a voting whole.)

fe.name: Member
fe.definition:
The person who used to belong to a Group.
Ex: I 'm afraid that ["mm" I] was EXPELLED from the Society after they found I endorsed him.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition:
A set of people standing in a semi-permanent relationship together.
Ex: Giles bemoaned his EXPULSION ["Group" from the Future Farmers of America]

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition: An empowered subset of the Group which decides to expel its former Member.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the Member is excluded.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A cause, reason, or other explanation for the exclusion of the Member.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the Member is excluded.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Authority excludes the Member.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes a participant in the exclusion event.

lexunit.name: expel.v
lexunit.definition: FN: force to leave

lexunit.name: excommunicate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: officially exclude from participation in the sacraments and services of the Christian Church.

lexunit.name: expulsion.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of expelling

lexunit.name: excommunication.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of officially excluding from participation in the sacraments and services of the Christian Church.

frame.name: Memorization
frame.definition:
A Cognizer applies themself to commit a Pattern to memory, so that the Cognizer would recognize future examples of the Pattern or be able to reproduce it.
Ex: ["cog" A gaggle of students] were ["man" frantically] MEMORIZING ["pat" the answers] ["pla" out in the hall]. Ex: It is possible to MEMORIZE ["mea" by rote] and at the same time have a full grasp of the underlying meaning. ["cog" CNI] ["pat" INI]
This frame differs from Education_teaching in that the Cognizer is construed as acting alone, with no indication of an interacting individual that provides guidance.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The sentient being that focuses on a Pattern so that it will remain in the memory.
Ex: ["cog" I] have MEMORIZED two kinds of knowledge from Allah's Apostle

fe.name: Pattern
fe.definition:
The phenomenon that the Cognizer observes and commits to memory.
Ex: Impress your friends by MEMORIZING ["pat" your phone numbers] and throwing away your PDA!

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Cognizer memorizes the Pattern.
Ex: Barney MEMORIZED the poem ["tim" yesterday].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location wherein the Cognizer memorizes the Pattern.
Ex: Herbert Kornfeldt MEMORIZED his speech ["pla" in the mailroom].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the memorization event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: ["man" Hurriedly], the bus-driver MEMORIZED the new route.

fe.name: Completeness
fe.definition:
The exactness of the match between the Cognizer's memory and the Pattern.
Ex: Whomever you emulate, internalize the sound of the soloist and MEMORIZE it ["com" exactly].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Cognizer by which they achieve memorization.
Ex: Don't MEMORIZE Morse code ["mea" by counting dots and dashes].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The goal that the Cognizer has in mind, which they believe will be accomplished by memorization.

lexunit.name: memorise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: learn by heart.

lexunit.name: memorization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of committing to memory

lexunit.name: learn.v
lexunit.definition: COD: commit to memory.

lexunit.name: commit_to_memory.v
lexunit.definition: COD: memorize

frame.name: Distinctiveness
frame.definition:
A Feature of an Entity serves to distinguish the Entity from other members of its type which have a different value for the Feature. Note that the Entity is often implicit.
Ex: His DISTINCTIVE flowing ["Feature" gait] and skill with the rapier set him apart from his fellows. Ex: ["Feature" The swinging axe-kick] was CHARACTERISTIC ["Entity" of Xena].

fe.name: Feature
fe.definition:
The aspect of the Entity which makes it different from the other members of its class.
Ex: That never depleting ammo in his arsenal - his SIGNATURE ["fea" smile] - is contagious.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The item which differs from other members of its class in the Feature's value.
Ex: These signatures may be DISTINCTIVE ["ent" of the entire Chlamydiales order].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the values of the Feature of the Entity and the Comparison_set are similar to each other.
Ex: The twins have a ["Degree" very] DISTINCT walk.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

lexunit.name: characteristic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: typical of a particular person, place, or thing.

lexunit.name: trademark.a
lexunit.definition: FN: distinctive

lexunit.name: signature.a
lexunit.definition: FN: characteristic

lexunit.name: distinctive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: individually characteristic; distinct from others of its kind.

lexunit.name: distinct.a
lexunit.definition: COD: recognizably different in nature; individual or separate

lexunit.name: characterize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a feature or quality) be characteristic of.

lexunit.name: signature.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a distinctive product or characteristic by which someone or something can be identified

lexunit.name: characteristic.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a feature or quality typical of a person, place, or thing.

lexunit.name: trademark.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a distinctive characteristic

lexunit.name: aspect.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular part or feature.

frame.name: Typicality
frame.definition:
An Entity is generally, or with regard to a particular Feature, representative of the Comparison_set of which it is a member.
Ex: The Elan truly is an UNUSUAL ["ent" car]; the first and only Lotus with a front engined/front wheel drive layout, and the first new Lotus to be introduced since 1975.
Ex: I need a plain, VANILLA ["ent" example] that doesn't use PRINT!
Ex: How smart is the AVERAGE ["ent" drug user/experimenter]?
Ex: It's not UNUSUAL ["Entity" to be loved by anyone], It's not unusual to have fun with anyone,
Ex: Is ["Feature" lying] NORMAL ["com" for a child this age], and how can I best handle this situation?

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Entity

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The concrete or abstract thing which is evaluated with regard to whether it exhibits the essential characteristics of a Comparison_set.
Ex: However I have always loved having an UNUSUAL ["ent" name] and I think it's a beautiful name. .

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition:
The set of indviduals, which are of similar kind to the Entity, and to which the Entity is compared.
Ex: It's not UNUSUAL ["com" for interviewers] to look beyond a resume and face-to-face meeting to find the unspoken clues about your personality.

fe.name: Feature
fe.definition:
A property of the Entity wherein it differs or is similar to members of a Comparison_set.
Ex: David Hasselhoff's daughters are NORMAL ["fea" in every way].

lexunit.name: normal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: conforming to a standard; usual, typical, or expected.

lexunit.name: unusual.a
lexunit.definition: COD: remarkable; exceptional.

lexunit.name: ordinary.a
lexunit.definition: COD: with no distinctive features; normal or usual

lexunit.name: average.a
lexunit.definition: COD: a usual or ordinary amount, level, or rate.

lexunit.name: odd.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unusual or unexpected; strange

lexunit.name: commonplace.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not unusual; ordinary

lexunit.name: vanilla.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having no special or extra features.

frame.name: Using
frame.definition: An Agent manipulates an Instrument in order to achieve a Purpose.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent uses the Instrument to achieve their Purpose.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent uses the Instrument.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent uses the Instrument.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the Agent uses the Instrument.
Ex: I went and USED that ball ["tim" yesterday] and i bowled 5 games and i left about 14 ten pins with it.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent uses the Instrument.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_ deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Agent that serves to bring about the Purpose of the Agent.
Ex: For cold conditions, we recommend USING ["ins" a heat gun or a hair dryer] to make the adhesive work better.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
An Instrument that has a function associated with it.
Ex: Mirabella shared the mischievous vision of childlike exuberance and USED ["Instrument" the chair] ["rol" as a pseudo jungle gym].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition:
The Outcome is the failure or success of the Agent's using the Instrument to achieve their Purpose.
Ex: It has been USED ["out" successfully] in physician offices, schools, and in sensory function laboratories for over 35 years.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
An event within which the Agent uses the Instrument. Often, the Containing_event will also give an indication of the Agent's Purpose.
Ex: In the 1950s, the titanium metal industry was established primarily in response to the emerging aerospace industry which USED it ["con" in the manufacture of airframe] .

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Depicitive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: This FE identifies the population within which the Using event occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Instrument or the Using act and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

lexunit.name: use.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take, hold, or deploy as a means of accomplishing or achieving something

lexunit.name: employ.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make use of.

lexunit.name: use.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of using or state of being used.

lexunit.name: avail oneself.v
lexunit.definition: COD: use or take advantage of.

lexunit.name: operate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: control a device (in order to acheive the prototypical function of the device).

lexunit.name: operation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of operating.

lexunit.name: apply.v
lexunit.definition: FN: put to use

lexunit.name: utilise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make practical and effective use of.

lexunit.name: utilisation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: making practical and effective use of

lexunit.name: application.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of putting something into operation.

lexunit.name: operational.a
lexunit.definition: COD: relating to the operation

lexunit.name: employment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: application or use in a particular situation.

frame.name: People_by_residence
frame.definition:
This frame contains words for individuals, i.e. humans, with respect to their proximity of residence. This relationship may be defined either symmetrically (as Residents) or asymmetrically (in terms of a Known_resident and a Indicated_resident). The Residents or the Indicated_resident may have an Age, Descriptor, Persistent_characteristic, or Ethnicity specified.
Ex: The dead included homeowner Todd Underfoot, 33, his wife Spring Back Underfoot, 32, ["kno" their] HOUSEMATE, ["ind" Luisa Life], 46, and two of the Underfoot's three children. Ex: ["kno" I] _have_ a ["eth" Swedish] ["ind" ROOMMATE] that translated for me!

fe.name: Known_resident
fe.definition:
The individual(s) that serve(s) as a reference point for the definition of the Indicated_resident due to the proximity of residences.
Ex: I have no problem with him becoming ["kno" Madonna's] NEIGHBOUR at all!

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
The place in which the ["res" Residents] or the ["ind" Indicated_resident] reside.
Ex: My old HOUSE-MATE ["loc" in Berkeley] thought it was a hilarious idea.

fe.name: Indicated_resident
fe.definition:
A person or group of people defined in terms of the fact that they reside in the proximity of the Known_resident.
Ex: ["ind" Bill Jankelow] is my HOUSE-MATE.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition:
The Age is the length of time the Indicated_resident has been alive.
Ex: Perhaps you know someone who has been doing errands for an ["age" elderly] NEIGHBOUR for years, or has performed an extraordinary act of heroism or kindness.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Indicated_resident.
Ex: If Western's administration is not careful about how they handle themselves in this situation, they could find themselves with some very ["des" angry] NEIGHBOURS on their front doorstep.

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition:
The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Indicated_resident which is concieved of as persisting over time.
Ex: We don't know his more ["per" irascible] NEIGHBOURS, of course, but we warm to them anyway.

fe.name: Residents
fe.definition:
The individuals who reside in proximity to each other.
Ex: ["res" Smithers and Kornfeldt] _are_ NEIGHBORS.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition:
The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Indicated_resident belongs.
Ex: With the real estate boom, half of my ["eth" Polish] NEIGHBOURS have sold their properties for a hefty price to young, left-wing, educated professionals.

lexunit.name: roommate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person occupying the same room, flat, or house as another.

lexunit.name: housemate.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A person occupying the same house, flat or apartment as another

lexunit.name: neighbor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person living next door to or very near to another.

frame.name: Participation
frame.definition:
An Event with multiple Participants takes place. It can be presented either symmetrically with Participants or asymmetrically, giving Participant_1 greater prominence over Participant_2. If the Event is engaged in intentionally, then there is typically a shared Purpose between the Participants. It is, however, possible that an expressed Purpose only applies to Participant_1.
Ex: MATAC looks forward to ["par1" your] PARTICIPATION ["eve" in helping promote telework in the Mid-Atlantic region].
Ex: FOAP provides PARTICIPANTS with comprehensive clerical skills. ["eve" DNI] Ex: FOAP provides ["par" participants] with comprehensive clerical skills.
Ex: ["par1" Our eight-year-old son] _was_ ["tim" recently] ["deg" peripherally] INVOLVED ["eve" in an incident which resulted in him being threatened with the strap].
Ex: A New York press agent must scramble when ["par1" his major client] _becomes_ EMBROILED ["eve" in a huge scandal].
Ex: ["Time" In his time as a first-team all-league player], ["Participant_1" Rife] _was_ IN ["Event" on 86 solo tackles].

fe.name: Participants
fe.definition:
The individuals or entities that have been participants in an Event.
Ex: Thereafter, ["par" everybody] PARTICIPATED in the 17 May parade ending in the Nordic Club.

fe.name: Participant_1
fe.definition:
Participant_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in an Event with multiple Participants.
Ex: Last year, ["par1" Bill] PARTICIPATED in the Montana State University Earth Systems Science distance learning course in the Atmosphere Unit.

fe.name: Participant_2
fe.definition:
A grammatically less prominent participant of an Event with multiple Participants.
Ex: The Second Amended Complaint alleges that Andrew S. Pitt ("Pitt"), Conectisys Corporation ("Conectisys" or the "Company"), and BM Capital Corp. PARTICIPATED ["par2" with Zaman and Smith Benton] in a fraudulent and manipulative trading scheme.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
An Event with multiple Participants, who may or may not be involved intentionally.
Ex: Some who PARTICIPATED ["eve" in D-Day] are finally ready to talk about it

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the multiple-participant Event occurs.
Ex: A survey of students who PARTICIPATED ["tim" last year] showed that 61 percent would be the first in their family to attend college.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Event involving multiple Participants occurs.
Ex: The most exciting tours for Mr. Osako were when he PARTICIPATED ["pla" in France, Belgium, Holland, Cuba and Japan].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). When the Participants are understood agentively frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of them that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
Ex: He had performed well on the varsity wrestling team and PARTICIPATED ["man" eagerly] in student government

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Participants or PARTICIPANT_1 intend to accomplish by performing the action indicated by the Event.
Ex: Mahoney PARTICIPATED ["pur" in order to protest racism in the United States in general].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by Participant_1 or the Participants that contributes to bringing off the Event.
Ex: WICS-TV PARTICIPATED ["mea" by handing out pamphlets, corporate job opening lists and other information regarding employment opportunities within the broadcasting field].

fe.name: Degree_of_involvement
fe.definition:
The extent to which Participant_1 contributes to the Event's coming off.
Ex: We built a new hospital here in 1991, but I was on the board then and only ["deg" peripherally] INVOLVED.

fe.name: Institution
fe.definition:
A group, location, or institution conventionally associated with an Event.
Ex: Several of the countries were unable to PARTICIPATE ["ins" in the market] .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE describes the length of time for which participation occurs (usually appears as a for-PP)

lexunit.name: participate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take part.

lexunit.name: participant.n
lexunit.definition: FN: somebody who participates in an event

lexunit.name: participation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of participating in a process or the state of participating in a relationship

lexunit.name: concerned.a
lexunit.definition: SMV: involved in an event

lexunit.name: involved.a
lexunit.definition: FN: engaged as a (willing or unwilling) participant

lexunit.name: involvement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of participating in an event with multiple participants

lexunit.name: embroiled.a
lexunit.definition: FN: deeply involved in a conflict or difficult situation.

lexunit.name: player.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person that is involved and influential in an activity.

lexunit.name: entangled.a
lexunit.definition: FN: participating involuntarily, without the ability to stop participating at once

lexunit.name: entanglement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: involuntary involvement in a complex affair such that rapid extrication is impossible.

lexunit.name: in.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: taking part in

lexunit.name: take part.v
lexunit.definition: COD: join in or be involved in an activity.

lexunit.name: party.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a participant in an event.

frame.name: Secrecy_status
frame.definition:
A Phenomenon, which may be an activity, state or object, is purposefully hidden from the awareness of a potential Cognizer. The person responsible for the hiding of the Phenomenon is not part of this frame and cannot be syntactically realized. The potential Cognizer may be realized, but is in fact rarely expressed. A period of Time during which the Phenomenon is secret may be indicated.
Ex: Few people would use ATMs if ["phe" the content of their transaction] _was_ SECRET ["cog" from their bank] and there was no paper trail verifying the transaction. .
Ex: The protesters were not on her list, and weren't allowed in, despite the fact that ["phe" the meeting] _was_ PUBLIC.
Ex: ["phe" Student disciplinary matters] are CONFIDENTIAL and should only be discussed with appropriate university officials

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: The Phenomenon is the activity, state or object that is purposefully hidden from the awareness of a potential cognizer.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Phenomenon is hidden from cognizers.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
A period of Time during which the Phenomenon is hidden from the awareness of potential cognizers.
Ex: There was stuff in there that was 'SECRET' ["Time" in the 1980s], but has since become pretty common knowledge.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the person who might become aware of the Phenomenon if it was not concealed.
Ex: Moreover, the blood and decorations were sacred and could only be removed in a procedure which was SECRET ["cog" from women]

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modifies the target to indicate the legal- or "by rule" domain within which it is true or operational. This legal domain is in contrast to reality, which may or may not reflect the "official" state-of-affairs. This FE can be realized in words like "formally" and"officially" plus maybe "technically" and "in law."

lexunit.name: clandestine.a
lexunit.definition: COD: surreptitious

lexunit.name: surreptitious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: covert or clandestine

lexunit.name: covert.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not openly acknowledged or displayed.

lexunit.name: secret.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not known or seen or not meant to be known or seen by others

lexunit.name: secretly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: in a secret manner, in secret

lexunit.name: open.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not concealed; manifest.

lexunit.name: public.a
lexunit.definition: COD: done, perceived, or existing in open view.

lexunit.name: confidential.a
lexunit.definition: COD: intended to be kept secret

lexunit.name: publicly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: done, perceived, or existing in open view

lexunit.name: concealed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: kept secret

lexunit.name: unclassified.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not officially designated as secret.

lexunit.name: shadowy.a
lexunit.definition: FN: concealed, obscured.

frame.name: Reveal_secret
frame.definition:
A Speaker reveals Information that was previously secret to an Addressee. In some cases, the Addressee is expected to keep the Information from other parties. The Information may be damaging to the reputation of the Speaker. Some lexical units in this frame imply that the Speaker has already been confronted with the Information.
Ex: Could it be true that Martin himself was ["spe" the one who] SPILLED the BEANS ["top" on Pops and Brad's planned wedding]?

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The Speaker is the sentient entity that reveals the Information (whether spoken or written).
Ex: ["spe" Kornfeldt] REVEALED that he had embezzled more than twice the amount his company owned.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee is the person to whom the Information is revealed.
Ex: Evelyn CONFESSED ["add" to Barney Holesum] about what had happened. Ex: An unknown intern in the White House LEAKED the "lunch menu" ["add" to the press].

fe.name: Information
fe.definition:
The Information is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is revealing to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase.
Ex: You shouldn't REVEAL ["inf" any murders you've been involved in], if you know what I mean.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the subject matter about which the Speaker is speaking. It normally only appears with noun targets, or in special constructions.
Ex: REVELATIONS ["top" about the coming of the Christ] surfaced in early Mediaeval times.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the revelation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the revelation (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_, _maliciously_).

fe.name: Completeness
fe.definition:
The degree to which Information is revealed.
Ex: When she confessed, she confessed ["com" completely].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Speaker makes a revelation. Ex: He REVEALED his true feelings about the matter ["mea" by giving her the thumbs-up behind his back].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to the revelation.
Ex: ["ica" Out of spite] Spuddmeier revealed his boss's affair.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement. Ex: Kim CONFIDED in me ["Medium" over the phone].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Speaker during the statement.
Ex: He LET SLIP his involvement in the coverup ["dep" in a drunken stupor] at an embassy party.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the revelation is made.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The FE specifies the place where the Information is revealed.
Ex: According to the report, he CONFESSED to eating onions and gargling with generic mouthwash ["pla" at the station].

fe.name: Re-encoding
fe.definition: An alternative description of expressed action

fe.name: Location_of_protagonist
fe.definition: This frame element is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion. In Release 1.2, this FE has various frame-specific names including Location of perceiver, or Location of participant; it was even (incorrectly) labelled Place in some frames.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Source_material
fe.definition: The medium in which the secret Information origninally resided.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole especially any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames.

fe.name: Period of iterations
fe.definition: This FE describes the length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: Frequency is defined as the number of times the Reveal_secret event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the revealed secret.

lexunit.name: reveal.v
lexunit.definition: COD: disclose (previously unknown or secret information).

lexunit.name: disclose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make (secret or new information) known.

lexunit.name: revelation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: making (secret or new information) known.

lexunit.name: expose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reveal the true, objectionable nature of.

lexunit.name: disclosure.n
lexunit.definition: FN: making (previously secret information) known

lexunit.name: divulge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make known.

lexunit.name: divulgence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: public revelation of previously secret information

lexunit.name: confess.v
lexunit.definition: COD: admit to a crime or wrongdoing.

lexunit.name: confession.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a statement admitting to a crime

lexunit.name: confide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: tell someone about a secret or private matter in confidence.

lexunit.name: spill beans.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reveal secret information unintentionally or indiscreetly.

lexunit.name: come_clean.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to tell the whole story

lexunit.name: let_slip.v
lexunit.definition: FN: reveal or divulge secret information.

lexunit.name: leak.v
lexunit.definition: COD: intentionally disclose (secret information).

lexunit.name: tip hand.v
lexunit.definition: FN: reveal inadvertantly

lexunit.name: admit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confess to be true or to be the case.

lexunit.name: come forward.v
lexunit.definition: FN: Volunteer information

lexunit.name: fess up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: admit information

frame.name: Ordinal_numbers
frame.definition:
An Item is picked out either by the order in which the members of a set would be encountered by an implicit cognizer, or by the order in which the members of a set participate in an event or state which serves as the Basis_of_order. The former case usually involves a Starting_point for going through the set, while the latter involves a Basis_of_order, which is normally an event that the Item along with other members of its Comparison_set has participated in. Note that Item should be annotated on a second layer, except in cases when the noun structure the ordinal participates in is predicative.
Ex: The FIRST ["typ" car] ["sta" from the left] _is_ a Magosix. Ex: ["ite" The first car from the left] is a Magosix. Ex: ["Item" Barney] _was_ only the SECOND ["Type" Asian student] ["bas" at my college]. Ex: ["ite" Felix] _was_ the FIRST ["com" of my cats] ["bas" to realize that human food was tastier]. Ex: Felix was the FIRST ["typ" of my cats] to realize that human food was tastier.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
The kind of entity that the Item belongs to.
Ex: Capitalizes the first letter of the FIRST ["typ" word] in each sentence

fe.name: Starting_point
fe.definition:
A usually spatial reference point from which the implicit cognizer scans across the members of the Comparison_set.
Ex: Yes, I covered the cycle issue in the SECOND paragraph ["sta" from the top].

fe.name: Basis_of_order
fe.definition:
A kind of event in which the members of the Comparison_set, including the Item, participate in a certain order.
Ex: Lorna was the THIRD student ["bas" to be expelled from the Academy].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The entity picked out by the implicit cognizer as occupying a certain place in the ordered Comparison_set.
Ex: Bennett is the FIFTH woman to be showcased. Ex: Bennett is ["ite" the fifth woman to be showcased].

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition:
A set of entites of which the Item is a member and which are ordered either by the Basis_of_order or by the order in which the implicit cognizer focuses attention on them.
Ex: The FIRST student ["com" of the college] to cross the ramp will present the name-card reader with a card having the name of the college printed on it. .

lexunit.name: first.a
lexunit.definition: COD: coming before all others in time or order.

lexunit.name: second.a
lexunit.definition: COD: constituting number two in a sequence; coming after the first in time or order

lexunit.name: third.a
lexunit.definition: COD: constituting number three in a sequence

lexunit.name: fourth.a
lexunit.definition: COD: constituting number four in a sequence

lexunit.name: fifth.a
lexunit.definition: COD: constituting number five in a sequence

lexunit.name: thirteenth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: constituting number thirteen in a sequence.

lexunit.name: nineteenth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: number 19 in a sequence.

lexunit.name: last.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the final one in a set

lexunit.name: eighth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: number 8 in a set

lexunit.name: tenth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: number 10 in a set

lexunit.name: ninth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: number 9 in a set

lexunit.name: seventeenth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: number 17 in a set

lexunit.name: sixteenth.a
lexunit.definition: FN: number 16 in a set

lexunit.name: final.a
lexunit.definition: FN: The last in a set

frame.name: Attributed_information
frame.definition:
A Proposition is attributed to a Speaker or a Text.
Ex: ACCORDING TO ["spe" the Press Trust of India] ["tex" in an article published on its Web site Thursday], ["pro" the woman has been identified as 31-year-old Aafia Siddiqui, who was being sought by U.S. officials last week along with two other men, including one whose last known address was in Miramar, Fla].
Ex: In addition, ACCORDING TO ["tex" Section I3.5b], ["pro" the spacing of stud shear connectors along the length of a supporting beam shall not exceed 36?].
Ex: ACCORDING TO ["spe" the Pope], ["pro" Muslims believe in the same God] and according to Jesus, Muslims are the greatest in Heaven.

fe.name: Proposition
fe.definition:
The information attributed to the Speaker or Text.
Ex: ["pro" Parents are present at and involved in the purchase or rental of games 83 percent of the time], ACCORDING TO a September 2000 Federal Trade Commission report

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
A sentient entity that has communicated the information encoded by the Proposition.
Ex: With the first big batch of music now blocked from Napster's file-swapping network, the average number of songs available on the service has dropped precipitously, ACCORDING TO ["spe" at least one research company].

fe.name: Text
fe.definition:
A written or verbal collection of statements, which imparts the information of the Proposition.
Ex: The son of the Syrian defense minister received 6 million barrels, ACCORDING TO ["tex" the document], worth about $3 million.

lexunit.name: according to.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: as stated by or in.

lexunit.name: on authority of.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: attributing to

lexunit.name: source.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who provides information.

lexunit.name: viewpoint.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person or other type of source that provides the proposition

frame.name: Cause_to_end
frame.definition:
An Agent or Cause causes a Process or State to end.
Ex: ["age" Bush] may LIFT ["sta" sanctions] on his own, despite opposition.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: Name of the event which is brought to an end.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Agent that causes the Process to end.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
Where the Process or State is caused to end.
Ex: They ENDED their relationship ["Place" in the same coffeehouse where it started].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the event is ended.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the event is ended.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Process is brought to an end.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event that causes the Process to end.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner of causing the Process to end.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual who causes the Process or State to end.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event that causes the Process to be ended.
Ex: ["cau" That move] ENDED her political career, she said in a 1994 Times Union interview.

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
A State which is ended by the Agent or Cause.
Ex: We should END ["sta" poverty].

lexunit.name: lift.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally remove or end (a legal restriction, decision, etc.).

lexunit.name: end.v
lexunit.definition: FN: bring to an end

lexunit.name: lifting.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of formally ending (esp. a restriction)

lexunit.name: arrest.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stop a process or freeze a state either permanently or temporarily

lexunit.name: put an end to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to be ended.

frame.name: Sign_agreement
frame.definition:
A Signatory signs an Agreement document, thereby taking on a commitment encoded in the Agreement.
Ex: . ["Time" During this time], ["sig1" 84 countries (including the United States)] SIGNED ["agr" the Protocol].

fe.name: Signatory
fe.definition:
The signatory of the Agreement.
Ex: ["sig1" Eisenhower] SIGNED a treaty with aliens.

fe.name: Signature
fe.definition:
The entity signifying the identity of the Signatory, resulting from the act of writing on the Agreement document.
Ex: The Attorney General seemingly never _put_ his ["sig" SIGNATURE] on the agreement.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
An expression of the state of the Signatory at the time of signing.
Ex: Jean SIGNED the contract ["dep" naked].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Signatory that interacts with the Agreement document so as to produce the Signature.
Ex: He SIGNED the contract ["ins" with a mixture of his own blood and spit].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the signing occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Signatory that also affect the action (_happily_, _eagerly_).
Ex: Bob ["man" eagerly] SIGNED the contract.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the action whereby the Signatory achieves the signing of the Agreement.
Ex: He SIGNED the contract ["mea" by writing his name, Cornelis Wynkoop].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose for which the Signatory commits to the Agreement.
Ex: ["pur" In order to become a Party] Australia will need to SIGN the Protocol by 31 March 1998 and then take the binding step of ratification.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which signature is given.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for putting signature to paper.

fe.name: Agreement
fe.definition:
The document which encodes the commitment of the Signatory.
Ex: I SIGNED ["agr" the contract] and now the dealership claims they made a mistake, quoted the price too low and now I have to pay them more money.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: The Co_participant signs the Agreement along with the Signatory.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: his extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The category of the Signatory in the Sign_agreement event.

lexunit.name: sign.v
lexunit.definition: FN: write one's name on (something) for the purposes of indicating agreement

lexunit.name: signature.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person's name written in a distinctive way as a form of indicating agreement

lexunit.name: signatory.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a party that has signed an agreement.

lexunit.name: accede.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become a party to a agreement or treaty

frame.name: Research
frame.definition:
A Researcher (an individual a group or institution) attempts to answer a Question by means of consulting literature, observation, or conducting experiments in a particular Field pertinent to the Question. The Question may be underspecified in the form of a Topic.
Ex: ["res" Simmons and Nadel] did RESEARCH ["top" pertaining to Ardea purpurea and Egretta garzetta] ["tim" in 1998]

fe.name: Researcher
fe.definition:
The people engaged in a research endeavor.
Ex: Before he became an astronaut, ["res" Grunsfeld] _did_ RESEARCH in physics.

fe.name: Field
fe.definition:
An area of inquiry.
Ex:

fe.name: Question
fe.definition:
A significant unanswered open proposition which the Researcher is attempting to resolve.
Ex: When we have RESEARCHED ["que" why Brazilian mothers have stopped breastfeeding], principal reasons given are 'poor milk' and 'insufficient milk' .

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
A phenomenon or idea involved in a Question.
Ex: Would you take part in RESEARCH ["top" on the best place to have a baby]?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the research is carried out.
Ex: ["tim" During summer of 1999], I did RESEARCH using a technique called "Path Integral Monte Carlo", to simulate quantum particles.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The experimentations, observations, or other procedures performed by the Researcher in order to find an answer to the Question.
Ex: The workgroup has RESEARCHED this issue ["mea" by reviewing the basin plans of other regions and other various sources].

fe.name: Population
fe.definition:
A group of entities that are studied by the Researcher to answer the Question. The studied group need not be the only kind of entity that provides evidence for answering the research Question.
Ex: Prior researchers have INVESTIGATED senile dementia ["pop" in relatively small populations].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Researcher that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: The West Chicago Park District ["man" carefully] RESEARCHED how much of an increase was needed to accomplish all of our goals.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
Purpose indicates an action that the Researcher intends to accomplish by performing research.
Ex: We RESEARCH this fungus ["pur" to fight ailments in tobacco and tomato fields].

fe.name: Duration_of_state
fe.definition:
The Duration_of_state is the period of time over which the research takes place.
Ex: That particular think tank RESEARCHED population change ["dur" for over three decades].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The physical place where the research is carried out.
Ex: Johnson and Randall's RESEARCH ["pla" in Africa] has proven extremely valuable.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
The Type, or subclass of research.
Ex: His lab conducts a lot of ["typ" mainstream] RESEARCH. Ex: Several institutes exist only for ["typ" theoretical] RESEARCH.

lexunit.name: research.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry out research into

lexunit.name: research.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions.

lexunit.name: investigate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: carry out research into (a subject).

frame.name: Inclusion
frame.definition: A Total has a Part, either as a member of an aggregate or as a constituent part of a simple entity.

fe.name: Total
fe.definition:
A complex entity, either an aggregate or a unit, of which a Part, a constituent or a component, is specified.
Ex: ["tot" His collection] INCLUDED two El Grecos

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A component or constituent that is specified to form part of the Total.
Ex: The larger album INCLUDES ["par" designs for his house at Whitehall].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE indicates the purpose for which some implicit (non-expressed) agent causes the inclusion of the Part within the Total. Ex: This electronic transmission INCLUDES encryption protocols ["pur" in order to prevent outside surveillance].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE identifies the frequency with which the Part is included int he Total. Ex: Software packages ["fre" often] CONTAIN promotional items.

fe.name: Contrast_set
fe.definition: This FE indicates other elements that are included within the Total. Ex: This book INCLUDES ["con" among other things] three chapters on macroeconomics.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the sub-location of the Total in which the Part is included.
Ex: This plan INCLUDES ["sub" within the final stage] three separate sub-stages. Ex: My list CONTAINS four names ["sub" in the final section].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Total includes the Part.
Ex: ["tim" Last year] the recognized departments INCLUDED the Russian and East European Institute, and the Office of International Programs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the Total includes the Part.
Ex: ["pla" In California], the category EXCLUDES minors and the mentally ill.

lexunit.name: include.v
lexunit.definition: COD: comprise or contain as part of a whole

lexunit.name: contain.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to have as part

lexunit.name: among.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: being a member or members of (a larger set).

lexunit.name: amongst.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: occurring as part of a larger group of event.

lexunit.name: have.v
lexunit.definition: FN: include as a part.

lexunit.name: integrated.a
lexunit.definition: FN: forming part of a whole

lexunit.name: exclude.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deny access to; keep out.

lexunit.name: excluding.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: not taking into account; except.

lexunit.name: inclusive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: containing (a specified element) as part of a whole.

lexunit.name: including.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: containing as part of the whole being considered.

lexunit.name: incorporate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take in or include as part of a whole.

frame.name: Unattributed_information
frame.definition: A Reported_fact is presented by the speaker as deriving from statements (made directly to them or to others) of third parties.

fe.name: Reported_fact
fe.definition:
An assertion of a state, event, property or existence or the assignment to a category that the speaker attributes to unnamed others.
Ex: Four PURPORTED ["rep" gang members] could face death penalty in Virginia slaying of federal informant.
Ex: Lester Hayes was PURPORTEDLY ["rep" joined in this suit by his wife].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Reported_fact was reported.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The span of time for which the Reported_fact has been circulating.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which or the apparant cause of the Reported_fact.

lexunit.name: purported.a
lexunit.definition: FN: alleged

lexunit.name: purportedly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: allegedly

lexunit.name: allegedly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: according to unspecified sources

lexunit.name: alleged.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having been claimed to exist or occur by unmentioned sources

lexunit.name: ostensibly.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: apparently true, but not necessarily so.

lexunit.name: ostensible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: apparently true, but not necessarily so.

lexunit.name: reportedly.adv

frame.name: State_continue
frame.definition:
Despite some implication that a State would be interrupted, the Entity remains in the specified State. Note that State includes locative relations.
Ex: ["ent" Online security] remains ["sta" elusive]. Ex:

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Concrete or abstract Entity

fe.name: State
fe.definition: State of an Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the State is found to still persist.
Ex: Financial recovery REMAINS elusive ["tim" in 2002].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Entity is in the State.
Ex: Martial law REMAINS in effect ["pla" in Absurdistan].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The state of affairs that explains why the State persists.
Ex: Simandle ruled that the contract REMAINS in force ["rea" because the GTMUA accepted $400,000 in connection fees from the trust].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The time period over which the State continues to hold of the Entity.
Ex: Our commitment to high-quality, distinctively Canadian programming has REMAINED constant ["dur" for more than six decades].

fe.name: Circumstances

fe.name: Explanation

lexunit.name: stay.v

frame.name: Activity_resume
frame.definition:
An Agent resumes participation in an Activity. Progress on the Activity is retained from before the interruption.
Ex: ["act" Normal Service] Will Be RESUMED ["Time" Shortly]. ["age" CNI]
["age" The Kinshasa government] has RESUMED ["act" supporting Rwandan rebels].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of Time for which the Activity is resumed

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The Activity which is being resumed by the Agent.
Ex: We have RENEWED ["act" our efforts to gain federal recognition].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Activity is resumed.

fe.name: Time

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Activity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also mark indications of salient characteristics of the Agent which affect the Activity.
Ex: The stock market RESUMED trading ["Manner" in an orderly fashion] on Monday

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent who resumes an Activity that they were engaged in earlier.
Ex: ["age" We] RENEWED our efforts to get things completed.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: his FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The consequence of the resuming of the Activity.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: n general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

lexunit.name: renew.v

frame.name: Being_necessary
frame.definition:
A Dependent state-of-affairs has a Requirement as a prerequisite for obtaining or occurring.
Ex: ["req" The atomic bombings] _were_ probably not NECESSARY ["dep" to win WWII without a mainland invasion of Japan].
Ex: We will take the REQUIRED ["req" measures], regardless of the yelping of the left. ["dep" DNI]
Ex: ["reqe" Two tokens] _are_ NECESSARY ["Dependent" for county to county trips].

fe.name: Dependent
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.

fe.name: Requirement
fe.definition: The entity or state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which militates that the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.
Ex: Such care is NECESSARY ["Condition" if you operate under martial law].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.
Ex: Unfortunately, such tactics appear to be ["dom" politically] NECESSARY nowadays.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.
Ex: ["pla" In the US], the political clout of big city mayors is NECESSARY to put this on the national agenda.

fe.name: Dependent_individual
fe.definition:
The individual who needs to have the Required_entity or for the Requirement state of affairs to obtain.
Ex: We ask you to obtain for us all that is NECESSARY ["dep" for us].

fe.name: Required_entity
fe.definition: An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: An characteristic or feature of the Requirement or Required_entity.

lexunit.name: requirement.n
