frame.name: Project
frame.definition:
An Agent, which may be an individual or group, is engaged in a complex Activity. A larger Goal which motivates the Agent carrying out the Activity may be indicated. Instead of a particular Activity, a Field of endeavor may be indicated. The project may also have a Name and the Time when as well as the Place where it is ongoing may be specified.
Ex: The ["act" New Car Assessment] PROGRAM (NCAP) is dedicated to helping the public buy a safer car.
Ex: The school will continue with ["age" its] PROJECT ["goa" to end all vio- lence related to racism, xenophobia and intolerance].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individual or organization that carries out the project.
Ex: The ["age" DOE] Human Genome PROGRAM also has developed high-throughput approaches to identifying is-regulatory sequences in the human and other genomes

fe.name: Field
fe.definition:
An area of human endeavor, typically scientifc in nature, in which the Agent's Activity falls.
Ex: Several PROJECTS ["fie" in computational linguistics] have recently stalled due to lack of funding .

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
What the Agent (an individual or the members of an organization) are dedicated to doing.
Ex: The ["act" New Car Assessment] PROGRAM (NCAP) is dedicated to helping the public buy a safer car.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
A name given to the project for identification.
Ex: Our agency is responsible for administering the ["nam" WIC] PROGRAM

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The larger aim that the Agent is pursuing by carrying out certain coordinated measures.
Ex: The PROGRAM ["goa" to analyze the composition of Titan's sludge] is nearly complete.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
An entity (abstract or concrete) which is involved in an implicit Activity.
Ex: Iran has vowed to continue its ["sal" nuclear] PROGRAM and is demanding that sanctions against it should be lifted . Ex: The DOE ["sal" Human Genome] PROGRAM also has developed high-throughput approaches to identify cis-regulatory sequences in the human and other genomes, based on shared

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the manner in which the Agent performs the Activity associated with the program.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time over which the project is lasts or is slated to last.
Ex: The government has initiated yet another ["dur" seven-year] PROGRAM.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the Activity of the project as the Agent.
Ex: It turned out that the company was doing a PROGRAM ["Co_participant" with a local Arab-American communal group].

fe.name: Project
fe.definition: The ongoing plan of action which allows the Agent to pursue the Activity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Project is ongoing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where a Project is pursued.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE is used to describe a characteristic of the Project.

lexunit.name: project.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an enterprise carefully planned to achieve a particular aim.

lexunit.name: program.n

lexunit.name: plan.n

lexunit.name: scheme.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a systematic plan or arrangement for attaining some particular object or putting a particular idea into effect.

frame.name: Degree_of_processing
frame.definition:
A Material has been processed (generally industrially) to some Degree in order to make it more useful for some (usually implicit) function. In some cases, an Alterant is used to process the Material.
Ex:

fe.name: Alterant
fe.definition: The Alterant causes a change in the Material.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
The substance which is altered in some useful way.
Ex:

fe.name: Degree

frame.name: Trajector-Landmark
frame.definition:
Basic Image Schema: contains a (more) profiled element, the Trajector, and an un- or less profiled element, the Landmark. In combination with a schematically-defined Profiled_region (with a pre-defined relationship to the Landmark), the Landmark serves as the basis for understanding the status or location of the Trajector.
This schema essentially establishes a point-of-view or focus. _above.prep_ and _below.prep_ both make use of the verticality schema, but are differentiated by whether the Landmark is associated with the upper region and the Profiled_region with the lower or vice-versa.
Ex: ["Trajector" The cat] IN ["Landmark" the shed] purred violently . Ex: ["Trajector" The shed] AROUND ["Landmark" the cat] shook . Ex: We 'll have to ["Trajector" leave] BEFORE ["Landmark" noon] . Ex: In the 1990s , though , ["Trajector" the rate at which DNA could be read] revved INTO ["Landmark" high gear] .

fe.name: Trajector
fe.definition: The entity whose status or location is (generally) unknown, and whose status or location is established by examining the Profiled_region.

fe.name: Landmark
fe.definition: The entity, generally presupposed, whose status or location is known or knowable and which thus serves as a basis for understanding the status or location of the Trajector by locating it in a Profiled_region which has a particular relation to the Landmark.

fe.name: Profiled_region
fe.definition: The region which has a particular shape, orientation, size, and location (literal or metaphorical) with respect to the Landmark. The shape of the Profiled_region is virtually always incorporated in the target. This shaped region usually includes the location of the Landmark, as seen with _in.prep, at.prep, on.prep_, but may also do exactly the opposite, as with _away from.prep_.

frame.name: Source_path_goal
frame.definition: Basic Image Schema: the Trajector moves (or is conceived as moving) from the Source along the Path to the Goal using the Means.

fe.name: Trajector
fe.definition: The entity that moves (or is conceived of as moving) from the Source, along the Path to the Goal.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: A description of the initial location of the Trajector, before a motion event begins.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: A description of the intermediate position of the Trajector, after departing the Source and before arriving at the Goal.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: A description of the location that the Trajector ends up.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action or state-of-affairs that causes the Trajector to change location.

frame.name: Toxic_substance
frame.definition:
A Toxic_substance causes death or harm when introduced into or absorbed by a living organism, the Victim. The Toxic_substance may be specified to be produced by or contained in a Toxin_source. The Toxic_substance may affect the Victim as a whole or a particular Body_part (understood here to include organs and other sub-systems). A Degree of harmfulness can be specified and the Toxic_substance may develop its effect only under particular Circumstances.
Ex: ["Toxic_substance" The main product , sulphide ,] _is_ TOXIC ["Body_part" to cells]
Ex: ["Toxic_substance" They] are better tolerated and _are_ ["Degree" less] TOXIC ["con" in overdose]
Ex: The reason he was close to danger was because an extremely POISONOUS ["toxs" beetle] was crawling down his shoulder.
Ex: ["tox" Ingested gliadin and PT-gliadin] _are_ TOXIC ["vic" to coeliac patients].

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition:
The Victim is the being or entity that is capable of being harmed by the Toxic_substance.
Ex: Chocolate can be POISONOUS ["vic" for some types of pets].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree is the degree to which the Toxic_substance is harmful to the Victim.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition:
The Body_part defines the part of the Victim's body that is harmed.
Ex: This vitamin taken in excess could _be_ POISONOUS ["bod" for the liver]

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A fact or action that explains why the Toxic_substance has a harmful effect on the Victim .

fe.name: Toxic_substance
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate the substance which potentially causes harm to a Victim.
Ex: Highly TOXIC ["tox" pollutants] could be safely disposed of by burning them

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
A set of circumstances, often the relative amount of the Toxic_substance that is present, under which the Toxic_substance is specified to have or lack a toxic effect.
Ex: Some metals, such as copper and selenium, are essential to normal metabolic function as trace elements but are TOXIC ["con" at high levels of exposure]

fe.name: Toxin_source
fe.definition:
A living organism, object or process that produces a Toxic_substance.
Ex: A young man was bitten by a POISONOUS ["toxs" snake] and lives to tell about it.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type identifies the kind or sort of Toxic_substance.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Temporal period for which the substance or source remains toxic to the victim.

lexunit.definition: COD: poisonous

lexunit.name: toxin.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a poisonous substance

lexunit.name: poison.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a substance that causes death or harm when introduced into or absorbed by a living organism.

lexunit.name: poisonous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: producing or of the nature of poison

lexunit.name: venom.n
lexunit.definition: COD: poisonous fluid secreted by animals such as snakes and scorpions and typically injected into prey or aggressors by biting or stinging

lexunit.name: venomous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: secreting or capable of injecting venom.

frame.name: Being_obligatory
frame.definition:
Under some Condition, usually left implicit, a Duty needs to be fulfilled by a Responsible_party. If the Duty is not performed, there may be some undesirable Consequence for the Responsible_party, which may or may not be stated overtly. Compare this frame to the Being_obligated frame.
Ex: It would BEHOOVE ["res" us] ["dut" to comprehend and personalize what Jesus had to tell his disciples]
Ex: Fressed too much at the OBLIGATORY ["dut" BBQ]. ["res" INI]
Ex: When I was in HS, ["dut" marching band] _was_ MANDATORY in order to participate in any of the other ensembles ["res" INI]
Ex: Should ["dut" insurance] _be_ COMPULSORY?

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the Condition under which the Duty is required of the Responsible_party.
Ex: The use of a spirometer is MANDATORY ["Condition" if early stages of chronic obstructive lung disease are to be detected].

fe.name: Consequence
fe.definition:
The Consequence will result if the Duty is not performed.
Ex: Attendance of the 341 meeting of creditors is MANDATORY ["cons" or you will not receive your discharge].

fe.name: Duty
fe.definition:
The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.
Ex: ["dut" Getting a shot against yellow fever] is OBLIGATORY for travellers to Benin.

fe.name: Responsible_party
fe.definition:
The person who must perform the Duty.
Ex: The use of TM software is OBLIGATORY ["res" for every freelance translator working on projects for our company].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the Duty is mandatory.
Ex: ["tim" These days], wearing a seat-belt is MANDATORY.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A location in which the Duty obtains.
Ex: Gymnasium is not OBLIGATORY ["pla" in Sweden], but nearly everyone attends gymnasium

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The positive consequence of the Duty being fulfilled.
Ex: Not acting as a savior is compulsory ["pur" to avoid misunderstanding and loss of confidence in partnership, which many American investors, particularly African Americans, may experience].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The reason why the Duty is necessary for the Responsible_party.
Ex: Rigorous posttreatment follow-up is MANDATORY, ["exp" because long-term recurrence rates after treatment of melanoma in situ with imiquimod are yet unknown].

lexunit.name: mandatory.a
lexunit.definition: COD: required by law or mandate; compulsory

lexunit.name: compulsory.a
lexunit.definition: COD: required by law or rule; obligatory

lexunit.name: obligatory.a
lexunit.definition: COD: compulsory

lexunit.name: incumbent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: necessary for (someone) as duty or responsibility

lexunit.name: behoove.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to be necessary for

frame.name: Exchange
frame.definition:
Two parties, the Exchangers, each give and receive from the other Themes. The parties are also construable separately as Exchanger_1 and Exchanger_2, in which case the Themes may be construed separately, too, as Theme_1 and Theme_2.
Ex: ["ex1" They] SWAPPED ["thm1" the island] ["ex2" with the Neapolitan government of the day] ["thm2" for the much smaller Capri]. Ex: Then ["exs" the teams] SWAPPED ["thms" their draftees]. Ex: We EXCHANGED ["thms" addresses] and he told us that next year when we are in Aruba we will visit with his family there.
Ex:
Notice that this frame is to be differentiated from the Replacing frame, where there is no notion of trade between two parties and the focus is only on the relationship between two items that successively fulfill a function or participate in a relation.

fe.name: Exchanger_1
fe.definition: In cases where the Exchangers involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, this FE identifies the conversational participant with greater semantic and syntactic prominence, as compared with Exchanger_2. That is, Exchanger_1 is generally encoded as Subject, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Exchanger_1. Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Exchanger_1, not necessarily that of Exchanger_2 or the group of Exchangers as a whole.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the exchange occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which Exchanger_1 or the Exchangers make the trade.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the exchange takes place.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which Exchanger_1 or the Exchangers effect the trade.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the exchange act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of Exchanger_1 or Exchangers that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: Theodosia and Felix ["man" carefully] EXCHANGED their bunches of flowers.

fe.name: Exchanger_2
fe.definition:
In cases where the Exchangers involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, Exchanger_2 refers to the semantically and grammatically less prominent group. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with). Note that it is possible for a single role to correspond to multiple referents. For example, if the prepositional object in the example below were plural, we would still assign it the single role Exchanger_2.
Ex: The TRADE ["ex2" with Cuba] went exactly as planned.

fe.name: Exchangers
fe.definition:
In some sentences both participants are expressed by the Subject, and there is no 'with'-phrase (cf example 1). In sentences like this, the Subject is assigned the FE role Exchangers. In such sentences, the Subject always denotes more than one person, and it is understood that the reciprocal communication takes place between these two (or more) people. The Subject may denote two or more people either through conjunction, as in example 1, or through plurality, as in example 2, or by denoting a group, as in example 3. In each of these cases the FE Exchangers is assigned. Notice that for nouns in the Exchange frame, it is possible for the Exchangers role to be expressed by a prepositional phrase as in example 4.
Ex: ["exs" Smithers and Kornfeldt] TRADED Pez dispensers. Ex: ["exs" My neighbors] SWAPPEDlawn mowers . Ex: ["exs" The group] EXCHANGED phone numbers. Ex: The prisoner EXCHANGE ["exs" between North and South Dakota] went bad somehow.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of Exchanger_1 or Exchangers during the exchange.
Ex: Howell TRADED brooms with Susanne, ["dep" uncertain of whether she would prefer his].

fe.name: Theme_1
fe.definition:
The item that begins in the possession of Exchanger_1.
Ex: I tucked the pistol between my belt and tunic top (how I wish I had kept it, but I later SWAPPED ["thm1" it] with a Canadian for some cigarettes.

fe.name: Theme_2
fe.definition:
The item that begins in the possession of Exchanger_2.
Ex: The organization bought the property in 1999, then SWAPPED it with the BLM ["thm2" for about 100 parcels in 10 counties ranging in size from one to 920 acres].

fe.name: Themes
fe.definition:
The items which change possession between the Exchangers.
Ex: They SWAPPED ["thms" guitars].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element denotes how often the Exchangers trade Themes.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

lexunit.name: exchange.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give something and receive something else, especially of the same kind, in return.

lexunit.name: trade.v
lexunit.definition: FN: exchange

lexunit.name: swap.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to give in trade

lexunit.name: exchange.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act or the action of exchanging.

lexunit.name: swap.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of exchanging one thing for another.

lexunit.name: trade.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a transfer; an exchange.

lexunit.name: switch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: exchange.

lexunit.name: change.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to exchange

frame.name: Take_place_of
frame.definition:
A New filler occupies a Role or serves a Function after the Old filler ceases to occupy the position. In many cases, the Role or Function is implicit.
Ex: ["new" Gas] can SUBSTITUTE ["deg" entirely] ["old" for petrol]. Ex: Sometime in the 1880s ["new" gas] REPLACED ["old" oil] ["fun" for manufacturing fuel]. Ex: ["tim" Twelve years later], ["new" oil] REPLACED ["old" coal] ["rol" as the energy of choice]. Ex: ["New" Honey] can REPLACE ["Old" sugar] ["Context" in this recipe].

fe.name: New
fe.definition:
The new filler of the Role that was previously occupied by the Old filler.
Ex: The traditional thatched roof has often been REPLACED ["new" by corrugated galvanized iron].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The category that the New and Old entities fit into as a result of the Function they serve.
Ex: What gas REPLACED Hydrogen ["rol" as a safer medium for use in balloons] on account it does not burn?

fe.name: Function
fe.definition:
The (generally desirable) state of affairs that the New and Old entities are involved in bringing about.
Ex: Oil and gas REPLACED coal ["fun" in heating homes, in industry, and in transportation].

fe.name: Old
fe.definition:
The entity that occupied the Role or served the Function before the New filler.
Ex: The electron was discovered and ["old" electricity] REPLACED gas lamps.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the New takes up the Role previously occupied by the Old.
Ex: When electricity REPLACED oil ["tim" in the early 1930's], the steady beam was replaced by a flashing light.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A Degree of replacement is generally only possible when New entities replace Old entities in multiple contexts.
Ex: In the case of Cyprus, all of the former non-flying terrestrial species were exterminated, and have been ["deg" entirely] REPLACED by species introduced deliberately or accidentally by man.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). The rapidity of replacement is also indicated as Manner.
Ex: On land the angiosperms ["man" rapidly] REPLACED the gymnosperms as the dominant plants

fe.name: Context
fe.definition:
The domain in which the New and Old entities function.
Ex: ["New" Machines] have REPLACED["Old" men] ["Context" in the work force]

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

lexunit.name: replace.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take the place of.

lexunit.name: substitute.v
lexunit.definition: FN: serve in place of

lexunit.name: take place.v
lexunit.definition: COD: replace

lexunit.name: replacement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: taking the place of.

lexunit.name: do duty.v
lexunit.definition: COD: serve or act as a substitute for

frame.name: Undergo_change
frame.definition:
An Entity changes, either in its category membership or in terms of the value of an Attribute. In the former case, an Initial_category and a Final_category may be expressed, in the latter case an Initial_value and a Final_value can be specified.
Ex: As soon as Tiffany kissed the frog, ["ent" Tiffany] TURNED ["finc" into a frog].
Ex: He chanted and ["ent" the rock] CHANGED ["att" shape], becoming a great double bitted axe.
Ex: The College has CHANGED ["deg" markedly] over the century since it first opened its doors.
Ex: If I'm understanding you correctly, you want the switchbar color to CHANGE ["Circumstances" whenever the bot says something]?
Ex: ["ent" My life] instantly CHANGED ["inic" from an empty life], ["finc" to a life full of joy and purpose].
Ex: As you can see, ["ent" the word WALK] CHANGED ["iniv" from red] ["finv" to green] rather than have a separate lens for each colour.
Ex: ["ent" My feet] TURNED ["finc" to stone].
Ex: ["ent" The promise] will TURN ["finc" to ashes] ["Circumstances" if progress is not made].
Ex: ["att" The price] CHANGED ["iniv" from $1.26] ["finv" to $1.27 per pint]. ["ent" DNI]
Ex: ["ent" At least one relative instruction] has CHANGED ["att" in size] ["iniv" from short] ["finv" to long]

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The concrete or abstract entity that undergoes a change.
Ex: How pleasing to see that ["ent" Martha] has CHANGED now.

fe.name: Final_category
fe.definition: The type of Entity that results from the change.

fe.name: Initial_category
fe.definition:
The category that the Entity belongs to before it undergoes the change.
Ex: The viccar CHANGED ["inic" from a professional clergyman] into an anti-ecclesiastical activist.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Entityundergoes the transformation.
Ex: ["tim" Then] she TURNED into a lizard.

fe.name: Initial_value
fe.definition:
The value of the Attribute before the change takes place.
Ex: At that time, my asthma CHANGED ["iniv" from very mild] to severe.

fe.name: Final_value
fe.definition:
The value of the Attribute that results from the change.
Ex: Its color CHANGED from red ["finv" to blue].

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
A characteristic of the Entity for which a value can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement , or observation.
Ex: Test to check if ["att" the color] CHANGES when you place your mouse over the JavaScript image

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Change event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
Ex: He also identified all of the places where cancer rates or pollution levels CHANGED ["man" quickly] over short periods of time.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the initial and final values or categories differ from each other.
Ex: Industrial economics has CHANGED ["deg" a lot] during the last two decades

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.
Ex: Information may CHANGE ["Circumstances" whenever the US Department of Education issues additional guidance or regulations].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event or state that causes the change to take place.
Ex: Doctor?s practices have CHANGED ["cau" due to concerns over medical litigation].

fe.name: Intermediate_value
fe.definition:
A value that the Attribute assumes before the Final_value obtains.
Ex: The slurry was stirred until the color of the suspension CHANGED from red ["intv" via orange] to yellow over a period of two hours.

fe.name: Value_range
fe.definition:
The Initial_value and Final_value taken together as the range through which the Entity changes.
The main faith of the church has CHANGED ["val" between Orthodox, Protestant and Greek Catholic] several times.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

lexunit.name: change.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become different

lexunit.name: turn.v
lexunit.definition: FN: change in nature, state, form, or colour

lexunit.name: change.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of changing

lexunit.name: veer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: change direction suddenly.

lexunit.name: swing.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move quickly changing direction

lexunit.name: plummet.v
lexunit.definition: FN: change rapidly for the worse

lexunit.name: transformation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a marked change in nature, form, or appearance.

lexunit.name: metamorphosis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a change in form or nature.

lexunit.name: changeable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: liable to unpredictable variation.

lexunit.name: shift.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a relatively sudden change.

lexunit.name: shift.v
lexunit.definition: FN: change relatively rapidly, often between multiple states.

lexunit.name: transition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process of changing from one state or condition to another.

frame.name: Change_tool
frame.definition:
An Agent changes Tools, from the Old_tool to a New_tool. The Tools may include vehicles, services providers, or more proto-typical implements.
Ex: If this happens one more time, ["age" we] 're going to SWITCH ["tos" operating systems].
Ex: ["age" Stephen] had to TRANSFER ["ite" five times] ["tim" by the time he got to Lincolnville]. ["tos" DNI].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that changes their situation.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent makes a change.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The aim of the Agent when they carry out the change.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Agent which brings about a change.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Agent's change which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Tools
fe.definition: The entities controlled by an Agent to achieve some Purpose.

fe.name: Old_tool
fe.definition: The tool that the Agent had been using.

fe.name: New_tool
fe.definition: The tool that the Agent ends up using.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of times that the action goes from start to finish.

lexunit.name: change.v
lexunit.definition: FN: discontinue use of and begin use of another

lexunit.name: transfer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: change to another place, route, or means of transport during a journey.

lexunit.name: switch.v
lexunit.definition: FN: change affiliation (to a provider of a service)

lexunit.name: swap.v
lexunit.definition: FN: exchange one tool for another available tool.

lexunit.name: trade.v
lexunit.definition: FN: switch one item (tool, accessory, etc.) for another.

frame.name: Containment
frame.definition: Basic Image Schema: has a Container, Interior, Exterior, Boundary, and an optional Portal.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: The non-point-like entity which has a Boundary which (largely or completely) separates the Interior region from the Exterior region. It normally also has a Portal which links the Interior and Exterior regions.

fe.name: Interior
fe.definition: The (finite) region which is inside the Boundary of the Container, disjoint from the Exterior, and overall closer or included in the Container.

fe.name: Exterior
fe.definition: The (larger) region surrounding an object, disjoint from the Interior, outside the Boundary, and overall more distant from the Container than the Interior.

fe.name: Portal
fe.definition: A (relatively small) region which goes through the Boundary, connecting the Interior and Exterior of the Container.

fe.name: Boundary
fe.definition: The finite region which is not part of the Interior or the Exterior.

frame.name: Containment_relation_IS
frame.definition: Image Schema based on a particular perspective on Containment which profiles the Container as the Landmark and the Interior as the Profiled_region, which serves to locate the Trajector.

fe.name: Profiled_region
fe.definition: The interior region of the Landmark, within which the Trajector is to be found.

fe.name: Landmark
fe.definition: The container which serves as a reference point for the Trajector which is surrounded by it.

fe.name: Trajector
fe.definition: The entity which is to be located with respect to the Landmark.

frame.name: Goal
frame.definition: A Landmark (in combination with the image schema evoked by particular targets) serves to pick out the final location of a Trajector in a construed or actual motion event.

fe.name: Landmark
fe.definition: The relatively locatable entity which serves as a basis for determining the location of the Trajector using the Profiled_region.

fe.name: Profiled_region
fe.definition: The location (located with respect to the Landmark) which is profiled by the particular image schema pertaining to the locative relation.

fe.name: Trajector
fe.definition: The entity which is construed to be in motion, whose location at the end of the construed motion event is in question.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Trajector is located in the Profiled_region.

lexunit.name: to.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: relating a location to a goal of motion

frame.name: In
frame.definition: Schema

lexunit.name: in.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: indication one entity existing within the bounds of another

frame.name: Into
frame.definition: Schema

lexunit.name: into.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: expressing a change of state or location into a bounded area

frame.name: Receiving_scenario
frame.definition: The sequence beginning with the Recipient not having the Theme and ending with the Recipient in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person who gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The aim of the Recipient, which they believe will be accomplished by accepting the Theme.
Ex: She ACCEPTED the ring ["pur" so that his suspicions would not be aroused].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The act that the Recipient performs which brings about their reception of the Theme.
Ex: She received the package ["mea" by signing her name on the delivery certification].

fe.name: Mode_of_transfer
fe.definition:
The system whereby the Theme travels (literally or metaphorically) so that the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.
Ex: I RECEIVED it ["mod" by e-mail].

frame.name: Pre_receiving
frame.definition: The state-of-affairs immediately before the Recipient gets the Theme which describes the Recipient's possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person who has the Theme and is about to give it to the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the way that the Recipient has the Theme.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_receiving event occurs.

frame.name: Post_receiving
frame.definition: The state-of-affairs immediately after the Recipient has come into possession of the Theme offered by the Donor.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The person who has just acted to come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person who has just given the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Recipient has the Theme

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_giving event occurs.

frame.name: Pre_getting
frame.definition: The state of the Recipient prior to the acquisition, i.e. before the Recipient gains possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual that is about to gain a possession.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity which is about to be acquired by the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the way that the Recipient has the Theme

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_getting event occurs.

frame.name: Exchange_currency
frame.definition:
A Money_owner exchanges Sum_1 in the Source_currency for Sum_2 in the Target_currency at some Exchange_service.
Ex: After checking into the Intourist-operated $30-a-day Hotel Zerafshon, we each EXCHANGED $50 for Uzbek currency with a shifty loiterer in the lobby at the rate .
Ex: ["mon" We] ["tim" recently] EXCHANGED ["sm1" $100] ["sm2" for £64.00 UK pounds].
Ex: If ["mon" he] EXCHANGED ["sm1" the money] ["tar" into Deutsch-marks], his 18 marks in Germany can just barely obtain four Big Macs.
Ex: He said the most crucial evidence was that of ["mon" former police reservist, Simo Petersen-Jessen, now in Australia, who] had CONVERTED ["sm1" the money] ["tar" into rands].

fe.name: Money_owner
fe.definition:
The person who exchanges Sum_1 for Sum_2 .
Ex: ["mon" Kornfeldt] hurried through customs, grabbed a city map at a tourist information desk, CHANGED $40 USD into about 300 Hong Kong dollars before leaving the airport

fe.name: Sum_1
fe.definition:
An amount of money in the Source_currency that the Money_owner exchanges for an amount in the Target_currency.
Ex: I said forget it and just EXCHANGED ["sm1" $40 US cash] into $47 and change in Canadian.

fe.name: Source_currency
fe.definition:
The kind of currency of the Money_owner has before the exchange.
Ex: We stopped at a bank were we EXCHANGED ["src" Euros] for Danish money.

fe.name: Sum_2
fe.definition:
The amount of money in the Target_currency that the Money_owner receives in exchange for Sum_1.
Ex: On the bus we EXCHANGED $50 ["sm2" for 1410 rubles].

fe.name: Exchange_service
fe.definition:
The individual or institution which changes the Money_owner's money into the Target_currency.
Ex: Bill EXCHANGED $100 ["exs" at a bank], before hitting the bike path for Krems.

fe.name: Target_currency
fe.definition:
The kind of currency that the Money_owner receives as part of the exchange.
Ex: We had EXCHANGED $100 ["tar" into francs] in LAX to be able to pay for the cab ride upon arrival.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the money is exchanged.
Ex: I EXCHANGED $100 ["pla" in croatia] because i needed a round trip bus ticket to sarajevo.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the currency is exchanged.
Ex: We walked around Eyre Square and EXCHANGED money ["tim" before walking into Taaffes pub and grabbing my first draught pint of Guinness of the trip]..

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the exchange event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Money_owner that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: He ["man" carefully] EXCHANGED his dollars for roubles.

fe.name: Exchange_rate
fe.definition: Ex: I EXCHANGED $100 in $20 bills ["exr" at an exchange rate of 24.4 to 1].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Money_owner whereby the exchange is acheived.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The action that the Money_owner is attempting to accomplish with the exchange.

fe.name: Money
fe.definition:
Currency that is being exchanged by the Money_owner.
Ex: ["Money_owner" I] EXCHANGED ["Sum_1" $1000] ["mon" of my money] ["exs" at the bank].

lexunit.name: exchange.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to have money in one currency replaced with money in another

lexunit.name: change.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to exchange into another currency

lexunit.name: convert.v
lexunit.definition: COD: change (money, stocks, or units in which a quantity is expressed) into others of a different kind.

frame.name: Post_getting
frame.definition: The stage after which the Recipient has acquired the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual that has just come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity which has just come into the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Recipient has the Theme

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Post_getting event occurs.

frame.name: Pre_giving
frame.definition: The stage of giving just before the Donor discontinues possession of the Theme, yielding it to the Recipient.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The individual that has possession of the Theme and is about to transfer possession to the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity which is in the possession of the Donor, which later ends up in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Donor possesses the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual who is about to come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_giving event occurs.

frame.name: Post_giving
frame.definition: The stage immediately after the Donor gives the Recipient the Theme, i.e. when the Recipient has possession of the Theme and the Donor no longer does.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The individual that has just given the Theme to the Recipient and no longer has the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity that the Donor has just given to the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Donor lacks the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual that has just come into possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_giving event occurs.

frame.name: Pre_transfer
frame.definition: The stage before the transfer has taken place, with the Theme in the possession of the Donor.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The individual that is about to transfer the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity which is in the possession of the Donor.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Recipient or Donor possesses the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual who is about to receive the Theme.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_transfer event occurs.

frame.name: Post_transfer
frame.definition: The stage after the Theme is in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The individual that has just given the Theme away.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity which has ended up in the possession of the Recipient

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way that the Donor possesses the Theme.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual that has ended up with the Theme.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_transfer event occurs.

frame.name: Giving_scenario
frame.definition: The sequence of events in which the Donor begins in possession of the Theme, then gives it to the Recipient, relinquishing possession.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person that begins in possession of the Themeand causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The object that changes ownership.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the manner in which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Purpose_of_theme
fe.definition:
The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme.
Ex: Please GIVE this list to the secretary ["pot" for entry into the client database].

frame.name: Getting_scenario
frame.definition: In this scenario, the Recipient begins without the Theme, then acquires the Theme from a Source.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the object that changes possession.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied. Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

frame.name: Transfer_scenario
frame.definition: In this scenario, the Theme begins in the possession of the Donor and ends up in the possession of the Recipient. Alternatively, these two participants may be jointly construed as Transferors.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The object that changes ownership.

fe.name: Donor
fe.definition: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

fe.name: Transferors
fe.definition: The Donor and Recipient conceived of as a unit.

frame.name: Being_operational
frame.definition: An Artifact, either a machine or a network of operationsm, is in a state ready to perform its intended function.

fe.name: Artifact
fe.definition: The device that no longer works.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Artifact exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for being operational.

lexunit.name: broken.a
lexunit.definition: FN: non-functional

lexunit.name: busted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not working.

lexunit.name: down.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a computer system) out of action

lexunit.name: work.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a machine or system) function, especially properly or effectively.

lexunit.name: operational.a
lexunit.definition: FN: be ready to function.

frame.name: Undressing
frame.definition:
A Wearer removes an item of Clothing from a Body_location (the part of the body that the Clothing is prototypically worn on.)
Ex: Walking on sand is better if ["wea" you] TAKE OFF ["clo" your shoes]. ["bod" INI]

fe.name: Wearer
fe.definition:
The individual who begins the action wearing the Clothing and ends the action without it.
Ex: ["wea" The suspects] had to STRIP publically and endure several blasts from a firehose.

fe.name: Clothing
fe.definition: The item that the Wearer is initially wearing but then removes.

fe.name: Body_location
fe.definition:
The initial location of the Clothing on the body, before it changes location. Quite often, the location is not overtly specified and is implicitly supplied by the location on the body that the Clothing is prototypically associated with.
Ex: He DOFFED his hat ["bod" from his bald head]. Ex: TAKE OFF your shoes and just set 'em over there. ["bod" INI]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the clothing removal which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Wearer that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: He ["man" slowly and deliberately] TOOK OFF each shoe and placed it on the rack.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means is an act whereby the Wearer achieves the removal.
Ex: With her burned hands, she could only TAKE OFF her jacket ["mea" by sort of vigorously shrugging].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: Result of an event

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Wearer undresses an item of Clothing.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which a Wearer undresses.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which a Wearer undresses.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

lexunit.name: doff.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remove (an item of clothing, especially a hat).

lexunit.name: take off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remove (clothing).

lexunit.name: slip.v
lexunit.definition: FN: gracefully take off clothing.

lexunit.name: kick off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to take off (footwear) by moving the feet and legs.

lexunit.name: peel off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to remove (clothing which is snug against the body)

lexunit.name: pull off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: remove (clothing) with some force

lexunit.name: remove.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take off (clothing or accoutrements on the body)

lexunit.name: shed.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take off (clothing)

lexunit.name: strip off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take off (clothing), generally rendering the wearer saliently underattired.

lexunit.name: throw off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: remove (clothing) quickly.

lexunit.name: undress.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take off one's clothes

frame.name: Dressing
frame.definition:
A Wearer puts on an item of Clothing, which then occupies the Body_location.
Ex: ["wea" You] didn't have to DRESS ["man" like a pirate] ["pur" to impress me]. ["bod" INI] Ex: He PUT ON ["Clothing" his thickest pair of gloves] and then went back out to see if he could move them now. ["bod" INI] Ex: Jack PUT ON ["Clothing" his watch] - ["bod" on his right wrist], and checked the time.

fe.name: Wearer
fe.definition: The individual that puts Clothing on their body.

fe.name: Clothing
fe.definition: Clothing is used for the item of clothing that the Wearer ends up wearing.

fe.name: Body_location
fe.definition: The body part that the Clothing ends up covering.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of the donning event which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Clothing's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Wearer or Clothing during the act.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is an act whereby the Wearer puts on the Clothing

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of the Placing.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of the Wearing that results from putting on the Clothing.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place indicates where the Donning occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason indicates why the Wearer puts on the Clothing.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Wearer puts an item of Clothing on.
Ex: She had PUT the dress ON ["tim" this morning] expecting it to be sunny.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Wearer intends to accomplish by putting on Clothing.

lexunit.name: don.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put on (an item of clothing).

lexunit.name: put on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: manipulate (a clothing or accoutrement) such that one ends up wearing it.

lexunit.name: slip on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: put on (clothing) gracefully or sensuously.

lexunit.name: pull on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: put on (an item of clothing)

lexunit.name: dress.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put on one's clothes.

lexunit.name: dress up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: dress in smart or formal clothes, or in a special costume.

lexunit.name: get on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: begin wearing

lexunit.name: throw on.v
lexunit.definition: FN: put on (clothing) quickly.

frame.name: Remembering_information
frame.definition:
A Cognizer retains facts in memory and is able to retrieve them. The Mental_content may be presented in clearly propositional form as a finite clause. It may also take the form of an embedded question or be a concealed question in the form of a simple NP.
Ex: I was impressed that ["cog" she] 'd actually REMEMBERED ["men" Radish 's name] (= what Radish's name is)
Ex: Oh, and for those who like to continually whinge about how the French are 'surrender monkeys' - REMEMBER ["men" Napoleon] (= who Napoleon was)?
Ex: ["cog" I] ca n't REMEMBER ["men" what DSP stands for].
Ex: And ["cog" Bill] can ["tim" still] REMEMBER ["men" the pattern] (= what the pattern is).
Ex: ["men" What] do ["cog" you] REMEMBER ["top" about your grandma]?
Ex: Notice that this frame is very general. It can be used to talk about detailed reports of past experience.
Ex: I don't know if I lost consciousness for a while. But I REMEMBER ["men" that I was lying in the middle of the road with people trying to assist me].
Ex:
Notice that Mental_content reported within this frame is presented as factive, i.e. as reliable and accurate. Consider the following contrasts:
Ex: 1a. I REMEMBER her as selfish--but I might be wrong. Ex: 1b. ??I REMEMBER that she was selfish--but I might be wrong.
Ex: 2a. Bill REMEMBERS her as smarter than she is. Ex: 2b.*Bill REMEMBERS that she is smarter than she is.
The (b) sentences, which belong in this frame, are less acceptable than the (a)-sentences as they suggest that the Cognizer takes their memory to be accurate while suggesting at the same time that the memory might be or is inaccurate. In the (a) sentences, which belong to the Remembering_experience frame, there is no contradiction as the remembering is taken to be subjective and not necessarily accurate. Ex: The concealed question uses with personal names that occur in this frame are not always easy to distinguish from instances of the Rembering_experience frame where a Salient_entity alone is referred to.In 3a and 3b, which belong to the Remembering_experience frame, there is no question of identity: remembering here means thinking of one's memories of the relevant person. 3c is different: the hearer is asked whether they know who the person is; it belongs in this frame.
Ex: 3a. I REMEMBER her fondly Ex: 3b. Please take a moment to REMEMBER Caesar and his Family. Ex: 3c. Do you REMEMBER ["men" Alexander the Great]? He was one of history's most prolific conquerors, and he did it all in his twenties.
Ex: This frame differs from Remembering_to_do in that this frame is strictly talking about a fact, whereas the Remembering_to_do frame is strictly about tasks which the Cognizer would be expected to do. Remembering_to_do uses normally occur with infinitival complements.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The person who retains and retrieves information.
Ex: I bet ["cog" Johno] can REMEMBER the name of the Ramones' drummer.

fe.name: Mental_content
fe.definition:
Mental_content stored by and accessible to the Cognizer. It may derive from experience or activity or simply from being informed of it.
Ex: Do you REMEMBER ["men" how to spell cupboard ?]

fe.name: Accuracy
fe.definition:
The extent to which the remembered Mental_content matches the information or experience that it is based on.
Ex: If I REMEMBER ["acc" correctly] the pre-War price for hanging a wall up, a roll of wallpaper was about sixpence a roll , and that included preparing as well.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Cognizer retrieves Mental_content or forgets it.
Ex: ["tim" Afterwards], I FORGOT what I was pissed off about, but I was.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
An entity, concrete or abstract, or an event that the remembered Mental_content is about.
Ex: The boy who suffered brain damage when he was hit by a vehicle while walking into school testified Friday he REMEMBERS nothing ["top" about being hit].

fe.name: Context
fe.definition:
A situation or a text from which the Mental_content was acquired.
Ex: You will REMEMBER ["con" from grade school] that you do not want to make the nuns impatient.

lexunit.name: remember.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to recall a fact to the mind

lexunit.name: forget.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be unable to remember a fact

lexunit.name: draw blank.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fail to remember

frame.name: Remembering_to_do
frame.definition:
A Cognizer thinks of and performs an Action that is a self- or other-imposed task or some other kind of desireable behavior. The Action may involve a Salient_entity in some way affected by the Cognizer. If a Salient_entity is mentioned, the Action is left unexpressed.
Ex: You invited everybody but you FORGOT ["sal" Harry].
Ex: Thank God ["cog" Smithers] REMEMBERED ["act" to return the video.].
Ex: If you FORGET ["sal" your textbook] and there is an assignment to be done, the highest grade you will receive on the work is aC (70%).
Ex: Did ["cog" you] REMEMBER ["sal" about the letter]?

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The person who thinks of or fails to think of an obligatory or desireable Action.
Ex: .["cog" Alex and Zach Swindle], Centre, visited their brother in San Francisco in June and REMEMBERED to take along a copy of The Post>.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
An Action that the Cognizer is supposed to carry out. This may be a Task imposed specifically on the Cognizer or it may be self- or socially imposed.
Ex: This time we REMEMBERED ["act" to turn the gas off before leaving].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
A Time when the Cognizer remembers or fails to carry out an Action.
Ex: He REMEMBERED ["tim" afterwards] to kiss her fingers.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
The Salient_entity is a person or thing that the Cognizer needs to affect or effect when carrying out the Action.
Ex: We piled into the taxi and right when we were about to leave, I realized we FORGOT ["sal" the video camera]

lexunit.name: remember.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep (something necessary or advisable) in mind.

lexunit.name: forget.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inadvertently neglect to do

frame.name: Remembering_experience
frame.definition:
A Cognizer calls up an episodic memory of past Experience or an Impression of a Salient_entity formed on the basis of past experience. The Cognizer may also remember the Salient_entity in a particular State, which serves as a frame of reference in the Cognizer's mind. When attention is focused on a Salient_entity, then mention of a global Experience is excluded and typically, but not always, either a State or Impression of the Salient_entity is presented.
Ex: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of events. It includes time, place, and associated emotions (which affect the quality of the memorization). Episodic memory contrasts and interacts with semantic memory, the memory of facts and concepts. The Remembering_information frame is concerned with this latter type of memory.
Ex: ["cog" Kozmo] could REMEMBER ["exp" when his modem was the fastest he could buy].
Ex: That's probably before my time, which was long time ago, ["cog" Fish] may REMEMBER ["exp" that time].
Ex: ["cog" Who] REMEMBERS ["exp" me being a total dork and going up to everyone saying "Hey, I'm Ashley Hunt from Chicago"]!?!
Ex: I wanted to REMEMBER ["exp" how good that felt].
Ex: Hummel says ["cog" staff, both students and professional,] REMEMBER ["sal" her] ["imp" as a "very good friend, available for new staff and well-respected by everyone."]
Ex: Somehow ["cog" I] REMEMBER ["sal" him] ["imp" as older, with long eyelashes, and doe eyes].
Ex: When he died he was just a kid himself but for some reason at the age of 44 ["cog" I] still REMEMBER ["sal" him] ["sta" as older than me].
Ex: Retro games are great, but a lot of the time ["cog" people] get clouded by nostalgia and REMEMBER ["sal" them] ["sta" to be better than they really were]
Ex: ["cog" He] REMEMBERED ["sal" him] ["imp" as a kindly man but not a very lively one.]
Ex: ["exp" The part] ["cog" I] ["viv" vividly] REMEMBER was about a South Seas tramp steamer captain .

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
A person who recalls memories of past experience or impressions.
Ex: I will truly miss Delmar and ["cog" I] will always REMEMBER when his eyes lit up everytime he got ice-cream.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
A person or thing that the Cognizer remembers as being involved in some state or event or as having some property.
Ex: today I saw a sister's exclassmate, and didn't recognise him, I REMEMBER ["sal" him] taller.

fe.name: Experience
fe.definition:
A past event or state that the Cognizer witnessed and is now recalling. The Experience may be a specific event or state or a vaguer period that is treated as a unit.
Ex: I can still REMEMBER ["exp" saying the pledge every morning before class in elementary school], a rare occurrence among elementary school kids nowadays.

fe.name: Impression
fe.definition:
A property that the Cognizer attributes to the Salient_entity based on their past experience of the Salient_entity or a category to which the Salient_entity is assigned.
Ex: I REMEMBER Peter ["imp" as immensely kind in those first three weeks before I was packed off to boarding school].

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
A property or role that a Salient_entity actually held and which frames the memories that the Cognizer has of the Salient_entity.
Ex: Atulprasad is principally REMEMBERED ["sta" as a musician and composer].

fe.name: Vividness
fe.definition:
The degree of detail and/or immediacy of a remembered Experience.
Ex: Brian Wooley only ["viv" dimly] REMEMBERED the hand falling on his shoulder

fe.name: Context
fe.definition:
A situation in which the Cognizer encountered the Salient_entity.
Ex: She was just how I REMEMBER her ["con" from school] .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Cognizer remembers the experience.
Ex: I 'll ["tim" never] FORGET being in hospital

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that affect the action (fondly).
Ex: Bill will be ["man" fondly] REMEMBERED by all.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The amount of time for which the Cognizer remembers the experience.
Ex: Your generosity and kindness will be long REMEMBERED ["dur" for years to come].

lexunit.name: remember.v
lexunit.definition: FN: think of a past experience

lexunit.name: forget.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fail to remember

lexunit.name: memory.n
lexunit.definition: COD: something remembered

lexunit.name: recall.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remember

lexunit.name: look back.v
lexunit.definition: FN: call to mind a past experience

lexunit.name: reminisce.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be engaged in enjoyable recollection of past events.

frame.name: Verification
frame.definition: An Inspector attains a degree of certainty in the Unconfirmed_content, generally by inspecting some evidence.

fe.name: Inspector
fe.definition:
The individual or individuals that ascertain that the Unconfirmed_content is true.
Ex: ["ins" His] later VERIFICATION of the facts is certainly beyond reproach.

fe.name: Unconfirmed_content
fe.definition:
An open proposition that the Inspector decides by examining evidence. It is usually a propostion put forward which some parties would disbelieve or contest.
Ex: It is extremely difficult to CONFIRM ["unc" the absence of something].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the verification which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Inspector that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Inspector by which the Inspector manages to establish the truth of the Unconfirmed_content.
Ex: We CONFIRMED our results ["mea" by repeating the experiment and measuring the output with a mass spec].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The amount of certainty which the Inspector achieves after the process of verification.
Ex: His involvement in the action has subsequently been ["deg" completely] CONFIRMED.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state of affairs that the Inspector hopes to bring about by going through the verification.
Ex: I spent a few minutes CONFIRMING his visa number ["pur" just to make him sweat].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The Medium is the piece of text or work in which the Inspector verifies the Unconfirmed_content: Ex: ["Medium" Chapter four] CONFIRMS the reader 's suspicions completely.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: A tool or instrument used by the Inspector in the verification process.

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition: The conditions under which the the verification will occur.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describes a characteristic of the verification event.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE identifies the "by rule" domain in which the verification event is true or operational (often denoted by words such as "technically," "technically," "formally," etc.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE describes the Time at which the verification event takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE describes where the verificiation event takes place.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for the state of the verification event.

lexunit.name: confirm.v
lexunit.definition: COD: establish the truth or correctness of.

lexunit.name: verify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make sure or demonstrate that (something) is true, accurate, or justified.

lexunit.name: confirmation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of confirming or state of being confirmed.

lexunit.name: verification.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process of verifying.

lexunit.name: identify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: establish the identity of.

lexunit.name: verifiable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: able to be verified

lexunit.name: substantiate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide evidence to support or prove the truth of.

lexunit.name: make sure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: confirm or ensure.

lexunit.name: certify.v
lexunit.definition: FN: attest or guarantee officially

frame.name: Renunciation
frame.definition:
A Speaker declares that they will no longer be involved with the Content. Such a declaration implies that the Speaker has decided that association with the Content is somehow undesirable.
Ex: That will only be possible if and when ["spe" the IRA] RENOUNCES ["con" armed struggle].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the person who communicates their cessation of association with the Content.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker is communicating. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to", or as a direct object.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The idea that the Speaker no longer associates with, whether it be an activity, a propostion, or a group.
Ex: Bonnie Charlie then RENOUNCED ["con" his aspirations to the throne].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the renunciation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Speaker that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: Your government then ["man" coldly and completely] RENOUNCED you.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Speaker makes a statement of renunciation.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their renunciation.
Ex: That 's when he finally RENOUNCED their friendship ["int" in despair].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement of renunciation.
Ex: Castro RENOUNCED all involvement with the group ["med" over the radio].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Speaker during the statement.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the statement is made.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

lexunit.name: renounce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: formally declare one's abandonment of (a claim, right, or possession).

lexunit.name: renunciation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of renouncing.

frame.name: Labeling
frame.definition:
A Speaker uses as a Label to refer to an Entity. The Label is not a conventional name for the Entity but a description categorizing the Entity and thereby expressing a judgment.
Ex: ["spe" Some] LABELED ["ent" him] ["lab" a womanizer].
Ex: During her lifetime, ["Speaker" her enemies] BRANDED ["Entity" her] ["Label" as a prostitute].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The Speaker is the person who conventionally uses a linguistic sign to refer to an Entity.
Ex: ["spe" They] CALL it a Mutt Mitt.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The concrete or abstract thing with which the Speaker has associated a particular linguistic sign.
Ex: He TERMED ["ent" it] "a pretty incredible discovery" on par with two other 10,000- to 11,000-year-old specimens

fe.name: Label
fe.definition:
The linguistic sign that the Speaker uses to designate the Entity.
Ex: In Texas, we CALL it ["lab" walking"]. Ex: Americans CALL it ["lab" a faucet]. What do the British call it ?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
A time period in which a Speaker uses the Label.
Ex: ["tim" Back in the olden days], they CALLED it "Bohemian people."

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A physical space whose occupants use the Label to refer to the Entity.
Ex: I really loved this movie. ["Place" In France], they CALLED it "Turbo Interceptor".

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
A text whose author applies a particular Label to an Entity.
Ex: ["med" Your article] LABELS him "Republican Senator Jim Exon".

fe.name: Particular_Iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Duration_Of_Final_State
fe.definition: Duration_of_final_state denotes the length of time from the beginning of a state resulting from the activity denoted by the target until the state no longer holds.

lexunit.name: label.v
lexunit.definition: COD: assign to a category, especially inaccurately.

lexunit.name: call.v
lexunit.definition: FN: use a particular name or description to refer to

lexunit.name: term.v
lexunit.definition: FN: apply a specified label to

lexunit.name: brand.v
lexunit.definition: COD: mark out as having a particular shameful quality:

frame.name: Namesake
frame.definition:
An Entity shares a name with its Namesake. Note that the shared name is not a frame element as it cannot be directly expressed as an argument of the target lexical units in this frame.
Ex: ["Entity" Alberta's] NAMESAKE caught in royal scandal Ex: ["Namesake" NAMESAKE] caught in royal scandal Ex: Instead, the EPONYMOUS ["Entity" character] is a mildly retarded woman, Martha (Winger), whose simplistic view on life places her in ethically compromising positions. ["Namesake" DNI] Ex: ["Namesake" He] is ["Entity" my] NAMESAKE, one amongst the many described in my homepage, and is much better qualified to write a page like this.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity about whom it is asserted that they share a name with a Namesake.
Ex: Homer's mythical enchantress was a weaver, and so is ["ent" her] NAMESAKE

fe.name: Namesake
fe.definition:
The person or thing that has the same name as the Entity.
Ex: ["nam" Claire] is her NAMESAKE

fe.name: Anchor
fe.definition:
A domain, often a place or time, in which the Namesake of the Entity is located.
Ex: Karam is a member of the Parti Socialiste Guyanais (PSG), which has long been the strongest political party and is allied to its ["anc" French] NAMESAKE.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any temporary or permanent property of the Namesake.
Ex: Adalvard the younger had visited and buried his ["desc" elder] NAMESAKE in 1060.

lexunit.name: namesake.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing that has the same name as another.

lexunit.name: eponymous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being an eponym of

frame.name: Referring_by_name
frame.definition:
A Speaker uses a particular linguistic form, a Name to refer to an Entity. The Entity often is an interlocutor but may be somebody that the Speaker is talking about, or even just a physical object. Note that we include titles such as "Sir" in the Name category.
Ex: They corresponded frequently and at length, exchanging intimate letters in which ["spe" he] ADDRESSED ["ent" her] ["nam" as Windflower].
Ex: ["spe" We] always CALLED ["ent" her] ["nam" "my lady,"] from the moment that she was put at the head of our section;
Ex: ["spe" Sharpton] CALLED ["ent" him] ["nam" Obama Baracka] in HIS speech .... of all the people to screw his name up!
Ex: And then in private ["spe" he] CALLED ["ent" me] ["nam" "Sausage"], which really pissed me off. Ex:
Ex: ["spe" Advanced Micro Devices] is going to CALL ["ent" its next chip] ["nam" the Athlon 4]

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The person who uses the Name to refer to the Entity.
Ex: ["spe" The Lord, who was charmed by her beauty,] ADDRESSED her as 'than kaadhali!' (My darling) and hence the name.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The entity that is designated by the Speaker with the Name used.
Ex: And that's the reason why we CALLED ["ent" him] 'Tom' when his real name was actually John.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The linguistic form used by the Speaker to refer to the Entity.
Ex: A male voice answered the call, and Jones ADDRESSED the man as ["nam" "Johnny."]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The point of time or interval when the Speaker uses the Name.
Ex: No one had ["tim" ever] CALLED her "my lady".

lexunit.name: address.v
lexunit.definition: FN: begin a conversational turn by referring to one's interlocutor

lexunit.name: call.v
lexunit.definition: FN: address by a specified name, title, etc.

lexunit.name: refer.v
lexunit.definition: FN: designate a person with a name or title

lexunit.name: name.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a word or set of words by which someone or something is known, addressed, or referred to.

lexunit.name: designation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a speaker's name or term for some entity.

frame.name: Simple_name
frame.definition:
A Term is the linguistic sign conventionally used by a Speaker to refer to a type of Entity.
Ex: ["Term" Perianth] _is_ a collective TERM ["ent" for the outer whorls of the flower, which protect the reproductive parts during development].
Ex: The ["Speaker" Polish] WORD ["ent" for it] is ["Term" czarnuszka]

fe.name: Term
fe.definition:
The linguistic sign that is used for referring to a type of Entity.
Ex: The French TERM for this is ["ter" rime pauvre or rime faible].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The type of Entity that is conventionally referred to by a Term.
Ex: Jews are still waiting for the "annointed one" to come; their WORD ["ent" for this] is Messiah.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
A speaker or speech community that uses a Term to refer to a particular Entity.
Ex: ["ter" An antigen] is ["spe" biologists?] TERM ["ent" for an invading organism], such as the influenza virus.

lexunit.name: term.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a word or phrase used to describe a thing or to express a concept

lexunit.name: word.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a single distinct meaningful element of speech or writing, used to form sentences with others

frame.name: Simple_naming
frame.definition:
A Speaker conventionally uses a particular Term to refer to an Entity.
Ex: The pattern of conservation is similar to that found in C1_1, therefore ["spe" we] have TERMED ["ent" this domain] ["Term" DC1] for divergent C1 domain.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The type of Entity that is conventionally referred to by a Term.
Ex: Because of that shift, physicists CALL ["ent" this effect] the "gravitational red shift."

fe.name: Term
fe.definition:
The linguistic sign that is used for referring to a type of Entity.
Ex: The French TERM this plant ["ter" Petit Chêne], from the shape of the leaves.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The speaker or speech community that uses a Term to refer to a particular Entity.
Ex: ["spe" Mathematicians] CALL this subject "arithmetic," reserving the word "algebra" for the more advanced aspects of the subject.

fe.name: Motivation
fe.definition:
A reason for why the Term used for the Entity is the one chosen.
Ex: They CALL their chip the C-Most ["mot" because it is a CMOS chip].

lexunit.name: call.v
lexunit.definition: FN: give a specified name

lexunit.name: term.v
lexunit.definition: COD: call by a specified term

frame.name: Inspecting
frame.definition:
An Inspector directs his perceptual attention to a Ground to ascertain whether the Ground is intact or whether an Unwanted_entity is present. Alternatively, the desired outcome of the inspection may be presented as a Purpose.
Ex: ["insp" The police] removed Flonnory and Barbour from the automobile and FRISKED ["gro" them] ["unw" for weapons]. Ex: DOUBLE-CHECK the form ["pur" to make sure all of the information has been entered correctly].

fe.name: Inspector
fe.definition:
The person who inspects the Ground to see if it is intact or without blemish.
Ex: ["insp" Smithers] PROOF-READ my paper on phlogiston production.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The entity that the Inspector inspects with his senses to ascertain whether it is intact.
Ex: ?Mister Thomas? said Holmes, ?have you EXAMINED ["gro" the lock] to determine whether or not it has been forced or otherwise tampered with??.

fe.name: Unwanted_entity
fe.definition:
An entity whose presence would impair the acceptability or usefulness of the Ground.
Ex: Security guards FRISKED all the spectators ["unw" for weapons] as they entered the stadium.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE is used for the Means by which the Inspector examines the Ground.
Ex: As in the second step the baby went to the toy and EXAMINED it ["Means" by placing it in his mouth].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
Some of the words in this frame occur with a constituent that expresses the desired outcome of the inspection. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by _for_, or a _to_-marked VP Complement.
Ex: CHECK all gutter brackets and clips ["pur" to ensure no water will drip on to the walls].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Inspector scrutinizes the Ground.
Ex: Leather is ["man" carefully] INSPECTED for softness, elasticity and texture

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the extent to which the Inspector examines the Ground.
Ex: This section was ["deg" partially] INSPECTED by the commissioner of Metro rail safety on Thursday

fe.name: Location_of_inspector
fe.definition: This FE is the position of the Perceiver during the act of perception. Typically, it is expressed in a _from_-PP. Ex: He moved toward the control panel and INSPECTED it ["loc" from a distance], without touching it.

fe.name: Desired_state
fe.definition:
The desirable state of affairs which the Inspector hopes to find to obtain when inspecting the Ground.
Ex: CHECK ["des" that the light is out] before you leave.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Inspector examines the Ground.
Ex: ["tim" Yesterday] we INSPECTED all the taps and water pipes at animal enclosures being utilized

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The circumstances under which the Inspector examines the Ground.
Ex: ["cir" Under pressure to find something], the team leader EXAMINED the site for signs of illicit activity.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity used by the Inspector to scrutinize the Ground.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: inspect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: look at closely

lexunit.name: proof-read.v
lexunit.definition: COD: read (printer's proofs or other material) and mark any errors

lexunit.name: frisk.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a police officer or official) pass the hands over (someone) in a search for hidden weapons or drugs.

lexunit.name: inspection.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an action of looking at something closely

lexunit.name: check.v
lexunit.definition: COD: examine the accuracy, quality, or condition of.

lexunit.name: double-check.v
lexunit.definition: COD: check again.

lexunit.name: examine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: inspect closely to determine the nature or condition of; investigate thoroughly

lexunit.name: pat down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to tap with the hand over a person's body in search of unwanted things carried

lexunit.name: examination.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a detailed inspection or investigation.

lexunit.name: reconnoitre.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make a military observation of (a region).

frame.name: Scouring
frame.definition:
A Searcher looks all over a Ground in order to find a Sought_entity. The Sought_entity is not presupposed to exist. The search activity is not concerned with the state of the Ground, which is the case in the Inspecting frame, but only with the finding of the Sought_entity, which is desirable.
