Ex: ["sea" The newcomers] COMBED ["gro" the area] looking for minerals Ex: ["sea" Scientists] SCOURED ["gro" the ice samples] ["sou" for signs of life]. Ex: ["sea" Mulder] RUMMAGED ["gro" through his toilet kit] ["sou" for a plastic razor].

fe.name: Searcher
fe.definition:
The person who is looking all over the Ground for the Sought_entity.
Ex: ["sea" They] first gained entry into the house of Raja Rao, who resides on the ground floor and RANSACKED the house for valuables.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The location that the Searcher covers in looking for the Sought_entity.
Ex: I had never really seen much on the bigfoot subject or I would have SCOURED ["gro" the area] for signs and looked for droppings

fe.name: Sought_entity
fe.definition:
The entity that the Searcher wants to find.
Ex: Coast Guard and Navy ships and aircraft COMBED the area ["sou" for the six aircraft]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Searcher scrutinizes the Ground.
Ex: We ["man" carefully] SCOURED the road for what damaged all of those tires and we finally found it- a piece of nasty, barbed wire, laying across the road.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE specifies the length of the interval during which the scouring activtiy takes place.
Ex: He COMBED the area ["dur" for hours] that night looking for the dogs and has been searching ever since.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Searcher scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity manipulated by the Searcher to examine the Ground.
Ex: They SCOURED the entire beach ["ins" with a metal detector], but found nothing.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Searcher that allows them to search the Ground.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Searcher hopes to bring about by searching a Ground.
Ex: We SCOURED the entire book ["pur" to find this supposed evidence].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Searcher scoures the Ground.

lexunit.name: scour.v
lexunit.definition: FN: search an area

lexunit.name: comb.v
lexunit.definition: COD: search carefully and systematically.

lexunit.name: ransack.v
lexunit.definition: COD: thoroughly search.

lexunit.name: sift.v
lexunit.definition: COD: examine thoroughly so as to isolate that which is important or useful.

lexunit.name: sweep.v
lexunit.definition: COD: search or survey (an area) for something.

lexunit.name: sweep.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an act of searching (an area) for something.

lexunit.name: rummage.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make a thorough but untidy search through

frame.name: Sharpness
frame.definition:
An Entity has a Sharpness characterized by its capability to cut. The Sharpness is a value of the Attribute of sharpness.
Ex: ["Entity" That axe] seems ["Degree" dangerously] SHARP.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity to which the Sharpness attribute is related.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The sharpness feature of the Entity.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Sharpness from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular value for Sharpness.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular value for the Sharpness.

fe.name: Sharpness
fe.definition: The Sharpness value of the Entity. This FE is denoted by the adjectives of the frame.

lexunit.name: sharp.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having an edge or point able to cut or pierce something.

lexunit.name: dull.a
lexunit.definition: FN: lacking sharpness.

lexunit.name: blunt.a
lexunit.definition: COD: lacking a sharp edge or point.

frame.name: Change_of_phase_scenario
frame.definition: The sequence of events in which the Undergoer begins as one state of matter and ends up as another.

fe.name: Undergoer
fe.definition:
The Undergoer is the entity that undergoes a change of phase.
Ex: ["Undergoer" The water] FROZE.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The FE Result indicates the result of the change of phase.
Ex: The lake FROZE ["Result" solid].

fe.name: Initial_state
fe.definition:
This is the original state of the Undergoer.
Ex: The rock SOLIDIFIED ["Initial_state" from its molten state].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
Degree to which the Undergoer changes phase.
Ex: The lake FROZE ["Degree" to depths of 30 feet].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Undergoer changes phase.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Undergoer changes phase.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the Undergoer changes phase.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the phase change occurs.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.
Ex: The cloth FROZE ["sub" around the edges].

frame.name: Cause_to_be_sharp
frame.definition:
An Agent or Cause makes a Patient sharper or duller. An Instrument or Means may be mentioned.
Ex: ["Agent" John] is in the basement SHARPENING ["Patient" his axe].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the sharpening (or dulling) action.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent causes the Patient to become more or less sharp. Ex: ["Agent" The smith] SHARPENED many knives in the days before the war.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient, causing it to change in sharpness. Ex: Never SHARPEN your knives ["Ins" with my whetstone].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Agent sharpens the Patient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent sharpens the Patient. Ex: George SHARPENED the bayonet ["Purpose" to please the sergeant].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent sharpens Patient.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The Patient is the entity that is sharpened. Ex: Several cuts into the log had DULLED ["Patient" the blade].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which the Agent changes the sharpness of the Patient. Ex: He SHARPENED the knife ["Mnr" silently].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Agent is responding to by executing the sharpening act.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Patient's sharpness is affected by the Agent.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of sharpness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes. Ex: ["Cause" The relentless impacts against the wood] gradually BLUNTED the edge of this axe.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The resulting configuration of the Patient.
Ex: SHARPEN this knife ["Result" to a nice point].

lexunit.name: sharpen.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make something sharp.

lexunit.name: dull.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make or cause to become less sharp.

lexunit.name: blunt.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make or cause to be less sharp.

frame.name: Operational_testing
frame.definition:
A Tester uses a concrete or conceptual Product in order to determine either whether it works or to find out how well or in which manner it works. The Tester may have particular Unwanted_characteristics in mind that they are specifically looking for. The operational test may also be carried out under a particular set of Circumstances that are typically relevant to the functioning of the Product.
Ex: ["Tester" Sun] has (hopefully) already TESTED ["pro" it] ["des" for compliance]. Ex: ["pro" The Velcro hook and loop closure system] has been TESTED ["Circumstances" under wet conditions] and retains its holding power after 10,000 open and close functions. ["tes" CNI] ["unw" INI] Ex: ["tes" Roe] revisited the compound and TESTED ["pro" it] ["fun" as a mosquito repellent].

fe.name: Tester
fe.definition:
The person who uses the Product to see if it is intact or to ascertain its characteristics during operation.
Ex: I just wish ["Tester" we] could have TESTED the car with a manual gearbox, instead of the five-speed automatic

fe.name: Product
fe.definition: The entity that the Tester uses to ascertain whether it is intact.

fe.name: Unwanted_characteristics
fe.definition:
An entity or property whose presence would impair the acceptability or usefulness of the Product.
Ex: To ensure that the remedy is complete, nCipher have fully reviewed the software and TESTED it ["unw" for similar errors].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE is used for a Means action which the Tester carries out in testing the Product.
Ex: ["mea" How] we TESTED the Radeon 9700 Pro video-card.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Tester intends to accomplish subjecting the Product to a test of its functioning.
Ex: Once you have copied your site and have TESTED it ["pur" to make sure it works normally], you're ready to pull out the scalpel and start hacking away.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the Tester uses the Product in order to evaluate its functioning.
Ex: Engineers ["man" carefully] TESTED the fields of view to make sure that security personnel would be able to view all critical areas.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the extent to which the Tester examines the Product.

fe.name: Location_of_tester
fe.definition: This FE is the position of the Tester during the act of testing. Typically, it is expressed in a _from_-PP.

fe.name: Desired_state
fe.definition:
The desirable state of affairs which the Tester hopes to find to obtain when using the Product.
Ex: Test-Driven Development requires you to set an expectation of a result and then TEST ["des" that the result is achieved].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Tester uses the Product to evaluate its functioning.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The FE Circumstances is used for circumstances that obtain during the test procedure. These are typically relevant to how the Product functions.
Ex: We TESTED the drive ["Circumstances" using the generic drivers of the OS].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of the time period during which the Tester continuously or repeatedly operates the Product to determine its operational characteristics.
Ex: Before launching BioCheck, we TESTED the system ["dur" for a year] in Washington DC in response to more than 50 actual 9-1-1 calls.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the test is carried out.
Ex: We TESTED the product ["pla" in California] first.

fe.name: Function
fe.definition:
A use to which the Product is put .
Ex: If you have HTML files from another source and you can't first read them into Microsoft Word, you can try the process, but I haven't TESTED it ["fun" for that use].

fe.name: Tested_property
fe.definition:
A variable of behavior of the Product which is specifically evaluated.
Ex: ILCSO staff have TESTED ["tpr" the behavior of the ILCSO-standard version of WebVoyage with several browsers].

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition:
The length of time from when the testing event began to be repeated to when it stopped.
Ex: This approach has been TESTED ["per" since 2001].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the Operational_testing.

lexunit.name: test.v
lexunit.definition: FN: subject to a test of functioning or operation

lexunit.name: test.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a procedure intended to establish the quality, performance, or reliability of something

lexunit.name: flight-test.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to test while in flight

lexunit.name: crash-test.v
lexunit.definition: COD: deliberately crash (a new vehicle) under controlled conditions in order to evaluate and improve its ability to withstand impact

lexunit.name: testing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of performing a critical evaluation of something by using it

lexunit.name: flight-testing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of testing the functioning of something while it is in flight

lexunit.name: flight test.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a flight of an aircraft or rocket to test its functioning.

lexunit.name: flight test.v
lexunit.definition: COD: to test while in flight

frame.name: Response
frame.definition: An Agent performs a Response action in consequence of a Trigger event. In many cases, a non-agentive Responding_entity causes the Response after the Trigger occurs.

fe.name: Response
fe.definition:
The means action whereby the Agent responds to the Trigger.
Ex: The diocese RESPONDED ["res" by taking the property]

fe.name: Responding_entity
fe.definition:
An non-agentive entity that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.
Ex: ["res_e" The pattern of lights]will RESPOND to an acoustic signal, such as vocal commands.

fe.name: Trigger
fe.definition:
An event that impinges upon the Agent or Responding_entity and produces a Response from it.
Ex: How has the modern welfare state RESPONDED ["tri" to the needs of working class women], and why?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The point in time when the Agent or Responding_entitymanifests its Response to the Trigger.
Ex: Israel RESPONDED ["Time" yesterday] to the killing of 22 people by Palestinian suicide bombers with a helicopter attack

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A characterization of the Responding_entity, Agent, or their Response action.
Ex: The government agencies RESPONDED ["man" slowly] and without much effort.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Response action takes place.
Ex: The auto industry has RESPONDED ["Place" in the U.S., but particularly in Asian and European markets] by manufacturing an entry-level segment of cars that is more appealing, better looking, and safer than in the past.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the Response action.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The intentional Agent that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.
Ex: Once again ["age" the Government] is RESPONDING to a crisis with measures that will only harm patients

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition:
A particular feature of the Responding_entity or Agent that is involved in the Response action.
Ex: Don't respond emotionally, RESPOND ["dim" rationally].
Ex: The body's ["dim" immune] RESPONSE to this agent is particularly extreme.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The capacity of of the Agent is their Response act.
Ex: His RESPONSE ["rol" as an official] was quite off-putting.

lexunit.name: respond.v
lexunit.definition: FN: do something as a reaction to

lexunit.name: response.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a reaction

lexunit.name: react.v
lexunit.definition: COD: respond to something in a particular way or with particular behaviour

lexunit.name: reaction.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an instance of reacting to or against something.

frame.name: Dodging
frame.definition:
A Dodger acts to avoid an oncoming moving Bad_entity. Ex: ["Dodger" Mo] DODGED ["Bad_entity" the flower pot that Larry threw in disgust].
The motion is relative, since the Dodger may be moving. Ex: Jogging through the dense woods, ["Dodger" Mo] DODGED ["Bad_entity" the low branches] .

fe.name: Dodger
fe.definition:
The Dodger acts to avoid an oncoming Bad_entity.
Ex: ["Dodger" Mo] DODGED the flower pot that Larry threw in disgust.

fe.name: Bad_entity
fe.definition:
The Bad_entity is the oncoming entity to avoid.
Ex: Mo DODGED ["Bad_entity" the flower pot that Larry threw in disgust].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the dodging occurs.
Ex: He SIDESTEPPED ["Degree" just enough] to soften the blow.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the dodging occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the dodging occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the dodging occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the dodging occurs.
Ex: He SIDESTEPPED just enough ["Purp" to soften the blow].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the dodging occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the dodging occurs.

lexunit.name: dodge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: avoid by a sudden quick movement

lexunit.name: dodge.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an instance of dodging

lexunit.name: sidestep.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an instance of sidestepping

lexunit.name: sidestep.v
lexunit.definition: COD: avoid by stepping sideways

frame.name: Forgoing
frame.definition:
AForgoer decides not to partake in something ordinary that is otherwise Desirable.
Ex: ["For" Chuck] often SKIPS ["Des" lunch].

fe.name: Forgoer
fe.definition:
TheForgoer decides not to partake in the desirable activity or event.
Ex: ["For" Chuck] often SKIPS lunch.

fe.name: Desirable
fe.definition:
Desirable identifies the event or activity in which is the Forgoer does not partake.
Ex: Chuck often SKIPS ["Des" lunch].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time at which the the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Forgoer does not partake in the Desirable.
Ex: Chuck SKIPS lunch ["Circumstances" even when he's hungry].

lexunit.name: forego.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go without something desirable

lexunit.name: skip.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fail to partake in

lexunit.name: abstain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: restrain oneself from doing something

lexunit.name: abstention.n
lexunit.definition: COD: abstinence

lexunit.name: abstinence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the fact or practice of abstaining, especially from drinking alcohol.

lexunit.name: forbear.v
lexunit.definition: COD: refrain from doing something.

lexunit.name: refrain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop oneself from doing something.

lexunit.name: forbearance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: patient self-control

lexunit.name: forbearing.a
lexunit.definition: COD: patient and restrained

lexunit.name: do_without.v
lexunit.definition: FN: restrain oneself from parttaking in something

lexunit.name: go_without.v
lexunit.definition: FN: restrain onself from partaking in something

frame.name: Elusive_goal
frame.definition:
An Experiencer does not achieve a Desired_goal. Typically, the Experiencer is the object of the verb. Metaphorically, a pursued entity is not captured.
Ex: ["Des" Success] ELUDES ["Exp" me]. Ex: ["Des" His point] ESCAPED ["Exp" the entire audience]. Ex: ["Des" A simple truth] has EVADED ["Exp" so many of us]. Ex: This frame is a metaphorical extension of the Evading frame. The Evading frame concerns literal motion of two self-directed entities, one of which moves in such a way as to successfully prevent the other from capturing it. In the case of the Elusive_goal frame, however, there is no literal motion, but rather a Desired_goal that is not "captured" by the Experiencer that would like the Desired_goal to be true or known.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The Experiencer does not achieve a Desired_goal, or capture a pursued entity.
Ex: Success ELUDES ["Exp" me].

fe.name: Desired_goal
fe.definition:
Desired_goal identifies the goal that is not achieved or the entity that is not captured.
Ex: ["Des" Success] ELUDES me.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Experiencerr fails to achieve a Desired_goal.
Ex: Success had eluded him ["Time" for years].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the Experiencer fails to achieve a Desired_goal.
Ex: Success had eluded him even i["Place" n his home town].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the goal is not achieved.
Ex: Success had ELUDED him ["Manner" ruthlessly].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Experiencer fails to reach a goal.
Ex: Success had ELUDED him ["Degree" completely].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time during which the Experiencer does not acheive the Desired_goal.
Ex: A proper solution ELUDED her ["dur" for several years].

lexunit.name: evade.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fail to reach

lexunit.name: escape.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fail to reach

lexunit.name: elude.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fail to be attained

frame.name: Taking_sides
frame.definition:
A Cognizer has a relatively fixed positive or negative point of view towards an Issue (or a Side in a debate concerning an Issue). The Cognizer's Degree of alignment may also be specified.
Ex: In interviews , it seems like ["cog" everyone] _is_ ["deg" completely] AGAINST ["iss" this expenditure] .

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The individual that holds an opinion on an Issue or Side.

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition: The matter, usually concerning a course of action, which the Cognizer has an positive or negative opinion about.

fe.name: Side
fe.definition: The party or individual (generally associated with a particular position on an Issue) that the Cognizer sides with.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Cognizer supports or opposes something.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Cognizer has the indicated point of view towards the Issue.
Ex: ["Time" Last year] she OPPOSED the bill, but changed her mind after she received correspondence supporting the bill.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Cognizer's taking the indicated view on the Issue logically follows.
Ex: Could it be that he SIDED with them ["exp" because it was the constitutionaly correct thing to do]?

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: An action taken by a Side or a view that the Side takes on an issue which the Cognizer either supports or opposes.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describes the person or element that is taking a side.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Taking_sides which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Capitulator that affect the action (reluctantly, meekly).

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Cognizer takes Sides on an Issue.

lexunit.name: oppose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: disapprove of, resist, or be hostile to.

lexunit.name: for.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: in favour of

lexunit.name: against.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: in opposition to.

lexunit.name: pro.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: in favour of.

lexunit.name: support.v
lexunit.definition: FN: approve of (in opposition to another side).

lexunit.name: side.v
lexunit.definition: COD: support or oppose in a conflict or dispute.

lexunit.name: side.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or group opposing another or others in a dispute or contest.

lexunit.name: opposition_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: resistance or dissent.

lexunit.name: in favor.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: in support or to the advantage of.

lexunit.name: supportive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: aligned in favor of.

lexunit.name: opponent.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who has taken an opposing position.

lexunit.name: supporter.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one who has taken a position in support of an issue.

lexunit.name: opposition_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: FN: opposing party

lexunit.name: endorse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: declare one's public approval of.

lexunit.name: take_part.v
lexunit.definition: SMV:take somebody's side

lexunit.name: back.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give material or moral support to.

lexunit.name: backing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: support

frame.name: Traversing
frame.definition: A Theme changes location with respect to a salient Path location.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not _required_ to be an animate mover, so it is different from Self_mover. Ex: ["Theme" Kim] CROSSED through the woods.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.
Ex: The cat CROSSED the street ["Source" from her yard].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal (see below) expresses the frame element Path, including directional expressions:
Ex: The bikers CRISSCROSSED ["Path" through the desert].
Ex: The cyclist ASCENDED ["Path" towards the gate].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Any expression which tells where the Theme ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal.
Ex: The children HOPPED ["Goal" into the neighbor's yard].
Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance: Ex: The children HOPPED ["Goal" over] and sat down.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions. Ex: The bikers CROSSED ["Manner" furiously] through the desert.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance. Ex: I LEAPED ["Distance" twenty feet] before slipping and falling.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Ex: The bikers CRISSCROSSED ["Area" the desert]. Note that this FE should not be used for any locational modifier which would occur just as naturally with a non-motion predicate, like speech.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way. Ex: The less experienced mountaneers ASCENDED ["Mns" by crawling].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the Theme moves.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:
Ex: The squirrel LEAPED ["Cotheme" after it].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action
Ex: We CRISSCROSSED the country ["Depictive" naked]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Theme, taken simultaneously. Ex: He CIRCLED downward ["PS" in a spiral].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction in which the Theme goes.
Ex: The frogs JUMPED ["dir" down] through the meadow.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the motion takes place.
Ex: They CRISSCROSSED the country ["tim" in April].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.
Ex: The participants CIRCLED around ["pur" in order to avoid the house.].

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Theme.
Ex: We CROSSED the river ["veh" by boat]. Ex: Bravo company broke an axle while trying to JUMP a ditch ["veh" in a Humvee].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Theme spends in motion.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Theme at the end of the event.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Theme.

fe.name: Reciprocation
fe.definition: An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, or an action thatReciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the Traversing occurs and which the Traversing is taken to be a part of.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: A larger conceptualization that includes the Traversing as an integral part. The Traversing expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Theme), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the Traversing.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Traversing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

fe.name: Endpoints
fe.definition:
The Source and Goal of either a single or a repeated motion taken together as End_points of the Path.
Ex: A large plastic "football" wildly PASSED ["End_points" between goal posts].

fe.name: Coordinated_event
fe.definition: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event-it does not allow states-that the Traversing is rhythmically aligned with. The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The time period within which the motion event occurs repeatedly.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

lexunit.name: traverse.v
lexunit.definition: FN: travel across or through.

lexunit.name: skirt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go around or past the edge of

lexunit.name: mount.v
lexunit.definition: COD: climb up or on to; ascend.

lexunit.name: descent.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of coming down (something).

lexunit.name: descend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move downward

lexunit.name: cross.v
lexunit.definition: FN: go to the other side of (a bridge or obstacle).

lexunit.name: crisscross.v
lexunit.definition: COD: move or travel around (a place) by going back and forth repeatedly.

lexunit.name: ascent.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of climbing up (an inclined entity).

lexunit.name: ascend.v
lexunit.definition: FN: climb up.

lexunit.name: jump.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pass over by jumping.

lexunit.name: pass.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go past or across; leave behind or on one side in proceeding.

lexunit.name: circle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move in a circle around

lexunit.name: hop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: jump over.

lexunit.name: leap.v
lexunit.definition: COD: jump across.

frame.name: Substance
frame.definition:
This frame concerns internally undifferentiated Substances.
Ex: As their gut bacteria ferment cellulose , they generate ["con" methane] GAS , which escapes from the rear ends of the insects.
Ex: The pipes are leaking ["des" noxious] GAS.
Ex: Some CH-47 "Bombers" were equipped to roll-out ["use" riot control] GAS or napalm onto Viet Cong bunker complexes from the rear cargo ramp.

fe.name: Constituents
fe.definition:
The frame element expresses substances/ingredients that make up the Substance.
Ex: ["con" Argon] GAS is added into the station's air mixture.

fe.name: Substance
fe.definition:
The undifferentiated entity which is presented as having a permanent existence.
Ex: ["sub" LIQUID] flowed over the rocks but it was not water.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Substance belongs to.
Ex: ["typ" Greenhouse] GASES trap heat and prevent its escape from the atmosphere.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The location that the Substance comes from, including both extraction sites and emission/production sources.
Ex: It retrieves most of the expensively generated heat from ["sou" flue] GASES and puts this heat back into the system. Ex: The transport of ["sou" Iraqi] PETROLEUM and petroleum products through the Kirkuk- Yumurtalik pipeline in Turkey is authorized by paragraph 1 a.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of the Substance.
Ex: The new Chrysler minivans will run on ["Descriptor" compressed] natural GAS.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The purpose for which the Substance is intended.
Ex: Supply and placing of ["use" filler] SAND shall be incidental to installation of the paving stones.

lexunit.name: gas.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an air-like fluid substance which expands freely to fill any space available, irrespective of its quantity.

lexunit.name: sand.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a loose granular substance, typically pale yellowish brown, resulting from the erosion of siliceous and other rocks and forming a major constituent of beaches, river beds, the seabed, and deserts

lexunit.name: oil.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a viscous liquid derived from petroleum, used especially as a fuel or lubricant.

lexunit.name: liquid.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a substance that flows freely but is of constant volume.

lexunit.name: methane.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a colourless, odourless flammable gas which is the main constituent of natural gas and the simplest member of the alkane series

lexunit.name: chemical.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a distinct compound or substance, especially one which has been artificially prepared or purified.

lexunit.name: iron.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strong, hard magnetic silvery-grey metal, the chemical element of atomic number 26, used in construction and manufacturing (especially as steel).

lexunit.name: material.n
lexunit.definition: FN: matter

lexunit.name: uranium.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the chemical element of atomic number 92, a grey dense radioactive metal used as a fuel in nuclear reactors.

lexunit.name: aluminum.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a strong, light, corrosion-resistant silvery-grey metal, the chemical element of atomic number 13

lexunit.name: plutonium.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the chemical element of atomic number 94, a dense silvery radioactive metal of the actinide series, used as a fuel in nuclear reactors and as an explosive in nuclear fission weapons.

lexunit.name: atropine.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a poisonous compound found in deadly nightshade, used in medicine as a muscle relaxant.

lexunit.name: yellowcake.n
lexunit.definition: COD: impure uranium oxide obtained during processing of uranium ore.

lexunit.name: solid.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a substance of constant shape and size that resists the tendency to flow and does not easily deform.

lexunit.name: ore.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a naturally occurring solid material from which a metal or valuable mineral can be extracted profitably.

lexunit.name: petroleum.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a hydrocarbon oil found in suitable rock strata and extracted and refined to produce fuels including petrol, paraffin, and diesel oil; oil.

frame.name: Active_substance
frame.definition:
A Substance causes an Effect. The Substance is produced by a process understood as directed towards the Effect. The Name for the material that makes up the substance may also be given.
Ex: A rationale for using ["sub" denatured gp160] as a ["eff" therapeutic] AGENT in HIV-infected people is to boost the immune response .
Ex: ["sub" The quinolones] now seem to _be_ the ["eff" antimicrobial] AGENTS of choice for acute bacterial prostatitis.
Ex: ["eff" Hormonally] ACTIVE ["sub" chemicals] have the potential to cause significant environmental injury.
Ex: Only after the potion has been drunk does the ACTIVE ["sub" ingredient] form. ["eff" DNI]
Ex: The ["nam" sarin] ["sub" AGENT] might have been a leftover shell from a chemical-arms dump.

fe.name: Effect
fe.definition:
The change brought about by the Substance.
Ex: There is a clear co-variation between allergic symptoms in children and the concentration of ["eff" softening] AGENTS in their homes.

fe.name: Substance
fe.definition:
The internally undifferentiated physical entity that has an Effect.
Ex: While marijuana?s advocates say ["sub" the drug] _is_ a mellowing AGENT that can be used for medicinal purposes, some police will say marijuana is a gateway drug.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of the Substance.
Ex: This ["des" transmissible] AGENT is a virus containing DNA.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Substance belongs to.
Ex: ["typ" Pharmacological] AGENTS could then be selected to modify these cascades.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The name of the material that makes up the active Substance.
Ex: ["nam" ]Anthrax AGENT in this form is particularly mobile.

lexunit.name: agent.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a substance that is capable of producing an effect

lexunit.name: active.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having a chemical or biological effect on something.

lexunit.name: bioactive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a substance) having a biological effect.

lexunit.name: causative agent.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a substance capable of causing a particular effect.

lexunit.name: irritant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a substance that irritates part of the body.

lexunit.name: incapacitant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a substance capable of temporarily incapacitating a person without wounding or killing them.

frame.name: Defend
frame.definition:
A Defender responds to an Assailant's attack on a Victim by directly, and usually violently, countering it.
Ex: ["def" Samantha] ["man" stalwartly] DEFENDED ["vic" the gateway] ["assail" from the wraiths], ["dep" crouching low over Stephen's prone form].

fe.name: Defender
fe.definition: This FE is the being or entity that responds forcefully to the Assailant's attack.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity used by the Defender fend off the Assailant .

fe.name: Assailant
fe.definition: The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Defender that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Defender that accomplishes their defense of the Victim.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Defender defends the Victim from the Assailant.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Defender defends the Victim from the Assailant. Ex: John DEFENDED the bear ["Purpose" to prove his manhood].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Defender is responding to that leads them to protect the Victim.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Defender takes forceful action against the Assailant.

fe.name: Location_of_participant
fe.definition: The starting-point of the motion of the Defender or projectiles of the Defender as they move toward the the Place that the Assailant is occupying. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Defender or Victim during the Assailant's attack.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: The individual or entity that is under attack from the Assailant .

lexunit.name: defend.v
lexunit.definition: COD: resist an attack on; protect from harm or danger.

lexunit.name: defense.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of defending from or resisting attack.

lexunit.name: defensive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: used or intended to defend

lexunit.name: hold.v
lexunit.definition: FN: defend, especially a fortified area.

lexunit.name: defender.n
lexunit.definition: FN: person who defends.

lexunit.name: defenses.n
lexunit.definition: COD: fortifications against attack.

lexunit.name: biodefense.n
lexunit.definition: FN: defense specifically concerned with biological agents

frame.name: Progress
frame.definition:
An Entity changes from a Prior_state to a Post_state in a sequence leading to improvement.
Ex: ["ent" Their offensive armament] has DEVELOPED ["pri" from short range missiles] ["pos" to long-range ballistic weaponry] in a relatively short period . Ex: The MATURATION ["ent" of warhead technology] is, perhaps, not far off . Ex: ["ent" Recovery in our major overseas markets] has PROGRESSED ["man" tentatively] and increased spending by consumers and government does not appear to be benefiting this Ex: ["cau" Why] have ["ent" we] DEVELOPED ["dom" economically] ["man" as we have]?

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The object that undergoes change.
Ex: ADVANCES ["ent" in marketing techniques] have since rendered it obsolete.

fe.name: Prior_state
fe.definition:
The former state of the Entity.
Ex: I think we have ADVANCED somewhat ["pri" from that way of thinking] .

fe.name: Post_state
fe.definition:
The state of the Entity following an advance.
Ex: The roads have now ADVANCED ["pos" to a level of perfection not seen since Rome] .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the progress occurs.
Ex: ["tim" When] did the X-wing PROGRESS beyond the drawing board?

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition:
The rate at which the change happens.
Ex: His captaincy has ["rat" slowly] MATURED until he has made us forget the sulky Nasser Hussian era

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (_the same way_).
Ex: Recovery in our major overseas markets has PROGRESSED ["man" tentatively] and increased spending by consumers and government does not appear to be benefiting this .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period over which the progress occurs.
Ex: Screwcap wine seals enable bottle maturation, and provide ideal conditions for MATURATION of wines ["dur" over a long period of time].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The amount of advancement that the Entity has attained.
Ex: Robert's music is DEVELOPING ["deg" further] as he hones his live set to bring in the diverse elements of pan-African music.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The relevant dimension of development.
Ex: Why have we DEVELOPED ["dom" economically] as we have?

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event or state of affairs that brings about the development of the Entity.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Progress occurs.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Progress event occurs.

fe.name: Circumstance
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: stagnate.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: fail to change towards a more advanced condition

lexunit.name: progress.v
lexunit.definition: FN: change towards a more advanced condition

lexunit.name: progress.n
lexunit.definition: COD: development towards a better, more complete, or more modern condition.

lexunit.name: advance.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make progress

lexunit.name: advance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a development or improvement.

lexunit.name: development.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process of developing or being developed.

lexunit.name: develop.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become more advanced

lexunit.name: mature.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become more advanced

lexunit.name: maturation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of maturing.

lexunit.name: advancement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of advancing.

lexunit.name: burgeon.v
lexunit.definition: COD: grow or increase rapidly.

frame.name: Stage_of_progress
frame.definition:
An Entity is at a particular stage of its development.
Ex: The NEXT GENERATION ["ent" Internet] (NGI) Program has been successfully completed.
Ex: Osama bin Laden, prime suspect in the US terror attacks, is outfoxing intelligence agencies with his LOW-TECH ["ent" communication methods]. Ex: ["ent" Kids] _are_ ["deg" much more] ADVANCED ["tim" today] ["deg" than they were in our era] that is for sure.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The object that has reached a particular stage of its development.
Ex: We offer advice for very ADVANCED ["ent" learners of English] on the different EFL/ESL exams.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the progress occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the stage of progress, frequently an evaluation.
Ex: The new version is ["man" wonderfully] ADVANCED.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The amount of advancement that the Entity has attained.
Ex: The province, which is ["deg" very] DEVELOPED economically, is at the same time a center of brassworking.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The relevant dimension of development.
Ex: The Soviet Union was more highly DEVELOPED ["dom" militarily] than China.

lexunit.name: mature.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having reached a sufficiently developed stage in a process.

lexunit.name: advanced.a
lexunit.definition: COD: far on in progress or life

lexunit.name: developed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having the specified level of development

lexunit.name: next generation.a
lexunit.definition: FN: belonging to the next stage of advancement

lexunit.name: low-tech.a
lexunit.definition: COD: involved in or employing low technology.

lexunit.name: sophisticated.a
lexunit.definition: FN: complex or advanced.

lexunit.name: modern.a
lexunit.definition: COD: characterized by or using the most up-to-date techniques, equipment, etc.

lexunit.name: cutting-edge.a
lexunit.definition: FN: very advanced.

lexunit.name: generation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a particular stage in the development of an item constituting a set of said item.

lexunit.name: state-of-the-art.a
lexunit.definition: FN: encompassing the very best in latest technology and innovation

lexunit.name: high-tech.a
lexunit.definition: FN: uses high, or advanced, technology

lexunit.name: old-fashioned.a
lexunit.definition: FN: belonging to an older stage of achievement

frame.name: Make_agreement_on_action
frame.definition:
Two (or more) people (the Parties, also encodable as Party_1 and Party_2) negotiate an agreement. Both sides are construed as making a commitment to assume an Obligation--the process is understood to be symmetrical or reciprocal. Instead of a specific mention of the Obligation, a Topic expression may be used to indicate the domain covered.
Ex: So far , ["par1" we] have AGREED["Obligation" to cede 100km of coastline to Kiribati] . ["par2" DNI]
Ex: At common law, ["pars" the parties] could _make_ an ["med" oral] AGREEMENT ["obl" to submit a dispute to arbitration] and such oral agreement would be valid.

fe.name: Party_1
fe.definition:
The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of the agreement, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus Manner is construed to be that of Party_1, not necessarily that of Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.
Ex: On Monday, ["par1" the airline] reached a DEAL with the Canadian Auto Workers.

fe.name: Party_2
fe.definition:
The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the agreement. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).
Ex: Mozilla Foundation has finally reached an AGREEMENT ["par2" with America Online].

fe.name: Obligation
fe.definition:
An expression of the commitment made by the Parties .
Ex: The US and Russia have AGREED ["obl" to share early warning data on missile launches].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
Topic is a description of the domain covered.
Ex: Some types of alloy steel have been covered in the expiring ["top" trade] AGREEMENT.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.
Ex: The parties made a ["med" written] AGREEMENT to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the act of making an agreement which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of either Party_1 or Parties that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: I ["man" readily] AGREED with her to end our wrestling match.

fe.name: Parties
fe.definition:
The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in making an agreement.
Ex: ["pars" The US and Russia] have AGREED to cooperate in destroying surplus portable anti-aircraft missiles.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agreement occurs.Ex: The town coucil members reached an AGREEMENT ["Place" at the City Hall plenary session].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agreement occurs.Ex: The town coucil members finally reached an AGREEMENT ["Place" at midnight].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describes a characteristic of the Obligation.

lexunit.name: agree.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reach agreement about.

lexunit.name: agreement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a negotiated and typically legally binding arrangement.

lexunit.name: deal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an agreement entered into by two or more parties for their mutual benefit

lexunit.name: treaty.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A formal agreement between two or more nations governed by international law.

frame.name: Delivery
frame.definition:
A Deliverer hands off a Theme to a Recipient or (more indirectly) a Goal location, which is accessible to the Recipient.
Ex: ["del" The staff of Ebags] DELIVERED ["Theme" the umbrella] ["Time" well ahead of schedule].
Ex: In each class ["del" a dove] flew in and DELIVERED ["Theme" a red rose] ["rec" to Ginny].
Ex: The Pontifical Delegation for the DELIVERY ["Theme" of the Icon of the Kazan Mother of God] will arrive tomorrow.

fe.name: Deliverer
fe.definition:
This is the person who completes the movement of the Theme after having transported it.
Ex: That afternoon, ["del" a staff courier] DELIVERED the box from St. Petersburg to Largo.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.
Ex: I DELIVERED the packages ["Goal" to the storage room].

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The objects being delivered.
Ex: I DELIVERED ["Theme" the documents] to the court house.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The vehicle employed by the Deliverer.
Ex: I polished it until the last blemish had vanished, then DELIVERED it ["veh" by wheelbarrow].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive phrase describing the Deliverer or Theme
Ex: They DELIVERED my cable box ["dep" broken] three times.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the delivery event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Deliverer that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: As was customary, she had ["man" eagerly] DELIVERED the morning paper to her parents' room

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition:
This is the Recipient of the sent Theme.
Ex: Tess DELIVERED a package ["rec" to Abby and her kitty].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose of the delivery.
Ex: Rachel DELIVERED the letter to her mother ["Purpose" to see how she would react on getting it].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for the delivery.
Ex: Letters are generally DELIVERED in the morning ["Reason" because that's when most people are home].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the delivery takes place
Ex: I DELIVERED the letter to you ["Time" last week], Sir.

fe.name: Co_theme
fe.definition:
An additional theme delivered along with the main Theme.
Ex: I ordered a cappuccino and he DELIVERED it ["CT" along with a ricebubble sweet snack].

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
A container in which the Theme is delivered.
Ex: We DELIVERED the roses ["con" in a beautiful vase] as you requested.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the delivery takes place.
Ex: Barney DELIVERED the letter on Monday ["Place" in Sheboygan]

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed at which the Deliverer delivers the Theme.
Ex: This service is for our clients who need ["spe" speedy] DELIVERY of their goods.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the delivery takes place.
Ex: Purchases over $400 are DELIVERED for free.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The location of the Theme before the delivery process begins.
Ex: We offer direct DELIVERY of all of your packages ["sou" from anywhere in the UK].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means are intermediate actions performed by the Deliverer in order to move the package to the Goal.
Ex: He always DELIVERS the papers ["mea" by tossing them through people's windows].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The path along which the Theme moves while being delivered.
Ex: He DELIVERED it ["pat" through the transom] .
Ex: Oil DELIVERIES were _made_ ["pat" along the interstate].

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: The person for whom the Delivery action occurs.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the Delivery event.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the Delivery event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

lexunit.name: deliver.v
lexunit.definition: FN: bring and hand over to the appropriate recipient.

lexunit.name: delivery.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of delivering something, especially letters or goods.

frame.name: Fields
frame.definition:
An individual or group (Practitioner) or a part of their work life (Work) is defined professionally by the Activity that they typically engage in. Alternatively, the Activity may be indicated by a Salient_entity conventionally associated with it.
Ex: ["pra" Chris] was _in_ the ["act" construction] INDUSTRY for 20 years before coming to GSCM.
Ex: ["wor" My career] _was_ IN ["sal" oil and gas].

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
An activity that defines a group of people in their professional capacity.
Ex: One of the companies we are presently invested in is Boral, which is in the ["act" building] SECTOR.

fe.name: Practitioner
fe.definition:
The individual, group, or organization that engages in the Activity as part of their profession.
Ex: ["pra" I] _am_ IN biology (molecular immunology).
Ex: The manufacturing ["pra" SECTOR] has complained to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) about the country's private commercial banks.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
A physical or abstract entity that is characteristically associated with the Activity.
Ex: These companies who have their roots in either the 19th or early 20th century have been IN ["sal" oil] all their existence.

fe.name: Work
fe.definition:
A phase of a Practitioner's career that is spent engaged in an Activity.
Ex: ["wor" My most recent job] was in the construction INDUSTRY.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: The subfield of the Activity that the Practitioner is engaged in.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Practitioner engages in the Activity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Practitioner engages in the Activity.

lexunit.name: sector.n

lexunit.name: in.prep

lexunit.name: field.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular branch of study or sphere of activity.

lexunit.name: area.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a subject or range of activity.

lexunit.name: artistic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having a talent for creating art.

lexunit.name: art.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the expression or application of creative skill and imagination, especially through a visual medium such as painting or sculpture.

lexunit.name: literary.a
lexunit.definition: COD: concerning the writing, study, or content of literature, especially of the kind valued for quality of form.

lexunit.name: literature.n
lexunit.definition: COD: written works, especially those regarded as having artistic merit.

lexunit.name: theater.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a play or other activity considered in terms of its dramatic quality.

lexunit.name: industrial.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of or from a particular branch of economic sector

lexunit.name: history.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the academic study concerned with understanding the events of the past

frame.name: Supply
frame.definition:
A Supplier gives a Theme to a Recipient to fulfill a need or purpose (Purpose_of_recipient) of the Recipient.
Ex: Habituating the ground nesting chimp groups is done by PROVISIONING ["Recipient" them] ["Theme" with sugar cane]. ["Supplier" CNI] ["Purpose_of_recipient" INI]
Ex: ["Supplier" I] have EQUIPPED ["Recipient" my leechtroopers] ["Theme" with tiny subspace displacement thingummies]. ["Purpose_of_recipient" INI]
Ex: She sat down on her bed, carefully folding her clothing and packing it into ["Theme" the small carryall] ["Supplier" Starfleet] had PROVIDED ["Recipient" her] ["por" for the journey].

fe.name: Supplier
fe.definition:
The person that begins in possession of the Themeand causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.
Ex: I approve of ["sup" your] having SUPPLIED him with a file of soldiers.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition:
The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.
Ex: VESID also SUPPLIED ["rec" him] with an all zone bus pass to help him travel to interviews.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The object that is given to the Recipient .
Ex: Cromwell merged men from multiple regiments into a single one and PROVISIONED them ["Thm" with red uniforms] to replace their former regiment colors.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place where the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
Ex: The Harpley was launched in Launceston on the 2nd February, 1847, and with the exception of her chain cables, was ["Place" there] SUPPLIED with all her materials and stores.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for which the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
Ex: Jesus EQUIPPED them ["Reas" because if they tried to do it in their own strength they would have understood defeat in a whole new way].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time is when the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
Ex: In Breidbach, water tankers were ["Time" yesterday] SUPPLIED to the community as the main water supply pipe had been washed away.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.
Ex: Some financial support can be PROVIDED ["Purp" in order to help you and MPI with the product approval process in an efficient and effective way].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means by which the Supplier acquires or gives the Theme to the Recipient.
Ex: Euell PROVISIONED them ["Mns" by foraging, hunting, and trapping whenever his father was away].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the supplying event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Supplier that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: P&G ["Man" secretly] PROVIDED Schwartz with several boxes of documents.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Theme is supplied.
Ex: ["Supplier" I] SUPPLIED ["Theme" the food] ["Circumstances" free of charge].

fe.name: Purpose_of_recipient
fe.definition:
The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme.
Ex: God gave them the promise of victory and EQUIPPED them ["por" for the battle].

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition:
The period over which the Supplier engages in (multiple) supplying acts.
Our company has supplied nations with voting machines ["per" SINCE 2000].

fe.name: Co_theme
fe.definition:
An additional theme which is supplied along with the main Theme.
Ex: Several cables were PROVIDED ["cot" with the printer], but I'm not sure which ones to use.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The source of the Theme.
Ex: We EQUIPPED them ["sou" from our own supply of equipment].

lexunit.name: supply.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide with something needed.

lexunit.name: provide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make available for use; supply

lexunit.name: supply.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of supplying.

lexunit.name: provision.v
lexunit.definition: COD: supply with provisions

lexunit.name: provision.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of providing or supplying

lexunit.name: supplier.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the person or organization that provides a resource

lexunit.name: equip.v
lexunit.definition: COD: supply with the items needed for a particular purpose.

lexunit.name: equipment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process of supplying needed resources

lexunit.name: outfit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide with an outfit of clothes or equipment.

lexunit.name: fix up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide someone with something.

lexunit.name: fuel.v
lexunit.definition: COD: supply or power with fuel.

lexunit.name: issue.v
lexunit.definition: FN: supply someone with something necessary

frame.name: Source_of_getting
frame.definition:
A Goal has a Source from which it has gotten a Theme. The Goal may be a sentient recipient who has actively obtained the Theme but it may also be a non-sentient entity that gets the Theme as a result of natural or other processes that it does not control.
Ex: ["sou" she] _is_ my friend...not to mention ["goa" my] SOURCE ["thm" for French madeleines]!
Ex: Pakistan informed IAEA and US officials investigating the network that ["sou" North Korea] _was_ the SOURCE ["thm" of the uranium shipment] ["goa" DNI].
Ex: ["sou" The state] remains the dominant SOURCE ["thm" of research funding]. ["goa" INI]
Ex: This is not true according to ["goa" our] ["sou" SOURCE]. ["thm" DNI]
Ex:
Note that we also take this frame to cover as metaphorical uses those cases where a person has obtained from another person or a textual source, which they typically intend to disseminate further.
Ex: Crews was held in contempt and ordered to jail after refusing to reveal ["goa" his] ["sou" SOURCE] ["thm" for the claim that Big Basketweaving is circumventing import tariffs on reed.]

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The abstact or concrete thing acquired by the Goal from the Source.
Ex: The sun doesn't burn up because its SOURCE ["thm" of power] is nuclear energy.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
A concrete or abstract entity from which the Goal has gotten the Theme.
Ex: ["sou" Dr Kelly] is his SOURCE for the specific information relating to phlogiston production.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
An entity or individual that has acquired a Theme from the Source.
Ex: The beetles thereby cut off ["goa" the tree's] SOURCE of nourishment and it dies.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any evaluative or descriptive characterization of the Source, pertaining either to temporary or permanent properties.
Ex: In fact , the amount of electricity produced by ["des" renewable] SOURCES in the UK has steadily declined over the past five years.

lexunit.name: source.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person or document that provides information.

frame.name: Ingredients
frame.definition:
A Material is used to make a Product.
Ex: These ["use" cooking] ["mat" INGREDIENTS] are readily available.
Ex: An ["des" aberrant] ["pro" hemoglobin] ["mat" PRECURSOR] has been discovered to be implicated.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
The entity which is used to make a Product.
Ex: Add all the ["mat" INGREDIENTS], toss and chill.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Material belongs to.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The location that the Material comes from, including both extraction sites and emission/production sources.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characterization of the Material.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The purpose for which the Material is intended.
Ex: Supply and placing of ["use" building] MATERIALS shall be incidental to installation of the paving stones.

fe.name: Product
fe.definition: The entity or substance that is created out of the Material.

lexunit.name: ingredient.n
lexunit.definition: FN: something that enters into a compound or becomes part of a combination or mixture.

lexunit.name: precursor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a substance from which another is formed, especially by metabolic reaction

lexunit.name: material.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the matter from which a thing is or can be made

lexunit.name: component.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a part or element of a larger whole, especially a part of a machine or vehicle.

lexunit.name: element.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the most basic factor or part that makes up something

frame.name: Cause_to_make_progress
frame.definition: An Agent works on a Project so that it reaches a more advanced and desirable state.

fe.name: Project
fe.definition: The object or idea that undergoes change due to the efforts of the Agent.

fe.name: Prior_state
fe.definition: The former state of the Project.

fe.name: Post_state
fe.definition: The state of the Project following an advance.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the progress occurs.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: The rate at which the change happens.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (_the same way_); in addition, it may describe characteristics and states of the Agent that also affect the development.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The period over which the Agent develops the Project.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The amount of advancement that the Project has attained.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The relevant dimension of development.
Ex: We have DEVELOPED our community ["dom" economically] in these last few years.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that brings about the development of the Project.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the the Project progresses.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent progresses the Project.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Agent which enables the advancement.

lexunit.name: develop.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to become more advanced.

lexunit.name: development.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of promoting the advancement of.

lexunit.name: gains.n
lexunit.definition: FN: progress made in a particular field.

lexunit.name: perfect.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause development at the highest standard.

lexunit.name: improve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make better.

lexunit.name: improved.a
lexunit.definition: FN: made better

lexunit.name: modernization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of making up-to-date.

lexunit.name: mature.v
lexunit.definition: FN: develop

frame.name: Range
frame.definition:
There is a certain physical Distance within which some other entity can participate in an Event (typically perception or manipulation) with the Participant. Alternatively, the Event may be indicated metonymically by a Instrument . [Note the connection with *Distance, Sufficiency, and Capability. Words in this frame can generally be paraphrased "close enough to be able to".]
Ex: I'm sorry, but he was well within the ["eve" blast] ["dis" RANGE]. Ex: They are now within ["par" our] ["ins" missile] ["dis" RANGE]. Ex: They are now within ["par" our missile 's] ["dis" RANGE]. Ex: They are now within ["ins" missile] ["dis" RANGE]. Ex: But then they passed out of ["par" my] ["dis" EARSHOT]. ["ins" INC] Ex: I would consider ["eve" striking] DISTANCE to _be_ ["dis" about two meters] for this weapon. Ex: Jordanian troops came within easy ["dis" STRIKE] of Israel.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: A type of occurrence whose effects extend a certain distance.

fe.name: Participant
fe.definition:
An entity that is conceived as driving the Event.
Ex: ["par" Their] missile RANGE has decreased, since we have degraded their sensors.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity which is deployable by the Participant to interact with things within a certain distance.
Ex: Their ["ins" laser] RANGE is four times ours .

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
The spatial extent over which the Participant can interact in an Event.
Ex: Our RANGE is ["dis" smaller than theirs]. Ex: Normal people have a REACH ["dis" of around one meter].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the description of a Participant's range holds.
Ex: The patient has a lesser RANGE of motion ["cir" in cold weather].

lexunit.name: power.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the distance within which it is possible for someone or something to exert influence on somebody or something

lexunit.name: range.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the distance that is possible (for someone or something to do something)

lexunit.name: earshot.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the distance over which one can hear.

lexunit.name: reach.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the extent or range of an entity's application, effect, or influence

lexunit.name: view.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the distance over which somebody can see (from a particular position)

lexunit.name: distance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the distance within which an event has an effect

lexunit.name: strike.n
lexunit.definition: FN: distance from which an attack can be launched.

lexunit.name: intercontinental.a
lexunit.definition: COD: relating to or travelling between continents.

lexunit.name: sight.n
lexunit.definition: FN: extent of vision (including metaphorical): in sight of land, out of sight of the enemy, in his sight

frame.name: Ratification
frame.definition:
A Ratifier responds to a Proposal constructed by another party to make it binding over the Ratifier's jurisdiction or constituency.
Ex: The RATIFICATION ["Proposal" of the Kyoto protocol] has been a long, hard slog. Ex: ["rat" The US] is considering RATIFYING ["pro" the cybercrime treaty]. Ex: ["rat" The Malaysian government] will RATIFY ["pro" the UN's anti-smoking programme] by the end of the year.

fe.name: Ratifier
fe.definition:
The individual or body that confirms a Proposal negotiated or created by another party, causing it to become binding in a jurisdiction represented by the Ratifier. In the case of direct democratic ratification, the jurisdiction and the Ratifier are the same.
Ex: If ["rat" we] RATIFY Management 's plan , we 'll have to take a drug test every week !

fe.name: Proposal
fe.definition:
The idea or course of action proposed by another individual or body which the Ratifier endorses and makes binding.
Ex: President Aleksander Kwasniewski RATIFIED ["pro" protocols to the Europol Convention].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Ratifier makes the Proposal binding.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is where the Ratifier ratifies the Proposal.
Ex:

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose is the goal of the Ratifier when they ratify the Proposal.
Ex: The South had to RATIFY these amendments ["pur" to be readmitted to the Union]

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the cognitive cause of the Ratifier's ratification.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the allowing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Ratifier that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: It is no coincidence that the EU, on behalf of its 25 member states, has ["man" eagerly] RATIFIED Rotterdam and other treaties, no doubt seeing it as the perfect opportunity.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action of the Ratifier whereby they make binding the Proposal.
Ex: After Inuit approve the Labrador Inuit Land Claim Agreement, the province will RATIFY it ["mea" by submitting it to the provincial cabinet for approval, and then signing it].

lexunit.name: ratify.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give formal consent to; make officially valid

lexunit.name: ratification.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of giving formal consent

frame.name: Obviousness
frame.definition:
A Phenomenon is portrayed with respect to the Degree of likelihood that it will be perceived and known, given the (usually implicit) Evidence, Perceiver, and the Circumstances in which it is considered. For several of the LUs, such as _visible, audible, etc._, the type of the Evidence is fixed by the targets themselves being a perceptual experience.
Ex: It_'s_ ["deg" abundantly] OBVIOUS ["phe" that we'll need to spend more time on public perception]. Ex: Are you certain that ["phe" the shovel] _was_ VISIBLE ["loc" from the door of the apartment]? Ex: I think they miss ["phe" some of the important impacts of the work that] _are_ not VISIBLE ["evi" just from looking at the vote tally]. Ex: ["phe" That the defense will declare a mistrial regardless] _is_ ["deg" quite] EVIDENT ["evi" from their consistent obstructionist tactics]. Ex: ["tim" In late July 2000] ["phe" it] _was_ ["deg" barely] VISIBLE ["per" to the unaided eye].

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
The entity or facts that are undeniable given the Evidence.
Ex: It is OBVIOUS for example ["phe" that 9/10 is not the same as 1].

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The gradable aspect of a Phenomenon which concerns how likely it is that the Phenomenon be known. This frame element is incorporated by the lexical units in this frame.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of the Phenomenon from the norm or from the value for another Phenomenon in terms of how likely the Phenomenon would be known.
Ex: It is ["deg" abundantly] OBVIOUS you have not a clue how the Retro Program works.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time during which the Phenomenon is obvious
Ex: It is OBVIOUS ["tim" now] that Senator O. T. Tawa has no plan.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the conditions under which the Phenomenon is likely to be known.

fe.name: Perceiver
fe.definition:
The sentient entity for whom perception or cognition of the Phenomenon is judged to be more or less likely.
Ex: It was OBVIOUS ["per" to Peter] he had made a wise choice.

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
A state-of-affairs that has a bearing on whether the Phenomenon will be perceived or apprehended cognitively. Evidence is often metonymically indicated by the mention of an entity whose existence or whose properties are relevant.
Ex: It is usually OBVIOUS ["evi" from the context] which meaning is appropriate.
Some lexical units such as _visible_, _audible_ etc. which refer directly to perception in a particular modality incorporate the Evidence frame element.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition:
The likelihood of a Phenomenon to be observed perceptually or cognitively in a particular Group of comparable background items may be contrasted, implicitly or explicitly, with different groups.
Ex: This correlation was OBVIOUS ["gro" in patients classified as acute myeloid leukemia (AML)as well as in the monocytic varieties of ANLL].

fe.name: Location_of_protagonist
fe.definition:
The physical location of a Perceiver of the Phenomenon or a metaphorical point-of-view location of a cognizer relative to the Phenomenon.
Ex: It is OBVIOUS ["loc" from here] that the crux of the climb is the ascent up to the southern peak.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.
Ex: The top of the mountain SHOWED ["Direction" through the mist]

lexunit.name: obvious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: easily perceived or understood; clear.

lexunit.name: evident.a
lexunit.definition: COD: plain or obvious; clear.

lexunit.name: manifest.a
lexunit.definition: COD: clear or obvious to the eye or mind.

lexunit.name: visible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be perceived or noticed easily

lexunit.name: audible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be heard.

lexunit.name: unclear.a
