lexunit.definition: COD: not obvious, definite, or certain.

lexunit.name: clear.a
lexunit.definition: FN: such that there is no doubt

lexunit.name: clearly.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: obviously; without doubt.

lexunit.name: obviously.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: readily deducible or perceivable.

lexunit.name: clarity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state or quality of being clear, distinct, and easily perceived or understood.

lexunit.name: clearly_((clarity)).adv
lexunit.definition: COD: with clarity.

lexunit.name: show.v
lexunit.definition: FN: obvious, apparent, able to be perceived

frame.name: Extradition
frame.definition: A Suspect in a Current_jurisdiction is forced by Authorities (of the Current_jurisdiction) to go to the Crime_jurisdiction, i.e. the jurisdiction which requested that the Suspect be handed over for trial for a crime which he or she is suspected to have committed in the Crime_jurisdiction. The purpose or reason for the extradition may also be expressed.

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition:
The Authorities act on behalf of the Current_jurisdiction, giving up the Suspect to the Crime_jurisdiction.
Ex: ["aut" French officials] EXTRADITED him back to Canada.

fe.name: Current_jurisdiction
fe.definition:
The jurisdiction (generally a nation) the Suspect starts off in.
Ex: Jones was EXTRADITED ["cur" from Mexico] last Thursday to face criminal charges in the United States.

fe.name: Crime_jurisdiction
fe.definition:
The jurisdiction (generally a nation) to which the Suspect is sent.
Ex: It was the third time a neo-Nazi was EXTRADITED from Denmark ["cri" to Germany].

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition:
The Suspect is forced to go to the jurisdiction where a crime he or she is suspected of took place or is being tried.
Ex: A hearing on whether or not to EXTRADITE ["sus" Johnson] to Isreal will be held tomorrow.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which the Authorities extradite the Suspect.
Ex: The authorities EXTRADITED him ["Purp" for trial] in the US.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for which the Authorities extradite the Suspect.
Ex: The authorities EXTRADITED him to the US ["Reas" for drug trafficking].

fe.name: Legal_Basis
fe.definition: This FE indicates the basis in law of an extradition. Ex: He was EXTRADITED ["LBasis" under the long-standing treaty between the two nations].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Suspect is moved.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the manner of the extradition.
Ex: They are seeking ["man" rapid] EXTRADITION.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A description of the Authorities or Suspect during the extradition.
Ex: It had been five years since his ["dep" handcuffed] EXTRADITION from France.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The act of the Authorities which brings about the transfer from the Current_jurisdiction to the Crime_jurisdiction.
Ex: The EXTRADITED him ["mea" by continually badgering the French].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the extradition occurs.
Ex: ["Place" In Europe] they EXTRADITE more freely than in North America.

lexunit.name: extradite.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hand over (a person accused or convicted of a crime) to the jurisdiction of the foreign state in which the crime was committed.

lexunit.name: extradition.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of giving up a person suspected or convicted of a crime to the jurisdiction of the place where the crime was committed.

frame.name: Organization
frame.definition: This frame describes intentionally formed human social groups (here termed Organizations) with some definite structure and Members. They may be relatively informal, consisting only of a group of individuals who are aware of who is and who is not a fellow member, or they may be complex and long-lasting, such as the Roman Catholic Church or the Conservative Party.

fe.name: Organization
fe.definition: The entity of which the individuals are Members.

fe.name: Members
fe.definition: A person belonging to an Organization.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which an Organization is formed.

fe.name: Period_of_existence
fe.definition: The interval during which the Organization exists.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: A name given to the organization for identification.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition:
The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within.
Ex: Or, if you want to work on women's human rights issues, work for a ["con" Canadian] ORGANIZATION that advocates on behalf of women.

lexunit.name: cartel.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an organization of producers (and sometimes middlemen) intended to control commerce in some commodity for the benefit of the members.

lexunit.name: club.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A voluntary social organization created for the benefit of its members; clubs may be informal, or large and highly organized.

lexunit.name: society.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: an organization formed by people with shared interests

lexunit.name: government.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the governing body of a state

lexunit.name: organization.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an organized body of people with a particular purpose, such as a business or government department.

lexunit.name: association.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a group of people organized for a joint purpose.

lexunit.name: league.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a collection of people, countries, or groups that combine for mutual protection or cooperation.

lexunit.name: intelligence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an organization devoted to the collection of information.

lexunit.name: agency.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a government office or department providing a specific service for a state.

lexunit.name: union.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a club, society, or association formed by people with a common interest or purpose.

lexunit.name: brotherhood.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a fraternity of men joined by like interests

lexunit.name: delegation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: An group of individuals meeting in a group in representation of others.

lexunit.name: committee.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A small group assembling to decide certain affairs or charge some endeavor.

lexunit.name: group.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an organized set of individuals set upon some task

frame.name: Cause_to_resume
frame.definition: An agent acts so as to cause some process to begin again after an interruption or suspension.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: A sentient being acts with the intention of causing a process to begin again. Ex: ["Agent" The driver] RESTARTED the truck after it stalled.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The process which begins again after a suspension.

fe.name: Hiatus
fe.definition: The period of time during which the process is suspended. Ex: The two countries REVIVED ["Process" diplomatic relations] ["Hiatus" after a lull of five years].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the process is restarted. Ex: This state REINSTATED ["Process" the death penalty] ["Time" in 1975].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that causes the process to resume. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.
Ex: ["Cause" The spring rains] RESTARTED ["Process" the flow of the stream].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Agent causes the Process to resume.
Ex: The two nations REVIVED relations ["pla" in Geneva] during the latest round of talks.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The intentional act performed by the Agent that results in the resumption of the Process.
Ex: He managed to REVIVE the controversy ["mea" by leaking the story to several tabloid magazines].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the manner in which the Agent causes the resumption of the Process.
Ex: Japanese banks have been ["man" rapidly] REVIVING business activity.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
The length of time for which the Process continues after being started by the Agent.
Ex: The project was RESTARTED ["dur" for several weeks] before it was permanently abandoned.

lexunit.name: revive.v
lexunit.definition: FN: To cause to begin again after a period of inactivity.

lexunit.name: restart.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to start again, after a period of inactivity.

lexunit.name: reinstate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: bring a process back into an active state.

frame.name: Needing
frame.definition:
The speaker believes that some state of affairs or entity (the Requirement) must be present in order to cause some other dependent state of affairs to occur (the Dependent). In the typical case, the Cognizer desires the occurrence of the Dependent and so also desires the obtainment or occurrence of the Requirement.
Ex: ["cog" I] NEED ["req" one more bolt]. ["dep" DNI] Ex: ["cog" I] NEED ["req" one more nail] ["dep" to finish building the cabinet]. Ex: ["dep" In order to complete the treaty], ["cog" the United States] wil REQUIRE ["req" several more diplomats]. Ex: ["cog" He] NEEDS ["req" everyone to leave his office] ["dep" to finish his work].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer requires or believes he/she requires the Requirement to hold so that the Dependent will occur.

fe.name: Requirement
fe.definition: The entity or state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Dependent
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the conditions under which the Requirement is likely to be needed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Cognizer requires the Requirement.
Ex: I NEED that book ["tim" now]!

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location of the Cognizer when he/she requires the Requirement.
Ex: ["pla" Over at Merv's house] they NEED three more cement trucks to finish the job.

fe.name: Consequences
fe.definition:
An undesirable state-of-affairs that results if the Requirement is not met.
Ex: He NEEDS to focus on his schoolwork, ["con" or he's not going to pass the third grade].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times the Cognizer has a need per some unit of time.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why the Cognizer needs the Requirement.

lexunit.name: need.v
lexunit.definition: COD: require (something) because it is essential or very important rather than just desirable.

lexunit.name: require.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have a believe that some object or state is necessary for some other (desirable) state to obtain.

lexunit.name: need.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a necessary or required circumstances or situation.

frame.name: Adjusting
frame.definition:
An Agent changes a Part of a complex entity with regard to some Feature in order to achieve some Imposed_purpose affected by the Feature. The complex entity is often a device or mechanism, but may also be an abstract entity such as the economy. Also, the full entity may be used in place of the Part.
Ex: ["Agent" I] need to ADJUST ["Part" the thermostat] ["Final_value" to around 80 degrees] ["Time" when she visits]. Ex: It didn't work the first time , so ["Agent" she] had to TWEAK ["Part" the oven] ["Degree" a little] . Ex: Greenspan expressed confidence that the ["Time" current] CALIBRATION ["Feature" of interest rates] was not an overcompensation .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that controls the value of a Feature.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: The part of the complex entity which is changed in the process of adjusting. Ex: She ADJUSTED ["Part" the injectors] to make the mixture leaner.

fe.name: Feature
fe.definition: The Feature with respect to which the Part is adjusted. Ex: She ADJUSTED ["Feature" the temperature of the oven] ["Purpose" so that the pie crust would brown a little].

fe.name: Imposed_purpose
fe.definition:
The state of the Part with respect to the Feature that the Agent brings about by making the adjustment.
Ex: You should ADJUST the antenna ["imp" to poke outside the bag].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action performed by the Agent which affects the Part.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the adjusting takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the adjusting occurs.

fe.name: Final_value
fe.definition: The value associated with the Feature that the system ends up in.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: An entity manipulated by the Agent to adjust the Part and Feature.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about by adjusting.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the adjustment act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A characterization of the amount that the Final_value and Initial_value differ.
Ex: Do n't ADJUST the pressure ["deg" by more than two PSI] .

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: adjust.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to change the location of some part or the degree of some quanity by a (relatively) small amount, especially in order to cause some system to function better

lexunit.name: adjustment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A (relatively) small change made in some part of a complex system made in order to cause it to function better.

lexunit.name: tweak.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to change the location of some part or the degree of some quanity by a very small amount, especially in order to cause some system to function better

lexunit.name: tweak.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A very small change made in some part of a complex system made in order to cause it to function better.

lexunit.name: calibrate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: To adjust something to make it accord with a standard or norm.

lexunit.name: calibration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of adjusting something so that it will accord with a norm or standard.

frame.name: Rank
frame.definition: This frame contains nouns denoting a rank or level within an extablished hierachy.

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: The Rank itself, usually denoted by the noun.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: An entity which holds a particular Rank.

lexunit.name: rank.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a level within a hierarchy of merit

lexunit.name: level.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a level within a hierarchy

lexunit.name: degree.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a level within a hierarchy, usually quite formal.

frame.name: Reassuring
frame.definition: A Speaker conveys Content to an Experiencer in order to reassure them about a Situation; Medium and the Means of the communication also may be expressed.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The sentient entity that uses language in the written or spoken modality to reassure another person. Ex: ["Speaker" He] REASSURED her that she was his favorite ice-skating star.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer receives reassurance from the Speaker. Ex: He tried to REASSURE ["Exp" his potential customers] that his company not only offered the best service, but also the most competitive prices.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
Content A proposition or set of propositions that the Speaker wants the Experiencerto believe in order to feel reassured.
Ex: How do you REASSURE them ["Content" that you really like them] ?

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition:
Situation is the problem plaguing the Experiencer, about which the Speaker reassures them.
Ex: The policeman REASSURED him ["Situation" about the safety of the neighborhood].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.

fe.name: Amount_of_reassurance
fe.definition: The amount of reassurance given. Ex: He never really ["Amount_of_reassurance" fully] REASSURED me about the situation.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Speaker.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Speaker reassures the ["Exp" Experiencer].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means by which the Speaker reassures the Experiencer.
Ex: Him mother reassured him ["Mns" with a pat on the back].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the reassurance takes place.

lexunit.name: reassurance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: allay the doubts and fears of

lexunit.name: reassure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: allay the doubts and fears of

frame.name: Occupy_rank
frame.definition:
This frame is about Items in the state of occupying a certain Rank within a hierarchy.
Ex: ["Item" He] RANKS ["Rank" second] ["com" in his class] ["dim" in mathematics].

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: The Rank which the Item occupies.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The Item which occupies the Rank in the hierarchy.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition: The dimension along which the ranking is defined. Ex: He RANKS second in his class ["Dimension" in mathematics].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which/period over which the Item occupies the Rank Ex: Jim RANKED as thirty-second degree Mason ["Time" in 1970].

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition:
The Comparison_set is the set of entities ranked in a hierarchy. The Item is a member of the set.
Ex: He RANKS highest ["com" among his peers] in the field of basket weaving.

lexunit.name: rank.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to occupy a (given) rank in a hierarchy.

lexunit.name: stand.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to be at a specified level or rank in a hierarchy.

lexunit.name: top.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the uppermost ranking

frame.name: Be_in_agreement_on_action
frame.definition: Two (or more) people (the Parties, also encodable as Party_1 and Party_2) have an agreement. Both sides are construed as having a commitment to an Obligation--the relationship is understood to be symmetrical or reciprocal. Instead of a specific mention of the Obligation, a Topic expression may be used to indicate the domain covered.

fe.name: Party_1
fe.definition:
The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of the agreement, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus Manner is construed to be that of Party_1, not necessarily that of Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.
Ex: ["par1" AOL 's] AGREEMENT with the ACLU will soon expire , and renogotiation is not a real possibility .

fe.name: Party_2
fe.definition:
The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the agreement. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).
Ex: Mozilla Foundation now has a bindingAGREEMENT ["par2" with America Online].

fe.name: Obligation
fe.definition:
An expression of the commitment of the Parties .
Ex: The US and Russia have an AGREEMENT ["obl" to share early warning data on missile launches].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
Topic is a description of the domain covered by the agreement.
Ex: Some types of alloy steel have been covered in the expiring ["top" trade] AGREEMENT.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.
Ex: The parties have a ["med" written] AGREEMENT to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.

fe.name: Parties
fe.definition:
The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in having an agreement.
Ex: ["pars" The US and Russia] have an AGREEMENT to cooperate in destroying surplus portable anti-aircraft missiles.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where an agreement was made.
Ex: The ["pla" Kyoto] TREATY has so far been relatively ineffectual.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the agreement was made.
Ex: The missile AGREEMENT ["tim" of 1952] was still in force, however.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the agreement not specified by the other FEs, including particularly salient characteristics of the parties.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: This FE describes a characteristic or description of the agreement_on_action.

lexunit.name: treaty.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A formal agreement between two or more nations governed by international law

lexunit.name: agreement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: negotiated and typically legally binding arrangement.

lexunit.name: deal.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an agreement entered into by two or more parties for their mutual benefit.

lexunit.name: accord.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an official agreement or treaty.

lexunit.name: convention.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an agreement between states, especially one less formal than a treaty.

frame.name: Required_event
frame.definition:
Unless a particular Required_situation obtains, Negative_consequences will follow. Alternatively, the Required_situation is required to achieve a Purpose (which avoids Negative_consequences). A set of Circumstances may be specified under which the requirement holds.
Ex: ["req" You] MUST ["req" turn in your test by 5 p.m.] Ex: ["req" You] BETTER ["req" have that fixed by tomorrow] ["neg" or else we'll fire you]. Ex: ["req" The book] NEEDS ["req" to be shorter] ["pur" to sell to such a young audience.]

fe.name: Required_situation
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which prevents Negative_consequences.

fe.name: Negative_consequences
fe.definition: An event or state of affairs that results if the required Required_situation does not occur and which impacts some deprofiled entity in a way that the speaker finds undesirable.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the requirement holds.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The event or state of affairs that is achieved by bringing about the Required_situation and which entails the non-occurrance of Negative_consequences.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The period during which the Required_situation is necessary to prevent negative consequences.
Ex: He was told that ["tim" when he got back] , his column NEEDED a serious rethink .

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location within which the Required_situation is required.
Ex: ["pla" In California] , seatbelts MUST be fastened at all times .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The reason why the Required_situation is necessary.
Ex: I do realize his pitch NEEDED to be wide-ranging ["exp" because of the differences between folks in the room] .

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Required_situation is necessary. The Degree may either imply a modification of the direness of the Negative_consequences, the probability of the Negative_consequences (if the Required_situation is not made to hold), or both.
Ex: He ["deg" absolutely] MUST be replaced .

lexunit.name: must.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be strongly required in order to avoid negative consequences, social or otherwise

lexunit.name: need.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be required in order to avoid negative consequences, usually physical

lexunit.name: had better.v
lexunit.definition: COD: would find it wiser to.

lexunit.name: better.v
lexunit.definition: FN: would find it wiser to.

lexunit.name: got_to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be obliged to; must

lexunit.name: gotta.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have got to.

lexunit.name: hafta.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have to

lexunit.name: oughta.v
lexunit.definition: FN: ought to

lexunit.name: have to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: must.

lexunit.name: should.v
lexunit.definition: FN: ought to be.

lexunit.name: ought to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: should.

lexunit.name: be_supposed_(to).v
lexunit.definition: COD: be required or expected to do something.

lexunit.name: best.v
lexunit.definition: FN: had better; ought to

frame.name: Desirable_event
frame.definition:
A particular State_of_affairs is desirable. The State_of_affairs may be required to achieve a Purpose. A set of Circumstances may be specified under which the assessment of desirability holds.
Ex: ["sta" You] SHOULD ["sta" take the doses about 12 hours apart and at the same time each day]. Ex: ["cir" If the metal is seriously rusted or warped], ["sta" it] SHOULD ["sta" be repaired or replaced with a chimney top damper]. Ex: ["pur" To ensure that], ["sta" you] SHOULD ["sta" have no CLASSPATH set].

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition: The State_of_affairs that the speaker finds desirable.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the State_of_affairs has the specified assessment of desirability.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The event or state of affairs that is achieved by bringing about the desirable State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the specified desirability of the State_of_affairs deviates from the expected desirability.

lexunit.name: should.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be a desirable state of affairs

lexunit.name: ought to.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be a desirable state of affairs

lexunit.name: bad idea.n
lexunit.definition: FN: be an undesirable course of action

lexunit.name: good idea.n
lexunit.definition: FN: be a desirable course of action

frame.name: Getting_vehicle_underway
frame.definition:
A Driver prepares a Vehicle for travel by placing it in the normal location for the operation of the vehicle or by detaching it from a place where it was held.
Ex: Throughout Irish history, ["Driver" countless generations of exiles] have CAST OFF ["Source" from the shores of Ireland]. Ex: "Good," said Matt as ["Driver" he] PULLED ["Vehicle" the car] ["Source" out of the parking space]. Ex: The next day, after WEIGHING ANCHOR, ["Driver" we] cleared Longboat Pass Bridge, and exited the ICW into the open waters of the Gulf of Mexico.

fe.name: Driver
fe.definition:
This is the being, typically human, that prepares the Vehicle for motion, and will control it once it is in motion.
Ex: ["Driver" He] shook his head in amazement and slowly PULLED the car out of the parking lot.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The device--such as a car, boat, spaceship,. etc.--which is used for transport and is prepared for travel by the Driver.
Ex: Lyle was feeling very pleased with himself as he PULLED ["Veh" the BMW] out of its parking space.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Any expression which describes the location that the Vehicle has been stationed at.
Ex: The ship CAST OFF ["Source" from Pier 21].

fe.name: Intended_goal
fe.definition:
The location that the Vehicle is intended to travel to.
Ex: At 1500 65 Royal Air Force personnel came aboard and the LCI 35 CAST OFF ["int" for England].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Driver that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: The Duchess of Northumberland ["Manr" slowly] WEIGHED ANCHOR and pulled away from the wharf at London.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Driver or Vehicle during the preparations.
Ex: We CAST OFF from the dock ["Dep" in fear] and headed for Pequaming.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action performed by the Driver by which they prepare the Vehicle for travel.
Ex: I WEIGHED ANCHOR ["mns" by hand] - an easy affair with a boat that weighs less than a ton - and headed south with the Class of '93-'94.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
Result of the Driver's action.
Ex: Bill PULLED his Maserati out ["Result" right into a truck].

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
An individual or vehicle that is also involved in the preparations.
Ex: On 8 April the Admiral WEIGHED ANCHOR ["cop" with three of his consorts], leaving the others to follow.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the preparation of the Vehicle takes place.
Ex: At sunrise I WEIGHED ANCHOR ["cir" in a light breeze] and set off for Spain.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place describes the location where the Driver prepares the Vehicle for motion.
Ex: At 0900 on 10 September 1945, DE 353 WEIGHED ANCHOR ["Place" in Victoria Harbor], adjacent to Labuan Island, Borneo.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
The length of the time that the Vehicle remains in the state of readiness.
Ex: We WEIGHED ANCHOR ["dur" for only 2 hours] before the storm became too intense.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Driver prepares the Vehicle for motion.
Ex: We WEIGHED ANCHOR ["Time" in the afternoon of October 9th] and got out of the harbour under all plain sail.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE marks a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

lexunit.name: launch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set (a boat or ship) afloat, especially by sliding it into the water.

lexunit.name: weigh anchor.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take up the anchor when ready to sail

lexunit.name: cast off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set a boat or ship free from her moorings.

lexunit.name: pull_(out).v
lexunit.definition: FN: to steer a vehicle out of a parking or holding space

lexunit.name: lift_(off).v
lexunit.definition: FN: Leave from the ground for air travel

lexunit.name: take_(off).v
lexunit.definition: FN: depart

frame.name: Success_or_failure
frame.definition:
An Agent has attempted to achieve a Goal, and the actual outcome of the Agent's action has been resolved, so that it either specifically matches the Agent's intent (e.g. _success_) or does not match it (e.g. _failure_).
Ex: ["age" He] PULLED OFF ["goa" his April Fool's Day prank] ["deg" by the barest of margins] . Ex: Unfortunately, ["age" we] _were_ n't SUCCESSFUL. ["goa" DNI] Ex: ["age" We] FAILED ["deg" miserably] ["goa" at getting the gay rights bill passed] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: ["Agent" John] MANAGED a feeble smile.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.
Ex: If you don't SUCCEED ["goa" in your subterfuge], then report back for further orders.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Goal is achieved (or not).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt occurs.
Ex: Your attempt at convincing me has ["deg" utterly] FAILED.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where an attempt succeeds or fails.
Ex: ["Place" On the bridge] he SUCCEEDED in putting the wig on the corpse.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
A participant function in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.
Ex: Benedikt was SUCCESSFUL ["rol" as a master brewer of beer].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE is applied to expressions which indicate the prevailing physical conditions for the event, or some concurrent states of affairs.
Ex: And could anybody have SUCCEEDED ["Circumstances" under those conditions], using other methods?

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.
Ex: Kerry FAILED ["exp" because of his inability to tell his own story].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part
Ex: He was SUCCESSFUL ["con" in the Smithers v Burns case].

lexunit.name: succeed.v
lexunit.definition: COD: achieve an aim or purpose.

lexunit.name: fail.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be unsuccessful in an undertaking

lexunit.name: successful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: accomplishing an aim or purpose.

lexunit.name: pull off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: succeed in achieving or winning something difficult.

lexunit.name: unsuccessful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not successful

lexunit.name: success.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the accomplishment of an aim or purpose.

lexunit.name: manage.v
lexunit.definition: FN: succeed in attaining a goal

lexunit.name: miss.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fail to attend, watch, or participate in.

lexunit.name: failure.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an endeavor that does not succeed

lexunit.name: failing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: characteristic failure or shortcoming

frame.name: Successful_action
frame.definition:
The Means action by which a deprofiled agent (the Protagonist) has attempted to achieve a Goal is finished and the actual outcome of the Means action has been resolved, so that it either specifically matches the Protagonist's intent (e.g. _success_) or does not match it (e.g. _failure_). In an alternative construal, an Instrument stands for the Means action that the deprofiled agent undertakes in order to achieve the Goal.
Ex: ["cau" Why] ["mea" our bid] _was_ SUCCESSFUL. ["goa" DNI] Ex: ["mea" Your attempt to unsubscribe] _was_ UNSUCCESSFUL, please try again later. ["goa" DNI] Ex: Well I did end up replacing the old co axial cables with new monster ones and ["mea" it] DID THE TRICK. ["goa" DNI] Ex: ["ins" The hammer] DID IT, not a scratch or dent in the parts as they came apart ["goa" DNI]. Ex: ["Means" What] has FAILED ["Place" in Palestine], will fail in Iraq. ["Goal" DNI]

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action that the agent undertakes to achieve the Goal.
Ex: ["mea" His daring, almost reckless, move] SUCCEEDED and he lived to fight another day.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is what the agent attempts to achieve by performing the Means action.
Ex: This move SUCCEEDED ["goa" in securing trade concessions and the release of imprisoned American sailors].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the agent as part of the Means action in order to accomplish the Goal.
Ex: All of my usual source books seemed incomplete, but ["ins" your website] DID THE TRICK!

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where Means action succeeds or fails.
Ex: A similar strategy, perhaps even bloodier, DID THE TRICK ["pla" in El Salvador].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails
Ex: But it DID THE TRICK ["tim" at the time].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event or state of affairs that causes the success or failure of the Means action.
Ex: This strategy DID THE TRICK ["cau" because it demonstrated that I was keen].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the successful action expressed by the target takes place.
Ex: The installation FAILED ["cir" under FreeBSD 5.2.1.]

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The Protagonist is the deprofiled individual who makes an attempt to achieve a Goal by performing the Means action, which may involve using an Instrument.
Ex: Download also FAILED ["pro" for me] on both March and May issues.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt involving a particular Means or Instrument succeeds.
Ex: A 1000 pf cap ["Degree" almost completely] DID THE TRICK so I went bigger with what happened to be handy

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
A participant function of an Instrument or Means in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.
Ex: The machine was SUCCESSFUL ["rol" as a reconnaissance vehicle].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.
Ex: The attempt FAILED ["exp" because of John's repeated interference.].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part
Ex: This argument SUCCEEDED ["con" in Waltons-Morse v Dorrington where a non-smoking secretary claimed she was forced to work in a smoke-filled office].

lexunit.name: succeed.v
lexunit.definition: FN: achieve an agent's aim or purpose

lexunit.name: do the trick.v
lexunit.definition: COD: achieve the required result

lexunit.name: do it.v
lexunit.definition: FN: achieve the result the agent aims for

lexunit.name: successful.a
lexunit.definition: FN: accomplishing an agent's aim or purpose.

lexunit.name: come off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: succeed; be accomplished.

lexunit.name: fail.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be employed unsuccessfully in bringing off an agent's undertaking

lexunit.name: unsuccessful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not successful

lexunit.name: manage.v
lexunit.definition: COD: succeed in achieving or producing (something difficult).

lexunit.name: failed.a
lexunit.definition: FN: characterizing an action that does not succeed

lexunit.name: come off.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: succeed.

lexunit.name: go wrong.v
lexunit.definition: FN: fail.

frame.name: Detaching
frame.definition:
The Detaching frame covers two situations: a scene in which somebody causes one thing to be physically detached from something else; or a scene in which somebody causes two things to be disconnected from each other. In the first, the frame includes an Agent who detaches an Item from a Source, creating an asymmetric relationship between the Item and the Source. In the second, the Agent attaches two Items to each other, where each serves as a Source relative to the other, creating a symmetric relationship between the two Items. Note in both cases, after the removal of the connector, the Items that were formerly attached re-appear as the two separate or potentially separate entities that they were throughout.
Ex: ["Agent" They] finally UNCHAINED ["Item" me] ["Source" from my desk at work] and I'm leavin town. Ex: ["Time" Before adding a new area of color], ["Agent" he] DETACHED ["Item" the canvas] ["Source" from the stretcher] and laboriously scraped away the old paint in that spot. Ex: ["age" She] UNHOOKED ["ite" the leash] ["sou" from Patty's collar], and pulled her up on the couch.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individual that causes the Item and Source to come apart by manipulating the connector.
Ex: After a few minutes ["Agent" he] got up and UNCHAINED me from the tree.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Item that the Agent detaches from the Source.
Ex: Mercer's cell phone vibrated and he UNHITCHED ["ite" it] from his belt to flip it open.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of a detaching event.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Source identifies the location to which an Item was attached before getting detached.
Ex: Mercer's cell phone vibrated and he UNHITCHED it ["sou" from his belt] to flip it open.

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the plural Items that are detached from each other, resulting in their separation.
Ex: When, later, they UNTIED ["Items" his ankles], the ropes were left draped over the beam.
Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Source can occur.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent detaches an Item or Items.
Ex: I must have DETACHED the macro lens ["Mns" by dragging my octopus hose over the camera as I was preparing to submerge].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the detaching event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: I used a paper clip to pry it off slightly, then ["Mnr" carefully] DETACHED it with a small screwdriver.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent detaches an Item or Items.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent intentionally detaches an Item or Items.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent detaches the Item from the Source.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent detaches an Item or Items. Typically, it transmits the force applied by the Agent, and is not left behind as a participant in the resultant state.
Ex: I DETACHED it ["Ins" with my penknife].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up detached.
Ex: Trypsin DETACHED the rest of the basal lamina ["Degr" completely] from the endothelium.

lexunit.name: detach.v
lexunit.definition: COD: disengage (something) and remove it.

lexunit.name: unhitch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: unhook or unfasten.

lexunit.name: unhook.v
lexunit.definition: COD: unfasten or detach (something held by a hook).

lexunit.name: unfasten.v
lexunit.definition: COD: open the fastening of; undo.

lexunit.name: untie.v
lexunit.definition: COD: undo or unfasten (something tied)

lexunit.name: unmoor.v
lexunit.definition: COD: release the moorings of

lexunit.name: unchain.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to free by removing a chain

frame.name: Becoming_detached
frame.definition: The Becoming_detached frame covers two situations: a scene in which one thing comes to be physically detached from something else; or a scene in which two things come to be disconnected from each other. In the first, the frame includes an Item that detaches from a Source, creating an asymmetric relationship between the Item and the Source. In the second, the Items detach from each other, where each serves as a Source relative to the other, creating a symmetric relationship between the two Items. The Items that were formerly attached re-appear as the two separate or potentially separate entities that they were throughout.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Item that detaches from the Source.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source identifies the location to which an Item was attached before getting detached.

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the plural Items that are becoming detached from each other, resulting in their separation.
Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Source can occur.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the detaching event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Item becomes detached.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Item becomes detached from the Source.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up detached.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

lexunit.name: detach.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to stop being attached.

lexunit.name: decouple.v
lexunit.definition: FN: separate or disengage from something.

lexunit.name: unhook.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come apart from something after being connected via a hook.

lexunit.name: unhinge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: detach a door or other hinged item

frame.name: Regard
frame.definition:
A Cognizer has a Judgment of an Evaluee, expressing how high or low their regard for the Evaluee is.
Ex: ["jud" What] do ["cog" you] THINK ["eva" of him] ["rol" as a linguist]? Ex: ["cog" She] ["man" secretly] THOUGHT ["jud" well] ["eva" of him] ["rea" for his role in defrocking Mr. Matthews]. Ex: Please understand, ["cog" I] _hold_ ["eva" you] _in_ the ["jud" highest] REGARD. Ex: ["cog" My] ["jud" low] OPINION ["eva" of him] was of long standing.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the one that makes a Judgment. This role is typically expressed as the External Argument (or in a _by_-PP in passives).
Ex: ["Cognizer" The boss] APPRECIATES you for your diligence. Ex: ["Cognizer" The boss] is very APPRECIATIVE of my work.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: Evaluee is the person or thing that a judgment is made with respect to. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object: Ex: He REGARDED ["eva" her] poorly.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
There may be a constituent expressing the Reason for the Cognizer's judgment. It is usually a _for_-PP.
Ex: I THINK highly of you ["Reason" for your honesty].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role is used for the capacity in which theEvaluee is judged, and is expressed in _as_-PPs.
Ex: My high REGARD for you ["rol" as a composer] is due strictly to political concerns.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive identifies any expression describing the state of a participant in the event.
Ex: We hold him in low ESTEEM, ["dep" certain that he will never redeem himself].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Cognizer's judgment which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions of events (_the same way, presumptuously, secretly_).

fe.name: Extent_of_acclaim
fe.definition:
The Extent_of_acclaim is a description of the number or locales of the Cognizers.
Ex: He is ["ext" widely] held in high REGARD.

fe.name: Judgment
fe.definition:
A description (from the point of view of the Cognizer) of the position of the Evaluee on a scale of approval.
Ex: I hold him in the ["jud" highest] ESTEEM.

lexunit.name: regard.n
lexunit.definition: FN: esteem

lexunit.name: esteem.n
lexunit.definition: FN: level of respect

lexunit.name: regard.v
lexunit.definition: FN: hold in a specified level of esteem

lexunit.name: impression.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a level of esteem

lexunit.name: opinion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an estimation of quality or worth

lexunit.name: think.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have a particular opinion, belief, or idea about someone or something.

lexunit.name: appreciate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: recognize the value or significance of.

lexunit.name: appreciative.a
lexunit.definition: COD: feeling or showing gratitude or pleasure.

frame.name: Being_detached
frame.definition:
An Item is detached from a Source, or Items are detached from each other.
Ex: When ["itm" the snow plow] is DISCONNECTED ["src" from the vehicle], extend the lift cylinder to the end of its stroke and coat the chrome rod with a light grease.
Ex: ["itm" The gold leaves that] are UNATTACHED ["src" to the engraved surfaces] fall off. Ex: By 5:00 to 5:30 (depending on the time of year) ["itm" the boat] is UNMOORED and loaded.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
Item identifies the entity that is detached from a Source.
Ex: I feel like ["itm" my head] is DETACHED from the rest of my body.

fe.name: Items
fe.definition:
Items identifies the plural items that are detached from each other.
Ex: ["Items" The neck vertebrae] are UNFUSED in rorquals and gray whales, which allows for some flexibility at the head and neck.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Source identifies the location from which the Item(s) is detached.
Ex: The toilet is LOOSE ["src" from the floor] and must be repaired.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item is in an detached state relative to a Source, or two Items are detached from each other.

lexunit.name: detached.a
lexunit.definition: COD: separate or disconnected.

lexunit.name: disconnected.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not having a connection to

lexunit.name: loose.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not bound or tethered.

lexunit.name: unfused.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not fused to something

lexunit.name: unmoored.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of a boat) not attached by cable or rope to the shore or to an anchor

lexunit.name: unattached.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not attached.

frame.name: Opinion
frame.definition:
A Cognizer holds a particular Opinion, which may be portrayed as being about a particular Topic.
Ex: ["cog" John] THINKS ["opi" that it looks better back] . Ex: Well, ["cog" my] ["opi" OPINION] ["top" about that] is none of your business.
Ex: ["opi" What] _'s_ ["cog" your] TAKE ["top" on the recent oil crisis] ?
Ex: ["cog" Your] VIEW ["top" of Smithers] ["opi" as an excellent secretary] is not shared by the rest of the UN.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the person whose Opinion is in question.
Ex: ["cog" My] TAKE is that Johnson will not actually make it to the last round . Ex: Everyone is entitled to ["cog" their] OPINION .

fe.name: Opinion
fe.definition:
The Cognizer's way of thinking, which is not necessarily generally accepted, and which is generally dependent on the Cognizer's point of view.
Ex: My TAKE is ["opi" that it is a version of the Macbeth story - what happens when people become violent but cannot quite handle it]. Ex: Svetlana knew that it was Sergei's VIEW ["opi" that the Berlin crises were merely a charade which it was necessary for both sides to enact and re-enact every few years]. Ex: Her child-like portrayal only manages to live up to the other characters' VIEW of her ["opi" as the deranged little sister].

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
The events or states-of-affairs that form the basis for the Cognizer's Opinion.
Ex: ["evi" From what I've seen so far], my OPINION is that it won't really matter.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
A phenomenon that the Cognizer is considering with respect to their Opinion. Note that this extra-thematic frame element occurs freely with nouns, but only in very restricted contexts with verbs.
Ex: My OPINION ["top" about that Tigers' win] is that it was completely bogus.

fe.name: Constancy
fe.definition:
The level of firmness with which the Cognizer holds an opinion. It refers to the amount of convincing that they would need to change their mind.
Ex: I ["con" really] THINK that you should reconsider.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of how the Cognizer holds an opinion which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quiet(ly)_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect their thinking (_presumptuous(ly), cold(ly)_).
Ex: She ["man" quietly] held the BELIEF that it was he that had betrayed the rebellion.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role describes the presuppositional terms of the Opinion by placing the Topic or the Cognizer of the Opinion into a category.
Ex: My OPINION of her ["Role" as a brother] isn't important anymore. Ex: Your TAKE on it ["Role" as a political event] is not in question at this time.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The aspects of the Opinion (and its Topic, if any) which are under consideration.
Ex: We seemed to have two quite different ["dom" moral] VIEWS about this situation. Ex: Noone could take seriously Dr. Furst's ill-advised ["dom" medical] OPINION that Terry was still alive.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Cognizer has the Opinion.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: opinion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a view or judgement not necessarily based on fact or knowledge.

lexunit.name: view.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular way of regarding something; an attitude or opinion.

lexunit.name: take.n
lexunit.definition: FN: way of considering (s.t.)

lexunit.name: think.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have a particular opinion, belief, or idea about someone or something.

lexunit.name: belief.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an acceptance that something exists or is true, especially one without proof.

lexunit.name: expect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: suppose or assume

lexunit.name: feel.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have a belief or impression, especially without an identifiable reason.

lexunit.name: figure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: think; consider.

lexunit.name: have feeling.v
lexunit.definition: FN: sense or believe

lexunit.name: hunch.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a feeling or guess based on intuition.

lexunit.name: suppose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: think or assume that something is true or probable, but without proof.

lexunit.name: believe.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have an opinion about a topic

frame.name: Resurrection
frame.definition:
A Protagonist which had been dead returns to life.
Ex: ["pro" He]'ll COME BACK ["pri" from the dead] ["tim" at 11:03PM exactly], ["rea" since that's what his suicide note indicated].

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The being or entity that becomes living again.
Ex: If ["pro" the Lord] RESURRECTED in three days, surely he could relieve my back pain in, say, a week.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the resurrection occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: An explanation of how the state-of-affairs came to pass.

fe.name: Prior_state
fe.definition:
The state of the Protagonist before resurrection.
Ex: If he COMES BACK ["pri" from the dead], we'll need this spell to ward him off.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
The state of the Protagonist which results from resurrection.
Ex: I just hope he doesn't COME BACK ["res" to life] again.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Protagonist during the resurrection.
Ex: The trouble is they always COME BACK to life ["dep" angry].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Protagonist returns from the dead.

lexunit.name: resurrect.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come back to life.

lexunit.name: come_back.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to become alive again

lexunit.name: rise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be restored to life.

lexunit.name: resurrection.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of resurrecting

lexunit.name: return.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come back to life

frame.name: Getting_up
frame.definition:
A Protagonist leaves the place where they have slept, their Bed, to begin or resume domestic, professional, or other activities. Getting up is distinct from Waking up, which is concerned only with the transition from the sleeping state to a wakeful state.
Ex: ["pro" I] ROSE ["bed" from bed], threw on a pair of camouflage shorts and drove my little Toyota Corolla to a construction clearing a few miles away. Ex: One recent Monday, for example, ["pro" Joe] ROSE ["bed" from bed] ["tim" extra early] ["pur" to catch an administrator at 8:30 am].
Ex: ["cir" In the summer] ["pro" I] GET UP ["tim" early] and get some miles in on my bike before the kids and Ange wake up. ["bed" INI]
Ex: He slept or threw up the whole day. ["pro" He] GOT UP ["dur" for 2 hours] ["tim" in the evening]. ["bed" INI]
Ex: ["cir" When it snowed] ["pro" Smithers] GOT UP ["tim" before everyone else] ["tim" at two o'clock] and swept the walkways. ["bed" INI]

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The person or animal that has slept in a particular place and now leaves it to engage in other activities.
Ex: ["pro" Melony] GOT UP from bed and changed clothes getting ready to go to the doctor.

fe.name: Bed
fe.definition:
The place where the Protagonist has slept.
Ex: She GOT UP ["bed" from bed] lazily and stretched her body and yawned.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Protagonist leaves their place of sleeping.
Ex: We GOT UP ["tim" at 6:30 in the morning].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which the Protagonist gets out of Bed.
Ex: I ROSE from bed ["pur" to rectify the situation].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_), secondary effects (_quietly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that affect the action (_eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: I ROSE from bed ["Manner" with urgency] early one morning because a light clicked on.

fe.name: World_state
fe.definition:
The World_state is the situation the Protagonist finds him or herself in upon getting up from Bed.
Ex: Hannibal admitted defeat at around 5 am and ROSE ["wor" to find Face and Ray already up making coffee].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the getting up event takes place.
Ex: ["cir" During spring break], we GOT UP at 7:45 and waited for the donut truck.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that the Protagonist is responding to in getting up.
Ex: I GET UP ["rea" because I have things I can't wait to do].

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
The length of the interval for which the Protagonist is not in Bed after getting up.
Ex: I was so tired yesterday that I went home and slept 3 hrs, GOT UP ["dur" for 2 hrs], then back to bed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Protagonist's Bed is situated.
Ex: We eventually ended up getting home about 5am and I ended up sleeping all day. ["pro" I] GOT UP ["tim" late] ["pla" at home], went to Steve's and slept at his house. ["bed" INI]

lexunit.name: rise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: get up from bed after sleeping

lexunit.name: get up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: rise from bed after sleeping

frame.name: Dough_rising
frame.definition:
The LUs of this frame describe a lump of Dough expanding as gas develops inside it. This is part of a process where, in order to produce a lighter, more easily chewed bread, Dough is leavened with yeast, baking soda or in another fashion to add gas to it before baking.
Ex: I've got no frozen boxed meals, and no other real options to make something to keep me going while ["dou" my pizza dough] RISES.

fe.name: Dough
fe.definition:
The paste made out of any cereals (grains) or leguminous crops by grinding, with some water added, which expands in volume as a result of leavening before baking.
Ex: While ["dou" the dough] was RISING, they heated the oven.

fe.name: Duration_of_activity
fe.definition:
The length of the interval during which the Dough rises.
Ex: The dough ROSE ["dur" for about 2 hours].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the expansion of the Dough takes place.
Ex: The dough ROSE beautifully ["tim" before it went into the fridge] but afterwards it never really recovered.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed at which the Dough expands.
Ex: The bread dough ROSE ["spe" quickly].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the rising of the Dough which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).
Ex: My dough ROSE ["man" nicely].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
A setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the event takes place. This FE also covers conditions that are causally connected to the event of the Dough rising.
Ex: The dough RISES higher ["cir" if made by the bread machine than made by a standard mixer].

fe.name: Size_change
fe.definition:
The amount by which the volume of the Dough increases.
Ex: While in the refrigerator, the dough ROSE ["siz" by about 25%].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The entity or state of affairs that leads to the event of the Dough's rising.
Ex: A slimmer approach relies on the bubbles of carbon dioxide created as the dough RISES ["cau" from the yeast].

lexunit.name: rise.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to puff up as a result of leavening

lexunit.name: prove.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of bread dough) become aerated by the action of yeast; rise

frame.name: Sidereal_appearance
frame.definition:
An Astronomical_entity comes into view above the horizon as part of a regular, periodic process of (apparent) motion of the Astronomical_entity across the sky. In the case of the sun, the appearance begins the day.
Ex: ["ast" Venus] ROSE ["tim" at 5:23 AM], twenty minutes before the sun which reached the horizon at 5:43 AM.
Ex: At the time of the new moon, ["ast" the moon] RISES ["tim" at about the same time the sun rises], and it sets at about the same time the sun sets.
Ex: And, as ["ast" the sun] CAME UP ["goa" over the trees], it became golden, and then turned again into a silvery path; and the water came alive
Ex: Each day ["ast" the sun's] RISE offers us a new day.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Astronomical_entity during the motion.
Ex: That morning the sun ROSE ["dep" blood red] in the east.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is the location above the horizon that the Astronomical_entity ends up in.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which the motion of the Astronomical_entity takes place. It covers any description of the appearance which is not covered by more specific FEs such as Speed, including general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_), and aesthetic judgements of the event .
Ex: The sun ROSE ["man" beautifully], but the air was cold.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The sequence of locations that the Astronomical_entity traverses as it comes over the horizon.
Ex: A pale copper sun ROSE ["pat" through a sea of muted cloud layers], and now there is no afterglow at all.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Speed at which the Astronomical_entity comes into view.
Ex: In the summer, the sun COMES UP ["spe" quickly], and you?ll need to work fast.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Astronomical_entity appears.
Ex: As the sun CAME UP ["tim" at 5:15 am], it made the red rocks almost glow.

fe.name: Astronomical_entity
fe.definition:
An entity which is periodically visible from the earth's surface.
Ex: Heku left one morning as ["ast" the sun] ROSE along the plain.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the location the Astronomical_entity is construed to occupy before coming above the horizon.
Ex: The night passed away, and the sun ROSE ["Src" from the ocean].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Result of the Astronomical_entity's motion.
Ex: As we continued moving east, the sun ROSE ["Result" high].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place from which the motion of the Astronomical_entity is viewed.
Ex: The very end of the eclipse will be visible as the sun RISES ["pla" in some locations in Africa and northeastern North America].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Astronomical_entity comes into view above the horizon.
Ex: When the sun ROSE ["deg" fully], painting the area a beautiful red gold his father would turn to him and smile.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
A setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the appearance of the Astronomical_entity takes place
Ex: The Sun ROSE ["cir" with just a few clouds along the eastern horizon] as we eagerly unpacked our gear.

fe.name: Correlated_event
fe.definition:
An event that takes place simultaneously with the Astronomical_entity's appearance.
Ex: The moon ROSE ["cor" with the early onset of dusk].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: FN: The amount of times the Astronomical_entity appears per unit of time.

lexunit.name: rise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of the sun, moon, or stars) appear above the horizon.

lexunit.name: come up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (for the sun, moon, or stars) to appear above the horizon

lexunit.name: rise.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the ascent of an astronomical entity above the horizon

frame.name: Being_up_to_it
frame.definition: An Entity meets the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity that is judged to be difficult for it to participate in, either due to inherent properties of the Entity or temporary Circumstances. A Degree modifier may indicate by how much the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.
Ex: ["Entity" Little Tommy] was not UP TO getting out of bed.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The Activity that the Entity may participate in.
Ex: He was a very meek and shy person, and always felt that he was not EQUAL ["act" to the task set before him].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Activity.
Ex: Blind parents are ["Deg" very much] UP TO driving their kids to soccer practice.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.
Ex: Bill was not equal to the task ["cir" with the distraction of the alien landing].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity.
Ex: ["Cause" Because of his mother's death], Smithers was not UP TO taking the final exam.

fe.name: Relevant_feature
fe.definition:
A characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Activity.
Ex: The robot is UP TO the task ["rel" in intelligence] but completely socially inept.

lexunit.name: sufficient.a
lexunit.definition: FN: qualified or competent to deal with a challenge

lexunit.name: up to.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: capable of undertaking a specified difficult activity

lexunit.name: equal.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having the ability or resources to meet a challenge

frame.name: Rising_to_a_challenge
frame.definition:
A Protagonist, by exerting great effort, comes to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity that is judged to be difficult for them to participate in, either due to their inherent properties or due to temporary Circumstances.
Ex: In conclusion, ["pro" our staff] ROSE ["act" to the challenge] ["mea" in developing the necessary training programs and delivery methods].
Ex: ["pro" Dr Runcie] ROSE TO THE OCCASION ["mea" with a simple address]. ["act" DNI]
Ex: There was still clearly much to do, but ["pro" the governor and his staff] had begun to RISE ["act" to the task].
Ex: Pacers say ["pro" they]'ll RISE ["act" to the pressure].

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The Protagonist who is exerting effort to meet the pre-conditions for participating in the Activity.
Ex: How ["pro" a small hospital] ROSE to the challenge of a legionella outbreak.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The Activity that the Protagonist expends efforts towards.
Ex: She ROSE TO THE OCCASION ["act" of bringing up her children single-handed even as a woman who was not educated except a few years in Primary school].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Protagonist exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Activity as a result of expending effort to get themselves ready.
Ex: I'm used to second books not living up the promise of the first, but Nero Blanc ["deg" fully] ROSE to the challenge.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the Protagonist exerts effort to meet the pre-conditions necessary for engaging in the Activity.
Ex: I recalled how she ROSE TO THE OCCASION ["cir" in mishaps, avalanches, oxygen shortage, lack of food, loss of comrades].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An entity, event, or state of affairs that causes the Protagonist to expend the effort necessary to meet the pre-conditions for participating in the Activity.
Ex: The installation was anything but a routine project from the beginning and everyone involved ROSE to the challenge ["cau" because it was gratifying to be contributing in some way to the tsunami relief effort].

fe.name: Relevant_feature
fe.definition:
A characteristic or behavior of the Protagonist that is considered when judging whether the Protagonist might participate in the Activity.
Ex: You are able to adapt quickly to important shifts in the world around you, and RISE to the challenge ["rel" where career is concerned].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Protagonist which enables them to overcome the difficulties and engage in the Activity.
Ex: Learn how one small shop ROSE to the challenge ["mea" through the use of gift tables].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Protagonist through expenditure of effort becomes capable of engaging in the Activity.
Ex: A president for whom the jury was still out for many Americans first appeared shaken, but ["tim" then] ROSE to the crisis.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Protagonist expends effort to become capable of engaging in the Activity.
Ex: Students from a number of Metropolitan schools ROSE to the challenge ["pla" at DMIT's Panorama Campus] on Friday 22nd August and spent the day participating in an annual 'Taste of Engineering' activity.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_), general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (_eagerly_).
Ex: Despite all odds the brave Macedonian people heroically ROSE to the task ["man" with valour].

lexunit.name: rise.v
lexunit.definition: COD: respond adequately to (a challenging situation).

lexunit.name: rise to the occasion.v
lexunit.definition: FN: respond adequately to a difficult situation

frame.name: Prominence
frame.definition:
An Entity stands out perceptually in comparison to other members of its type.
Ex: ["Entity" Pilot Mountain in NC] _is_ ["Degree" very] PROMINENT.
Ex: First, from the Saturday images, the most PROMINENT ["Entity" feature] is a sharp spike emerging from the tailward side of the nucleus.
Ex: I was left with a deep and CONSPICUOUS ["Entity" scar] (about 10cm long) which felt uncomfortably tight and itchy.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity for which the saliency Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.
Ex: If you are asked to search for the plus sign with red-vertical and green-horizontal elements, ["Entity" all the red and green plus signs] may seem to _become_ SALIENT.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The feature of the Entity which is under discussion, namely perceptual salience.
Ex: The diagram, (a frequency distribution chart) shows a ["att" prominently] CONSPICUOUS region of stars that extend from the extremely bright and hot stars to the faint and cool variety.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of the prominence from the norm or from the value for another Entity.
Ex: The gobies (the family Gobiidae) are not a ["Degree" very] CONSPICUOUS part of the fish fauna in most of. the Mekong Basin.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular salience.
Ex: The affection for American culture seemed more PROMINENT ["tim" last year].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular degree of prominence.
Ex: Europa is also PROMINENT ["cir" at a distance of 25000 km] and Io is visible in the distance.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE refers to the location where the Entity has a prominence of some Attribute.

lexunit.name: salient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: most noticeable or important

lexunit.name: prominent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: particularly noticeable.

lexunit.name: conspicuous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: attracting notice or attention

lexunit.name: eye-catching.a
lexunit.definition: COD: immediately appealing or noticeable.

lexunit.name: flashy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: ostentatiously stylish.

lexunit.name: blatant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: open and unashamed; flagrant.

lexunit.name: quiet.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not flashy, noticeable, or eventful.

frame.name: Within_distance
frame.definition:
As is usual for locative relations, the location of the Figure is specified as being inside a region defined relative to the Ground. In this case, the region measures outward from the Ground with a width specified by the Distance.
Ex: The number of ["fig" large galaxies] WITHIN ["dis" 5 million light years] is three. ["gro" DNI] Ex: ["fig" What] _'s_ WITHIN ["dis" 100 miles] ["gro" of you] ? Ex: ["fig" Two of Russia's long-range bombers] flew around Iceland last Friday -- _coming_ WITHIN ["dis" striking distance] ["gro" of the United States] for the first time in five or six years .

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure, as inside a region measured outward from the Ground and of a width specified by Distance.
Ex: Our galaxy is just one of thousands that lie within 100 million light years. ["gro" DNI] Ex: We allow no civilians WITHIN 50 feet ["gro" of these aircraft].

fe.name: Figure
fe.definition:
The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location.
Ex: ["fig" I] am WITHIN spitting distance of one of the finest farmer's markets in the area.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Distance between the Ground and the borders of the region within which the Figure is located.
Ex: The childhood leukaemia risk is doubled for children living within ["dis" 100 metres] of high voltage.

lexunit.name: within.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: not further off than (a particular distance).

frame.name: Explaining_the_facts
frame.definition:
A Question about the reason or cause of a known State_of_affairs is presented as being answered by the existence of a particular Fact. The exact chain of reasoning, including the answer itself, of which the Fact is a part is not specified.
Contrast this frame with the Evidence frame which casts a Support (a fact) as providing Evidence for, or conclusively proving, the Proposition (another proposed fact). Thus, there is no open question in the Evidence frame.
Ex: ["fac" Ruby's orange vest marked with the words "service dog"] ACCOUNTS ["que" for why the 3-year-old goes along].
Ex: ["fac" The nation's history] EXPLAINS ["que" why the current conflict succumbs to, and yet simultaneously transcends, the stereotype].
Ex: Then ["sta" that I exist] is EXPLAINED ["fac" by A and B having come together].
Ex: ["fac" Lack of potential for improvement in the immediate future] ACCOUNTS ["sta" for the low number of returnees into South Ossetia, even for the Ossetian ethnic group].
Ex: ["fac" That] EXPLAINS ["sta" it].
Ex: ["mea" Somehow] ["fac" this] EXPLAINS ["que" why Apple is always the last man to get the technology].

fe.name: Fact
fe.definition:
A fact which can be connected by a chain of reasoning to the State_of_affairs.
Ex: ["fac" This fact] alone EXPLAINS the Sun/climate anomaly.

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
A fact whose cause is under consideration.
Ex: Do increased proinsulin concentrations EXPLAIN ["sta" the excess risk of coronary heart disease in diabetic and prediabetic subjects]?

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies how much of the State_of_affairs is explained by the Fact.
Ex: This, in my opinion, ["deg" partially] ACCOUNTS for why Anakin became a ghost.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE indicates salient characteristics of the Fact considered as an explanation.
Ex: Current life-history theory would ["man" readily] EXPLAIN the small males in B if juvenile male mortality were higher than that of females , but adult mortality should not affect the timing of maturity or adult size .

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intermediate logical step that justifies the relationship between the Fact and the State_of_affairs.
Ex: This gives an EXPLANATION for the observation ["mea" by identifying it as an instance of general pattern]

fe.name: Point_of_view
fe.definition:
The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Fact an explanation for the State_of_affairs.
Ex: ["poi" To her], this EXPLAINS things, and we therefore need not discuss it any longer.

fe.name: Question
fe.definition:
An open proposition concerning the cause of the State_of_affairs.
Ex: The fact that this remained in Pandora's box EXPLAINS ["que" why men have hope].
Ex:

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: The state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the Concessive.

lexunit.name: explain.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make the existence of a state of affairs plain or understandable

lexunit.name: account.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a satisfactory record or explanation of.

lexunit.name: explanation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a fact that makes a state of affairs understandable

frame.name: Temporal_subregion
frame.definition:
A Sub_part of a Time_period is picked out. In some cases, the part (as opposed to the entire Time_period) may be described by a Sub_part_property. The Time_period may be indicated by an event which takes place during the Time_period.
Ex: I nearly kicked my TV this afternoon after watching the ["subpp" shambolic] ["subpar" END] ["tim" of the Austrian Grand-Prix] . Ex: Jack Yan looks at how the branding profession will be affected in the ["subpar" EARLY] ["tim" 2000s] by globalization .

fe.name: Sub_part
fe.definition:
The part of the Time_period which is profiled.
Ex: The findings mark the ["subpar" BEGINNING] of a new age of planetary science, in which "extrasolar" planets can be directly measured and compared.

fe.name: Sub_part_property
fe.definition:
Some description which pertains specifically to the Sub_part (rather than the Time_period.
