Ex: Indeed, the ["subpp" sorry] END of the HCI period, with Korea in recession and. in the throes of rampant political turmoil, has led some analysts to conclude that the prior period had been underlyingly unstable despite its appearance of promise.

fe.name: Time_period
fe.definition:
A temporal span conceived of as a whole.
Ex: A zillion copies and clones have been made of this Russian game since it first was released in the mid ["tim" 80's].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time that is being referred to.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: late.a
lexunit.definition: COD: belonging or taking place far on in a particular time or period.

lexunit.name: later.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the late part (as opposed to some other mentioned part of the period)

lexunit.name: middle.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a middle point or position.

lexunit.name: middle.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of a larger time period) denoting a part contrasted with the earlier and later parts.

lexunit.name: early.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of, at, or near the beginning of a particular time, period, or sequence.

lexunit.name: earlier.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the early part (as opposed to some other mentioned part of the period)

lexunit.name: mid.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of a larger time period) denoting a part that contrasts with the earlier and later parts.

lexunit.name: end.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a final part of something.

lexunit.name: beginning.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the first part of something.

lexunit.name: outset.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the start or beginning.

lexunit.name: start.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the beginning.

lexunit.name: dawning.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the beginning or first appearance of something.

lexunit.name: turn.n
lexunit.definition: FN: point at which one century ends and the next century begins.

frame.name: Seeking_to_achieve
frame.definition:
An Agent intends and takes steps towards bringing about a State_of_affairs or, metonymically, towards acquiring a Sought_entity .
Ex: ["age" Libya] SOUGHT ["sou" nuclear weapons] ["Time" in the 1960s].
Ex: ["age" North Korea] SOUGHT ["sou" several billion dollars in cash from the US] ["Time" during bilateral missile talks].
Ex: The talks in Berlin ended without agreement after ["age" Bora Bora] SOUGHT ["soa" to link large-scale economic assistance to joint recovery operations].
Ex: ["Agent" India] had SOUGHT ["soa" her extradition] ["exp" for forging documents to procure a passport].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a State_of_affairs or to obtain a Sought_entity.
Ex: ["age" Those states] SOUGHT a remedy that would substantially change the company's business practices.

fe.name: Sought_entity
fe.definition:
The entity that the Agent attempts to acquire.
Ex: Or the monstrous Saddam, who filled mass graves to bursting, invaded two neighboring countries, and avidly SOUGHT ["sou" weapons of mass destruction].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition:
The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to acquire a Sought_entity.
Ex: WWDA also ["out" successfully] SOUGHT funding from Office of the Status of Women

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt at achieving a State_of_affairs or at acquiring the Sought_entity is made.
Ex: Agassi SOUGHT relief ["Means" by taking Advil].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the amount of effort put into an attempt.
Ex: He also SOUGHT ["Degr" intensely] to know more of Christ.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where the Agent is seeking to achieve a particular State_of_affairs or to acquire a Sought_entity.
Ex: The disclosure came as prosecutors successfully SOUGHT ["Place" in federal court] to keep Luise Garofalo behind bars.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent makes the attempt.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The time period over which the attempts at achieving a State_of_affairs or acquiring the Sought_entity take place.
Ex: Finally the peace I've SOUGHT ["Duration" for years]!

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by bringing about a particular State_of_affairs or acquiring the Sought_entity.

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
A state or event that the Agent wants to bring about. The Agent may but need not be a participant in that State_of_affairs.
Ex: His enemies SOUGHT ["soa" his destruction].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A proposition from which the occurrence of the seeking event follows.
Ex: About 6% of all abortions are SOUGHT ["exp" because either the woman or fetus has medical reasons].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
An individual or organization that helps the Agent bring about the State_of_affairs or delivers the Sought_entity to the Agent.
Ex: He has lain that way ever since and has given power to all who SOUGHT it ["src" from him].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE introduces the underlying situation(s) in which seeking occurs.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition:
This FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the Sought_entity or State_of_affairs .
Ex: Jed SOUGHT the world's largest diamond ["Beneficiary" for his Jeda] .

lexunit.name: seek.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take steps towards obtaining an entity or bringing about a state of affairs

lexunit.name: pursue.v
lexunit.definition: COD: seek to attain (a goal).

lexunit.name: pursuit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of pursuing.

frame.name: Infrastructure
frame.definition:
A group of entities exist (as an infrastructure) such that a particular type of Activity is either enabled or facilitated. The entities may or may not have been organized specifically for the Activity. The infrastructure is constituted by Resources that can be made use of by Users, and the infrastructure may be specified for its Place or Possessor.
Ex: While the ["Possessor" US] ["Activity" transportation] ["Infrastructure" INFRASTRUCTURE] continues to crumble, competitors in Brazil and Argentina are investing millions to improve their transportation
Ex: The exacerbated sprawl like growth in the last decades has been a direct result of decisions taken in the creation, boost, and development of ["Resource" highway] ["Infrastructure" INFRASTRUCTURE].
Ex: Mexico's Ministry of Tourism expects to see more than $1.78 billion invested to further develop ["Possessor" the country's] ["Activity" tourism] ["Infrastructure" INFRASTRUCTURE].

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The Activity which is enabled or facilitated by the infrastructure.
Ex: At present, you'll find that Belize has a ["act" travel] INFRASTRUCTURE that's improving but still far from polished. Ex: As a result , one of the central policy priorities of government has been to strengthen significantly the ["act" academic] INFRASTRUCTURE.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location of the infrastructure.
Ex: Much of the transportation INFRASTRUCTURE ["Place" in the US] was developed when there was no need for private money.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
The organization, institution, or individual who owns the infrastructure.
Ex: Increase the value of ["pos" your company's] technology INFRASTRUCTURE

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition:
The infrastructure may be conceived of as consisting of Resources that can be made use of by Users in performing an Activity.
Ex: Members of the organization can use the ["res" service] INFRASTRUCTURE to perform management tasks. Ex: It is critical to point out that, while our ["res" highway] INFRASTRUCTURE continues to deteriorate, highway use is on the rise.

fe.name: User
fe.definition:
The people for whom the infrastructure is designed to be used by. In the cases where the constituent denoting the user also evokes the Activity, we annotate this on the second FE layer.
Ex: There are no specific barriers to investment in Bulgaria's ["user" tourist] INFRASTRUCTURE or in the import of products to be used for tourist infrastructure development. Ex: There are no specific barriers to investment in Bulgaria's ["act" tourist] INFRASTRUCTURE or in the import of products to be used for tourist infrastructure development. Ex: Our company makes constant use of the vast INFRASTRUCTURE ["user" for businesses] offered by the government.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characterization of the infrastructure.

fe.name: Infrastructure
fe.definition: The collection of entities and/or institutions that help to promote an Activity of a public character.

lexunit.name: infrastructure.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the basic facilities, installations, or other components needed for the operation of a system or organization

lexunit.name: base.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a system that allows for a particular activity to take place.

frame.name: Amassing
frame.definition:
A Recipient (who may or may not be agentive) ends up in possession of a Mass_theme (which may be conceptualized as a single mass entity, or may be a group of individual entities). Some lexical units (e.g. STOCKPILE) specifically indicate an intentional Recipient.
This frame differs from Gathering_up in that this frame refers specifically to the acquisition and (according to expectation) long-term possession of entities, rather than (as in the Gathering_up frame) simply talking about causing a group of entities to be located in the same place. In sum, Gathering_up concerns (co-)locations, but Amassing concerns possession.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Mass_theme.

fe.name: Mass_theme
fe.definition: The collection of objects that ends up in the Recipient's possession.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Source is the location that the Mass_theme formerly occupied. Persons that begin in possession of the Mass_theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place denotes where the Mass_theme is acquired.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional amassment is performed.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is the action of the Recipient which results in their possession of the Mass_theme.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the Amassing which is not covered by more specific FEs. It includes such specifications as comparisons to other events (_similarly_), rates of acquisition (_slowly_), and descriptions of the Recipient which also influence the action (_eagerly_).
Ex: If you press the show duplicates button, then all the redundant bookmarks that you have ["man" haphazardly] ACCUMULATED will be neatly displayed in alphabetical order .

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state that either the Recipient or the Mass_theme end up in after the acquisition.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE describes the length of time over which amassing occurs.
Ex: Bogs ACCUMULATE carbon ["Dur" for thousands of years] .

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which amassing occurs.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role is used for the capacity in which the Recipient amasses stuff, and is expressed in _as_-PPs.
Ex: By the time I was 16 , I was winning major contests , AMASSING a few quid in the bank ["Rol" as a part-time model] and walking as though I had a brush handle up my arse .

lexunit.name: amass.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accumulate over time.

lexunit.name: accumulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: gather together a number or quantity of.

lexunit.name: stockpile.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accumulate a large stock of.

frame.name: Foreign_or_domestic_country
frame.definition:
A Current_country is identified as matching or not matching the instance of the Discourse_salient_country.
Ex: ["cur" FOREIGN] sales account for only 20% of IBM's income .

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up the Current_country.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The location that the Current_country is a part of.

fe.name: Current_country
fe.definition:
The country or countries that the speaker is indicating in the current instance, which may match or be distinct from the Discourse_salient_country.
Ex: AutoPartsPlace.com offers discount prices on millions of import auto parts, ["cur" DOMESTIC] car parts, and car accessories.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases). This FE is used for the Names of Locales.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition: A place that the Current_country is located with respect to.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Current_country which is not covered by more specific FEs.

fe.name: Population
fe.definition: The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale.

fe.name: Discourse_salient_country
fe.definition: The country that has been featured in the discourse, or that the speaker/hearer identify with or are located in; it serves to identify the Current_country by specifying it as the same or different. This FE is incorporated in the targets of this frame.

lexunit.name: foreign.a
lexunit.definition: COD: dealing with or relating to other countries.

lexunit.name: domestic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: existing or occurring within a country.

lexunit.name: international.a
lexunit.definition: FN: of multiple nations, especially excluding the current one.

lexunit.name: home.n
lexunit.definition: FN: one's own nation.

lexunit.name: homeland.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's native land.

frame.name: Relational_natural_features
frame.definition: The Focal_feature is defined in relation to a Landmark_feature, either as a particular part, or as an immediately bordering entity.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: Salient parts of the Focal_feature.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The location that the Focal_feature is a part of.

fe.name: Formational_cause
fe.definition: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Focal_feature about.

fe.name: Focal_feature
fe.definition: A stable bounded area defined by its relation to another landform.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: This FE is used for the Names of Focal_features.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition: A place that a Focal_feature is located with respect to.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: The Type is the subtype of natural feature.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Focal_feature which is not covered by more specific FEs.

fe.name: Landmark_feature
fe.definition: The landform with respect to which the Focal_feature is defined.

lexunit.name: shore.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the land along the edge of a sea, lake, etc

lexunit.name: coast.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the part of the land adjoining or near the sea.

lexunit.name: delta.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a triangular tract of sediment deposited at the mouth of a river, typically where it diverges into several outlets

lexunit.name: bank.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the land alongside or sloping down to a river or lake.

lexunit.name: seaboard.n
lexunit.definition: FN: land near the sea

lexunit.name: mouth.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the place where a river enters the sea.

lexunit.name: source.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a spring or fountain head from which a river or stream issues

lexunit.name: summit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the highest point of a hill or mountain.

lexunit.name: peak.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the pointed top of a mountain

lexunit.name: foothill.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a low hill at the base of a mountain or mountain range

lexunit.name: estuary.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the tidal mouth of a large river.

lexunit.name: shoreline.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The place where the shore of a body of water and a landmass meet.

frame.name: Have_as_requirement
frame.definition:
The obtaining of a Requirement state of affairs or the presence of a Required_entity is profiled as a prerequisite for the obtaining or occurring of a Dependent state-of-affairs.
Ex: ["Dependent" This game] DEMANDS ["Requirement" great skill].
Ex: ["Dependent" The war on terror] REQUIRES ["Requirement" little sacrifice for most Americans].
Ex: ["Dependent" Glass art] DEMANDS ["Requirement" great patience] ["Required_individual" from the student].

fe.name: Dependent
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the state of affairs of the Requirement or the presence of the Required_entity.

fe.name: Requirement
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that must obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Required_entity or the obtaining of the Requirement.
Ex: A performance like this ["deg" absolutely] DEMANDS charm.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which militates that the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.
Ex: This Par 5 DEMANDS great shotmaking ["Condition" if the player is to equal or better par].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.

fe.name: Required_entity
fe.definition:
An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain.
Ex: Believe it or not, but this cake REQUIRES ["Required_entity" a pound of mild sausage].

fe.name: Required_individual
fe.definition:
An individual that has to provide the Required_entity or to see to it that the Requirement state of affairs holds.
Ex: It's a sport that DEMANDS everything ["reqi" of me].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.
Ex: ["pla" In the US], putting this on the agenda REQUIRES the political weight and leadership of big city mayors.

lexunit.name: demand.v
lexunit.definition: COD: require; need.

lexunit.name: require.v
lexunit.definition: FN: demand (the meeting of an enabling condition)

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: COD: need or call for.

lexunit.name: need.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to require something in order to be operational.

frame.name: Requirement_scenario
frame.definition:
One state of affairs, the Dependent, cannot occur without another state of affairs, the Requirement, also obtaining. This Requirement is construed to be under the control of some implicit force or actor. In an alternative construal, the Dependent state of affairs may be presented as depending on the presence of a Required_entity. Individual that profit from the occurrence of the Dependent state, Dependent_individuals, are backgrounded. The same goes for individuals (Required_individual) that are required to provide any Required_entity or to see to the occurrence of the Dependent state of affairs.
The nexus between Requirement and Dependent can be qualified further in terms of the Degree of strength of the link between the two eventualities, the Place and Time where this nexus obtains, the Reason for its existence, or a specification of Condition when it applies.

fe.name: Dependent
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.

fe.name: Requirement
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs which militates that the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent to obtain.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.
Ex: Such care is NECESSARY ["Condition" when under martial law].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.

fe.name: Dependent_individual
fe.definition: The individual in whose interest it is to have the Required_entity or for the Requirement state of affairs to obtain.

fe.name: Required_entity
fe.definition: An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain

fe.name: Required_individual
fe.definition: An individual that has to provide the Required_entity or see to it that the Requirement state of affairs holds.

frame.name: Obligation_scenario
frame.definition: Under some, usually implicit, Condition a Duty needs to be fulfilled by a Responsible_party. If the Duty is not performed, there may be some undesirable social Consequence for the Responsible_party. This Consequence may or may not be stated overtly.

fe.name: Responsible_party
fe.definition: The person who must perform the Duty.

fe.name: Duty
fe.definition: The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty.

fe.name: Consequence
fe.definition: The undesirable Consequence that will result if the Duty is not performed.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time interval during which the Responsible_party is obligated to fulfill the Duty.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .
Ex: I almost forgot to tell you that ["pla" in Sweden] we are OBLIGATED to spend atleast 7.5 months in the army for training.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The deviation of the requirement from the norm.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The desirable situation which can be brought about by fulfilling the Duty.

frame.name: Imposing_obligation
frame.definition:
A Duty is imposed on a Responsible_party according to a Principle which regulates how the Responsible_party should respond to a Situation. The Situation may be expressed metonymically by reference to an Obligator, whose action invokes the Principle. It is only rarely the case that the Principle and the Situation/Obligator are both expressed overtly.
Ex: They escaped total Soviet invasion and occupation only by entering into ["Principle" a separate agreement] ["Principle" that] OBLIGATED ["Responsible_party" them] ["Duty" to military action against the retreating German armies].
Ex: ["pri" The lease agreements] BOUND ["Responsible_party" them] ["Duty" to make rent payments to Homeowners Rescue].
Ex: It was also discovered that with out her knowlege, ["Obligator" he] had COMMITTED ["Responsible_party" her] ["Duty" to a new TV series] and he had already taken an advance on the money.
Ex: ["sit" The Generality's invitation to give a conference on the theme] OBLIGATED ["Responsible_party" me] ["Duty" to study Gaudí's work even more].

fe.name: Responsible_party
fe.definition:
The person who must perform the Duty.
Ex: The winning bid COMMITTED ["Responsible_party" her] to paint an oil portrait for the high bidder.

fe.name: Duty
fe.definition:
The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.
Ex: Had she really said the word which PLEDGED her ["Duty" to marry Horace Holmcroft in a fortnight]?

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the Duty is imposed on the Responsible_party by the Obligator or the Situation.
Ex: The City Council ["Time" then] OBLIGATED themselves to have the sewers made ready and the streets leveled off without any additional cost to the Sisters.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .
Ex: ["Place" At Dayton], the parties OBLIGATED themselves to respect and promote fulfillment of the annexes.

fe.name: Obligator
fe.definition:
The Obligator is the person who imposes the Duty on the Responsible_party.
Ex: ["Obligator" She] PLEDGED him to pay her the money back.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that results in the Responsible_party being obligated to carry out the Duty in accordance with the Principle.
Ex: ["sit" Admitting a genocide was occurring] would have OBLIGATED them, based on their signing the December 1948 Convention on the repression of genocide, to do something about it.

fe.name: Principle
fe.definition:
A regulating idea (which may be instantiated as a document) that the Responsible_party is subject to.
Ex: And ["Principle" no law] OBLIGATED him to talk to the police, let alone the media

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Obligator hopes to bring about by imposing the obligation.
Ex: She PLEDGED him to work on the project ["pur" just to get him out of her hair] .

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any holistic description of the details of the action, either comparing to another event or describing the action in terms of characteristics of the Obligator that affect the action holistically.
Ex: You COMMITTED me to this ["Manner" maliciously] !

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An event which brings about the obligation.
Ex: She did n't understand that she OBLIGATED me to stay ["mea" by always getting in trouble] .

lexunit.name: bind.v
lexunit.definition: COD: impose a legal or contractual obligation on.

lexunit.name: obligate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: compel legally or morally.

lexunit.name: commit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pledge or bind to a course, policy, or use.

lexunit.name: pledge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: obligate (someone) by swearing

lexunit.name: require.v
lexunit.definition: COD: specify as compulsory

lexunit.name: charge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: entrust with a task.

lexunit.name: charge.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an obligation placed upon another.

frame.name: Operating_a_system
frame.definition:
An Operator manipulates the substructure of a System such that the System performs the function it was created for.
This frame differs from the Using frame in that this frame does not profile the purpose of an agent but rather their manipulation of an entity (System/Instrument). In the case of using, the Agent need not manipulate the Instrument at all, as in: _Mrs. Adams used the room as a place to hang the family laundry to dry_.
Ex: This true story of domestic bliss was related to me by ["Operator" a friend of mine] ["Operator" who] for a time OPERATED ["System" a bar] ["Place" in San Francisco].
Ex: A California man has plead guilty to federal charges that ["Operator" he] RAN ["System" a pyramid scam which defrauded nearly 7000 investors.]

fe.name: System
fe.definition:
The entity that the Operator gets to perform its intended function.
Ex: Robert Faye, who has RUN ["sys" the organization] since its inception in 1991, said all the money the group has raised has been properly distributed.

fe.name: Operator
fe.definition:
The invididual who manipulates the substructure of the System.
Ex: ["ope" WELS Kingdom Workers] OPERATES this program for students interested in doing ministry for a summer job.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the Operator runs the System.
Ex: North Korea OPERATES a Restaurant ["Place" in Vietnam].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Operator runs the System.
Ex: The City OPERATES the system ["pur" to ensure high quality water at competitive rates].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the Operator runs the System.
Ex: This guaranteed donation to the charity was begun by Eric Von Stroh, Mike Cioli and Andrew Seligson, the three men who RAN the business ["Time" last year].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which an Operator runs the System.
Ex: By the end of the film you'll be marveling at Buster's dexterity while he OPERATES the steamboat ["Means" by climbing up and over or jumping down and around the ship].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the running of the System which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Operator that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: The farm is owned and ["Mnr" carefully] OPERATED by John and Janice Maloney in Newberry Springs, California.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
Duration denotes the length of the time interval in which the Operator runs the System.
Ex: The vendor has OPERATED this business ["dur" for the last 7 years].

lexunit.name: operate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: control the functioning of (a device, system, or institution)

lexunit.name: run.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to be in operation

lexunit.name: manage.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be in charge of; run.

frame.name: Be_in_agreement_on_assessment
frame.definition:
The Cognizers have a similarity (or dissimilarity) in their Opinion. The Cognizers may be expressed separately, with Cognizer_2 being the basis for establishing the Opinion of Cognizer_1. Rather than a specific Opinion, a phenomenon about which a similar or differing Opinion is held, the Topic, may be specified. A specific Opinion may also go unmentioned when the Opinions of the Cognizers are understood as answers to a Question.
Ex: ["Cognizers" Dr. Gerry and Mr. Pond] AGREE ["Question" in their impressions].
Ex: ["Cognizers" This copyeditor and I] ["Degree" mostly] SEE EYE TO EYE ["Topic" on things].
Ex: ["Cognizer_1" I] AGREE ["cog2" with you] ["Opinion" that everything should be monitored to keep the person from wasting time and protecting the interests of the company].

fe.name: Cognizers
fe.definition: This FE marks constituents that express the set of Cognizers whose similarity of opinion is at issue.

fe.name: Cognizer_1
fe.definition: When there is an asymmetry, Cognizer_1 is the individual characterized by their similarity in opinion to Cognizer_2, whose opinion is assumed to be known. Cognizer_1 is often an external argument.

fe.name: Cognizer_2
fe.definition: When the Cognizers are expressed separately, Cognizer_2 is the one whose opinion is assumed to be known; it serves as a basis for establishing the opinion of Cognizer_1.

fe.name: Question
fe.definition:
This FE denotes an implicit question in response to which the Cognizers give their Opinions, which are then assessed for their similarity. The Question may concern the identitiy of a particular entity, as in the first example below, or it may be of the yes/no-type, as in the second example below.
Ex: I think we SEE EYE TO EYE ["que" in our ultimate goal], which is that we want to see a democratic Serbia.
Ex: ["Cognizers" Almost all anarchists], in contrast, would AGREE ["que" in their condemnation of warfare, ie, violent conflict between governments].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Cognizers are similar in their Opinions.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizers are in agreement or disagreement.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the general area in which the Cognizers are in agreement or disagreement.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE is for descriptions of the agreement state not covered by more specific FEs, especially characterizations of the state as a whole or of one of the Cognizers or Cognizer_1.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the agreement or disagreement logically follows.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Cognizers

fe.name: Opinion
fe.definition:
A state of affairs believed by the Cognizers.
Ex: We AGREE ["opi" that babies should not be dropped from helicopters].

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: A phenomenon that the Cognizers are considering with respect to their Opinion.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state-of-affiars under which aggreement occurs (as independent of the act of agreement).

lexunit.name: agree.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have the same opinion about something.

lexunit.name: see eye to eye.v
lexunit.definition: FN: completeley agree on a topic or issue.

lexunit.name: concur.v
lexunit.definition: FN: agree on an opinion.

lexunit.name: agreement.n
lexunit.definition: COD: accordance in opinion or feeling.

frame.name: Giving_in
frame.definition:
A Capitulator who has been opposing a Force, which is typically exerted by a Compeller, ceases opposing that Force. As a result, the Force runs its course and an Issue is resolved against the interests of the Capitulator.
Ex: Accordingly, there is no basis to conclude that ["Capitulator" Tazewell] ACQUIESCED ["Force" in the rule against claim-splitting]. Ex: Accordingly, there is no basis to conclude that Tazewell ACQUIESCED in the rule against ["Issue" claim-splitting].
Ex: My uncle continued trying to placate Nuayman until ["Capitulator" the latter] RELENTED. ["Issue" DNI] ["Force" DNI]
Ex: ["Capitulator" Genesis] ACQUIESCED ["Resultant_action" to doing a short Q and A session]. ["Force" DNI]
Ex: ["Capitulator" The government] would not YIELD ["Force" to pressure] , the spokeswoman promised . ["Issue" DNI]

fe.name: Capitulator
fe.definition:
The individual that yields to the Force exerted by the Compeller.
Ex: I sensed that if ["cap" John] CAVED IN to her that it would hurt his game.

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition:
The matter, usually concerning a course of action, in which the Capitulator has disagreed with the Compeller.
Ex: Historically, the Senate has YIELDED to the House ["iss" on the issue].

fe.name: Compeller
fe.definition:
An individual that intentionally exerts Force on the Capitulator.
Ex: Relatively new to business, poor Kellie had eventually CAVED IN ["com" to him].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Capitulator yields to the Compeller on the Issue.
Ex: Ms Marinkovic RELENTED ["tim" yesterday] under intense international pressure.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Capitulator's giving in on the Issue logically follows.
Ex: I YIELDED to him ["exp" because I wanted to be a team player].

fe.name: Force
fe.definition:
A state of affairs, typically brought about by a Compeller, that impinges on the Capitulator and eventually causes them to no longer pursue their own view on the Issue.
Ex: In 1649, Descartes YIELDED ["for" to the request of Queen Christina of Sweden that he join her distinguished circle she was assembling in Stockholm].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the Capitulator ceases to oppose the Force.
Ex: John refused to heed the barons? early calls for reform, but in June 1215 he CAPITULATED ["pla" at Runnymede].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Capitulator intends to accomplish by ceasing their opposition.
Ex: Corfu in 229 BC, after several raids and suzerainties, was forced to ask the protection of the Romans and finally YIELDED to them ["pur" in order to protect itself] .

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Giving_in which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Capitulator that affect the action (_reluctantly_, _meekly_).
Ex: Congress ["man" reluctantly] CAPITULATED to this final demand on Sept. 1.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of how the Issue is resolved from the desires of the Compeller.
Ex: She ["deg" partially] GAVE IN, admitting her anti-urban bias was mostly in part to her parents brainwashing her from a young age.

fe.name: Resultant_action
fe.definition:
The action that the Capitulator engages in after giving in to the Force.
Ex: After months of pressure by my staff, I have finally YIELDED ["Resultant_action" to doing a commentary on advertising].

lexunit.name: relent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: abandon or mitigate a harsh intention or cruel treatment.

lexunit.name: acquiesce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accept or consent to something without protest

lexunit.name: yield.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give way to demands or pressure; submit.

lexunit.name: cave in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stop resisting

lexunit.name: give in.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cease fighting or arguing

lexunit.name: give way.v
lexunit.definition: FN: yield

lexunit.name: capitulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cease to resist an opponent or an unwelcome demand; surrender.

frame.name: Surrendering_possession
frame.definition:
A Surrenderer is compelled to transfer a Theme to a Recipient.
Ex: Shortly after ["Surrenderer" the boy] SURRENDERED ["Theme" the gun], the three remaining warriors made a rush for liberty.
Ex: ["Surrenderer" He] ["Time" finally] SURRENDERED ["Theme" the item] ["Time" after cops and Secret Service agents showed up at his home Saturday].
Ex: ["Surrenderer" D?Augustino] YIELDED ["Theme" the weapon] ["Recipient" to Herrick].

fe.name: Surrenderer
fe.definition: The person compelled to transfer the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The object that changes possession.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE denotes a proposition from which the surrendering event logically follows.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the manner in which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Surrendering event itself and any of its participants.
Ex: John SURRENDERED the gun ["cir" with everybody looking on in stunned silence].

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE describes the legal- or "by rule" domain within which the surrendering event is true or operational and may be expressed by words like ?formally? and ?officially? plus maybe ?technically? and ?in law.?

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an surrendering event.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: surrender.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give up (a person, right, or possession) on compulsion or demand.

lexunit.name: yield.v
lexunit.definition: COD: relinquish possession of

lexunit.name: relinquish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: voluntarily cease to keep or claim; give up.

lexunit.name: give up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to unwillingly give an item to a recipient

frame.name: Being_in_effect
frame.definition:
A particular Binding_principle is (or is not) operative, that is, any obligations, restrictions, and any other aspects of the Binding_principle are (or are not) in effect. The Binding_principle can be expressed as being in effect for a particular Duration, or at a particular Time or Place, or under certain Circumstances.
Ex: ["bin_pri" This law] will only _become_ _in_ EFFECT ["dur" during the last three weeks of the year]. Ex: ["bin_pri" The statutory wetlands definition] _is_ EFFECTIVE ["tim" immediately]. Ex: ["Binding_principle" This contract] is BINDING ["obl" on all parties].
Although the is properly in this frame, is analyzed in the Execute_plan frame. This is in part because to is to actually execute the plan (to evacuate), while to is to determine that in the future the plan may have to executed, i.e., to make the plan binding. Similar observations can be made for .

fe.name: Binding_principle
fe.definition:
The Binding_principle is the law, contract, principle, or other (set of) obligations that is (or is not) operational.
Ex: Once ["bin_pri" the treaty] is in EFFECT, US port authorities and the Coast Guard will monitor compliance by checking any yacht 79 feet or longer.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time for which the Binding_principle is or is not in effect.
Ex: The contract will be EFFECTIVE["dur" for three fiscal years].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Binding_principle is in effect.
Ex: All patent applicants and owners should be aware of the current uncertainty as to what patent fees will be in EFFECT ["tim" on October 1, 1998]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place at which the Binding_principle is or is not operational.
Ex: This promotion is VOID ["pla" in the state of Florida].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs under which the Binding_principle is/isn't operational.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A cause, reason, or other explanation for the status of the Binding_principle
Ex: Your contract is NULL ["exp" because you left the county].

fe.name: Obligated_party
fe.definition:
The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Binding_principle.
Ex: This statute is in EFFECT ["obl" for holders of H-1 visas] until January.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: effective.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a law or policy) operative.

lexunit.name: effect.n
lexunit.definition: FN: (with in or into) the state or quality of being operational or effective.

lexunit.name: force.n
lexunit.definition: FN: (with in or into) state or quality of being in effect.

lexunit.name: valid.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having legal efficacy.

lexunit.name: void.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not valid or legally binding.

lexunit.name: null.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having no legal force; invalid.

lexunit.name: binding.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (especially of contracts) having legal force.

frame.name: Store
frame.definition: A Supply of a Resource is kept safe and available for a future Use. The Supply may be under the control of a Possessor.

fe.name: Supply
fe.definition:
This FE denotes the Supply of Resources.
Ex: And, yes, some have a vast ["sup" STORE] of honorably gained material goods.

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition:
The goods or commodity that is being stored in a Supply.
Ex: India has made great strides in agriculture and now not only meets it own grain needs but has a sizeable RESERVE ["res" of basic grains, mainly rice and wheat].

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The future Use for the Resource.
Ex: Due to restrictions imposed by our export control, the Japanese have begun to use a portion of their ["use" war] RESERVE of petroleum.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
The entity that possesses the Supply.
Ex: In 1997, ["pos" France's] STOCK of unirradiated civil plutonium increased to 72 tons.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of the Supply itself, rather than the Resource.
Ex: Institutions have focused on Broward County?s ["des" dwindling] SUPPLY of land, continued population growth and elevated income levels.

lexunit.name: store.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a quantity or supply kept for use as needed.

lexunit.name: stock.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a supply of goods or materials available for sale or use

lexunit.name: stockpile.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large accumulated stock of goods or materials.

lexunit.name: supply.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a stock or amount of something supplied or available.

lexunit.name: inventory.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a quantity of goods in stock.

lexunit.name: reserve.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a reserved supply of a commodity.

lexunit.name: cargo.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a quantity of goods that is roughly equivalent to that which can be stored in a cargohold of some kind

frame.name: Correctness
frame.definition:
A particular piece of Information is evaluated for its accuracy. The Degree of correctness may also be expressed. The Source of information may also metonymically stand in for the Information.
Ex: Is your reputation at risk due to INCORRECT ["inf" information]? Ex: If your dealership service people make such ["deg" totally] WRONG ["inf" claims], I would be uncomfortable trusting their warranty claims too. Ex: All users must verify the CORRECTNESS ["inf" of their own information.] Ex: We found ["inf" all of his information] to _be_ RIGHT.

fe.name: Information
fe.definition:
The Information matches or does not match the facts of the world.
Ex: ["inf" That statement] is totally INCORRECT.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Information matches or does not match the facts of the world.
Ex: Vague prophecies, interpreted with maximum latitude, are likely to appear ["deg" at least somewhat] ACCURATE.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The aspect of reality which is accurately modeled by the Information.
Ex: That claim may be factually ACCURATE ["dom" in terms of in vitro pharmacology] but that may have no clinical relevance.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
The aspect of the Information which accurately models reality.
Ex: Don't select an option just because it contains ["par" factually] CORRECT information about the clinical situation.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Information is correct.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is the agent who holds the correct/incorrect information.
Ex: ["Source" He] is correct

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame, which typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Source is correct/incorrect.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Information or the Source is correct.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The physcial context that the Information is found in.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modified the target to indicate the legal- or "by rule" domain within which it is true or operational.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The outcome of the correctness if the Source or Information.

fe.name: Communicative_act
fe.definition: The event which communicates the Information.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic about which the Source has accurate information.

lexunit.name: correct.a
lexunit.definition: COD: free from error; true; right.

lexunit.name: incorrect.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not in accordance with fact or particular standards; wrong.

lexunit.name: wrong.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not correct or true.

lexunit.name: right.a
lexunit.definition: COD: factually correct.

lexunit.name: accurate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: correct in all details.

lexunit.name: correctness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state or quality of correctness.

lexunit.name: exact.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not approximated in any way; precise.

frame.name: Estimating
frame.definition:
A Cognizer carries out an approximate calculation or considers some Evidence so as to arrive at an approximate Value for some Feature of an Item.
There are two alternative construals. In one, the Feature is presented as a Question about the Item and the Value is conceived as an answer to the Question.
In the second construal, a fully propositional Estimation by the Cognizer is presented which expresses the result of the Cognizer's approximation.
Ex: ["Time" Until 1971], ["Question" dolphin mortality] could be ESTIMATED ["Evidence" only from analyses of vessels ' logbooks] -- and the figures are probably underestimates. ["Cognizer" CNI]
Ex: ["Cognizer" The UK government] ESTIMATES ["Estimation" that there is sufficient gas in the UK sector to meet UK demand for some 17 to 35 years] .
Ex: ["Cognizer" The astronomers] ESTIMATED ["Question" how much energy was needed to create the cavities by calculating the density, temperature and pressure of the hot gas].
Ex: ["Item" The banner] is ESTIMATED ["Feature" in value] ["Value" at $500]. ["Cognizer" CNI]
Ex: ["Time" When Congress passed the Medicare bill in late 2003], ["Cognizer" the Congressional Budget Office] ESTIMATED ["que" its cost] ["Value" at $395 billion over 10 years].
Ex: ["Cognizer" We] estimated ["que" how much we had] ["Value" at around 12 thousand].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The individual who considers evidence or performs calculations to arrive at an approximation.
Ex: ["cog" The government] ESTIMATED the cost of meeting EC water standards at £3-4 billion.

fe.name: Feature
fe.definition:
The feature is a scalar property of the Item.
Ex: In one march from 42 Street down to Washington Square Park, the crowds were ESTIMATED ["fea" in size] from 125000 (NYPD estimate) to over 200000 (march organizers).

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
The position or area on the Feature scale that the Cognizer concludes the Item occupies.
Ex: Sotheby 's have ESTIMATED its value ["val" at $10m-$14m].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The entity that possesses the Feature whose Value the Cognizer seeks to approximate.
Ex: I ESTIMATED ["Item" the house] at about 60-65% full.

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
Some fact perceived by the Cognizer which contributes to their estimation of the Feature's Value.
Ex: He then needs to ESTIMATE the desired shelf stock size ["Evidence" on the basis of this record of use].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Cognizer forms the estimate of the Feature's Value.
Ex: The US Forest Service ESTIMATED ["Time" last year] that 45 million piñons have died so far in north-central New Mexico.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Cognizer forms their estimate.
Ex: ["Place" At the London School of Economics] they ESTIMATED that China would have to spend 2% of gross. domestic product on higher. education for 15 years

fe.name: Estimation
fe.definition:
A proposition expressing the Cognizer's approximation of a Feature's Value.
Ex: At the time they ESTIMATED ["est" there to be as many as four million to the acre].

fe.name: Question
fe.definition:
An open proposition for which the Cognizer seeks to approximate the Value of a variable.
Ex: Then Sandia ESTIMATED ["que" how many people would die and be injured within the first year due to their radiation exposure].
Ex: He ESTIMATED ["que" the length of his nose] at 6 inches but it was only 2 inches.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer enabling estimating.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner is used for any expression which describes a property of the activity of Estimating

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Cognizer estimates.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state-of-affairs enabling the estimating to occur.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE describes how the Estimation made by the Cognizer corresponds to reality. This FE can be represented by "correctly" or "wrong."

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

lexunit.name: estimate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form an estimate of

lexunit.name: estimation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of estimating (some feature's value)

lexunit.name: guess.v
lexunit.definition: COD: estimate or suppose (something) without sufficient information to be sure of being correct.

frame.name: Military
frame.definition: Some Possessor, either a nation, institution, or private individual, controls a Force whose primary functions to defend the Possessor (or, in the case of an institution or individual, some area of land significant to them) and to carry out offensive actions for the Possessor. The Domain of operation of the Force may be expressed.

fe.name: Force
fe.definition:
The Force is the body of soldiers that acts in military capacity for the Possessor.
Ex: Large ground-based ["for" FORCES] will attack to defeat and fix the enemy's front line.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
The Possessor is the nation, institution, or individual who possesses and/or controls the Force.
Ex: The American invasion, which drew 26000 American troops against ["pos" General Noriega's] ARMY, was the largest US military operation since Vietnam. Ex: Unfortunately, ["pos" They] don't _have_ a very strong ARMY.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of the Force.
Ex: And while Serbia is keen to invest in its ["des" dilapidated] ARMED FORCES, Montenegro wants to introduce a 4000-strong professional army.

fe.name: Members
fe.definition:
The consituent members of the Force.
Ex: The US has an entirely ["mem" citizen] ARMY.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain in which the Force operates.
Ex: The Persians originally planned to rely solely on their ["dom" land] ARMY to advance beyond Athens. Ex: You seem to think that our intelligence and ["dom" covert ops] FORCES and our military are only able to conduct one mission at a time.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
A (permanent or temporary) Goal of the Force.
Ex: Right at this time of emergency, the ["goa" revolutionary] ARMY made one attack after another in their rear, thus adding to their confusion.

fe.name: Period_of_existence
fe.definition: The length of time that the particular military organization has existed.

lexunit.name: military.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the armed forces, particularly of a nation.

lexunit.name: force.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an organized body of military personnel, police, or workers.

lexunit.name: navy.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the branch of the armed services that operates at sea.

lexunit.name: air force.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a branch of the armed forces concerned with fighting or defence in the air.

lexunit.name: army.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an organized military force equipped for fighting on land.

lexunit.name: naval.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of, in, or relating to a navy or navies.

lexunit.name: armed forces.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the army, navy, and air force.

lexunit.name: military.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of, relating to, or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces.

lexunit.name: military forces.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the army, navy, etc. of a nation.

lexunit.name: national guard.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the branch of the armed services that functions more like a militia - is more of a reserve force, and is capable of functioning in both military and law enforcement situations

frame.name: Estimated_value
frame.definition:
A Cognizer has carried out an approximate calculation or considered some Evidence and produced an approximation of the Value of a feature of an Item. There are two alternative construals in which the relationship between the feature and the Value is conceived. Either a holistic Estimation by the Cognizer is presented, or the Question that is addressed by the Cognizer's estimating is given.
Ex: You can list a ["Value" BALLPARK FIGURE] ["Item" for shipping and handling].
Ex: Moreover, ["Cognizer" their] ["Value" ESTIMATE] ["est" of 0.27 °C mean surface warming per century due to land-use changes] is at least twice as high as previous estimates based on urbanization alone.
Ex: Our decision to trust people depends on ["Cognizer" our] ["Value" ESTIMATE] ["que" of how trustworthy they are].
Ex: To help you anticipate the cost of your move, movers will give you an ["Value" ESTIMATE] ["que" of the price].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The individual who has considered evidence or performed calculations to produce the approximation.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Her] ESTIMATION was that they had exported up to 180000 fish.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
The position or area on the feature scale that the Cognizer has concluded the Item occupies.
Ex: Sotheby 's ESTIMATE of its value _was_ ["val" $10m-$14m].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The entity that possesses a feature whose Value the Cognizer has approximated.
Ex: He's an engineer and he is supposed to know the ESTIMATE ["Item" of the house].

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
Some fact perceived by the Cognizer which has contributed to their estimation of the Value.
Ex: The ["Evidence" habitat area based] ESTIMATE is probably the more reliable projection of the two.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Cognizer formed the estimate.
Ex: That is 30000 higher than ["Time" last year's] ESTIMATE of 2.65 million

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location in which the Cognizer has formed their estimate.

fe.name: Estimation
fe.definition:
A proposition expressing the Cognizer's approximation of a feature's Value.
Ex: One ESTIMATE _was_ ["est" that eventually I had lost about 80% of my blood].

fe.name: Question
fe.definition:
An open proposition for which the Cognizer has approximated the Value of a variable.
Ex: Galliard decided Rwanda was different, and he went public with his ESTIMATE ["que" of how many people had been killed in a matter of two weeks].

lexunit.name: estimate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an approximate calculation or judgement.

lexunit.name: estimation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: approximate calculation (of a feature's value)

lexunit.name: ballpark figure.n
lexunit.definition: FN: approximate value

frame.name: Withdraw_from_participation
frame.definition:
An individual that is scheduled to be a Participant, or already is a Participant in an Activity or an Organization, indicates that they will no not or no longer participate in that Activity or Organization. Note that the Organization often is one that is constituted by a treaty or agreement.
Ex: ["Participant" The Moslem contingent] had WITHDRAWN ["Activity" from the EC talks] ["Time" on May 27].
Ex: ["Participant" The right-wing nationalist Tsomet Party] formally WITHDREW ["Organization" from the ruling coalition].

fe.name: Participant
fe.definition:
The individual or individuals that are engaged or are scheduled to be engaged in an Activity.
Ex: Instead, ["par" he] was challenged by Neil Gaudry, and WITHDREW from the race when it appeared that he would not be victorious.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The event that the Participant is engaged in or was scheduled to be engaged in.
Ex: In any event , in mid-April he WITHDREW ["act" from the contest].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the withdrawing event logically follows.
Ex: Washington says it WITHDREW from the agreement ["exp" because Pyongyang admitted to secretly developing nuclear weapons].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Participant ends the participation in the Activity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Participant ends their participation in the Activity.

fe.name: Organization
fe.definition:
The Organization is an intentionally formed human social group with some definite structure to which the Participant belongs.
Ex: This led to the decision to WITHDRAW ["org" from IMF agreements] in May 1987 .

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Participant hopes to bring about by withdrawing

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The act done by the Participant that accomplishes their withdrawal.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The document that the Participant uses to communicate their withdrawal.
Ex: ["med" In a memorandum dated May 6], they withdrew from the NPT.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the attitude of the Participant which also affects the character of the withdrawal.
Ex: After that, she ["man" gladly] WITHDREW from the match.

lexunit.name: withdraw.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cease to participate in an activity or be a member of a team or organization.

lexunit.name: withdrawal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of ending participation in an activity or being a member of a team or organization

lexunit.name: pull out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: withdraw from an undertaking.

lexunit.name: pull-out.n
lexunit.definition: FN: withdrawal from an undertaking.

lexunit.name: beg off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: withdraw from a promise or undertaking.

frame.name: Accomplishment
frame.definition: After a period in which the Agent has been working on a Goal, the Agent manages to attain it. The Goal may be a desired state, or be conceptualized as an event.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Agent that lets them accomplish their Goal.
Ex: Can you , too , ACHIEVE omniscience ["Mns" by calling on the power of God] ?

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional act that fulfills the Goal.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Agent that allows them to achieve their Goal.
Ex: ["Ins" With a simple hammer and saw] , you can ACCOMPLISH almost anything !

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the Agent achieves their Goal.
Ex: She had already ACHIEVED that feat ["Place" in Burma] .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the Agent achieves their Goal.
Ex: ["Time" By 1700] , our forces will have ACHIEVED total victory .

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: Perhaps you ACHIEVED perfection ["man" too quickly] .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A state-of-affairs from which the accomplishment would be predicted.
Ex: Yes, he was humble, but he ACHIEVED enlightenment ["exp" only because he came from the upper class].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Agent achieves the Goal.
Ex: He has only ["Degr" partially] ACHIEVED his objective .

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The state or action that the Agent has wished to participate in.
Ex: Iraq had ACHIEVED ["goa" its programme objective of producing nuclear weapons] .

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of accomplishing a Goal.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which Goal is accomplished.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that it takes for Goal to be accomplished.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The particular aspect or domain of the Goal that is achieved.
Ex: No one can surpass his ["dom" economic and financial] ACHIEVEMENTS.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: accomplish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: achieve or complete successfully.

lexunit.name: achieve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring about or accomplish by effort, skill, or courage.

lexunit.name: accomplishment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: something that has been achieved successfully.

lexunit.name: achievement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: Something that has been successfully achieved.

lexunit.name: bring about.v
lexunit.definition: FN: Cause goal to be accomplished.

frame.name: Submitting_documents
frame.definition:
A Submittor gives Documents to an Authority so that they can be processed as part of an application, evaluation or other official or bureaucratic process.
Ex: I was sure I had passed as soon as ["Submittor" I] HANDED IN ["Documents" the test]. ["Authority" DNI]
Ex: She stated that ["Submittor" she] TURNED IN ["Documents" the paperwork] ["Time" yesterday].
Ex: After ["Submittor" the applicant's] SUBMISSION ["Authority" to the department], the department chairperson must evaluate.
Ex: I acknowledge ["Submittor" my] SUBMISSION ["Documents" of the Material] ["Authority" to you] shall not lead to a concurrent review by any of your affiliate and subsidiary channels.

fe.name: Submittor
fe.definition:
The person that begins in possession of the Documentsand gives them over into the possession of the Authority for processing.
Ex: The Human Services financial worker cannot decide if you will get food support benefits until ["Submittor" you] TURN IN the form and needed verifications.

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition:
The individual or organization that ends up in possession of the Documents and processes them.
Ex: If an application is late, whether you SUBMITTED it late ["aut" to us] or it was held up at your Command, NMETC will not be able to fund registration fees.

fe.name: Documents
fe.definition:
The artifacts containing content, typically in the form of text and images, that the Submittor gives to the Authority.
Ex: Once you have SUBMITTED ["doc" the form], a request to make an oral statement will be generated based on the information you supplied.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place where the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which event of the Submittor's giving the Documents to the Authority logically follows.
Ex: Two of the establishments SUBMITTED the application ["exp" because they were producing a new product].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time period during which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner is the manner in which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.
Ex: The company ["Man" hastily] SUBMITTED the manuscript to three additional reviewers.

fe.name: Purpose_of_theme
fe.definition: The Authority's intended purpose for the Documents.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

lexunit.name: submit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: present (a proposal or application) for consideration or judgement.

lexunit.name: submission.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of presenting (a proposal or application) for consideration or judgement.

lexunit.name: hand in.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hand something over to (an authority)

lexunit.name: turn in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: hand something in (to an authority)

lexunit.name: file.v
lexunit.definition: FN: Submit document to be placed in a file.

frame.name: Intercepting
frame.definition:
A volitionally acting Interceptor takes control, without being authorized to do so by the sender, of a Theme that is underway from a sender to a recipient. The Interceptor (or somebody on whose behalf they act) believes that the Theme reaching its goal would be against their interest.
The Theme may be a physical thing that is being conveyed, a self-moving entity, or information that is broadcast.
Ex: ["Interceptor" Police] INTERCEPTED ["Theme" the call] and raided the address.
Ex: ["Theme" The vessel] got INTERCEPTED ["Place" in the Mediterranean] ["Interceptor" by the German navy] .
Ex: ["Interceptor" A Royal Navy frigate] INTERCEPTED ["Theme" his yacht] ["pla" off Gibraltar].

fe.name: Interceptor
fe.definition:
The volitional agent who without authorization of sender or recipient takes control of a Theme that is en route to a destination.
Ex: Two days later, ["int" an aerial patrol] INTERCEPTED an enemy trying the same thing.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The entity, physical or abstract, construed as traveling from a sender to a goal location, which is taken hold of by the Interceptor without permission.
Ex: They could either sail west down the Channel or north-east to INTERCEPT ["the" an enemy making for the Thames estuary].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which the Interceptor takes control of the Theme.
Ex: She had been INTERCEPTED ["pla" outside Guy 's room] and would be severely punished.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Interceptor takes control of the Theme.
Ex: The five had been INTERCEPTED ["tim" after a DFLP attack on March 5].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the intercepting event as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Intercepting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate also salient characteristics of the Interceptor that also affect the action (_carefully_).
Ex: With the help of John Poindexter, I've ["Manner" carefully] INTERCEPTED communications from cycling's best and brightest.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The circumstances under which the interception takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Interceptor hopes to bring about by intercepting.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action performed by the Interceptor that results in success.

lexunit.name: intercept.v
lexunit.definition: COD: obstruct and prevent from continuing to a destination

lexunit.name: interception.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of intercepting

frame.name: Resolve_problem
frame.definition:
An Agent resolves an outstanding Problem by finding its solution, explanation, answer, etc. Alternatively, some non-agentive Cause may resolve the Problem. The Means, Degree, Time and Place may also be expressed.
Ex: As it turns out, ["cau" putting all of my eggs in one basket] ["deg" completely] SOLVED ["pro" all of my problems]. Ex: ["age" Students] ["tim" finally] WORKED THROUGH ["pro" all of the difficult problems] ["mea" by working together].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent finds the solution or explanation to the outstanding mystery or Problem.
Ex: If ["age" we] have not been able to RESOLVE a problem to your satisfaction, please email us.

fe.name: Problem
fe.definition:
The Problem is the predicament or mystery that is resolved.
Ex: Likewise, once the students WORKED THROUGH ["pro" the problem] and obtained their results, their next assignment would be to publish these to the web.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
The Cause is the non-Agentive event or state of affairs that brings about the resolution of the Problem.
Ex: First, ["cau" the Tripartite Agreement of 1979] actually SOLVED the only significant friction between the two countries.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means is an intermediate action taken by the Agent in order to resolve the Problem.
Ex: I FIXED the floorplate issue ["mea" by shaving off the excess stock around the floorplate that was keeping it from closing]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Time at which the Problem is resolved.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE indicates the location at which the Problem is resolved.
Ex: A group of international scientists SOLVED the fundamental particle hierarchy question ["pla" at an underground accelerator].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree to which the Agent or Cause resolves the problem.
Ex: Our plan, I believe, wil ["deg" completely] RESOLVE all outstanding questions.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the resolution, such as secondary effects ( _quietly_ ) or comparisons of events ( _the same way_ ). In agentive cases, Manner may also describe salient characteristics of the Agent which affect the action.
( _carefully_, _dilligently_, _deliberately_ etc. )

fe.name: Resultant_Situation
fe.definition:
The Resultant_Situation is any situation which arises as a result of resolving a Problem .
Ex: The question was : could the situation be RESOLVED by improving the integration of the thought and design processes , ["Resultant_Situation" so that what was built better achieved what was intended] ?

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition:
The Outcome is the failure or success of resolving a Problem .
Ex: This issue must have been raised before and BSM would presumably be gratified to see the situation ["Outcome" successfully] RESOLVED , once and for all .

fe.name: Containing_Event
fe.definition:
The Containing_Event denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the resolution of the Problem occurs.
Ex: There are tricky design and methodological issues which would need to be worked out , as foreshadowed earlier in this paper and by no means fully RESOLVED ["Con" in the preliminary study] .

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Some specification of the circumstances under which the Problem is resolved.
Ex: Such issues can only be RESOLVED ["Cir" at local level] .

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
The Instrument is an entity used for resolving the Problem .
Ex: ["Inst" Using modern computers] , many practical elastic and other problems may be SOLVED by manipulation of this matrix .

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition:
This FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the resolution of a Problem .
Ex: I wanted you to believe that I was as grateful as you that the baby had died and SOLVED the problem ["Ben" for us] of concealing the birth .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the length of time taken to resolve a Problem .
The government RESOLVED the beach ball crisis ["Dur" in just 22 hours].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Role is used for the capacity in which the Agent resolves a Problem or the role of the Problem in being resolved, and is expressed in _as_-PPs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
Frequency describes how often the Agent or Cause resolves this problem.
Ex: Unfortunately , when such influences are considered as explanations of the results of free-running experiments , the following problems have ["Freq" never] been satisfactorily DEALT with.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This FE identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the Problem is resolved.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: A person who participates in resolving a Problem along with the Agent.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Agent is trying to bring about by solving the Problem in the specified way.

lexunit.name: resolve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: settle or find a solution to.

lexunit.name: solve.v
lexunit.definition: COD: find an answer to, explanation for, or way of dealing with (a problem or mystery).

lexunit.name: work through.v
lexunit.definition: FN: solve, especially a difficult problem requiring several steps.

lexunit.name: deal.v
lexunit.definition: FN: take action to resolve a problem.

lexunit.name: fix.v
lexunit.definition: FN: solve a problem so that a state of normalcy returns.

lexunit.name: clear up.v
lexunit.definition: COD: solve or explain something.

lexunit.name: do something about.v
lexunit.definition: FN: go about resolving a problem

lexunit.name: address.v
lexunit.definition: COD: think about and begin to deal with.

frame.name: Redirecting
frame.definition:
An intentional Agent or a causing event (Cause) event causes a Theme which is already in motion to take a different Path or Direction, or reach a different Goal than the Original_path.
Ex: The hotel business didn't last - especially after ["Cause" the construction of a railroad] DIVERTED ["Theme" travelers] ["Goal" a few miles west to what is now the village of Eagle]
Ex: ["Agent" Pakistan government officials] helped and DIVERTED ["Theme" the trucks] ["Goal" to another camp in the no-man's land in Mach].
Ex: ["Time" Prior to the arrival of the president's motorcade], ["Agent" the police] REDIRECTED ["Theme" the protesters] ["Direction" away from the main road]once more.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The entity that is in motion, and changes path due to the action of an Agent or due to a Cause.

fe.name: Original_path
fe.definition:
The route that the Theme was originally headed for. In cases when the Theme is an intentional actor or is controlled by an intentional actor, the Original_path correlates with the (former) plan of the actor. In other cases, the Original_path corresponds to what would be expected for the path of the Theme from general principles or physics. (In some cases, the Original_path may indicate the intended destination, and not just the path, of the Theme.)
Ex: VTA DETOURED motorists ["ori" from southbound I-880] onto Airport Boulevard to access Coleman Avenue.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Theme ends up travelling after being diverted.
Ex: Traffic was REDIRECTED Tuesday ["Path" along Melrose Avenue] to make way for the scoreboard columns, Mellecker said.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The location the Theme ends up in after being redirected.
