Ex: Not knowing any better, he REDIRECTED people ["Goal" to the city center].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the redirection of motion occurs.
Ex: ["Time" Last Tuesday] they were DETOURING everybody down onto 5th avenue .

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the redirection which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: Anything flagged as suspect by this system would be ["Manr" carefully] DIVERTED to another nearby area, remote from public access. and well shielded, for a second screening .

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Theme or Agent during the redirection.
Ex: The emergency personnel REDIRECTED the cars back towards the border, ["Dep" unaware of the recent conflagration].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is the location at which the redirection occurs.
Ex: They REDIRECTED us ["" at the corner of Alstone and Bokchoy Avenue].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the current deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that does not necessarily correspond to the Goal. Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Theme, the orientation imposed by an implicit observer, or the inherent orientation of the scene.
Ex: Flight 93 left Newark, NJ, earlier that day, bound for San Francisco, but it was hijacked by four terrorists who DIVERTED it ["dir" back toward Washington, DC] .

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Agent intends to bring about by redirecting the Theme.
Ex: She was talking about how the passengers DIVERTED the plane in order ["pur" to protect the nation's capital].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
An individual that determines the change in course of the Theme.
Ex: When we ended up over in Marrakech, or Dakar, ["age" they] DIVERTED us up to Tobruk.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event that brings about the change in the Path of the Theme.
Ex: We even got a bonus morning in Tokyo's international airport when ["Cause" a bad storm] DIVERTED us on the way to Asia.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The method by which the Agent redirects the Theme.

lexunit.name: redirect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: direct differently

lexunit.name: detour.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to take a different route so as to avoid some location

lexunit.name: divert.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to change course or take a different route.

frame.name: Terms_of_agreement
frame.definition:
A condition that is set out in an Agreement imposes Requirements on a Party or parties, with respect to some Regulated_entity. If the conditions are not met, the Agreement as a whole ceases to be valid or, more specifically, a Desired_state_of_affairs cannot occur. (The Desired_state_of_affairs typically is an interaction between the parties that benefits one or both sides.)
Ex: Breach of contract occurs where one of the parties fails to perform any one of the ["Agreement" contract] TERMS . Ex: Breach of contract occurs where one of the parties fails to perform any one of the contract ["req" TERMS] .
Ex: ["req" What] _are_ ["par" your] CONDITIONS ["Desired_state_of_affairs" for a peaceful settlement?]
Ex: Please read ["par" our] CONDITIONS ["des" of Sale] carefully Ex: Please read our ["req" CONDITIONS] of Sale carefully
Ex: We will verify compliance with the ["reg" financial] TERMS ["Agreement" of the contract]. Ex: We will verify compliance with the financial ["req" TERMS] of the contract.
Ex: The Engineering Division has violated the ["reg" seniority] PROVISION ["Agreement" of the collective bargaining agreement.] Ex: The Engineering Division has violated the seniority["req" PROVISION] of the collective bargaining agreement.

fe.name: Agreement
fe.definition:
A mutual commitment to an obligation made by two or more parties.
Ex: The right to remove tenants ' fixtures may be given by the TERMS ["Agreement" of the lease].

fe.name: Regulated_entity
fe.definition:
A salient entity, an activity or behavior by the parties to the agreement to which a particular stipulation pertains.
Ex: Many believed that the ["reg" military] TERMS of the armistice made the resumption of hostilities virtually impossible for Germany.

fe.name: Requirements
fe.definition:
The Requirements that a particular stipulation of the Agreement imposes on one or both of the parties.
Ex: Each time you use the site, a CONDITION of use _is_ ["req" that you comply with the above terms].

fe.name: Desired_state_of_affairs
fe.definition:
An event or state of affairs that is desirable to some or all of the parties to the Agreement and which is conditional on the Requirements being met.
Ex: What are your CONDITIONS ["des" of Sale]?

fe.name: Party
fe.definition:
A party who demands that certain Requirements be met before they will enter into an Agreement or allow a Desired_state_of_affairs to be realized.
Ex: ["par" Our] political and military TERMS of peace will be designed to prevent a repetition of Germany's misdeeds

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A description of the Requirements that are imposed by the Agreement.
Ex: No reason why SU would have to impose ["scr" harsh] TERMS, the lease payments would pay the bank loan used to buy the stadium.

lexunit.name: condition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a state of affairs that must exist before something else is possible.

lexunit.name: stipulation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: demand that is part of a bargain or agreement.

lexunit.name: provision.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a condition or requirement in a legal document.

lexunit.name: clause.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular and separate article, stipulation, or proviso in a treaty, bill, or contract

lexunit.name: term.n
lexunit.definition: COD: stipulated or agreed requirements.

lexunit.name: parameter.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

frame.name: Used_up
frame.definition:
Through use, a Resource is diminished in quality or quantity (up to complete attrition) such that it becomes less capable of sustaining future use.
Ex: ["res" My entire life savings] _is_ DEPLETED ["exp" due to university and medical bills].
Ex: ["res" All significant oil and gas reserves] _are_ EXHAUSTED or have dwindled to an uneconomical level except for those of the Middle East.
Ex: Use shampoo and conditioner every day until ["res" the shampoo and conditioner] _are_ ["deg" completely] USED UP.

fe.name: Resource
fe.definition:
The Resource is a physical entity or an ability to perform work that was used in an earlier process, typically in pursuit of a goal.
Ex: ["res" The battery] _is_ slightly WORN OUT

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A measure of the amount of the Resource that is gone, or of the degree to which its quality is reduced.
Ex: Don't put the battery on a charger until it is ["deg" totally] SPENT.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes an event or state from whose occurrence the Resource's being used up logically follows.
Ex: Others say that the Canadian marketing talent pool is DEPLETED ["exp" because fewer young people are being attracted to the business].

fe.name: Excess
fe.definition:
This FE indicates that the presence of an overwhelming amount of a kind of entity or the high intensity of an event is sufficient to bring about the used up state of the Resource.
Ex: Rent it for nostalgia, but I don't recommend buying it unless you own the video and it is WORN OUT ["Excess" with so much use].

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition:
Subregion denotes a sub-part of the Resource in which the it is specifically exhausted or worn out.
Ex: Sometimes if you have a shoe and it is WORN OUT ["sub" on one side] you'll see that if you put your foot in it, it leans in that direction.

lexunit.name: spent.a
lexunit.definition: COD: used up; exhausted.

lexunit.name: worn out.a
lexunit.definition: FN: exhausted

lexunit.name: depleted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being reduced in number or quantity

lexunit.name: used up.a
lexunit.definition: FN: exhausted

lexunit.name: exhausted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of resources or reserves) used up completely.

lexunit.name: through.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having finished an activity, relationship, etc.

frame.name: Ranked_expectation
frame.definition:
An Entity is rated as unexpected for its context in terms of its magnitude. Either some different type of Entity with a different scope would be expected, or a different amount of the Entity.
Ex: The ENTIRE ["ent" apple] was riddled with worms . Ex: The inevitable fate of the Warsaw Resistance fighters was not finally sealed until nine WHOLE ["ent" weeks] of vicious fighting had taken a terrible toll on the people .
Ex: A MERE ["ent" two percent] of Afghan women are registered to vote. Ex: The crime scene doesn't wrap up in an hour, never mind an ENTIRE ["ent" investigation] . Ex: It 's a huge engineering project when you 're building a WHOLE ["ent" car] . Although there are some words that overlap between this frame and Completeness, the words in this frame indicate specifically that the magnitude of the Entity is different from what is expected, rather than grading an entity as to whether all its parts are present. The Ranked_expectation uses must occur with an explicit or implicit quantification. The Completeness uses can only occur with entities that have salient necessary parts and structure.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The item which is described in terms of its expectedness in the context.
Ex: The ENTIRE ["ent" day] was spent on the project .

lexunit.name: entire.a
lexunit.definition: COD: with no part left out; whole

lexunit.name: whole.a
lexunit.definition: COD: emphasizing a large extent or number

lexunit.name: mere.a
lexunit.definition: COD: that is solely, or no more or better than, what is specified.

frame.name: Completeness
frame.definition:
A Whole, an entity with a substructure, is assessed for whether or not it has all the necessary parts that are defined for it or for an entity of its kind. The entity can be a concrete physical thing, an abstract thing, or a process with goals or sub-goals.
Ex: What happens after ["who" the PPB investigation] _is_ COMPLETE?
Ex: Enter the number of days since the last COMPLETE ["who" backup] was made.
Ex: This distinguishes them from organisms in the phylum Platyhelminthes, who have only an INCOMPLETE ["who" digestive tract].
Ex: We now have an ["deg" almost] COMPLETE ["who" understanding] of the model
Ex: Auditors should also assess the accuracy and COMPLETENESS ["who" of the systems and data].
When the entity is a process with a goal, then what is assessed for completeness can either be the extent to which all candidate participants are involved in or affected by the process, or the stage that the process has reached. Thus the last of the above examples can either mean that all parts of the model are understood or that the model is fully understood as opposed to, for instance, merely intuitively apprehended.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
An expression indicating a deviation of the actual level of completeness from the level indicated by the target.
Ex: This course is ["deg" very] COMPLETE and addresses all aspects necessary to get a good understanding of hazardeous areas and the use of instrumentation.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
The entity that is being assessed for having all its necessary parts or not.
Ex: ["Whole" Our list of participants] _is_ still INCOMPLETE.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The interval of time when the completeness of the entity is assessed.
Ex: My journey to the dark side is ["Time" now] COMPLETE.

lexunit.name: complete.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having all the necessary or appropriate parts

lexunit.name: incomplete.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not complete

lexunit.name: completeness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being complete or the degree of completeness

lexunit.name: total.a
lexunit.definition: COD: complete; absolute.

lexunit.name: full.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not lacking or omitting anything; complete.

frame.name: Electricity
frame.definition:
Lexical units in this frame refer to Electricity, in particular as a form of energy harnessed for particular uses (such as powering machines). The Source of the Electricity may also be expressed, or incorporated in the meaning of the LUs.
Ex: A compound to generate ["sou" wind] ["ele" ELECTRICITY] was built on the other side of those mountains.
Ex: China's ["ele" HYDROELECTRIC] dam is being built primarily for flood control and energy production.

fe.name: Electricity
fe.definition:
Electricity is the physical force that is used as power.
Ex: The Brunswick Electric Membership Corporation supplies ["ele" ELECTRICITY] for sections of Brunswick and Columbus counties.
Ex: ["ele" POWER]'s out!

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source of the Electricity.
Ex: The ELECTRICAL POWER ["sou" from the plant] will be fed into the public grid Ex: And that is part of the reason Italy is now rethinking its ban on ["sou" nuclear] POWER.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of some property of the Electricity.
Ex: Finally, electricity pricing will be determined by pooling ["des" cheaper] HYDROELECTRICITY with more expensive thermoelectric plants (natural gas).

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The intended Use of the Electricity.
Ex: The government provides free ELECTRICITY ["use" for cooking and cleaning only].

lexunit.name: electricity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the supply of electric current to a building for heating, lighting, etc.

lexunit.name: electric.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of, worked by, or producing electricity.

lexunit.name: power.n
lexunit.definition: COD: energy that is produced by mechanical, electrical, or other means.

lexunit.name: electric power.n
lexunit.definition: FN: electric energy.

lexunit.name: juice.n
lexunit.definition: COD: electrical energy.

lexunit.name: electrical.a
lexunit.definition: COD: concerned with, operating by, or producing electricity.

lexunit.name: hydroelectric.a
lexunit.definition: FN: related to the production of electricity by waterpower.

lexunit.name: hydroelectricity.n
lexunit.definition: FN: electricity produced by water power.

lexunit.name: photoelectric.a
lexunit.definition: COD: characterized by or involving the emission of electrons from a surface by the action of light.

lexunit.name: photoelectricity.n
lexunit.definition: FN: electricity created or affected by light.

lexunit.name: energy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: power derived from physical or chemical resources to provide light and heat or to work machines.

lexunit.name: electrical power.n
lexunit.definition: FN: electric energy.

frame.name: Being_active
frame.definition:
An Agent is described as pursuing an Activity, expending some effort. The Agent may be active in a particular Role. Alternatively, the Activity itself may be described as having an Agent who is expending effort. In some cases, the Activity may involve a Salient_entity which may stand in for it.
Ex: ["Agent" Sky, a Korean War veteran,] _was_ ACTIVE ["Activity" in his opposition to Vietnam] and continues to protest current combat in Iraq.
Ex: ["Agent" She] _is_ ACTIVE ["Place" in the community] ["Activity" by establishing parent groups, life skills program, sharing circles and various Aboriginal cultural activities for young women.].
Ex: ["Agent" John Colville] _was_ quite ACTIVE ["Role" as a land speculator] ["Place" in both Virginia and Maryland].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the amount of Time for which an Activity is ongoing.
Ex: Upon his release from federal detention in 1947 he joined the IWW and has remained ACTIVE ["Dur" for five decades] as a graphic artist, poet, and advisor.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the name of the ongoing Activity in which an Agent engages.
Ex: He is always ACTIVE ["Activity" demolishing the painted figures of men's faith] and then is astonished to find the faith still there clothed in new figure.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the Activity is pursued.
Ex: He is retired from Whirlpool Corp. in Clyde and is ACTIVE ["Place" at the YMCA].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent is engaged in an ongoing Activity.
Ex: Throughout her life, Bertha was ACTIVE in civic organizations ["pur" in order to establish chiropractics in the public eye].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Activity is pursued.
Ex: Commercial selling was ACTIVE ["Time" yesterday] but a lack of interest allowed the market to push sharply higher into the mid-session.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the Activity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably_, _presumably_, _mysteriously_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _deliberately_).
Ex: The Government was ["Manner" deliberately] INACTIVE in respect of Maori. language teacher training and teaching.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent engages in an ongoing Activity.
Ex: ["Agent" He] _was_ ACTIVE for six decades as a painter, graphic designer and theorist of art and design.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
An entity acted upon by the Agent.
Ex: ["sal" As many as 324 companies' stocks] were ACTIVE across the board.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the role filled by the Agent which is saliently associated with an Activity.
Ex: Jacques Fuller has been ACTIVE ["rol" as a sculptor] in Bloemfontein for almost two decades.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree to which the Agent or Salient_entity is active.
Ex: Mick was an ["Degree" extremely] ACTIVE volunteer for the Air Force IT Day committee.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

lexunit.name: active.a
lexunit.definition: FN: participating vigorously in a particular sphere or activity.

lexunit.name: inactive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not participating vigorously in a particular sphere or activity.

frame.name: Installing
frame.definition:
An Agent places a Component in a Fixed_location so that the Component is attached and interconnected and thereby functional.
Ex: Displays were given an overhaul in the 1950s, with ["Component" canopies] INSTALLED ["fix" above the Christmas counters] ["pur" to allow calendar and gift bows to be displayed]. ["Agent" CNI]
Ex: ["loc" At the street] ["Component" an 8'' culvert] will be INSTALLED ["fix" under the driveway]. ["Agent" CNI]
Ex: ["fix" In the space where the piano was, right next to the washing machine,] ["Agent" my grandmother] INSTALLED ["Component" her first dryer].
Ex: ["Agent" My handyman] INSTALLED ["Component" it] ["Time" yesterday] and then I sort of forgot about it.
Ex: Now Marvin Odum, InterGen's Chief Executive Officer, has committed to moving up INSTALLATION ["Component" of the pollution control technology] on its two other turbines.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person (or other force) that installs the Component.
Ex: ["Agt" John] INSTALLED it last night on my Gentoo system and everything is going fine so far.

fe.name: Component
fe.definition:
The Component is the object that is placed in a Fixed_location.
Ex: My plumber INSTALLED ["com" the shower pan].

fe.name: Location_of_protagonist
fe.definition:
This frame element specifies the location of the Agent (or of parts of their body) in cases where the Agent cannot manipulate the Component in straightforward fashion during the installation.
Ex: The front was easy for me to install, I held the bar and bolt in place from below and INSTALLED the nut ["loc" from the top around the control arm bushing].

fe.name: Fixed_location
fe.definition:
The Fixed_location is the location where the Component is placed and to which it is attached so as to be useful.
Ex: I assembled the fuel tank using a vent line and a supply line, and then I INSTALLED the tank ["fix" in the fuselage].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the installation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (_deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree indicates the degree to which the installation is completed.
Ex: Is the riser complete at the point the stab fittings are complete or when the fittings are complete and the riser is ["Degree" completely] INSTALLED in the bracket with the bolts tightened?

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Component that is installed.
Ex: We delivered and INSTALLED it ["Dep" unfinished] because the customers wanted to finish it themselves.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the installation of the Component.
Ex: We INSTALLED the spindle assembly ["Means" by starting with the lower-ball joint, followed by the upper].

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
The Duration_of_final_state is the amount of time for which the Component is to remain part of the System.
Ex: Per the suggestion of A. Briggs Geddis, Mr. McChord informed the Commission that a curtain drain could be INSTALLED and monitored ["dur" for two months] to try to lower the groundwater level in the proposed septic area.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place indicates where the installation occurs.
Ex: When I INSTALLED the server ["Place" there] last winter they only had two rows of racks, mostly empty.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation indicates why the installation occurs.
Ex: I INSTALLED a new HDD ["exp" because it had numerous bad sectors].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period in which the Component is installed.
Ex: When we INSTALLED our hood ["Time" last month], the folks at Dallas Auto Body painted our roll pan at the same time.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
The Area is the setting into which multiple Components or a complex Component is installed.
Ex: I INSTALLED tongue and groove pine flooring ["Area" through my entire house].

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
This is a second component that is installed alongside the primary Component or an individual performing the installation together with the Agent.
Ex: The Hewlett Packard 5989A MS Engine was INSTALLED in 1991 ["cop" together with the Hewlett Packard 5890 Series II Gas Chromatography (GC/MS)].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the installation.
Ex: North Johnston High School INSTALLED many technologies ["pur" in order to dramatically improve the energy efficiency of our building].

lexunit.name: install.v
lexunit.definition: COD: place or fix (equipment) in position ready for use.

lexunit.name: installation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of installing or being installed

frame.name: Place_weight_on
frame.definition:
An Agent who is engaged in an Undertaking accords a Degree of importance to a Consideration that influences the success of an Undertaking. As a consequence, the Agent acts in a way that reflects that judgment of importance.
Ex: ["Agent" Our company] EMPHASIZES ["Consideration" marketing tried and true products and services].["Competing_consideration" INI]
Ex: In fact, ["Agent" most search engines] PLACE ["Degree" little] WEIGHT ["Consideration" on words placed in meta tags] ["Undertaking" when creating their relevancy rankings].["Competing_consideration" INI]
Ex: The EMPHASIS _is_ ["Consideration" on the fundemental principles from which the automotive technolgies of the future will develop], ["Competing_consideration" rather than on present-day processes].
Ex: ["Agent" Our] EMPHASIS ["Consideration" on quality] does not stop with our products. ["Competing_consideration" INI]
Ex: ["Undertaking" When shooting in my studio], ["Agent" I] EMPHASIZE ["Consideration" a relaxed atmosphere].["Competing_consideration" INI]

fe.name: Consideration
fe.definition:
An event or state of affairs, an attribute, or an entity whose properties have the potential to influence the success of the Agent's Undertaking.
Ex: The ICBL has PRIORITISED ["con" working to achieve universalisation of the Mine Ban Treaty in South Asia by 2004].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which the Consideration is important to the Undertaking.

fe.name: Undertaking
fe.definition:
The Undertaking is a process or state or field of activity in which the Agent participates.
Ex: ["Undertaking" In my classes] I _place_ greater EMPHASIS on the importance of staying relaxed and being aware of one's physical limits rather than exactness of form.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which the Consideration is important to the Undertaking.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the individual who devotes time, concentration, or other resources to a Consideration that is important for the success of a larger Undertaking.
Ex: Dell said Friday ["age" the company] will put more EMPHASIS on selling software

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by assigning the specified level of importance to the Consideration.
Ex: Wilson said it is necessary to PLACE less WEIGHT on SAT scores ["pur" in order to maintain diversity].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that allows the Agent to respond to the importance of the Factor to the Undertaking.

fe.name: Competing_consideration
fe.definition:
The Competing_consideration is another factor that is relevant to the Undertaking to which the Agent devotes less attention or effort.
Ex: Monophysite Christians EMPHASIZED Christ's divinity ["com" over his humanity].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Agent attaches a specified degree of importance to the Consideration to further the success of the Undertaking.
Ex: ["Time" In the 1960s] Foucault PLACED great WEIGHT on the notion of archeology.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Agent attaches the specified level of importance to the Consideration.
Ex: ["pla" In Arizona] we EMPHASIZE western bats with a special focus on species identification.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any further description of the Agent's placing of importance on the Consideration.
Ex: Our teacher always _places_ ["man" vigorous] EMPHASIS on controlling our spiritual energy.

fe.name: Artifact
fe.definition:
The Artifact is a physical object designed with some Consideration in mind, such that it functions to facilitate the Undertaking.
Ex: Water is a scarce commodity on French Island so ["art" the guest house] places strong EMPHASIS on water conservation.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
The Action is performed with importance placed on the Consideration.
Ex: Result ORIENTED ["act" Management] Ex: ["act" UN efforts] FOCUSED on the rehabilitation and economic development of south Lebanon

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times. In the future, we will further distinguish Particular_iteration, which is intended to pick out a particular iteration from a series.

lexunit.name: emphasize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: devote relatively more attention and effort to

lexunit.name: prioritize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: designate or treat as most important.

lexunit.name: emphasis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

lexunit.name: place weight.v
lexunit.definition: FN: attaching importance to something

lexunit.name: centered.a
lexunit.definition: COD: taking a specified subject as the most important element

lexunit.name: focused.a
lexunit.definition: FN: directed towards or placing importance on a particular subject.

lexunit.name: focus.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pay particular attention to.

lexunit.name: oriented.a
lexunit.definition: FN: specifically designed for or placing particular attention on a subject.

lexunit.name: growth-oriented.a
lexunit.definition: FN: specifically designed for or placing particular attention on economic growth.

lexunit.name: stress.v
lexunit.definition: COD: emphasize.

frame.name: Convey_importance
frame.definition:
Through a Message, a Speaker (sometimes encoded metonymically by a Medium) communicates the relative importance of the state of affairs denoted by the Message.
Ex: ["Speaker" Reid] EMPHASIZED ["Message" that he and Dean meet every month]. Ex: Above all , ["Speaker" Mr Tsongas] STRESSED ["Message" the need for his message to be heard]. Ex: ["Speaker" Professor Perkin] has STRESSED ["Message" how favourable Britain 's situation was] . Ex: ["Speaker" The courts] have ["Iteration" repeatedly] STRESSED ["Message" that the making of an order is discretionary]. Ex: ["Message" "The whole Muslim society should respect these rights,"] ["Speaker" he] STRESSED. Ex: ["Speaker" The panelists] STRESSED ["Addressee" to an audience of about 100 at North Dakota State University's Memorial Union] ["Message" that people of different religions in this community need to talk - and find out they're not all that different].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.
Ex: ["Speaker" Juhl] EMPHASIZED the importance of UPMC System investments, stating that their contribution to the school's funds had tripled in recent years.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee is the audience to which the Speaker communicates the Message.
Ex: Pastor Host EMPHASIZED ["Add" to him] that as you study a passage, a theme develops from the text.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition:
The proposition whose denotation the Speaker presents as important.
Ex: He EMPHASIZED to me ["Message" that my words will go down in history and that this poem has made a difference in our world].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
Ex: ["Medium" The report] EMPHASIZED that Iraq's unwillingness to cooperate represents a serious problem for the progress of this work.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, in particular secondary effects (_loudly_), general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_), and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: You will note above that I have ["Manner" deliberately] STRESSED our ability as mental health professional to make a determination of current suicide risk.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means by which the Speaker communicates the importance of the state of affairs denoted by the Message.
Ex: Mr. Rose STRESSED this ["Mns" by pointing out that the latest offender had been fined over $5000].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Speaker communicates a Message.
Ex: However, Cockerill STRESSED ["Time" last week] that he had had many meetings about these obvious synergies and that he had pursued these aggressively.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition:
The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Speaker conveys a Message whose denotation they present as an important fact to be aware of.
Ex: During Chen's telephone call with Soong, Hsieh said at a press conference, Soong EMPHASIZED ["Iteration" multiple times] his commitment to the 10-point consensus.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree of importance that the Speaker conveys the Message's denotation as having.
Ex: The need to understand design is often ["deg" heavily] STRESSED during conversations or articles about desktop publishing .

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Speaker delivers the Message.
Ex: Putin STRESSED ["pla" in Beijing] that Russia does not favor independence for Taiwan.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Period of iterations
fe.definition: This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative. Period_of_iterations can co-occur with either the peripheral FE Duration or the extra-thematic FE Duration_of_final_state (although these cannot occur together).

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

fe.name: Particular Iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

lexunit.name: stress.v
lexunit.definition: COD: emphasize

lexunit.name: emphasize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: convey the importance of

lexunit.name: underline.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stress.

lexunit.name: underscore.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stress, underline.

frame.name: Storing
frame.definition: An Agent has placed a Theme in an accessible but somewhat out of the way Location for the purposes of maintaining it free from harm and illegitimate use while it is not being used.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person who has placed the Theme in the Location.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the object that is kept in a Location by the Agent

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: The location where the Theme is kept.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the storing state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme of the storing event.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme remains in the Location.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place indicates where the Storing occurs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the storing event logically follows.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: Time is the time period during which the Theme is stored.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The Area is the setting into which a mass Theme is placed.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the storing event either as a co-agent or a co-theme.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the storing action.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

lexunit.name: storage.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of storing.

lexunit.name: store.v
lexunit.definition: FN: keep for future use

lexunit.name: warehouse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: store (goods) in a warehouse

lexunit.name: cache.v
lexunit.definition: COD: store in a cache.

lexunit.name: keep.v
lexunit.definition: FN: store

frame.name: Indigenous_origin
frame.definition:
An Entity began its existence in the context of a location of Origin, which is a discourse-salient place, or culture.
Ex: Obviously there are ["Entity" species] ["Entity" that] are NATIVE ["Origin" to China] or used in Chinese Medicine that aren't used in Western or Cherokee Medicine and vice versa.
Ex: The INDIGENOUS ["Entity" people], women and the elderly are the most affected. ["Origin" DNI]
Ex: The Athenians believed that ["Entity" they] _were_ 'AUTOCHTHONOUS' ["Origin" in Attica].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The item whose Origin is under discussion.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition: The discourse-salient place or culture where the Entity was produced.

lexunit.name: indigenous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: originating or occurring naturally in a particular place; native.

lexunit.name: native.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having grown or originated in a given location

lexunit.name: autochthonous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having originated where encountered

lexunit.name: stranger.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who does not know, or is not known in, a particular place.

lexunit.name: non-native.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not of indigenous origin to an area

lexunit.name: local.n
lexunit.definition: FN: One who is native to a particular place.

frame.name: Being_at_risk
frame.definition:
An Asset is in a state where it is exposed to or otherwise liable to be affected by a Harmful_event, which may be metonymically evoked by reference to a Dangerous_entity. Words expressing relative safety (i.e., lack of risk) are also in this frame.
Ex: If you are a farmer, ["Asset" you] _are_ _at_ RISK ["Harmful_event" for hearing loss caused by noise exposure in your work].
Ex: ["Asset" No child] _is_ SECURE ["Harmful_event" from the temptation to do what "my friends" are doing].
Ex: Our nation is making a disastrous mistake thinking that ["Asset" we] can _have_ SECURITY ["Dangerous_entity" from people]: There is only security with people.
Ex: ["Asset" You] don't _have_ SECURITY ["Harmful_event" against impersonation] unless you have security against eavesdropping.

fe.name: Asset
fe.definition:
Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.
Ex: There is a locked padlock that guarantees ["Asset" the information] is SECURE.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Asset and the state indicated by the target itself.
Ex: My mail is ["deg" totally] SECURE in this box.

fe.name: Harmful_event
fe.definition:
An action that may occur or a state which may hold which could result in the loss of or damage to the Asset.
Ex: Our system ensures that information stored within hardware is SECURE ["har" from external software attack and physical theft].

fe.name: Dangerous_entity
fe.definition:
A concrete or abstract entity which may come to cause the loss of, or damage to the Asset either due to its participation in a Harmful_event.
Ex: We make sure your BMW is SECURE ["dan" against intruders].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
A particular location in which the Asset is secure. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location protect the Asset from a potential Harmful_event.
Ex: Workers need to make sure their property is SECURE ["pla" at work].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Asset enjoys the specified level of security from a Harmful_event.
Ex: Israel is INSECURE ["Time" today] not because it does not have enough military power.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the state of security or insecurity of the Asset logically follows.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition:
The Situation under which the Asset is safe or unsafe.
Ex: Our children are SAFE ["sit" with that criminal behind bars].
Most expressions of Time and Place also express the Situation and should be labeled as such on the 2nd FE layer.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain in which the Asset has a degree of safety.
Ex: Students with Asthma need to _be_ ["dom" medically] SAFE at school.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

lexunit.name: secure.a
lexunit.definition: COD: certain to remain safe and unthreatened.

lexunit.name: security.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being or feeling secure.

lexunit.name: safe.a
lexunit.definition: COD: protected from or not exposed to danger or risk; not likely to be harmed or lost.

lexunit.name: insecure.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not secure

lexunit.name: unsafe.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not safe or secure; in danger.

lexunit.name: safety.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the condition of being safe.

lexunit.name: risk.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the possibility that something unpleasant will happen.

lexunit.name: vulnerable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: exposed to being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

lexunit.name: vulnerability.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being exposed to or likely to suffer harm.

lexunit.name: danger.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the possibility of suffering harm or injury.

frame.name: Waiting
frame.definition:
A Protagonist delays a planned action because they cannot or do not want to proceed until an Expected_event occurs. The Expected_event may be evoked by reference to a Salient_entity that participates in it. If a Salient_entity is expressed, the Expected_event is typically the arrival of the Salient_entity at the Place where the Protagonist is located.
Ex: ["pro" The cat] WAITED ["pla" on top of the washer] ["Time" as Elmer popped the lid off the can of cat food] and then pounded the can's contents onto the plate
Ex: The family was furious that ["pro" their 84-year-old dad] had to WAIT ["dur" 52 hours] ["pla" in the emergency room].
Although in both frames a Protagonist/Agent is not performing some desired action for some period of time, the use of wait.v in this frame is different from that in Holding_off_on in that Waiting prominently portrays a future event that will allow the Protagonist to proceed (with doing something), whereas Holding_off_on does not necessarily imply that there is some event or state-of-affairs that will allow the Agent to proceed, rather focussing on the action that the Agent is not yet taking.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The sentient being who cannot proceed with their planned activities until a Salient_entity has arrived or an Expected_event has occurred.
Ex: ["pro" He] politely WAITED, hat in hand, until he could speak.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
A concrete or abstract entity that the Protagonist expects to participate in an Expected_event, typically that of arriving at the Place of the Protagonist.
Ex: In busier times several passengers are WAITING ["sal" for the train].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Protagonist is waiting.
Ex: At least 17 ships were WAITING ["Time" yesterday] to come up the river.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Protagonist is waiting.
Ex: Reporters are WAITING ["pla" outside the State Guesthouse] for the talks to start .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the waiting to its end.
Ex: He WAITED ["dur" for three hours] this night, but no one showed up.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the waiting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_) and salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (_patiently_, _anxiously_).
Ex: She WAITED ["man" tensely] for him to appear

fe.name: Expected_event
fe.definition:
The Expected_event is an event that needs to take place or a state that needs to begin to hold before the Protagonist can proceed with their planned activities.
Ex: She did n't WAIT ["exp_e" for a reply], but spelled out the answer herself. Ex: Then you have to WAIT about thirty seconds ["exp_e" for there to be enough charge for a second jolt]. Ex:

fe.name: End_point
fe.definition:
The point in time, defined either as a clock time or in terms of an event that takes place, at which the Protagonist ends the waiting.
Ex: I am willing to WAIT for him ["end" until 10 o'clock].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the waiting event logically follows.
Ex: I WAITED for your brother to give me advice ["Explanation" because I wasn't sure I was actually going to do this crazy thing].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE describes the Protagonist as being in some state during the waiting.
Ex: We WAITED ["dep" with a smile on our faces and a chortle in our hearts] when the race organizers handed out the first weather charts.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Protagonist intends to accomplish by waiting.
Ex: Cussing under his breath, he said he went back outside and WAITED quietly ["pur" in order to avoid further argument].

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co_participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

lexunit.name: wait.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stay where one is or delay action until a particular time or occurrence.

lexunit.name: bide_time.v
lexunit.definition: SMV: delay action until a particular time or occurrence.

frame.name: Clarity_of_resolution
frame.definition:
The Outcome of a contest is described in terms of the Margin between what would be required for victory and the actual Outcome.
Ex: The Basque nationalists won a NARROW ["Outcome" victory] in the regional elections on Sunday.
Ex: It was a major victory for workers, and a DECISIVE ["Outcome" defeat] for the Tory.

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome of a contest whose Margin is under consideration.

fe.name: Margin
fe.definition: The difference between the minimum required for victory and the actual Outcome.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Value from what is expected given the Outcome and the Value indicated by the target.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Outcome has a particular Value for the Margin.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition: The generally implicit Value of the Margin.

lexunit.name: narrow.a
lexunit.definition: COD: barely achieved

lexunit.name: decisive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of the outcome of a contest) having a wide margin

lexunit.name: decisiveness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the fact of (an outcome) having a wide margin

lexunit.name: close.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of an outcome) having a small margin

lexunit.name: narrowly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: with a small margin.

frame.name: Exertive_force
frame.definition:
An Entity is able to exert a Force of the Magnitude specified by the target.
Ex: Physically, ["Entity" she] _is_ ["Degree" very] STRONG and uses her strength to benefit her football.
Ex: Yes, Bronstein had the chance to punish his MIGHTY ["Entity" opponent] for his three-year neglect of work on chess.
Ex: CCE faces STRONG ["Action" opposition] from WCA and other groups.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity which possesses an ability to exert Force, whose Magnitude is under consideration.

fe.name: Force
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Magnitude of Force that the Entity can exert from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of being able to exert a Force of a particular Magnitude.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity is able to exert a Force of the specified Magnitude .

fe.name: Magnitude
fe.definition: The generally implicit value of the Force.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: An action in which the Entity exerts Force.

lexunit.name: strong.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (capable of) exerting great force.

lexunit.name: weak.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not (capable of) exerting great force

lexunit.name: mighty.a
lexunit.definition: COD: possessing great power or strength.

frame.name: People_along_political_spectrum
frame.definition:
An Individual belongs to a group that is categorized in terms of the political views on particular issues that the members of the group tend to share, in opposition to other groups that hold different beliefs on the issues. The views on particular issues that the Individual shares with the other members are assumed to result from general principles or beliefs rather than being accidental or temporary.
Ex: ["Individual" LEFTISTS] vow huge protests during inauguration

fe.name: Individual
fe.definition:
The Individual who is referred to in terms of their place along the political spectrum.
Ex: Why the ["Individual" LEFT] has lost credibility.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Individual resides.
Ex: We need to reshape the agenda of the LEFT ["Place" in Hungary].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
A set of issues that is used to identify a sub-set of the group members.
Ex: So where, oh where, can Democrats find a candidate who is a ["Domain" fiscal] CONSERVATIVE, a social moderate and well-liked in the West?

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition:
The Origin is the place where the Individual was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.
Ex: We won the cold war and a lot of the ["ori" French] LEFT has never gotten over that little fact of life.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Individual.
Ex: I'm another one of those ["Descriptor" angry] CONSERVATIVES that everyone hates!

fe.name: Persistent_characteristic
fe.definition: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Individual which is conceived of as persisting over time.

fe.name: Age
fe.definition:
The Age is the length of time the Individual has been alive.
Ex: There is a history of ["Age" young] LEFTISTS gaining publicity and buzz.

fe.name: Ethnicity
fe.definition: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Individual belongs.

fe.name: Position_qualifier
fe.definition: A phrase that indicates more precisely the location in political space of the Individual relative to the center of the region designated by the target.

lexunit.name: left.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a group or party favouring radical, reforming, or socialist views.

lexunit.name: leftist.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a left-wing person

lexunit.name: conservative.n
lexunit.definition: FN: (in a political context) a person favouring free enterprise, private ownership, and socially conservative ideas.

lexunit.name: far-left.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a group or party favouring particularly radical, reforming, or socialist views.

lexunit.name: far left.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a group or party favouring particularly radical, reforming, or socialist views.

frame.name: Ammunition
frame.definition:
A piece of Ammunition is a disposable artifact to be fired as a projectile in a weapon with the purpose of causing harm or damage.
Ex: The octagenarian inventor's vest repels ["Use" armor-piercing] ["amm" BULLETS].
Ex: It is armed with a automatic loaded 105 mm gun firing ["Use" anti-tank] ["amm" ROUNDS]
Ex: ["Material" Depleted uranium] ["amm" MUNITIONS] are primarily used by the US and the UK.

fe.name: Ammunition
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Ammunition that is designed to have a particular Use.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The use for which a piece of ammunition is intended.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: An individual or individuals that bring the Ammunition into existence.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition: The time at which an Ammunition comes into existence.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The term used to refer to an Ammunition.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An indication of the subtype of Ammunition.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: Any indication of what makes up the Ammunition, including components, ingredients, etc.

lexunit.name: ammunition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a supply or quantity of bullets and shells

lexunit.name: ammo.n
lexunit.definition: COD: ammunition

lexunit.name: ordnance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: ammunition for heavy weapons (including missiles and large rounds)

lexunit.name: round.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the amount of ammunition needed to fire one shot

lexunit.name: munitions.n
lexunit.definition: FN: ammunition and single-use weapons

lexunit.name: bullet.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a projectile fired from a small firearm, typically metal, cylindrical and pointed.

frame.name: Going_back_on_a_commitment
frame.definition:
A Protagonist has made a Commitment but does not honor it, thereby doing harm to an Affected_party.
Ex: ["Protagonist" My buddy Tom's girlfriend] BACKED OUT ["Commitment" of going to the show with me].
Ex: However, ["pro" the employer] ["Time" then] BACKED OUT ["Commitment" of that statment] and did not pay the STD!
Ex: ["Protagonist" The government] had RENEGED ["Commitment" on promises to give them land].
Ex: When ["pro" she and her family] WENT BACK ["com" on their police statement] ["pla" in the Vadodara court] ["Time" in May 2003], it stirred a huge controversy.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The Protagonist is the person who has committed themselves to do something and later does not follow through on it.
Ex: The human rights situation is infinitely better now than under the Taliban, but ["pro" the Bush administration] has RENEGED on its pledge of a new Marshall Plan.

fe.name: Affected_party
fe.definition:
The individual or group to whom the Protagonist had made the Commitment and who is negatively affected by the Protagonist's not honoring the Commitment.
Ex: Two people BACKED OUT ["aff" on me] a few days earlier.

fe.name: Commitment
fe.definition:
An expression of the commitment that the Protagonist has taken on earlier and which they fail to follow through on.
Ex: It appears that Schwarzenegger will RENEGE ["com" on an agreement he made with teachers].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, secondary effects (_quietly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (_coldly_).
Ex: They ["man" deliberately] BACKED OUT of Government last November because they knew that the 'hard men' were not ready for it.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Protagonist fails to honor their commitment.
Ex: When a host city BACKED OUT ["Time" at the last minute] and Russellville, Ark., landed the opportunity to host the Babe Ruth 16-Year-Old World Series.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Protagonist fails to honor the commitment they made.
Ex: But his efforts came to nought when 18 of the 19 accused were bailed out as most witnesses BACKED OUT ["pla" in court].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the Protagonist's failure to honor the Commitment logically follows.
Ex: The buyer BACKED OUT ["exp" because the seller asked for more money]

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition:
In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the Protagonist's act of going back on their Commitment as a whole.
Ex: When Roy Jones ["eve" cowardly] BACKED OUT of a fight with Heavyweight Buster Douglas, Toney again offered himself as a replacement.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: How much the Protagonist goes back on their Commitment.

fe.name: Re_Encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Protagonist backed out on a commitment.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The outcome of the Protagonist going back on a commitment.

lexunit.name: back out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: withdraw from a commitment

lexunit.name: go back.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fail to keep (a promise).

lexunit.name: renege.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go back on a promise, undertaking, or contract.

frame.name: Importing
frame.definition:
An Importer receives Goods from an Exporting_area, across a boundary or border to a different area, the Importing_area. The Path along which the Goods pass may also be indicated.
Ex: ["Importer" The U.S.] IMPORTED ["Goods" some wheat] ["Time" in the period], although it exported about ten times as much. Ex: ["Importer" We] IMPORT ["Goods" most of the Tahitian seashells] ["Path" through Japan]. Ex: IMPORTATION ["Goods" of wildlife] has gotten more difficult. ["Importer" INI] ["Importing_area" INI] ["Exporting_area" INI]

fe.name: Importer
fe.definition: The conscious entity, generally a person, that brings the Goods into the Importing_area.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: A mobile entity directed by the Importer that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Importer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Importer that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The items of value whose location is changing.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which the Importer moves the Goods.
Ex: Some department stores IMPORT expensive items ["Purpose" to please their higher-paying customers].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that explains the Importer's importation of the Goods.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Importer moves the Goods.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action Ex: Kazakhstan IMPORTED the petroleum, ["Depictive" unaware of its own reserves].

fe.name: Importing_area
fe.definition: The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.

fe.name: Exporting_area
fe.definition: The place where the Goods are initially, before the being moved.

lexunit.name: importation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of moving goods into an area.

lexunit.name: import.v
lexunit.definition: COD: bring (goods or services) into a country from abroad.

lexunit.name: import_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of importing.

lexunit.name: import_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: an imported commodity, article, or service.

frame.name: Exporting
frame.definition:
An Exporter moves Goods across a border from an Exporting_area to an Importing_area.
Ex: ["Exporter" Several companies] actually make most of their income by EXPORTING ["Goods" goods] ["Exporting_area" out of the country]. Ex: EXPORTATION ["Importing_area" into nations of "special interest"] is essentially prohibited.

fe.name: Exporter
fe.definition:
The conscious entity, generally a person, that moves the Goods across a border out of the Exporting_area.
Very often, an Exporting_area will metonymically stand in for the person or persons directly responsible for the movement of the Goods. In such cases the constituent should be labeled Exporter on the first layer and with the appropriate locational FE on the second layer. Ex: ["Exporter" The U.S.] EXPORTS most of its peanut products.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: A mobile entity directed by the Exporter that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Exporter that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Exporter that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The items of value whose location is changing.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the state-of-affairs that the Exporter is attempting to bring about by exporting.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state of affairs that explains why the Exporter moves the Goods across the border.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Exporter moves the Goods.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action Ex: Kazakhstan EXPORTED the petroleum, ["Depictive" gleeful at how much they were earning].

fe.name: Importing_area
fe.definition: The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.
Ex: The EXPORTATION of goods ["Path" across state lines] is strictly prohibited.

fe.name: Exporting_area
fe.definition: The place where the Goods are initially, before the the Exporter moves them.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Exporting event belongs to.

lexunit.name: exportation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of moving goods out of an area for purposes of sale.

lexunit.name: export.v
lexunit.definition: COD: send (goods or services) to another country for sale.

lexunit.name: export_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the exporting of goods or services.

lexunit.name: export_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: an exported commodity, article, or service.

frame.name: Product_delivery
frame.definition: In order to facilitate the purchase of Goods which start off in a location distant from a Purchaser, a Deliverer transports and hands off the Goods to a Purchaser or (more indirectly) a Goal location which is accessible to the Purchaser.

fe.name: Deliverer
fe.definition: This is the person who completes the movement of the Goods after having transported it.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The objects being delivered.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: The vehicle employed by the Deliverer.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Goods or the Deliverer during the action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the delivery event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Deliverer that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Purchaser
fe.definition: The individual who purchases and receives the Goods.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Deliverer hopes to bring about by delivering to the Purchaser.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state-of-affairs that explains why the Goods were delivered.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the delivery takes place

fe.name: Co_theme
fe.definition: An additional theme delivered along with the main Goods.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition: A container in which the Goods is delivered.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the delivery takes place.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed at which the Deliverer delivers the Goods.
Ex: This service is for our clients who need ["spe" speedy] DELIVERY of their goods.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The conditions under which the delivery takes place.
Ex: Purchases over $400 are DELIVERED for free.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The location of the Goods before the delivery process begins.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The intermediate actions performed by the Deliverer in order to move the Goods to the Goal.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The path along which the Goods move while being delivered.

frame.name: Reforming_a_system
frame.definition:
Because it no longer functions adequately under the given circumstances, an Agent (or non-Agentive Cause) undertakes steps to change the structural makeup of a complex Entity with interdependent parts, for instance an institution or a system of laws. The Degree of change is typically gradual and partial rather than revolutionary and total. Note that with some LUs the Entity can be unexpressed when it is identical to the Agent.
Ex: ["Agent" They] want to REFORM ["Entity" the law on Sunday trading]. Ex: At the same time , ["Agent" the government] REFORMED ["Entity" the rating system as it applied to companies].
Ex: This study investigates ["Manner" how] and ["Explanation" why] ["Agent" the majority of large Slovak companies] RESTRUCTURED ["Means" without the help of foreign investors or a government]. ["Entity" DNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity that effects a change in the Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the change of the Entity is caused.
Ex: The House of Representatives, on a bipartisan basis, sought to REFORM the program ["Time" this year].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Entity differs from its former state at the end of the reform.
Ex: I am trying to ["deg" completely] OVERHAUL my diet, and i need help.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event causing the change of the Entity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_), general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_), and salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (_carefully_).

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which reform event logically follows. In many cases, the state of affairs denoted is specifically one that the Agent takes as a reason for reforming the entity.
Ex: But his great-grandson, Aurangzeb (1618-1707), REFORMED the policy ["exp" due to religious conflicts].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
This FE denotes a complex, abstract, human-created entity with interdependent parts which has either deteriorated or is no longer adequate for its purpose given a change in circumstances and which the Agent therefore wants to modify.
Ex: Particular attention will be devoted to recent proposals to REFORM ["ent" UK competition policy].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by effecting a change in the Entity.
Ex: Indeed, as the world becomes increasingly paperless, it would be prudent to consider OVERHAULING the rules ["pur" in order to adapt them to a digitalized society].

fe.name: Initial_category
fe.definition:
The category of which the Entity is a member before the Agent causes a change in its makeup.
Ex: Since 1986, the Vietnamese Government has performed a 'doi moi' (renovation) policy that REFORMED the economy ["ini" from central planning economy] to market.

fe.name: Final_category
fe.definition:
The category that the Entity belongs to after it has undergone the change.
Ex: We have also REFORMED the office managing system from a "proprietorship" ["Final_category" to a "partnership"].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the steps or actions directly enabling reform.

fe.name: Re-encoding
fe.definition: An alternative description of expressed action

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE is used for phrases that describe the event of reforming as a whole .

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE describes the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the reform process.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time over which reforming takes place

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
This FE is for non-human causes, such as a processes or institutions, responsible for reform.
Ex: Thus , ["Cause" radical reform] RESTRUCTURES rape offences in ways that it is hoped will facilitate the prosecution process without jeopardising the interests of the accused .

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the reformation occurs.

lexunit.name: reform.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of reforming.

lexunit.name: reform.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make changes in (something, especially an institution or practice) in order to improve it.

lexunit.name: overhaul.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make changes so as to improve the functioning of

lexunit.name: overhaul.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of making changes so as to improve the functioning of

lexunit.name: restructure.v
lexunit.definition: FN: change the organization of a system.

frame.name: Economy
frame.definition:
A Political_region, often a nation, has an economic system, theEconomy, defined by the level of production and consumption of goods and services. The Market_type or Domain may be specified.
Ex: The ["pol" Canadian] ["Economy" ECONOMY] will continue to expand in 2005. Ex: Medical industry is a new force in the ["dom" industrial] ["Economy" ECONOMY] ["pol" of Lin'an].

fe.name: Political_region
fe.definition: The Political_region is the nation, state, or other political body within which an economic system exists.

fe.name: Economy
fe.definition: The Economy is the state of the Political_region as defined by the production, consumption, etc. of goods and services.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain of the state for which the Economy is being considered.
Ex: In this way the ["dom" agrarian] ECONOMY of the mainland might have proceeded towards a further specialization in agricultural products and a more effective production of food.

fe.name: Market_type
fe.definition:
The type of economic market in which the Economy exists.
Ex: For much of its post-1947 history, India ran a ["mar" socialist] ECONOMY. Ex: China's ["mar" free-market] ECONOMY is generating unprecedented but not unlimited press freedoms, and there's momentum.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A further depction of the Economy.
Ex: Hertfordshire enjoys a ["des" buoyant] ECONOMY.

lexunit.name: economy.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of a country or region in terms of the production and consumption of goods and services and the supply of money.

lexunit.name: economic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of or relating to economics or the economy.

frame.name: Extreme_point
frame.definition:
An Entity that has characteristics which change over time is at a point or in a phase of its development in which, compared to other actual or expected stages of development, it possesses extremely high or low powers or intensity. The high or low level of development correlates with the occurrence of a Marker, a product produced by the Entity or an event in which it participates, which is indicative of the Entity's abilities or intensity.
Ex: ["Marker" The Tang Dynasty] was the HIGH POINT ["Entity" of the Silk Road's importance].
Ex: ["Marker" Meeting Fiona Bennett] _was_ the LOW POINT ["Entity" of my summer].
Ex: It must be remembered that this man was born at the ["Marker" ZENITH] ["Entity" of the Victorian age] and witnessed the glory of Britain at her greatest.
Ex: But Lubitsch was at the ["Marker" HIGH POINT] ["Entity" of his genius], and he has made a masterpiece not to be missed.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
An concrete or abstract entity that possesses characteristics that change over time.
Ex: Midway was the ZENITH ["ent" of Japanese military advancements].

fe.name: Marker
fe.definition:
A point or phase in time when, viewed across the actual or expected development, the Entity's powers have reached an extreme high or low point. The point or phase is often identified metonymically by reference to a product created by the Entity or an event involving the Entity.
Ex: ["Marker" Watergate] _was_ the ZENITH of American investigative journalism.

lexunit.name: high-water mark.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a maximum recorded level or value.

lexunit.name: high point.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a point of high development or power

lexunit.name: low point.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a point of low development or power

lexunit.name: zenith.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the time at which something is most powerful or successful.

lexunit.name: nadir.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the lowest or most unsuccessful point

frame.name: Alliance
frame.definition: After having worked separately for some time, two or more organizational or individual Members are now organized in an Alliance so that they may better pursue some common Purposes. The formerly separate Members may be presented separately as Member_1 and Member_2.

fe.name: Alliance
fe.definition: The entity of which the individuals are Members.

fe.name: Members
fe.definition: The persons or groups belonging to the Alliance.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which an Alliance is formed.

fe.name: Period_of_existence
fe.definition:
The interval during which the Alliance exists.
Ex: Hezbollah was founded in 1982 in response to the Israeli invasion of Lebanon, and subsumed members of the ["per" 1980s] COALITION of groups known as Islamic Jihad.

fe.name: Member_1
fe.definition:
That group or individual which has joined the Alliance which is grammatically more prominent when the Members are presented separately.
Ex: ["me1" Our] ALLIANCE with Japan is the cornerstone of Asia-Pacific security strategy.

fe.name: Member_2
fe.definition:
That group or individual which has joined the Alliance which is grammatically less prominent when the Members are presented separately.
Ex: Thanks in part to their COALITION ["me2" with McCoy], but thanks also to their seniority and the knowledge of some of their leaders, they hold considerable influence

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A characterization of some property of the Alliance.
Ex: The two leaders enjoy an ["Descriptor" uneasy] ALLIANCE.

lexunit.name: alliance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a union or association formed for mutual benefit

lexunit.name: coalition.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a temporary alliance, especially of political parties forming a government.

frame.name: Holding_off_on
frame.definition:
An Agent decides temporarily not to perform a Desirable_action or not to interact with a Salient_entity.
Ex: ["Agent" I] have actually HELD OFF ["Desirable_action" on buying some movies by WB] ["Explanation" because of those damned cases].
Ex: ["Agent" We] HELD OFF ["Desirable_action" on reporting this] ["Explanation" because, by all accounts, the young Oscar-nominee has NOT been offered the role].
Ex: This meant WAITING ["Desirable_action" with dinner] until late. ["Agent" CNI]
Ex: ["Agent" I] WAITED ["Desirable_action" with going to him] and in retrospect think that that was a mistake.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
TheAgent decides not to engage in a Desirable_action for a while or not to interact with a Salient_entity.
Ex: Instead, ["Agent" he] HELD OFF on a public announcement of his decision for more than a year.

fe.name: Desirable_action
fe.definition:
Desirable_action identifies the event or activity in which the Agent does not engage for a while.
Ex: The board also WAITED ["Des" with the appointment of seven members to the planning and zoning commission] until a policy is set regarding requirements.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the temporary forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the temporary forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which the temporary forgoing occurs.
Ex: Portland General Electric, for example, has HELD OFF on retail rate increases ["Means" by selling some excess power at high wholesale prices].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the temporary forgoing occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the interval of Time during which the the forgoing occurs.
Ex: Saskatchewan teachers are not a happy lot as they had voted for a strike in June ["Time" then] HELD OFF on it to give negotiations a chance during the summer.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Purpose for which the temporary forgoing occurs.
Ex: We HELD OFF on taking him out ["Purp" so as to not disrupt the plans for the invasion of Iraq]?

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
