The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the Agent's decision to temporarily forgo a Desirable_action or to not interact with a Salient_entity logically follows.
Ex: Yes yes I saw them, but I WAITED with a reply for sometime ["exp" because I wanted first to show them to my guildmates].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Agent does not engage in the Desirable_action.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
An entity that evokes a contextually inferrable Desirable_action that the Agent is temporarily forgoing.
Ex: I ordered the blackberry cobbler with ice cream for dessert and HELD OFF ["sal" on another pint] as the rain kept coming down.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Agent's decision to forgo a Desirable_action to the point in time when the Agent engages in the action.
Ex: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) WAITED with the deal ["dur" for nearly five years] because of a dispute with the Pentagon about the avionics.

fe.name: End_point
fe.definition:
The point in time, defined either as a clock time or in terms of an event that takes place, at which the Agent engages in the Desirable_action or interacts with the Salient_entity.
Ex: We WAITED on technology development ["End_point" until we had made instructional plans].

lexunit.name: hold off.v
lexunit.definition: FN: temporarily forgo

lexunit.name: wait.v
lexunit.definition: FN: temporarily refrain from

fe.name: Party_1
fe.definition: The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of the commercial agreement, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus manner expressions are construed to apply to Party_1, not necessarily to Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.

fe.name: Party_2
fe.definition: The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the agreement. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).

fe.name: Obligation
fe.definition: An expression of the commitment which the Parties have to engage in a commercial transaction.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: Topic is a description of the domain covered by the commercial agreement.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.
Ex: The parties have a ["med" written] AGREEMENT to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.

fe.name: Parties
fe.definition: The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in having a commercial agreement.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where an agreement was made.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the agreement was made.

frame.name: Waver_between_options
frame.definition:
A Cognizer faces a choice on some Issue. They have several Options available but keep changing their mind between Option_1 and Option_2. The Cognizer may in fact act on their choice at some point but they need not; the Options can simply be considered for some time with one being favored for a while and then the other.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Dave Hayes] WAVERED ["Issue" about moving to California] ["Explanation" because so many of his friends are in Baltimore].
Ex: ["Cognizer" He] had WAVERED ["Options" between half a dozen places]; it was pure chance that he had chosen Marvis Bay.
Ex: In any event, ["Cognizer" I] ["Time" still] GO BACK AND FORTH ["Issue" on what I want to do].
Ex: ["Cognizer" He] was firm in his beliefs, ["Time" never] WAFFLED ["Option_1" from one platform] ["Option_2" to another] and was always harshly clear in his stance.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Upper management] WAFFLED ["Issue" whether Fletcher fit their salary structure].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the person who repeatedly changes their mind about which of the Options to choose.
Ex: ["Cog" I] WENT BACK AND FORTH over whether to post it or not, but the fact is that this blog is as much for you as it is for me.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which it logically follows that the Cognizer keeps changing their mind about the Issue.
Ex: The arbitrator WAVERED on the issue ["exp" because of the consequences of such a decision on the worker's employment status].

fe.name: Options
fe.definition:
The Options are the alternative courses of action or the alternative physical or concrete entities that the Cognizer can choose from.
Ex: In the late 1890s Carnegie VACILLATED ["Options" between wanting to dominate the steel industry and wanting to sell out].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies thePlace where the Cognizer keeps changing their mind between the Options that present themselves.
Ex: Do they know better than us that our DITHERING ["Place" at the UN] gave Saddam time to hide, destroy, and shuffle his weapons programs?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE denotes the Time interval during which the Cognizer keeps changing their mind about which of the Options to select.
Ex: Here, however, the Romeros had provided some assurance to Ryan's mother of care, although the court ["Time" later] WAFFLED upon how much supervision was guaranteed

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the selecting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of the Cognizer that also affect the action.
Ex: American allies like Italy and Greece ["Manner" nervously] VACILLATED on their support for the bombing

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition:
The Issue is a question about a course of action or a choice between items.
Ex: Editors GO BACK AND FORTH on a daily basis ["Issue" about what gets in the paper].

fe.name: Option_1
fe.definition:
When there is an explicitly separate construal of the Options, Option_1 is the first-mentioned alternative, typically in the form of a from-PP. When it is clear that the Cognizer actually acted on their choice, Option_1 is the alternative they embraced first before pursuing Option_2.
Ex: You've WAFFLED ["op1" from one explanation] to another.

fe.name: Option_2
fe.definition:
When there is an explicitly separate construal of the Options, Option_2 is the second-mentioned alternative, typically in the form of a to-PP. When it is clear that the Cognizer actually acted on their choice, Option_2 is the alternative they embraced after abandoning Option_1.
Ex: The heroine WAFFLED from one plan ["op2" to another] and all of them were way out in "left field".

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
In the cases where the Cognizer does not act on their choice, the Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cognizer's deliberations to the end. In situations where the Cognizer does act on the Options, the Duration denotes the length of the interval during which the Cognizer repeatly changes from one option to the other.
Ex: Jack WAVERED ["dur" for about six months].

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE describes the number of times within a given period that the Cognizer wavers.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Cognizer wavers.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: waver.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be unable to firmly settle on one of several options

lexunit.name: vacillate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: waver between different opinions or actions.

lexunit.name: waffle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: fail to make up one's mind.

lexunit.name: go back and forth.v
lexunit.definition: FN: waver between

lexunit.name: flip-flop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make an abrupt reversal of policy.

lexunit.name: dither.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be indecisive.

frame.name: Actually_occurring_entity
frame.definition:
Against the background of a contextually salient non-real world, for instance a hypothetical, imagined, simulated, expected, projected, or dream world, an Instance of a Type encountered in a relation or event in the real world is presented as being different from the instance found in the non-real world. Of course, the real-world Instance of the expected Type may also be presented as not occurring, as in the last example below.
Ex: ACTUAL ["Type" results] may vary. Ex: ["ins" ACTUAL results] may vary.
Ex: Also present is the ACTUAL ["Type" policeman], now 20 years older and helping to cast and prepare the young actor who'll be portraying him onscreen. Ex: Also present is ["ins" the ACTUAL policeman], now 20 years older and helping to cast and prepare the young actor who'll be portraying him onscreen.
Ex: Of course, an ACTUAL ["Type" car] with all these capabilities simply did not exist. Ex: Of course, ["ins" an ACTUAL car] with all these capabilities simply did not exist.

fe.name: Instance
fe.definition:
The real-world individual--a concrete or abstract thing or an event--which differs from its counterpart in a discourse-salient non-real world.
Ex: In May of 1994, FBI agents working for Mr. Fiske interviewed Mrs. Foster, showed her ["ins" an ACTUAL gun], not a photo, and asked her if she could identify the gun.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
A kind of entity, instances of which are expected to occur in both the real and the non-real world.
Ex: His ACTUAL ["Type" name] was Nabu-Kudurri-Usur.

lexunit.name: actual.a
lexunit.definition: COD: existing in fact.

frame.name: Rashness
frame.definition:
A Protagonist performs some Action without fully considering the circumstances under which he or she acts, or the possibly (negative) consequences of the Action. Alternatively, the Action itself may be portrayed as having been performed under rushed circumstances.
Ex: Would it _be_ a little IMPATIENT ["pro" of me] ["act" to ask when an album might appear]? Ex: He was quick to move, alert and forceful, as ["pro" he] _was_ IMPETUOUS ["act" in attacking an enemy]

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The Protagonist acts or is apt to act with some degree of consideration regarding the circumstances and possible consequences of an Action he or she may perform.
Ex: I feel that most do, but typically ["pro" people] _are_ RASH, and often reach anger and hostility quickly. Ex: I think it _was_ PATIENT ["pro" of me] ["act" to wait another month].

fe.name: Action
fe.definition:
The Action is carried out by the Protagonist with or without regard for the circumstances under which it is performed or consideration of possible consequences.
Ex: ["act" What he did] _was_ IMPETUOUS and quite irrational - some might say ill-considered. Ex: Caryn thinks Tom made a RASH ["act" choice] by electing to move to the new camp.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The period of time when the Protagonist acts with (or without) consideration regarding an Action.
Ex: _Were_ n't you IMPETUOUS ["tim" when you were young]?

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Action of the Protagonist deviates from the expected in its rashness.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

lexunit.name: rash.a
lexunit.definition: COD: acting or done impetuously, without careful consideration.

lexunit.name: impatient.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having or showing a lack of patience or tolerance.

lexunit.name: impetuous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: acting or done quickly and rashly.

lexunit.name: patient.a
lexunit.definition: FN: acting without haste, with reasonable consideration.

lexunit.name: precipitate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: done, acting, or occurring suddenly or without careful consideration.

lexunit.name: precipitous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: acting with undue haste.

frame.name: Proper_reference
frame.definition:
A speaker marks explicity that he intends to describe an Entity in a more restricted sense than it was used in the immediately preceding discourse, and that therefore his Intended_referent is different from the one that the hearer might have picked out based on the way the Entity label was previously used.
Ex: Of these, nowadays there are 308 within the ["Entity" city] PROPER, and 534 if suburbs are included. Ex: Of these, nowadays there are 308 within ["Intended_referent" the city PROPER], and 534 if suburbs are included.
Ex: The writing in the WSJ is always excellent, with the majority of its writing staff located in ["Entity" New York] PROPER. Ex: The writing in the WSJ is always excellent, with the majority of its writing staff located in ["Intended_referent" New York PROPER].
Ex: Israel Radio said Israel would turn over the ["Entity" town] ITSELF, while agreeing to resume discussions over the surrounding villages in two weeks. Ex: Israel Radio said Israel would turn over ["Intended_referent" the town ITSELF], while agreeing to resume discussions over the surrounding villages in two weeks.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The name of a particular entity that otherwise might be interpreted as having a broader reference.
Ex: Private quarters are in the ["Entity" tower] PROPER with a chapel at the very top

fe.name: Intended_referent
fe.definition:
The entity that the speaker intends to refer to using the Entity in a more restricted sense. The Intended_referent is typically a part of the referent that the hearer might have identified based on the broader use of the Entity.
Ex: The gatehouse providing entry from the outer defences to ["int" the Castle PROPER] was erected by King James III and originally formed part of a splendid fore-front .

lexunit.name: proper.a
lexunit.definition: COD: strictly so called

lexunit.name: self.n
lexunit.definition: FN: used to emphasize a particular thing, person, or group already mentioned.

frame.name: Adopt_selection
frame.definition:
An Agent has an Attribute which can take different Values, and the Agent selects and then begins to use some Value for that Attribute. The Attribute includes both physical (shape, color) and abstract (belief, practice) types. For some LUs in this frame, it is common for only the Value to be expressed, with the Attribute implicit. (Often this implicit attribute can be given second-layer expression on the Value. Note that such second-layer annotation should be assumed in the first two examples below.)
Ex: ["age" They] scoff at their opponents and ASSUME ["val" an air of superior knowledge] Ex: There are times when ["age" teachers] should ADOPT ["val" a neutral stance] in discussion of morally controversial issues. Ex: A person does not have to make the statement "["age" I] ADOPT ["val" this] ["att" as my position]" to do so.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent selects a Value for his/her Attribute and begins to use it.
Ex: ["age" Some organizations, like the Sierra Club], have ADOPTED a position of neutrality on US immigration policies.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The Attribute of the Agent can take on several Values, selected by the Agent.
Ex: The Council of Constance (1414-18) ADOPTED conciliarism ["att" as a stance], hoping that it would permit the election of a pope acceptable to both Catholic factions.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
The Value, chosen and made effective by the Agent, specifies the Attribute.
Ex: He crammed his cap back again into his pocket and re-entered the office, ASSUMING ["val" an air of absentmindedness].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period when the Agent selects and begins to put into effect the Value.
Ex: ["tim" On January 1, 2001], our nation will ADOPT the US dollar as our official currency.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the adoption of a position which is not classified under more specific descriptions, including comparisons to other events (_similarly_), rates of adoption (_slowly_), and descriptions of the Agent which also influence the action (_eagerly_).
Ex: Israel has ["man" reluctantly] ADOPTED a non-violent defensive measure to protect its citizens from death.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent adopts the Value of the Attribute.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: This FE identifies the role filled by a particular participant of the clause headed by the target. In so doing, it relates the state of affairs evoked by the target to another background state of affairs by indicating that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills a second kind of role in the background, either generically or in some specific instance.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent has the Attribute which can take different Value.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

fe.name: Particular iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which an Agent adopts a Value for an Attribute.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The instument through which an Agent adopts a Value for an Attribute.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modified the target to indicate the legal- or "by rule" domain within which it is true or operational. This legal domain is in contrast to the reality, which may or may not reflect the ?official? state-of-affairs.

lexunit.name: adopt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: choose to take up or follow (an option or course of action).

lexunit.name: assume.v
lexunit.definition: FN: begin to use or take on some characteristic.

lexunit.name: embrace.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accept or support (a belief or change) willingly.

frame.name: Information
frame.definition:
A Cognizer knows or comes to know some piece of Information about a Topic. In this frame, many LUs encode a specific Means_of_Gathering and/or Source, but these may also be expressed separately.
Ex: Also, the big problem is that ["cog" our] ["inf" INTEL] ["top" about WMD's] has many times been wrong.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Anyone] _got_ the ["inf" STRAIGHT DOPE] ["Topic" on this]?
Ex: _Get_ the ["Source" inside] ["inf" SCOOP] ["Topic" on sprint football player Austin Wilson]. ["Cognizer" CNI]
Ex: I know him pretty well and ["Cognizer" I] _have_ a lot of ["inf" DIRT] ["Topic" on him] so I can always hold him over a barrel.
Ex: ["inf" What]_'s_ the INFO ["Topic" about the new scanner chip]? ["Cognizer" INI]

fe.name: Information
fe.definition:
The Information that the Cognizer possesses or comes to posess.
Ex: Not long before Bill Marlin died, he shared with me his INFORMATION ["inf" that Mrs Wright was with her husband on the day Wright was born].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is aware of the Information.
Ex: ["cog" Our] INFORMATION shows that soon after the turn of the 1900's, John Dazey was making can openers in the Dallas Texas area at the time.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is what the Information is about in general.
Ex: What happens to ["Topic" my] INFORMATION if I quit my membership?

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Cognizer obtains the Information from the Source.
Ex: How credible is the INFORMATION ["Source" from the Internet]?

fe.name: Means_of_Gathering
fe.definition:
An action or method used by the Cognizer that results in the acquisition of the Information.
Ex: Who can see and use ["Mea" survey] INFORMATION?

lexunit.name: information.n
lexunit.definition: COD: facts or knowledge provided or learned as a result of research or study.

lexunit.name: intelligence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: politically or militarily valuable information, often gathered by covert means.

lexunit.name: intel.n
lexunit.definition: FN: information gathered by covert means; intelligence.

lexunit.name: dirt.n
lexunit.definition: COD: scandalous or sordid information or material.

lexunit.name: scoop.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the latest news.

lexunit.name: dope.n
lexunit.definition: COD: information.

lexunit.name: straight dope.n
lexunit.definition: FN: reliable, inside information.

lexunit.name: data.n
lexunit.definition: COD: facts and statistics used for reference or analysis.

lexunit.name: info.n
lexunit.definition: COD: short for information.

lexunit.name: skinny.n
lexunit.definition: COD: confidential information or gossip.

lexunit.name: details.n
lexunit.definition: FN: specific information

frame.name: Path_travelled
frame.definition:
A Path, a series of connected locations, is traversed by a Theme, moving under its own power or under the influence of a physical force. The Path may be described in various terms depending on whether it is bounded or not. If it is bounded, the Path may be identified by its Endpoints, which may be presented separately as Source and Goal.
Ex: For Earth, these perturbations slowly change the eccentricity of ["Theme" the planet's] ["Path" ORBIT] ["Landmark" around the Sun].
Ex: From the eyewitness accounts, as well as satellite data, videos and photos, Brown and his team have worked out ["Theme" the meteor's] ["pat" PATH] ["Ground" through space].
Ex: Its period around Saturn is just under one Earth day, meaning that it really barrels along, to cover its ["Length" 700,000 mile] ["pat" ORBIT] in such a short time.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The series of interconnected locations that the Theme traverses.
Ex: In insects, blood is confined to vessels during only a portion of its ["pat" CIRCUIT] through the body.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The Source is one of the Endpoints treated as a source.
Ex: The Cassini spacecraft will travel 3.5 billion kilometers (2.175 billion miles) along its PATH ["Src" from Earth] to Saturn.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is the endpoint of the Path.
Ex: The Cassini spacecraft will travel 3.5 billion kilometers (2.175 billion miles) along its PATH from Earth ["Goal" to Saturn].

fe.name: Endpoints
fe.definition:
The Endpoints are two (or more) named endpoints of the Path.
Ex: This Pacific typhoon traveled far inland, knocking down everything in its PATH ["Endpoints" between Los Angeles and Denver].

fe.name: Characteristic
fe.definition:
The Characteristic is a characteristic(s) of the Path.
Ex: Unlike Hubble, Compton was not designed to be serviced by astronauts in its ["Char" 270 mile] ORBIT.

fe.name: Landmark
fe.definition:
An entity relative to which the Theme moves on its Path .
Ex: Lenny killed at least nine people and caused millions of dollars in damage on its COURSE ["Landmark" past 16 Caribbean islands].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The Direction is the direction or directions the Path runs.
Ex: There was huge relief that Hurricane Emily's projected ["Dir" westward] PATH across the Caribbean is likely to track to the south of oil and gas fields.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
A setting location through which the Path goes.
Ex: Hurrican Dennis was blamed for five deaths in Florida and Georgia -- but was much more brutal in its PATH ["gro" across the Caribbean].

fe.name: Length
fe.definition:
The Length is the distance the Path extends.
Ex: The bolt traveled smoothly in its ["Length" short] PATH through the air to Santa.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The moving object whose motion describes the Path.
Ex: The thick white line shows ["the" the army's] PATH from Uzbekistan through Iran, Iraq, Palestine, and into Italy.

lexunit.name: orbit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the regularly repeated elliptical course of a celestial object or spacecraft about a star or planet.

lexunit.name: course.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the route or direction followed by a ship, aircraft, road, or river

lexunit.name: circuit.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a course around the periphery of a location

lexunit.name: path.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the direction in which a person or thing moves.

frame.name: Continued_state_of_affairs
frame.definition:
A State_of_affairs has held and continues to hold up to the Reference_occasion.
Ex: ["ref" TO DATE], ["soa" the Department already has numerous requests for new systems to be developed].
Ex: ["soa" SAGE has no activities planned] ["ref" AS OF YET].
Ex: PBGC guarantees the benefit ["soa" that you had earned] UP TO ["ref" the date of plan termination]
Ex: I think that ["soa" she 's] ["ref" STILL] ["soa" in her office] .

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
A state which holds prior to and up through the Reference_occasion.
Ex: ["soa" How is your course going] SO FAR?

fe.name: Reference_occasion
fe.definition:
The time or event (normally speech time) with respect to which the State_of_affairs is located.
Ex: She was loving and concerned about others UP TO ["ref" her dying breath].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: so far.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: up to this time.

lexunit.name: to date.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: until now.

lexunit.name: up to.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: until and possibly beyond

lexunit.name: as yet.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: until now or that time

lexunit.name: as of yet.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: until and (possibly) beyond now or that time

lexunit.name: still.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: even now or at a particular time

frame.name: Extreme_value
frame.definition:
An Entity possesses a Value for a certain Attribute which is extreme when compared to the values either of other entities or to values of the same Entity at other points of time.
Ex: ["Entity" Airfares] _hit_ a ["Period" 10-year] ["Value" LOW] today. ["Attribute" DNI]
Ex: ["Period" Today's] ["Attribute" temperature] HIGH _was_ ["Value" 71F], and the low was 50F. ["Entity" INI]
Ex: ["Entity" The index] hit a ["Period" post crash] HIGH ["Value" of 2,423.9]. ["Attribute" DNI]
Ex: By 1972, ["Entity" the campus] had _reached_ a historic ["Attribute" enrollment] HIGH ["Value" of 6,300].
Ex: So, right after the company's IPO, you happily bought at the HIGH ["Value" of $14 per share], because you believed they were the first player into this market? ["Attribute" DNI] ["Entity" INI]
Ex: We are currently expecting a ["Attribute" price] ["Value" LOW] associated with the 9-Month (40-Week) Cycle. ["Entity" INI]
Ex: The ["Entity" Swiss] LOW ["Value" of 5.8 percent in 1999] was followed by a high of 12.6 percent in 2001. ["Attribute" DNI]

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity whose Value of a particular gradable Attribute is extreme.
Ex: ["Entity" JetBlue's] HIGH of $55.15 was reached on May 6

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.
Ex: East Harlem reached its historic ["Attribute" population] HIGH of 210000 in 1950.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.
Ex: The state of Michigan reported a new unemployment HIGH ["Value" of 7%].

fe.name: Period
fe.definition:
The period for which values of a particular Attribute of one or more entities are compared.
Ex: Food stamp error rates are at an ["Period" all-time] LOW.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The Domain for which there is a Value of an Attribute of an Entity.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characterization of some property of the Extreme_value.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason for which the Extreme_value event occurs.

lexunit.name: high.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a high point, level, or figure.

lexunit.name: low.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a low point, level or figure.

lexunit.name: acme.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the highest point of achievement or excellence.

lexunit.name: maximum.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the greatest amount, extent, or intensity possible or recorded.

lexunit.name: maximum.a
lexunit.definition: COD: greatest in amount, extent, or intensity.

lexunit.name: minimum.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the least or smallest amount, extent, or intensity possible or recorded.

lexunit.name: minimum.a
lexunit.definition: COD: smallest or lowest in amount, extent, or intensity.

frame.name: Familiarity
frame.definition:
An Entity is presented as having been seen or experienced by a (typically generic and backgrounded) Cognizer on a certain number of occasions, causing the Entity to have a certain degree of recognizability for the Cognizer.
Ex: ["Entity" Susanna Fulton's work] _is_ NEW ["Cognizer" to me].
Ex: ["Entity" Two of these frames] _were_ NEW ["cog" to me] ["Role" as a beginning professor].
Ex: ["ent" This] _was_ ["deg" as] NEW ["cog" to him] ["deg" as the rest of the outcity].
Ex: ["ent" JSON] _is_ ["deg" fairly] NEW ["cog" to me] ["Role" as a data format].
Ex: Moreover, ["Entity" this way of describing and categorizing architecture] _is_ FAMILIAR ["Cognizer" to most people].
Ex: ["Entity" Coronaviruses] _are_ not UNFAMILIAR ["Cognizer" to the epidemiological world].
Ex: Abbey Stadium will bring us into contact with one FAMILIAR ["Entity" face] at least.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
A concrete thing or abstract phenomenon or fact that is assessed in terms of how well recognizable it is to a Cognizer.
Ex: He gave ["ent" an address] quite FAMILIAR to the chauffeur.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The (typically non-specific and backgrounded) sentient being for whom the Entity possesses a specified level of recognizability.
Ex: The information used to illustrate the concept is FAMILIAR ["Cognizer" to the reader].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The deviation of the actual level of recognizability of the Entity from the level specified by the target.
Ex: He gave an address ["Degree" quite] FAMILIAR to the chauffeur.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the role filled by a particular participant of the clause headed by the target. In so doing, it relates the specification of a level of familiarity to another background state of affairs by indicating that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills a second kind of role in the background, either generically or in some specific instance.
Ex: I wanted to go with what was FAMILIAR to me ["Role" as an artist].

lexunit.name: familiar.a
lexunit.definition: COD: well known

lexunit.name: unfamiliar.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not known or recognized; uncharacteristic

lexunit.name: new.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unfamiliar or strange to

lexunit.name: know.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be familiar or friendly with.

lexunit.name: acquainted.a
lexunit.definition: COD: know personally.

lexunit.name: ken.n
lexunit.definition: COD: one's range of knowledge or sight.

lexunit.name: intimate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: closely acquainted; familiar.

frame.name: Fastener
frame.definition:
The Fastener is an artifact created to close a Container (e.g. coat, jar). Sometimes, the Container_portal rather than the Container is expressed.
Ex: The ["cop" door] ["Fastener" SEAL] prevented air from getting in and the kids' screams from getting out.
Ex: She has an ["Time_of_creation" antique] ["Material" ivory] Fastener at the front and another vintage button on her apron.
Ex: NIST designed a ["Type" high pressure] ["Fastener" SEAL] ["Use" for the extension sleeve] using a series of metal washers to load the window under pressure.

fe.name: Container
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the item that is closed with the Fastener.
Ex: On Friday night, many men will simply elect to remove their tie and unbutton their top ["con" shirt] BUTTON.

fe.name: Fastener
fe.definition:
The artifact created to close a Container.
Ex: Man, I have just bought the exact same belt ["Fastener" BUCKLE] and it won't open.

fe.name: Container_portal
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the active zone of the container where the Fastener is located.
Ex: We couldn't close the ["Container_portal" tent flap] ZIPPER and a lot of flies came in .

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
This FE identifes the material from which the Fastener is made.
Ex: It has a matching fabric back strap with a ["mat" metal] BUCKLE and grommet.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Fastener.
Ex: So, he?s standing there in the dirt road in his slacks and black dress shoes, gut over a ["des" big] ["des" stupid] BUCKLE and his short sleeve shirt and his tie all messed up.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
An individual or individuals that bring the Fastener into existence.
Ex: We have 3 vintage ["crea" Levi Strauss] BUCKLES for sale.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which the Fastener comes into existence.
Ex: This is a ["tim" 1960s] BUCKLE made by Diablo Silversmiths.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The term used to refer to the Fastener.
Ex: Our popular ["nam" Essex] BUCKLE is combined with this Laurel terminal to make an elegant set.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
An indication of the subtype of the Fastener.
Ex: A flap portion is foldable over the ["typ" Ziploc] SEAL, secured in the closed position by a snap closure.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Fastener is made.
Ex: The unit has an adjustable diagonal ZIPPER ["use" for heat control].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When an interaction with the Sent_item occurs.
Ex: Finally, ["Time" today's] MAIL contained yet another book by the same author.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place in which the Sent_item is located.
Ex: After that, I notice the MAIL ["Place" on the table].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any characterizations or evaluations of the the Sent_item that introduce another frame, in which the Sent_item figures.
Ex: A cat could have kittens before the ["des" stupid] SHIPMENT rolled in.

lexunit.name: mail.n
lexunit.definition: COD: letters and parcels sent by post.

lexunit.name: post.n
lexunit.definition: COD: letters and parcels delivered.

lexunit.name: shipment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a consignment of goods shipped.

frame.name: System
frame.definition:
A Complex with a particular Function is formed out of Component_entities. The function may be expressed by reference to a Salient_entity involved in the working of the Complex.
Ex: ["pos" The body's] ["fun" immune] ["plx" SYSTEM] can be mobilized against cancer.
Ex: The ["com" sewer] ["plx" SYSTEM] carries wastewater from homes and businesses to the Water Pollution Control Plant for treatment.

fe.name: Component_entities
fe.definition:
The entities that function together as a unit.
Ex: The people of Bangkok had the opportunity to experience the long awaited underground ["com" train] SYSTEM.

fe.name: Complex
fe.definition:
The unit formed by the Component_entities.
Ex: The DeKalb County School ["plx" SYSTEM] cordially invites you to attend the Ground Breaking Ceremony for Peachtree Middle School.

fe.name: Function
fe.definition:
The activity that the Complex entity performs by virtue of its Component_entities interacting.
Ex: These cells form part of the ["fun" immune] SYSTEM and help to prevent the body from getting diseases .

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any characterization or evaluation of the Complex.
Ex: Kwame Kilpatrick is taking a hard look at Detroit's ["des" highly inefficient] bus SYSTEM.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
A person or organization that possesses or owns the Complex or a larger entity of which the Complex itself is a part.
Ex: ["pos" China's] transportation SYSTEM has undergone profound changes in recent years.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition:
The kind of entity that the Complex operates on as part of its Function.
Ex: The lifespan of a central ["sal" sewage] SYSTEM is about 80 years.

lexunit.name: system.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a complex whole; a set of things working together as a mechanism or interconnecting network.

lexunit.name: complex.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an interlinked system; a network.

lexunit.name: cascade.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a succession of devices or stages in a process, each of which triggers or initiates the next.

frame.name: Network
frame.definition:
A set of entities of the same or similar types (Nodes) are linked to each other by Connections to form a Network allowing for the flow of information, resources, etc.
Ex: For the most part, ["net" the Interstate System] _is_ a ["des" connected] NETWORK ["Connections" of highways] bounded by the Canadian and Mexican borders, the Gulf of Mexico, and the Atlantic.
Ex: Through ["pos" our] ["des" worldwide] ["net" NETWORK] ["Nodes" of representatives and agents], Lozenger Inc. was able to serve customers in countries around the globe.

fe.name: Network
fe.definition:
The system functioning as a unit that is constituted by the Nodes and Connections.
Ex: Efforts are underway to improve the road ["net" NETWORK] in the state.

fe.name: Nodes
fe.definition:
The entities that are connected into a Network.
Ex: The National NETWORK ["nod" of Libraries of Medicine] is dedicated to making the world's biomedical information available throughout the US.

fe.name: Connections
fe.definition:
The relationships or physical entities that connect the Nodes.
Ex: Every computer has its own cable to be connected straight to the server or by the NETWORK ["con" of cables and T-connectors].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any characterization or evaluation of the Network.
Ex: But its ability to deliver these programs was severely compromised by its ["des" outdated] computer NETWORK.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
A person or organization that possesses or owns the Network or a larger entity of which the Network itself is a part.
Ex: This file-swapping activity on ["pos" a company's] computer NETWORK exposes a company to legal risk.

lexunit.name: network.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a system of entites of the same type interconnected for the purpose of exchange

lexunit.name: web.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a complex system of interconnected elements.

frame.name: Disgraceful_situation
frame.definition:
An implicit cognizer judges that a particular State_of_affairs for which a Protagonist is responsible is socially unacceptable.
Ex: He called it a DISGRACEFUL ["soa" situation]. ["Protagonist" INI]
Ex: To my mind it was undoubtedly the ["deg" most utterly] SHAMEFUL ["soa" act the chess world had witnessed since 1485]. ["Protagonist" INI]
Ex: It is not at all SHAMEFUL ["pro" for a man] ["soa" to allow himself to be ruled by others].
Ex: We are grateful to Mr. Mattick for bringing this DISGRACEFUL ["soa" building] and its vile nuisance to the attention of the Henley District . ["Protagonist" INI]
Ex: ["soa" That comparison] _is_ SHAMEFUL ["exp" because it is comparing apples and oranges]. ["Protagonist" INI]

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
The entity or event which brings disgrace upon the Protagonist.
Ex: You will soon learn the penalty for your DISGRACEFUL ["soa" conduct].

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The person or organization responsible for the occurrence of the State_of_affairs.
Ex: It is DISGRACEFUL ["pro" to our Public Works Department].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the State_of_affairs diverges from the social norm for things of its kind.
Ex: "This is ["deg" absolutely] DISGRACEFUL," she said .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the judgment of disgrace logically follows.
Ex: And Harvard's policy is SHAMEFUL ["exp" because it insults the memory and the principles of American patriotism at the very birthplace of American patriotism].

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

lexunit.name: disgraceful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: shockingly unacceptable.

lexunit.name: shameful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: worthy of or causing shame.

frame.name: Rejuvenation
frame.definition:
The action of an Agent or the occurrence of a Cause event returns an Entity to an earlier state of vigor and strength.
Ex: ["Cause" Falling prices and wireless connectivity] have BREATHED NEW LIFE ["Entity" into the PDA market].
Ex: While ["Agent" Paul Reubens] RESUSCITATES ["Entity" his career], Pee-wee fans use the Web to keep the 'adventure' alive.
Ex: ["Entity" Athens' democracy] was ["eve" unexpectedly] REINVIGORATED ["Cause" by its great defeat].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The concrete or abstract thing that is brought into an earlier state in which it was more effective and powerful.
Ex: The REINVIGORATION ["ent" of the tourism] economy is recognised by many as an ambitious but necessary objective.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent puts the Entity into a state of renewed vigor.
Ex: ["Agt" We] REVITALIZED the Golden Mountaineer Card, and we gave seniors a prescription drug benefit.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the place where the Agent brings about the change in the Entity's state.
Ex: New York's distinction as America's tax cut leader has REVITALIZED the economy ["Place" in every corner of the state].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent brings about the revitalization of the Entity.
Ex: Older neighborhoods throughout the area should be REVITALIZED ["Purp" in order to be retained as neighborhoods having unique identities].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the Agent causes the renewal of the Entity.
Ex: Production was REVITALIZED ["Time" last June].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the action that the Agent performs in order so as to bring about the reinvigoration of the Entity.
Ex: Natalie Cole RESUSCITATED her career ["Means" by recording a posthumous duet with her father on his old hit "Unforgettable"].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).
Ex: They assessed the effectiveness of four different species of native trees for ["Mnr" rapid] REJUVENATION of the mined land.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain within which the Entity is affected.
Ex: Course wares and websites should be changed and RENEWED ["dom" creatively] often.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition:
The number of times that an Entity is caused to return to a more effective state.
Ex: Ancient Egypt twice fell into a similar state of decrepitude, and was ["ite" twice] REJUVENATED and suffused with energy and artistic creativeness.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event or state whose occurrence brings about the Entity's return to a vigorous state.
Ex: Rock has been REJUVENATED creatively and commercially ["cau" by hip-hop-inspired rock acts].

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition:
This FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole, either appraisals of the event, or descriptions of the rejuvenation event as role fillers in other frames.
Ex: Blair's career was ["eve" miraculously] REVITALIZED, personal liberties were compromised, and the global neocon war-agenda moved forward.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The device used by the Agent to help accomplish the action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Role is used for the capacity in which the Entity is Rejuvinated, and is expressed in _as_-PPs.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The end state of the Rejuvination action.

lexunit.name: rejuvenation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of making younger or more vital

lexunit.name: revitalize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: imbue with new life and vitality.

lexunit.name: revitalization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of imbuing with new life and vitality.

lexunit.name: rejuvenate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make or cause to appear younger or more vital.

lexunit.name: refresh.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give new strength or energy to.

lexunit.name: reinvigorate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give new energy or strength to.

lexunit.name: reinvigoration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of giving new energy or strength to.

lexunit.name: breathe new life.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reinvigorate

lexunit.name: breathe fresh life.v
lexunit.definition: FN: reinvigorate

lexunit.name: resuscitate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make active or vigorous again.

lexunit.name: reawaken.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cause to be alert and active again

lexunit.name: resuscitation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of making active or vigorous again.

lexunit.name: renew.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give fresh life or strength to.

lexunit.name: invigorate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give strength or energy to.

lexunit.name: revival.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an improvement in the condition or strength of something.

lexunit.name: restore.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to bring something back to its original condition

frame.name: Recording
frame.definition:
An Agent sets down in permanent form information about the occurrence of a Phenomenon. Alternatively, the Agent records that an Entity had a particular Value for one of its Attributes.
Ex: ["Time" While visiting in Port Alberni, the day before he was diagnosed,] ["Agent" we] RECORDED ["Phenomenon" him] ["Phenomenon" to have 14 drinks and go to the bathroom 10 times].
Ex: ["Phenomenon" William Hickey's death] is not RECORDED. ["Agent" CNI]
Ex: ["Attribute" The voter turnout] was RECORDED ["Value" as over 90 percent]. ["age" CNI] Ex: The ["Entity" voter] turnout was RECORDED as over 90 per cent .
Ex: ["Phen" A number of US expressions of alarm presented during those weeks to the Israeli government] were REGISTERED ["med" in the premier's diary]. ["age" CNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the sentient entity that creates a permanent record of the Phenomenon.
Ex: Police informed Mr Wong that ["age" they] RECORDED the attack as a racial incident.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
The Phenomenon is the entity or situation in the world of which a Agent becomes aware.
Ex: Adams took some very good advice and meticulously RECORDED ["Phen" the events that ensued].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifes the action whereby the Agent creates a record of the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent creates the record of the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The goal that the Agent has in mind in creating a record of the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Agent uses an Instrument in order to create a record of the Phenomenon or to measure an Entity's Value for a specified Attribute.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
That feature of the Entity which is under discussion.
Ex: When Mohammed was sentenced to death in the Anti-Terrorism Court in Rawalpindi the court RECORDED ["Attribute" his age] as 17 or 18.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition:
The value of the Entity that is recorded for the specified Attribute.
Ex: In the fiscal year 2000, Nepal's imports from China and Tibet were RECORDED ["Value" at 166.6 million dollars].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
An entity for which the Agent records the Value of an Attribute.
Ex: At the time the Army RECORDED ["ent" him] as a married resident of the Town of Two Creeks.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the physical entity in which the Agent creates a record of their impression of the Phenomenon.
Ex: In fact, Pepys RECORDED everything ["med" in his diary].

fe.name: Language
fe.definition:
The symbolic system used by the Agent.
Ex: I RECORDED my notes ["med" in English], usually translating from French.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Agent sets down the facts.
Ex: From what the book says, these events were RECORDED ["pla" in the Chamber of Mazarbul] .

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Phenomenon has been documented.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The amount of times the Agent records something per unit of time.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: This FE denotes a duration in which the recording event occurred iteratively.

lexunit.name: record.v
lexunit.definition: COD: state or express officially.

lexunit.name: register.v
lexunit.definition: FN: record

lexunit.name: document.v
lexunit.definition: COD: record in written, photographic, or other form.

lexunit.name: chronicle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: record (a series of events) in a factual and detailed way.

frame.name: Set_of_interrelated_entities
frame.definition:
A group of Component_entities along with their interrelations is viewed as a Complex.
Ex: By definition, no external forces act upon an ["des" isolated] ["plx" SYSTEM] ["com" of particles].
Ex: ["plx" Earth] _is_ a ["des" contained] SYSTEM ["des" which receives energy from the sun].

fe.name: Component_entities
fe.definition:
The entities that function together as a unit.
Ex: How could consciousness arise in a SYSTEM ["com" of matter]?

fe.name: Complex
fe.definition:
The unit formed by the Component_entities.
Ex: An open ["plx" SYSTEM] is any distinct entity -- a cell, a person, a forest, or an orchestra organization -- that takes in resources from its environment, processes them in some way, and produces output.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any characterization or evaluation of the Complex.
Ex: Because the earth is a ["des" closed] SYSTEM, disposing of products at the end of their useful life can waste usable materials.

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition: A person or organization that possesses or owns the Complex or a larger entity of which the Complex itself is a part.

lexunit.name: system.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a group of independent but interacting elements conceived of as a unified whole

frame.name: Expected_location_of_person
frame.definition:
A Person usually resides or works in a Location.
Ex: _Is_ ["Person" Mr. Adams] IN ["tim" today]? ["Location" DNI]

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
The Location is the place of business or residence prototypically occupied by the Person.
Ex: I couldn't access the details of prospective buyers and sellers and was uncontactable when I was OUT ["loc" of the office].

fe.name: Person
fe.definition:
The Person is located in or at a place that they customarily occupy.
Ex: ["per" The doctor] is not IN right now.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Person occupies the Location.
Ex: Call work, tell them you'll be IN ["tim" in the afternoon].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of the time interval during which the Person occupies the Location.
Ex: It's only nine o'clock, so he won't be IN ["dur" for another two hours].

lexunit.name: in.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: present at one's home or office.

lexunit.name: out.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: not at home or one's place of work.

lexunit.name: home.n
lexunit.definition: COD: to or at one's home.

frame.name: Institutionalization
frame.definition:
A Patient is commited to the care of a medical Facility by a proper Authority. Regardless of whether the Patient agrees or does not agree with their placement in the Facility, the Authority judges that it is in the best interest of the Patient or his environment that the Patient receive treatment in the Facility.
Ex: ["Time" Ten years after Abraham Lincoln's assassination], ["aut" a Chicago court] declared his 56-year-old widow Mary insane and COMMITTED ["pat" her] ["fac" to a mental institution].
Ex: ["pat" A pregnant woman] was HOSPITALIZED ["dep" with gunshots to her shoulder and abdomen]. ["aut" CNI] ["fac" INI]
Ex: Arberg issued a two-sentence statement saying ["pat" Rehnquist] was HOSPITALIZED ["aff" for a fever] and undergoing tests. ["aut" CNI] ["fac" INI]
Ex: The HOSPITALIZATION ["pat" of the Saudi king] upset the skittish oil markets. ["aut" INI] ["fac" INI]

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition:
The person who is committed to a facility with a view towards helping them mentally or physically.
Ex: Buffy's got this hospital phobia because her caring parents INSTITUTIONALIZED ["pat" her] for a while before she moved to Sunnydale.

fe.name: Facility
fe.definition:
The facility where the Patient is taken for treatment.
Ex: Unfortunately for Mrs. Lincoln, her son, Robert, INSTITUTIONALIZED her ["fac" in the Batavia Asylum] shortly after the visit to St. Charles.

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition:
The Authority is the actor carrying out the institutionalization with proper legal authorization, either invested into them in general by the government or granted due to power of attorney over the Patient.
Ex: Goodrum then went to see ["aut" a private doctor] ["aut" who] HOSPITALIZED him.

fe.name: Affliction
fe.definition:
The condition exhibited by the Patient, which is deemed to merit institutionalization by the Authority.
Ex: Her parents INSTITUTIONALIZED her ["aff" for what was essentially typical bad adolescent behavior].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the institutionalization happens.
Ex: ["Time" Later] her mother became depressed and was INSTITUTIONALIZED.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose of the institutionalization.
Ex: His squabbling parents would rather INSTITUTIONALIZE him ["pur" to rid themselves of their problem].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Authority that brings about the institutionalization of the Patient.
Ex: Without informing Volkobraun or her attorney of the court's decision, police ["Mns" forcibly] COMMITTED her to a psychiatric hospital.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the institutionalization event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Authority that affect the action (_ruthlessly_).
Ex: St Remy, of course, is most noted for being the place where Van Gogh COMMITTED himself ["man" voluntarily] to an asylum.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the institutionalization event logically follows.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the length of the time period for which the Authority has placed the Patient in the Facility.
Ex: This time, physicians HOSPITALIZED him ["dur" for more than a month].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Facility is situated.
Ex: The widow of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. suffered a stroke on Wednesday, and was HOSPITALIZED ["pla" in Atlanta].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE describes a participant of the institutionalization as being in some state during the action.
Ex: A man was HOSPITALIZED ["dep" in stable condition] after he was mauled by a ?pet? bear.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE marks the amount of times the Patient is committed to the Facility per unit of time.

lexunit.name: institutionalize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: place in a residential institution.

lexunit.name: institutionalization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of placing in a residential institution.

lexunit.name: commit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: send to psychiatric hospital

lexunit.name: commitment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of sending to a psychiatric hospital

lexunit.name: hospitalize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to place in a hospital for treatment

lexunit.name: hospitalization.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of placing in a hospital for treatment

frame.name: Complaining
frame.definition:
A Complainer communicates their negative emotional reaction to some state of affairs in a Complaint. As an alternative to the specific Complaint, the Topic of the speaker's Complaint may be specified.
Ex: The ["Complainer" top US commander in Iraq] COMPLAINED ["Add" to the Pentagon] ["Time" last winter] ["Complaint" that his supply situation was so poor that it threatened Army troops' ability to fight].
Ex: He said ["Complainer" he] will _lodge_ a COMPLAINT ["Add" with the ACCC]. ["Complaint" DNI]
Ex: ["Time" On the rare occasions] ["Complainer" I] COMPLAINED ["Add" to him] ["Topic" about media bias], Peter immediately ordered up a story that included conservative objections to mainstream reports .

fe.name: Complainer
fe.definition:
The Complainer is the sentient entity that produces the Complaint (whether spoken or written).
Ex: ["Complainer" Peter] has MOANED about it on another thread but it sure must be nice for him to wallow again.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee is the person to whom the Complaint is communicated.
Ex: Fresh out of prison, Martin WHINGED ["Add" to Sonia] about his life.

fe.name: Complaint
fe.definition:
The lamentable situation that the Complainer is communicating to the Addressee.
Ex: One observer GROUSED ["com" that Skagway was "little better than hell on earth."]

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the subject matter to which the Complaint pertains.
Ex: Ferdinand attended the reception at the city hall and COMPLAINED vociferously ["Topic" about his reception at the city].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the complaining event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Complainer that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _bitterly_, _vociferoursly_ ).
Ex: The crowd COMPLAINED ["Manr" vociferously] when the other aldermen met Brewer?s proposal with silence.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
Ex: Robert ["fre" always] COMPLAINS to the neighbor whose children step on his flowers and ride bikes on his lawn.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An act whereby the Complainer makes a complaint.
Ex: These people shouldn't be BELLY-ACHING about it ["Mns" by accusing the downfall of their candidate because it was all "whiteys" fault]!

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The emotional or physical state of the Complainer that leads to their complaining.
Ex: 'Oooh,' he MOANED ["Internal_cause" in frustration].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Complainer to transmit the Complaint.
Ex: I don't mean to discount any of what he has BITCHED about ["Medium" in his article], because most of his points are actually valid.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Complainer while making the Complaint.
Ex: ["Dep" Pacing the floor at the American Club and getting increasingly drunk], he LAMENTED, "I want to evacuate but my country won't let me leave."

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the complaint is made.
Ex: Now ["Time" yesterday] I PISSED AND MOANED about Rolling Stone magazines choice for the number 1 song of all time.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The FE specifies the place where the complaining takes place.
Ex: Guest Relations actually refunded the full eighty-five dollar price of the event to many event attendees who COMPLAINED ["Place" at City Hall].

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition:
Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular complaining event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.
Ex: This is the ["par" third] COMPLAINT of a similar nature filed by Naber against CN.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs.

fe.name: Occasion
fe.definition: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes. This often means that the Explanation causes the complaint, but not in all cases. In particular, there are cases when the connection is a bit weaker than normal for causation. In these instances, cause is mediated by some actor responding in a complex way to the situation. Such cases are not paraphrasable in the language of direct causation.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: An event or state which results from the complaining.

lexunit.name: whinge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: complain persistently and peevishly

lexunit.name: whine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: complain in a feeble or petulant way

lexunit.name: complain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express dissatisfaction or annoyance.

lexunit.name: moan.v
lexunit.definition: COD: complain or grumble

lexunit.name: bitch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make malicious or spitefully critical comments.

lexunit.name: complaint.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act or the action of complaining

lexunit.name: grouse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: complain pettily; grumble.

lexunit.name: lament.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express regret or disappointment about.

lexunit.name: gripe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express a trivial complaint; grumble.

lexunit.name: belly-ache.v
lexunit.definition: COD: complain noisily or persistently.

lexunit.name: gripe.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a trivial complaint.

lexunit.name: piss and moan.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to whine or bitch about something in an annoying and persistent manner.

lexunit.name: grumble.v
lexunit.definition: COD: complain or protest in a bad-tempered but muted way

lexunit.name: grousing.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the general act of complaining.

frame.name: Expressing_publicly
frame.definition:
A Communicator publically communicates some difficult-to-express Content which they (or a social group of which they are a member) have had for some time. The Content may not have been previously communicated due to inability or social stricture. In cases where the individuals addressed are a smaller group than the public at large, a separate Addressee may be expressed.
Ex: ["con" Those grievances] can be AIRED ["Time" during Board meetings]. ["com" CNI]
Ex: ["com" Saddam] VOICED ["Content" his joy] ["Time" when he was told Spain's new government had left the US-led military coalition in Iraq].

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition:
The Communicator is the person who expresses the Content (whether spoken or written).
Ex: ["com" Reagan] GAVE VOICE to the innate patriotism of the American people.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee is the person to whom the Content is communicated.
Ex: After waiting 2-hours for his appointment, Kiyosaki VENTED his frustration ["Add" to his rich dad].

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The attitude or feeling that the Communicator had not previously expressed.
Ex: Members AIRED ["con" their grievances] and resented the way higher education was being dealt with.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (_hard_, _softly_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Communicator that also affect the action (_eagerly_).
Ex: The girl's grandfather's body was frail but his ideas were strong and his voice rose as he ["Manr" furiously] EXPRESSED his ideas.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An act whereby the Communicator communicates the Content.
Ex: The students EXPRESSED their gratitude ["Mns" by creating colorful hand-made cards for Annie and Renita].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotional or physical state of the Communicator that leads to their communication.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the observable action or product of the Communicator.
Ex: I do not especially espouse the ideas ARTICULATED by Diana Plesa ["Medium" in her article].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Communicator during the statement.
Ex: Hermann considered her to be a tramp unworthy of the Kafka name, and VENTED his ire ["Dep" with full passion].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Content is communicated.
Ex: Sometimes, children may ["Time" later] PUT INTO WORDS a memory from early life, but not customarily.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The FE specifies the place where the communication takes place.
Ex: John Ryan VOICED concerns ["Place" in Parliament] about the suggestion that somehow the inquiry was not independent.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose is the desired result of public expression.
Ex: Because of its spread of membership , it has retained value as a forum where a wide range of ideas and views can be AIRED ["Pur" for discussion] .

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.
Ex: An important policy matter which has been AIRED ["Frequency" occasionally] in recent years is the size of academic library collections , compared with the amount of use they receive .

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the communication and any of its participants. Quite often, Circumstances secondarily provide an Explanation for the particular communication.
Ex: ["cir" With half the opposition in exile], hardly anyone dared GIVE VOICE to their deep misgivings .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the particular public expression logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the expression, but not in all cases.
Ex: The mute had to VOICE the concerns of her community ["exp" because there was no-one else to do so].

lexunit.name: vent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give free expression to (a strong emotion)

lexunit.name: air.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express (an opinion or grievance) publicly.

lexunit.name: express.v
lexunit.definition: COD: convey (a thought or feeling) in words or by gestures and conduct

lexunit.name: voice.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express in words

lexunit.name: give voice.v
lexunit.definition: FN: express

lexunit.name: expression.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of expressing something.

lexunit.name: articulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: clearly express (an idea or feeling)

lexunit.name: put into words.v
lexunit.definition: FN: express

frame.name: Respond_to_proposal
frame.definition:
A Speaker addresses a Proposal made by an Interlocutor, either agreeing to it or rejecting it. Agreeing entails a social responsibility on the Speaker to bring about some state of affairs encoded in the Proposal.
Ex: ["Interlocutor" They] were REBUFFED ["par" again] ["pla" in the larger city of Provo]. ["Speaker" CNI]
Ex: ["Time" Last month] ["Speaker" Mr Duisenberg] _delivered_ a ["Manner" sharp] REBUFF ["int" to Mr Welteke].
Ex: ["Speaker" He] REBUFFED ["Proposal" Singh's every overture], ["Depict" relentlessly pursuing a cap on India's nuclear capability].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The Speaker is the person who communicates the reply or response.
Ex: ["Speaker" Iran] on Saturday REJECTED Europe's proposal for ending the standoff over Tehran's nuclear program.

fe.name: Interlocutor
fe.definition:
This is the person who made the Proposal to the Speaker and to whom the Speaker communicates their response. This frame element stands in for the Proposal and is only licensed when the Proposal can be understood from the context.
Ex: But senior SLN officials had REBUFFED ["int" the man who is ever so willing to please the guerrillas].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: As with Medium in other Communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed, usually as a PP Complement headed by "on" or "in".

fe.name: Proposal
fe.definition:
The Proposal is the prior communication or action to which a response is given.
Ex: Dr. Carolyn Herrington has ACCEPTED ["pro" our offer to become Dean of the College of Education] .

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_).
Ex: Moreover, as with Surrey, myths have proliferated, such as that Oxford ["Manr" cruelly] REJECTED his wife in 1576.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive phrase describing the Speaker.
Ex: She TURNED it DOWN, ["Depict" unaware she would some day become a member].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Meansby the Speaker responds to the Proposal.
Ex: Others, I would say have actually TURNED me DOWN ["Mns" by not replying and not responding].

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker mental or emotional state.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Speaker makes a verbal response.
Ex: Legislation that would have required smaller school districts to share administrators has been REBUFFED repeatedly ["pla" in the Oklahoma House of Representatives].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.
Ex: This must make ["tim" yesterday's] Taliban REBUFF all the more wounding.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.
Ex: He was asked to join the National Assembly ruling party, but repeatedly TURNED them DOWN ["pur" in order to continue his work as a journalist].

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of response events.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role denotes the capacity in which the Interlocutor is judged.
Ex: The Policy Committee had REJECTED her ["rol" as a candidate for chronic dialysis] because of her young age. .

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: The Group is the set of people within which the Respond_to_proposal is occuring.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.

lexunit.name: turn down.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reject an offer or application of something or from someone.

lexunit.name: rebuff.v
lexunit.definition: COD: reject in an abrupt or ungracious manner.

lexunit.name: rebuff.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an abrupt rejection.

lexunit.name: reject.v
lexunit.definition: COD: refuse to consider or agree to

lexunit.name: accept.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to give a favorable response to

lexunit.name: acceptance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of giving a favorable response

lexunit.name: rejection.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of refusing a proposal by another

lexunit.name: refuse.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to not accept an offer

frame.name: Bragging
frame.definition:
A Speaker talks about a Topic, which may be an action performed by the Speaker or an entity or state of affairs that they are associated with in order to suggest that the Speaker is worthy of admiration. The Speaker may give an explicit Reason why the Topic redounds to their credit. Alternatively, a Message frame element can be used to directly describe what the Speaker says, leaving the more specific Reason for admirability to be inferred. Instead of the Speaker, the action may be attributed metonymically to the Medium, or possibly the Expressor.
Ex:
Ex: ["Speaker" Turkish officials] BOASTED ["Topic" of giving 'tens of thousands of dollars in surreptious payments' to a prominent American politician].
Ex: ["Speaker" He] ["Time" then] VAUNTED ["Topic" his own clan], but failed to mention Emanuel Ungaro, who described the omission as ''lamentable''.
Ex: ["Medium" The press release] BOASTS ["mes" that "a direct connection between the cartridge and the system" means no more having to blow dust out of game cartridges].
Ex: ["Speaker" 70's comics like Chevy Chase and Steve Martin] over-stated their egotism and PREENED ["Topic" over their superiority].

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition:
The Speaker is the person who produces a message about a Topic.
Ex: During the 1990s ["Spkr" Rio Grande Do Sul's governor, Olivio Dutra of the PT,] PREENED about the province's GE-free status.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker communicated a message.
Ex: Sheppard said Turner apparently was backing up his BOAST ["Add" to a bystander] when a patrol officer saw him writing on the sign and arrested him.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is a positively judged entity or state of affairs with which the Speaker is associated and about which they talk.
Ex: Mike Wallace was told that Canseco had BRAGGED ["top" about steroids].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).
Ex: She insulted everyone she spoke to, and BOASTED ["Manner" loudly] about a salary that no one else in the office could ever hope to make.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An act whereby the Speaker makes a boastful statement.
Ex: He BRAGGED about himself ["Mns" by saying: 'I understand the language of the birds.']

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement.
Ex: CNN's Jeff Greenfield BRAGGED ["Medium" on the air] recently that ratings are high.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Speaker during the statement.
Ex: His ["Dep" drunken] BOAST, however, cost him his life.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the statement is made.
Ex: The public does not care, but the media definitely do as Haddock herself BOASTED ["Time" the next morning] on Good Morning America.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.
Ex: 'I'm Pat Crowe,' he BOASTED ["Place" at the police station].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A characteristic of the entity or state of affairs denoted by the Topic which explains why the Speaker is proud of the association with the Topic referent.
Ex: He's not a particularly great one, but he's VAUNTED by the Democrats ["Reason" as the greatest threat to their party], so who are we to argue?

fe.name: Message
fe.definition:
A description of the state of affairs that redounds to the Speaker's credit
Ex: Cosmai BRAGGED ["mes" that Hyundai's latest quality rankings place the automaker on par with Honda and Toyota].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role is used for the capacity in which the Topic entity or state of affairs is judged, and is expressed in _as_-PPs.
Ex: Ricky constantly BRAGGED about his father ["rol" as a musician] but he never had much to say about him as a parent.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
Expressor is the body part or action that conveys the feeling of pride of the Speaker.
Ex: The senator's BOASTFUL ["exp" exaggerations of her academic record at a New Hampshire campaign event]also contributed to her withdrawal.

fe.name: Occasion
fe.definition: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
