fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their speaking.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs.

lexunit.name: brag.v
lexunit.definition: COD: boast

lexunit.name: boast.v
lexunit.definition: COD: talk with excessive pride and self-satisfaction about oneself

lexunit.name: boast.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of boasting.

lexunit.name: preen.v
lexunit.definition: FN: gloat or exult

lexunit.name: rodomontade.v
lexunit.definition: FN: boast pretentiously

lexunit.name: vaunt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: boast about or praise (something), especially excessively.

lexunit.name: boastful.a
lexunit.definition: FN: indicative of pride felt

lexunit.name: rodomontade.n
lexunit.definition: COD: boastful or inflated talk or behaviour

lexunit.name: gripe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express a trivial complaint; grumble

lexunit.name: braggart.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who brags.

frame.name: Agree_or_refuse_to_act
frame.definition: A Speaker either agrees to or refuses to engage in a Proposed_action, proposed by an Interlocutor.

fe.name: Speaker
fe.definition: The Speaker is the person to whom a particular action has been proposed and who responds to the request or offer made.

fe.name: Interlocutor
fe.definition: This is the person who proposed the Proposed_action to the Speaker and to whom the Speaker communicates their response.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: As with Medium in other communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed.

fe.name: Proposed_action
fe.definition: The Proposed_action is an action that the Speaker would perform if they were to accept or refuse the request or offer.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_).

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Speaker.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Meansby which the Speaker responds to the request or offer made.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker mental or emotional state.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location in which the Speaker gives their verbal response to the proposed action.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response concerning the proposed action.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by agreeing or refusing to perform the Proposed_action that is requested of, or suggested to them.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of response events.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
Role denotes the status that the Interlocutor requested to be granted.
Ex: A serious injustice was committed by Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC) when it REFUSED her ["Role" as a political refugee].

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition: This FE identifies the subevent of the agreeing/refusing to act.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times (within a given period) that the agreeing/refusing to act occurs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness, and consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

lexunit.name: refuse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: indicate unwillingness to accept or grant (something offered or requested)

lexunit.name: decline.v
lexunit.definition: COD: politely refuse

lexunit.name: refusal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the action of indicating unwillingness to accept or grant (something offered or requested).

lexunit.name: agree.v
lexunit.definition: COD: consent to do something.

frame.name: Preference
frame.definition:
An Experiencer has a greater desire to participate in some Event, as against another (contextually recoverable) event which exhibits a specific Contrast with the Event. Alternatively, the Experiencer may have a greater desire that some Focal_participant participate in the Event. The Location_of_Event may also be mentioned.
Ex: ["Explanation" Why] do ["Experiencer" women] prefer ["Focal_participant" manly faces]? Ex: ["Experiencer" I] PREFER ["Focal_participant" open source programs] ["Contrast" over proprietary ones]. Ex: ["Experiencer" Other customers] PREFER ["Event" to send us an order together with a cheque]. Ex: ["Experiencer" I] PREFER ["Focal_participant" my tartar sauce] ["Location_of_Event" on fish].

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the Event to occur.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The change that the Experiencer would like to see.

fe.name: Focal_participant
fe.definition: This is the entity that the Experiencer wishes to be affected by some Event.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the extent of the Experiencer's Desiring.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Experiencer desires something.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation shows why the Experiencer wants the Event to occur. This FE occurs frequently as a PP complement headed by _for_.

fe.name: Purpose_of_Event
fe.definition: The Purpose_of_Event is the purpose pertaining to the desired Event.

fe.name: Time_of_Event
fe.definition: The time that the Event would ideally occur.

fe.name: Location_of_Event
fe.definition: The Location_of_Event is the place involved in the desired Event.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Experiencer desires something.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place. Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Experiencer has desired something.

fe.name: Contrast
fe.definition:
An alternative Event or Focal_participant that is less desirable for the Experiencer.
Ex: I always PREFERRED trackballs ["con" over mouses].

lexunit.name: prefer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: like (someone or something) better than another or others; tend to choose.

lexunit.name: disprefer.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to like or tend to choose less.

lexunit.name: favor.v
lexunit.definition: FN: prefer

frame.name: Protecting
frame.definition:
Some Protection prevents a Danger from harming an Asset.
Ex: ["Protection" The rubber on her sneakers] PROTECTED ["Asset" her] ["Danger" from the mud].
Ex: ["Protection" The coral reefs] SHIELDED ["Asset" the coastline] ["Danger" from the worst of the waves].
Ex: ["Protection" A growing number of sustainable farmers] are preserving agricultural variety and PROTECTING ["Asset" biodiversity] ["Means" by raising ?heritage? or ?heirloom? varieties].
Ex: ["Protection" The man responsible for this entire ordeal] ["Event_description" cowardly] SHIELDED ["Asset" himself] ["Danger" from justice] ["Instrument" with the little boy's struggling body].

fe.name: Protection
fe.definition:
The person, entity, or action that prevents harm to an Asset.
Ex: ["pro" The tabloid's deal with the woman] SHIELDED Schwarzenegger.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where the Danger threatened the Asset.
Ex: To make his way on a foreign soil, he needed different guardians from those that PROTECTED him ["Place" in his own birthplace] .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Danger threatens.
Ex: Regardless of the distribution media, USPTO information is SAFEGUARDED ["Time" before, during, and after dissemination] from improper access and modification.

fe.name: Danger
fe.definition:
A situation that could damage the Asset.
Ex: Other nations tended to muffle or modulate their occasional annoyance with the country that was their SHIELD ["Danger" against the Soviet threat].

fe.name: Asset
fe.definition:
Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Protection which might be lost or damaged.
Ex: Almost 10 years later, that agreement INSULATED ["Asset" Microsoft] from liability on copyright claims over the graphical user interface (GUI).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An event involving the Protection that removes the Asset from potential harm through the Danger.
Ex: Jackson SECURED the flank ["mea" by timely charging the enemy and driving him back].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by a volitional agent acting as a Protection which interacts with an undergoer to accomplish the security of the Asset from harm by the Danger.
Ex: Your Brake Pads Parts order is encrypted and SAFEGUARDED ["ins" with the latest SSL technology] for a protected and secure shopping experience!

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the protecting event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (_hard_, _softly_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases of agentive Protection, it may indicate salient characteristics of an agent that also affect the action (_carefully_).
Ex: Finally, I thank all of the curators of all of the museums around the world who have ["man" carefully] PROTECTED the Ivory-billed specimens in their care.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: Tthis FE is used for phrases that describe the protecting event as a whole. It applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. It also applies to descriptions of the protecting event as a role filler in another frame.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A description or characteristic of the Protection.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the act of protecting logically follows.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: FN: This FE denotes the length of time in which the Asset is protected.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: FN: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: FN: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the protecting event.

lexunit.name: protect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep safe from harm or injury.

lexunit.name: shield.v
lexunit.definition: COD: protect from a danger, risk, etc.

lexunit.name: safeguard.v
lexunit.definition: COD: protect with a safeguard.

lexunit.name: insulate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: protect from something unpleasant.

lexunit.name: secure.v
lexunit.definition: COD: protect against threats

lexunit.name: protection_((event)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or state of protecting or being protected.

lexunit.name: protection_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing that protects.

lexunit.name: safeguard.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a measure taken to protect or prevent something.

lexunit.name: shield.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing providing protection

lexunit.name: bulwark.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a strong support or protection

lexunit.name: guard.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to keep watch over some asset

frame.name: Willingness
frame.definition:
A Cognizer would engage in an Activity if asked or otherwise prompted to do so.
Ex: ["Cognizer" The court] _is_ WILLING ["Activity" to depart from the usual range of sentencing] .
Ex: ["Cognizer" The Nicaraguan National Assembly] has _been_ RELUCTANT ["Activity" to destroy the remaining stockpile].
Ex: The Turks are in GRUDGING ["act" acceptance] of terms set by EU.
Ex: Would ["Cognizer" you] _be_ PREPARED["Activity" to give up some of your privacy to industry to help improve customer service]?

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer is the individual that is willing to engage in the Activity.
Ex: ["Cog" My mom] _is_ very LOATH to take any drugs without medical supervision.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition:
The Activity is what the Cognizer would do under certain circumstances.
Ex: Does biology really matter more than a WILLINGNESS ["act" to take an active role in a child's life]?

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the Cognizer's willingness logically follows.
Ex: The other companies would have been UNWILLING to participate ["exp" because of the project's high risk].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies thePlace where the Cognizer is willing to engage in the Activity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer is willing to engage in the Activity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state of affairs that the Cognizer wants to achieve by being willing to engage in the Activity.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of the willingness from the norm or from the value for another Cognizer.
Ex: If you need help or have any problems, she is ["deg" extremely] WILLING to work with you.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE denotes the number of times the Cognizer is willing per some unit of time.

lexunit.name: willing.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not opposed to

lexunit.name: unwilling.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not willing.

lexunit.name: reluctant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unwilling and hesitant.

lexunit.name: willingness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state or degree of being unopposed to

lexunit.name: loath.a
lexunit.definition: COD: reluctant; unwilling:

lexunit.name: grudging.a
lexunit.definition: FN: resentfully unwilling to

lexunit.name: unwillingness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state or degree of being opposed to

lexunit.name: prepared.a
lexunit.definition: FN: willing (as a result of consideration)

frame.name: Board_vehicle
frame.definition:
A Traveller boards a Vehicle that they intend to use as a means of transportation either as a passenger or as a driver.
Ex: On the 5th of December, 1834, ["tra" we] EMBARKED ["Vehicle" on board the merchant ship Hellespont].
Ex: ["Traveller" She] BOARDED ["Vehicle" the train] ["Time" ahead of him].
Ex: ["Time" On 19 September] ["Traveller" the battalion] EMBUSSED and headed southward into the Swordfish training area some 40 miles away.

fe.name: Traveller
fe.definition:
The Traveller is the entity which boards the Vehicle.
Ex: At approximately 07:30 hours ["tra" we] EMPLANED in England and after circling to gather other units that made up the 1st Airborne Army, we headed for the Rhine.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The Vehicle is the intended means of conveyance of the Traveller.
Ex: When he had MOUNTED ["Vehicle" the horse], his armour glittered in the sun, and he looked so brave and handsome.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion outside of or off the Vehicle expresses the frame element Source.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path describes the trajectory of the Traveller's motion onto the Vehicle.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition: The amount of time the Traveller spends on the Vehicle after boarding it.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
The state of the Traveller or Vehicle during the boarding.
Ex: Kate Lawler (no relation) reportedly BOARDED a plane ["Depictive" drunk] after hitting the bar when her flight was delayed for five hours.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the boarding of the Vehicle takes place.
Ex: Therese ENTRAINED ["Time" at 9am on 4 October] for the Brandhoek area. .

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Traveller. This may be an entity the Traveller transports or a co-traveller moving under their own power.
Ex: This woman GOT on the bus ["CT" with a whole gaggle of little children].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Traveller boards the vehicle.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Traveller boards the Vehicle.
Ex: You can GET on the shuttle bus ["pla" at the Bank of America across from the BART station].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: board.v
lexunit.definition: COD: get on or into (a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle).

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: FN: enter or mount a vehicle

lexunit.name: embark.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go on board a ship or aircraft.

lexunit.name: emplane.v
lexunit.definition: FN: go on board an aircraft.

lexunit.name: entrain.v
lexunit.definition: FN: board a train.

lexunit.name: mount.v
lexunit.definition: COD: get up on (an animal or bicycle) in order to ride it.

lexunit.name: hop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: jump on to (a vehicle)

lexunit.name: embarkation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of embarking on a vessel or aircraft

lexunit.name: embarkment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the act of passengers and crew getting aboard a ship or aircraft

lexunit.name: embus.v
lexunit.definition: FN: get on a bus

frame.name: Disembarking
frame.definition:
A Traveller leaves from or dismounts a Vehicle.
Ex: ["tra" The passengers] DISEMBARKED ["pla" in Southampton].
Ex: They then informed the passengers that, if the aircraft were to leave the runway, ["tra" they] would likely be DEPLANING ["Path" through the rear cabin doors].

fe.name: Traveller
fe.definition:
The Traveller is the entity which disembarks from the Vehicle.
Ex: ["tra" We] GOT off at the wrong bus stop.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The Vehicle is the means of conveyance that the Traveller disembarks from.
Ex: The victim stopped the tractor and DISMOUNTED ["Vehicle" from it].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path describes the trajectory of the Traveller's motion off or out of the Vehicle.
Ex: As we GOT off the plane ["Path" via a set of steps] we were immediately guided into a bus.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition: The amount of time the Traveller spends off or outside of the Vehicle after disembarking from it.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Traveller or Vehicle during the disembarking.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the disembarking of the Vehicle takes place.
Ex: ["Time" Yesterday], we ALIGHTED onto this tiny hilly island, site of a Singaporean October festival.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
A theme that leaves the Vehicle together with the main Traveller. This may be an entity the Traveller transports or a co-traveller moving under their own power.
Ex: Many people were waiting for him when he GOT off the ship ["CT" with his wife, Estelita Villafane].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Traveller disembarks from the vehicle.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location in which the Traveller disembarks from the Vehicle.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The location that the Traveller reaches by leaving the Vehicle.
Ex: The driver and the majority of passengers DISMOUNTED ["goa" onto the road] as onlookers quickly formed an unruly squabbling mass.

lexunit.name: disembark.v
lexunit.definition: COD: leave a ship, aircraft, or train

lexunit.name: debark.v
lexunit.definition: COD: leave a ship or aircraft.

lexunit.name: deplane.v
lexunit.definition: COD: disembark from an aircraft.

lexunit.name: detrain.v
lexunit.definition: COD: leave a train, or cause or assist to leave a train.

lexunit.name: dismount.v
lexunit.definition: COD: alight from a horse or bicycle.

lexunit.name: alight.v
lexunit.definition: COD: descend from public transport.

lexunit.name: debus.v
lexunit.definition: FN: alight from a motor vehicle

lexunit.name: disembarkation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of getting off a ship, aircraft, or train

lexunit.name: get.v
lexunit.definition: FN: exit a vehicle

frame.name: Getting_underway
frame.definition:
A Self_mover begins the motion away from a relatively deprofiled Source location. The focus is on the motion rather than on the location that is being departed. The label Self_mover here also includes vehicles that are steered by an intentional agent.
Ex: ["Time" After a lunch of sandwiches on paper plates], ["sel" we] GET UNDER WAY.
Ex: When ["Self_mover" I] GOT GOING ["dur" for the day] I had horrible pain down my buttocks and leg.
Ex: ["Self_mover" We] GOT GOING ["Path" via Tikul] and after a light lunch finally found the pottery place recommended in the guide,
Ex: I'll make this brief, as ["Self_mover" I] need to HEAD OUT ["Goal" for the bookstore] ["Time" in a bit].
Ex: ["Self_mover" The band "Killers"] is HEADING OUT ["Journey" on 25-date tour through Europe and Japan] ["Time" this week].

fe.name: Self_mover
fe.definition:
The Self_mover is the volitional agent that moves.
Ex: ["Self_mover" Tom and I] GOT UNDER WAY in the wee hours of the morning, planning to get to the confluence area between the onsets of nautical and civil twilight.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Source refers to the starting-point of the Self_mover's motion.
Ex: The vessel GOT UNDER WAY ["Source" from San Francisco] on 14 June and completed two round-trips to Manila before the cessation of hostilies.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Path is any description of the Self_mover's trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.
Ex: We can GET GOING ["Path" via Fife]

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Goal is any expression that tells where the Self_mover ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.
Ex: On the 17th, the vessel GOT UNDER WAY ["Goal" for Tarawa, Gilbert Islands].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Ex: She slipped the Dyna-Cruiser into gear and we ["Manner" slowly] HEADED OUT for a drive.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which a Self_mover begins the motion.
Ex: We GET UNDER WAY ["Mns" by heading up through the alpine meadows of la Balme 2140m and then past some sparse pine forests].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the Self_mover begins the motion away from the Source.
Ex: We GOT GOING ["Time" at 5 am] in the rain, just to make the massive hike to Davenport Gap.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Self_mover when she begins the motion away from the Source.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition: The length of time of the Self_mover's absence from the Source.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation is the transportation device that a human Self_mover uses to travel.
Ex: The traffic, when we finally GOT GOING ["mot" in Jamaorn's car], was appalling.

fe.name: Journey
fe.definition:
The journey is the trip or expedition on which the Self_mover embarks.
Ex: I'm HEADING OUT ["Journey" on a mission].

lexunit.name: get under way.v
lexunit.definition: FN: start motion and make progress towards a goal

lexunit.name: get going.v
lexunit.definition: FN: begin motion away from a location

lexunit.name: head out.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to begin motion away from a location

lexunit.name: hit the road.v
lexunit.definition: COD: set out on a journey

frame.name: Intentional_traversing
frame.definition:
A Self_mover intentionally moves in a Directionon a Path relative to landmark that is neither the Source nor the Goal of the overall motion. The shape or configuration of the Path may be expressed with a Path_shape
Ex: ["Self_mover" Ambrose Powell] FORDED ["Path" over] ["Vehicle" on one horse], and we drove the others after him.
Ex: ["Self_mover" We] repassed the first day's battlefield and ASCENDED ["Path" the road to the city].
Ex: ["Self_mover" Jeff Manor and I] CLIMBED ["Path" the North Face of Mt Shuksan], ["cir" with cold, clear weather and solid ice].

fe.name: Self_mover
fe.definition:
This is a sentient being or a vehicle steered by a sentient being which moves.
Ex: ["Self_mover" We] drive down dusty roads, FORDED through a stream, and tried to get up a mountainside on a rocky road.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.
Ex: We FORDED ["Src" from the island] to the mainland.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path, excluding directional expressions:
Ex: We decided to CUT ["Path" through the forest].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Any expression which indicates where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal.
Ex: I'll CUT across the Sahara desert ["Goal" up to Algeria and Morocco].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (_hard_, _softly_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Self_mover that also affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: Immediately, the monk invited her to sit on his shoulders and he ["Manner" carefully] FORDED the river, depositing her on the opposite bank.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.
Ex: He followed the coast as far as Fronteras, then CUT ["Dist" 160 miles] across the Gulf of Mexico to the Yucatán Peninsula.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An event involving the Self_mover that results in their moving in the specified way.
Ex: The enemy had FORDED the river ["Mns" by piling up the bodies of their fallen comrades in the river bed].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.
Ex: Motorists once again must ["Speed" quickly] CUT across three lanes of traffic to get from Exit 7 to Exit 8.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
This is a second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique, relative to which the Self_mover moves.
Ex: They CUT across the bushes ["Thm_c" after him] and watched him Go into a small shrine-like building at the very center of the compound

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
Depictive phrase describing the Self_mover.
Ex: I actually FORDED the river ["Dep-Und" in my ski boots].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.
Ex: The common brook is best FORDED ["Place" south of the hut].

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The direction in which the Self_mover goes.
Ex: We followed the trail (which is well marked with cairns) and then CUT ["dir" west] across a grassy meadow for about 1000 feet to the crest of the nearby saddle lying below North Peak.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the motion takes place.
Ex: The Federal Army of the Potomac FORDED the river ["Time" in August 1862].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.
Ex: I CUT through the alley in order ["Purpose" to escape my pursuers].

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.
Ex: The General was received by Colonel Thayer, and ASCENDED the hill ["Vehicle" in a landau], escorted by the officers of the post.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time that the Self_mover spends in motion.
Ex: We FORDED Cooper Cr. ["dur" for several hours] then built a fire to dry out gear.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.
Ex: Streams were FORDED ["Explanation" because there were no bridges over meandering Back Creek].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the Intentional_traversing occurs and which the Intentional_traversing is taken to be a part of.
Ex: He had comfortably FORDED it ["Containing_event" on his trip to Beatrice]

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.
Ex: Early in the morning, Chapman had ["Frequency" twice] FORDED the river a short distance north of the footbridge.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition:
A larger conceptualization that includes the Intentional_traversing as an integral part. The Intentional_traversing expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.
Ex: The 133rd Infantry hurriedly FORDED the river ["ree" in an attempt to capture a bridge intact].

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition:
An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the Intentional_traversing.
Ex: I CUT across Arnold's new backyard ["Consecutive" only to find literally hundreds of squirrels everywhere].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Traversing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.
Ex: These waterways can be FORDED by infantry ["cir" at low water], but at other times a six-foot tide makes them difficult to cross.

fe.name: Endpoints
fe.definition:
The Source and Goal of either a single or a repeated motion taken together as End_points of the Path.
Ex: It is located at the place where explorers Marquette and Jolliet FORDED ["End_points" between the Chicago and Des Plaines Rivers].

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition:
Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co_participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.
Ex: John FORDED the river ["Co_participant" with his cousin].

lexunit.name: ford.v
lexunit.definition: FN: cross a stream at a shallow place

lexunit.name: cut.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to go directly across rather than around an area

lexunit.name: climb.v
lexunit.definition: FN: traverse an inclined surface so as to rise in elevation

lexunit.name: ascend.v
lexunit.definition: FN: move up an inclined surface

lexunit.name: traverse.v
lexunit.definition: FN: travel across or through.

frame.name: Quitting_a_place
frame.definition: A Self_mover leaves an initial Source location. The Path by which the Self_mover departs, and the Intended_goal of the Direction may also be mentioned. In many words which evoke this frame, there is an additional implication that the Self_mover is discontented with the Source location.

fe.name: Self_mover
fe.definition: This is the entity which moves under its own power.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: A relation to a landmark that describes the trajectory in the midst of the motion. (It is thus neither a Source nor the Intended_goal.)

fe.name: Intended_goal
fe.definition: Any expression which tells where the Self_mover intends to end up as a result of the motion.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An event involving the Self_mover that results in the Self_mover moving in the specified way.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: A second moving object that moves in coordination with the Self_mover.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Self_mover during the action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: The direction in which the Self_mover goes.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the motion takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition: The length of time that the Self_mover spends away from the Source.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Self_mover at the end of the event.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.

fe.name: Reciprocation
fe.definition: An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, and/or is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of departure and which the departure is taken to be a part of.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: A larger conceptualization that includes the departing as an integral part. The departure expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the departing.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the departing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

fe.name: Coordinated_event
fe.definition: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event (it does not allow states) that the departing is rhythmically aligned with. (This would then further require that the departing be iterated.) The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance from the Source that the Self_mover ends up.

lexunit.name: quit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: leave, especially permanently

lexunit.name: withdraw.v
lexunit.definition: FN: depart from a place

lexunit.name: withdrawal.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of withdrawing or retreating from a place

lexunit.name: vamoose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: depart hurriedly.

lexunit.name: skedaddle.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (no obj. informal) depart quickly or hurriedly.

lexunit.name: split.v

lexunit.name: vacate.v

lexunit.name: sally.v

lexunit.name: retreat.n

lexunit.name: retreat.v
lexunit.definition: FN: withdraw from a difficult, exposed, or uncomfortable situation

lexunit.name: escapee.n
lexunit.definition: FN: somebody that has escaped, especially from prison

lexunit.name: emigre.n

lexunit.name: emigration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: leaving a country to settle in another

lexunit.name: emigrate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

lexunit.name: emigrant.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who leaves their own country in order to settle permanently in another.

lexunit.name: desertion.n
lexunit.definition: FN: leaving a post of obligation in violation of oath or orders

lexunit.name: desert.v
lexunit.definition: FN: leave (a place)

lexunit.name: defect.v
lexunit.definition: COD: abandon one's country or cause in favour of an opposing one.

lexunit.name: defection.n

lexunit.name: bolt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: run away suddenly

lexunit.name: abandon.v
lexunit.definition: COD: desert or leave permanently

frame.name: Translating
frame.definition:
A Cognizer produces a Target_symbol which represents, in the Target_representation format, a Content that pre-exists in the form of a Source_symbol in a Source_representation format. Ex:
Ex: ["Source_symbol" This word] is ["Time" sometimes] TRANSLATED ["Target_symbol" as ` girl ']. ["Cognizer" CNI]
Ex: They all wore symbolic black clothes over bright yellow T-shirts and all spoke in Welsh, ["Content" their statements] being TRANSLATED ["Target_representation" into English] ["Time" afterwards]. ["Cognizer" CNI]
Ex: ["Source_symbol" His texts] were TRANSLATED ["Source_representation" from French] ["Target_representation" into Scots] ["Cognizer" by Carl Gronau].
Ex: Perhaps when Irish monks spoke in Latin about lionn, meaning ale, ["Cognizer" they] TRANSLATED ["Source_symbol" the word] ["Equivalence" literally] ["Source_representation" from Irish] ["Target_representation" into Latin] ["Target_symbol" as biber, 'drink'].
Ex: ["Source_symbol" Each of the ten Greek nouns below] can be ["Equivalence" accurately] TRANSLATED ["Mns" by using just one English word]. ["Cog" CNI].

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
This is the person who carries out the translation.
Ex: The text was published in Lescarbot's Les Muses de la Nouvelle-France (Paris 1609) and later TRANSLATED ["Cog" by HT Richardson].

fe.name: Source_symbol
fe.definition:
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.
Ex: Biblical scholars typically TRANSLATE ["sous" kenosis] as self-emptying or self-offering.

fe.name: Source_representation
fe.definition:
The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.
Ex: More books were TRANSLATED ["sour" from other languages] into Russian in the 1980s , including record numbers from English , German and French.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the translation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: His book, ["Manner" carefully] TRANSLATED by Teresa Lavender Fagan, is a fascinating account for the layman, of the cuisine of the Mesopotamia.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Cognizer which accomplishes the translation of the Content.
Ex: We also TRANSLATED the queries into Chinese ["Mns" by looking up each English word in the bilingual dictionary].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.
Ex: ["Time" Last year] I TRANSLATED a short book on the artist Anne Ratkowski (of the pre-war November Group in Berlin) from German into English.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.
Ex: ["cir" With everybody waiting for him], he simply TRANSLATED the word as ?son? or ?child?.

fe.name: Target_symbol
fe.definition:
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.
Ex: Together with the French Prime Minister, Guizot, he TRANSLATED it into French ["tars" as entente cordiale] for King Louis Philippe to use in his speech.

fe.name: Target_representation
fe.definition:
The representation system into which the Content is rendered by the Cognizer.
Ex: Well they TRANSLATED it ["Target_representation" into Spanish] as "Uno-Dos-Tres Meneha Meneha!"

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.
Ex: She guided me through the dishes available that afternoon and TRANSLATED ["con" my order] into Spanish for the older woman in the kitchen.

fe.name: Equivalence
fe.definition:
An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.
Ex: The Japanese term hai is ["equ" literally] TRANSLATED as yes.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The Medium is a text produced by the Cognizer in which she uses a Target_symbol to express Content from a Source_representation system.
Ex: Gearóid Ó Cairealláin TRANSLATES Texas as Teicseas ["Medium" in an article in Lá].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the translation takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by translating.

lexunit.name: translate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: express the sense of (words or text) in another language.

lexunit.name: translation.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of translating.

frame.name: Setting_out
frame.definition:
A Self_mover begins a journey at a Source location, in a particular Directiongenerally setting out with an Intended_goal in mind.
Ex: ["Time" At about 1:00 in the morning], ["Self_mover" climbers] SET OUT ["Intended_goal" for the summit]. Ex: ["Self_mover" The expedition] SET OUT ["Source" from Granada] ["Time" early in March], leaving only one hundred men to garrison the fort which overlooks the city. Ex: ["Time" After that] ["Self_mover" the earl] SET OUT ["Direction" south] ["Cotheme" with his host], and Kari went with him, and Njal's sons too.

fe.name: Self_mover
fe.definition: This is the entity which moves under its own power.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: A relation to a landmark that describes the trajectory in the midst of the motion. (It is thus neither a Source nor the Intended_goal.)

fe.name: Intended_goal
fe.definition: Any expression which tells where the Self_mover intends to end up as a result of the motion.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An event involving the Self_mover that results in the Self_mover moving in the specified way.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: A second moving object which the Self_mover moves to follow.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Self_mover during the action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: The direction in which the Self_mover goes.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the motion takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.

fe.name: Duration_of_final_state
fe.definition: The length of time that the Self_mover spends away from the Source.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Self_mover at the end of the event.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.

fe.name: Reciprocation
fe.definition: An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, and/or is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of departure and which the departure is taken to be a part of.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: A larger conceptualization that includes the departing as an integral part. The departure expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the departing.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the departing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

fe.name: Coordinated_event
fe.definition: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event (it does not allow states) that the departing is rhythmically aligned with. (This would then further require that the departing be iterated.) The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance from the Source that the Self_mover ends up.

lexunit.name: set off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (support verb set) begin a journey.

lexunit.name: set out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: begin a journey

lexunit.name: decamp.v
lexunit.definition: COD: depart suddenly or secretly.

frame.name: Successfully_communicate_message
frame.definition:
A Communicator speaks to an Addressee in such a way that the Addressee understands and fully appreciates the truth and/or relevance of the Message.
Ex: Marred by overblown writing , ["Medium" this first novel by Wilbur Smith 's wife] effectively CONVEYS ["Message" some of South Africa 's problems] .["Add" INI]
Ex: ["Communicator" He] CONVEYS vividly the absurdity of a situation , but he is incurious about the underlying processes which shape it. ["Add" INI]
Ex: ["Communicator" We]'ve got to GET ["Message" the message] THROUGH ["Add" to them] ["Time" before they become sexually active].
Ex: Have you been using PowerPoint (PPT) for years and feel ["Communicator" you] don't ["Time" always] GET ["Message" your point] ACROSS ["Addressee" to the audience]?
Ex: It 's impossible to CONVEY ["Message" how lost I felt]. ["Communicator" CNI] ["Add" INI]
Ex: But , alas , ["Medium" the printed word] can not ["Adequacy" adequately] CONVEY ["Message" the panting , gasping misery of this particular torment]. ["Add" INI]

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition:
The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.
Ex: ["Communicator" Nobody] seems to be able to GET the idea THROUGH to her that she needs a job!!!!

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.
Ex: According to Masztalics, a good teacher uses experiments to GET the point ACROSS ["Add" to the class].

fe.name: Message
fe.definition:
Message A proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.
Ex: He tried to GET THROUGH to his wife ["Msg" that the debt he's taken on buying stocks poses no risk].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
Ex: ["Medium" The article] CONVEYS Mr. Handley's disrespect for those who disagree with him.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.
Ex: Rais ["Manner" carefully] CONVEYS his own personal faith journey while respecting those who may have distinctly different views or experiences.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means by which the Communicator communicates.
Ex: She finally GOT her point ACROSS ["Mns" by miming a shark's fin with her hands over her head].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the communication takes place.
Ex: Greenspan GOT his point ACROSS ["Time" yesterday] that a measured pace of rate hikes is still the plan.

fe.name: Adequacy
fe.definition:
The degree to which the Communicator's efforts are effective at making the Addressee understand and appreciate the Message.
Ex: The ads ["ade" clearly] GOT ACROSS the need to respect the health of non-smokers.

lexunit.name: convey.v
lexunit.definition: FN: successfully communicate (a message)

lexunit.name: get through.v
lexunit.definition: FN: succeed in communicating (a message) to someone.

lexunit.name: get across.v
lexunit.definition: COD: manage to communicate an idea clearly.

frame.name: Change_direction
frame.definition:
A Theme that is in motion assumes a new Direction in which it moves.
Ex: ["Thm" We] took our chances and TURNED ["dir" right] ["Place" by a petrol station] and, bingo, there she was--Fir Park.
Ex: Molly followed silently as ["Thm" Desmond] left the large paneled hall and TURNED ["Direction" right] ["Path" through a swing door] ["Goal" into a long, bare corridor].
Ex: Cross O'Connell Bridge and continue along D'Olier Street, _make_ a ["Direction" right] TURN ["Goal" onto College Street]. ["Theme" CNI]
Ex: Go past the unattended guardhouse, and _take_ a ["ang" sharp] ["Direction" left] TURN ["Path" down the ramp]. ["Theme" CNI]
Ex: Take the elevator to the sixth floor and _make_ ["Frequency" two] ["dir" LEFTS]. ["Thm" CNI]

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not _required_ to be an animate mover, so it is different from a self-mover.
Ex: At that point ["Thm" the truck in front of me] TURNED right into the huge ditch/field that separates the interstate from the access road.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.
Ex: One of those ugly landcuisers CUT left ["Src" from the opposite lane] in moving traffic.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal (see below) expresses the frame element Path, excluding directional expressions.
Ex: They TURNED right ["Path" through another gate] into a courtyard opening.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
Any expression which indicates where the Theme ends up as a result of the change of direction.
Ex: Finally, where the road begins to climb steeply, CUT right ["Goal" onto a small trail near a sign in a tree], and go downhill to the stream..

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (_hard_, _softly_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In agentive frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Theme that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: I ["Manner" carefully] TURNED left onto Narragansett and worked my way through the debris.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way.
Ex: Participants drove a vehicle model that rolled on flat ground and TURNED right or left ["Means" by steering front wheels as in a typical car].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition:
The Speed is the rate at which the Theme changes direction.
Ex: Suddenly, the jeep ["Speed" quickly] TURNED left down a side road.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition:
This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:
Ex: I TURNED right ["Thm_c" after them], closed in on the rear plane but then discovered another plane from the formation nearing me from the right side.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A phrase describing the state of the Theme during the act of changing direction.
Ex: The big forward picked up speed entering Edmonton's end, CUT to the right ["Depictive" with Charlie Huddy draped over him] and left a pass for Lemieux as Stevens battled Kevin Lowe into a screen in front of Fuhr.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is the setting where the change of direction during the Theme's motion occurs.
Ex: TURN right ["Place" at the stop light] and follow Park Avenue.

fe.name: Path_shape
fe.definition:
The configuration formed by the Path that the Theme traverses during the change of direction.
Ex: The tank rumbled, backed quickly, TURNED left and right ["Path_shape" in a sine curve].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
The new direction in which the Theme continues its motion.
Ex: Eventually, though, I backtracked to Kel Tole and _hung_ a ["dir" LEFT] toward Kilgal Tole.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the change of direction takes place.
Ex: ["Time" Then] I TURNED left onto 220th Street.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.
Ex: That car was attempting to back in, and had to CUT to the left ["pur" in order to back up the vehicle].

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition:
The device or bodypart that serves to move the Theme.
Ex: Go back to where you TURNED left ["Vehicle" in your car] to reach the trailhead.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A factor which explains the change of direction of the Theme.
Ex: We've TURNED north ["Explanation" because we've struck desert heading south].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the change of direction occurs and which the change of direction is taken to be a part of.
Ex: Anyway, ["con" on my first trip to Wakefield], I TURNED right off Falls of Neuse Road, which is generally where the middle-class and upper middle-class houses and apartments are going.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
The number of times that a change of direction occurs.
Ex: They TURNED right ["Frequency" three times] and approached the sea lions from behind.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition:
A larger conceptualization that includes the change of direction as an integral part. The change of direction expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.
Ex: The pilot of N3602D TURNED left ["ree" in an attempt to avoid a collision].

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition:
An unexpected event that affects the Theme, which is enabled by, and occurs after, the change of direction.
Ex: I have a tendency to shoot straight forward after the initial drop and then CUT to the left ["consec" only to meet a knee-high rush of white water].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the change of direction event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

fe.name: Angle
fe.definition:
The angle between the old and the new Direction in which the Theme moves.
Ex: There we TURNED right ["ang" by almost 180 degrees] and by a winding road, going steeply up we went to And?lka.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The situation that results from the change of direction

frame.name: Have_as_translation_equivalent
frame.definition:
A Source_symbol in a Source_representation system is presented to be matched by a Target_symbol in a Target_representation in the ability to express a particular Content.
Ex: ["Source_symbol" A palintonon or palintone] TRANSLATES ["Target_symbol" as "V-spring"] and euthytonon or euthytone translates as "straight-spring" ["Source_representation" from Greek].
Ex: It can be confusing if ["Source_symbol" one word] TRANSLATES ["Target_symbol" into sereval] ["Target_representation" in Spanish], ["Target_symbol" which don't have the same gender].
Ex: Therefore, ["Source_symbol" this word] TRANSLATES ["Target_symbol" as "a male"].
Ex: ["Source_symbol" Perak] TRANSLATES ["Target_symbol" as ?silver?] ["Source_representation" in the Malay language].
Sentences such as the following are actually to be handled in the Be_translation_equivalent frame, which has the reverse point of view from the current frame. Ex: We have just seen how each Bible program makes it easy to get a definition of ["Source_symbol" the Greek or Hebrew word] ["Source_symbol" which] ["Target_symbol" a given English word] TRANSLATES. The difference is essentially between whether both speaker and addressee in the context where the word is used are starting with the Target_symbol in mind. When they are, the symbols are being compared for how they correspond and Be_translation_equivalent can be used. Otherwise, generally where the information conveyed by the predication is what the Target_symbol is, Have_as_translation_equivalent is used.

fe.name: Source_symbol
fe.definition:
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.
Ex: ["Source_symbol" "Hi, dude"] TRANSLATES into Spanish as Hola tío.

fe.name: Source_representation
fe.definition:
The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.
Ex: The bands' name TRANSLATES into English as Killer Bananas ["Source_representation" from their native French] and they play metal and horror themed punk rock 'n' roll.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The period of time during which the translation equivalence holds.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.
Ex: ["cir" In other contexts] the word TRANSLATES as 'function' or 'intention'.

fe.name: Target_symbol
fe.definition:
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.
Ex: The word giallo TRANSLATES into English as ["Target_symbol" 'yellow'].

fe.name: Target_representation
fe.definition:
The representation system within which the Target_symbol is equivalent in its signification to the Source_symbol within the Source_representation system .
Ex: More sinister still is the fact that Homeland TRANSLATES ["tarr" into German] as Fatherland.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition:
The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.
Ex: ["Content" The disclaimer in question] TRANSLATED as: "Yo, Gringo! This episode of The Twilight Zone was paid for by Robinson for Congress."

fe.name: Equivalence
fe.definition:
An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.
Ex: The Swedish word, pepparkakor, ["equ" literally] TRANSLATES as pepper cakes.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
A text in which the Source_symbol is rendered by a Target_symbol to express a particular Content.
Ex: ["med" In the New Testament] the Greek word ekklesia TRANSLATES 115 times as "church".

lexunit.name: translate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be expressed in a target language as

frame.name: Be_translation_equivalent
frame.definition:
A Target_symbol in a Target_representation system is presented as equivalent to a Source_symbol in a Source_representation system in the ability to express a particular Content.
Ex: ["Target_symbol" The term employment area] TRANSLATES ["Source_symbol" the French zone d'emploi]. Ex: The term employment area TRANSLATES ["Source_representation" the French] zone d'emploi.
Ex: ["Target_symbol" The term] TRANSLATES ["Source_symbol" the Russian raznorechie (literally "different-speech-ness")]. Ex: The term TRANSLATES the ["Source_representation" Russian] raznorechie (literally "different-speech-ness".

fe.name: Source_symbol
fe.definition:
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.
Ex: This expression TRANSLATES ["Source_symbol" the Greek word Hades].

fe.name: Source_representation
fe.definition: The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The period of time during which the translation equivalence holds.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.

fe.name: Target_symbol
fe.definition:
A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.
Ex: ["Target_symbol" The Tibetan sequence of words] TRANSLATES the Chinese Ti- shih.

fe.name: Target_representation
fe.definition: The representation system within which the Target_symbol is equivalent in its signification to the Source_symbol within the Source_representation system .

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.

fe.name: Equivalence
fe.definition:
An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.
Ex: Choose the Russian expression that ["Equivalence" correctly] TRANSLATES the English word or phrase.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
A text in which the Target_symbol is used to render the Content of a Source_symbol.
Ex: ["med" In the Greek Scriptures] the word TRANSLATES the Greek word "theos".

lexunit.definition: FN: be the translation equivalent of

frame.name: Physical_artworks
frame.definition:
A physical object, the Artifact, is produced by a Creator to stimulate the perceptions, emotions, or cognition of an audience. Though it need not, in many cases, the created Artifact is intended to represent an actual or imagined entity or event, the Represented. The Represented may be specifically shown in a particular state (State_of_represented).
Ex: Sir Denis Mahon is the owner of the most important private collection of ["Time_of_creation" Italian Baroque] ["Artifact" PAINTINGS].
Ex: He presented Eddie with a ["Type" watercolour] ["Artifact" PAINTING] and a bouquet of flowers to his wife Frances
Ex: I just took a PICTURE ["Represented" of the screen] and plan to share it with 6.4 billion of my closest friends on the Internet tonight.

fe.name: Artifact
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use.
Ex: The first of the two ["Artifact" DRAWINGS] by Parmigianino recently acquired for the National Gallery is a study for the Madonna dal collo lungo.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition:
The use for which the Artifact is intended.
Ex: The author's lucid text and ["Use" instructional] DRAWINGS provide a strong foundation in the basic and functional anatomy of the pain's region.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
An individual or individuals that bring the Artifact into existence.
Ex: ["Creator" Italian] PAINTINGS include an allegorical work by Garofalo which was mentioned in Vasari 's ` Vite ' .

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition:
The time at which an Artifact comes into existence.
Ex: Here's a ["Time_of_creation" 1987] PHOTO of how the Union School building had deteriorated after many years of neglect.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
The term used to refer to an Artifact.
Ex: In his PAINTING ["Name" The Fall of Man] Albrecht went through a hard time trying to achieve a geometrical figure of two beings known as man and woman.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition:
An indication of the subtype of Artifact.
Ex: The ["Type" Impressionist style] PAINTINGS of 1896-7 are rare but of great interest

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
Any indication of what makes up the Artifact, including components, ingredients, etc.
Ex: The exhibition also features a ["Material" marble] STATUE of a naked Aphrodite crouching at her bath

fe.name: Represented
fe.definition:
The entity--which may be a thing, an action or a state--that is represented by the Artifact.
Ex: I was able to take a fine PHOTO ["rep" of his arrival].

fe.name: State_of_represented
fe.definition:
A characterization of the state in which the Represented entity is portrayed.
Ex: Within the church is the PAINTING of Virgin Mary ["sta" sitting on the throne holding a child among various saints].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
This FE identifies a characteristic, description, or evaluation of the Artifact.
Ex: The cover features a ["Descriptor" horrible] PHOTO of the man.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Artifact is presently located.

lexunit.name: photograph.n

lexunit.name: painting.n

lexunit.name: picture.n

lexunit.name: drawing.n

lexunit.name: statue.n

lexunit.name: statuette.n

lexunit.name: bronze.n

lexunit.name: diagram.n

lexunit.name: sculpture.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a three-dimensional, solid piece of artwork, typically made from wood, metal, or plaster.

frame.name: Create_representation
frame.definition:
A Creator produces a physical object which is to serve as a Representation of an actual or imagined entity or event, the Represented.
Ex: ["cre" Epstein] saw the machine-man and CARVED ["Represented" him] ["Material" in shiny metal].
Ex: ["cre" Picasso] DREW ["Represented" some violent looking birds].
Ex: Towards the end of his life, ["Creator" Munch] PAINTED ["Represented" himself] ["Depictive_of_represented" as a ghost].
Ex: Dan Grant was the model for Norman Rockwell when ["Creator" the artist] PAINTED ["Represented" him] ["Role" as "The Barefoot Boy"] for a Depression-era Coca Cola calendar.
Ex: ["Place" There] ["Creator" the Finnish artist] SKETCHED ["Represented" him], ["Depictive" creating a stunning portrait].

fe.name: Representation
fe.definition:
The entity produced by the Creator to evoke in an audience the idea of the Represented.
Ex: The bell became famous after being PAINTED by Jamie Wyeth ["Representation" in his painting Bronze Age].

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
An individual or individuals that bring the Representation into existence.
Ex: Since ["Creator" Frans] PHOTOGRAPHED them ten years ago the population has increased.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which a Representation is created.

fe.name: Represented
fe.definition:
The entity--which may be a thing, an action or a state--that is represented by the Representation.
Ex: When Nadar PHOTOGRAPHED ["repd" her], Desbordes-Valmore was sixty-eight.

fe.name: Depictive_of_represented
fe.definition:
A characterization of the state in which the Represented entity is presented.
Ex: He CARVED St. Francis ["Depictive_of_represented" tumbling around], and St. Thomas banging his fist on a table.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Creator that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _carefully_).
Ex: She set up her plywood on saw horses and ["man" carefully] DREW her mother.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: This FE identifies a Role that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills in a background context, either generically or in some specific instance.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
This FE describes the Creator as being in some state during the creation of the Representation.
Ex: ["Depictive" As a young man] he PAINTED Philip IV as a fashionable equestrian.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition:
The physical Material that is used in the production of the Representation.
Ex: I DREW him ["Material" on a sheet of paper] first.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Creator intends to accomplish by creating the Representation.
Ex: He also PHOTOGRAPHED them ["Purpose" in order to form a composite girl for one end of the bench and a composite boy for the other end].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the artist produces the representation.
Ex: I DREW him ["Place" at work] a bunch of times, mainly for the amusement of the staff.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The entity used by the Creator to make a Representation of the Represented entity.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Creator that allows them to make a Representation of the Represented entity.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: Iteration is the number of times the Creator creates the representation.

frame.name: Create_physical_artwork
frame.definition:
A Creator creates an artifact that is typically an iconic Representation of an actual or imagined entity or event. The Representation may also be evocative of an idea while not based on resemblance.
Ex: ["Representation" Diagrams] must be ["Manner" clearly] DRAWN ["Location_of_representation" on construction paper]. ["cre" CNI]
Ex: ["cre" I] TOOK ["Representation" his picture] and told him that if it came out well I would make him a copy.
Ex: ["Time" In about 1305 and 1306] ["cre" Giotto] PAINTED ["Representation" a notable series of 38 frescoes].

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition:
An individual or individuals that bring the Representation into existence.
Ex: Supposedly, ["cre" the artist] DREW the picture from memory.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which a Representation is created.
Ex: My brother TOOK this picture in France ["Time" almost 10 years ago], and has recently scanned it in.

fe.name: Representation
fe.definition:
The entity that is created to represent either iconically or abstractly.
Ex: Most of us know where we TOOK ["Representation" a photo] but have a harder time remembering the time we took it.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Creator that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: This FE identifies a Role that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills in a background context, either generically or in some specific instance.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes the Creator as being in some state during the creation of the Representation.

fe.name: Location_of_representation
fe.definition:
The physical location that holds the Representation.
Ex: I DREW him ["locr" on a sheet of paper] first.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Creator intends to accomplish by creating the Representation.
Ex: Masha also TOOK the picture ["Purpose" to prove that you can find an Internet Cafe even here in Murmansk].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Creator produces the Representation.
Ex: I TOOK this picture ["Place" in Italy] a couple of weeks ago.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the creation of the Representation ogically follows.
Ex: Well, I PAINTED the picture ["Explanation" because the quarry was visually exciting].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The entity which the Creator uses to create the work of art.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action performed by the Creator which brings about the creation of the Representation.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Creator or the Representation.

lexunit.name: paint.v
lexunit.definition: FN: create a representation by applying (a liquid) to a surface

lexunit.name: draw.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce (a picture or diagram) by making lines and marks on paper.

lexunit.name: take_((picture)).v
lexunit.definition: FN: to produce a photographic image

lexunit.name: artist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who practises or performs any of the creative arts.

lexunit.name: sculpt.v

lexunit.name: cast.v

frame.name: Fleeing
frame.definition:
A Self_mover responds to a (real or imagined) danger by moving away from it.
Ex: ["Self_mover" She] had FLED ["Source" from DCS facilities] several times before.. Ex: ["Self_mover" Pakistanis in US] trying to FLEE ["Goal" to Canada] hit roadblocks. Ex: ["Self_mover" Anderson's division] suddenly BOLTED ["Direction" north] ["Source" from Devil's Den], flanked out III Corps almost entirely, and shattered the entire Corps. Ex: ["Self_mover" We] FLED ["Distance" for several miles] before reaching our safe-house.

fe.name: Self_mover
fe.definition: Self_mover is the living (or self-directed) being which moves under its own power.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Source is used for any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is used for any description of a trajectory of motion involving a landmark which is neither a Source nor a Goal. This includes "middle of path'' expressions.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is used for any expression which tells where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
An expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory or rate of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.
Ex: They had to FLEE ["Manner" on foot] through the desert.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the motion occurs.

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: An entity whose motion is correlated with that of the Self_mover, following and tracking the Self_mover, being followed and tracked, or with both parties mutually matching Paths.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The rate at which the location of the Self_mover changes with respect to time.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby the Self_mover achieves movement.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the world which exists because of the motion of the Self_mover

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition: The emotional or mental state of the Self_mover which motivates them toward motion or the particular manner of motion.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time for which the Self_mover moves.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Self_mover moves. Ex: John RAN AWAY with her ["Purpose" to shelter her from disapproval].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location within which a defined motion takes place. Any specified or implied Source, Path or Goal should designate a location contained with the Place.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The state of affairs that leads to the particular motion that the Self_mover adopts.

fe.name: External_cause
fe.definition:
External_cause is something in the external environment that causes the Self_mover to move.
Ex: They FLED ["ext" at the sound of her voice].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition: The direction that the Self_mover heads in during the motion.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: The entity used by the Self_mover in getting away from the undesirable Source.

lexunit.name: bolt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: run away suddenly.

lexunit.name: flight.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: escaping from a place or situation

lexunit.name: flee.v
lexunit.definition: FN: escape the site of a disaster.

lexunit.name: run away.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take flight; escape.

frame.name: Artificiality
frame.definition:
An Entity is evaluated for whether or not it belongs to a particular Type in a context where its category membership is doubtful. The criterion or criteria that are relevant to evaluating Type membership depend on the individual lexical units and/or on the context. Typically, either the material composition of the Entity, its method of creation, or the identity (and proper authority) of its creators are critical for proper category membership. Note that Entity also covers behaviors.
Ex: It can be hard to get your money back after discovering you've bought a BOGUS ["Type" autograph] for hundreds or thousands of dollars!
Ex: It can be hard to get your money back after discovering you've bought ["Entity" a BOGUS autograph] for hundreds or thousands of dollars!
Ex: A BOGUS ["Type" policeman] pulling over motorists was arrested after stopping a car carrying four real officers.
Ex: ["Entity" A BOGUS policeman pulling over motorists] was arrested after stopping a car carrying four real officers.
Ex: You people are pretty thick if you think you have evidence to prove that ["ent" the moon landing] _was_ FAKE. Ex: You people are pretty thick if you think you have evidence to prove that the ["Type" moon landing] _was_ FAKE.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity that is being evaluated in terms of whether it is an instance of the Type.
Ex: ["ent" The bomb found at the US Embassy in Berlin] _was_ FAKE.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: The type relative to which the Entity is evaluated.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Entity seems to belong (or not, if so specified by the lexical unit) to the category of the Type is clear. Typically, this frame element is realized as an end-of-scale expression.
Ex: Of course, the picture was ["deg" completely] FAKE, as could be seen by a number of clues.

lexunit.name: artificial.a
lexunit.definition: COD: made as a copy of something natural.

lexunit.name: bogus.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not genuine or true

lexunit.name: fake.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not genuine.

lexunit.name: counterfeit.a
lexunit.definition: COD: made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

lexunit.name: false.a
lexunit.definition: COD: artificial.

lexunit.name: genuine.a
lexunit.definition: COD: truly what it is said to be; authentic

lexunit.name: ersatz.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not real or genuine

lexunit.name: phoney.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a fraudulent person or thing.

lexunit.name: pseudo.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not genuine; fake, pretentious, or insincere.

lexunit.name: phoney.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not genuine.

frame.name: Forging
frame.definition:
An Agent produces a Forgery, an entity that they intend to pass off as a particular (instance of) a Standard. An instance of the Standard may actually exist that served as an original that is copied by the Agent, or the Standard exists only as an idea.
Ex: So who was it that FAKED the photo "showing" Jane Fonda and John Kerry with the Vietcong?

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person that creates a Forgery with the intent of passing it off as (an instance of) the Standard.
Ex: ["agt" He] even FAKED her signature.

fe.name: Forgery
