fe.definition: The Forgery is the product that the Agent creates with the intent of passing it off as (an instance of) the Standard.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the forging event logically follows.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action or state that the Agent intends to accomplish by producing the Forgery.

fe.name: Standard
fe.definition: The Standard is the actually existing or imagined (kind of) thing that the Agent wants to pass the Forgery off as.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity manipulated by the Agent in order to produce the Forgery.
Ex: Fortunately, he FORGED it ["ins" with a black pen], which couriers never use.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location in which the Agent makes a Forgery.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the forgery takes place.

fe.name: Fidelity
fe.definition:
The way in which the Forgery does or does not match the Standard.
Ex: What I don't know is why she tried to FORGE it ["fid" half-size].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
An entity corresponding to the Standard which the Agent scrutinizes in order to copy.
Ex: He FAKED his travel documents ["sou" from the ones his sister used last year].

lexunit.name: falsify.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to produce a fake

lexunit.name: counterfeit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: imitate fraudulently.

lexunit.name: forge.v
lexunit.definition: COD: produce a fraudulent copy or imitation of.

lexunit.name: fake.v
lexunit.definition: COD: forge or counterfeit.

lexunit.name: forgery_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of producing a fraudulent copy or imitation of (a banknote, work of art, etc.).

lexunit.name: forgery_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: FN: a fraudulent copy or imitation of (a banknote, work of art, etc.).

lexunit.name: fake.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or thing that is not genuine.

frame.name: Posing_as
frame.definition:
An Agent behaves as if they were a particular individual or type of Simulated_entity with the intent of misleading observers of their behavior. This is generally accomplished by altering their normal appearance (especially dress), mannerisms, voice, and other observable characteristics.
Ex: ["Agent" The belfast bank robbers] POSED ["Simulated_entity" as police].
Ex: ["Agent" These groups] are MASQUERADING ["Simulated_entity" as mainstream groups], yet after taking a closer look you see they are the most extreme.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that they are a particular individual or type of Simulated_entity.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the posing event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _eagerly_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Agent that contributes to the his or her being perceived as a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
Ex: Some activists POSED as delegates ["Means" by wearing suits].

fe.name: Simulated_entity
fe.definition: The type or individual that the Agent gives the impression of being.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by posing as a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
Ex: He POSED as a Hurricane Katrina evacuee ["pur" in order to get food, clothing and money from Good Samaritans in Shreveport].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the posing event logically follows.
Ex: They POSED as patients ["exp" because the paper's previous attempt at a formal survey met strong resistance].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Agent gives the impression that they are the Simulated_entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Agent impersonates the Simulated_entity.

lexunit.name: pose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pretend to be.

lexunit.name: impersonate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pretend to be (another person) for entertainment or fraud

lexunit.name: masquerade.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pretend to be someone that one is not.

lexunit.name: impersonation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: pretense of being (another person) for entertainment or fraud

lexunit.name: impostor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who assumes a false identity in order to deceive or defraud.

frame.name: Passing_off
frame.definition:
An Agent acts in such a way as to cause others to think that an Item is an instance of a particular kind of Simulated_entity.
Ex: ["agt" He] had, under the name of Armitage, PASSED ["Item" her] OFF ["Simulated_entity" as a member of one of the most distinguished families of the capital].
Ex: He undoubtedly believes you are ["agt" the impostor] ["agt" who] PALMED ["Item" himself] OFF at Bar Harbor ["Simulated_entity" as the Baron von Kissel].
Ex: Knowing his likeness to the family of Lord Polperro ["agt" she] PALMED ["Item" him] OFF ["Audience" on them] ["Simulated_entity" as a distant relative].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that the Item is a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
Ex: Most recently, ["agt" Grant Palmer] has PALMED himself OFF as a high-placed "insider" in the Church.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the passing off event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _eagerly_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Agent that contributes to the Item being perceived as a (particular kind of) Simulated_entity.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
The Item is the concrete or abstract entity that the Agent misleadingly represents as a particular (kind of) Entity.
Ex: From all reports Muhammad PASSED ["Item" the child] OFF as his son and behaved accordingly.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by passing the Item off as a (particular kind of) Simulated_entity.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the passing-off event logically follows.

fe.name: Simulated_entity
fe.definition:
The Simulated_entity is a particular individual or a token of a particular type that the Item is represented as.
Ex: The colleague who stole your idea and PASSED it OFF ["Simulated_entity" as her own]?

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is the location that is the setting for the passing off event.
Ex: ["Place" In London] she PASSED herself OFF as a rich American heiress.

fe.name: Audience
fe.definition:
The Audience denotes the people that the Agent intends to mislead into thinking that the Item is a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.
Ex: Ritchie PASSED it OFF ["Audience" to them] as his own original thinking.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Agent gives the impression that the Item is the Simulated_entity.

lexunit.name: pass off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: falsely represent something as.

lexunit.name: palm off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: sell or dispose of something by misrepresentation or fraud.

frame.name: Imitating
frame.definition:
An Agent displays a Characteristic of a Standard in his or her own way of behaving.
Ex: I guessed ["agt" he] was trying to IMITATE ["Characteristic" the movements of a skier]
Ex: ["Containing_event" In a tv commercial last year], ["Agent" she] APED ["Characteristic" male slobbiness] ["Depictive" in a singlet and Y-front-style underpants, kicking back on the couch, watching sport].
Ex: 'You are all the same ,' ["agt" he] said, IMITATING ["Characteristic" not her voice but its angry cadence].
Ex: Antony, after he had seen this man, IMITATED ["Standard" him] ["Characteristic" in piety].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person that borrows a Characteristic behavior from a Standard.
Ex: Mimic Snotlings do n't really think for themselves, ["agt" they] merely MIMIC the actions of Orcs and Goblins around them.

fe.name: Characteristic
fe.definition:
The Characteristic is a behavior or property that the Standard possesses and which the Agent adopts in his or her own behavior.
Ex: They were all MIMICKING ["Characteristic" my accent].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: She MIMICKED him ["Manr" carefully] as he moved, her movements naturally graceful.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation.
Ex: Alhough proud of their strong balance sheets , most European superbanks have yet to IMITATE the Japanese ["Means" by lending aggressively abroad].

fe.name: Standard
fe.definition:
The Standard is the entity that exhibits a certain Characteristic that the Agent models their own behavior on.
Ex: The singer says Gwen has COPIED ["Standard" her] in many different ways.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the imitation.
Ex: Kashi's soul remembered all the characteristics of Kashi, the boy, and therefore MIMICKED his hoarse voice ["Purpose" in order to stir my recognition].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the imitation event logically follows.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the imitating event as being in some state. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the imitating event.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the imitation event occurs and of which the imitating event is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Agent's way of behaving is similar to that of the Standard.
Ex: Kurt Cobain APED him ["Degree" to perfection].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the imitation occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Agent imitates some entity which acts as a Standard.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

lexunit.name: imitate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to behave in a way characteristic of

lexunit.name: mimic.v
lexunit.definition: COD: imitate in order to entertain or ridicule.

lexunit.name: ape.v
lexunit.definition: COD: imitate, especially in an absurd or unthinking way.

lexunit.name: copy.v
lexunit.definition: COD: imitate the behaviour or style of.

frame.name: Hiding_objects
frame.definition:
An Agent causes a Hidden_object to become perceptually inaccessible to potential perceivers by placing it in a Hiding_place or putting in place an Obstruction that screens the object.
Ex: Therefore, as I passed the school, ["Agent" I] HID ["Hidden_object" the gun and holster] ["Hiding_place" in the mailbox]
Ex: ["Agent" Gruenwald] HID ["Hidden_object" the money] ["Place" at a local garbage dump] then retrieved it the following morning.
Ex: In later books ["Agent" Harry] often tries to HIDE ["Hidden_object" his scar] ["Obstruction" with his hair].

fe.name: Obstruction
fe.definition:
The entity that the Agent uses to block the Hidden_object from being perceptible.
Ex: She SHROUDED the tub ["Obstruction" with fabric featuring birds and flowers].

fe.name: Hidden_object
fe.definition:
The Hidden_object is the entity which is blocked from view.
Ex: Michael Jackson gave wine to the 13-year-old cancer patient at the center of the molestation charges he's battling but CONCEALED ["Hidden_object" it] inside a Coke can.

fe.name: Potential_observer
fe.definition:
The Potential_observer denotes a person who might perceive the Hidden_object if it was not hidden.
Ex: The wife claims she HID the gun ["poo" from him] but retrieved it after he became abusive.
Phrases such as "from view" and "from sight" are assumed to indicate that the Hidden_object is not visible to any Potential_observer.
Ex: He HID the motorbike ["poo" from view] under a few nearby bushes.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Hidden_object becomes perceptually inaccessible.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person who causes the Hidden_entity to be not perceptually accessible to potential perceivers.
Ex: ["age" The deputy] CONCEALED the bayonet under his coat.

fe.name: Hiding_place
fe.definition:
The location in which the Hidden_object is placed so as not to be perceptually accessible.
Ex: He had CONCEALED the necklace ["Hiding_place" behind him].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the spatial setting in which the hiding event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: Time denotes the interval of time during which the Agent causes the Hidden_object to become hidden from perceptual access.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the hiding event logically follows.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Agent that brings about the hiding of the Hidden_object.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about by hiding the Hidden_object.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

lexunit.name: hide.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put or keep out of sight.

lexunit.name: conceal.v
lexunit.definition: FN: prevent from being perceptually accessible

lexunit.name: mask.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to cover so as to diminish perceptually accessibility

lexunit.name: shroud.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cover or envelop so as to conceal from view

lexunit.name: camouflage.v
lexunit.definition: FN: hide by blending the Hidden_object in with its surroundings

frame.name: Delimitation_of_diversity
frame.definition: An Item which encompasses characteristics or types whose diversity is indicated by adducing a Limit1 and a Limit2 which differ considerably from each other. In some cases, the Limit2 and Limit1 are construed together as Limits. Alternatively, the values of a particular Variable for the Item and its Limits may be profiled.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The entity whose scalar property is specified.

fe.name: Variable
fe.definition: The scalar property that the Item possesses.

fe.name: Limit1
fe.definition: The first-mentioned possibility of the range of variation.

fe.name: Limit2
fe.definition: The second item of the range of variation.

fe.name: Limits
fe.definition: The range of positions on the scale that the Item occupies. Ex: Prices RANGE ["Limits" between 10 and 20 dollars].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The deviation of the Upper_limit and the Lower_limit from each other (and thus from some single value).
Ex: The weights RANGE ["deg" alot] .

lexunit.name: range.v
lexunit.definition: COD: vary or extend between specified limits

lexunit.name: from_to.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: indicating extreme points of a range.

frame.name: Being_awake
frame.definition: A Protagonist is awake at some Time and Place. This entails the Protagonist having a higher general level of awareness of the surroundings than when asleep.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition:
The entity that is not sleeping.
Ex: ["pro" She] was AWAKE through the whole football game.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Protagonist is awake.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Protagonist is awake.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the event takes place.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The degree to which the Protagonist is awake.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Protagonist being awake which is not covered by more specific FEs including secondary effects (quietly, noisily), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

lexunit.name: awake.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not asleep.

lexunit.name: conscious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: aware of and responding to one's surroundings

lexunit.name: wakeful.a
lexunit.definition: COD: unable or not needing to sleep.

lexunit.name: watch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: remain awake for the purpose of religious observance.

frame.name: Resolve_attempt_scenario
frame.definition: An Agent and their Action succeed or fail inasmuch as the result of an Action matches the Goal that they hope to bring about by the Action.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: ["Agent" John] MANAGED a feeble smile.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.
Ex: If you don't SUCCEED ["goa" in your subterfuge], then report back for further orders.

fe.name: Action
fe.definition: This FE identifies the means by which the Goal is achieved (or not).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent during the Action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where an attempt succeeds or fails.
Ex: ["Place" On the bridge] he SUCCEEDED in putting the wig on the corpse.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
A participant function in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.
Ex: Benedikt was SUCCESSFUL ["rol" as a master brewer of beer].

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE is applied to expressions which indicate the prevailing physical conditions for the event, or some concurrent states of affairs.
Ex: And could anybody have SUCCEEDED ["Circumstances" under those conditions], using other methods?

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or failure, but not in all cases.
Ex: Kerry FAILED ["exp" because of his inability to tell his own story].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition:
This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part
Ex: He was SUCCESSFUL ["con" in the Smithers v Burns case].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Action succeeds or fails.

frame.name: Attempting_scenario
frame.definition: An Agent has a particular Goal in mind, and then uses some Means that they believe will bring about the Goal. The Agent succeeds or fails inasmuch as the result of the Means action matches the Goal.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: ["Agent" John] ATTEMPTED to climb Mt. Everest.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.
Ex: John ATTEMPTED ["Goal" to climb Mt. Everest GOAL].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to achieve a Goal.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means action performed by the Agent which they hope will bring about their Goal.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where an attempt is made.
Ex: ["Place" On the bridge] he ATTEMPTED to put the wig on.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time period over which the attempts take place.

frame.name: Scrutinizing_for
frame.definition: A Cognizer examines a Ground closely, alert to the presence of a Phenomenon.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Leslie] EXAMINED the glass for cracks.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon.
Ex: Leslie EXAMINED ["Ground" the glass] for cracks. Ex: Kim SEARCHED ["Ground" the woods] for mushrooms.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
The entity that the Cognizer is alert for in the Ground.
Ex: Leslie EXAMINED the glass ["Phenomenon" for cracks]. Ex: Kim SEARCHED the woods ["Phenomenon" for mushrooms].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Cognizer which allows them to scrutinize the Ground.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The event that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by looking for the Phenomenon.
Ex: You should INSPECT your mail ["Purp" to determine the outcome of the module transfer].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Cognizer that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.
Ex: The temperature controller MONITORED the temperature ["ins" with a calibrated silicon diode].

frame.name: Searching_scenario
frame.definition: A Cognizer seeks a Phenomenon within the Ground.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground in order to find instances of a type of Phenomenon.
Ex: ["Cognizer" Leslie] EXAMINED the glass for cracks.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon.
Ex: Leslie EXAMINED ["Ground" the glass] for cracks. Ex: Kim SEARCHED ["Ground" the woods] for mushrooms.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
The entity that the Cognizer is alert for in the Ground.
Ex: Leslie EXAMINED the glass ["Phenomenon" for cracks]. Ex: Kim SEARCHED the woods ["Phenomenon" for mushrooms].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Cognizer which allows them to scrutinize the Ground.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The event that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by looking for the Phenomenon.
Ex: You should INSPECT your mail ["Purp" to determine the outcome of the module transfer].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity directed by the Cognizer that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.
Ex: The temperature controller MONITORED the temperature ["ins" with a calibrated silicon diode].

frame.name: Measures
frame.definition: An Entity is measured in some (implicit) Attribute by quantifying the Count of a particular Unit whose value for the Attribute is known. LUs and constructions whose meanings inherit from Measures are used in a relatively small, delimitable set of constructions. They may be complements of particular lexical constructions (a _length_of 20 ft., _measures_ 20 ft.) or parts of non-lexical constructions (including Transparent Noun constructions and Measurement_plus_adjective and Measurement_plus_PP).

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units of the measured Entity. Ex: The ads had been absorbed into her brain during ["Count" many] ["Unit" HOURS] ["Entity" of television watching].

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: The known quantity with respect to an Attribute.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The item which is quantified in terms of the Attribute.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The aspect of the Entity which is being described and quantified.

frame.name: Measure_scenario
frame.definition: An Entity has a particular Value for an Attribute which may be described in several different ways, including: Ex: Degree of deviation from the Value expected for the kind of Entity seen in a particular instance, or in comparison to some other explicit comparison set. Ex: Absolute quantification in terms of the number of Counts of a particular Unit which equal the Value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Value
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Value from the norm.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: A standard measure, having a known value for the Attribute.

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units which are equivalent to the Value of the Entity.

frame.name: Change_operational_state
frame.definition:
A Device or machine is put in (or out of) service either by a volitional Agent or by a Cause event or force acting on the Device. The Time when and the Place where the Device is put in or out of use may be specified, as may be the Purpose of the human Agent in changing the operational state of the Device.
Ex: The laborer realized that ["age" he] ACTIVATED ["Device" the machine] but did not know how to stop it.

fe.name: Device
fe.definition:
The Device or machine that is in or out of operation.
Ex: ["Device" The night lights] were TURNED ON in the secondary school.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when a Device is put into or out of operation.
Ex: My dad TURNED the lights ON for me ["Time" at 10 o'clock]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place in which the Device is put into or out of operation.
Ex: Suddenly, the lights _got_ TURNED ON ["Place" on the Jamaica road bridge].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person who changes the operational state of the Device.
Ex: Instantly ["age" Sue] ACTIVATED the commlink on the wall.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the Device to begin to operate.
Ex: He was in his stocking feet while standing in the bayou that formed when ["Cause" the wind] TURNED the shower ON in that one upstairs bathroom.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The FE Purpose denotes a state of affairs that the Agent wants to bring about by putting the Device into operation.
Ex: They then ACTIVATED the beacon ["pur" in order to inform the International coastguard of their position].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the event of the Device's being caused to operate or cease to operate logically follows.
Ex: It works great for this price, I haven't ACTIVATED the cable box ["Explanation" because analog cable works like any TV tuner would].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (_hard_, _softly_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: I ["Manner" carefully] TURNED OFF the computers, turned off the lights, locked that back door, and went to my office to do the paper work.

lexunit.name: activate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make active or operative.

lexunit.name: turn on.v
lexunit.definition: COD: start the operation of something by means of a tap, switch, or button.

lexunit.name: turn off.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop the operation of something by means of a tap, switch, or button.

lexunit.name: boot.v
lexunit.definition: COD: start (a computer) and put it into a state of readiness for operation.

lexunit.name: shut off.a
lexunit.definition: FN: turning off, making non-operational

lexunit.name: deactivate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make (technical equipment or a virus) inactive by disconnecting or destroying it.

lexunit.name: cut.v
lexunit.definition: FN: deactivate, esp. a motor or device driven by a motor.

frame.name: Relation_between_individuals
frame.definition: Two sentient beings have a permanent or semi-permanent Relation to each other. This relation may be symmetrically construed as between the Individuals or it may be construed assymetrically, such that Individual_1 is identified by their relation to the (implicitly better-known) Individual_2.

fe.name: Individual_1
fe.definition: The individual being described in terms of Individual_2.

fe.name: Individual_2
fe.definition: The individual whose identity serves to identify Individual_2.

fe.name: Relation
fe.definition: The type of connection between the Individuals.

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: The individuals in a (symmetrically construed) Relation to each other.

frame.name: Use_vehicle
frame.definition: A Driver transports themself and possibly other passengers (the Theme) to another location.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme is the entity which moves by means of the Vehicle. Ex: ["Theme" Margeret] FLEW to Cabo San Lucas.

fe.name: Vehicle
fe.definition: The Vehicle is the means of conveyance of the Theme. It is usually expressed in a _PP_-complement or the direct object. Ex: Professor Frink SAILED to Italy ["Vehicle" on an oceanliner].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. Ex: We FLEW ["Source" from Atlanta].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory. Ex: Samantha always RODE ["Manner" gracefully] on the back of a motorcycle.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path describes the trajectory of the motion. Ex: The caravan RODE ["Path" through the desert].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is the endpoint of the trajectory of motion. Ex: We SAILED ["Goal" to Morocco].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The Distance is the extent of the motion. Ex: We FLEW ["Distance" 300 miles] in 40 minutes.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration is the amount of time the motion takes. Ex: We RODE in the van ["Duration" for 45 minutes].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs. Ex: We FLEW["Speed" at nearly 600 miles per hour].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: The Area is the location where the motion takes place. Ex: We RODE ["Area" around the state].

fe.name: Road
fe.definition: The Road is the thoroughfare on which the Vehicle travels. Ex: We RIDE the bus ["Road" on highway 580].

fe.name: Route
fe.definition: The Route is the usual path that the Vehicle travles. Ex: I RIDE ["Route" the London-Birmingham route] almost everyday.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the riding takes place. Ex: We will FLY back to New York ["Time" in September].

fe.name: Cotheme
fe.definition: A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Theme. Ex: My family always FLIES to New York ["CT" with our good friends, the Jacksons].

fe.name: Driver
fe.definition: The individual that directs the motion of the Vehicle

frame.name: Knot_creation_scenario
frame.definition: An Agent manipulates a long thin object (the Rope and creates a Knot.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the sentient being who manipulates the Rope.
Ex: ["Agent" Melissa] BRAIDED Jessica's hair.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which the Rope is manipulated.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Prof. Frink BRAIDED my hair ["Purpose" to make me look beautiful].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Terri TIED the rope around her waist ["Time" before scrambling up the side of the mountain].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Kelly TIED her laces around the back of her heel ["Reason" to combat loose shoes].

fe.name: Rope
fe.definition:
The basically linear object which is manipulated by the Agent to produce a Knot.
Ex: He TIED ["Rope" an electrical cable] around the trunk and his neck before hanging himself .

fe.name: Knot
fe.definition:
The stable configuration of a Rope which results from tying.
Ex: Jake TIED the cravat ["Knot" into an acceptable knot].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner in which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: John KNOTTED the tie ["Manr" tightly] around his neck.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.
Ex: Kelly TIED her laces ["Loc" around the back of her heel] to combat loose shoes.

frame.name: Mental_activity
frame.definition: In this frame, a Sentient_entity has some activity of the mind operating on a particular Content or about a particular Topic. The particular activity may be perceptual, emotional, or more generally cognitive. This non-lexical frame is intended primarily for inheritance.

fe.name: Sentient_entity
fe.definition: The individual whose mind has a particular piece of Content in it, or, more generically portrayed, whose mind is focussed on a particular Topic.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The situation or state-of-affairs that the Sentient_entity's attention is focussed on.

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition: The source of awareness or knowledge of the Content.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: A description of the kind of Content in the Sentient_entity's attention in terms of an idea which is salient throughout the Content.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the cognitive act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Sentient_entity that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: Expressor is the body part that reveals the Sentient_entity's state to the observer.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The category that an element of the Content is considered to belong to.

fe.name: Paradigm
fe.definition:
The system of knowledge which serves as the basis for the Sentient_entity's awareness.
Ex: ["Content" The formation of black holes] should be UNDERSTOOD ["Paradigm" in astrophysic terms].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time interval during which the Sentient_entity has the Content in their attention.

frame.name: Emotions
frame.definition: An Experiencer has a particular emotional State, which may be described in terms of a specific Stimulus that provokes it, or a Topic which categorizes the kind of Stimulus. Rather than expressing the Experiencer directly, it may (metonymically) have in its place a particular Event (with participants who are Experiencers of the emotion) or an Expressor (a body-part of gesture which would give an indication of the Experiencer's state to an external observer).

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition: The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

fe.name: Empathy_target
fe.definition: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response. In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus. Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

fe.name: State
fe.definition: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

frame.name: Summarizing
frame.definition:
A Communicator processes some information (either from textual or real-world/perceptual sources) regarding a State_of_affairs into a concise form (a summary) that contains the essential content in briefer form, and communicates this summary to an Addressee, or records it in a Medium. The State_of_affairs may be represented directly (e.g., outline _what happened_, _the situation abroad_), or as a textual source (summarizing _the documents_), or metonymically as some focal entity (a synopsis _of the candidates_).
Ex: ["Communicator" Frank] has already SUMMARIZED ["State_of_affairs" some of the reactions] ["med" on his weblog]. Ex: ["com" Director Van Auken] _gave_ a brief informational SYNOPSIS ["sta" of each applicant]. Ex: ["Communicator" He] BOILED DOWN ["State_of_affairs" the argument for domestic wiretapping] in one plainspoken and effective, if also deceptive, line... Ex: You should be able to summarize your findings to a lay audience. Ex: In her materials, she also OUTLINED the situation and major problems facing the company.
Some LUs, such as _summarize_ and _synopsis_ entail a preexisting body of information that has been processed into a briefer form by the Communicator. Others, such as _outline_ and _blueprint_ are compatible with, but do not entail, a preexisting, fully fleshed-out concept. E.g.,
Ex: Her book OUTLINES a new proposal for handling grammaticalization, though she doesn't flesh it out entirely.

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The Communicator creates and communicates the summary of the Information.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition: The Communicator communicates the summary to the Addressee.

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition: The State_of_affairs is summarized by the Communicator.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The textual or other Medium through which the Communicator summarizes.

fe.name: Summary
fe.definition:
The content that results from the summarization.
Ex: She SUMMARIZED our involvement ["sum" as a "qualified success"]. Ex: Aston BOILEDthe situation DOWN ["sum" to one word: FUBAR].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Communicator makes the Summary.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Communicator communicates.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the details of the action beyond the identity of the participants and the setting, especially descriptions of the Communicator that affect the action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action performed by the Communicator that brings about the communication.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that the Communicator is attempting to bring about by communicating.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time taken by the Communicator in creating and conveying the Summary.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: summarize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: give a discription of the main point(s) of something.

lexunit.name: synopsis.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a brief summary of something.

lexunit.name: boil down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: give a concise summary.

lexunit.name: outline.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a summary of.

lexunit.name: sum up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to summarize a State_or_affairs (note: this is the transitive usage e.g. "I'll sum up what he said...")

frame.name: Releasing_from_custody
frame.definition: The Authorities release a Suspect who has been held under supicion of having committed a crime.

fe.name: Authorities
fe.definition:
The Authorities are those who have the official authority to release a Suspect.
Ex: ["Auth" The police] RELEASED the suspect.

fe.name: Suspect
fe.definition:
The Suspect is the person released by the Authorities, having been held under suspicion of having committed a crime.
Ex: The police RELEASED ["Susp" the suspect].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner is the way in which the Authorities release the Suspect.
Ex: The police RELEASED the suspect ["Manner" carefully].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means identifies the means by which the Authorities release the Suspect.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The Reason identifies the reason for which the Authorities are releasing the Suspect.
Ex: The police RELEASED the suspect ["Reason" because he had a good alibi].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Authorities release the Suspect.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Placeidentifies the place where the Authorities release the Suspect.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Timeidentifies when the Authorities release the Suspect.

fe.name: Holding_location
fe.definition: The place that the Suspect is no longer confined to.

frame.name: Undergoing
frame.definition: An Entity is affected by an Event.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The thing which is affected by the Event.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: A change in the world which affects the Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the Entity undergoes the Event.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the Entity undergoes the Event.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: victim.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person harmed, injured, or killed as a result of a crime, accident, etc.

lexunit.name: undergo.v
lexunit.definition: COD: experience or be subjected to (something unpleasant or arduous).

lexunit.name: casualty.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person killed or injured in a war or accident.

frame.name: Execute_plan
frame.definition:
An Agent acts according to a , carrying it out (or taking steps to carry it out). In some cases, the Agent is a focal participant in the Plan, although a separate Focal_participant may also be mentioned. The Plan may be specified for the Duration for which it is in effect.
Ex: Health authorities say ["Agent" they] have _put_ ["Plan" measures] _into_ EFFECT ["Place" in all ports of entry and in centers of provinces]. Ex: ["Agent" Channing House] has recently IMPLEMENTED ["Plan" a new dining program for residents on pureed diets].
Note: the phrase is in the Being_in_effect frame.

fe.name: Plan
fe.definition: The Plan is a goal or purpose that the Agent carries out.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time for which the Plan is or is not in effect.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Agent puts the Plan into effect.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place at which the Plan is or is not operational.
[CHANGE: or, place where agent puts into effect? 2 fes?]

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs under which the Agent puts the Plan into effect.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A cause, reason, or other explanation for the implementation of the Plan

fe.name: Focal_participant
fe.definition:
The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Plan.
[CHANGE: may only be relevant for "implemented the policy for residents of florida only"]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent, often an institution or governmental organization, puts a Plan into effect. The Agent is generally a primary participant in the Plan, but a separate Focal_participant may be specified.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner describes some state of the Agent, or provides additional characterization of the event of executing the plan.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is an intermediate action done by the Agent in order to execute the Plan.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent executes the Plan.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes how fully the Plan was executed.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This FE describes the medium through which a plan was executed. It may occur in the same syntactic position as the Agent. Ex: The policy will be IMPLEMENTED ["Medium" by a new computer system].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of executing the plan. Ex: We IMPLEMENTED the new approach ["Outcome" with astounding results]

lexunit.name: implement.v
lexunit.definition: COD: put into effect.

lexunit.name: implementation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of implementing a plan.

lexunit.name: effect_((into_effect)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being or becoming operative.

lexunit.name: institute.v
lexunit.definition: FN: implement something

lexunit.name: force_((into_force)).n
lexunit.definition: FN: into effect

frame.name: Shooting_scenario
frame.definition: A firearm is discharged, causing the motion of a projectile. This frame exists primarily to relate frames.

fe.name: Firearm
fe.definition: The device used by the Agent to cause the motion of the Projectile.

fe.name: Projectile
fe.definition: The entity whose rapid, dangerous motion is caused by the Agent and/or Firearm.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the motion of the Projectile.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Projectile. Ex: Pat THREW the Javelin ["Distance" 50 meters].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion. Kim THREW the cat ["Goal" into the garden].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act of the Agent whereby the rapid motion of the Projectile is achieved.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: This FE is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal. I PUSHED the trolley ["Path" along the street].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: This FE is the starting point of motion. Pat dragged the box ["Source" out of the cupboard].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A description of the state of the Agent or Projectile during the event.
Ex: He SHOT three arrows at the target, ["dep" all unsuspecting as to why Harold had done so well].

fe.name: Area
fe.definition: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element. Kim PUSHED the lawnmower ["Area" around the garden].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location in which the shooting event takes place.
Ex: The bankrobbers were crazy enough to SHOOT at the clerks with an AK-47 ["Place" inside the bank]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the shooting event takes place.
Ex: The robbers SHOT at the clerks ["Time" as they ran out of the bank]

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The Agent's purpose in launching the Projectile
Ex: We mistook a satellite LAUNCHED ["pur" to study earthquakes] to be a missile, so we shot it down over the Pacific.

frame.name: Renting
frame.definition: A Lessee gains the use of Goods owned by a Lessor by payment to the Lessor.

fe.name: Lessee
fe.definition:
The individual that gains temporary use of the Goods by paying the Lessor
Ex: ["Lessee" We] 've been RENTING from him for years .

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is an item which is temporarily exchanged for Money in a transaction. Ex: I tried to HIRE ["Goods" a bicycle] .

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Ex: Will they allow you to LEASE the airfield ["Mns" by check]?

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for tempory use of the Goods. Ex: Sam CHARTERED the ship ["Money" for only $12,000].

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In isome cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: Jon RENTED a car for ["Rate" twenty dollars a day] .

fe.name: Lessor
fe.definition:
The individual who has permanent ownership of the Goods and allows them to be used by the Lessee temporarily.
Ex: Kim and Pat RENT the apartment ["Lessor" from Jess].

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Lee RENTS rooms ["Unit" by the hour].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location the renting takes place.
Ex: I RENTED the car ["Place" right next to the airport] .

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose for which the renting is performed.
Ex: Though he was already wanted , he RENTED a car ["Purpose" to make a getaway] .

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state-of-affairs from which the renting logically follows.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the purchasing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Lesseethat affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: She quit her old job and ["Manner" gleefully] LEASED a cheap, Upper East Side apartment.

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition: The individual intended by the Lessee to receive the Goods. Ex: She RENTED ["Recipient" him] a cadillac from the lot next door and they hit the road .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time that the Goods are (or have been) in the Lessee's possession.
Ex: Our neighbors have been RENTING their house ["Duration" for the last ten years].

fe.name: Purpose_of_goods
fe.definition: The Lessee's intended purpose for the Goods. Ex: I RENTED a computer["POG" to sit in my office].

lexunit.name: lease.v
lexunit.definition: COD: take (property) on lease; rent.

lexunit.name: rent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: with obj.; pay someone for the use of.

lexunit.name: charter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: hire (an aircraft, ship, or motor vehicle).

lexunit.name: hire.v
lexunit.definition: COD: obtain the temporary use of in return for payment.

frame.name: Renting_out
frame.definition: A Lessor who owns some Goods allows a Lessee to use the Goods temporarily in exchange for Money.

fe.name: Lessee
fe.definition: The Lessee has Money and wants the Goods. Ex: Lee RENTED a textbook ["Lessee" to Abby].

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The FE Goods is the item which is temporarily exchanged for Money. Ex: Kim RENTED ["Goods" the shed] out .

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. Ex: Abby RENTED her room ["Means" by putting an ad in the Examiner].

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. Ex: The x-ray machine was LEASED ["Money" for $12,000] to a small firm in Menlo Park .

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. Ex: The hostel RENTS a bunk ["Rate" for about 20 dollars a night] .

fe.name: Lessor
fe.definition: The Lessor has possession of the Goods and temporarily exchanges them for Money from a Lessee. Ex: So far, ["Lessor" my company] has RENTED the video more than three million times .

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP. Ex: Bob RENTS rooms ["Unit" by the hour].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the leasing takes place.
Ex: U-haul RENTS ["Place" almost everywhere].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A state-of-affairs from which the renting logically follows.
Ex: I RENTED it OUT ["Explanation" because since Ned died, nobody's been using it for anything].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the renting takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the renting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Lessor that affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_). Ex: Stuart ["Manner" reluctantly] RENTED her his last apartment .

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state of the Lessor after the sale has occurred. Ex: I SOLD the whole lot ["Result" at a loss].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time that the Goods are (or have been) in the Lessee's possession.
Ex: Our neighbors have RENTED their house out ["Duration" for the last ten years].

fe.name: Purpose_of_Goods
fe.definition: The Lessee's intended purpose for the Goods. Ex: He LEASED the filing robot to me ["POG" to organize all my legal documents].

fe.name: Reversive
fe.definition:
This FE indicates that the selling act reverses an earlier separate act in which the current Lessor rented or bought the Goods from the current Lessee.
Ex: There is a plan for Mercer to buy the ground and LEASE it ["Reversive" back] to the club

fe.name: Relay
fe.definition:
This FE indicates that the current leasing constitues a re-lease by the current Lessor of Goods that they bought or rented earlier from a third person (not the Lessee of the current leasing act).
Ex: My housemates RENTED my room ["Relay" on] to an English student .

lexunit.name: lease.v
lexunit.definition: COD: grant (property) on lease; let.

lexunit.name: rent.v
lexunit.definition: COD: let someone use (something) in return for payment.

frame.name: Trust
frame.definition: A Cognizer thinks that the Information given by a particular Source is correct. The specific Content or Topic of the Information may also be described.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer is the person who has an opinion about the reliability of a Source or the Information from the Source.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer trusts information about.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Degree to which the Cognizer trusts the Source.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of an aspect of the Cognizer that also affects the nature of the trusting, or a general comparison of the state-of-affairs to others.
Ex: She ["Manner" foolishly] BELIEVED him .

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
An object or action associated with the Cognizer which is so affected by the Cognizer's belief that it reveals the Cognizer's state.
Ex: Her UNBELIEVING ["Expressor" eyes] filled with tears of joy.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The individual that gives Information to the Cognizer.
Ex: Why should we BELIEVE ["sou" him] ?

fe.name: Information
fe.definition:
The text or speech which the Cognizer has heard and evaluates the truth of.
Ex: America TRUSTED ["inf" his declaration] , to their detriment .

lexunit.name: believe.v
lexunit.definition: COD: accept the statement of (someone) as true.

lexunit.name: reliable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: trustable.

lexunit.name: trustworthy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be relied on as honest, truthful, or reliable.

lexunit.name: credulous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a tendency to believe that a state of affairs exists without adequate evidence

lexunit.name: trust.v
lexunit.definition: FN: believe (someone, something)

lexunit.name: reliability.n
lexunit.definition: FN: degree to which (something) should be believed.

lexunit.name: trust.n
lexunit.definition: COD: firm belief in someone or something.

lexunit.name: credence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: belief in or acceptance of something as true.

lexunit.name: gullible.a
lexunit.definition: FN: having a tendency to trust a person too readily; easy to deceive

lexunit.name: faith.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the belief in something (often religious)

frame.name: Becoming_a_member
frame.definition: A New_member becomes a member of a socially-constructed Group. Ex: ["New_member" Seven new members and the three countries] JOINED ["Group" the alliance] ["Time" five years ago]. Ex: ["New_member" Most new students] ENROLL ["Group" in a university] ["Manner" without declaring a major]. Ex: It represents ["New_member" every man and woman who] has ENLISTED ["Group" in the armed forces] ["Purpose" to protect our families and serve the community].

fe.name: New_member
fe.definition:
The New_member becomes a member of a (socially-defined) Group.
Ex: Have ["new" you] SIGNED UP for the new Medicare Prescription program?

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the joining occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the purpose for which the New_member joins the Group.
Ex: In 1714 he ENLISTED in the Venetian army ["Purp" to fight against the Moslem Turks.]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the New_member joins the Group.
Ex: An avid skier myself, I ventured to Aspen and ENROLLED in Nevin's school ["Time" last winter] to see what all the fuss was about.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the New_member becomes part of the group.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a New_member that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency with which the New_member becomes a member of a Group.

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: The Group is a socially-constructed entity composed of members. Ex: Please JOIN ["gro" our club]! ["New_member" CNI]

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
A factor that explains why the New_member joins the Group.
Ex: I ENLISTED in the Navy ["exp" because no one else in my family had ever been in it before].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The capacity or role in which the New_member is placed upon joining the Group.
Ex: Rogers JOINED our company last year ["rol" as Vice President].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the New_member when they join.

fe.name: Reciprocation
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event paired with that of the main clause, which explains why the event of the main clause is expected. In particular, reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished in the main clause, or an action that is paired with the action in the main clause as the other side of an agreement.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.

lexunit.name: join.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become a member of.

lexunit.name: enlist.v
lexunit.definition: FN: join a group, especially a military organization.

lexunit.name: enroll.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to enter a group, especially by signing up.

lexunit.name: sign up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to agree to be a member of a group.

lexunit.name: enter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: join (an institution or profession).

frame.name: Front_for
frame.definition: An individual or organization, the Front, serves as a cover for an Illicit_activity or an Illicit_organization.

fe.name: Front
fe.definition: The Front acts as a legitimate individual, organization, or enterprise, but is truly a cover for an illicit organization or activity.

fe.name: Illicit_organization
fe.definition: The existence and activities of the Illicit_organization are concealed by the Front.

fe.name: Illicit_activity
fe.definition: The Illicit_activity of the Illicit_organizationis concealed by (the activities of) the Front.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the deceptive activity occurs

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Front is attempting to bring about.
Ex: He FRONTED for the mob ["pur" to get out of paying protection].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the fronting occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action taken by the Front to ensure successful deceit of authorities.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the similarity of the event to some other event, particularly descriptions of the Front that also affect the details of the action.

lexunit.name: front.v
lexunit.definition: FN: act legitimately so as to to conceal an organization or their activities.

lexunit.name: front.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person or organization serving as a cover for subversive activities.

lexunit.name: blind.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a cover for illicit activity.

frame.name: Terrorism
frame.definition: A Terrorist commits a violent or otherwise harmful Act upon a Victimin order to coerce or terrorize a government or populace. The Act may be commited in particular for political or ideological reasons, and is often directed at civilians, as opposed to government or military officials. It is most often in violation of one or many laws.

fe.name: Terrorist
fe.definition:
The Terrorist commits the Act of terror for political or ideological gains.
Ex: Several domestic ["Terrorist" TERRORISTS] were operating from the site during the mid 1990s.

fe.name: Act
fe.definition:
The Act is the harmful action performed by the Terrorist or terrorist organization.
Ex: Many have suffered due to their acts of ["Act" TERRORISM].

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition:
The Victim is most directly affected or harmed by the Act of terrorism.
Ex: Cowardly acts of TERRORISM ["vic" upon innocent men, women, and children] is not a doorway to Heaven, but a gateway to Hell.
Ex: Never have I seen such TERRORISM ["vic" on Christians] in Pakistan before.

fe.name: Organization
fe.definition:
A Terrorist may be part of a larger group or Organization of such people.
Ex: Several ["org" Pioneer Liberation] TERRORISTS were arrested earlier today.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any characterization or evaluation of the Terrorist or Act.
Ex: The ["des" armed] TERRORISTS were caught on tape.
Ex: TERRORISM

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Terrorist commits the Act.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The intermediate action performed by the Terrorist in order to comit the Act.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The location in time when the Act takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Act takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The action or state-of-affairs that the Terrorist is trying to accomplish by commiting the Act.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
The Instrument is used by the Terrorist in order to inflict harm or commit the Act.
Ex: The most recent threat to our security is ["ins" biological] TERRORISM.
Ex: Large-scale ["ins" CBW] TERRORISM is a constant worry to those in power.

lexunit.name: terrorism.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the use of violent acts against a population or government for political or ideological reasons.

lexunit.name: terrorist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who uses violence and intimidation in the pursuit of political aims.

lexunit.name: ecoterrorism.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the use or threat of use of destructive force upon the environment or natural resources in order to coerce a government.

lexunit.name: ecoterrorist.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who threatens to destroy natural resources or the environment in order to coerce governments.

lexunit.name: bioterrorism.n
lexunit.definition: FN: terrorism using biological weapons as a means of harm.

lexunit.name: bioterrorist.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a person who uses biological weapons as a means to inflict harm for political gain.

lexunit.name: ecoterrorist_((environmentalist)).n
lexunit.definition: FN: a terrorist primarily concerned with advancing pro-environmental causes.

lexunit.name: ecoterrorism.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the use or threat of violent acts in order to advance pro-environmental causes.

lexunit.name: terror.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the means by which terrorists wage war

frame.name: Money
frame.definition:
Money is a medium used for exchanging goods and services. It is in most cases issued by a govenment (its Creator) in the form of coins and banknotes. Particular amounts of it may have a designated or planned Use, or may have come from some Origin.
Ex: The ["mon" MONEY] ["Use" for our daughter's college education] is currently earning interest in a savings account.
Ex: The entire project ended up being funded with ["cre" Swiss] ["mon" FUNDS].
Ex: The use of ["Material" paper] ["mon" MONEY] really caught on in Europe in the 1700s

fe.name: Money
fe.definition: Money is used as a medium of exchange.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The use for which the Money is intended or designed.

fe.name: Creator
fe.definition: The government (or possibly other organization) that mints, issues and guarantees the legal use of the Money.

fe.name: Time_of_creation
fe.definition: The time at which an Money comes into existence or begins to be circulated.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The term used to refer to the Money.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: An indication of the subtype of Money.

fe.name: Material
fe.definition: Any indication of what makes up the Money, including components, ingredients, etc.

fe.name: Origin
fe.definition:
The process or means by which the MONEY comes to be possessed.
Ex: It turns out that the company used ["ori" drug] ["mon" MONEY] to develop this regionv

fe.name: Possessor
fe.definition:
The Possessor has control over the use the Money.
Ex: They managed to scam him out of most of ["pos" his] ["mon" CASH].

lexunit.name: money.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a medium of exchange in the form of coins and banknotes.

lexunit.name: cash.n
lexunit.definition: COD: money in coins or notes.

lexunit.name: funds.n
lexunit.definition: COD: financial resources.

lexunit.name: dough.n
lexunit.definition: FN: money (informal).

lexunit.name: capital.n
lexunit.definition: COD: wealth owned by a person or organization or invested, lent, or borrowed.

lexunit.name: dinero.n
lexunit.definition: COD: money.

lexunit.name: sterling.n
lexunit.definition: FN: money, esp. in the U.K.

frame.name: Risky_situation
frame.definition:
A particular Situation is likely (or unlikely) to result in a harmful event befalling an Asset. The Situation may be a state, an activity, or some focal entity that must be inferred to be part of some larger Situation involving both it and the Asset. Although the idea of a harmful event is crucial to the understanding of this frame, it is not expressible as an argument of the LUs in this frame.
Ex: _Is_ ["Situation" climate change] DANGEROUS ["Asset" for mankind]? Ex: Customers can make complaints about UNSAFE ["dan_ent" products]. Ex: The primary RISK _is_ ["Asset" to our infrastructure].
See the Run_risk frame for discussion on differentiation regarding the noun _risk_.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition:
The Situation which may lead to a harmful event.
Ex: Most people agree, ["Situation" going over 100mph] _is_ UNSAFE.

fe.name: Asset
fe.definition:
Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.
Ex: Honey is not SAFE ["Asset" for babies].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Situation and the state indicated by the target itself.
Ex: Rogue nations _are_ our ["Degree" greatest] THREAT.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: A particular location for which the Situation is safe. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location make various Situations safe or unsafe.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time period during which the Situation has the specified level of safety.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain in which the Situation is safe.
Ex: All of our websites _are_ ["dom" educationally] SAFE.

fe.name: Dangerous_entity
fe.definition:
A concrete or abstract entity which may come to cause the loss of, or damage to the Asset.
Ex: ["Dangerous_entity" That man] is a RISK!

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Asset encounters the Risky_situation.

lexunit.name: safe.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not likely to lead to harm or injury.

lexunit.name: unsafe.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not safe; dangerous.

lexunit.name: dangerous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able or likely to cause harm or injury.

lexunit.name: risky.a
lexunit.definition: FN: involving the chance of a negative outcome.

lexunit.name: risk.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a situation involving exposure to danger.

lexunit.name: threat.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the possibility of trouble or danger.

lexunit.name: danger.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a cause of harm or injury.

lexunit.name: riskily.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: incurring risk; exhibiting risky behavior.

lexunit.name: safely.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: without incurring any risk.

frame.name: Risk_scenario
frame.definition: An Asset is in a particular Situation, which has a likelihood of leading to or inviting a Harmful_event which will negatively affect the Asset.

fe.name: Asset
fe.definition: Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.

fe.name: Harmful_event
fe.definition: An event that may occur or a state which may hold which could result in the loss of or damage to the Asset.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition: The Situation under which the Asset is safe or unsafe.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Asset, the Situation, and state indicated by the target itself.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the degree of safeness holds.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place at which the degree of safeness holds.

frame.name: Process_uncompleted_state
frame.definition: A Process is in a state where it can no longer be completed.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the state takes place.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: This FE identifies the name of the Process that occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

frame.name: Process_pause
frame.definition: The Process stops making progress towards completion, but should resume and continue.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition: The Process which is halting.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the pause takes place.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Cause of the pause.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the pause in the Process occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which the event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the pause.

fe.name: Last_subevent
fe.definition:
The Last_subevent of an event.
Ex: The peace march STOPPED ["Last" with a prayer].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which a pause occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that a Process remains stopped.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition:
The number of times that the Process stops.,
Ex: Mining activities on the opal fields CEASED ["Freq" twice] in the last two weeks due to heavy rain storms

frame.name: Change_event_duration
frame.definition:
In this frame, an Agent or Cause changes the duration of an Event. The Event will then take place for a New_duration, rather than the Initial_duration. This can be done with by certain Means, in a certain Manner or to a certain Degree.
Ex: Don't let ["Agent" him] PROLONG ["Event" the discussion] ["New_duration" to an absurd length].
Ex: Harsh weather made it necessary to CUT ["Event" the tour] SHORT ["ini" from its original four months] ["new" to three]. ["Agent" CNI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The sentient entity that changes the duration of the Event.
Ex: Don't let ["Agent" him] PROLONG the discussion to an absurd length.

fe.name: New_duration
fe.definition:
The new duration of the Event.
Ex: Don't let him PROLONG the discussion ["new" to an absurd length].

fe.name: Initial_duration
fe.definition:
The planned duration of the Event before the change takes place.
Ex: Harsh weather combined made it necessary to CUT the tour SHORT ["ini" from its original four months] to three.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the change in duration of the Event is caused.
Ex: ["tim" Last week], he unnecessarily PROLONGED the agony, thinking that he could tough it out.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the initial and final durations differ from each other.
Ex: Too bad we can't EXTEND our vacation ["deg" even more].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event causing the change of the Event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).
Ex: Rain ["man" so cruelly] CUT SHORT the game against Bangladesh.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change of duration.
Ex: ["rea" Why] would someone CUT our time SHORT like that?

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The Event's duration is changed.
Ex: Don't let him PROLONG ["eve" the discussion] to an absurd length.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An event that causes the change in Event duration.
Ex: ["cau" Rain] so cruelly CUT SHORT the game against Bangladesh.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by changing the duration of the Event.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Event's duration.
Ex: It seems they are bent on PROLONGING conflict ["mea" by ignoring normal wartime conventions].

lexunit.name: prolong.v
lexunit.definition: COD: extend the duration of.

lexunit.name: abbreviate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: shorten.

lexunit.name: drag_out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: protract something unnecessarily.

lexunit.name: protract.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prolong; draw out.

lexunit.name: extend.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make longer; prolong.

lexunit.name: cut short.v
lexunit.definition: FN: abbreviate, stop prior to completion.

lexunit.name: shorten.v
lexunit.definition: COD: decrease the duration of something.

frame.name: Thriving
frame.definition:
An Entity is in a state such that it participates in a preponderance of states and events which are desirable for it. For living entities, this may entail a proliferation of instances of the entity, or of desireable properties associated with the (single) entity. For non-living entities (economies, political locales, academic topics, etc.), this entails a proliferation of instances, or of activities that lead to instances, or any attribute that would prevent the entity from disappearing. This state is conceived of as temporary, or at least contingent on a number of changeable factors. Words expressing the opposite state, i.e., a lack of such positive activity, are also in this frame.
Ex: ["tim" In the 1920s] ["ent" the peach industry] FLOURISHED ["pla" in Upson County].
Ex: ["ent" Construction companies] THRIVE ["cir" on public projects].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The ENTITY is experiencing a period of desirable events or states.
Ex: In the 1920s ["ent" the peach industry] THRIVED in Upson County.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.
Ex: In those nations, the economy LANGUISHES ["cir" under repressive regimes which do not govern for their people but rather against them].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time during which the Entity thrives.
Ex: ["tim" In the 1920s] the peach industry THRIVED in Upson County.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place where the thriving takes place.
Ex: Why was it that democracy FLOURISHED ["pla" in America]?

fe.name: Frequency
