fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The category in which the Entity thrives.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation for why or how the Entity thrives.

lexunit.name: thrive.v
lexunit.definition: COD: prosper; flourish.

lexunit.name: flourish.v
lexunit.definition: COD: grow or develop in a healthy or vigorous way.

lexunit.name: prosper.v
lexunit.definition: COD: succeed or flourish, especially financially; thrive.

lexunit.name: languish.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be in a weakened, unactive or depreciated state.

lexunit.name: slump.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a period of inactivity.

lexunit.name: do.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be (in the specified desirable or undesirable state).

lexunit.name: fare.v
lexunit.definition: COD: perform in a specified way in a particular situation or period:

lexunit.name: prosperity.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state or degree of (financial) well-being.

frame.name: Cause_change_of_strength
frame.definition: An Agent causes a Patient to be more strong, often resulting in something that is more secure and safe.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent fortifies the Patient.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The Patient is the entity that is being made stronger.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The resultant state of the action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by anAgent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Agent makes the Patient stronger.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Agent fortifies the Patient.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event which causes the Patient to become stronger.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances of the world at the time of the event (which do not bear directly on the event itself).

lexunit.name: fortify.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make stronger, more able to resist or exert force.

lexunit.name: strengthen.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make stronger.

lexunit.name: reinforce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give added strength to.

lexunit.name: weaken.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make weak.

frame.name: Change_resistance
frame.definition: An Agent changes a Patient's ability to resist literal or figurative attack. This frame differs from Cause_change_of_strength only in that the Patient is restricted to acting as a defensive force, i.e., it can resist but not exert force.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent makes the Patient more resistant to attack.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The Patient is the entity that is being made more resistant.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The resultant state of the action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by anAgent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Agent makes the Patient more resistant.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the Agent makes the Patient more resistant.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event which causes the Patient to become more resistant.

lexunit.name: buttress.v
lexunit.definition: COD: support or strengthen

lexunit.name: bulwark.v
lexunit.definition: FN: provide with a stronger defense; fortify.

lexunit.name: brace.v
lexunit.definition: COD: make stronger or firmer with wood, iron, etc.

frame.name: Means
frame.definition:
An Agent makes use of a Means (either an action or a (system of) entities standing in for the action) in order to acheive a Purpose.
(This frame may be broadened to include non-agentive intermediate actions.)
Ex: The primary MEANS ["Purpose" of gas detection] _is_ ["Means" mass spectroscopy] . Ex: ["Purpose" They learned of the attack] BY ["Means" monitoring the allied communications channels] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent uses the Means to acheive a Purpose.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action performed by the Agent.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The goal or purpose of the Agent.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Means.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Agent uses the Means.

lexunit.name: means.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an action or system by which a result is achieved.

lexunit.name: way.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a means for doing something.

lexunit.name: method.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a particular procedure for accomplishing or approaching something.

lexunit.name: technique.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a procedure that is effective in achieving an aim.

lexunit.name: procedure.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a series of actions conducted in a certain order or manner.

lexunit.name: approach.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a way of dealing with something.

lexunit.name: course_of_action.n
lexunit.definition: FN: way of dealing with a problem

lexunit.name: mechanism.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a process by which something takes place or is brought about.

lexunit.name: modus_operandi.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a way of doing something.

lexunit.name: nuts_and_bolts.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the basic means by which something is normally achieved.

lexunit.name: process.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a series of actions or steps towards achieving a particular end.

lexunit.name: recipe_((cooking)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: a set of instructions for preparing a dish.

lexunit.name: by.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: through the agency or means of.

lexunit.name: tactic.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an action or strategy carefully planned to achieve a specific end.

lexunit.name: on.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: by use of

frame.name: Surviving
frame.definition:
A Survivor manages to avoid being negatively affected, despite encountering a Dangerous_situation. The negative effect is most often death, destruction, or a metaphorical construal of one of these.
Ex: Wilderness Survival: Could ["sur" You] SURVIVE ["dan" the Wild]?
Ex: ["sur" More than 400 of the 600 residents] RODE OUT ["dan" the hurricane] ["Place" in Gulfport's 11-story high-rise beachfront facility].

fe.name: Survivor
fe.definition: The Survivor lives through a Dangerous_situation.

fe.name: Dangerous_situation
fe.definition: The Dangerous_situation is one in which people are likely or expected to be negatively affected.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Survivor (primarily) lives during the Dangerous_situation.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the surviving takes place.
Ex: ["tim" Last year], Florida residents SURVIVED the devastating triple punch of Hurricanes Frances, Ivan and Jeanne,

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action performed by the Survivor that enables them to live throug hthe Dangerous_situation.
Ex: They SURVIVED the devastation ["mea" by using age-old early warning systems].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Degree to which the Survivor survives.
Ex: Growing up in a rough section of the Bronx, New York, Bobby ["deg" barely] SURVIVED several serious bouts of rheumatic fever that left him with a damaged heart.

lexunit.name: survive.v
lexunit.definition: COD: continue to live or exist in spite of (an accident or ordeal).

lexunit.name: ride_out.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come safely through something.

lexunit.name: weather.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come safely through.

lexunit.name: survival.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being alive or existing

frame.name: Colonization
frame.definition:
A group of Colonists from a Homeland migrate to and proceed to settle in a New_area. The New_area then becomes their permanent home. The New_area and Homeland are in some way construed as being part of the same organization or system. In the case of (people from) nation-states colonizing other areas, the colony and nation-state are considered a single political entity. In the extended sense of living things in general colonizing or settling a new area, the original Homeland must still inhabited by some of the same group. In this sense Colonization is distinct from migration or exodus.
Ex: ["tim" In the 7th century BC], ["col" Phoenicians] COLONIZED ["new" the eastern section of Libya]. Ex: In the 7th century BC, ["hom" Phoenicians] COLONIZED the eastern section of Libya. Ex: ["col" Finns] COLONIZED ["new" the land] from the south ["tim" some 2,000 to 4,000 years ago] Ex: If a COLONY ["new" from Britain] was established in that large tract of Country, and if we were at war with Holland or Spain, we might very powerfully annoy either state from our new settlement.
This frame also includes metaphorical uses involving animals or plants, or abstract domains such as ideas.
Ex: ["col" Deciduous trees such as red alder] ["tim" subsequently] COLONIZED ["new" the logged area].
Ex: Conservatives don't get what the left gets, which is that ["col" the left] has ["tim" already] COLONIZED and converted ["new" whole university departments].
Ex: As the years progressed and adaptations occurred ["col" new species and subspecies] began to POPULATE ["hom" the islands].

fe.name: Colonists
fe.definition:
A group of people who move together to an area outside their Homeland for the purpose of settling.
Ex: ["col" Spain] SETTLED the northern areas of Mexico through the use of missions, civil settlements, and presidios.
Often the phrase expressing the Colonists will also encode the Homeland (e.g., _French people_, _China_), which we indicate with second-layer FE annotation.
Ex: In the 7th century BC, ["col" Phoenicians] COLONIZED the eastern section of Libya. Ex: In the 7th century BC, ["hom" Phoenicians] COLONIZED the eastern section of Libya

fe.name: Homeland
fe.definition: The Homeland is where the Colonists are originally from.

fe.name: New_area
fe.definition:
The Colonists move to the New_area, inhabiting it and (in the case of nation-states) extending the control of the Homeland.
Ex: Norse invaders in the 900s COLONIZED ["new" the North Midlands] more densely than any other part of England"

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the colonizing takes place.
Ex: The English COLONIZED the islands ["tim" in 1632].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the group of Colonists spreads across or inhabits the New_area.
Ex: In the reign of Elizabeth, the English strove to ["deg" thoroughly] COLONIZE Ireland, which they had originally invaded in the twelfth century.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose for which the colonizing is done.
Ex: Humans in the future may end up COLONIZING outer space ["pur" in order to survive].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Colonists, Homeland, or New_area.

lexunit.name: colonize.v
lexunit.definition: FN: extend the territory of a nation-state (or other system) by establishing other land as an area for settlement.

lexunit.name: colonist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a settler in or inhabitant of a colony.

lexunit.name: colony.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a country or area under the political control of another country and occupied by settlers from that country.

lexunit.name: settle.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (for a nation-state, or members thereof) go to a new area to live.

lexunit.name: settlement_((act)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action or process of settling.

lexunit.name: settlement_((entity)).n
lexunit.definition: COD: a place where people establish a community.

lexunit.name: settler.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who settles in an area, especially one with no or few previous inhabitants.

lexunit.name: people.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come to inhabit.

lexunit.name: populate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: form the population of (a place).

lexunit.name: repopulate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to grow a population again in an area after previous population that decreased or dispersed.

frame.name: Dominate_situation
frame.definition:
An Agent acts so as to be the strongest force, or most important causal factor in some Situation, to the exclusion of other competing actors.
Ex: York dominated the game as they held the ball on offense almost the entire 70 minutes. Ex: Is there a future for Unix in a market increasingly dominated by Microsoft? Ex: Walz dominated the debate so completely it was almost embarrassing.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the most forceful and pivotal factor in the situation.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition: The Situation is primarily affected by the Agent, in particular how it develops or concludes.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time when the Agent is dominant.
Ex: As discussed above, Ford DOMINATED the market ["tim" in the 1920s], then left the business to create production capacity for the Model A.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time over which the domination occurs.
Ex: Dinosaurs were vertebrate animals that DOMINATED the terrestrial ecosystem ["dur" for over 160 million years].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the domination takes place.
Ex: Indeed, ["pla" in all Latin America], United States corporations DOMINATED the key sectors of the economy.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the event as a whole, or of any of the participants that does not fit any of the other more specific Frame Elements.
Ex: Most predict that the top teams from last year to ["man" ruthlessly] DOMINATE the league.

lexunit.name: dominate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have a commanding or controlling influence over.

lexunit.name: domination.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a state of controlling force over a situation.

lexunit.name: dominant.a
lexunit.definition: COD: most important, powerful, or influential.

lexunit.name: predominate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be the strongest or main element.

frame.name: Dominate_competitor
frame.definition:
An Agent, by virtue of strength or forcefulness, controls, rules, or strongly influences some Patient in some Situation.
Ex: ["age" The fireballing righthander] looked poised to DOMINATE the Yankees yet again, striking out seven straight batters during one stretch

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent controls the Patient by being forceful and possibly aggressive.

fe.name: Patient
fe.definition: The Patient is trying to gain control of a situation, but ends up being subject to the control and influence of the Agent.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition: The Situation within which the Agent is able to gain control over the Patient (thus excluding them from controlling the Situation).

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The period of time over which the domination occurs.
Ex: For England and France, DOMINATION over their colonies ["dur" during the colonial period] was mainly a cultural obligation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
A description of the event as a whole, or of any of the participants that does not fit any of the other more specific Frame Elements.
Ex: He managed to be DOMINANT over most of the rest of the staff, ["man" in a good way].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where the domination occurs.
Ex: Women tend to DOMINATEmen ["pla" at home and at Church].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the domination takes place.
Ex: Their role models might have DOMINATED women ["tim" in the past]; they may not have understood the concept of equality.

lexunit.name: dominate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: control, rule, or influence.

lexunit.name: domination.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of control over someone or something.

lexunit.name: strongman.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a leader who rules by the exercise of threats, force, or violence.

frame.name: Domination
frame.definition:
An Agent has a influential, controlling position in a Situation, and is the primary causal factor in the development of the Situation, leaving other Competitors unable to take controlling positions.
Two perspectives are taken on this frame, one where the Agent is viewed as controlling primarily the Situation, and another where the Agent is viewed as primarily influencing the other Competitors in the Situation.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent has a controlling position in the Situation.

fe.name: Situation
fe.definition: The Situation is primarily affected by the Agent, in particular how it develops or concludes.

fe.name: Competitor
fe.definition: The Competitors are trying to gain control of a situation, but end up being subject to the control and influence of the Agent.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the domination takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location of the dominationw

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner of the domination.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time over which the domination takes place.

frame.name: Control
frame.definition:
A Controlling_entity, Controlling_situation, or Controlling_variable control a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable. The latter, dependent, element or some aspect of it is not just influenced, but determined by the controlling element.
Ex: Can ["cone" you] CONTROL ["depe" the robot]? Ex: Although ["cone" you] may not be able to CONTROL ["deps" every situation], you can control your reaction. Ex: ["cone" Students] do not _have_ CONTROL ["depv" over the temperature of the heating water]. Ex: Everyone knows that ["conv" the price of oil] CONTROLS ["depv" the price of asphalt].

fe.name: Controlling_entity
fe.definition: A thing or person whose behavior controls a Dependent_situation, Dependent_variable, or Dependent_entity.

fe.name: Dependent_entity
fe.definition: An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by an Controlling_entity or an Controlling_situation.

fe.name: Controlling_variable
fe.definition: A scalar variable (with unspecified value) which has an effect on the Dependent_entity, Dependent_variable, or Dependent_situation.

fe.name: Dependent_situation
fe.definition: A situation that whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by an Controlling_entity, Controlling_event, or Controlling_variable.

fe.name: Dependent_variable
fe.definition:
A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of an Influencing_entity, a Influencing_variable, or an Influencing_situation.
Ex: Move the slider on the SpeedBar while playing audio or video material to CONTROL ["depv" playback speed].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Influencing_entity effects the Dependent_entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the controlling occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the controlling occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Influencing_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

lexunit.name: control.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to (primarily) determine various features of some situation or entity.

lexunit.name: determine.v
lexunit.definition: COD: cause to occur in a particular way; be the decisive factor in.

frame.name: Be_in_control
frame.definition: A Controlling_entity is in conscious control over a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.

fe.name: Controlling_entity
fe.definition: A thing or person whose behavior controls a Dependent_situation, Dependent_variable, or Dependent_entity.

fe.name: Dependent_entity
fe.definition: An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by an Controlling_entity or an Controlling_situation.

fe.name: Dependent_situation
fe.definition: A situation that whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by an Controlling_entity, Controlling_event, or Controlling_variable.

fe.name: Dependent_variable
fe.definition:
A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of an Influencing_entity, a Influencing_variable, or an Influencing_situation.
Ex: Move the slider on the SpeedBar while playing audio or video material to CONTROL ["depv" playback speed].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Controlling_entity effects the Dependent_entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the controlling occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the controlling occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Controlling_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

lexunit.name: control.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have control or command of.

lexunit.name: control.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the power to influence people's behaviour or the course of events.

frame.name: Destiny
frame.definition:
An State_of_affairs will come to hold with respect to a Protagonist at some future time. The Protagonist may or may not be conceived of as having control over whether the State_of_affairs will hold: previous actions or circumstances, or some hidden power may have already determined that it will occur.
Ex: ["soa" Exile] _was_ ["pro" his] FATE and he triumphantly turned it into the fruit of his life.
Ex: One could say that it _was_ ["pro" Indonesia's] DESTINY ["soa" to initiate the decolonization process].
Ex: ["pro" The sun's] ultimate FATE _is_ ["rol" as a white dwarf, a dense, cold core the size of the earth].
Ex: At the time it did not appear that ["soa" greatness] _was_ _in_ her STARS.

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition: The State_of_affairs that is destined to occur to the Protagonist.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist is the one for whom the future State_of_affairs is destined.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A description of the sort of State_of_affairs that will occur.
Ex: You are an important person with a ["des" glorious] DESTINY and you have a wonderful biography written about you.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition:
The Role filled by the Protagonist in his/her destiny.
Ex: Deciding that his true DESTINY _is_ ["rol" as a healer], Henderson returns home, planning to enter medical school.
Ex: His DESTINY ["rol" as the disciple of Shri Krishna] is to become the prototype of the perfect Yogi

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time for which the Protagonist's future is determined.
Ex: Their DESTINY ["tim" over those years] was to gradually take charge of most of the world's operations.

lexunit.name: destiny.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the events that will necessarily happen to a particular person in the future.

lexunit.name: fate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the development of events outside a person's control, regarded as predetermined by a supernatural power.

lexunit.name: lot.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's destiny, luck, or condition in life.

lexunit.name: fortune.n
lexunit.definition: FN: destiny.

lexunit.name: kismet.n
lexunit.definition: COD: destiny; fate.

lexunit.name: stars.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a planet, constellation, or configuration regarded as influencing one's fortunes or personality.

lexunit.name: doom.n
lexunit.definition: COD: death, destruction, or another terrible fate.

lexunit.name: the breaks.n
lexunit.definition: FN: unavoidable circumstances, fate.

frame.name: Luck
frame.definition: A State_of_affairs is evaluated as good (or bad), against a background assumption that previously, the State_of_affairs was thought to be unlikely to occur. The State_of_affairs holds for a particular Protagonist.

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition: The State of affairs that is evaluated.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist is the one for whom the destiny is evaluated.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A description of the sort of State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The Role filled by the Protagonist.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time for which the Protagonist's destiny is good.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the State_of_affairs is lucky (either a degree of goodness or a degree of unexpectedness, or both).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Protagonist has luck.

lexunit.name: lucky.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (of positively-evaluated events or states) be apparantly the result of chance or unknown forces.

lexunit.name: luck.n
lexunit.definition: COD: success or failure apparently brought by chance.

lexunit.name: happy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: fortunate and convenient

lexunit.name: fortunate.a
lexunit.definition: COD: favoured by or involving good luck.

lexunit.name: luckily.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: by luck.

lexunit.name: fortunately.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: by good fortune.

lexunit.name: fortune.n
lexunit.definition: COD: luck, especially good luck.

lexunit.name: fortuitous.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being of a causeless happy accident

frame.name: Coincidence
frame.definition: A State_of_affairs (a state or event) either holds or occurs, and is presented as being causally independent of other (implicit) states or events that might otherwise have been expected to be causally related to the State_of_affairs. The Time or Place may also be mentioned.

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
A State_of_affairs (that is, an event or state) that holds independently of (potentially) causally-related States of affairs.
Ex: Is it a COINCIDENCE ["soa" that most of the planets fall within the Titius-Bode law's boundaries]?

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the State_of_affairs holds.
Ex: ["tim" Last night's] COINCIDENCES were too much for me to handle.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place where the State_of_affairs holds.
Ex: Several strange COINCIDENCES ["pla" at the airport] got the attention of federal officials.

lexunit.name: coincidence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a remarkable concurrence of events or circumstances without apparent causal connection.

lexunit.name: happenstance.n
lexunit.definition: COD: coincidence.

lexunit.name: accident.n
lexunit.definition: COD: something that happens by chance or without apparent cause.

lexunit.name: happen.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come about by chance.

frame.name: Enforcing
frame.definition:
An Agent acts to ensure that a Rule (often a constraint on behavior) is being followed. The Agent's action is according to a general plan for Rules (such that implicit in the Rule is the affordance to certain entities to ensure that the Rule is followed). The Rule may be specified for the Duration for which it is in effect.
Ex: Why don't ["Agent" we] ENFORCE ["Rule" the 20000 gun laws currently on the books across the nation]? Ex: ["Medium" Computer systems] can ["Manner" ruthlessly] ENFORCE ["Rule" rules and standards] ["Duration" indefinitely]. Ex: Can ["Agent" a landlord] ["Rule" rules] ["Focal_participant" upon tenants]?

fe.name: Rule
fe.definition:
The Rule is the set of constrants on behavior that the Agent implements (i.e., forces others to obey or face consequences).
Ex: Employers should strictly ENFORCE ["Rule" a prohibition against use of any substance that may affect a worker's physical or mental ability].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time for which the Rule is or is not in effect.
Ex: The coat-and-tie dress code for the Plimsoll Club in the World Trade Center was strictly ENFORCED ["dur" for years].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Agent enforces the Rule.
Ex: That particular regulation was only ENFORCED ["tim" in 1920].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place at which the Rule is or is not enforced.
Ex: For this reason they ENFORCED the settlement system ["place" in America] just as strictly as in Germany.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs under which the Agent puts the Rule into effect.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A cause, reason, or other explanation for the enforcing of the Rule.

fe.name: Focal_participant
fe.definition:
The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Rule.
Ex: Can a landlord rules ["Focal_participant" upon tenants]?

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent, often an institution, governmental organization, or arm thereof, puts into effect (i.e., enforces) a Rule.
Ex: Can ["Agent" a landlord] rules upon tenants?

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner describes some state of the Agent, or provides additional characterization of the event.
Ex: The coat-and-tie dress code for the Plimsoll Club in the World Trade Center was ["Manner" strictly] ENFORCED for years.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The Means is an intermediate action done by the Agent in order to enforce the Rule.
Ex: Since 1961 the church has ENFORCED it ["mea" by "disfellowshipping" or expelling un-repentant members who wilfully accept prohibited blood components].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent enforces the Rule.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes how fully the Rule was enforced.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: This FE describes the medium through which the rule was enforced. It may occur in the same syntactic position as the Agent. Ex: The rules will be ENFORCED ["Medium" by a new computer system that tracks people's movements].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of enforcing the rule.

lexunit.name: enforce.v
lexunit.definition: COD: compel compliance with (a law, rule, or obligation).

lexunit.name: enforcement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The act of enforcing.

frame.name: Emptying_scenario
frame.definition: The abstract scene in which an Agent affects a Container and a Theme so that the Theme ends up not co-located with the Container.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying. Ex: ["Agent" Pat] CLEARED the table of dishes.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of". Ex: Pat CLEARED the table ["Thm" of dishes].

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The Sourceis the region or container which is emptied of something. In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object. Ex: Pat CLEARED ["Src" the table].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. Ex: Kim EMPTIED the basin ["Path" over the edge of the balcony].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Ex: The children EMPTIED the toy box ["Goal" onto the floor].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying. Ex: ["Dep" Naked], ["Agent" Millhouse] EMPTIED ["Source" the trash can].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the Agent emptying the Source.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source. Ex: I EMPTIED the tub ["Inst" with a bucket]. Ex: I PEELED the oranges ["Inst" with a knife].

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying. Ex: ["Cause" A basic washing] can DEGREASE ["Source" your workclothes].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the emptying takes place.
Ex: Don't EVISCERATE him ["pla" in the house]!

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the emptying takes place.
Ex: The prisoners were DELOUSED ["tim" in June and August].

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

frame.name: Besieging
frame.definition:
An Assailant, a group of armed forces, surrounds the Victim, a military location and the people within it, in an attempt to cut the Victim off from the outside, with the goal of either forcing their surrender or weakening them so that an invasion would be successful. A successful siege is often followed by the Assailant taking control of (the land held by) the Victim.
Ex: ["tim" Towards the end of the summer], ["ass" a great English host] BESIEGED ["vic" the Danish fort of Tempsford] and took it, killing the last Danish king of East Anglia.

fe.name: Assailant
fe.definition: The Assailant is a group of armed forces (or, metonymically, their commander or the organization they represent) that encircles, surrounds, or otherwise cuts off the Beseiged in an attempt to force surrender.

fe.name: Victim
fe.definition: The Victim is the fortification or geopolitical entity that is being attacked.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.

fe.name: Weapon
fe.definition: An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

lexunit.name: besiege.v
lexunit.definition: COD: surround (a place) with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender.

lexunit.name: siege.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling the surrender of those inside.

lexunit.name: beleaguer.v
lexunit.definition: COD: lay siege to.

lexunit.name: invest.v
lexunit.definition: COD: surround (a place) in order to besiege or blockade it.

lexunit.name: investment.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act or process of laying siege to.

lexunit.name: siege.v
lexunit.definition: FN: lay siege to.

lexunit.name: besiegement.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act or process of besieging.

frame.name: Be_subset_of
frame.definition:
A Part is considered to be a member of the set described by the Total. The relationship between Part and Total subset-superset rather than part-whole (as it is in the frames Part_whole and Including).
Ex: ["Part" Dr. Nelson] NUMBERS ["Total" among the world?s foremost geotechnical engineering experts].
Ex: ["Part" Restaurant-Pizzeria Dante] COUNTS ["Total" among the few restaurants of Florence where you can find good typical Tuscan and fish dishes and a first-class pizza].

fe.name: Total
fe.definition:
The complex multi-part entity of which a constituent Part is specified.
Ex: As a representative in Congress in the years 1783-85, Gerry NUMBERED ["Total" among those who had possessed talent as Revolutionary agitators and wartime leaders].

fe.name: Part
fe.definition:
A subset of the Total.
Ex: Just be glad that ["par" you] number among the living.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the frequency with which the Part is included in the Total.
Ex: The sort of equipment that astronomers use to detect extrasolar objects ["fre" often] COUNTS among the equipment found in any radio enthusiast's workshop.

fe.name: Contrast_set
fe.definition: This FE indicates other totalities that the Part may also be a subset of.

fe.name: Subregion
fe.definition: This FE indicates the sub-location of the Total in which the Part is included. [MAY BE UNNECESSARY]

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the subset relation holds.
Ex: ["tim" At that time], the factory NUMBERED among the largest in the western half of North America.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place at which the subset relation holds.
Ex: ["pla" In Europe], the sport COUNTS among the economic branches of industry which generate employment among the young people.

lexunit.name: number.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be a member a group.

lexunit.name: count.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be a member of a group.

lexunit.name: among.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: being a member or members of (a larger set).

lexunit.name: subset.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a part of a larger group of related things.

frame.name: Being_in_category
frame.definition: An Item belongs to a Category, as (often implicitly) conceived of by a Cognizer.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition:
This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an oblique.
Ex: But ["Cog" to me], a bad thought CONSTITUTES a sin just as well.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition:
This is the entity which is is an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as the external argument.
Ex: To me, ["Item" finding this] _is_ TANTAMOUNT ["Category" to finding the fabeled El Dorado].

fe.name: Category
fe.definition:
This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by _as_ or _under_.
Ex: I'd say that this book COUNTS ["Cat" as fiction].

fe.name: Criteria
fe.definition:
This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified _by color_ or _by finish (matte or gloss)_; if they are classified by color, one can be classified _as orange_ and another _as red_. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by _by_, or as a complex PP of the form _on the basis of..._:
Ex: If it COUNTS as knowledge in part ["Crit" on the basis of justification from another source], it must be in part based on that source

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which an Item (metaphorically) is construed as being in a Category.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act or state of affairs by which the Item (perhaps metaphorically) is interpreted as being in a Category.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization holds.
Ex: Fold in inflation and what COUNTED as shameful gouging ["Time" 20 years ago] is today called charging what the market will bear.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds. Ex: Material posessions COUNT as valuable ["Circumstances" in a particular society].

lexunit.name: tantamount.a
lexunit.definition: COD: equivalent in seriousness to; virtually the same as.

lexunit.name: count.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be a member of.

lexunit.name: amount.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be the equivalent of.

lexunit.name: constitute.v
lexunit.definition: COD: be or be equivalent to.

frame.name: Inclusion_scenario
frame.definition: A Part is either a subset of a collection of items that make up a Whole, or is a subpart of a singular Whole. This frame covers both super/sub-set relations and part-whole relations.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the inclusion relation holds.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the inclusion relation holds.

frame.name: Being_included
frame.definition: A Part is profiled as being a subset or constituent subpart of a Whole. This is in contrast to Inclusion frame, wherein the same relation is seen from the point of view of the Whole.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.

frame.name: Set_relation
frame.definition: A Superset has several members, a part of which is the Subset. This frame exists largely for the purposes of inheritence.

fe.name: Superset
fe.definition: The Superset is the larger collection of entities that includes the Subset.

fe.name: Subset
fe.definition: The Subset comprises a part of the Superset.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the set relation holds.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the set relation holds.

frame.name: Wholes_and_parts
frame.definition: A Whole is made up of multiple Parts, which themselves may not be independent of each other or of the Whole. Wholes_and_parts is contrasted with Set_relation, where the Whole is simply a set of a number of (usually independent) parts.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.

fe.name: Part
fe.definition: The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the inclusion relation holds.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the inclusion relation holds.

frame.name: Vocalizations
frame.definition: This frame is concerned with the sounds produced by animate entities by means of their vocal tracts. Descriptions of sounds from artifacts meant to emulate such sounds, or to act as vocalizing animals or people, are also treated here as figurative language.

fe.name: Sound_source
fe.definition:
An entity that is construed as a single point source emitting sound.
Ex: He woke up because of the CRIES ["Sound_source" of the crows outside].

fe.name: Location_of_sound_source
fe.definition:
The place from which the sound emanates.
Ex: There followed a small silence that was interrupted by a distant CRIESof caged birds["Location_of_sound_source" from the interior].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location at which sound is produced. This FE differs from Location_of_sound_source in that it does not highlight the sound's spreading from its source to the perceiver's location, which is usually indicated by the preposition "from".
Ex: The HISS of snakes ["Place" outside the tent] was a constant source of worry.

fe.name: Internal_cause
fe.definition:
The noise-making may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, that is the mental or emotional state of an animate Sound_source.
Ex: She checked a GIGGLE ["Internal_cause" of hysteria]

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Certain properties of the sound relating to its production, loudness, etc may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of a sounds as such: loudly, shrilly, etc.
Ex: The Brigadier had heard the ["Manner" faint] SQUAL of rats.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Expressions that indicate the loudness of the sound.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE idntifies the Reason that the Sound_source produces the sound. Generally, this is some external stimulus that prompts the Sound_source to make noise.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The Path along which the sound travels away from the Sound_source.
Ex: The books he wrote later tell how he never forgot the HOWL of the wolf ["Path" across the icy field of Otsego] on cold winter nights.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Vocalization event occurs.

lexunit.name: cry.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a distinctive call of a bird or other animal.

lexunit.name: howl.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a long doleful cry uttered by an animal such as a dog.

frame.name: Carry_goods
frame.definition: A Distributor sells, lends, or otherwise distributes a class of Goods. In the prototypical case, the Distributor is a retailer who generally keeps some type of Goods on site for the purpose of selling it to a buyer. Extentions include lending Goods (e.g., libraries, movie rental outlets), organization-internal distribution (as in a hospital), or other non-commercial distribution centers. The Goods are constrained to be a type of item (e.g., _canned goods_, _antique dressers_) rather than a particular or unique item (e.g., _Smith's last self-portrait_, _that guitar I saw here last week_). Note that a Distributor may _carry_ some particular goods, but may not have it _on hand_ at that exact moment.

fe.name: Distributor
fe.definition: The Distributor maintains a store of Goods for the purpose of selling or otherwise distributing them.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: The Goods are kept on hand and distributed by the Distributor.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Distributor carries the Goods.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place indicates where the carrying of Goods occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the storing of goods which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_) and salient characteristics of a Distributor that also affect the action (_deliberately_, _carefully_).

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE indicates the length of time that the Distributor carries the Goods.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

lexunit.name: carry.v
lexunit.definition: COD: keep a regular stock of.

lexunit.name: stock.v
lexunit.definition: COD: have or keep a stock of

frame.name: Breaking_off
frame.definition:
An single Sub_part breaks off from a Whole.
Ex: ["sub" The original sword] may have CHIPPED ["Whole" off of the statue] ["Time" long ago].

fe.name: Sub_part
fe.definition:
The part of the Whole that is conceived as being broken or taken off from the remaining part of the whole.
Ex: ["Sub_part" The handle] BROKE off of the pot.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The piece that is presented in a less prominent position, and which is the landmark or remaining whole from which Sub_part breaks off. Ex: The handle BROKE ["who" off of the pot].

fe.name: Criterion
fe.definition: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the breaking off of the Sub_part happens.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the breaking off occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking off.

lexunit.name: chip.v
lexunit.definition: FN: break off, especially a small piece.

frame.name: Fragmentation_scenario
frame.definition:
A Whole fragments or breaks into Parts, or alternatively a part, Part_1, breaks off from the rest of the item, called Part_2.
Ex: ["Time" Last year], ["Part_1" it] BROKE ["Part_2" off from the Ross Ice Shelf] and began drifting out to sea.
Ex: ["Whole" The calved ice] BROKE ["Parts" into three large icebergs, named A22, A23 and A24].

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The Whole is a single entity which breaks into Parts.

fe.name: Parts
fe.definition: This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from fragmentation of a Whole.

fe.name: Part_1
fe.definition: Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned. This is most often the external argument of a verb.

fe.name: Part_2
fe.definition: Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement.

fe.name: Criterion
fe.definition: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing any of the undergoers of the fragmentation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the fragmenting occurs.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the breaking occurs.

fe.name: Resistant_surface
fe.definition:
The hard surface against which the Whole (or Part_1) breaks.
Ex: Too fragile a knife will SHATTER ["res" on the stone].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action or state that enables the fragmentation.
Ex: As the energy of the string increases, it FRAGMENTS ["mea" by producing quark-antiquark (or diquark-antidiquark) pairs at the breakpoints].

lexunit.name: break.v
lexunit.definition: COD: separate into pieces as a result of a blow, shock, or strain.

lexunit.name: shatter.v
lexunit.definition: COD: break suddenly and violently into pieces.

lexunit.name: fragment.v
lexunit.definition: COD: break into fragments.

lexunit.name: splinter.v
lexunit.definition: FN: break into splinters.

lexunit.name: snap.v
lexunit.definition: FN: break quickly, often with a sharp sound.

frame.name: Breaking_apart
frame.definition:
A Whole breaks apart into Pieces, resulting in the loss of the Whole (and in most cases, no piece that has a separate function).
Ex: ["Whole" The plane] ["Manner" violently] BROKE APART ["Place" in mid-air].
Ex: And then, I finally realized that it must have been the case that ["who" a meteorite] BROKE APART ["Pieces" into at least 3 large pieces].

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition: The Whole goes into Pieces which were not (necessarily) definable subparts prior to breaking.

fe.name: Pieces
fe.definition: The Pieces result from the breaking apart of the Whole.

fe.name: Criterion
fe.definition: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the breaking apart takes place.w

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location at which the breaking apart takes place.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking apart.
Ex: The crew donned immersion suits and abandoned ship into a life raft as their vessel BROKE APART ["mea" by wave action].

lexunit.name: break_apart.v
lexunit.definition: FN: break into fragments.

lexunit.name: break down.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come apart into small fragments.

frame.name: Becoming_separated
frame.definition:
A Whole separates into Parts, or one part of a whole, called Part_1, becomes separate from the remaining portion, Part_2.
Ex: ["Whole" This small channel] meanders through marsh and wetland, SPLITTING ["Parts" into several smaller channels that empty into Lake St. Clair].
Ex: Just crack one open and if ["Part_1" the yoke] ["Manner" quickly] SEPARATES ["Part_2" from the whites], they are probably bad.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
The Whole is a single entity or an aggregate of entities which separates into Parts.
Ex: Metalworkers? union to SPLIT ["Whole" into regional divisions]

fe.name: Parts
fe.definition:
This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from separation of a Whole:
Ex: These daughter chromosomes then begin to SEPARATE ["Parts" from each other], each moving away from the metaphase plate and toward one of the two spindle pole regions. Ex: Watch as they SPLIT ["Parts" into many differently-shaped bits].

fe.name: Part_1
fe.definition:
Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned.
Ex: Initially, ["Part_1" the front part] SEPARATED from the rest of the body.

fe.name: Part_2
fe.definition:
Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement.
Ex: Initially the front SPLIT ["Part_2" from the rest of the body]

fe.name: Criterion
fe.definition: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the separation. Criterion is typically expressed as a PP headed by _by_, or as a complex PP of the form _on the basis of_.... Ex: Particles will therefore only SEPARATE ["Crit" on the basis of contact angle] as long as their mass is between an upper and lower critical value.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the undergoers of the separation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An intermediate action or event that enables the separation.
Ex: Explore how cells DIVIDE ["Mns" by undergoing mitosis].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Time when the separation occurs.
Ex: However it is believed they SEPARATED ["Time" at least 2 if not 3 million years ago]..

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
Where the separation occurs.
Ex: The two parts likely SEPARATED ["Place" above the Atlantic].

lexunit.name: separate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come apart.

lexunit.name: split.v
lexunit.definition: FN: come into pieces, especially violently.

lexunit.name: divide.v
lexunit.definition: FN: separate into parts.

frame.name: Having_or_lacking_access
frame.definition: A Theme has access to a Useful_location or is blocked from it by a Barrier.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme whose motion is blocked or free.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the Theme exceeds or falls short of the ability to move to the Useful_location
Ex: He has ["Degree" full] ACCESS to the facilities.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances under which the Theme meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions for getting to the Useful_location.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An entity, event, or state that causes the Theme to be meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for entering the Useful_location.

fe.name: Useful_location
fe.definition: The place or thing that the Theme is headed towards, despite a potential or actual Barrier.

fe.name: Barrier
fe.definition: An entity that (at least potentially) prevents the Theme from getting to the Useful_location.

lexunit.name: access.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the right or opportunity to use something or see someone.

lexunit.name: blocked.a
lexunit.definition: FN: unable to enter or access.

lexunit.name: accessible.a
lexunit.definition: COD: able to be accessed.

frame.name: Access_scenario
frame.definition: A Theme is or is not capable of entering or accessing a Useful_location because of/despite a Barrier.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme whose motion is blocked or free.

fe.name: Useful_location
fe.definition: The place or thing that the Theme is headed towards, despite a potential or actual Barrier.

fe.name: Barrier
fe.definition: An entity that (at least potentially) prevents the Theme from getting to the Useful_location.

frame.name: Openness
frame.definition: A Useful_location is accessible to some (possibly generic) Theme despite a potential Barrier, or is not accessible because of the Barrier.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme whose motion is blocked or free.

fe.name: Useful_location
fe.definition: The place or thing that the Theme is headed towards, despite a potential or actual Barrier.

fe.name: Barrier
fe.definition: An entity that (at least potentially) prevents the Theme from getting to the Useful_location.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which a Theme can easily access the Useful_location

lexunit.name: open.a
lexunit.definition: COD: allowing access, passage, or view; not closed, fastened, or restricted.

lexunit.name: closed.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not open or allowing access.

frame.name: Earnings_and_losses
frame.definition:
An Earner receives Earnings by providing Goods to a Buyer; providing the Goods also generally entails a cost, which may or may not be included in the consideration. This frame emphasizes the effect on the Earner and often generalizes across an indefinite number of transactions with various parties. Some of the LUs (e.g. _earn.v_) primarily refer to the to the Earnings without reference to cost, others to the amount the Earnings differ from the cost, emphasizing either a net loss (e.g. _loss.n_) or net gain (e.g. _net.n_).
Ex: This reflects the 15 % jump in ["Earnings" EARNINGS] over 1994 . Ex: ["Earner" We] MADE ["Earnings" nearly two million] ["Goods" on resales alone] ["Time" last year] . Ex: After a ["Earnings" $ 1.5 million] LOSS , the company is in no state to continue .

fe.name: Buyer
fe.definition: The Buyer is the source of the Earnings of the Earner.

fe.name: Earner
fe.definition: The Earner is involved in a transaction or set of transactions as the party that receives payment.

fe.name: Earnings
fe.definition: Earnings are the money given to the Earner in a transaction, generally in exchange for Goods.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: Goods is anything including labor or time, for example, which is exchanged for Earnings in a transaction.

fe.name: Rate
fe.definition: In some cases, earning is described per unit of Goods.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a _by_-PP.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The means by which the Earner gains money.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the action of earning which reveals correllated details, especially characterizations of the Earner which influence the event.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Earner intends to bring about as a result of participating in the Commercial Transaction.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Earner makes their Earnings.
Ex: She MADE a lot of money ["Place" in Africa] .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time when the Earner makes their Earnings.
Ex: Pfizer MADE billions ["Time" in the 1990s] .

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

lexunit.name: earn.v
lexunit.definition: COD: obtain (money) in return for labour or services.

lexunit.name: earnings.n
lexunit.definition: COD: money or income earned.

lexunit.name: profit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a financial gain, especially the difference between an initial outlay and the subsequent amount earned.

lexunit.name: loss.n
lexunit.definition: FN: money spent by a company, cutting into profit.

lexunit.name: revenue.n
lexunit.definition: COD: income, especially when of a company and of a substantial nature.

lexunit.name: income.n
lexunit.definition: COD: money received, especially on a regular basis, for work or through investments.

lexunit.name: net.n
lexunit.definition: FN: amount earned after subtracting losses and other costs.

lexunit.name: make.v
lexunit.definition: COD: gain or earn (money or profit).

lexunit.name: net.v
lexunit.definition: COD: acquire (a sum) as clear profit.

lexunit.name: lose.v
lexunit.definition: COD: earn less (money) than one is spending.

lexunit.name: result.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the outcome of a business's trading over a given period, expressed as a statement of profit or loss.

lexunit.name: pull.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make in money

frame.name: Fame
frame.definition:
An Entity is well-known among a wide range of people (in general or in a particular domain) for a particular Reason, which may be a behavior, characteristic, or some other associated item. In the case of events, fame entails a large number of people being aware of the event's occurance; in the case of concrete entities, including humans, fame entails awareness of existence. In both cases, often fame is accompanied by awareness of the Entity's significance in historical, cultural, or social contexts.
Ex: ["Entity" Shakespeare] _was_ FAMOUS ["Time" during his life] ["Explanation" because he performed in front of Queen Elizabeth I more than anyone else].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity which is widely known and recognized.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the degree of fame of the Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is famous.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity is considered famous.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state of affairs that provides an explanation (via reasoning, causation, etc.) for the level of fame of the Entity.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The behavior, attribute, or associated entities that provide the reason for the Entity being famous.
Ex: This station is FAMOUS ["rea" for the many ramen shacks surrounding it].
Ex: Google is WELL KNOWN ["rea" for having attracted and kept some of the best minds in the industry].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time during which the Entity is famous.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Entity is famous.
Ex: Certain people are WELL-KNOWN ["pla" only in North America].

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The Role underwhich the Entity become famous.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The way in which the Entity becomes famous.

lexunit.name: famous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: known about by many people.

lexunit.name: name.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: a person's reputation

lexunit.name: fame.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being famous.

lexunit.name: stature.n
lexunit.definition: COD: importance or reputation gained by ability or achievement.

lexunit.name: legendary.a
lexunit.definition: COD: remarkable enough to be famous; very well known.

lexunit.name: well known.a
lexunit.definition: FN: famous.

lexunit.name: infamous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: well known for some bad quality or deed

lexunit.name: renown.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being famous.

lexunit.name: renowned.a
lexunit.definition: FN: famous, especially for widely appreciated acts.

lexunit.name: notorious.a
lexunit.definition: FN: infamous

lexunit.name: notoriety.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being notorious

lexunit.name: reputation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the opinion of others directed towards an Entity

lexunit.name: epic.a
lexunit.definition: FN: being known from (or hypothetically deserving of reference within) poetry of the epic tradition.

frame.name: Obscurity
frame.definition:
An Entity is obscure, unnotable, and in general little-known. In the case of an eventive Entity, lack of fame entails a large number of people not being aware of the event's occurance; in the case of a concrete Entity, including humans, lack of fame entails non-awareness of existence.
Ex: ["Entity" Geoffrey Rush] _was_ LITTLE KNOWN ["Place" outside his native Australia] ["Time" when he soared to international prominence].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity which is not widely known and rather obscure.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the degree of fame of the Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is not well known.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity is considered not to be famous.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state of affairs that provides an explanation (via reasoning, causation, etc.) for the level of fame of the Entity.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition:
The reason that the Entity is not famous.
Ex: Some tech companies are LITTLE KNOWN ["rea" because they mostly operate behond the scenes].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time during which the Entity is not famous.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Entity is not famous.
Ex: Certain academic works are OBSCURE ["pla" only in North America].

lexunit.name: little known.a
lexunit.definition: FN: not widely known, obscure.

lexunit.name: obscure.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not important or well known.

lexunit.name: unsung.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not celebrated or praised.

lexunit.name: recondite.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a subject or knowledge) obscure.

frame.name: Shopping
frame.definition: A Buyer looks for Goods in order to purchase them.

fe.name: Shopper
fe.definition: The person who attempts to find the Goods. ["Shopper" John] SHOPPED for a pencil.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: This is the entity to which the Cognizer pays attention. It is referred to as GROUND because it serves as the background or context for the Goods. This FE is usually expressed as a preposition phrase.

fe.name: Goods
fe.definition: This is the entity that the Ground may contain. Typically, it is expressed as a_for_-PP.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An act of the Shopper that allows them to look for (and perhaps purchase) the Goods.
Ex: They SHOPPED for hot items ["Mns" by camping out overnight at shopping malls].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The failure or success of an attempt.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: A spatial setting larger than the Ground in which the Shopping event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the time when the shopping occurs.
Ex: The children were SHOPPING for gifts for their parents ["Time" before Christmas].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: An action that the Shopper intends to accomplish by performing the search.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the amount of effort put into shopping.

lexunit.name: shopping.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the purchasing of goods from shops.

lexunit.name: shop.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go to a shop or shops to buy goods.

frame.name: Relational_political_locales
frame.definition:
A Locale is defined politically to be the head of state of another, larger political locale, the Container_possessor.
Ex: She had repeatedly been to the ["Locale" CAPITAL] ["Container_possessor" of the nation], and there had met with a reception none too cordial.
Ex: He decided to stay in the ["Locale" CAPITAL] ["Container_possessor" of Iraq] for two months while he recuperated to fight another day.
Ex: The largest city in the area, ["Locale" Oakland] _is_ the COUNTY SEAT ["Container_possessor" of Alameda county].

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up a Locale.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The political locale that the Locale is a the head of. Ex: People come from all over the nation to work in and visit the CAPITAL ["ContP" of the United States].

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition:
The politically or administratively-defined locale that functions as the head of state for the containing entity.
Ex: Most of the major government buildings are in the center of the ["Lcl" CAPITAL]

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
This FE is used for the Names of Locales.
Ex: Gyeonggi Province is located in the west-central area of the Korean Peninsula, and surrounds the Korean CAPITAL ["Name" of Seoul].

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
A place that the Locale is located with respect to.
Ex: All the CAPITALS ["RelLoc" in Canada] are clean.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.
Ex: He essentially was the head of the ["des" largest] COUNTY SEAT ["des" in northern California].

fe.name: Population
fe.definition: The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale, typically expressed with a PP-_of_.

lexunit.name: capital.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the governmental or administrative head city of a region.

lexunit.name: county seat.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the town that is the administrative capital of a county.

lexunit.name: see.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the place in which a cathedral church stands, identified as the seat of authority of a bishop or archbishop.

frame.name: Trendiness
frame.definition:
An Behavior, attributed to an Evaluee conforms with or is heavily influenced by a popular trend or practice, often in the realm of fashion, design, though extending social and interactional behavior in general. Trendiness differs from Popularity in adding a factor of aesthetic or other judgement to behaviors and individuals, and judging these with respect to social behavior; Popularity is about amount of acceptibility or utilization based on general (often non-aesthetic) desirability.
Ex: ["Behavior" Wearing flowered brocaded silks] _was_ FASHIONABLE ["Time" in the first few years of the decade].

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior which is trendy.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the degree of trendiness from the norm or from the value for another Behavior.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Behavior is trendy or fashionable.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Behavior is trendy or not.

fe.name: Evaluee
fe.definition: The Evaluee is judged to conform to some degree with popular fashion with respect to his or her behavior.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment of trendiness.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Behavior is trendy..

lexunit.name: fashionable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: characteristic of or influenced by a current popular trend or style.

lexunit.name: trendy.a
lexunit.definition: COD: very fashionable or up to date.

lexunit.name: hip.a
lexunit.definition: COD: fashionable.

lexunit.name: style.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being fahsionable.

lexunit.name: fashion.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being fashionable.

lexunit.name: chic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: elegantly and stylishly fashionable.

lexunit.name: cool.a
lexunit.definition: COD: fashionably attractive or impressive.

lexunit.name: big.a
lexunit.definition: COD: exciting great interest or popularity.

frame.name: Temporary_stay
frame.definition:
A Guest stays for a time at a Location, which is not his or her permanent residence, for some Duration. The Location is often the permanent residence of a Host.
Ex: ["pro" I] usually STAY ["Host" with my aunt] ["loc" at her summer house] ["Time" when I go to Seville].
Ex: ["dur" For a few days] ["pro" my father] LODGED ["loc" at a hotel] ["cor" with a buddy who was a biology student].

fe.name: Guest
fe.definition:
The Guest remains for a relatively short period of time in the Location.
Ex: Originally, ["pro" we] planned on ROOMING with our relatives in Reno.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
The Location where the Guest spends a short amount of time.
Ex: Originally ["pro" we] planned on STAYING ["loc" at the Hilton].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of time that the Guest remains at the Location.
Ex: My wife and have just returned from a ["dur" two day] STAY at Ocean Key.

fe.name: Co-guest
fe.definition:
Another person who, along with the Guest, is temporarily living at the Location.
Ex: I will STAY at my parents' home, ["cor" along with my wife and cats].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the temporary stay takes place.
Ex: He'll be LODGING here ["tim" next month].

fe.name: Host
fe.definition:
The Host is living at the Location on a permanent basis, and is allowing the Guest to stay there.
Ex: You should avoid STAYING ["res" with old college buddies] when on business trips.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that the Guest hopes to achieve by the stay.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Guest that brings about their ability to stay at the Location.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the type of event by comparison to other events (_the same way_) or by characterizing a state of the Guest that affects the action.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The average number of times the event occurs over a period.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of times that the event occurs.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
A description of one of the participants in the temporary stay, or of the staying state-of-affairs in general.
Ex: I hope you have a ["des" pleasant] STAY at our lodge.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place indicates the larger physical setting of the temporary stay.
Ex: ["pla" In London], I STAYED at a hotel.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state of affairs that provides an explanation for the temporary stay.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time of the temporary stay, and which is taken to be a part of the stay.

lexunit.name: stay.v
lexunit.definition: COD: live somewhere temporarily as a visitor or guest.

lexunit.name: stay.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a period of staying somewhere.

lexunit.name: lodge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stay at someone else's home.

lexunit.name: room.v
lexunit.definition: FN: temporarily live at another's residence.

lexunit.name: guest.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to temporarily reside (with) as guest.

lexunit.name: overnight.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stay overnight.

lexunit.name: sleep over.v
lexunit.definition: FN: stay overnight at another's home.

lexunit.name: stay over.v
lexunit.definition: FN: spend the night at another's home.

frame.name: Guest_and_host
frame.definition:
Two individuals, the Guest and the Host are in a temporary social relationship within which the Host provides use of a location or resources for the Guest at a location highly associated with the Host (in many cases, where the Host lives or works). The Guest is not expected to recprocate the hospitality of the Host while the relationship holds, though may be expected to act as Host at a later time.
Ex: ["gue" Commander Silvers] _was_ ["hos" the President's] GUEST ["Time" last week] ["hos_loc" at the White House].
Ex: ["Host" Steve Stephens] will _be_ ["Guest" your] HOST ["Duration" for the weekend].

fe.name: Host
fe.definition:
The Host provides a location and/or resources for the Guest at the Host_location.
Ex: Commander Silvers _was_ ["hos" the President's] GUEST last week. Ex: Would ["hos" you] please _be_ the HOST for our visiting scholar this time around?

fe.name: Guest
fe.definition:
The Guest receives the hospitality of the Host.
Ex: ["gue" Commander Silvers] _was_ the President's GUEST last week.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: Degree to which event occurs

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive phrase describing the Guest or Host.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act whereby a focal participant achieves an action indicated by the target.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The length of the relationship.
Ex: I was Manu's GUEST ["Duration" for few days] in Allepey, in a very beautiful old house.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition:
The location associated with the Host, where the Guest is staying, working, etc.
Ex: Edward VIII _was_ a GUEST ["Host_location" of my hotel] in 1920.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the guest-and-host relationship holds.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A trait or characteristic of the Guest or Host.

lexunit.name: guest.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who is invited to visit someone's home or take part in a function.

lexunit.name: host.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who receives or entertains other people as guests.

frame.name: Working_on
