frame.definition:
An Agent expends effort towards acheiving a Goal. Alternatively, a Salient_entity involved in the Goal can be expressed in place of a Goal expression.
Ex: In addition, ["Agent" our organization] will WORK ["Goal" on improving accountability in every department].
Ex: If ["Agent" somebody] is WORKING ["sal_ent" on the pipes of your house] and you turn on the faucet hard, you get sand, junk.
Ex: You could see ["Agent" several students] PLUGGING AWAY ["Goal" at the problem].
Ex: We have benefited greatly from ["Agent" their] WORK ["sal_ent" on this problem].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent puts effort into reaching Goal.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: The Goal is what the Agent expends effort to achieve.

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to achieve a Goal.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the effort is done.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the effort occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the work is done.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent puts in effort in acheiving the Goal.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time peiod over which the work takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which the Agent puts effort into achieving the Goal.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is independent of the the attempt of the Agent to achieve the Goal.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The domain or area within which the work towards the Goal belongs.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition: An entity that is centrally involved in the Goal that the Agent is attempting to acheive.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Agent works.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness.

lexunit.name: work.v
lexunit.definition: FN: exert effort towards acheiving a goal.

lexunit.name: work.n
lexunit.definition: COD: activity involving mental or physical effort done in order to achieve a result.

lexunit.name: plug away.v
lexunit.definition: COD: proceed steadily and laboriously with a task.

lexunit.name: peg away.v
lexunit.definition: COD: work hard over a long period.

frame.name: Diversity
frame.definition:
A Group is described as having members which are similar or dissimilar to each other. The Degree of similarity may also be expressed. Some of the nouns in this frame are transparent (e.g. _range.n_) whereas others denote the scale of diversity (_diversity_); _variety.n_ is usable both ways but is normally transparent.
Ex: The DIVERSITY ["Group" of students here] is to be applauded . ["Dimension" INI] Ex: A ["Group" RANGE] ["Group" of answers] were proposed .

fe.name: Group
fe.definition: This FE marks constituents that express the set of objects or types whose diversity is at issue.

fe.name: Dimension
fe.definition: This FE marks constituents which express a property in respect to which the similarity of the Group is assessed.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The extent to which the members of the Group are similar to each other, in general or with respect to some Dimension(s)
Ex: The songs on the album are ["Degree" incredibly] DIVERSE .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Group is diverse or homogenous.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the general area in which diversity occurs or exists.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which Dimension is similar or different

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An inanimate entity or process that causes the diversity or homogeneity.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Group

lexunit.name: diversity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state of being diverse.

lexunit.name: variety.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the quality or state of being different or diverse.

lexunit.name: diverse.a
lexunit.definition: COD: widely varied.

lexunit.name: various.a
lexunit.definition: COD: different from one another; of different kinds or sorts.

lexunit.name: range.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a set of different things of the same general type.

lexunit.name: broad.a
lexunit.definition: COD: large in area or scope.

lexunit.name: breadth.n
lexunit.definition: COD: wide range

lexunit.name: varied.a
lexunit.definition: COD: incorporating a number of different types or elements; showing variation or variety.

lexunit.name: medley.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a varied mixture.

lexunit.name: miscellany.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a mixture.

lexunit.name: array.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an impressive display or range of a particular thing.

lexunit.name: uniform.a
lexunit.definition: COD: not varying; the same in all cases and at all times.

lexunit.name: uniformity.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality of being uniform.

lexunit.name: assortment.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a miscellaneous collection.

lexunit.name: assorted.a
lexunit.definition: COD: of various sorts put together.

lexunit.name: multifarious.a
lexunit.definition: COD: having great variety and diversity.

lexunit.name: diverseness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the state or condition of wide variation.

lexunit.name: heterogeneous.a
lexunit.definition: COD: diverse in character or content.

lexunit.name: heterogeneity.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality of being diverse in character or content.

lexunit.name: mixed bag.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a diverse assortment.

lexunit.name: multifariousness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the quality of having great variety and diversity.

lexunit.name: manifold.a
lexunit.definition: COD: many and various.

lexunit.name: multiplicity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a large number or variety.

lexunit.name: variability.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the extent of diversity.

lexunit.name: scope.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a set of various items.

frame.name: Interrupt_process
frame.definition: A Cause (or associated Actor) causes an ongoing

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
A force, process, or event that produces the interruption.
Ex: ["Cause" Leaving the page after you've clicked "Download"] will INTERRUPT the transfer.

fe.name: Process
fe.definition:
The Process goes into a paused state due to the Cause or Actor.
Ex: Leaving the page after you've clicked "Download" will INTERRUPT ["Process" the transfer].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the interruption takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the interruption occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the interruption occurs.

fe.name: Actor
fe.definition:
An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not, but effectively causing the interruption.
Ex: In such cases ["Actor" the server] will automatically INTERRUPT the process.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (_the same way_) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor or Cause's influence on the character of the event.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The natural reason for which the interruption occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action or sub-event through which the Actor or Cause interrupts the Process.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the interruption occurs.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

lexunit.name: uninterrupted.a
lexunit.definition: FN: without interruption.

lexunit.name: interrupt.v
lexunit.definition: COD: stop the continuous progress of.

lexunit.name: interruption.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the ceasing of a process by an event.

frame.name: Temporal_collocation
frame.definition:
An Trajector is identified as occurring at the same time as some better-known Landmark. We consider sequenced calendric units (e.g. Tuesday, 1987, January) as periods for the purposes of this frame. Some lexical items allow certain types of frame elements while disallowing others (e.g. *DURING Tuesday...).
Several words of this frame (e.g. _now.adv_) have deictic incorporation of the Landmark_period.
Ex: ["Trajector_event" He tried to take care of that] ON ["Landmark_event" his last visit] . Ex: I especially like ["Trajector_entity" brunch] ON ["Landmark_period" Sunday]. Ex: Dinosaurs lived in PREHISTORIC ["Trajector_period" eras].
Ex: ["Trajector_event" He did it] ["Landmark_period" THEN].

fe.name: Trajector_entity
fe.definition:
The entity that occurs at some time.
Ex: The CURRENT ["Trajector_entity" President of Georgia] was born in Tbilisi.
Ex: ["Trajector_entity" Books] IN the early 19th century had fewer pictures.

fe.name: Landmark_event
fe.definition:
The event which designates the time at which a trajector occurs.
Ex: DURING ["Landmark_event" last night's walk] , I stubbed my toe.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes the state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

fe.name: Trajector_period
fe.definition:
The period that occurs with respect to some other time.
Ex: FUTURE ["Trajector_period" eras] will be vastly changed from today.

fe.name: Landmark_period
fe.definition:
The period in which a trajector takes place. This period can be cyclical and, in that case, is interpreted contextually.
Ex: I went to the store ON ["Landmark_period" Tuesday]. Ex: IN ["Landmark_period" the Triassic Era], the first flying vertebrates appeared.

fe.name: Trajector_event
fe.definition:
The event that occurs at some time.
Ex: CURRENTLY, ["Trajector_event" researchers are making new discoveries very quickly.]

fe.name: Landmark_entity
fe.definition: The entity which designates the time of some trajector. Note: this FE is infrequent or non-existent in English and is included for completeness.

frame.name: Simultaneity
frame.definition: Two Events happen at the same time. This may either be construed symmetrically as a relation holding between the Events, or asymmetrically as holding between a Landmark_event whose known occurrence is used to describe when a Profiled_event took place.

fe.name: Profiled_event
fe.definition: The event which is asserted to occur at the same time as the Landmark_event.

fe.name: Landmark_event
fe.definition: The event or time period whose timing the Profiled_event is judged against.

fe.name: Events
fe.definition: The states-of-affairs which are asserted to be co-timed.

lexunit.name: co-occurrence.n

frame.name: Attempt_distant_interaction_scenario
frame.definition: An Agent attempts to interact with a relatively distant or indirectly accessible Target using some Instrument (which may be a body part, e.g. _hand_). The Agent's ability to manipulate the Instrument and put it in the Target location is in question. The most common types of distant interaction involve an Agent attempting to move the Instrument ballistically so that it contacts the Target (e.g. Shooting_scenario), or an Agent attempting to direct an Instrument that enables perception at a Target_location to be examined.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent tries to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Target
fe.definition: The Target is the entity located in an indirectly accessible location relative to the Agent.

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt occurs.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent during the event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where an attempt is made.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Agent makes the attempt.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time peiod over which the attempt or attempts take place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which the Agent attempts to interact with the Target

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is independent of the the attempt of the Agent.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Target_location
fe.definition: The location that the Agent is attempting to access using the Instrument.

frame.name: Aiming
frame.definition:
An Agent adjusts an Instrument to enable it to interact directly with a difficult-to-access Target_location. Usually, there is a Targeted entity at the Target_location which is mentioned in its place.
Ex: If ["Agent" you] AIM ["Instrument" your weapons] ["Target_location" somewhere else] , I 'll be more likely to talk . Ex: ["Means" The sortie] TARGETED primarily ["Targeted" resupply points] , but these included several civilian areas . ["Instrument" INI] Ex: ["Agent" A good marksman] still should take AIM ["Duration" for a moment] ["Time" before each shot] . ["Instrument" INI] ["Target_location" INI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual that manipulates the Instrument to enable interaction with the Targeted.

fe.name: Targeted
fe.definition:
The Targeted is the entity located in an indirectly accessible location relative to the Agent.
Ex: I tried to TARGET ["Targeted" his left thigh] .

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the aiming is achieved.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent takes aim.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent during the event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the Agent aims at the Targeted.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any generalized description of the details of the event in terms of comparison to another event or what would be expected of the details given some state of the Agent.
Ex: She took ["Manner" careful] AIM before shooting .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time peiod over which the adjustment of the Instrument takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which the Agent attempts to interact with the Targeted

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is independent of the the aiming of the Agent, but contextualizes it.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Targeted.

fe.name: Target_location
fe.definition:
The location that the Agent wishes to ready the Instrument to access.
Ex: If you TARGET ["Target_location" towards the bridge] , make sure to avoid the church .

fe.name: Location_of_protagonist
fe.definition:
The location from which the proto-agent acts or perceives. This does not include the location of a thing which is affected or perceived in the event.
Ex: With remote drones , you can TARGET Moscow ["" from your own living room] .

frame.name: Hit_or_miss
frame.definition:
An Agent succeeds or fails to interact perceptually or physically with the Target or Target_location. The Instrument which is used to interact with the Target may stand in metonymically for the Agent.
Ex: At first ["Agent" he] shot ["Degree" very] WIDE ["Target" of his target] . Ex: Because I programmed the scope wrong , ["Agent" I] kept MISSING ["Target" Jupiter] . Ex: ["Agent" She] scored two HITS ["Target_location" on the deer 's left side] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The individual who tries to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Target
fe.definition: The Target is the entity located in an indirectly accessible location relative to the Agent.

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt at interaction, incorporated in the LUs of the frame.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent achieves a Purpose.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which the interaction takes place at the Target_location.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when something hits or misses.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A description of the Agent during the event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the Agent manages or fails to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of how the details of the event compare to others, either generally (_the same way_), or in terms of a state of the Agent which influences the event (_carelessly_).

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which the Agent attempts to interact with the Target

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which contextualizes the hitting or missing of the Agent but is not conceived of as caused by it.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Target_location
fe.definition: The location that the Agent is attempting to access using the Instrument.

fe.name: Iterations

fe.name: Deviation
fe.definition: The distance of the actual location from the Target_location.

frame.name: Accuracy
frame.definition:
An Agent is involved in an activity whose degree of success is dependent on a parameter of the action matching a particular set of values of a continuous variable or variables (e.g. quantity, location, time).
The Agent, or metonymically the Instrument or Means action, is described in terms of the actual or expected Deviation between the location, time, or quantity in the activity and the location, time, or quantity which is necessary for the intended event.
Ex: ["Instrument" The Longview Rangefinder] is ACCURATE ["Deviation" to within one foot per hundred yards] . Ex: ["Means" His estimate] was OFF ["Deviation" by an order of magnitude] .
Ex: ["Agent" The fork truck operator] must be ["Degree" fairly] ACCURATE ["Means" in his aim].
Ex: The PRECISION ["Means" of the daily measurements] is dependent on a number of factors.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The individual who tries to interact with the Target.
Ex: ["Agent" The mailman] is very EXACT about addresses -- he has to be .

fe.name: Target
fe.definition: The Target is the entity whose attributes (esp. position) the Agent is attempting to match in an action.

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt at interaction, incorporated in the LUs of the frame.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent attempts to hit a Target_value.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: How closely the expected or actual location that the Instrument interacts with corresponds to the Target_value.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when something hits or misses.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the Agent manages or fails to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Target.

fe.name: Target_value
fe.definition: The value or values for a parameter that match the Agent's intent.

fe.name: Deviation
fe.definition:
Expected or actual deviation from the Target_value.
Ex: For this they would need a thermometer ACCURATE ["Deviation" to within a microkelvin].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The particular aspect or domain in which something is accurate.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Agent, Means, or Instrument is accurate.

frame.name: Lively_place
frame.definition: A Location is characterized by a high amount of (often goal-oriented) Activity, or metonymically, with Individuals who are engaged in the activity.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: The Location where a lot of activity is taking place, or prototypically takes place.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation in amount of activity from the norm or from the amount for another Location.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Location is characterized by a lot of activity.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Location has some degree of activity or liveliness.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The larger or general area where the Location is lively.
Ex: ["pla" On this side of town] the streets are LIVLIER.

fe.name: Activity
fe.definition: The Activity that is conceptually filling the Location.

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: The Individuals are engaged in the Activity, creating a lively Location.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Individuals or Location is engaging in the Activity.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

frame.name: Cause_proliferation_in_number
frame.definition:
An Agent (or inanimate Cause) affects a Set so that the number of entities that make up the Set changes from an Initial_number to a Final_number. Alternatively, the situation can be described in terms of an Initial_state and a Final_state. In some cases the Attribute (i.e., number) or Difference in number may be mentioned.
Ex: More and more resources have been devoted to halting ["Agent" rogue nation's] PROLIFERATION ["Set" of controlled nuclear technology].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The person who causes the Set to increase in number.

fe.name: Difference
fe.definition: The distance between the orginial value (Value-1) and the final value (Value-2) of the entity on the scale (Variable).

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The scale along which the Set ranges in, i.e., number.

fe.name: Initial_number
fe.definition: The initial number of entites in the Set.

fe.name: Final_number
fe.definition: The final number of entities in the Set.

fe.name: Co_Variable
fe.definition: The Co-Variable is the scale that the amount of the Setis measured against.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Item) along the scale between its initial (Value-1) and its final position (Value-2).

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.

fe.name: Set
fe.definition: The entity whose amount is being changed.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the number of the Set.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: The force that causes the change.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: >Any description of the Agent changing the number of the Setwhich is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Agent changes the number of the Set.

lexunit.name: proliferation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of increasing the number of something.

lexunit.name: multiplication.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of increasing the number of something.

frame.name: Individual_history
frame.definition:
This scenario describes a series of Events, associated a single Participant, i.e., the history of the Participant. The Events do not necessarily form a coherent whole (e.g., are not necessarily causally related), but merely occupy a period of time. In many cases the history is limited to what are considered the important or significant events. Words in this frame can also denote the time period over which the sequence of Events took place.
Note: uses of words in this frame to describe a record of the series of events are not in this frame (e.g., _we compiled a history of Rome_).
Ex: We've been worried about ["Participant" our recent hire's] ["Events" HISTORY] ["Domain" of deceiving employers].
Ex: The following sections document the entire ["tim" 25-year] ["Events" HISTORY] ["Participant" of the company].
Ex: Our areas of strength are ["Participant" British, American and European] ["Events" HISTORY] ["Start_time" from 1492] ["End_time" to 2000].

fe.name: Participant
fe.definition:
The Participant is either an active participant in all of the Events (e.g., Agent or Patient), or is more peripherally associated with the Events (e.g., Location or Topic).
Ex: We've been worried about ["par" our recent hire's] HISTORY of deceiving employers.
Ex: I was charmed, and also determined to learn more about ["par" the factory's] HISTORY.

fe.name: Events
fe.definition:
The Events which the Participant is a part of. This FE is used to mark the frame-evoking element.
Ex: We will focus on events in her recent ["eve" HISTORY].

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is to be included in consideration of the Participant's history.
Ex: One of my colleagues is an expert on the ["dom" economic] HISTORY of the Hellenistic period
Ex: The Netherlands' long HISTORY ["dom" of trade with China] provides important information for modern political economies.

fe.name: End_time
fe.definition:
The end of the span of time during which the Events occur.
Ex: This article discusses mainly the geography and the HISTORY of Palestine ["end" until the United Nations took up the Palestine problem in 1947].

fe.name: Start_time
fe.definition:
The beginning of the time span over which the Events occur.
Ex: The introduction describes the history of geography ["sta" from the eighteenth century onwards].

fe.name: Time_span
fe.definition:
The span of time over which the Events take place.
Ex: We have traced the flag?s PAST ["tim" between its original conception in the 14th century and its end a hundred years later].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The Duration, often expressed in calendric units, of the history of the Participant.
Ex: The following sections document the entire ["dur" 25-year] HISTORY of the company.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A characterization of the Participant or Events.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Events concerning the Participant occured.

lexunit.name: history.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the whole series of past events connected with someone or something.

lexunit.name: past.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person's or thing's history or earlier life.

frame.name: Touring
frame.definition: A Tourist experiences an Attraction, a location with a unique history or other societally recognized individual character, with the goal of seeing and learning about it. Typically, the Attraction has a source of information about the Attraction--a guide, pamphlets, or displays.

fe.name: Tourist
fe.definition: The individual that is seeking an experience at an Attraction.

fe.name: Attraction
fe.definition: The societally-recognized unique location that the Tourist experiences.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Tourist or the Attraction during the tour.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: The perceptual background against which the Attraction is experienced by the Tourist.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the details of the event in terms of how they compare to other events (_the same way_) or in terms of how the state of the Tourist affects them (_happily, obliviously_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means indicates a method the Tourist is using to participate in a tour.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time that the touring takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: Some action that the Tourist is trying to accomplish with touring. This is generally (at a minimum) for the purposes of entertainment and learning.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the touring takes place.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time the touring activity lasts.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

lexunit.name: tour.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a journey for pleasure in which several different places are visited.

lexunit.name: tourist.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person who travels for pleasure.
