lexunit.name: sights.n
lexunit.definition: COD: places of interest to tourists and other visitors.

lexunit.name: do.v
lexunit.definition: FN: see/travel around (a place).

lexunit.name: sight seer.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a tourist; one who sees the sights of a tourist location.

lexunit.name: sight-see.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to visit tourist locations and landmarks

lexunit.name: tourism.n
lexunit.definition: FN: peoples visiting a foreign land for pleasure and with the intention of becoming more aquainted with the particularities of the area.

frame.name: Historic_event
frame.definition:
In the course of history, an Event or Entity is taken to have importance or significance.
Ex: Throughout the campaign ["Entity" activists] have MADE ["dom" financial] HISTORY ["Time" as one by one major corporations have yielded to protester power]
Ex: ["Event" The conference] _was_ HISTORIC ["Entity" for Atlanta's growth as a city].
Ex: Many of the HISTORIC ["Ent" sites] offer additional outdoor recreation activities.
Ex: The James River is arguably the most HISTORIC ["Ent" river] in the country and one of the most important rivers in the Southeast.
Ex: Take in the ["Ent" HISTORY], the sawdust-covered floors, and the legendary backroom where the ale flowed during Prohibition.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Reason for which an event occurs.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: This FE identifies the entity, concrete or abstract.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is part of the Event's history.
Ex: Throughout the campaign activists have MADE ["dom" financial] HISTORY as one by one major corporations have yielded to protester power

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: historic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: famous or important in history, or potentially so.

lexunit.name: make history.v
lexunit.definition: FN: participate in a historical event.

lexunit.name: historic_((entity)).a
lexunit.definition: FN: pertaining to entities that have historic significance.

frame.name: Visiting
frame.definition:
An Agent matches location with an Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.
Quite often, the Purpose is social- or entertainment-oriented.
Ex: I ca n't remember how many times ["Agent" he] VISITED ! ["Entity" DNI] Ex: ["Time" Now] ["Agent" she] _was_ _on_ an ["Purpose" inspection] VISIT . Ex: ["Agent" You] have to VISIT ["Entity" your parents] ["Frequency" every once in a while] .

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity that is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The physical entity that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose. During the visit, the Agent matches location with the Entity.

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition: A state (of the Agent) that results as a consequence of the Agent being situated at the Entity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which a visit is made.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that the Agent spends with the Entity.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any overall description of the details of the visit, either in terms of how it matches other events (_the same way_) or in terms of states of the Agent that affect the action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: A description of the position of the Agent during the visit.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Agent that enables their visit.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of instances of the described event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: A characterization of the average number of times a visit happens over a period of time.

lexunit.name: visitor.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a person visiting a person or place, especially socially.

lexunit.name: visit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: go to see and spend some time with (someone) socially or as a guest.

lexunit.name: visit.n
lexunit.definition: COD: an act of visiting.

lexunit.name: revisit.v
lexunit.definition: COD: come back to or visit again.

lexunit.name: call.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a visit

frame.name: Visitor_scenario
frame.definition: An Agent leaves their Normal_location and matches location with an Entity in pursuit of a Purpose. The Agent temporarily remains with the Entity to fulfil this Purpose and then departs again, usually back to the Normal_location.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: A place that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

frame.name: Visitor_arrival
frame.definition: An Agent arrives at a Goal that should enable their Purpose.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: Agent is the object that moves under its own power.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Agent moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is any expression that tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Although always conceptually present and specific, Goalmay sometimes be understood from context, rather than expressed by any separate constituent. Ex: Our visitors ARRIVED yesterday.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent arrives.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: I REACHED Canada ["Mode_of_transportation" by car]. Ex: I REACHED Mexico ["Mode_of_transportation" on foot].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent arrives at the Goal.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the arrival occurs.

frame.name: Visitor_departure
frame.definition: After a visit is complete, the Agent departs the Source, normally bound for their normal haunts.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: This is the individual which moves under their own power.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Agent, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'. Ex: Spiderman LEFT ["Path" through the window].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE labels any expression which tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source. Ex: Our visitors LEFT ["Goal" for Los Angeles].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels. Ex: The messenger LEFT the room ["Manner" clumsily].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Agent which results in their departure. Ex: He RETREATED from his opponent ["Means" by taking a quick leap backwards].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Agent is moving. Ex: He ["Speed" quickly] EXITED the crowded terminal.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: We SET OUT ["Mode_of_transportation" by boat] for Nova Scotia. Ex: Wilbur DEPARTED ["Mode_of_transportation" on foot] for London.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance that the Agent has traveled. Ex: He WITHDREW ["Distance" a little] from her.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the departure takes place.Ex: We LEFT ["Time" in the morning].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent departs from the Source.

frame.name: Provide_lodging
frame.definition: A Host provides a temporary Residence for a Lodger.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host is the individual (or group of individuals) that own or control the Residence and allow the Lodger to temporarily stay there.

fe.name: Lodger
fe.definition: The Lodger is the individual who is given permission to lodge in the Residence.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Host provides lodging.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Host provides a Residence to the Lodger

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the Host provides a temporary Residence.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose is the goal of the Host in allowing the Lodger to stay.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the cognitive cause of the Host's granting of permission.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the provision of lodging which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Host that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action of the Host whereby they communicate or enact the granting of permission to stay in the Residence.
Ex:

fe.name: Residence
fe.definition: The location controlled by the Host which the Lodger stays at temporarily.

lexunit.name: house.v
lexunit.definition: COD: provide with shelter or accommodation.

lexunit.name: lodge.v
lexunit.definition: FN: provide with requested accommodation.

lexunit.name: host.v
lexunit.definition: FN: act as a host to in-house visitor's.

lexunit.name: put up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: provide a guest with accomodation.

frame.name: Lodging_scenario
frame.definition: A Host provides a Residence for a Lodger to temporarily stay.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host is the individual (or group of individuals) that own or control the Residence and allow the Lodger to temporarily stay there.

fe.name: Lodger
fe.definition: The Lodger is the individual who is given permission to lodge in the Residence.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Host provides a Residence to the Lodger

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the Host provides a temporary Residence.

fe.name: Residence
fe.definition: The location controlled by the Host which the Lodger stays at temporarily.

frame.name: Aging
frame.definition:
An Entity is undergoing a change in age typically associated with some detioration or change in state.
Ex: ["Entity" This bark] AGES and turns black.
Ex: The U.S. is to upgrade AGING ["Entity" missile defense systems] with advanced tech.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity which is undergoing aging.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity ages.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity undergoes the aging event.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (_hard_, _softly_), secondary effects (_quietly_, _loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In agentive frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Theme that affect the action (_presumptuously_, _coldly_, _deliberately_, _eagerly_, _carefully_).
Ex: These kinds of condoms AGED ["Manner" quickly].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE indicates where the Entity is located.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The end Result of the Entity aging.

lexunit.name: aging.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of growing older.

lexunit.name: age.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to become older.

lexunit.name: mature.v
lexunit.definition: FN: become older

frame.name: Locale_by_event
frame.definition:
A place defined in terms of an event which occured (or will occur) there. Ex: ["Locale" Woodstock, NY] _was_ the SITE ["DefEvnt" of the most important rock concert of 1969]. Ex: ["DefEvnt" Our] ["DefEvnt" meeting] SITE was chosen for its solitude.
In the second example, the event FE is labeled with two labels, because the two words do not form a syntactic constituent; the first would be GF Genitive PT Possessive, and the second, GF Dependent and PT NP.

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition:
A stable bounded area. It is typically the denotation of the nouns in Locale_by_event, which will be annotated on the target word.
Ex: We need to find a suitable VENUE ["DefEvnt" for such a large wedding]. Ex: ["Locale" Tours] _was_ the SITE ["DefEvnt" of the defeat of the Turks by the French].

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition:
Salient parts that make up a Locale.
Ex: We need a meeting SITE ["Constituent_parts" with more computers] .

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition:
A place that a Locale is located with respect to.
Ex: The SITE ["DefEvnt" of their first meeting], ["rel" west of the Mississippi], has never been disclosed.

fe.name: Defining_event
fe.definition: The event for which the locale is known or is named Ex: The driver died at the SCENE ["DefEvnt" of the accident].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition:
The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Locale.
Ex: The next day, the governor visited the ["des" still-smoldering] SITE ["DefEvnt" of the fire].

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The name of the locale. Ex: The ["Name" Bonneville] SITE has been a favorite of drivers for many years.

lexunit.name: site.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The place at which an event takes place; may be on any scale: the site of the factory, the instertion site of the hypodermic.

lexunit.name: scene.n
lexunit.definition: Denotes the place where something occured: the scene of the accident, of the fight. Not: "A scene of great beauty unfolded before them."

lexunit.name: venue.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The place where an event, typically large and organized such as a meeting or artistic performance, takes place

lexunit.name: theater_((of_war)).n
lexunit.definition: FN: a large region in which a part of a still larger war takes place.

lexunit.name: field.n
lexunit.definition: FN: An outdoor area in which some activity takes place, as in "Will this camera be sturdy enough to use in the field?"

lexunit.name: battlefield.n
lexunit.definition: FN: A location at which a battle between armed opponents takes place.

frame.name: Presence
frame.definition:
An Entity exists at a particular Location, at a particular Time, as observed by an implicit observer. A Depictive and/or Duration phrase is often found.
This frame differs from Existence in that the Location is profiled as a ground where an observer is conceived of as confirming the Entity's existence.
Ex: ["Entity" Liquid water] _was_ PRESENT ["Location" on the surface of Mars] ["Time" billions of years ago].
Ex: ["Entity" Urate] _was_ PRESENT ["Depictive" in varying concentrations] ["Location" in the bathing solution only].
Ex: ["Entity" No one] _was_ PRESENT. ["Location" DNI]
Ex: ["Entity" Your] PRESENCE is appreciated. ["Location" DNI]
In some cases, the Location may be recoverable from phrases that primarily express peripheral information:
Ex: _Was_ ["Entity" the senator] PRESENT ["Duration" for the committee vote]? Ex: Was the senator PRESENT ["Location" for the committee vote]?

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity whose existence at the Location is confirmed.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition: The Location of the Entity. The Location is conceived as a ground for an event of inspection to determine the presense of the Entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time when the Entity is present at the Location.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A separate description of the state of the Entity when it is present.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Entity is present. In this frame, Duration may be expressed with _for_ preceding an event which stands for the duration of the event. In cases where the Entity is sentient, there may be an inference that the Entity's intent is to be present so as to participate in the event.
Ex: I can be PRESENT ["dur" for the first half of the ceremony and the last part of the reception], but I'll have to leave in the middle.
Ex: A catalyst should typically be PRESENT ["dur" for the thermal and/or photochemically induced curing of the coating composition applied onto a suitable substrate].

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The purpose of the Entity.
Ex: Mr. Jones will be PRESENT ["pur" to answer your questions].

lexunit.name: present.a
lexunit.definition: COD: being or occurring in a particular place.

lexunit.name: absence.n
lexunit.definition: SMV: the state or fact ofnot being present.

lexunit.name: presence.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the state or fact of being present.

frame.name: Relational_quantity
frame.definition:
The Denoted_quantity is (generally) an imprecise characterization of the quantity of Individuals or a Mass, made with reference to a relatively easily and precisely imaginable Reference_quantity.
Ex: It took ["Denoted_quantity" ABOUT] ["Reference_quantity" three] ["Individuals" hours], but we 're done now . Ex: But there were ["Denoted_quantity" BARELY] ["Reference_quantity" 300] in the whole district . ["Individuals" DNI] Ex: Put in right ["Denoted_quantity" AROUND] ["Reference_quantity" a pinch and a half] . ["Mass" DNI] Ex: She waited ["Denoted_quantity" A GOOD] ["Individuals" second] before knocking . Ex: She waited A GOOD ["Reference_quantity" second] before knocking .

fe.name: Denoted_quantity
fe.definition: The quantity denoted by phrases headed by the Target.

fe.name: Mass
fe.definition: A substance that is being quantified.

fe.name: Individuals
fe.definition: A collection of entities.

fe.name: Q_Prop
fe.definition: A property of the Denoted_quantity.

fe.name: Reference_quantity
fe.definition: A relatively precise quantity in some oft-used form that is used as the basis for defining the Denoted_quantity.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

lexunit.name: about.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: approximately.

lexunit.name: a good.a
lexunit.definition: FN: close, confident approximation of (some value)

lexunit.name: over.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: at least

lexunit.name: almost.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: very nearly.

lexunit.name: approximately.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: estimating a value; about.

lexunit.name: around.prep
lexunit.definition: COD: approximately.

lexunit.name: circa.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: at approximately (some date).

lexunit.name: or so.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: about the value of

lexunit.name: in neighborhood (of).prep
lexunit.definition: FN: in vague approximation of some value.

lexunit.name: in vicinity (of).prep
lexunit.definition: FN: a ballpark estimate of

lexunit.name: nearly.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: very close to; almost.

lexunit.name: under.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: below some value

lexunit.name: close (to).a
lexunit.definition: FN: near to some value.

lexunit.name: roughly.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: approximately.

lexunit.name: upwards of.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: at least (some value)

lexunit.name: precisely.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: exactly

lexunit.name: exactly.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: precisely at some value; no more, no less.

lexunit.name: some.art
lexunit.definition: COD: (used with a number) approximately.

lexunit.name: something like.prep
lexunit.definition: FN: around (some value)

lexunit.name: at least.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: in estimation of a value at its minimum.

lexunit.name: tops.n
lexunit.definition: FN: at the most

lexunit.name: minimum.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the least or smallest amount, extent, or intensity possible or recorded.

lexunit.name: at most.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: in estimation of a value at its maximum.

lexunit.name: thereabouts.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: used to indicate that a date or figure is approximate.

lexunit.name: barely.adv
lexunit.definition: COD: just at and no more above (some value).

lexunit.name: odd.a
lexunit.definition: COD: in the region of.

lexunit.name: much.art
lexunit.definition: FN: a lot of (some number of individuals/mass)

lexunit.name: little.art
lexunit.definition: FN: not very much of (mass/individuals)

frame.name: Reference_text
frame.definition:
In a text, a Source_of_information is given that provides a reader of the text with further Information relevant to the text. In this frame the author and reader are completely deprofiled, with the Source_of_information made salient.
Ex: In Densmore's days it was sometimes made of an old-fashioned man's celluloid collar (CF. ["soi" Densmore 1943: 116]).
Ex: The 'foaming regions' play the role of 'internal shocks' (CF. ["soi" Piran's recent publication] ["inf" for a review]) of GRB theory.
Ex: Use my() for local variables whenever you can get away with it (but SEE ["soi" perlform] ["inf" for where you can't]).

fe.name: Source_of_information
fe.definition:
The Source_of_information is referred to as a source of information related to the current text.
Ex: The accreting matter forms a disc whose instabilities trigger outbursts (SEE ["soi" Lasota 2001] for a review of the instability model).

fe.name: Information
fe.definition:
The Source_of_information contains Information that the reader is directed to.
Ex: The accreting matter forms a disc whose instabilities trigger outbursts (SEE Lasota 2001 ["inf" for a review of the instability model]).

lexunit.name: see.v
lexunit.definition: FN: confer for further information.

lexunit.name: cf.v
lexunit.definition: COD: compare with.

lexunit.name: qv.v
lexunit.definition: COD: used to direct a reader to another part of a text for further information.

frame.name: Appointing
frame.definition:
A Selector, often an individual in a leadership role, appoints a Official to assume an official Role in an organization (which can be expressed as the Body).
Ex: ["Selector" Press secretaries] ACCREDIT ["Official" journalists] ["Body" to the sessions].

fe.name: Selector
fe.definition: The Selector is responsible for the appointment of the new official. Typically, it occurs as the External Argument of verbs.

fe.name: Official
fe.definition: The Official is a person appointed to a recognized position.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: Frequently, the Official is referred to only by his/her role. However, the Role can be expressed separately from the leader, usually as either a secondary predicate or in a PP Complement (headed by _as_).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE indicates the Degree to which an event occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: Depictive indicates the state of one of the participants during the action.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE is used for the Manner of performing an action.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which the Selector accomplishes the designation of the Official.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE is used for indicating the Result of an event.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: This frame element describes the situation that brought about the new appointment.

fe.name: Function
fe.definition:
The Function is the purpose the Official will fufill.
Ex: Under the new program, SCC will ACCREDIT organizations ["Function" to assess wood flow from certified forests to workshops or factories].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the designation of the official takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the appointment takes place.

fe.name: Body
fe.definition: A group of individuals who are elected or appointed to perform some function, and to which the Official is assigned.

lexunit.name: accredit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: give authority to act in an official role.

lexunit.name: appoint.v
lexunit.definition: COD: assign a job or role to.

lexunit.name: accredited.a
lexunit.definition: FN: officially designated.

lexunit.name: designate.v
lexunit.definition: COD: give a specified position or status to

lexunit.name: finger.v
lexunit.definition: COD: identify or choose (someone) for a particular purpose.

lexunit.name: tap.v
lexunit.definition: COD: designate or select for a task or honour.

lexunit.name: name.v
lexunit.definition: FN: designate someone to perform a duty.

frame.name: Nuclear_process
frame.definition:
An Initial_element is converted into a Final_element via a process of decay, fusion, or fission which changes the number or type of hadrons (protons or neutrons) in the nucleus of the atoms that make up the Element.
Ex: ["Element" 5.5 percent of nucleii] DECAY ["Initial_element" from tritium] ["Final_element" to He3] ["Period_of_iterations" in a year] .

fe.name: Element
fe.definition: A substance definable in terms of the kind(s) of atoms that make it up.

fe.name: Final_element
fe.definition: The type of Element that results from the process.

fe.name: Initial_element
fe.definition: The type of Element that begins the process.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Elementundergoes the transformation.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Change event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_) and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Element's substance is converted to the Final_element.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An event or state that causes the change to take place.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the nuclear process occurs.

lexunit.name: fissile.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (of an atom or element) able to undergo nuclear fission.

lexunit.name: decay.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the process of undergoing change to a different form by emitting radiation.

lexunit.name: decay.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (of a radioactive substance, particle, etc.) undergo change to a different form by emitting radiation.

lexunit.name: fuse.v
lexunit.definition: COD: join, blend, or coalesce to form a single entity.

lexunit.name: fusion.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the process or result of fusing.

lexunit.name: fission.v
lexunit.definition: COD: (chiefly of atoms) undergo fission.

lexunit.name: fission.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the action of splitting or being split into two or more parts.

lexunit.name: nuclear.a
lexunit.definition: COD: relating to or using energy released in nuclear fission or fusion.

lexunit.name: thermonuclear.a
lexunit.definition: COD: (chiefly with reference to weapons) using or denoting nuclear fusion reactions that occur at very high temperatures.

lexunit.name: radioactive.a
lexunit.definition: COD: emitting or relating to the emission of ionizing radiation or particles.

lexunit.name: radioactivity.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the emission of ionizing radiation or particles caused by the spontaneous disintegration of atomic nuclei.

frame.name: Scope
frame.definition: An Event is desribed in terms of the diversity of entities that are affected or considered in the Event. Alternatively a Salient_entity which enables or brings about the Event can be similarly described.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that affects a set of entities.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Salient_entity which is under discussion.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition: The entity which enables or causes the Event being judged.

lexunit.name: scope.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the number or variety of things affected or considered.

frame.name: Preliminaries
frame.definition:
This frame describes means actions (Preparatory_acts) that are taken by an Agent for the purpose of preparing for a later act.
Contrast this frame with a scenario involving earlier versions of some entity being superceded by later versions (e.g., _preliminary results, advance copy_).

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent uses the Preparatory_act to acheive a Purpose.

fe.name: Preparatory_act
fe.definition:
The action performed by the Agent that is a preliminary to the achievement of the Purpose. The Preparatory_act may also be expressed by a result of such an act.
Ex: ["pre" The company's actions at that stage] _were_ simply PRELIMINARY to the takeover. Ex: Nothing remarkable could be found, as it was almost certainly a PRELIMINARY ["pre" book] to the final publication of results.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The ultimate goal or purpose of the Agent, which the Preparatory_act enables.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A characteristic of the Preparatory_act, Agent, or other participant.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Preparatory_act is distant from the achievement of the Purpose.

fe.name: Domain_of_relevance
fe.definition:
The area, field, or domain for which the preliminary action is relevant.
Ex: This laid the ["dom" political] GROUNDWORK for his victory in May.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Preparatory_act takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the Preparatory_act takes place.

fe.name: Preparatory_phase
fe.definition:
The part of the larger process that is preliminary to the achievement of the Purpose.
Ex: We are still in the PRELIMINARY ["pre_pha" phases].

lexunit.name: preliminary.a
lexunit.definition: COD: preceding or done in preparation for something fuller or more important.

lexunit.name: preliminary.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a preliminary action or event.

lexunit.name: exploratory.a
lexunit.definition: FN: done for the purpose of discovering facts in order to proceed in a course of action.

lexunit.name: groundwork.n
lexunit.definition: COD: preliminary or basic work.

lexunit.name: prefatory.a
lexunit.definition: FN: (especially of speech) done initially, as preparation for later exposition.

lexunit.name: preparatory.a
lexunit.definition: COD: serving as or carrying out preparation.

frame.name: Ineffability
frame.definition:
A Stimulus inspires a feeling of awe and interest in a (generally implicit or generic) Experiencer due to desirable qualities which are difficult to explain. Alternatively, the Attribute of the Stimulus may be described instead.
Ex: _There is_ a certain JE-NE-SAIS-QUOI ["Stimulus" about that city] .

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition: The entity which inspires a feeling of amazement at its exceptionality.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer experiences the emotion brought about by the Stimulus

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: An expression of how unusual the ineffability of the Stimulus is.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Stimulus is able to bring about the emotion.
Ex: ["Circumstances" When sunny] the view is IMPRESSIVE.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
The Parameter is the area in which the Stimulus brings about an effect on the Experiencer.
Ex: This art work is ["Parameter" aesthetically] PLEASING. Ex: The book is ["Parameter" emotionally] DISTURBING.

fe.name: Comparison_set
fe.definition: The Comparison_set is the set of individuals the Stimulus is compared to when determining the Degree of the emotional reaction.

fe.name: Property
fe.definition:
A feature of the Stimulus which causes a particular experience.
Ex: That night was MAGIC ["Property" in every way] .

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition:
An expression of the attribute of ineffability.
Ex: She had a MAGICAL ["Attribute" quality] .

lexunit.name: magic.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a mysterious and enchanting quality.

lexunit.name: magic.a
lexunit.definition: COD: a mysterious and enchanting quality.

lexunit.name: magical.a
lexunit.definition: FN: characterized by a a mysterious and enchanting quality.

lexunit.name: ineffable.a
lexunit.definition: COD: too great or extreme to be expressed in words

lexunit.name: ineffability.n
lexunit.definition: FN: being too great or extreme to be expressed in words

lexunit.name: je ne sais quoi.n
lexunit.definition: FN: indescribableness

lexunit.name: magicalness.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the condition or quality of having a mysterious and enchanting quality.

frame.name: Possibilities
frame.definition:
There exist a number of different possible Events that may happen in the future. In most cases, there is an Agent involved who has to consider which of the possible Events will or should occur. A Salient_entity which is deeply involved in the Event may also be mentioned.
Ex: ["Agent" You] _have_ ["Number_of_possibilities" but two] ["Event" CHOICES] ["Salient_entity" for your daughter] .

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: Something that may happen in the future.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: An individual involved in the Event.

fe.name: Number_of_possibilities
fe.definition: The number of different future Events under consideration.

fe.name: Salient_entity
fe.definition: An entity intimately involved in the Event.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about which is associated with some of the possible Events but not others.
Ex: There 's only one CHOICE ["Purpose" to get what you want] .

lexunit.name: way.n
lexunit.definition: FN: option

lexunit.name: alternative.n
lexunit.definition: COD: one of two or more available possibilities.

lexunit.name: chance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an opportunity

frame.name: Have_associated
frame.definition:
A Topical_entity has properties which are affected by the existence and association of an Entity.
Ex: ["Time" By the 1920s] ["Topical_entity" a characteristic book] HAD ["Entity" black and white photographic illustrations only] .
Ex: ["Topical_entity" Their schools] HAD ["Ent" an improved and more balanced curriculum] .
Ex: ["Circumstances" With dual citizenship] , ["Topical_entity" Stephen] ["Time" now] HAD ["Entity" two presidents he hated] .

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Some entity, abstract or concrete, which is stated to exist and be associated with the Topical_entity.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Entity exists and is associated with the Topical_entity

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The period during which the Entity exists in association with the Topical_entity.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: A situation, force, or entity which brings about the existence of the Entity or its association with the Topical_entity.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the Entity is associated with the Topical_entity.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Entity is declared to exist in association with the Topical_entity.

fe.name: Point_of_view
fe.definition:
The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Entity to be associated with the Topical_entity.
Ex: ["pov" For him], THERE 'S just too much drink in the world.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Topical_entity
fe.definition: The entity under discussion, whose states and properties are impacted by its association with the Entity.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

frame.name: Visit_host
frame.definition: A Visitor matches location with a Host by going to a place strongly associated with a Host, the Host_location (often a place of residence, employment, or government), in order to acheive a Purpose. The Host allows the use of his/her resources. The visit is often social in nature.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: An individual that allows the use of his or her resources for the benefit of the Visitor.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the hospitality of the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition: The location associated with the Host, where the Visitor arrives at and remains during the visit.

frame.name: Visiting_scenario
frame.definition: An Agent and an Entity become co-located. The Agentin pursuit of a Purpose, and temporarily remains with the Entity to fulfil this Purpose and then departs again, usually back to their Normal_location.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: A place that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

frame.name: Visitor_and_host
frame.definition: A Visitor and a Host become co-located at a location strongly associated with the Host. The Visitor is allowed by the Host to use the Host's location and/or resources for the achievement of a Purpose. The visit is often social in nature.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: An individual that allows the use of his or her resources for the benefit of the Visitor.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition: A location strongly associated with (in the territory of) the Host, often a place of residence, government, or employment. The Visitor is allowed onto the Host_location and may be invited to make use of it or resources contained within it.

frame.name: Visiting_scenario_arrival
frame.definition: An Agent arrives at a location that should help them achieve their Purpose. This situation is point-of-view-neutral.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: Agent is the object that moves under its own power.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Agent moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Goal. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: Goal is any expression that tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. Although always conceptually present and specific, Goalmay sometimes be understood from context, rather than expressed by any separate constituent.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent arrives.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent arrives at the Goal.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the visiting occurs

frame.name: Visiting_scenario_departing
frame.definition: An Agent departs from the Source, normally bound for their normal location. This is a point-of-view-neutral conception of the departure.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: This is the individual which moves under their own power.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Agent, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'. Ex: Spiderman LEFT ["Path" through the window].

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE labels any expression which tells where the Agent ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source. Ex: Our visitors LEFT ["Goal" for Los Angeles].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels. Ex: The messenger LEFT the room ["Manner" clumsily].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Agent which results in their departure. Ex: He RETREATED from his opponent ["Means" by taking a quick leap backwards].

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Agent is moving. Ex: He ["Speed" quickly] EXITED the crowded terminal.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Agent is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Agent. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.
Ex: We SET OUT ["Mode_of_transportation" by boat] for Nova Scotia. Ex: Wilbur DEPARTED ["Mode_of_transportation" on foot] for London.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance that the Agent has traveled. Ex: He WITHDREW ["Distance" a little] from her.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the departure takes place.Ex: We LEFT ["Time" in the morning].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent departs from the Source.

frame.name: Visiting_scenario_stay
frame.definition: An Agent matches location with an Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose. Quite often, the Purpose is social- or entertainment-oriented. This scene is point-of-view-neutral.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The sentient entity that is temporarily with the Entity in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The physical entity that is permanently associated with entities or characteristics that the Agent wishes to use for some Purpose. During the visit, the Agent matches location with the Entity.

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition: A state (of the Agent) that results as a consequence of the Agent being situated at the Entity.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the Entity and that the Agent wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Agent normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which a visit is made.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that the Agent spends at the Entity.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any overall description of the details of the visit, either in terms of how it matches other events (_the same way_) or in terms of states of the Agent that affect the action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: A description of the position of the Agent during the visit.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Agent that enables their visit.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of instances of the described event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: A characterization of the average number of times a visit happens over a period of time.

frame.name: Drop_in_on
frame.definition: A Visitor arrives at the Host_location as a guest of the Host, for the purpose of acheiving a Purpose. The Purpose is often social in nature, i.e., the visit itself constitutes a goal.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The Visitor arrives at the Host_location to visit the Host for a Purpose.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Visitor moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor the Host or Host_location. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host is the person highly associated with the goal location of the Visitor, and who allows the Visitor onto his/her territory, and possibly to make use of available resources. The Host and Visitor and in a host-guest relationship.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Visitor arrives.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Visitor arrives at a location associated with the Host.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition: The Host_location is a place primarily associated with the Host.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: The Containing_event denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the visiting takes place.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The frequency with whic hthe Visitor drops in on a Host.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time that the Visitor remains with the Host.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The larger area within which the visiting takes place.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: This FE indicates that the visiting is a particular instance in a series of repeated visiting events.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state of affairs that explains why the Visitor is making a visit.

lexunit.name: drop in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make an unannounced visit.

lexunit.name: stop in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make a short visit.

lexunit.name: pop in.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make a short, unannounced visit.

frame.name: Visit_host_arrival
frame.definition: The Visitor arrives at the Host_location to visit the Host.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The Visitor goes to the Host

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent. If present, they often express a general direction from which a Visitor moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Host_location. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host welcomes the Visitor as a guest. The location strongly associated with the Host serves as the goal of the Visitor's motion.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A Manner expression describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Means by which an Visitor arrives.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Visitor arrives at the Host or Host_location.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition: The Host_location is a location associated with the Host, and is commonly the place of residence or employment of the Host.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the arrival event occurs.

frame.name: Visit_host_stay
frame.definition: A Visitor is located with a Host for a visit.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The sentient entity that is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host welcomes the Visitor to his/her location, with which he/she is permanently associated. The Host allows the Visitor use of resources to accomplish a Purpose. During the visit, the Visitor matches location with the Host.

fe.name: Dependent_state
fe.definition: A state (of the Visitor) that results as a consequence of the Visitor being situated with the Host.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The activity that is enabled by the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.

fe.name: Normal_location
fe.definition: The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which a visit is made.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that the Visitor spends with the Host.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any overall description of the details of the visit, either in terms of how it matches other events (_the same way_) or in terms of states of the Visitor that affect the action.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: A description of the position of the Visitor during the visit.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Visitor that enables their visit.

fe.name: Iterations
fe.definition: The number of instances of the described event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: A characterization of the average number of times a visit happens over a period of time.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition: The Host_location is the location permanently associated with the Host, and which the Visitor stays at temporarily for the acheiving of some Purpose.

frame.name: Visit_host_departure
frame.definition: A Visitor departs from a Host_location after having visited a Host.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The Visitor departs from the location of the Host.

fe.name: Host_location
fe.definition: The Visitor departs from the Host_location, a location strongly associated with the Host.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition: This FE labels any expression which tells where the Visitor ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action of the Visitor which results in their departure.

fe.name: Speed
fe.definition: This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Visitor is moving.

fe.name: Mode_of_transportation
fe.definition:
The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.
In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition: The distance that the Visitor has traveled.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the departure takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: >The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Visitor departs from the Source.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host allows the Visitor to use his/her resources, and to remain temporarily at the Host_location.

frame.name: Receive_visitor_scenario
frame.definition: A (potential) Visitor arrives at a location associated with a (potential) Host. The Host permits the Visitor to enter the location, and allows the Visitor to avail him/herself of available resources, in order to pursue some goal. The visit is often for social or entertainment reasons. After a temporary stay at the Host's location, the Visitor departs.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host allows the Visitor to remain with him/her to acheive a goal.

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The Visitor temporarily remains with the Host in order to achieve his/her purpose.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The goal of the Host in allowing the Visitor to enter the Host's location.

frame.name: Have_visitor_over
frame.definition: A Host, at a location strongly associated with him/herself (such as a place of employment or residence), temporarily hosts a Visitor so that the Visitor can achieve a goal. The purpose of the visit is often social in nature.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host allows the Visitor to enter his/her location (house, office, etc.) for a temporary period so that the Visitor can achieve a goal. The goal is often socially-motivated (e.g., socialization between the Visitor and the Host).

fe.name: Visitor
fe.definition: The Visitor is a guest of the Host at a location strongly associated with the Host.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose of the Host in hosting the Visitor.

lexunit.name: have over.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be host to a visitor at, e.g., one's home.

frame.name: Version_sequence
frame.definition: An entity goes through several versions, from initial to final.

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The Item is one version among several versions (which may or may not yet exist), progressively getting closer to a final version.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The degree of the distance the Item is from the final version.
Ex: I warn you, this is a ["deg" very rough] DRAFT.

lexunit.name: preliminary.a
lexunit.definition: FN: initial, at an early stage.

lexunit.name: initial.a
lexunit.definition: FN: at the beginning stage.

lexunit.name: draft.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an initial or rough version (especially of a written document).

lexunit.name: final.a
lexunit.definition: FN: final, finished.

lexunit.name: rough.a
lexunit.definition: FN: near the initial stages, unpolished.

lexunit.name: working.a
lexunit.definition: FN: provisional, temporarily fulfilling a purpose.

frame.name: Hospitality
frame.definition: A Host is judged regarding their attitude as a potential host in a guest-host relationship. The Host exhibits a Behavior that is judged as demonstrating a particular degree hospitality towards a Guest. Alternatively, the Host may reveal an Expressor that indicates a particular sort of attitude.

fe.name: Host
fe.definition: The Host is the person whose Behavior towards others as a (potential) host is evaluated.

fe.name: Guest
fe.definition: The Guest is the entity which is positively or negatively treated by the Host.

fe.name: Behavior
fe.definition: The Behavior is the action of the Host on which the evaluation of the Host's character is based.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree is the extent to which the Host exhibits the particular Behavior towards others.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the situation or person that the Host's Behavior responds to or is related to.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Host.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner is the way in which the Host embodies the characters of a good or poor host.

fe.name: Judge
fe.definition: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the evaluation.

lexunit.name: hospitality.n
lexunit.definition: FN: willingness to warmly and coridally accept guests.

lexunit.name: hospitable.a
lexunit.definition: FN: welcoming of guests.

lexunit.name: red carpet.n
lexunit.definition: FN: respectful and lavish treatment of an important guest.

frame.name: Containment_relation
frame.definition: An Entity is described as located inside a Container.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.

frame.name: Supporting
frame.definition:
A Supporter asists to strengthen the Supported by lending itsself in material aid (or abstract assistance in the case of metaphorical uses).
Ex: ["Supported" The bottom of the wall] is SUPPORTED ["Supporter" by the foundation].
Ex: ["Supporter" Many legislators] have SUPPORTED ["Supported" the industry] ["Time" in the past].
Ex: ["Supporter" The revetment layers] BUTTRESSED ["Supported" the mud-mortared cobblestone core wall].
Ex: ["Supporter" Online gambling] can BOLSTER ["Supported" the US economy].

fe.name: Supporter

fe.name: Supported

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The measure to which the Supporter's assistance brings the Supported added strength and support.
Ex: The physical therapist must ["Degree" totally] SUPPORT tthe patient during the exercises.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The time period during which the Supporter supports the Supported.
Ex: ["Duration" For some seventy years], this judicial fabrication BUTTRESSED racial segregation.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity used by the Supporter in service of the Supported's strength by support.
Ex: Water buffalo have BUTTRESSED humanity’s survival ["Instrument" with their meat, horns, hides, milk, and butterfat].

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Manner in which a Supporter supports the Supported.
Ex: The British Government ["Manner" happily] BUTTRESSED Saddam's appalling oppression of his people.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
An action that the Supporter undertakes in service of the Supported's strengthening.
Ex: The foundation SUPPORTS the building ["Means" by distributing the load to the ground below.]

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Place where the support occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
This FE identifies when the support occurs.
Ex: ["Time" Early in the twentieth century], such economic arguments BUTTRESSED the creation of a National Park Service.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The situation that the Supporter wishes to bring about by supporting the Supported.
Ex: The porch tower of Saint-Germain-des-Prés is sturdily BUTTRESSED ["Purpose" to support the weight of its massive bells].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: A state-of-affairs from which the accomplishment would be predicted.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: A clause describing the event as a whole.

The ["Hunter" Hunter] hopes the attempt will result in the catching and killing of the living entity that is intended for human consumption. The act of seeking ["Food" Food] inherently involves the assistance of some tool, which can be an extension of the ["Hunter" Hunter]'s body or an artifact fashioned or exploited for the use of food seeking, catching, and/or killing.
Ex: ["Place" In the Congo], ["Hunter" he] hunted ["Food" big game] ["Particular_iteration" for the first time].

frame.name: Proximity_image_schema
frame.definition: A Profiled_region is picked out which is near to (or far from) the Ground to a certain Degree. The Profiled_region cannot contact or overlap the location of the Ground, as this is categorically different--see Contact_image_schema and Collocation_image_schema.

fe.definition: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

fe.name: Interior
fe.definition: A region of space located inside a Ground.

fe.name: Exterior
