frame.name: Alignment_image_schema
frame.definition: An Alignment_match region has the same orientation as the relatively linear Ground. The Alignment_mismatch region is oriented perpendicularly to the Ground.

fe.name: Alignment_match
fe.definition: A region of space oriented the same as the Ground.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: An entity whose location and orientation is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Alignment_match and Alignment_mismatch regions.

fe.name: Alignment_mismatch
fe.definition: A region oriented approximately perpendicular to the Ground

frame.name: Conquering
frame.definition:
This frame describes a Theme losing its autonomy and perhaps sustaining material damage as the result of a successful invasion on the behalf of a Conquerer.
Ex: ["Conquerer" The Spaniards] CONQUERED ["Theme" the Incas] ["Instrument" with both the Cross and the arquebus]
Ex: He said that the aim had been the TAKEOVER ["Theme" of the Soviet government] ["Conquerer" by "advocates of swift privatization"]
Ex: ["Theme" The Romans] FELL ["Conquerer" to the Goths] ["Time" in 410 AD].
Ex: ["Conquerer" Bright Star campaign forces] CAPTURED ["Theme" the garrison town of Kajo Kaji]

fe.name: Conquerer
fe.definition:
The Conquerer is the entity that overtakes the Theme.
Ex: ["Conquerer" The Achaemenid monarch Cambyses] CONQUERED Egypt in the year 525 BC

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Theme is the land, government, and its people that is seized by the Conquerer.
Ex: Britain had an opportunity to CONQUER ["Theme" Europe].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE describes the intensity and extent of the conquering event.
Ex: Britain had been ` ["Degree" completely] CONQUERED and immediately thrown away '

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The manner in which the Conquerer takes over the Theme.
Ex: He ["Manner" violently] CAPTURED the castles of La Haye , Preuilly and Champigny

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action by which the conquering event is made possible through the efforts of the Conquerer.
Ex: They CAPTURED the haunted castle ["Means" by bombarding it with low-energy x-rays].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The location where the Conquerer takes over the Theme.
Ex: ["Place" On Planet Earth], humans prefer to CONQUER those lands whose acquistion offers some economic benefit or advantage.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The Time at which the Conquerer seizes the Theme.
Ex: China 's ["Time" 1997] TAKEOVER would push over 10 per cent of the population out of the colony.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The reason why the Conquerer seized the Theme.
Ex: Rome initially CONQUERED lands ["Purpose" in order to enrich itself].

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
The tool used by the Conquerer to seize the Theme.
Ex: The army will CONQUER the far-away lands ["Instrument" with the most sophisticated weapons ever made].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

lexunit.name: conquer.v
lexunit.definition: FN: seize a land and its government by force

lexunit.name: takeover.n
lexunit.definition: FN: The seizing of a land, its people, and its goverment by force.

lexunit.name: capture.v
lexunit.definition: FN: forcibly taking over a land, its people, and its governement.

lexunit.name: fall.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to be taken over and potentially destroyed by an army

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to occupy and have authority over a locale and its people.

frame.name: Invading
frame.definition:
The Invader enters a ["Land" Land] in an aggressive attempt to cripple or dominate its people and its goverment.
Ex: ["Time" In August 1990] ,["Invader" Iraq] was INVADING ["Land" Kuwait] , which led to the Gulf war .
Ex: Some towns in Russia were ravaged by ["Invader" barbarian] INVASIONS ["Time" in the thirteenth century].

fe.name: Land
fe.definition:
The political area that is being crippled by the Invader's entry.
Ex: Henry II had made no attempt to INVADE ["Land" France.]

fe.name: Weapon
fe.definition: An entity used by the Invader to assist in the invasion of the Land.

fe.name: Invader
fe.definition:
The army or other self-directed entity that is entering the Land in a hostile manner.
Ex: Indeed , three months later ["Invader" Hitler] INVADED Austria.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Invader that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An intentional action performed by the Invader that accomplishes the assault.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the location where the Invader invades the Land.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Invader attacks the Land.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: A state of affairs that the Invader is responding to that leads them to make an assault on the Land.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Invader invades Land.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition: The starting-point of the motion of the Invader or projectiles of the Invader as they move toward the the Place that the Land is occupying in the attack. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Invader or Land while the Invasion occurs.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result of the invasion on the Land by the Invader.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held. Form: once, twice, Cardinal expression + /it times, /it lots/a lot

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole and describes and describes the event more generally.

fe.name: Path
fe.definition: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Invader travels.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Invader invades the Land.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: This FE indicates the subtype of invasion into the Land.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes how intense the invation of the Land is.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: For how long the Land is invaded by the Invader.

lexunit.name: invade.v
lexunit.definition: FN: aggressively enter into a region.

lexunit.name: invasion.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the act of invading

lexunit.name: overrun.v
lexunit.definition: FN: invade an area in great numbers

frame.name: Contact_image_schema
frame.definition: A Profiled_region occupies the space in contact with the Ground.

fe.name: Profiled_region
fe.definition: A region of space in contact with a Ground.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

frame.name: Invasion_scenario
frame.definition: An Invader enters a land in an attempt to dominate the Attacked and they either fail or succeed.

fe.name: Invader
fe.definition: The Invader is the entity that overtakes the Attacked.

fe.name: Attacked
fe.definition: The Attacked is the land, government, and its people that is seized by the Invader.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes the intensity and extent of the invasion event.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which the Invader takes over the Attacked.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action by which the conquering event is made possible through the efforts of the Invader.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Invader takes over the Attacked.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time at which the Invader seizes the Attacked.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason why the Invader seized the Attacked.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The tool used by the Invader to seize the Attacked.

frame.name: Repel
frame.definition: A Defender successfully repels the aggressive attempt of takeover by an Enemy.

fe.name: Enemy
fe.definition:
The ["Enemy" Enemy] is the entity that fails to overtake the Defender.
Ex: General Monk would REPEL ["Enemy" Jacobite invaders].

fe.name: Defender
fe.definition:
The Defender is the land, government, and its people that the Enemy fails to seize.
Ex: ["Defender" General Winter] REPELLED invaders from Napoleon to Hitler.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes the intensity and extent of the repelling event.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The manner in which the Defender repels the Enemy.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action by which the repelling event is made possible through the efforts of the Defender.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Defender repels the Enemy.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Defender succeeds to repel the Enemy.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason why the Defender repels the Enemy.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The tool used by the Defender to repel the Enemy.

fe.name: Invasion_act
fe.definition:
This FE refers to the Invasion_act perpetrated by the Enemy.
Ex: ["Defender" Spain] pledged to REPEL ["Invasion_act" any Allied invasion].

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: This FE describes the outcome of the repelling event.

lexunit.name: repel.v
lexunit.definition: FN: push back an enemy

lexunit.name: resist.v
lexunit.definition: FN: withstand an offending force

frame.name: Region_with_portal
frame.definition: A Portal, Exterior, Surface, Boundary, and Interior are picked out relative to a Ground.

fe.name: Interior
fe.definition: A region of space located inside a Ground.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Interior, Surface, or Boundary.

fe.name: Surface
fe.definition: The region located outside of, but in contact with, the Ground.

fe.name: Boundary
fe.definition: The region associated with the boundary of the Ground.

fe.name: Exterior
fe.definition: The region which is not located inside or in contact with the Ground.

frame.name: Becoming_dry
frame.definition: An Entity loses moisture with the outcome of being in a dry state.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity is the thing that loses moisture and becomes dry.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The intensity with which the Entity becomes dry.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Entity becomes dry.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Entity becomes dry.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Entity becomes dry.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The situation in which the ["Entity" Entity] is becoming dry.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: This FE indicates that the visiting is a particular instance in a series of repeated visiting events.

lexunit.name: dry up.v
lexunit.definition: FN: FN: To lose moisture and become completely dried out.

lexunit.name: exsiccate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to lose water

lexunit.name: dehydrate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to lose water

lexunit.name: dry.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to lose moisture

frame.name: Attending
frame.definition:
An Agent goes to an Event and is present in a relatvely non-participatory way.
Ex: ["Agent" The Angolan guerrillas] will ATTEND ["Event" a September meeting] ["Place" in Zaire].
Ex: ["Agent" We] just GO ["Event" to the movies] ["Time" when it rains].
Ex: ["Agent" His] ATTENDANCE ["Event" at the funeral] did not go unnoticed.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person who chooses to make himself present at the Event.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The Event is the deliberate set of happenings given at a particular time and place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Agent went about going to the Event.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: Through what strategies and efforts the Agent made possible his attendance at the Event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Agent attends the Event.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Agent attends the Event.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Under what conditions the Agent goes to the Event.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason why the Agent goes to the Event.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes the event as a whole.

lexunit.name: attend.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to be present at a given time and place

lexunit.name: go_(to).v
lexunit.definition: FN: be at and attend an event

lexunit.name: attendance.n
lexunit.definition: FN: being present at an event

frame.name: Abandonment
frame.definition:
An ["Agent" Agent] leaves behind a ["Theme" Theme] effectively rendering it no longer within their control or of the normal security as one's property.
Ex: ["Agent" Carolyn] ABANDONED ["Theme" her car] and jumped on a red double decker bus.
Ex: Perhaps ["Agent" he] LEFT ["Theme" the key] in the ignition
Ex: ABANDONMENT ["Theme" of a child] is considered to be a serious crime in many jurisdictions.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The ["Agent" Agent] is the person who acts to leave behind the Theme.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The ["Theme" Theme] is the entity that is relinguished to no one from the ["Agent" Agent]'s possession.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Agent gives up the Theme.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Agent gives up the Theme.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The style in which the Agent gives up the Theme.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: For what expanse of time the Agent has given up the Theme.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Explanation denotes a proposition from which the act of abandonment logically follows.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The FE Depictive describes the Agent during the abandoning event.

lexunit.name: leave.v
lexunit.definition: FN: let remain in another place as abondoned

lexunit.definition: FN: the act of relinquishing to no one

lexunit.name: abandoned.a
lexunit.definition: FN: the state of being left behind

lexunit.name: forget.v

frame.name: Soaking_up
frame.definition:
An Item works to become imbued with a Substance.
Ex: ["Item" Paper and board] ABSORB ["Substance" moisture] ["Time" in the winter].
Ex: ["Item" A stable soil] SOAKS UP ["Substance" water].

fe.name: Item
fe.definition: The Item is the absorbant friendly thing that takes in the Substance.

fe.name: Substance
fe.definition: The Substance is the material that is taken in by the Item.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Item takes in Substance.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Item takes in Substance.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: For what length of time the Item is imbued with Substance.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Item soaks in the Substance.

frame.name: Cause_emotion
frame.definition:
An Agent acts to cause a Experiencer to feel a certain emotion.
Ex: ["Experiencer" I] was ["Degree" so] OFFENDED ["Agent" by her behaviour towards me].
Ex: It does not matter if ["Agent" the cartoon] _is_ INSULTING ["Experiencer" to men].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person who's action's cause an emotion in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The Experiencer feels an emotion as caused by the Agent.
Ex: ["Experiencer" You] will perhaps be AFFRONTED by my frankness

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.
Ex: I had ["Degree" mortally] OFFENDED her.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
The tool used by the Agent to cause an emotion in the Experiencer.
Ex: We will INSULT you ["Instrument" with our compassion]

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An act performed by anAgent that enables them to act upon the Experiencer.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: In what way the Agent causes an emotion in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE describes the event as a whole, often as a VPing.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE describes the reason for the state of affairs described by the target.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: For how long instances of an Agent causing the Patient an emotion has repeatedly occured.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Agent causes emotion in the Experiencer.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The Event is the occasion or happening that evokes emotions in the Experiencer. This Event occurs as the direct result of a sentient being's actions.

fe.name: Type
fe.definition: Type designates the kind of emotion that the Agent causes the Experiencer to have.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Agent causes the Experiencer to feel an emotion.

lexunit.name: affront.v

frame.name: Emotions_by_stimulus
frame.definition:
An Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State has an emotion as brought on by an Stimulus or Topic.
Ex: The JOYFUL ["Event" reunion] took place on Sunday.
Ex: The Polish-born Pope was driven past JUBILANT ["Experiencer" crowds].
Ex: ["Experiencer" I] am GLAD ["Topic" about the sheep] .

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition:
The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.
Ex: At Medicine Man's ragtime dance contest, a JUBILANT ["Experiencer" girl] drove the crowd wild.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs. It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.
Ex: Earl is JUBILANT ["Topic" about his new swim trunks].

fe.name: Stimulus
fe.definition:
The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.
Ex: ["Stimulus" Putin’s initiative] caused JOYFUL ["State" excitement] in Baku on Friday.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

fe.name: Empathy_target
fe.definition: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

fe.name: Expressor
fe.definition:
The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state. They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.
Ex: He met me with a GLAD ["Expressor" face].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response. In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus. Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.
Ex: Armed officials marred the JOYFUL ["State" mood] at the recent Mon festival in Samut Sakhon..

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in.
Ex: I am helping them to have the JOYFUL ["Event" birth] they want.

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, Event, or State can be described as having said emotion.

fe.name: Issue
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Issue that the Agent deals with.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the person who is acting to deal with the Issue.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the intentional act occurs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the reason why the Agent confronts the issue.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies the way in which an Agent goes about facing the Issue.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (_presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully_).

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The Domain within which the Agent acts.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The Result describes the resulting outcome of the confronting act.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE gives a description of the confronting event as a whole.

lexunit.name: face.v
lexunit.definition: FN: put oneself in the position to understand and being dealing with something unpleasant.

lexunit.name: confront.v
lexunit.definition: FN: begin to try to handle a problem

frame.name: Dying
frame.definition:
A Protagonist is near or approaching death.
Ex: But a DYING ["Protagonist" patient] is still a living patient.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The FE Protagonist is the being or entity that dies.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the dying event happens.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason why the dying event occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the dying event occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: How long the Protagonist is dying.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the dying event occurs.

lexunit.name: dying.a
lexunit.definition: FN: In the state and process of approaching death.

lexunit.name: moribund.a
lexunit.definition: FN: At the point of death

frame.name: Prevent_from_having
frame.definition:
An Agent or Preventing_cause keeps a Protagonist from having a State_of_affairs that they need or desire.
Ex: ["Agent" His parents] DEPRIVED ["Protagonist" him] ["State_of_affairs" of food] ["Duration" for days on end].
Ex: ["Preventing_cause" Our lonely city] STARVES ["Protagonist" us] ["State_of_affairs" of original live music].
Ex: ["Protagonist" Employees] were DENIED ["State_of_affairs" overtime pay and meal breaks]. ["Agent" CNI]

fe.name: Preventing_cause
fe.definition:
The Preventing_cause is the agent or force which keeps the Event from happening.
Ex: ["Preventing_cause" Israeli law] effectively DEPRIVED ["Protagonist" the owners] ["State_of_affairs" of their homes and lands].

fe.name: State_of_affairs
fe.definition:
The is the situation, state-of-affairs, or state of having a possession that the Protagonist is kept from having.
Ex: Their parents DENIED them ["State_of_affairs" a brand new car] upon their sweet 16.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time is when the Preventing_cause keeps the Event from taking place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The Place is where the Preventing_cause keeps the Event from taking place.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the person who keeps the Event from happening.
Ex: ["Agent" The uncaring King Frank] often STARVES his citizens of tax relief.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: The Protagonist is the person who is kept from having the State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition:
The reason why the Agent keeps the Protagonist from having the State_of_affairs.
Ex: I have suggested DEPRIVING children of TV-viewing time ["Purpose" as a sanction].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time for which the Protagonist is denied the State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition:
How it is possible that the deprivation event occurs.
Ex: ["Explanation" By acting as his own agent], Joe DEPRIVED himself of this valuable information.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE marks the frequency with which the Protagonist is prevented from having the State_of_affairs.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of prevention and which the prevention is taken to be a part of.

lexunit.name: deprive.v
lexunit.definition: FN: keep from having

lexunit.name: starve.v
lexunit.definition: FN: render someone totally without a desired possession or state-of-affairs.

lexunit.name: deny.v
lexunit.definition: FN: not allow to have something

frame.name: Relating_concepts
frame.definition:
A Concept_1 is related to Concept_2 by some Evidence.
Ex: ["Evidence" The single remaining piece of evidence] LINKED ["Concept_1" Kirov the tailor] ["Concept_2" to Kirov the dissident activist].
Ex: There is ["Evidence" ample data] RELATING ["Concept_1" earnings] ["Concept_2" to years of schooling.]

fe.name: Concept_1
fe.definition:
The concept which is linked to Concept_2.
Ex: High death rates among smokers CONNECT ["Concept_1" cigarettes] with disease.

fe.name: Concept_2
fe.definition:
The concept which is tied to Concept_1.
Ex: Skid marks on the street CONNECTS my neighbor's car ["Concept_2" to my broken mailbox].

fe.name: Point_of_view
fe.definition:
The point of view from which the connection exists.
Ex: ["Point_of_view" As far as we are concerned] this evidence TIES the secretary to the case of the missing apple fritters.

fe.name: Evidence
fe.definition:
The phenomenon that points to or proves the connection between Concept_1 and Concept_2. Generally expressed as an external.
Ex: ["Evidence" Footprints] CONNECT her to the crime.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the connection exists.
Ex: ["Circumstances" If we get the protocal right] the study will LINK leprosy to too much stress-inducing homework.

fe.name: Concepts
fe.definition:
The two concepts expressed jointly.
Ex: ["Concept_1" Ample evidence] is able to CONNECT ["Concepts" the two].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree of connection between the Concepts.
Ex: This ["Degree" definitively] CONNECTS our water shortage problems to the ascendance of a new governor.

fe.name: Specification
fe.definition:
A further specification on the linkage.
Ex: The evidence ["Specification" causally] LINKS these two.

lexunit.name: link.v
lexunit.definition: FN: bring two things together as being related

lexunit.name: connect.v
lexunit.definition: FN: relate one thing to another

lexunit.name: tie.v
lexunit.definition: FN: act as evidence for the connection between two ideas

lexunit.name: associate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: tie two things as at least loosely related

lexunit.name: relate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: connect two ideas as related

frame.name: Being_strong
frame.definition:
An Entity can bear a great outer force so as to resist destruction and damage.
Ex: The great and IMPREGNABLE ["Entity" fortress] still stands today.
Ex: ["Entity" His heart] _is_ ["Degree" by no means] STRONG, so he should ease into his exercise regime.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity is the item that cannot be penetrated.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE describes the intensity and extent of the Entity's strength.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Entity is strong.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The action by Entity earns its strength.

fe.name: Place

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time when the Entity is strong.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason why the Entity has strength.

fe.name: Force
fe.definition: The Force is the power against which the Entity has strength.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state and conditions of the world when the Entity is strong.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target. In some cases, the Depictive describes the participant by characterizing a subpart.

frame.name: Launch_process
frame.definition:
An Agent acts to begin the life of a ["Process" Process].
Ex: ["Time" After discovering her knack for organization], ["Agent" she decided to try to ] LAUNCH ["Process" a career in human resources].
Ex: ["Agent" The City of Bratislava] has LAUNCHED ["Process" a pilot project of providing internet access in the city centre].

fe.definition: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the process that the Agent initiates.

fe.definition: This FE identifies the Place where the Process is initiated.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means is the way in which the Agent initiates the Process.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE is for the Time when the Agent initiates the Process.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Agent initiates the Process.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the actor responsible for starting the Process.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: To what end the Agent initiates the Process.

fe.name: Subevent
fe.definition: This FE identifies the first Subevent of the started Process.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Agent initiates the Process.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modifies the target to indicate the legal- or "by rule" domain within which the event if initiating the ["Process" Process] is considered true.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why or the way in which the Agent initiates the Process.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world at the time when the Agent produces the Process.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Consecutive
fe.definition: A consecutive event to the starting of the Process of the Agent.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Concessive
fe.definition: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness.

fe.name: Beneficiary
fe.definition: The party for who's benefit the Process is launched.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Process is launched.

lexunit.name: launch.v
lexunit.definition: COD: begin (something) energetically and enthusiastically

frame.name: Passing
frame.definition: An Agent literally transfers a Theme to a Recipient.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition:
The Agent is the one who passes the Theme. The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.
Ex: ["Agent" Pat] PASSED me the ball.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The FE Theme is generally an NP Object that is passed to the Recipient.
Ex: Pat PASSED ["Theme" the ball] to the goalie.

fe.name: Source
fe.definition:
The FE Source is the starting point of the passing action
Ex: Pat PASSED the ball ["Source" from behind the defensemen].

fe.name: Path
fe.definition:
The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.
Ex: I PASSED him the ball ["Path" over the wall].

fe.name: Recipient
fe.definition:
The FE Recipient is the entity which possesses the Theme as a result of the passing.
Ex: Kim PASSED the salt ["Recipient" to her mother].

fe.name: Distance
fe.definition:
The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.
Ex: Pat PASSED the ball ["Distance" 50 meters] to me.

fe.name: Area
fe.definition:
The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which passing takes place when the passing is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.
Ex: The team PASSED the ball ["Area" around the court].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of a participant during the passing action. Ex: We PASSED the ball around, ["Depictive" gleeful].

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
Cause marks expressions that indicate a non-agentive force that causes the Theme to be passed.
Ex: ["Cause" The ATM] PASSED some money to me.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition:
An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme. It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.
Ex: When playing basketball, you should PASS ["Ins" with both hands].

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).
Ex: The players PASSED the ball to each other ["Place" at the park].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the passing of the Theme occurs.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition:
A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.
Ex: The center PASSED the ball ["Result" clear of the double-team].

fe.name: Initial_State
fe.definition:
A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.
Ex: Paul PASSED the ball away ["Initial_State" from the danger of the double-team].

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

fe.name: Competitor
fe.definition: The individual or individuals involved in the Competition.

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Competitor afterward.

fe.name: Margin
fe.definition: The amount by which the Competitor's and Scores differ.

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: The rank (according to Score) that a Competitor acheives.

fe.name: Prize
fe.definition: A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Competitor according to Score or Rank.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Competitor that results in the outcome of the Competition.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Competitor which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Competitor that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Competition takes place.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Competition takes place.

fe.name: Venue
fe.definition: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a Competition.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Competition
fe.definition: The event in which the Competitor competes.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why the Competitor wins the Competition.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when winning events began to be repeated to when they stopped.

fe.name: Opponent
fe.definition: The individual that the Competitor has been competing against.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world when the Competitor wins the Competition.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that prevails as a result of the Competitor winning the Competition.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Competitor wins the Competition.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modifies the target to indicate the legal- or other domain within which the winning event is considered true.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness, or a description of the state-of-affairs introduced by the winning event.

lexunit.name: win.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be victorious

frame.name: Beat_opponent
frame.definition: A Winner has victory over an Loser.

fe.name: Winner
fe.definition: The individual or individuals who beat the Loser.

fe.name: Score
fe.definition: A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Winner afterward.

fe.name: Margin
fe.definition: The amount by which the Winner's and Loser's Scores differ.

fe.name: Rank
fe.definition: The rank (according to Score) that a Winner acheives.

fe.name: Prize
fe.definition: A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Winner according to Score or Rank.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: An action of the Winner or Loser that makes the beating event possible.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the Winner or Loser which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Winner or Loser that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Winner has victory over the Loser.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Winner has victory Loser.

fe.name: Venue
fe.definition: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why the Winner has victory over the Loser.

fe.name: Period_of_iterations
fe.definition: The length of time from when winning events began to be repeated to when they stopped.

fe.name: Loser
fe.definition: The individual or individuals that get beat by the Winner.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world when the Winner beats the Loser.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily.

fe.name: Result
fe.definition: The state-of-affairs that prevails as a result of the Winner beating the Loser.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition: The frame element Iteration is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Winner beats the Loser.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: This FE modifies the target to indicate the legal- or other domain within which the winning event is considered true.

fe.name: Event_description
fe.definition: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness, or a description of the state-of-affairs introduced by the winning event.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A qualitative measure of how much the Winner beat the Loser.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

fe.name: Competition
fe.definition: The event in which the Competition competes.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Winner beats the Loser.

lexunit.name: prevail.v

lexunit.name: defeat.n

lexunit.name: trounce.v

lexunit.name: rout.n

lexunit.name: rout.v
lexunit.definition: FN: defeat decisively

frame.name: Punctual_perception
frame.definition:
A Perceiver briefly perceives a Phenomenon, often resulting in partial or uncertain perception. A Body_part that enables the perception may be mentioned, either metonymically replacing the Perceiver or in addition to the Perceiver.
Ex: ["Perceiver" I] 've been waiting here to _catch_ a GLIMPSE ["Phenomenon" of the snow leopard] for seven hours. Ex: If you go in there, ["Perceiver" you] 'll GET an EYEFUL. ["Phenomenon" INI]

fe.name: Perceiver
fe.definition:
The being who has a perceptual experience, generally construed to be not on purpose.
Ex: When she looked back, ["Perceiver" Maria] GLIMPSED an arm clawing around the corner.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition:
The entity or phenomenon that the perceiver experiences with his or her senses. It is typically expressed as Object with verbs.
Ex: The waiter GLIMPSED ["Phenomenon" a fly] disappearing under the surface of the soup.

fe.name: Body_part
fe.definition:
The Body_part is the location on the body where the perceptual experience takes place. It is typically expressed in a PP.
Ex: Mata Hari turned to her lawyer as ["BodP" her eyes] GLIMPSED the blindfold.

fe.name: Location_of_perceiver
fe.definition:
The Location_of_perceiver during the perceptual experience. It is typically expressed in a _from_-PP.
Ex: She had only GLIMPSED him briefly ["Location_of_perceiver" from behind a veil].

fe.name: Direction
fe.definition:
This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.
Ex: Hard to be certain what I GLIMPSED ["Direction" through the crack of the door].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The state of the Perceiver during the event of perception.

fe.name: Ground
fe.definition:
The perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver.
Ex: Had he caught a GLIMPSE of her face ["Ground" among the crowd]?

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Any description of properties of perception, such as: _clearly_, _loudly_, etc.
Ex: Pat ["Manner" clearly] ESPIED a dent on the hood.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
The Degree indicates the degree to which the Perception is experienced.
Ex: A nightmare creature, ["Degr" barely] GLIMPSED in the swirling dense smoke, was beating at the flames coming from its own body.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
The action whereby the Perceiver perceives.
Ex: He just GLIMPSED the car ["Mns" by craning his neck].

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time, generally construed as punctual, at which the Perceiver or the Body_part perceives the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

lexunit.name: glimpse.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to briefly see.

lexunit.name: glimpse.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the event or fact of briefly seeing.

lexunit.name: get_a(n)_eyeful.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to briefly see (a sufficient quantity of s.t. prurient)

frame.name: Ruling_legally
frame.definition:
An Authority with the power to make decisions hands down a Finding over a question presented in a formal or informal Case.
Ex: ["Authority" The judge] RULED ["Time" yesterday] ["Finding" that the revisions were not adequate]. ["Case" DNI]
Ex: ["Authority" A high court in London] RULED ["Case" on the case] ["Finding" that a vulture fund can extract more than $20 million from Zambia for a debt].
Ex: ["Case" In the California case], ["Authority" a judge] RULED ["Time" Oct. 12] ["Finding" that Tendler must pay the bloggers' legal fees].

fe.name: Authority
fe.definition:
The Authority (which may be the jury, judge, magistrate or court) decides on the Finding.
Ex: ["Authority" The US International Trade Commission] RULED ["Finding" that a 1987 anti-dumping tariff against frozen concentrated orange juice from Brazil could be revoked] ["Case" DNI].

fe.name: Finding
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the outcome of the Authority's deliberation or consideration.
Ex: Miss Mahmod's father RULED ["Finding" that she would never marry him].

fe.name: Case
fe.definition:
This FE describes the question on which the Authority gives a Finding.
Ex: US Supreme Court RULED ["Case" on flag salutes in public schools] today.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the Authority gives his Finding.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the Finding takes place.

fe.name: Legal_Basis
fe.definition: This FE indicates the basis in law of a Finding.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances under which the ruling was reached.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Authority acts.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: This FE identifies the purpose why the Authority returns a particular Finding.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE identifies an action that the Authority performs in order to return the verdict.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for the Finding.

fe.name: Re_encoding
fe.definition: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Epistemic_stance
fe.definition: The domain within which the ruling event is considered to be true.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The amount of time that a Finding holds.

lexunit.name: rule.v
lexunit.definition: COD: pronounce authoritatively and legally to be the case

frame.name: Mention
frame.definition:
A Communicator or Medium briefly references something in a Message, in which only a subpart of the full content is profiled.
Ex: ["Communicator" The General Secretary] MENTIONS ["Specified_content" some of them] ["Medium" in his report].
Ex: ["Medium" The Queen 's Speech] also MENTIONS ["Message" the importance of making sure that Iraq complies with United Nations resolutions].
Ex: When ["Specified_content" Barack Obama’s name] was MENTIONED, boos filled the room. ["Communicator" CNI]

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition:
The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.
Ex: ["Communicator" Her father] never MENTIONED it.

fe.name: Addressee
fe.definition:
The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.
Ex: I MENTIONED it ["Addressee" to him] in direct terms.

fe.name: Message
fe.definition:
A proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.
Ex: A CBS report did MENTION ["Message" that the First Lady was required to wear a flak jacket for her safety].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition:
The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.
Ex: ["Medium" The report] also MENTIONED contamination problems during the manufacture.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.
Ex: Her mother MENTIONED ["Manner" casually] that Parr had gone to Belfast.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Communicator communicates.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the the Message is mentioned.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration is the length of time during which the communication takes place.

fe.name: Iteration
fe.definition:
The number of times the Message is mentioned by the Communicator.
Ex: I MENTIONED it ["Iteration" fourteen times] and it still wasn't enough.

fe.name: Particular_iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the Communicator mentions the Message.

fe.name: Specified_content
fe.definition:
The relevant entity or state-of-affairs that the Communicator mentions.
Ex: If someone MENTIONS ["Specified_content" things like ration books] , my stomach turns.

fe.name: Containing_event
fe.definition: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world when the Communicator mentions the Message or Specified_content.

lexunit.name: mention.v
lexunit.definition: COD: refer to briefly.

frame.name: Indicating
frame.definition:
A Communicator or Medium assigns linguistic meaning to an Unresolved_referent thereby identifying the specific actor or entity which fulfills the answer to this question.
Ex: Can ["Communicator" you] NAME ["Unresolved_referent" all the U.S. Presidents]?
Ex: ["Communicator" No doctor] can NAME ["Unresolved_referent" the disease that's killing him].
Ex: ["Frequency" Every year], ["Medium" InfoWorld] NAMES ["Unresolved_referent" 100 companies that have made the best use of technology].

fe.name: Communicator
fe.definition: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey the Unresolved_referent to another person.

fe.name: Unresolved_referent
fe.definition: The thing to which the Communicator or Medium refers for identification purposes.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The physical or abstract setting in which the Unresolved_referent is conveyed.

fe.name: Amount_of_information
fe.definition: The amount of information exchanged when communication occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The Manner in which the Communicator makes the indication.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the Communicator makes the indication.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
When the the Communicator is makes the indication.
Ex: ["Time" When this is resolved], I will NAME the winner.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: Duration is the length of time during which the indicating takes place.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition:
How often the Communicator or Medium indicates the Unresolved_referent.
Ex: ["Frequency" Every month], new people NAME him in connection with these crimes.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The reason why the Communicator is indicating the Unresolved_referent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Communicator or Medium indicates the Unresolved_referent.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: To what end the Communicator or Medium makes the indication.

frame.name: Cycle_of_existence_scenario
frame.definition: An Entity comes into being, exists for some time, and ceases to be.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Concrete or abstract entity that did not exist, then came into existence, then (potentially) ceased to exist.

frame.name: Event_in_history
frame.definition: This frames picks out the individual events that collectively make-up the whole of the line of history.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition: The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is part of the Event's history.

frame.name: Socially_significant_history_scenario
frame.definition: A series of Events are important to humankind and its culture.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

fe.name: Place

fe.name: Time

fe.name: Manner

fe.name: Domain

frame.name: Ceasing_to_be
frame.definition: An Entity ceases to exist.

fe.name: Place

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifes the Time when a new Entity ceases to be.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: This FE labels the Cause of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.

fe.name: Components
fe.definition: This FE identifies the components into which the Entity dissipates.

fe.name: Duration_of_endstate
fe.definition: This FE identifies the length of time before the Entity comes into existence again.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.

fe.name: Period_of_Iterations
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Period_of_Iterations during which habitual or iterative actions are performed.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Entity disappears.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The completeness of the disappearance of the Entity

frame.name: Out_of_existence
frame.definition:
An Entity has ceased to exist.
Ex: ["Entity" Theses termites] are HISTORY.
Ex: ["Entity" Hillary] is TOAST ["Time" after Texas and Ohio].
Ex: ["Entity" They] are GONE ["Cause" because you killed them all].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: Concrete or abstract entity that does not exist after the event.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This is the Place where the Entity (saliently) does not exist.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: A point at which the Entity (saliently) does not exist.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: This FE labels the Cause of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: This FE identifies the length of time before the Entity comes into existence again.

fe.name: Role
fe.definition: The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: The way in which the Entity disappears.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

lexunit.name: toast.n
lexunit.definition: FN: (effectively) out of existence; no longer relevant

lexunit.name: gone.a
lexunit.definition: FN: no longer in existence; depleted

lexunit.name: a thing of the past.n
