frame.name: Cycle_of_life_and_death
frame.definition: A Protagonist is born or sprouts, lives, dies, and then is dead.

fe.name: Protagonist
fe.definition: Protagonist identifies the being or entity that is dead or alive. Ex: ["Prot" Frank] was DEAD.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

frame.name: History
frame.definition:
A recordable sequence of events is associated with a given Topic.
Ex: And that is where the HISTORY ["Topic" of art] begins.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
The Topic is the subject about which the history is given.
Ex: The role of the Byzantine Empire in ["Topic" European] HISTORY is not understood by all.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is to be included in consideration of the Topic's history.
Ex: Elizabethan Stage remain classics of ["Domain" literary] HISTORY.

fe.name: End_time
fe.definition: The end of the span of time during which the Topic occurs.

fe.name: Start_time
fe.definition: The beginning of the time span over which the Topic occurs.

fe.name: Time_span
fe.definition: The span of time over which the events related to the Topic take place.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The Duration, often expressed in calendric units, of the history of the Topic.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the events concerning the Topic occured.

lexunit.name: history.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the sum of events associated with a given person, place, thing, or idea.

frame.name: Possibility
frame.definition:
A Possible_event is deemed to have some probability of occurrence, if some (generally implicit) further Condition pertains. The Condition, whether overt or implicit, usually concerns the decision of an agent to attempt to bring the Possible_event about. The primary implication is that certain other aspects of the situation that might have been expected to prevent the Possible_event, usually lack of capability or permission, do not pertain.
Ex: ["Possible_event" You] CA n't ["Possible_event" burn glass] . ["Condition" INI] Ex: ["Possible_event" You] CAN ["Possible_event" have two more] ["Condition" if you want] . Ex: ["Possible_event" This sense of lack] CAN ["Condition" never] ["Possible_event" be satisfied] . Ex: ["Possible_event" We] just CA n't ["Possible_event" stand it] ["Time" anymore] . ["Condition" INI]

fe.name: Possible_event
fe.definition: The Possible_event has met its preconditions, and will occur if some further Condition holds.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition:
The Circumstances under which the preconditions of the Possible_event are met.
Ex: ["Circumstances" In this weather], an experienced pilot CAN still manage to fly 500 miles.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition:
An entity, event, or state that brings about the possibility of the Possible_event.
Ex: They were not ABLE to go outside ["cau" because of the rain].

fe.name: Condition
fe.definition:
The state-of-affairs that does not hold, but if it did, the Possible_event would occur.
Ex: ["Condition" If he wants] , he CAN have all the fishsticks .

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Possible_event can occur.
Ex: You CAN come in ["Time" now].

lexunit.name: can.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be able to

frame.name: Duration_relation
frame.definition: A Period or Eventuality is related to its Duration. Alternatively, an Entity may stand in metonymically for an Eventuality that it is involved in.

fe.name: Eventuality
fe.definition:
A situation, action or event whose duration is being described. The Eventuality occurs as the External Argument if the adjective is used predicatively, or as the modified noun if the adjective is used attributively:
Ex: ["Eventuality" The lecture] did n't LAST long . Ex: ["Eventuality" My unease] PERSISTED for some time . Ex: PERSISTING decades past the end of the war , ["Eventuality" the economic disaster] was to shape the fate of central Europe .

fe.name: Period
fe.definition:
Sometimes a period of time, rather than an event or state is described.
Ex: ["Period" This difficult period] lasted only a short while .

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition:
The amount of time that the Eventuality, Period, or Entity lasts.
Ex: If the film LASTS ["Duration" more than one hour] , I ca n't stay .

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
An item which is metonymically related to an Eventuality. Some common eventualities that are metonymically entailed are the effect of the entity in its capacity as an instrument and the existence of the entity.
Ex: ["Entity" The anesthesia] LASTED four hours . Ex: ["Entity" You] would n't LAST five minutes !

fe.name: User
fe.definition:
An individual that deploys a resource to receive a benefit. The construction that introduces this FE is idiosyncratic, combining with _last_ (in this frame), _cost_, and _take_--and more marginally _see_ (in "saw me through the winter") and _keep_ (in "It 'll keep me for a while .") In this frame, the resource maps onto the Entity, and the benefit is the Eventuality.
Ex: A gallon of water wo n't LAST ["User" us] more than a few days .

lexunit.name: last.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have a duration or period of relevance of

lexunit.name: persist.v
lexunit.definition: FN: (of an undesirable thing) have a duration of

frame.name: Duration_scenario
frame.definition: An Event or Period has a particular Duration. The Duration may be characterized in several different ways: as a Durational direct measure, a Degree of deviation from an expected Duration, or as a Count of Units of standard, known duration.

fe.name: Period
fe.definition: The Period whose the duration Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Period which is under discussion, namely the duration.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the Period's absolute duration.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Duration from the norm.

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition: A standard measure, having a known duration.

fe.name: Count
fe.definition: The number of Units which are equivalent to the Duration of the Period.

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: An process whose duration is measured.

frame.name: Delimited_state_scenario
frame.definition: A State (often an ongoing process) is ongoing for some period of time.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the State's absolute duration.

fe.name: State
fe.definition: An ongoing state whose duration can be measured.

frame.name: Tolerating
frame.definition:
he words in this frame describe an Experiencer's feelings of tolerating with respect to some Content. A Reason for the toleration may also be expressed. Although the Content may refer to an actual, current state of affairs, quite often it refers to a general situation which causes the emotion.
Ex: ["Experiencer" He] could not TOLERATE ["Content" the smell of coconut] .

fe.name: Experiencer
fe.definition: The Experiencer experiences tolerance with respect to the Content.

fe.name: Content
fe.definition: Content is what the Experiencer's feeling of tolerance is directed towards.. The Content differs from a stimulus because the Content is not construed as being direcly responsible for causing the emotion. Ex: ["Experiencer" Everyone] must ENDURE ["Content" some disappointments in life].

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason is the explanation for why an Experiencer experiences the particular emotion. Ex: ["Experiencer" People] LOVE ["Content" giant pandas] ["Reason" because they look like teddy bears].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The Degree to which the toleration occurs.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Manner of performing an action

fe.name: Parameter
fe.definition:
The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Content.
Ex: Very few physical science students stressed the ["Parameter" intellectual] ENJOYMENT of the degree course.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition: The Topic is the area about which the Experiencer has the tolerated experience(s). Ex: ["Experiencer" They] 're very TOLERANT ["Topic" about boys' mess in the home and untidiness generally].

fe.name: State
fe.definition: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer. Ex: ["Experiencer" Tracy] was in an IRRITATED ["State" mood].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition: The Eventis the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in. Ex: The end of the film was filled with JUBILANT ["Event" scenes]. Here we know that the scenes are filled with jubilant Experiencers.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances FE encodes the circumstances or conditions under which the Experiencer experiences the emotion. Unlike Content it does not give the specific content of the emotion, but the Content can often be inferred from the Circumstances.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition:
The time at which the Experiencer is in the state of toleration.
Ex: ["tim" When they are young,], they cannot STAND extremes of temperature.

lexunit.name: stand.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to withstand, endure

lexunit.name: endure.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to stand, undergo without failing

lexunit.name: tolerant.a
lexunit.definition: FN: able to accept or tolerate

lexunit.name: bear.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to withstand (e.g. hardship, pain)

lexunit.name: toleration.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the capacity or tendency to accept or endure (something that might be a problem or difficulty)

lexunit.name: tolerate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to accept or withstand (something which might be a problem or dificulty)

frame.name: Attempt_means
frame.definition:
An Agent attempts to achieve a Goal using some Means. The Means are crucially focused upon, typically appearing as the Object of the Target.
Ex: ["Agent" John] TRIED ["Means" using a crowbar] ["Goal" to open the door].
Ex: ["Agent" They] TRIED ["Means" opening the window] ["Goal" in order to rob the store].

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: ["Agent" John] TRIED a crowbar.

fe.name: Goal
fe.definition:
The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.
Ex: John TRIED using a crowbar ["Goal" to enter the locked door].

fe.name: Outcome
fe.definition:
Note: this FE might not be in frame. It is temporarily here during the early stage of annotation. (JGK)
The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to achieve a Goal. Ex: John's third ["Outcome" failed] ATTEMPT began propitiously.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition:
This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt occurs.
Ex: John TRIED ["Means" using a crowbar].

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition:
The place where an attempt is made.
Ex: ["Place" On the bridge] he TRIED using the crowbar.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
The Manner in which the Agent makes the attempt.
Ex: He TRIED using the crowbar ["man" quietly].

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: The time peiod over which the attempts take place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The reason for which the Agent attempts the Goal.

fe.name: Particular iteration
fe.definition: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is independent of the the attempt of the Agent to achieve the Goal.

fe.name: Domain
fe.definition:
Note: this FE might not be in frame. It is temporarily here during the early stage of annotation. (JGK)
The area of work to which the Attempt event belongs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: This FE denotes the number of times an event is attempted per some unit of time.

lexunit.name: try.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make an attempt using some means

frame.name: Pattern
frame.definition:
This frame describes the interrelation of a collection of Entities; they may be physical entites or shapes in a recognizable configuration, a pattern of events, or a relation among abstract entities. The pattern is not the individual Entities nor the set of Entities, but an abstraction of their interrelations, as a gestalt.
Ex: The Cougers are playing in a ["Name" Wing-T] FORMATION tonight. Ex: The auditors noticed a ["Descriptor" suspicious] PATTERN ["Entities" of withdrawals from the maintenance account] . Ex: The digits of irrational numbers do not repeat in any kind of PATTERN

fe.name: Entities
fe.definition: The entities whose interrelations form the pattern.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The name of the pattern, such as "wing-T".

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A descriptor of the pattern, such as "regular".

lexunit.name: pattern.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a configuration of entities, concrete or abstract

lexunit.name: formation.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an arrangement of entities forming a recognizable shape

frame.name: Sequence
frame.definition:
The words in this frame describe entities that occur in some temporally-ordered sequence. The entities thus have some sort of relation between them that might be described by the Relative_time frame. However, at this time, this frame has no Frame Relation with that frame (though this is still under discussion). Additionally, it should be noted that the words in this frame have a metaphorical link to the words in Shape.
Ex: Describe in detail the SEQUENCE ["Entities" of steps taken during an emergency].

fe.name: Entity1
fe.definition: This entity occurs in some sequence with Entity2.

fe.name: Entity2
fe.definition: This entity occurs in some sequence with respect to Entity1.

fe.name: Entities
fe.definition: Entities that occur in some temporal order.

fe.name: Relation_type
fe.definition:
A characterization of the sequence in which the entities occur.
Ex: The study consisted of a ["Relation_type" chronologically varied] SERIES of grotesque heads.

lexunit.name: sequence.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a temporal arrangement of entities

lexunit.name: succession.n
lexunit.definition: FN: sequence

lexunit.name: series.n
lexunit.definition: FN: entities placed in some temporal order

lexunit.name: sequential.a
lexunit.definition: FN: occurring in some sequence

lexunit.name: successive.a
lexunit.definition: FN: occurring in sequence without any intervening entities

lexunit.name: order.n
lexunit.definition: COD: the arrangement or disposition of people or things according to a particular sequence or method.

frame.name: Manipulate_into_shape
frame.definition: An Agent manipulates a Theme so that it ends up in a particular shape or configuration.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent is the volitional actor who manipulates the Theme.

fe.name: Instrument
fe.definition: The Instrument with which the Theme is manipulated.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The Means by which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The object which is manipulated by the Agent into a particular shape.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition:
Manner in which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.
Ex: John COILED the wire ["Manr" tightly] around the spool.

fe.name: Location
fe.definition:
Where the manipulation of the Theme takes place.
Ex: Kelly WOUND the laces ["Loc" around the back of her heel] to combat loose shoes.

lexunit.name: wind.v
lexunit.definition: FN: put a long, thin object into a roughly circular configuration, often by encircling another object.

lexunit.name: loop.v
lexunit.definition: FN: arrange an object into a loop or a shape approximating a loop.

lexunit.name: coil.v
lexunit.definition: FN: make into a coiled shape.

lexunit.name: twist.v
lexunit.definition: FN: turn or bend.

frame.name: Go_into_shape
frame.definition: A Theme, which may or may not have a default shape or configuration, goes into a particular shape. Depending on the type of shape, there may be a Locus about which the Theme changes shape.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: Where the shape-changing event takes place.

fe.name: Reason
fe.definition: The Reason for which the change into the shape occurs.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the changing into a particular shape occurs.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: How long the event takes place.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: Any description of the shape-changing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (_probably, presumably, mysteriously_), force (_hard, softly_), secondary effects (_quietly, loudly_), and general descriptions comparing events (_the same way_).

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: How often the shape changing occurs.

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition: The Theme goes into a particular shape.

frame.name: Capacity
frame.definition:
An Entity has the ability to contain a Theme.
Ex: ["ent" Our facility] SEATS ["the" up to 500 people].

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition:
The Entity whose ability to contain items is assessed.
Ex: ["ent" Our facility] SEATS up to 500 people.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for holding the items.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions for containing.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be able or unable to hold the items.

fe.name: Relevant_feature
fe.definition:
The characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Event.
CHANGE EXAMPLE
Ex: These computers have the ["rel" processing] CAPACITY to compute the precise date of the end of the world.

fe.name: Status
fe.definition: The status of the capability (e.g., innately, with modifications).

fe.name: Theme
fe.definition:
The Entity has the ability to contain the Theme, often expressed with a quantity.
Ex: Our facility SEATS ["the" up to 500 people].

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition:
A description of one of the participants, typically theTheme but possibly the Entity.
Ex: Our facilities SEAT 500 people ["dep" seated].

lexunit.name: seat.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have the capacity for holding a number of seated individuals.

lexunit.name: fit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be able to contain.

lexunit.name: take.v
lexunit.definition: FN: be able to contain.

lexunit.name: sleep.v
lexunit.definition: FN: have the capacity for a number of sleeping individuals.

frame.name: Event_instance
frame.definition: This frame describes a particular instance of an event.

fe.name: Instance
fe.definition:
The particular Instance of a given event.
Ex: He dumped trash for the last ["Instance" TIME].

fe.name: Event
fe.definition:
The event that occurred in one or more instances.
Ex: ["Event" Listen to this song] six TIMES.

fe.name: Instance_Prop
fe.definition:
A property of the particular Instance.
Ex: This is the ["Instance_Prop" first] TIME I've grown such delicious tea.

lexunit.name: time.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a particular instance of the occurence of an event.

lexunit.name: once.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: having just one instance of an event

lexunit.name: twice.adv
lexunit.definition: FN: having two instances of an event

frame.name: Point_in_time
frame.definition: The word(s) in this frame detail a particular moment in time.

fe.name: Relative_time
fe.definition: Relative_time denotes words that locate the time with respect to an identifiable reference point.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition:
Name denotes the name of the particular point in time.
Ex: Make sure you lock the doors at ["Name" closing] TIME.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
The Whole describes the larger unit of which the target word describes one part.
Ex: What TIME ["Whole" of day] is it?

fe.name: Unit
fe.definition:
The particular point in time, as denoted by the target word.
Ex: The ["Unit" TIME] is 10:00.

fe.name: Salient_event
fe.definition: Salient_event is an event that is associated with the given point in time. Ex: It is TIME ["Salient_event" to go].

fe.name: Measurement
fe.definition: Measurement marks a specific point in time relative to a 24 hour time system. Ex: The TIME is ["Measurement" 8:45].

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: A Descriptor is any characterization or description of the point in time that is not covered by a more specific FE.

lexunit.name: time.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a particular moment in time

frame.name: Timespan
frame.definition:
The words in this frame describe a period of time, as opposed to an exact length or point in time.
Ex: The ["Descriptor" best] TIME ["Whole" of year] ["State" for planting] tends to be fairly regular.

fe.name: Duration
fe.definition: A quantity or other characterization of the State's duration. In this frame, the duration is inexact.

fe.name: State
fe.definition:
An ongoing state whose duration can be measured.
Ex: ["State" He was a great actor] _in_ his TIME.

fe.name: Whole
fe.definition:
The Whole is the larger moment in time of which the target is a part.
Ex: What TIME ["Whole" of year] do you suggest we visit Tbilisi?

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Any characterization or evaluation of the timespan not covered by a more specific FE.

lexunit.name: time.n
lexunit.definition: FN: an indefinite period of time

frame.name: Concessive
frame.definition:
A speaker marks a Statement as being or implying a contradiction to the Main_statement. Some LUs specify the Main_statement, others the Statement, as referring to the preceding discourse (i.e. DNI), while yet others are conjunctions joining the two.
Ex: ALTHOUGH ["Statement" she had some trouble] , ["Main_statement" she was able to finish about two hours early] . Ex: NEVERTHELESS , ["Main_statement" we did win] . ["Statement" DNI] Ex: ["Statement" I wanted to come] , BUT ["Main_statement" I did n't remember where the party was] .

fe.name: Statement
fe.definition: A proposition or set of propositions that the speaker wants the addressee to believe or take for granted.

fe.name: Topic
fe.definition:
An entity which metonymically stands in for an associated Message.
Ex: She got married IN SPITE OF ["Top" him] . Ex: DESPITE ["Topic" her] , they finished on time .

fe.name: Main_statement
fe.definition: The statement that the speaker wishes to contradict part of without denying overall validity.

lexunit.name: despite.prep
lexunit.definition: In spite of

lexunit.name: in spite of.prep
lexunit.definition: in spite of

lexunit.name: though.scon
lexunit.definition: in spite of the fact that

lexunit.name: although.scon
lexunit.definition: in spite of the fact that

lexunit.name: nevertheless.adv
lexunit.definition: in spite of it

lexunit.name: but.c
lexunit.definition: except for the fact that

lexunit.name: however.adv
lexunit.definition: in spit of that

lexunit.name: while.scon
lexunit.definition: when on the other hand

frame.name: Cause_to_perceive
frame.definition:
An Agent, Actor, Entity, or Medium causes a Phenomenon to be perceived by a Perceiver. With an Actor, Entity, or Medium, the Perceiver is usually unspecified.
Ex: ["Agent" Aileen] SHOWED ["Perceiver" Rob] ["Phenomenon" the book]. Ex: ["Actor" He] EXHIBITED ["Phenomenon" great interest in the project]. Ex: ["Medium" The second scene] DEPICTS ["Phenomenon" Dad ] ["Phenomenon" holding the ball for a place kick]. Ex: ["Entity" The economy] is SHOWING ["Phenomenon" signs of growth].
NB: This may change in the future, but as of now this frame subsumes three closely-related cause/perceiver alternations: a.) perception of a specific Perceiver caused by an Agent, b.) perception of some implicit audience caused, possibly unintentionally, by an Actor, and c.) perception of a some implicit audience caused by a Medium or Entity.

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: The Agent intentionally creates a situation in which the Perceiver observes or experiences the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: The Phenomenon is an entity or idea that is perceived by the Perceiver.

fe.name: Perceiver
fe.definition: The Perceiver is made to have a perceptual experience by the Agent.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: The instrument or method by which the Perceiver was shown the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Manner
fe.definition: A description of the way in which the Agent presents the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: When the event occurs.

fe.name: Frequency
fe.definition: Frequency describes how often the Agent presents the Phenomenon.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The location where the Agent causes the perception of the Perceiver.

fe.name: Purpose
fe.definition: The purpose of the Agent in creating the perception of the Perceiver.

fe.name: Actor
fe.definition: An Actor is a sentient being who is exhibiting, possibly uninintentionally, some Phenomenon.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The Medium through which a Phenomenon is expressed.

fe.name: Co_participant
fe.definition: A Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the Actor or Agent.

fe.name: Explanation
fe.definition: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

lexunit.name: show.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to make visible or noticeable

lexunit.name: demonstrate.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to give an explanation and/or exhibition of

lexunit.name: present.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to exhibit something to others

lexunit.name: point.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to indicate the existense or direction of something or some event

lexunit.name: depict.v
lexunit.definition: COD: represent by a drawing, painting, or other art form

lexunit.name: represent.v
lexunit.definition: WN: express indirectly by an image, form, or model

lexunit.name: exhibit.v
lexunit.definition: FN: to display or show

frame.name: Representing
frame.definition: A non-agentive Medium, usually a work of art or a piece of media, or an Entity represents some Phenomenon through its existence and/or defining characteristics. Sometimes a Cognizer, a people or group of people who believe in the representation, is expressed. Ex: ["Entity" A bear] SYMBOLIZES ["Phenomenon" strength] ["Cognizer" in some cultures].

fe.name: Medium
fe.definition: The Medium through which a Phenomenon is expressed.

fe.name: Phenomenon
fe.definition: The event or idea evoked by the Medium or Entity.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition:
This FE describes the Degree to which the Medium represents the Phenomenon.
Ex: ["Medium" That mural] IS ["Degree" hardly] A SYMBOL ["Phenomenon" of what we're all about!]

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time period in which the representing occurs.

fe.name: Means
fe.definition: This FE describes the action through which the representing occurs. Ex: ["Phenomenon" What] does ["Entity" a black and white snake] SYMBOLIZE ["Means" in a dream]?

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.

fe.name: Cognizer
fe.definition: The Cognizer is the person or group of people who believe in the representation.

lexunit.name: symbolize.v
lexunit.definition: COD: represent by means of a symbol (usually a work of art)

lexunit.name: be symbol.v
lexunit.definition: FN: represent or symbolize (something)

frame.name: Labor_product
frame.definition:
An Agent or a Cause mentally or pysically expends energy rendering an Input, whether implicit or explicit, into a Output.
Ex: ["Output" Erosion] _is_ the WORK ["Cause" of wind and water] ["Input" on rock].
NB: The Input in the case of artistic Output or an " artistic work" as more commonly refered to usually has an INI Input, because the material at hand being rendered is usually an idea or artistic material that is taken as common foreground knowledge by the semantics of the Agent's professional role.
Ex: One of ["Agent" Chinua Achebe's] greatest WRITINGS _was_ ["Output" Things Fall Apart]. ["Input" INI]

fe.name: Agent
fe.definition: A sentient entity whose physical and mental faculties are directly expended on the Input to create the Output.

fe.name: Cause
fe.definition: A non-sentient entity whose physical faculties are directly expended on the Input to create the Output.

fe.name: Input
fe.definition: The mental or physical faculties onto which the Agent or Cause expends energy.

fe.name: Output
fe.definition: The end product, either a concept or physical object onto which the Agent or Cause has exerted its mental or physical faculties from the rudimentary state of Input.

fe.name: Depictive
fe.definition: A word or phrase that characterizes the target.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The time at which the Output was committed into reality.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where the Output was birthed.

fe.name: Honoree
fe.definition: The entity for whom the Output is created.

fe.name: Presentation
fe.definition: The place where the target or Output is presented.

lexunit.name: oeuvre.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the life work of an artist.

lexunit.name: work.n
lexunit.definition: FN: the product or result of one's effort.

frame.name: Sound_level
frame.definition: An Entity is judged by a sound Attribute of some perceived level of Volume intensity.

fe.name: Entity
fe.definition: The Entity for which the sound level Attribute is under consideration.

fe.name: Attribute
fe.definition: The feature of an Entity which is under consideration.

fe.name: Volume
fe.definition: A quantity or characterization of the Entity's sound output with repspect to its Attribute.

fe.name: Degree
fe.definition: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Volume from the norm.

fe.name: Circumstances
fe.definition: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Volume for the Attribute.

fe.name: Time
fe.definition: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular Volume for the Attribute.

fe.name: Place
fe.definition: The place where an Entity is located.

lexunit.name: loud.a
lexunit.definition: FN: an acoustic output percieved as being a high volume

lexunit.name: quiet.a
lexunit.definition: FN: an acoustic output percieved as being a low volume

frame.name: Locale_by_ownership
frame.definition:
A place defined by an Owner.
Ex: Get off ["Owner" my] ["Locale" property]!

fe.name: Locale
fe.definition: A stable bounded area. It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.

fe.name: Relative_location
fe.definition: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.

fe.name: Owner
fe.definition: The individual or group of individuals who hold posses the Locale.

fe.name: Constituent_parts
fe.definition: Salient parts that make up a Locale.

fe.name: Descriptor
fe.definition: Any feature or characteristic of the Locale not covered by more specific FEs.

fe.name: Container_possessor
fe.definition: The location that the Locale is a part of.

fe.name: Name
fe.definition: The name of the Locale.

fe.name: Use
fe.definition: The activity that is carried out in the Locale.

lexunit.name: land.n
lexunit.definition: FN: a location that is someone's or something's property (e.g. real estate land, stewardship land, etc.)

lexunit.name: property.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a building and the land belonging to it

lexunit.name: estate.n
lexunit.definition: COD: a property consisting of a large house and extensive grounds

frame.name: Long_or_short_selling
frame.definition: A common finance market concept that involves a Lender who lends some form of Assets to an Intermediary who in turn will sell those Assets to the Market. The eventual intent is for the Intermediary to repurchase the Assets from the Market for profit and return them to the Lender.

fe.name: Lender
fe.definition: The original owner and soon to be Lender of the Assets.

fe.name: Assets
fe.definition: The financial Assets being traded.

fe.name: Intermediary
fe.definition: The entity that is the borrower to the Lender and the seller and later repurchaser to the Market.

fe.name: Market
fe.definition: The aggregate selling place of many types of financial stocks, bond, securities, etc. The Market is also a metonym for the people who buy the Assets.

lexunit.name: sell long.v
lexunit.definition: FN: the intermediary profits from selling stocks high and buy them back lower then he/she bought them.

lexunit.name: sell short.v
lexunit.definition: FN: the intermediary profits from selling stocks high and buy them back lower then he/she bought them.
